dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-meadows.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE sciences to Years 9 to 11: Cambridge 0610, 0620, 0625 and 0654, and the Pearson Edexcel equivalents. Each one works from the paper structure your child's school entered them for, not a generic science scheme of work.

intro.heading: The science grade is decided in the ninety minutes after the school run
paragraphs: The Meadows is nine villa sub-communities inside Emirates Living, bounded by Sheikh Zayed Road on one side and Al Khail Road on the other. Almost no child here walks to school. Emirates International School Meadows sits inside the community, and everyone else drives out to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, Al Safa, Emirates Hills or Motor City in the morning and back again at half past three. That daily shape, not the syllabus, is what decides whether science tuition works for a family in Meadows 3 or Meadows 8.

Most British-curriculum secondary timetables in this part of Dubai finish between 15:00 and 15:30, and many run activities until roughly 16:30. Check your own child's timetable rather than an average, because the difference between a 15:05 and a 15:35 bell is the difference between a session that starts at five and one that starts at six. By the time a Year 11 student has been collected from Al Barsha, eaten something and found their folder, the usable science window in a Meadows household runs from about 17:00 to 18:30 on a weekday, with a second, shorter slot after 19:30 that is good for reviewing marked work and poor for new theory.

A tutor who drives loses that window twice over. The same Al Khail Road traffic that carried your child home carries the tutor in, then carries them out again before the next appointment, and the family pays for both journeys in the hourly rate. Market rates for in-home visits in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour depending on level and travel, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, on the figures published by Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table and by agencies including Unitors and EdFlik. The gap is largely the car.

The second thing the school run decides is which tutor is even possible. A radius of twenty minutes around Emirates Living contains a certain number of people who can teach science. It does not reliably contain someone who has taught Cambridge 0654 Paper 4 for eight years and can tell you, from the way your child writes a conclusion, whether the marks are being lost on command terms or on significant figures. Teaching over live video removes the radius from the equation, and that is the whole of the argument for it.

What follows is written for that household: which science route your child is actually sitting, where each paper's marks sit, when a session realistically fits around a Meadows weekday, and what the entry deadlines look like counted backwards from the exam. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run only in India. Everything here is delivered as one-to-one tuition over live video, with the first lesson free so you can judge the tutor before you commit a term to them.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-meadows.programmesIntro: Science at IGCSE is not one qualification. Four routes run through schools near The Meadows, and the tutoring that helps a 0654 candidate is not the tutoring that helps someone sitting three separate codes. Match the route first.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Sciences
programmes.description: Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625, Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 and Combined Science 0653. Extended candidates sit Paper 2, Paper 4 and either the Paper 5 practical test or the Paper 6 alternative to practical. Core candidates sit Papers 1, 3 and 5 or 6, with a grade ceiling at C. The route and tier appear on the statement of entry, which is the document a tutor should see before the first lesson.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs a June and a November series, plus Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong zone timetable was used. Dubai schools sit the zone timetable their centre is assigned, so the official timetable PDF matters more than any date a tutor quotes from memory.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Science
programmes.description: Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1, Physics 4PH1 and Science (Double Award) 4SD0. Practical skills are assessed inside the written papers rather than in a separate practical exam, which changes revision completely: there is no apparatus list to rehearse, but experimental method questions are embedded in papers that also carry theory and calculation. Students who moved from Cambridge mid-course often revise for a practical paper that does not exist on their entry.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson offers International GCSE in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so the live PDF on qualifications.pearson.com is the only version worth planning around.

programmes.name: Year 9 pre-IGCSE science
programmes.description: The year the route is chosen. A Year 9 student who is comfortable rearranging equations and reading a results table will cope with three separate sciences; one who is not will carry that gap through two years of Paper 4 calculations. Work in this year is about arithmetic fluency, unit handling and writing a conclusion that answers the question asked, rather than coverage of IGCSE content a term early.
programmes.countryNote: Option forms in Dubai British-curriculum schools usually go out in the second term of Year 9, and the science decision is frequently made by the timetable rather than the family. Ask the head of science whether the school allows a move from Co-ordinated Sciences to three separate codes after the options deadline, and whether that move is possible in Year 11 at all. The answer varies school by school across Al Barsha and Al Sufouh.

programmes.name: IGCSE science into IB Diploma or A Level
programmes.description: The exit route changes what a Year 11 grade needs to be. Higher Level Chemistry and A Level Physics both assume fluency with material that IGCSE treats lightly: moles beyond simple ratio, logarithms, and graph gradients read as physical quantities. A student who scrapes a 6 in 0654 and then takes Higher Level Biology spends the first Diploma term closing a gap that could have been closed in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Schools around The Meadows split both ways at 16. Emirates International School Meadows runs the IB continuum through to the Diploma; Dubai British School Emirates Hills, Dubai College and Jumeirah College run A Levels; several families move from one campus to another at that point. KHDA has confirmed seven new private schools for the 2026-27 intake - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - adding 16,846 places, so the sixth-form market around Emirates Living is still shifting.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-meadows.subjectsIntro: Science tutoring is specific to a code and a tier. These are the entries that actually appear on statements of entry at schools serving The Meadows, with what each one assesses and where the marks tend to go missing.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Extended candidates sit Paper 2, Paper 4 and Paper 5 or 6. Marks concentrate in the long structured questions on transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance. The commonest avoidable loss is a Punnett square drawn correctly and then explained without naming the genotypes, which earns the diagram mark and loses the explanation marks.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic chemistry carry the Extended paper. Students who can balance an equation but cannot convert between mass, moles and concentration lose Paper 4 marks in clusters rather than singly, because the later parts of a question depend on the answer to the earlier parts. Rate-of-reaction graph interpretation is the second recurring gap.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity is where most students lose ground: series and parallel circuits, potential dividers, and the difference between what an ammeter and a voltmeter are measuring. Thermal physics questions ask for particle-level explanations and get answers written in terms of heat moving around, which the mark scheme does not credit.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: Two IGCSE grades from a single entry, which makes it the default on most British-curriculum timetables in Dubai. The Extended Paper 4 runs two hours and covers all three sciences in one sitting, so pacing is a skill in its own right: students who spend thirty minutes on the biology section arrive at physics with too little time to finish.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: One grade covering all three sciences, usually chosen when a student carries a heavy language or humanities load. The content is narrower than 0654, which helps, but universities and sixth forms read a single award differently from a double award, so the route choice should be checked against what the student intends to study at 16.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: Paper 1 carries the bulk of the marks and the longer questions; Paper 2 is shorter and heavier on the sections Cambridge spreads across its papers. Practical method questions appear inside both papers rather than in a standalone practical exam, so revision has to include apparatus and variables even though no lab exam exists on this specification.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Calculation style differs enough from Cambridge that a mid-course transfer notices it. Edexcel asks for more multi-step quantitative work in a single question part, and marks are tied to showing the route rather than the final figure. Students who were trained to write only the answer lose method marks they would have kept on 0620.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Equation recall matters more here than on some specifications, because the formula sheet does not cover everything the papers ask for. Waves, radioactivity and electrical circuits reward students who can write the equation, substitute with units, and state the unit of the answer. The last of those three is the step most often skipped.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Science (Double Award) 4SD0
subjects.description: Six shorter papers rather than two long ones, which suits students who lose accuracy over a two-hour sitting. Each science contributes two papers, and the double award produces two grades. Schools sometimes run this alongside a separate single science, so a tutor needs the full entry list to know which content is examined where.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Listed here because it is the single strongest predictor of a science grade. Rearranging formulae, standard form, percentage change and reading gradients off a graph are maths skills examined inside science papers. A student losing physics marks on calculation is often losing maths marks in a physics costume, and the fix belongs in a maths lesson.

sections.heading: Find out which science route your child is actually sitting
paragraphs: Four separate things get called "IGCSE science" by parents in Dubai, and they are not interchangeable. Three separate sciences produce three grades. Co-ordinated Sciences produces two from a single entry. Combined Science produces one. The Pearson Edexcel versions sit different papers again, with no standalone practical exam. A tutor who starts work without knowing which of these your child is entered for will spend the first three lessons teaching content that may not be examined.

The document that settles it is the statement of entry, which the school issues before each series. It carries the syllabus code, the tier and the components. If it has not arrived yet, the school's exams officer can confirm the code, and the head of science can confirm the tier. Those two facts are worth more to a tutor than any amount of description of how your child is finding the subject.

Tier matters as much as route. Cambridge Core papers cap the available grade at C, so a student who is capable of a B and has been entered for Core cannot reach it however well they prepare. Moving between tiers has a deadline, and that deadline sits with the entry rather than with the exam. A Year 11 parent asking in January whether a move is still possible is often asking after the window has shut.

The table below sets out the routes as the specifications define them. Confirm your child's own code against the statement of entry before using any of it to plan, because schools near The Meadows run several of these in the same year group and change the mix between cohorts.

sections.heading: A Meadows weekday, bell to screen
paragraphs: Tuition fails on logistics far more often than on teaching. The usual version of that failure in Emirates Living is a session booked at 16:00 in September, when the afternoon is still quiet, which collides with swimming in October and is quietly abandoned by November. The fix is to build the slot around the one thing that does not move, which is the school bell, and then leave room for the drive.

Finish times vary by school and by year group. Most British secondary timetables in the Al Barsha and Al Sufouh corridor end between 15:00 and 15:30, with activities running to roughly 16:30, and the IB campus inside Emirates Living runs its own pattern. Use your own child's timetable. The point of the clock below is not the exact minute but the shape: pick-up and travel consume the first hour after school, and the hour after that is the best teaching hour of the day.

The second window, after 19:30, is not a substitute for the first. It is good for a different job. Reviewing a marked past-paper question, going through where the method marks went, rehearsing a Paper 6 method description - these work late. Learning electrolysis from a standing start at eight in the evening does not, and a tutor who agrees to try is agreeing to waste your money.

Friday and the weekend are the only slots long enough for a full timed paper plus a review of it. Families who are serious about the final eight weeks before a series put one weekend session in the diary from the start of the term rather than adding it in panic in April.

sections.heading: Where the grade actually sits, component by component
paragraphs: Parents usually know their child's predicted grade and rarely know how that grade is assembled. On the Cambridge Extended route the written theory paper carries half the marks on its own, the multiple-choice paper carries almost a third, and the practical component carries a fifth. Revision time that is split evenly across those three is split wrongly.

The multiple-choice paper is where the cheapest marks in IGCSE science are won and lost. Forty items, forty-five minutes, no method marks and no credit for partial understanding. The distractors are written from the misconceptions examiners see most often, which means a student who half-knows a topic will be pulled towards the wrong answer by design. Practising it as a timed drill, with every wrong answer traced back to the misconception behind it, moves marks faster than almost anything else available.

The theory paper rewards something different: reading the command term and answering the question that was asked. "Explain" answered as "describe" earns nothing, however accurate the description. "Suggest" invites an answer from outside the taught content and students leave it blank because they are waiting to recall something. Teaching the vocabulary of the mark scheme is teaching the subject, not a trick.

The practical component is 20% that is examinable entirely in writing. Significant figures, units in table headings, the difference between a controlled variable and a control experiment, plotting a line of best fit rather than joining the dots - all of it is written work, all of it is drillable, and most of it is left until the last fortnight.

sections.heading: The entry deadline sits months before the exam
paragraphs: Of everything a Year 10 or Year 11 family gets wrong about IGCSE, the timeline is the most expensive and the least discussed. Competitor pages in this market name no session, no entry deadline and no results date at all. The entry is made months before the paper is sat, and the decisions locked in at entry - route, tier, which sciences - are the decisions that set the ceiling on the grade.

Pearson gives the cleanest worked example, because its International GCSE windows are published as dates a parent can check: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Entries for each of those windows closed months ahead of the first paper. Cambridge has the same shape across the two series a Meadows candidate can sit, June and November, with the June entry made in the spring and results in August -- the February and March series belongs to India and should be ignored here. The lesson is the same either way: the fork in the road is in the autumn term, not in the exam season, and the exact deadline comes from your school's exams officer rather than from a page like this one.

Pearson's calendar runs on the same logic. International GCSE is offered in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables in advance and revises them, so plan against the live PDF rather than a remembered date.

Two practical consequences for a Meadows household. First, ask the exams officer in October which series your child is entered for and confirm the tier at the same time. Second, if tuition is going to happen at all, it is worth more in the term before the entry closes than in the fortnight before the paper, because in the earlier term the route is still a choice.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE science marks are actually lost, topic by topic
paragraphs: A diagnostic lesson is worth more than a syllabus walkthrough, because the losses in IGCSE science are concentrated and predictable. Across Cambridge and Edexcel alike, the same half-dozen places account for most of the gap between a 6 and an 8. Naming them is how a tutor earns the second lesson.

In chemistry the gap is almost always quantitative. A student who can balance an equation but cannot move between mass, moles and concentration loses marks in clusters, because later parts of a structured question are built on the answer to the earlier part. One wrong conversion in part (b) costs parts (c) and (d) as well. Rate-of-reaction graphs come second: reading a gradient as a rate, and explaining why the curve flattens, are two separate skills and students often have only the first.

In physics it is electricity, every year. Series and parallel circuits, where the current divides and where the voltage does, what a potential divider is for, and which instrument measures which quantity. Thermal physics is the other recurring loss, where the mark scheme wants a particle-level explanation and gets an answer about heat travelling around the room. In biology the losses sit in long-answer questions on transport, homeostasis and inheritance, where the diagram is right and the explanation never names the structures doing the work.

Two cross-cutting failures matter more than any topic. The first is maths dressed as science: standard form, rearranging a formula, percentage change. The second is command terms, which are the vocabulary the mark scheme is written in. Both are faster to fix than content, and both are invisible on a school report that says a child needs to revise more.

sections.heading: Teaching practical science when the tutor is on a screen
paragraphs: The honest question a Meadows parent asks about online science tuition is whether the practical side survives it. The answer depends on separating two different things: doing experiments, and being examined on them. Your child does the first at school, in the school's laboratory, under the school's supervision, and no tutor of any kind replaces that. The second is a written exam, and a written exam can be taught in full over video.

Paper 5 candidates sit a supervised practical and record readings live. What decides their marks is rarely the manipulation of apparatus: it is table design, significant figures, unit handling, scale choice, plotting, and reading a value off a line of best fit. Every one of those is a written convention, drillable with shared past papers on screen and a tutor watching the student's working as it is produced. Paper 6 candidates never touch apparatus in the exam at all - their paper is entirely about describing method, identifying variables and interpreting someone else's results.

Screen sharing turns out to help here rather than hinder. A tutor watching a student plot a graph in real time sees the moment the scale is chosen badly, which is the moment the marks are lost, and can stop it there. In a classroom of twenty-four that moment is invisible. Edexcel candidates, whose practical skills are assessed inside the written papers, are in the same position: the examinable material is all on paper.

What a tutor must not do is produce or complete any assessed work. Coursework, where a specification carries it, and any school-set investigation remain the student's own. A tutor teaches the method, reviews the student's own draft, and gives feedback on it. Anything beyond that is a malpractice risk for your child and a line IB Gram does not cross.

sections.heading: What families around Emirates Living pay, and the three ways the money is wasted
paragraphs: Market rates for tutoring in Dubai are public if you go looking, and they vary by a factor of ten. Budget online tutoring, usually delivered by university students, advertises from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour - EdFlik publishes from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to AED 52. A qualified subject tutor working online runs roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home visits, with travel priced in, run roughly AED 180 to AED 500. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutors run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and premium named tutors advertised as high as AED 650. These are other people's published figures, quoted as the market, not as our price list.

The first way the money is wasted is paying a travel premium to get a smaller choice of tutor. A twenty-minute radius around Emirates Living is a real constraint on who can teach your child, and it is the constraint that produces a generalist teaching Paper 4 chemistry. The second is buying a long package before the tutor has taught a single lesson. Three sciences bought as a term block in September, with no diagnostic lesson, is how families end up paying for coverage of topics their child already has.

The third is the group class sold as one-to-one economics. Four students at a lower rate each is cheaper per hour and is not the same product: the whole value of one-to-one science is that the tutor watches this child's working and interrupts at the point the error happens. In a group the tutor is teaching a mean, and the mean is not your child.

Worth holding alongside all of this: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai will not rise for 2026-27, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School costs are flat this year. That makes it a reasonable year to spend on the thing the school day does not cover, rather than a year to buy more hours than the household can actually sit through.

sections.heading: Starting from The Meadows, with the limits stated up front
paragraphs: Getting started is deliberately short. You tell us the syllabus code, the tier, the school and your child's actual finish time; we propose a tutor who teaches that code; the first lesson is free and is used as a diagnostic rather than a sales call; and if the match is wrong we change it. Nothing about that requires anyone to drive anywhere, which is why a 17:00 slot on a Tuesday is genuinely available rather than theoretically available.

The limits, stated plainly. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address, and home visits in Dubai are not something we sell - that service exists only in India. Every lesson here is one-to-one over live video. We hold no accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and any page that implies otherwise about any provider is worth treating with suspicion. We are an independent tutor-matching platform, nothing more and nothing less.

On permits, the position in the UAE is clear and worth knowing before you hire anyone, including from a classified ad. Private tuition is regulated: Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced a private tutor work permit through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific figure you read with caution. The application route is MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service.

Availability is finite and we say so. A tutor for Extended 0620 chemistry is usually matched within a few days. A niche request - a specific Edexcel double-award combination at short notice in exam season, say - sometimes is not, and when a UAE-based tutor is not free the alternative offered may be a specialist elsewhere in the world working to Gulf Standard Time. You will be told which before you book, not after.

process.title: Send the statement of entry
process.description: The syllabus code and tier decide everything else. If the statement has not arrived, the school's exams officer can confirm the code and the head of science the tier. Those two lines of information save a tutor three lessons of guessing and save you the cost of them.

process.title: Tell us the real finish time
process.description: Not the school's published end of day, but the time your child is actually home in Meadows 5 with a folder open. That single number decides whether the weekly slot is 17:00 or 18:00, and a slot built on a guess is the slot that gets abandoned in November.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic lesson
process.description: One lesson, free, one per family, no card details required. It is used to find where the marks are going - command terms, mole conversions, circuits, graph conventions - and ends with a written view of what the next six weeks should cover. You decide afterwards whether to continue.

process.title: Fix one weekly slot per science
process.description: One science per session, same time each week, for the term. Three sciences means three slots rather than one longer lesson covering all three thinly. Marked work from the previous week opens each session, which is what makes homework worth setting.

process.title: Switch to paper practice eight weeks out
process.description: The last stretch before a series moves from topics to papers: Paper 2 timing, Paper 4 structured questions, then the practical component. One weekend slot is added for full timed papers, because a weekday evening cannot hold a two-hour paper and a review of it.

whyPoints.title: The tutor matches the code, not the subject
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0654 and Edexcel 4SD0 are both "double award science" and they examine differently. Matching on the code means the tutor already knows the paper structure, the mark scheme wording and where that specification punishes a weak method description.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the price, no radius on the choice
whyPoints.description: Market in-home rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel priced in. Removing the drive removes both the premium and the twenty-minute radius that limits who can teach your child in the first place.

whyPoints.title: Built around the Emirates Living clock
whyPoints.description: Sessions are scheduled against your child's own bell time and the drive home, not against a template. The 17:00 to 18:30 window is the one that survives a full term, and a slot that survives is worth more than a slot that looked convenient in September.

whyPoints.title: The practical component is treated as 20%, not an afterthought
whyPoints.description: Paper 5 and Paper 6 are worth a fifth of the grade and are examined in writing. Table design, significant figures, variables and graph conventions are taught deliberately rather than left to the fortnight before the exam.

whyPoints.title: Clear lines on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, review and give feedback on the student's own work. No tutor here produces coursework, an investigation write-up or any assessed task. That line protects your child's entry, and it is the line the essay-selling end of this market crosses.

whyPoints.title: Limits disclosed before you book
whyPoints.description: Rates quoted on this page are other providers' published market figures with the source named. Availability gaps are stated rather than hidden, and we claim no regulator approval, no UAE office and no school partnership, because we hold none.

faqs.question: Is my child sitting Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 or three separate IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry answers it, and the difference is large. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is one entry producing two IGCSE grades, with a two-hour Paper 4 covering biology, chemistry and physics in a single sitting. Three separate sciences means 0610, 0620 and 0625, three entries, three grades and three sets of papers. Combined Science 0653 produces one grade. Schools near The Meadows run more than one of these in the same year group, often split by option block, so a parent cannot infer it from what another family's child is doing. Ask the exams officer for the code and the tier together.

faqs.question: How do I find out which science syllabus code my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Three sources, in order of reliability. The statement of entry, issued by the school before each series, lists the code, the tier and the components. The exams officer can confirm the same information at any point in the year, and usually faster. The head of science can confirm the tier and whether a move between Core and Extended is still possible. A textbook cover is not a reliable source, because schools sometimes teach from one publisher while entering candidates on a different specification. Send the code to any tutor before the first lesson.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor really help with Paper 5, the practical exam?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the part that carries the marks. Paper 5 candidates record readings live in a supervised practical, but marks are concentrated in written conventions: table headings with units, significant figures, scale choice, plotting, and reading values off a line of best fit. All of that is teachable over video with shared past papers, and a tutor watching the working as it happens catches a bad scale choice at the moment it is made. The experiments themselves stay at school, in the school's laboratory, under the school's supervision. No tutor of any format replaces school lab time.

faqs.question: What is Paper 6 and why does it carry twenty per cent of the grade?
faqs.answer: Paper 6 is the alternative to practical: a written paper in which candidates describe methods, identify variables, read results tables and interpret someone else's data without touching apparatus. It carries the same weight as the practical test it replaces, around a fifth of the Extended grade, which makes it the single most under-prepared component in IGCSE science. The commonest loss is a method description that never names the controlled variable, followed by graph work where the axes are chosen badly. It is entirely drillable, and it is usually left until the last fortnight.

faqs.question: My child finishes school at 3:15 in Al Sufouh. What time can a Meadows session start?
faqs.answer: Allow for the drive back into Emirates Living and the twenty minutes that follow it, and 17:00 is the realistic earliest start, with 17:30 safer if there is an activity on that day. The afternoon window between 17:00 and 18:30 is the best teaching hour available in most Meadows households: late enough that everyone is home, early enough that a Paper 4 calculation still lands. Sessions after 19:30 work well for reviewing marked work and badly for new content. Tell us the actual finish time rather than the school's published one, because they differ by year group.

faqs.question: Which schools do children in The Meadows usually attend for IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: Emirates International School Meadows sits inside the community and runs the IB continuum. For IGCSE, families drive out: Dubai British School Emirates Hills and Regent International School nearby, then the Al Barsha and Al Sufouh corridor with GEMS Wellington International School, Kings' School Al Barsha, Dubai College, Jumeirah College, Repton School Al Barsha and Nord Anglia International School Dubai. Further out sit Safa Community School, Dubai Heights Academy and GEMS Metropole Motor City. We have no affiliation with any of them; they are named as the local context that shapes bell times and option blocks.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE science tutor who will come to our villa in Meadows 7?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses, and home visits in Dubai are not part of what we sell - that service runs only in India. The market for in-home visits does exist and advertises roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel priced in, so the honest comparison is cost and choice: a drive-in tutor must live within about twenty minutes of Emirates Living, while an online specialist can be the person who has taught Extended 0620 for a decade. Our lessons are one-to-one over live video, first one free.

faqs.question: We are eight weeks from the exam and physics is the weak subject. What can still be done?
faqs.answer: A great deal, provided the work switches from topics to papers. Eight weeks allows roughly two sessions a week plus one weekend slot for full timed papers. Week one is diagnostic: a past Paper 4 marked against the official scheme to find whether the losses are circuits, calculation or command terms. Weeks two to six attack the four weakest topics with timed question sets. The last fortnight goes to Paper 2 timing drills and the practical component. Nobody can promise a particular grade from eight weeks, and any tutor who does should be treated with real scepticism.

faqs.question: Should my child move from Core to Extended science in Year 11?
faqs.answer: It depends on the arithmetic and the deadline. Cambridge Core caps the available grade at C, so a student capable of a B cannot reach it from a Core entry however hard they work. Extended demands fluency with rearranging formulae, standard form and multi-step calculation, which is where the decision actually turns. The move has to happen while the entry can still be amended, and that window closes with the entry deadline rather than the exam. Ask the head of science and the exams officer in the same conversation, and ask early in the autumn term.

faqs.question: Does Edexcel International GCSE science have a practical exam like Cambridge?
faqs.answer: No. On Pearson Edexcel specifications such as 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and the 4SD0 double award, practical skills are assessed inside the written papers rather than in a separate practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. The consequence for revision is specific: there is no apparatus list to rehearse for its own paper, but experimental method and variables questions appear inside papers that also carry theory and calculation. Students who transferred from a Cambridge school mid-course sometimes revise for a practical paper that does not exist on their entry, which is wasted time.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE science lessons cost around Emirates Living?
faqs.answer: Published market figures rather than ours: budget online tutoring advertises from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to AED 52. Qualified subject tutors online run roughly AED 150 to AED 300, Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home visits run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 with travel included. IGCSE and IB specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and above. For what IB Gram itself would charge for your child's code and tier, take the free trial lesson and ask on the call.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover biology, chemistry and physics for the same child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is usually the wrong economy. A Co-ordinated Sciences candidate who is broadly fine but slipping can work well with one tutor who knows 0654 as a whole. A student losing marks on organic chemistry and on circuits needs two specialists, because the diagnosis in each case is subject-specific and deep. The compromise most Meadows families settle on is one tutor for the weakest science weekly, and a short block of sessions on the second weakest before the series. Three sciences taught thinly in one hour helps nobody.

faqs.question: Do private science tutors in Dubai need a permit from MoHRE?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, issued through MoHRE and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The application runs through MoHRE's 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so distrust any specific amount quoted to you.

faqs.question: Will five IGCSEs including sciences be enough for Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, the Ministry's requirement as reported is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among those five, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure, which is wrong. Verify your child's own case against moe.gov.ae or the attestation authority directly. Equivalency is a process families complete themselves; IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees it.

faqs.question: Can a weekly science slot move later during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most Emirates Living families ask for it. School hours shorten during Ramadan, which frees the afternoon, and many households prefer to move a session to after iftar when the house has settled. Both directions work: an earlier slot in the shortened school day, or a later one in the evening. The thing worth protecting is the slot's consistency rather than its time, so we agree the Ramadan pattern in advance and revert to the usual slot afterwards. Exam-season sessions take priority if a series falls close by.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-meadows.closingHeading: Start with the code, the tier and your child's actual finish time
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-meadows.closingBody: Those three facts are enough to propose a tutor for an IGCSE science entry in The Meadows, and the first lesson costs nothing - one per family, no card details required. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time and built around the window between 17:00 and 18:30 that a Meadows weekday actually leaves open. We hold no regulator approval and no school affiliation, we do not send tutors to UAE addresses, and we will tell you before you book if nobody is free for the code you need. Send the statement of entry and we will tell you what the next six weeks should cover.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-springs.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences to students across The Springs and Emirates Living. Each is matched to one science rather than to all three, and every lesson is one-to-one over live video.

intro.heading: Science is one word on a timetable and three different jobs
paragraphs: The question behind this search is a fair one and deserves a straight answer. Yes, there are science tutors available to families in The Springs, and no, most of them do not know all three sciences to the same depth. Biology, chemistry and physics are examined by the same board in the same fortnight and they reward completely different habits. A tutor who is genuinely strong in one is often adequate in the second and guessing in the third, and the only way a parent finds out is by asking questions specific enough that a general answer cannot hide.

Here is what differs. Biology marks are won and lost on terminology: the mark scheme accepts particular words and rejects near-synonyms, so an answer that sounds right scores nothing. Chemistry marks turn on arithmetic and on symbolic accuracy - moles, balanced equations, state symbols, and the tables of tests for ions and gases supplied with the paper. Physics marks depend on unit discipline, rearranging an equation under pressure, and reading a gradient rather than a data point. Three subjects, three diagnostic patterns, three different first lessons.

The second thing worth establishing is which qualification is on the entry. Cambridge separate sciences carry the codes 0610 for biology, 0620 for chemistry and 0625 for physics, with Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 as a double award and Combined Science 0653 as a single. Pearson uses 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, with Double Award Science 4SD0. The paper counts differ, and so does how practical skills are assessed: Cambridge sets a separate practical or alternative-to-practical component, while Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers. A tutor who does not ask which of these applies has told you something already.

The third is tier, where it exists. Cambridge separate sciences are entered at Core or Extended, and that decision caps the grade available regardless of how good the teaching is. A family paying specialist rates to chase a top grade while the entry sits at Core tier is paying for an outcome the entry form has excluded. Ask the department which tier each science is entered at, because it is not unusual for one of the three to differ from the other two.

Delivery, stated plainly: all lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, because home tutoring is a service offered only in India. For science specifically, the online format makes practical work easier to teach rather than harder, because a tutor can put a real examiner's photograph of apparatus on the screen and ask what is wrong with it, which a textbook at a kitchen table cannot do.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-springs.programmesIntro: Science support from a Springs household arrives at four recognisable points, and what a tutor should be doing is different at each. Naming the point first prevents a general plan being applied to a specific problem.

programmes.name: Year 9, before the science route is chosen
programmes.description: The decision that matters most is whether the student takes three separate sciences, a double award or a single. A child on double award cannot later present separate physics and chemistry grades to a department that asks for them. Tutoring here is advisory and short: two or three sessions to establish whether the separate route is realistic.
programmes.countryNote: Option evenings in schools serving The Springs sit in the spring term of Year 9, with forms due within a fortnight. Ask specifically how many periods a week the separate-science route takes and what it displaces, because in several Dubai schools it costs the second language or the arts option.

programmes.name: Year 10
programmes.description: Content is being taught for the first time, which makes consolidation cheap and effective. The highest-value work here is building the habits the mark schemes reward: writing in the terminology biology expects, setting out chemistry calculations line by line, and stating units in physics every single time.
programmes.countryNote: Tier is usually provisional through Year 10 in Dubai schools and firms up over the year. A diagnostic now is the strongest evidence a parent can bring to a conversation about moving a science from Core to Extended, and it is far easier to have that conversation in Year 10 than in Year 11.

programmes.name: Year 11 and the examination series
programmes.description: The work narrows to the components the mock actually flagged: extended-answer structure, the practical paper, and the three or four topics losing most marks. General revision across three sciences at this stage spreads thin and produces little. One science at a time, diagnosed, is the pattern that works.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge examines IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and Pearson International GCSE in May/June and November. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, so by the spring term the route and the tier are fixed and only technique remains movable.

programmes.name: Into A Level or the IB Diploma
programmes.description: The science grade is read as a prerequisite, and the separate-science route is read as evidence of readiness. A Level chemistry departments look hardest at the quantitative work; IB Diploma coordinators look at whether a student can sustain an extended investigation, which IGCSE barely asks for.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, with enrolment up six per cent during 2025-26. Post-16 science options from The Springs are broader than they were for an older sibling and worth checking rather than assuming.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-springs.subjectsIntro: These are the science subjects and components Emirates Living families most often ask about, with what each one actually assesses. The description is the thing to test a prospective tutor against.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: A terminology subject before it is a science subject. Transport in plants, enzyme graphs, genetic crosses and homeostasis carry most of the lost marks, usually because an answer used an everyday word where the mark scheme wanted a precise one. Highly trainable once a student sees the pattern.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic, balanced and ionic equations with state symbols, and the supplied notes on tests for ions and gases. Students who can recite a reactivity series still lose marks on titration calculations and on writing formulae for compound ions.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Equation selection and rearrangement, unit discipline, and reading gradients rather than points. Electricity, waves and momentum are the recurring Dubai weak spots, and most of the mark loss is procedural rather than conceptual.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: One qualification worth two grades, covering all three disciplines in less depth than the separate route. A student on 0654 does not need three tutors; they need one who knows precisely which parts of each discipline the double award includes and which it leaves out.

subjects.name: Combined Science (Cambridge 0653)
subjects.description: One grade across all three sciences, with the narrowest content of the Cambridge routes. Often the right choice for a student whose strengths lie elsewhere, and a route where tutoring should focus on securing the grade rather than extending the content.

subjects.name: Biology (Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Two written papers with practical skills assessed inside them rather than in a separate component. The extended-answer questions carry more weight than students expect, and the command word in the stem governs what structure the answer needs.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Two written papers, with quantitative chemistry and organic nomenclature the two areas where Dubai cohorts most often lose marks. Practical method questions appear in the written papers, so experimental technique still has to be taught explicitly.

subjects.name: Physics (Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Two written papers. Some equations are provided and others must be recalled, and knowing which is which is itself a revision task. Mark loss concentrates in multi-step calculations where a unit conversion was skipped early.

subjects.name: Double Award Science (Pearson 4SD0)
subjects.description: Two grades from a combined course, with papers in each discipline. Useful for a broad timetable, and worth confirming with the school because its content map differs from Cambridge 0654 in ways that matter to a tutor.

subjects.name: The practical and alternative-to-practical component
subjects.description: Cambridge sets a practical test or a written alternative. Both reward method, variable control, tabulated results and graph discipline rather than manual dexterity, which is why they can be taught on a screen with real apparatus photographs and real data sets.

subjects.name: Extended-answer questions
subjects.description: The four- to six-mark questions where most of the recoverable marks sit. They need a structure keyed to the command word, a stated number of distinct points, and no repetition. Rarely taught explicitly and consistently worth two grade boundaries.

subjects.name: Mathematical skills in science
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, standard form, significant figures, percentage change and gradient calculation. A student weak here loses physics and chemistry marks that look like science errors and are actually arithmetic ones, which is why a maths diagnostic often belongs in a science plan.

sections.heading: Three sciences, three failure modes, three different first lessons
paragraphs: The useful starting point for a Springs parent is not which tutor is nearest but which of the three sciences is actually failing and why. The reason matters: a student losing biology marks and a student losing physics marks have different problems that happen to show up as the same number on a report. Treating them with the same weekly hour of general science help is why so many families report that tutoring did not change anything.

Biology fails on language. The content is largely accessible and the mark schemes are strict about wording, so a student who understands osmosis perfectly can score zero for describing it in everyday terms. The first lesson should involve marking the student's own written answers against real criteria and showing them which words earned marks and which did not. That single exercise changes more biology grades than a term of content revision.

Chemistry fails on arithmetic and symbols. Moles, concentrations, balanced equations, state symbols and formulae for compound ions are where the marks go, and a student can be confident about reactions and still lose a third of a paper. The first lesson should be a set of quantitative questions worked line by line, because setting out is itself where the method marks live.

Physics fails on procedure. Selecting the right equation, rearranging it before substituting, converting units at the start rather than the end, and reading a gradient instead of a single point. Almost none of that is conceptual, which is why physics often responds faster to tutoring than parents expect. The first lesson should be multi-step calculation questions with the working forced into a fixed format.

sections.heading: Biology: the vocabulary problem nobody names as a vocabulary problem
paragraphs: Most biology mark loss in Dubai cohorts is linguistic. A mark scheme asking about water movement wants water potential or concentration gradient, not thicker and thinner. A question on enzymes wants active site and denatured, not broken. The student who writes the everyday version has understood the biology and scored nothing, which is why the report says they are weak at a subject they can explain confidently at the dinner table.

The second pattern is incompleteness. Four-mark questions need four distinct points, and students routinely write the same point three ways because it feels like more writing. Mark schemes do not reward elaboration of one idea; they reward distinct ideas. Learning to count the marks and plan that many separate points is a technique lesson, not a content lesson, and it is cheap to deliver.

The third is the diagram. Biology papers ask for labelled diagrams, annotated graphs and completed tables, and marks are routinely lost to unlabelled axes, missing units on a rate, or a label line that touches the wrong structure. None of this requires a laboratory, which is one reason biology teaches well on a screen: the student writes, the tutor marks it live, and the habit changes within three or four lessons.

Where genuine content gaps exist in this community, they cluster around transport in plants, the specifics of enzyme graphs, genetic crosses with more than one trait, and homeostasis. A tutor who names those without being prompted has taught the syllabus. One who talks about building confidence in biology has not answered the question.

sections.heading: Chemistry: the mole, the equation and the tables supplied with the paper
paragraphs: Chemistry is where a Springs family most often sees a gap between apparent understanding and marks, and the cause is usually arithmetic rather than chemistry. Moles, molar masses, concentrations, reacting masses, percentage yield and titration calculations make up a substantial run of marks in the Extended papers, and they are scored on method as much as on the final answer. A student who writes a single line and a wrong number loses everything; a student who sets out each step loses one mark and keeps the rest.

Symbolic accuracy is the second area. Balanced equations with correct formulae and state symbols, ionic equations with spectator ions removed, and formulae for compound ions such as sulfate, carbonate and nitrate. These are memorisable and routinely not memorised, and a tutor who drills them methodically recovers marks across the whole paper rather than in one topic.

The third is specific to Cambridge: the notes on qualitative analysis supplied with the paper, covering tests for cations, anions and gases. Students who know the notes are provided often fail to practise using them, then meet them cold under time pressure. Practising with the supplied material is a distinct exercise and takes about two lessons.

Organic chemistry at this level is largely nomenclature, homologous series and a small set of reactions, and it is one of the cheapest topics to fix because it is rule-based. Where chemistry is genuinely difficult for a student, it is almost always the quantitative work, and that is where the hours should go.

sections.heading: Physics: units, rearrangement and the gradient
paragraphs: Physics is the science that most often responds quickly to tutoring, because the mark loss is procedural. A multi-step calculation question gives marks for selecting the correct relationship, for substituting correctly, for the arithmetic and for the unit. A student who converts centimetres to metres at the end rather than the start loses the arithmetic mark and sometimes the unit mark too, on a question they fully understood.

Which equations are supplied differs by board, and knowing that is a revision task in itself. Pearson provides some relationships in the paper and expects others from memory; Cambridge expects recall of the relationships listed in its syllabus. A tutor should be able to tell you, for your child's specification, which list applies and which equations therefore have to be learned. Anyone who cannot has not opened the specification recently.

Graph work is the third concentration of marks. Papers ask for a line of best fit, a gradient calculated from two widely separated points on the line rather than from data points, and an interpretation of what the gradient represents physically. Students draw good graphs and then calculate the gradient from the nearest two crosses, which is the single commonest graph error in this market.

Content-wise, electricity, waves and momentum carry most of the lost marks in Dubai cohorts. Electricity in particular is usually a circuit-reading problem rather than a physics problem: a student who can redraw a circuit as a series of simple loops can answer most of what is asked, and that is a teachable habit rather than a talent.
bullets: Convert units at the start of a calculation, not at the end
Know which equations your board supplies and which must be recalled

sections.heading: The command word decides what the answer has to look like
paragraphs: Cambridge publishes a glossary of command words in its syllabuses, and Pearson's mark schemes are written to the same logic. The command word is not decoration. It tells the student how many kinds of thing the answer needs and in what relationship. State wants a bare fact. Describe wants what happens. Explain wants why, with a causal link. Suggest wants a plausible answer applied to an unfamiliar context. Compare wants both sides in the same sentence.

Most lost extended-answer marks in all three sciences come from answering a different command word than the one printed. A student asked to explain who describes instead has written something true that cannot be awarded. A student asked to compare who writes a paragraph about each substance separately loses the comparison marks even though both paragraphs are correct. This is the cheapest mark recovery available in science, and it is barely taught.

The method is mechanical, which is why it works. Read the command word. Count the marks. Plan that many distinct points. Write them without repeating. For explain questions, make sure a because or a therefore appears. For compare questions, make sure every sentence contains both things. Four lessons of marked practice generally embeds it, and the gain shows across all three sciences at once.

The table gives the common command words and the typical way each is mishandled. Check the glossary in your child's own syllabus, because wording and emphasis vary slightly between boards and between series.

sections.heading: One tutor for three sciences, or three specialists, and what each costs
paragraphs: This is the practical decision most Springs households face, and the answer depends on the route rather than the budget. A student on Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 or Pearson Double Award 4SD0 is best served by one tutor who knows exactly which parts of each discipline the double award covers, because the risk with three specialists is that each teaches their full separate-science content and the student revises material the examination will not ask about.

A student on three separate sciences at Extended tier is usually better served by specialists, and rarely needs all three at once. The efficient pattern is sequential: diagnose all three, tutor the weakest for a block, then reassess. Running three weekly slots simultaneously costs three times as much and consumes three evenings, and in most households the second and third sciences improve anyway once the student's answer-writing and calculation habits change.

The cross-cutting block is the exception worth buying for all three at once. Command-word technique, extended-answer structure and the practical component transfer directly between the sciences, so six to eight lessons on those skills with one tutor benefits biology, chemistry and physics together. That is usually the best value purchase in the whole science budget.

Published Dubai rates for reference, read in October 2026: qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150; named specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's table showing 200 to 450 and above; budget online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 with EdFlik and AED 33 to 52 with Tutopiya; in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 including travel, Bestimate showing 180 to 350. Bestimate's monthly figures for one hour a week are AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. These are other providers' published figures, not ours.

sections.heading: How to tell in ten minutes whether somebody knows your child's specification
paragraphs: This is the honest answer to the question in the search. You cannot verify a science tutor by credentials alone, because a biology degree says nothing about whether somebody has read the 0610 syllabus this year. What you can do is ask five questions whose answers are either specific or empty, and listen for which you get. The whole exercise takes ten minutes on a trial call.

Ask which code and tier the student is entered for, and what that changes. A specialist will ask you back rather than guess, and will know that Core and Extended are different papers with different grade ranges. Ask how the practical skills are assessed on that specification: Cambridge sets a separate practical or alternative-to-practical component, Pearson assesses within the written papers, and somebody who does not know which applies has not prepared a student for this examination recently.

Ask what the difference is between a describe and an explain question and how they mark it. Ask, for chemistry, what the supplied qualitative analysis notes contain and how they would teach a student to use them under time pressure. Ask, for physics, which equations that board provides and which must be recalled. Each of those has a concrete answer that takes thirty seconds, and a general reply about building strong foundations is itself the answer to your question.

Finally, ask what they would do in the first four lessons given a specific marked paper. A tutor who has taught the specification will name topics and components. A tutor who has not will describe a process. Neither answer is dishonest; only one tells you they have read the document your child is being examined on.

sections.heading: Practical records, coursework and the line a science tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Science at this level involves written-up practical work, and in some routes that work contributes to an assessment. The boundary is the same across every board and it is worth hearing stated plainly before lessons begin. A tutor may teach experimental method, explain how variables are controlled, show how results should be tabulated, demonstrate graph conventions and give feedback on a write-up the student has produced. A tutor must never write the practical record, supply results for a student to present as their own, or edit a piece to completion.

The same applies to any investigation that a school submits. Providers in this market openly sell completed coursework, including finished Internal Assessments at four-figure prices. Buying that does not purchase a grade; it purchases a malpractice risk that falls on the student, not the seller. Ask any prospective tutor where they draw this line, and treat a vague answer as the answer.

Board materials are the second boundary. Past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents are the boards' copyright. A responsible tutor references them, links to the official source and works through questions in the lesson, rather than distributing a folder of reproduced material. Your child's school has legitimate access through its own board account, which is the proper route to past material.

Both boundaries are differentiators rather than limitations in this particular market, where at least one visible provider sells assessed work outright. A tutor who teaches method and refuses to produce the artefact is doing the job that actually helps, and a parent who asks the question early will hear the difference immediately.
bullets: A tutor teaches method and reviews the student's own write-up
A tutor must never write a practical record or supply results to present
Board papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked, not redistributed
Ask where the line sits before the first lesson, not after a submission

sections.heading: Starting science support from The Springs, and what we will say no to
paragraphs: The sequence is short and the first two steps cost nothing. Email the examinations officer for the board, code and tier of each science, because it is common for one of the three to differ from the others. Find a recent marked paper or the school's question-level analysis of a mock, which tells a tutor more in two minutes than a parents' evening does in twenty. Pick the slot the week can hold: for most of this community that is 17:00 on a weekday or a Saturday morning, since the bus reaches the higher Springs numbers closer to 16:45.

The free trial lesson is sixty minutes of teaching on the student's own paper, not a sales call. It ends with the tutor writing down which of the three sciences is actually weakest, whether the cause is terminology, calculation or procedure, and how many lessons the diagnosis justifies. If the answer is six lessons on command words rather than a year of weekly chemistry, that is what the note will say.

Three things we will say no to. We do not send tutors to homes in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, because home tutoring is an India-only service; every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. We do not claim regulator or examination-board accreditation, because IB Gram holds none, and any provider in this market claiming board approval for its tutors is making a claim worth questioning closely. And no tutor can guarantee a grade in any science.

One more honest limit. A narrow request - a specific board and tier in a single science at a fixed half-hour - cannot always be filled from the UAE-based pool. When it cannot, we say so and offer a specialist elsewhere teaching in your Gulf Standard Time slot at the same rate, or a different hour with the right person. Putting an available but unsuitable tutor into a booked slot is the thing this page exists to argue against.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE science tutor near The Springs who actually knows my child's specification?
faqs.answer: There are science tutors available to this community, and the honest caution is that a science degree does not mean somebody has read the current syllabus. Ten minutes of specific questions will tell you. Ask which code and tier your child is entered for and what the tier changes, how practical skills are assessed on that specification, and what separates a describe answer from an explain answer in the mark scheme. Specific answers come back in seconds. A general reply about building foundations is itself the information you were looking for. Lessons are delivered online one-to-one.

faqs.question: Should we hire one tutor for all three sciences or a specialist for each?
faqs.answer: It depends on the route. A student on Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 or Pearson Double Award 4SD0 is better served by one tutor who knows exactly what the double award covers, because three separate-science specialists will teach content the examination never asks for. A student taking three separate sciences is better served by specialists, but rarely needs all three at once: diagnose all three, tutor the weakest for a block, then reassess. The exception is a cross-cutting block on command words and the practical paper, which benefits all three together.

faqs.question: Why does my child explain biology perfectly at home and score badly in tests?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly terminology. Biology mark schemes accept precise words and reject everyday equivalents, so a student who says the water moves from thick to thin has described osmosis correctly and earned nothing. The second cause is incompleteness: a four-mark question needs four distinct points, and students often write one idea three ways because it feels like more writing. Both are fixed by marking the student's own written answers against real criteria, word by word, which usually changes the habit within three or four lessons.

faqs.question: My child understands chemistry but loses the calculations. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Quantitative chemistry is marked on setting-out as much as on the answer. Moles, molar masses, concentrations, reacting masses, percentage yield and titration questions award method marks line by line, so a student who writes one line and a wrong number loses everything while a student who sets out each step loses one mark. Add the symbolic side - balanced equations with state symbols, ionic equations, formulae for compound ions - and you have most of the gap. It is drilling work rather than conceptual work, which is why it responds quickly.

faqs.question: Is physics the fastest science to improve with tutoring?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, because most physics mark loss is procedural rather than conceptual. Selecting the right relationship, rearranging it before substituting, converting units at the start rather than the end, and calculating a gradient from the line of best fit rather than from two data points. Those are habits, and habits change with marked practice in a fixed working format. Content gaps do exist, usually in electricity, waves and momentum, and electricity in particular is usually a circuit-reading problem that a redrawing technique solves.

faqs.question: How are practical skills assessed if my child never does a practical with the tutor?
faqs.answer: The components reward method, not manual dexterity. Cambridge sets either a practical test or a written alternative to practical; Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers. Both ask about variable control, apparatus choice, tabulating results with units in the headings, plotting and interpreting graphs, and identifying sources of error. All of that is taught better with a real examiner's apparatus photograph on screen and a flawed data set to criticise than with a textbook, and an online lesson keeps every annotated diagram for revision.

faqs.question: What does a command word have to do with my child's science grade?
faqs.answer: A great deal, and it is the cheapest mark recovery available. The command word tells the student what shape the answer needs: state wants a bare fact, describe wants what happens, explain wants a causal link, suggest wants a plausible answer applied to an unfamiliar context, compare wants both sides in the same statement. Most lost extended-answer marks come from answering a different command word than the one printed. The fix is mechanical: read the word, count the marks, plan that many distinct points, include a because where one is needed.

faqs.question: Does Core entry in a Cambridge science limit what we can achieve?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it should be checked for each science separately, because it is common for a student to sit Extended in one and Core in another. Core entry makes a restricted grade range available and nothing above it, whatever the tutoring. If you are paying specialist rates in the hope of a top grade while the entry sits at Core, the entry form has already excluded that outcome. Ask the department which tier each science is entered at, what evidence that rests on, and when the final entry deadline falls.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science do Emirates Living families most often ask for help with?
faqs.answer: Chemistry and physics arrive more often than biology, which reflects what actually goes wrong rather than which subject is hardest. Chemistry requests are usually about quantitative work, and physics requests about multi-step calculations and electricity. Biology requests come later, often after a mock, because the problem there is written expression and it is invisible until somebody marks the student's own answers properly. In many households the right first purchase turns out to be a cross-cutting block on answer-writing rather than a subject-specific one.

faqs.question: What does science tutoring cost for a family in The Springs?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures, read in October 2026: qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150; named specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270; budget online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 with EdFlik and AED 33 to 52 with Tutopiya; in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 including travel. Bestimate's monthly figures for a weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid, AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more in an examination year. Those are other providers' numbers, quoted so you can judge a quote.

faqs.question: Are three weekly science slots ever the right answer?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and it should be a deliberate crisis decision rather than a default. Three simultaneous slots consume three evenings in a household that also has activities and homework, and cost roughly three times a single slot - around AED 1,800 to 3,600 a month at the published mid band. The pattern that works better is sequential: diagnose all three, take the weakest for a block of six to eight lessons, then reassess. The other two frequently improve on their own once answer-writing and calculation habits change.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write up my child's practical investigation?
faqs.answer: No, and that boundary is worth hearing before lessons start. A tutor may teach experimental method, explain variable control, show how results are tabulated, demonstrate graph conventions and give feedback on a write-up the student has produced themselves. A tutor must never write the practical record or supply results for the student to present. One provider in this market sells completed coursework outright; buying that purchases a malpractice risk that falls on your child, not on the seller.

faqs.question: When do we need to decide between separate sciences and a double award?
faqs.answer: At the Year 9 option evening, which in schools serving The Springs sits in the spring term with forms due within about a fortnight. The decision is hard to reverse: a child on double award cannot later present separate physics and chemistry grades to a department that asks for them. Ask the school how many periods a week the separate route takes and what it displaces, because in several Dubai schools it costs the second language or an arts option. Two advisory sessions at this point are better value than six months of lessons afterwards.

faqs.question: Do science lessons run through Ramadan and the summer break?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the timing moved rather than the plan. School days shorten during Ramadan and the useful window shifts later, so a 17:00 slot usually becomes 20:30 or later for the month; arranging that in advance keeps continuity instead of losing four weeks. The long summer, from late June or early July into early September, is the only uninterrupted block in a two-year course and the best time for a practical-skills block, which needs longer sessions than a weekday hour allows. Lessons continue while a family travels.

faqs.question: Is the person teaching my child science legally permitted to tutor in the UAE?
faqs.answer: They should hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time. The u.ae guidance states that tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so nobody should quote you an amount.

faqs.question: What if no specialist is free for our board, tier and science at the hour we need?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than filling the slot. A narrow request - Extended-tier Cambridge physics at a fixed half-hour on a Tuesday, for instance - cannot always be matched from the UAE-based pool. The options are then a specialist elsewhere teaching in your Gulf Standard Time slot at the same rate, a different hour with the right person, or an honest wait with an estimate. Putting an available but unsuitable tutor into a booked slot is exactly the outcome this page argues against, and it is also how families conclude tutoring does not work.
