intro.heading: Three subjects, one calendar, and a workload nobody planned
paragraphs: Science is the part of an IGCSE timetable that goes wrong quietly. A student taking three separate sciences is taking three full subjects with three sets of content, three practical skills components and three sets of papers, and in Dubai schools that is normal rather than exceptional. The trouble is that it is usually treated as one block on a timetable and one line on a report, so a family discovers in the fifth term that one of the three has been drifting since Year 10 while the other two were fine.

That makes the calendar the right organising idea for this page. The question is not whether your child needs science tutoring. It is which of the three subjects needs it, in which term, and what the remaining weeks can realistically deliver in each. A tutor engaged in the first term of Year 10 is building; one engaged in the fifth term is converting knowledge into marks. Both are legitimate purchases and they are not the same purchase.

Before anything else, two facts set the outer edges. Cambridge International examines IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and its February and March series is offered to India only, so it is not a route for a candidate sitting in Dubai. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Entry decisions, including which award route and which tier, close months before the papers, and those are the deadlines that actually constrain what tutoring can change.

The second thing to establish is which route your child is on. Three separate sciences, a coordinated or combined double award, and single-award arrangements are different qualifications with different paper counts and different grade outcomes, and students on a double award are sometimes told they are doing triple. The school's examinations officer can confirm the syllabus codes, and it is worth asking before booking anything, because the revision and the past papers differ, and a term spent on the wrong set is a term nobody gets back.

Delivery is online and said plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in The Sustainable City. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, with diagrams, calculations and graph work on a shared whiteboard and past-paper questions on screen. Home visits exist in our India operation only. For the science practical papers, which are written rather than laboratory-assessed in both boards' international specifications, the online format loses nothing at all. What it gains is the two car journeys a visit would consume, and a tutor chosen for the syllabus code your child sits rather than for the distance between their home and Al Qudra Road at five in the afternoon.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-sustain.subjectsIntro: What follows is the content map across the three sciences and the award routes, with the specific place marks go missing in each. Naming a subject and a topic produces a far better first session than describing science as the problem.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume rather than difficulty is the obstacle, and terminology precision decides the band. Osmosis answers lose marks for omitting concentration gradient; genetics answers lose them for incomplete Punnett square notation; enzyme questions lose them for saying an enzyme is killed rather than denatured.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and reacting-mass calculations are the single largest source of lost marks, followed by qualitative analysis answers written imprecisely. Students who learn the ionic equations as patterns rather than as memorised recipes handle unfamiliar questions considerably better.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Circuits, moments and equilibrium are where Extended and Higher tier candidates reliably drop marks. A large share of physics losses are mathematical rather than scientific: rearranging before substituting, prefixes, and reading a gradient from a graph that is not quite straight.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.description: Covers all three sciences in fewer papers, with reduced content depth per subject. Students on these routes often believe they are taking triple science, and revise from the wrong past papers as a result. Confirm the syllabus code before a single revision session happens.

subjects.name: Pearson Science Double Award
subjects.description: The Edexcel double-award route, examined across papers covering all three sciences. Content is narrower than the separate subjects but the question style still rewards precise explanation, and the practical skills content is examined on paper in the same way.

subjects.name: Practical skills assessment
subjects.description: In both boards' international specifications, practical skills are assessed on a written paper rather than in a laboratory. What is tested is reading apparatus diagrams, identifying independent and controlled variables, criticising a method, completing results tables and plotting graphs — and almost nobody practises it deliberately.

subjects.name: Graph and data work
subjects.description: Plotting, line of best fit, gradient and interpolation, plus judging whether a relationship is supported. It appears in all three subjects and in the practical paper, which makes it the highest-leverage single skill in the whole science timetable. It cannot be revised by rereading notes.

subjects.name: Explanation technique
subjects.description: Science mark schemes award a chain of reasoning. A student who describes what happens earns the description marks and loses the explanation ones, which over three subjects is a substantial loss. The fix is mechanical: underline the command word and name the mechanism before writing anything else.

subjects.name: The mathematics inside science
subjects.description: Rearranging, ratio, percentage, standard form, prefixes and significant figures. A student losing marks here will look weak in two sciences at once, which is a useful diagnostic signal: if chemistry and physics are both drifting while biology is fine, the cause is usually arithmetic.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. These grades sit on the report beside the sciences and add to the week a Year 11 student already has.

sections.heading: Which science route is your child actually on
paragraphs: This sounds like a trivial question and it is the most common source of wasted revision in science. Three separate sciences, a coordinated or combined double award, and single-subject arrangements are different qualifications with different paper counts, different content depth and different past papers. Students frequently describe themselves as doing triple science when the school has entered them for a double award, and then revise from separate-science past papers that cover material they were never taught.

The codes settle it. Cambridge separate sciences are 0610 biology, 0620 chemistry and 0625 physics; Coordinated Sciences double award is 0654 and Combined Science is 0653. The Pearson separate sciences are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, with Science Double Award at 4SD0. Ask the examinations officer for the codes rather than the subject names, because the difference between 0654 and the three separate codes is a materially different revision programme with a different paper count behind it.

The route also has consequences after Year 11. Some post-16 science courses, in Dubai and abroad, prefer or require the separate sciences for progression to A Level or Higher Level study in that subject. A student on a double award aiming at Higher Level chemistry should check their own school's entry requirement early rather than discovering a constraint at the point of selection. The table below sets out what each route commits a student to, and it is worth reading with the school's confirmation of the codes in hand rather than from memory.

sections.heading: The science year counted backwards from the June series
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a science calendar, which is a gap worth filling because science has milestones the other subjects do not. Work the list below upwards and the logic is clear: the series is fixed by the board, study leave by the school, the mock block sits a term earlier because predicted grades depend on it, and entry decisions — award route and tier — close before any of that. Those entry deadlines are the ones families most often meet by accident.

What makes science distinctive is the practical component and the sheer volume of content across three subjects. There is no coursework deadline in the international specifications to force early work, which sounds like a relief and is actually the problem: nothing in the first three terms creates urgency, so drift in one subject goes unnoticed. The internal Year 10 examinations are the only real checkpoint, which is why they deserve more attention than schools' reporting cycles usually give them.

The practical consequence for a family here is a simple rule. Use the Year 10 internal results to decide which of the three sciences needs a weekly slot, then protect that slot through Year 11 rather than spreading hours across all three in the final terms. Families who do the reverse end up with three partially supported subjects and no completed between-session work in any of them, at three times the monthly cost. sections.heading: The practical paper almost nobody prepares for
paragraphs: In both boards' international science specifications, practical skills are assessed on a written paper rather than through laboratory assessment. That is good news for an online tutor and, more importantly, it means a component worth a meaningful share of each science grade can be prepared from past questions. It is also the component students practise least, because it does not look like revision: there is nothing to re-read and no notes to highlight.

What the paper actually tests is narrow and repetitive, which is exactly why it rewards practice. Students are asked to identify independent, dependent and controlled variables; read and interpret apparatus diagrams; criticise a given method and suggest improvements; complete and read results tables; plot graphs and draw lines of best fit; and comment on reliability and anomalies. The same question shapes recur across series, and a student who has worked twenty of them recognises every one.

The leverage here is that the skills transfer across all three sciences at once. A student who learns to spot the controlled variable in a biology method does the same job in chemistry and physics. That makes a four to six session practical block the best value available in a triple-science timetable, because one short engagement raises marks in three subjects. It is also the clearest example of a component where online delivery costs nothing whatsoever, because every one of these skills is exercised on a page rather than at a bench.

sections.heading: Three sciences, and which one to tutor
paragraphs: The instinct when science marks fall is to tutor science, and in a triple timetable that means three subjects and three hours a week. For a Year 11 student carrying nine or ten subjects plus the mandatory UAE subjects, that is more than the between-session work can absorb, so all three engagements become half-used. The better approach is diagnostic: find out which of the three is actually the problem and whether the cause is shared.

There is a useful pattern that families can read themselves. If chemistry and physics are both drifting while biology holds, the cause is almost always arithmetic — rearranging, ratio, prefixes, significant figures — rather than three separate content problems. One engagement on the mathematics inside science fixes two subjects at once. If biology alone is weak, the cause is usually terminology precision and volume management, which is a different kind of work entirely.

If all three are weak, the cause is usually explanation technique or data handling, both of which are shared across the subjects, and both of which respond to a single engagement. That is why we ask for marked papers in all three before recommending anything: the pattern across them tells us whether this is one problem wearing three subject labels or three genuinely separate problems, and that determines whether a family needs one tutored hour a week or two. It is also free information: three photographs of marked papers, read side by side, settle the question before anybody is booked.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can do in the sciences
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the usual commitment and in science it buys more than families expect, because the question types are strongly patterned. A student who understands the biology but writes imprecise explanations can move a grade in that time. A student who has not met a third of the chemistry specification cannot, and a tutor who implies otherwise is selling hope by the hour. The target has to be set honestly at the start.

The highest-yield eight-week plan in science is usually not content at all. It is the practical paper, explanation technique and data handling, in that order, because all three transfer across subjects and all three are under-practised. A student who adds those to existing content knowledge picks up marks in every paper they sit rather than in one topic. Content repair comes after, and only on the two or three topics that recur most heavily in past papers.

The first two weeks are diagnostic and look slower than parents expect: timed questions rather than teaching, with lost marks classified by reason rather than counted. The classification is the useful output. A student who learns that four of eight lost marks were explanation marks and two were units has a plan; a student who learns they scored sixty-one per cent has a feeling. That distinction is most of what separates a useful block from eight weeks of general revision, and it costs nothing except the discomfort of two weeks that look unproductive.

sections.heading: What science tutoring costs when there are three subjects
paragraphs: The arithmetic of three subjects is what makes science different from other tutoring decisions. Published Dubai rates put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors advertising IGCSE from AED 150. At the mid-point of that band, three weekly hours is a monthly figure most households did not intend, and the between-session work for three subjects will not get done anyway, so the money buys less than one hour used properly.

The rest of the market, for context: budget online tutoring at AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65; specialists in IGCSE and A Level at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270; in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to AED 350; and one premium provider advertising AED 650 an hour. Monthly packages include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour home visits.

For IGCSE science the qualified online tier is usually the right purchase, and the right quantity is usually one hour rather than three. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour are AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market. Every figure here belongs to the company or rate guide that published it and was read in October 2026. IB Gram publishes no hourly list on these pages and quotes after a free trial, for the specific subject and code.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and what equivalency needs
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. The market context: 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the following academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package.

Two regulator facts touch a science timetable directly. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and combined classes prohibited; instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a Year 11 student taking three sciences, those lessons are part of why there is less room in the week than a tutoring plan assumes. The second is that the emirate determines the regulator, with ADEK in Abu Dhabi, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

On equivalency, the sourced rule is specific: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the count, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong. Equivalency is a process your family manages with the Ministry rather than something a tutoring company performs, and nobody should suggest tutoring is required for it. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, Ministry, Cambridge or Pearson approval and no UAE office.

sections.heading: Fitting three sciences into a Dubai week
paragraphs: A Year 11 student taking three sciences has a timetable that is already full before any tutoring is added, and the UAE week does not help. Monday to Friday with a half-day Friday leaves Saturday and Sunday as the only full days, and those are also when families travel and host. Add the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons, plus sport, and the number of genuinely free evenings is usually one or two rather than four.

Where a family lives decides which of those evenings is usable. A student at school inside The Sustainable City is home by mid-afternoon and can take a short weekday session with time left for the work it sets. A student commuting to Motor City, Dubai Sports City or Al Barsha is not realistically free until 5.30pm, and in a sports-heavy household that evening is contested. For those families a weekend block carrying the practical and data work is usually the better structure.

On our side, slots are held in Gulf Standard Time, move after Iftar through Ramadan with the same tutor retained, and can pause during a school's own examination fortnight when adding sessions produces fatigue rather than marks. We do not rotate students between tutors to fill a diary. With three sciences in play, a tutor who already knows which of the three is the real problem is carrying information that takes several weeks to rebuild with somebody new, and that is worth more than a perfectly filled calendar.

faqs.question: How do we find out whether our child is taking triple or double award science?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer for the syllabus codes rather than the subject names. Cambridge separate sciences are 0610 biology, 0620 chemistry and 0625 physics; Coordinated Sciences double award is 0654 and Combined Science is 0653. Pearson separate sciences are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, with Science Double Award at 4SD0. This matters because students regularly believe they are taking triple science when the school has entered a double award, and then revise from separate-science past papers covering content they were never taught.

faqs.question: Which of the three sciences should we tutor if money is limited?
faqs.answer: Whichever the pattern points to, and the pattern is readable from marked papers in all three. If chemistry and physics are both drifting while biology holds, the cause is almost always arithmetic — rearranging, ratio, prefixes, significant figures — and one engagement fixes two subjects. If biology alone is weak, it is usually terminology precision. If all three are weak on long questions, it is explanation technique, which is also one engagement. Tutoring three subjects separately is usually paying three times for one underlying problem.

faqs.question: How is the practical component assessed for IGCSE science in Dubai?
faqs.answer: In both boards' international specifications it is assessed on a written paper rather than through laboratory assessment. The paper asks students to identify independent and controlled variables, read apparatus diagrams, criticise a given method and suggest improvements with their effects, complete results tables with correct units, plot graphs and draw lines of best fit, and comment on anomalies and reliability. Those question shapes repeat heavily across series, so it is the component that responds fastest to deliberate practice — and the one almost nobody practises.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor prepare a student for the science practical paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, completely, because the paper is written rather than laboratory-assessed in both international specifications. Everything it tests can be practised over a screen using the boards' own past questions: variables, apparatus diagrams, method criticism, tables, graphs and anomaly comments. Laboratory handling remains the school's responsibility and no online tutor should claim otherwise. The useful point is that the component the grade depends on is the written paper, and a four to six session block on it raises marks in all three sciences at once.

faqs.question: Does my child sit the February or March series for science?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International's February and March series is offered to India only, so it is not a route available to a candidate sitting in Dubai. UAE candidates sit the June series, with November as the resit and alternative route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. If a revision plan, website or tutor refers your Dubai child to a March examination window, that plan was written for a different country and the dates in it should not be relied on.

faqs.question: Why does science drift without anyone noticing until Year 11?
faqs.answer: Because nothing creates urgency in the first three terms. The international specifications have no coursework deadline to force early work, science often appears as one block on a timetable and one line on a report, and three subjects are reported together often enough that a single weak subject hides behind two strong ones. The only genuine checkpoint is the internal Year 10 examinations, which is why they deserve more attention than schools' reporting cycles tend to give them, and why award route and tier decisions should be taken from them.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting science tutoring eight weeks before the series?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the right target. In eight weeks the achievable gains are the practical paper, explanation technique and data handling, all of which transfer across the three sciences and all of which are usually under-practised. Narrow content repair on heavily recurring topics is also possible. What is not achievable is covering a third of a specification that has never been met. We set that target in the first conversation rather than discovering it with you in the sixth week.

faqs.question: Do you cover both boards for all three sciences?
faqs.answer: Yes, matched to the code rather than the subject, because the specifications differ in paper structure and question style and their past papers are not interchangeable. Cambridge biology, chemistry and physics are 0610, 0620 and 0625; the Pearson equivalents are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. We also cover the double award routes. Coverage is strongest in chemistry and physics, where demand in this belt concentrates, and good in biology. If we cannot match a specific code and tier quickly, we will say so.

faqs.question: My son does triple science and says he has no time. Is that true?
faqs.answer: Probably. A Year 11 student with three sciences, the KHDA-mandated Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons, and a sport usually has one or two genuinely free evenings a week, not four. That is the constraint a tutoring plan has to respect: a session whose between-session work never gets done produces almost nothing. The honest answer is one tutored hour chosen by diagnosis, with the work it sets actually completed, rather than three hours that displace the work entirely.

faqs.question: How much should we expect to pay for IGCSE science tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates put qualified subject tutors working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors advertising IGCSE from AED 150, and Bestimate's monthly estimate for one weekly hour at AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market. Budget online tutoring runs AED 33 to AED 65. In-home visits are AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included. The important figure for a science family is the quantity rather than the rate: one hour used properly beats three hours half-used, at a third of the monthly cost.

faqs.question: Will a science tutor come to our villa if we pay extra?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE at any price, and nobody will arrive at an address in The Sustainable City or a neighbouring community. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with diagrams, calculations and graph work on a shared whiteboard. Home tutoring is a service we operate in India only. For the science practical papers, which are written rather than laboratory-based in both international specifications, the online format loses nothing at all.

faqs.question: Does a double award limit what my daughter can study after Year 11?
faqs.answer: It can, and it is worth checking early rather than at the point of selection. Some post-16 science courses, in Dubai and abroad, prefer or require the separate sciences for progression to A Level or Higher Level study in that subject, and schools set their own entry requirements. If your daughter has a particular science in view for post-16 study, ask her school for its stated requirement in writing while there is still time to adjust the entry route rather than after the entry deadline has passed.

faqs.question: What is the fastest improvement available in a science grade?
faqs.answer: Explanation technique, in most cases. Science mark schemes award a chain of reasoning, and a student who writes an accurate description of what happens earns the description marks and loses the explanation ones. Across three subjects that is a large, repeated loss. The fix is mechanical — underline the command word, name the mechanism before anything else — and it shows up in the next marked paper. The practical paper runs it close, because its question types repeat so heavily.

faqs.question: Do you provide past papers and mark schemes for the sciences?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the boards' copyright. We reference them, cite the official sources, and work from material your child's school legitimately holds, with questions shown on screen during sessions. Any service advertising an unlimited paper bank invites a fair question about provenance. The school's own holdings are also the papers your child will be marked against, which makes them the better source in practice as well.

faqs.question: How soon will we see whether it is working?
faqs.answer: For explanation technique and data handling, about three to four weeks, because the change appears directly in the next marked paper. For arithmetic causes, four to eight weeks, since fluency improves through repetition. Genuine content gaps take one to three weeks per topic. Each session note records which error classes appeared rather than which topics were covered, so the trend is visible in the record. We publish no improvement statistics, because figures without a sample size, a date and a method are not evidence.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-valley.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IGCSE biology, chemistry and physics to students living in The Valley and along the Al Ain road, on both the Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel specifications. Each is matched to a syllabus code and tier rather than to science in general, because the three subjects lose marks in three different places.

intro.heading: Three sciences, three completely different failure modes
paragraphs: The least useful thing a family can conclude is that a child needs help with science. Biology, chemistry and physics are three separate subjects with three separate mark schemes, and they fail in ways that have almost nothing in common. Biology marks are lost on the exact wording of an explanation. Chemistry marks are lost on calculation discipline, most often moles. Physics marks are lost on the mathematics wrapped around the physics. Treating those as one problem is how a term of tutoring passes without a grade moving.

So this page is written subject by subject. It sets out the specific wording biology mark schemes reward and what students write instead, the moles and formula discipline chemistry assumes without teaching, the mathematical operations that quietly cost physics marks, and what the practical skills paper actually asks for in both boards' international specifications. The aim is that a parent can read a marked paper afterwards and name the cause themselves.

Start with the codes, because the boards differ. Cambridge biology, chemistry and physics are 0610, 0620 and 0625, with Coordinated Sciences double award at 0654 and Combined Science at 0653. The Pearson Edexcel separate sciences are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, with Science Double Award at 4SD0. These are separate qualifications whose past papers are not interchangeable, and students on a double award frequently believe they are taking triple science.

The Valley makes that confirmation more necessary than elsewhere. This is a newer community on the road to Al Ain with no school inside its own boundary at the time of writing, so students travel outward in two directions and attend several different schools entering different specifications. The child next door may be sitting a different qualification in the same subject, which means a board cannot be inferred from a neighbour and the examinations officer is the only reliable source.

Delivery is stated plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in The Valley. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with questions shared on screen, a whiteboard for working and diagrams, and an optional recording. Home visits exist in our India operation only. For the science practical papers, which are written rather than laboratory-assessed in both international specifications, the online format loses nothing at all. What it does remove is the two car journeys either side of a visit, which in a household where the school run has already taken an hour from the day is the difference between a session a student can use and one they merely sit through. The rest of this page is the subject detail that should decide where an hour a week goes.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-valley.subjectsIntro: What follows is the content map, organised by where each subject actually loses marks rather than by syllabus order. Naming a subject and a topic produces a far better first session than describing science as the problem.

subjects.name: Biology: transport and exchange
subjects.description: Osmosis, diffusion and active transport answers lose marks for omitting the phrase concentration gradient, and for describing movement without stating it is passive or requires energy. The mark scheme wants specific words, and a paraphrase that means the same thing often earns nothing.

subjects.name: Biology: enzymes and metabolism
subjects.description: Students write that an enzyme is killed rather than denatured, or that the active site changes shape without saying the substrate no longer fits. Both lose marks. Rate graphs require the limiting factor to be named rather than implied, which is the second recurring loss here.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Punnett square answers lose marks for incomplete notation, missing gamete rows or ratios given without the phenotypes they belong to. Terminology must be exact: allele against gene, genotype against phenotype, and the difference matters to the mark scheme in every question.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and reacting masses
subjects.description: The single largest source of lost marks across the subject. Approximate moles work contaminates every later step, and students who round early produce answers outside the acceptable range even with a correct method. The fix is procedural rather than conceptual.

subjects.name: Chemistry: qualitative analysis and tests
subjects.description: Test answers need the reagent, the observation and the conclusion, and students routinely give two of the three. Precipitate colours and gas tests must be stated exactly as the specification expects rather than approximately described.

subjects.name: Chemistry: electrolysis and redox
subjects.description: Half-equation answers lose marks for unbalanced charges and for electrons on the wrong side. Students who learn the pattern of oxidation at the anode and reduction at the cathode as a rule without the reasoning fail the unfamiliar electrolyte questions.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Where higher-tier candidates drop the most marks, usually by treating a potential divider as independent components or by rearranging a formula after substituting rather than before. The physics is often sound and the arithmetic is not.

subjects.name: Physics: forces, moments and equilibrium
subjects.description: Moment calculations lose marks on distances measured from the wrong point and on units left in centimetres. Equilibrium questions require both conditions to be stated, and students frequently satisfy one and assume the other.

subjects.name: Practical skills, all three sciences
subjects.description: Assessed on a written paper rather than in a laboratory. It asks for variable identification, apparatus reading, method criticism with the effect stated, results tables with correct units, graph plotting and comment on anomalies. The question shapes repeat heavily across series.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. These lessons are part of why a Year 11 science week has less room than a tutoring plan assumes.

sections.heading: Biology: the subject where the exact words are the marks
paragraphs: Biology is the science families most often misread, because a student can write an answer that is entirely true and score nothing. Mark schemes in this subject reward named terms rather than correct meaning. An answer explaining that water moves from where there is more of it to where there is less is accurate and will not earn the mark reserved for concentration gradient. Students conclude the marking is unfair; in fact the specification is explicit about the vocabulary it expects.

The recurring examples are consistent enough to be worth publishing. Enzymes are denatured, not killed. The active site changes shape so the substrate no longer fits, and both halves of that sentence carry marks. Transport is passive or requires energy, and saying neither loses the distinction. In genetics, allele and gene are different words, as are genotype and phenotype, and ratios must be attached to the phenotypes they describe. None of this is conceptually hard; all of it is specific.

The fix is mechanical and fast, which is why it represents good value. Four to six sessions working the student's own marked answers against the published wording usually eliminates the pattern, and the gain shows up in chemistry and physics explanation questions too, because the underlying habit — name the mechanism in the terms the scheme expects — transfers. It is also something a parent can reinforce at home without any subject knowledge, simply by asking which word was missing.

sections.heading: Chemistry: the subject where the arithmetic is the subject
paragraphs: Chemistry at this level is less about understanding than about discipline, and the discipline is almost entirely moles. Reacting mass, concentration, gas volume and titration questions all route through the same arithmetic, and a student who is approximate there will lose marks across the entire paper regardless of how well they understand bonding or the periodic table. The marks are not lost where the difficulty feels greatest; they are lost in the routine step everyone assumes is safe.

Three habits account for most of it. Rounding early, which produces a final answer outside the acceptable range even with a correct method. Omitting units or using inconsistent ones, particularly between grams and kilograms or between cubic centimetres and litres. And failing to write the balanced equation first, which makes the ratio step guesswork. Each is procedural, each takes two to four weeks of enforcement rather than explanation, and together they are usually worth more marks than any topic.

The second cluster is qualitative analysis, where answers need the reagent, the observation and the conclusion, and students give two of the three. Precipitate colours and gas tests have to be stated as the specification expects rather than approximately described. This is memorisation rather than reasoning, and it responds to short, frequent testing instead of long sessions, which suits the weekday slot in a commuting household well. A student who can produce reagent, observation and conclusion automatically has removed a predictable set of losses from every paper they sit.

sections.heading: Physics: how much of it is actually mathematics
paragraphs: A substantial share of lost physics marks at IGCSE are not physics losses at all. The commonest profile is a student who identifies the right relationship, selects the right formula, and then loses the mark by rearranging after substituting, mishandling a prefix, or reading a gradient from a curve as though it were straight. Under timed conditions those slips multiply, and the student concludes they are bad at physics when they are in fact slow at algebra.

This matters for how a family spends. A student in that position does not need more physics teaching; they need three or four weeks of dense manipulation and unit practice in physics contexts, which is cheaper and faster than a term of content review. It is also why we ask for a marked paper before the first session: the distinction between a physics gap and an arithmetic one is visible in the working and invisible in a conversation.

There is a useful diagnostic signal families can read themselves. If chemistry and physics are both drifting while biology holds up, the cause is almost certainly arithmetic rather than two separate content problems, because biology carries terminology and volume while the other two carry calculation. One engagement on the mathematics inside science then lifts two subjects at once, which is the cheapest outcome available in a triple-science timetable and the one most often missed. It is also readable by a parent without any subject knowledge, simply by comparing three marked papers side by side.

sections.heading: The practical skills paper, and what a mark scheme accepts
paragraphs: In both boards' international specifications practical skills are assessed on a written paper rather than through laboratory assessment, which means a meaningful share of each science grade can be prepared from past questions. It is also the component students practise least, because it does not look like revision: there is nothing to re-read and no notes to highlight, so it quietly gets skipped by otherwise diligent candidates.

What the paper asks is narrow and repetitive. Identify the independent, dependent and controlled variables in a given method. Read an apparatus diagram or a scale. Criticise the procedure and suggest improvements, with the effect of each improvement stated rather than implied. Complete a results table with consistent units and decimal places. Plot data and draw a line of best fit rather than joining points. Comment on an anomaly, saying what it does to the result.

That last distinction is where most marks are lost. Identifying an anomaly earns little; explaining its effect earns the mark. The same applies to improvements: suggesting more repeats is worth nothing unless the student says what repeating improves. Because the question shapes recur across series, twenty worked past questions covers nearly everything the paper can ask, and the skills transfer across all three sciences, which makes a short block on it the best return in a triple timetable. sections.heading: Core, Extended and the award routes compared
paragraphs: Confirming the route matters as much in science as the board does, and students are frequently wrong about it. Cambridge separate sciences at 0610, 0620 and 0625 split into Core and Extended, with Core capping the achievable grade and Extended reaching the top bands while carrying harder content. Coordinated Sciences double award at 0654 and Combined Science at 0653 cover all three sciences across fewer papers with reduced depth per subject. Pearson offers separate sciences and Science Double Award at 4SD0.

A student on a double award who revises from separate-science past papers will spend weeks on content they were never taught, which is a waste that no amount of tutoring recovers. Equally, a student entered for Core who revises Extended material is working beyond their paper. Both situations are common and both are solved by one email to the examinations officer asking for the syllabus codes rather than the subject names.

The route also has consequences beyond Year 11. Some post-16 science courses prefer or require the separate sciences for progression to A Level or Higher Level study in that subject, and schools set their own entry requirements. A student on a double award with a particular science in view should ask their school for its stated requirement while there is still time to adjust the entry route, rather than discovering a constraint at the point of selection. In this community that question is worth asking directly, because children attend several different schools and the thresholds are not the same at each.

sections.heading: Which subject to tutor, and why not all three
paragraphs: A student taking three separate sciences has three full subjects, and the instinct when marks fall is to tutor all of them. In a household with an outbound school run that is three hours a week plus the between-session work, which is more than a Year 11 student carrying nine or ten subjects and the mandatory UAE lessons can absorb. The result is three half-used engagements and a family concluding that tutoring does not work.

The better approach is to read the pattern across marked papers in all three subjects, because the cause is frequently shared. If chemistry and physics are drifting while biology holds, the cause is arithmetic and one engagement fixes two subjects. If all three are weak on long-answer questions, the cause is explanation wording and one engagement fixes three. If biology alone is weak, it is terminology precision, which is specific to that subject but still a short block rather than a term.

Only when the papers genuinely show three separate content problems is three-subject tutoring the right answer, and in that case the honest advice is usually to sequence rather than parallelise: one subject at a time, rotated, with the between-session work actually completed. That costs a third as much in any given month and produces more, which is why we ask for all three sets of marked work before recommending anything at all. That reading costs nothing and it is the single most useful thing a family can do before spending a dirham.

sections.heading: What science tutoring costs, and the quantity question
paragraphs: Read the published Dubai bands the way a three-science family has to read them, which is per subject and then multiplied. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors advertising IGCSE from AED 150, so one weekly hour in each of biology, chemistry and physics starts near AED 450 a week before anyone has asked whether all three need it. Budget online tutoring runs AED 33 to AED 65, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65, and that is the only band where buying three subjects at once is casually affordable, which is part of why the paragraph below argues against buying three. Above the qualified tier, specialists in IGCSE and A Level are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, while in-home visits sit at AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included, a figure that quietly assumes a tutor can reach The Valley and get home inside the same evening.

For IGCSE science the qualified online tier is usually the right purchase, because the work is diagnosis and enforcement rather than rare expertise. The more consequential decision is quantity. One hour a week chosen by diagnosis, with the between-session work completed, produces more than three hours chosen by subject with the work left undone, and costs a third as much. In a commuting household that is not a preference; it is arithmetic about available evenings.

Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour home visits, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market. Every figure here belongs to the company or rate guide that published it and was read in October 2026. IB Gram publishes no hourly list on these pages and quotes after a free trial, for the specific subject, code and tier your child is entered for.

sections.heading: Materials, honesty and the regulator position
paragraphs: The most common request we get in science is a shared drive full of past papers, and it is the request we decline. Cambridge and Pearson hold the copyright in their syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables. What we do instead is cite the official source and work from the material your child's school legitimately holds, with questions put on screen during the session, which for the practical paper is the better arrangement anyway: a question worked through live is where the mark-scheme wording set out in section three actually gets enforced, and a downloaded PDF enforces nothing. A service advertising an unlimited paper bank invites a fair question about provenance, and the school's own holdings are in any case the papers your child will be marked against.

Where a science subject carries assessed work completed outside the examination hall, the boundary is explicit: submitted work must be the student's own and is authenticated by the school. A tutor may teach the content, explain the criteria, question whether a method is reproducible and comment on the student's own writing. A tutor may not write any part of a submission, redraft to completion, or supply a model to be edited. One operation in this market sells completed internal assessments for another qualification at AED 3,750, which shows what the trade costs and why it should be refused.

On regulators: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from any of them or from Cambridge or Pearson, and no UAE office. An individual tutoring privately in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years.

sections.heading: Fitting three sciences into a Valley week
paragraphs: A Year 11 student taking three sciences has a full timetable before any tutoring is added, and in this community an outbound school run in one of two directions takes more of the day than families expect. Add the KHDA-mandated Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons and a sport, and the number of genuinely free evenings is usually one, not four. Any plan that assumes otherwise will be abandoned by the third week.

The structure that works splits by the type of work. Terminology testing and arithmetic drills are short and benefit from frequency, so they fit a weekday evening slot and daily between-session sets. The practical skills paper, whole papers and graph work need uninterrupted attention, which in a community with a long commute genuinely exists only at the weekend. One weekday slot and one weekend block is the pattern that survives all three terms.

The UAE calendar shapes the rest. The working week runs Monday to Friday with a half-day Friday, leaving Saturday and Sunday as the only full days. During Ramadan school hours shorten and the useful window moves after Iftar, where a science session is frequently better than any afternoon slot in that month. We hold slots in Gulf Standard Time, move them after Iftar with the same tutor retained, and pause blocks during a school's own examination fortnight rather than adding sessions that produce fatigue. We also keep the same tutor across a term rather than rotating students to fill a diary, because knowing which of the three sciences is the real problem is information that takes weeks to rebuild with somebody new.

process.description: Whether your child sits three separate sciences, a coordinated or combined double award, or a mix, and the codes rather than the subject names. In this community children attend several different schools entering different specifications, so a neighbour's answer is not evidence about your own child.

process.description: Not only the weakest. The pattern across the three is what shows whether the cause is shared — arithmetic, explanation wording — or genuinely three separate content problems, and that determines whether you need one tutored hour a week or two.

process.description: Run by the tutor who would continue, using an unfamiliar question rather than a revision topic. It ends with the tutor stating which subject they would address and whether the cause is shared across the three. If the match is wrong, we propose someone else.

process.description: You receive a plan naming the subject, the specific topics or skills, and whether a terminology or practical block is part of it, plus the date it counts back from and the weekday and weekend split. Named causes mean the plan can be checked.

process.description: Each note records which error classes appeared: wording, arithmetic, command word, data handling or content. Over a month those classes either thin out or they do not, and if they do not we change the method or the tutor rather than adding a second subject.

whyPoints.description: Biology fails on wording, chemistry on calculation discipline, physics on the mathematics inside it. A tutor who treats science as one subject will spend the term on whichever part they prefer, which is how a family pays for work the student did not need.

whyPoints.title: Shared causes found before money is spent

whyPoints.title: The practical paper taken seriously

faqs.question: Why does our daughter lose biology marks when her answers are correct?
faqs.answer: Because biology mark schemes reward named terms rather than correct meaning. Writing that water moves from where there is more of it to where there is less is accurate and will not earn the mark reserved for concentration gradient. Enzymes are denatured, not killed. Transport is passive or requires energy. Allele and gene are different words. None of this is conceptually hard, but all of it is specific, and four to six sessions working her own marked answers against the published wording usually eliminates the whole pattern.

faqs.question: What single habit costs the most chemistry marks?
faqs.answer: Approximate moles work, by a wide margin. Reacting mass, concentration, gas volume and titration questions all route through the same arithmetic, so a student who rounds early or uses inconsistent units produces answers outside the acceptable range even with a perfect method, across the whole paper. Writing the balanced equation before anything else is the second habit, because without it the ratio step becomes guesswork. Both are procedural, both take two to four weeks of enforcement, and together they are usually worth more marks than any single topic.

faqs.question: Chemistry and physics are both slipping but biology is fine. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: Almost always that the cause is arithmetic rather than two separate content problems. Chemistry and physics both carry calculation, rearranging, prefixes and significant figures, while biology carries terminology and volume. A student holding up in biology and drifting in the other two is usually losing marks to the mathematics inside science, and one engagement of three or four weeks on that lifts two subjects at once. It is the cheapest outcome available in a triple-science timetable and the one families most often miss.

faqs.question: How do we confirm whether our son is on triple or double award science?
faqs.answer: Email the examinations officer and ask for the syllabus codes rather than the subject names. Cambridge separate sciences are 0610, 0620 and 0625; Coordinated Sciences double award is 0654 and Combined Science is 0653. The Pearson separate sciences are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, with Science Double Award at 4SD0. This matters because a student on a double award who revises from separate-science past papers spends weeks on content never taught, and in The Valley a neighbour's answer carries no information about a different school.

faqs.question: Is the practical paper really worth separate preparation?
faqs.answer: It is the best return available in a science timetable. In both boards' international specifications practical skills are examined on a written paper, the question shapes repeat heavily across series, and almost nobody practises it because there is nothing to re-read. Twenty worked past questions covers nearly everything it can ask, and the skills transfer across all three sciences at once. Most of the marks hinge on one distinction: stating the effect of an improvement or anomaly rather than merely identifying it.

faqs.question: What does the mark scheme accept for method improvements?
faqs.answer: The improvement plus what it improves. Suggesting more repeats earns nothing on its own; saying that repeats allow an anomalous result to be identified and a mean calculated earns the mark. The same applies to anomalies: identifying one is worth little, while explaining what it does to the conclusion is worth the mark. That single distinction accounts for a large share of practical paper losses, and it is correctable within two or three sessions because the phrasing is formulaic.

faqs.question: Should we tutor all three sciences in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Almost never. Three tutored hours a week plus the between-session work for each is more than a Year 11 student carrying nine or ten subjects, the KHDA-mandated Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons, a sport and an outbound school run can absorb. The result is three half-used engagements. Read the marked papers from all three subjects first: a shared cause such as explanation wording or arithmetic is fixable in one engagement that lifts all three, and sequencing beats parallelising.

faqs.question: Does a double award limit what my child can study post-16?
faqs.answer: It can, and it is worth checking early rather than at the point of selection. Some post-16 science courses prefer or require the separate sciences for progression to A Level or Higher Level study in that subject, and schools set their own entry requirements. If your child has a particular science in view, ask their school for its stated requirement in writing while there is still time to adjust the entry route. After the entry deadline the route is fixed regardless of how the year goes.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor cover practical science properly?
faqs.answer: For everything the paper assesses, yes, because in both international specifications practical skills are examined in writing rather than through laboratory assessment. Variable identification, apparatus reading, method criticism, results tables, graph plotting and anomaly comments all work over a screen using the boards' own past questions. Laboratory handling remains the school's responsibility and no online tutor should claim to replace it. The useful point is that the written paper is what the grade actually depends on.

faqs.question: Our son changed school mid-year and some science topics are missing. How much work is that?
faqs.answer: Usually a half-term of targeted work rather than a programme. Schools teach the same specification in different orders, so a mid-year arrival typically has two or three genuinely unmet topics and two or three covered twice, which is a jagged profile rather than a deficit. The diagnosis is to work through mixed past questions and record which ones he cannot start at all. In The Valley this is common, because families move in from across Dubai and often change board as well as school.

faqs.question: How much should we budget for IGCSE science tutoring?
faqs.answer: Published rates put qualified subject tutors working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors advertising IGCSE from AED 150, and Bestimate's monthly estimate for one weekly hour at AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market. Budget online tutoring runs AED 33 to AED 65 and in-home visits AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included. The more important figure is quantity: one hour chosen by diagnosis beats three chosen by subject, at a third of the monthly cost. Those figures were read in October 2026.

faqs.question: Will a science tutor come to our house in The Valley?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in this community. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with diagrams, calculations and graph work on a shared whiteboard and questions on screen. Home tutoring is a service we operate in India only. For the science practical papers, which are written rather than laboratory-based in both international specifications, the online format loses nothing at all.

faqs.question: How should the week be structured with three sciences and a long commute?
faqs.answer: Short work on a weekday and long work at the weekend. Terminology testing and arithmetic drills benefit from frequency rather than length, so they suit a weekday evening slot plus daily between-session sets. The practical skills paper, whole papers and graph work need uninterrupted attention, which in this community genuinely exists only on Saturday or Sunday. One weekday slot and one weekend block is the pattern that survives all three terms of Year 11 here.

faqs.question: Which science is hardest at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: The question is less useful than it sounds, because the three fail differently rather than ranking cleanly. Biology has the most content and punishes imprecise wording. Chemistry is the most procedural and punishes approximate arithmetic. Physics has the most mathematics embedded in it and punishes slow algebra. Which one a particular student finds hardest depends on whether their weakness is vocabulary precision, calculation discipline or manipulation speed, and that is readable from a marked paper rather than from a general ranking.

faqs.question: Why do you want marked papers before the first session?
faqs.answer: Because science losses are diagnosable from the page and not from a description. Looking at marked work shows whether a biology loss is wording, a chemistry loss is rounding or units, and a physics loss is rearranging or prefixes, and those need different sessions with sometimes different tutors. A parent's report that science is a problem is honest and not actionable; three lost wording marks in one biology answer is actionable immediately, and it usually saves a month of generalised hours.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-valley.closingHeading: Three codes and three marked papers
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-valley.closingBody: Send the syllabus codes for all three sciences and marked work from each, not only the subject that feels worst. The pattern across the three is what shows whether this is one cause wearing three subject labels — arithmetic, explanation wording, terminology precision — or three genuinely separate problems, and that decides whether you need one tutored hour a week or two. Next is a free trial lesson on the subject that is actually drifting, with the tutor who would continue, then a written plan naming subjects and causes with a weekday and weekend split. Lessons run one-to-one over live video into The Valley, with no UAE home visits.

intro.heading: The price of IGCSE science support in The Views, written down
paragraphs: The Views sits inside Emirates Living, between The Greens and The Meadows, a short drive from Al Barsha and a slightly longer one from Al Sufouh. Families here are close to Regent International School, Emirates International School - Meadows, Dubai British School Emirates Hills and Dubai International Academy, and that proximity is exactly why the money question gets muddled. A tutor who lives nearby is easy to find and feels like the frugal choice. The hourly rate rarely tells you whether that tutor has taught the Extended tier of Cambridge Physics 0625 to a Year 11 class, or only the Core tier, or neither.

Market rates in Dubai for science tuition run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 for a named premium tutor. That is a fourteenfold spread for what is advertised as the same service. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this cluster publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, a currency no family in The Views pays school fees in. The first table on this page fixes that: the bands, the tier each belongs to, and the published source that quoted it in October 2026.

The second thing the price does not tell you is how many hours the job needs. IGCSE science is three subjects with three mark schemes, and at Extended tier each one carries a multiple-choice paper, a long theory paper and a practical component. A student who cannot finish the theory paper has a timing problem, which is four to six timed papers with marking in between. A student who loses marks on graph scales and anomalous points has a Paper 6 problem, which is a different three or four sessions. Buying twenty hours of general revision when you needed six hours of paper technique is the most common way families here overspend.

The third variable is format, and it is the only one that moves the arithmetic by a large margin. An in-home visit in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, and the drive sits inside that rate. From The Views the realistic school-run-hour journey to Al Barsha or Emirates Hills is twenty to forty minutes each way, which is paid for twice: once in the tutor's rate and once in the slot it blocks. Online one-to-one removes that line item and widens the pool from whoever will drive to Emirates Living at 4pm to every specialist free at that hour.

IB Gram delivers tuition for UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; in-home teaching is a service we run only in India. That is stated plainly here because the honest version is also the better-value version for a science subject: the thing a Year 11 student in The Views needs is a Chemistry 0620 specialist marking their Paper 4 to the scheme, and geography should not be allowed to decide who that is.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-views.programmesIntro: Four routes matter to a family in The Views choosing science support at fourteen to sixteen. Two are IGCSE boards with different paper furniture, one is the IB Middle Years Programme that some Emirates Living families sit instead, and one is what happens after the exams. The cost of each is different, and so is the tutoring it needs.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE sciences
programmes.description: Cambridge runs the three sciences as separate qualifications - Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625 - plus Combined Science 0653 and Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 for students taking a reduced load. Entry is tiered: Core or Extended. At Extended tier a candidate sits a multiple-choice paper, a structured theory paper and either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper. Each paper has its own failure modes, which is why a tutor who knows the syllabus code is worth more per hour than one who knows the topic.
programmes.countryNote: Most British-curriculum schools near The Views enter candidates at Extended tier for at least two sciences, and tier decisions are usually confirmed with the final entry in the autumn before a June series. Ask your child's head of science which tier has been entered before buying any tutoring, because Core and Extended need different work and the Core-tier ceiling is lower than many parents in Emirates Living realise.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSE sciences - Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1, Physics 4PH1 - cover similar ground with different paper architecture and no separate practical paper, practical skills being assessed inside the written papers. Pearson also publishes a modular route on some subjects, which changes when a student can bank a result. The specification is the document that settles weightings and content, and it is free to read on the Pearson qualifications site.
programmes.countryNote: A handful of schools in the Al Barsha and Barsha Heights belt enter Pearson rather than Cambridge, and a few enter a mixture by subject. That matters to a The Views family because past-paper work is board-specific: Cambridge practice does not prepare a candidate for Pearson question stems. Confirm the board per subject, not per school, before the first paid session.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme, years 4 and 5
programmes.description: Some Emirates Living families sit the MYP rather than IGCSE at sixteen. Sciences there are assessed against four criteria rather than against papers, with no multiple-choice paper and no alternative-to-practical. The work is scientific inquiry, processing data and reflecting on the impact of science. Tutoring costs the same per hour and buys something different: criterion language and task-specific clarifications rather than past papers.
programmes.countryNote: If your child is at an IB continuum school near The Views and will enter the Diploma rather than A Level, the science question at sixteen is whether the inquiry skills are strong enough for a Diploma internal assessment. That is a cheaper problem to fix in MYP 5 than in DP1, and it is the only argument for spending money on science support in a year with no external exam.

programmes.name: What the science grades are actually for
programmes.description: An Extended-tier grade in two or three sciences is the entry ticket to IB Diploma Higher Level sciences or to A Level, and in some cases to a medicine or engineering route that will ask for Chemistry. Spending on IGCSE science is therefore partly an investment decision about a sixth-form subject list. A grade that just clears a school's internal threshold is not the same as a grade that survives the step up to Higher Level content.
programmes.countryNote: Schools around Emirates Living set their own entry grades for Higher Level sciences and A Level, typically published in the sixth-form guide. Read the threshold for the subject your child wants before deciding how many tutoring hours the spring term is worth. It converts a vague worry into a number, and a number can be budgeted against.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-views.subjectsIntro: Science is priced as three subjects, not one, and the hours each needs are not equal. The list below is the set a family in The Views actually asks for, with the syllabus code attached, because the code is what makes past-paper work usable rather than decorative.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity, magnetism and waves are where the Extended-tier marks go missing: circuit analysis with more than one unknown, and ray diagrams drawn without the construction lines the scheme wants. Paper 6 questions on apparatus and precision are the other reliable loss. Both are technique problems, which means they respond to a small number of targeted hours rather than a long general course.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis and organic nomenclature account for most of the gap between a grade 6 and a grade 8 at Extended tier. Candidates lose marks for unbalanced equations, for omitting state symbols, and for describing a test without naming the observation. Marked past-paper work in Chemistry has a faster return per hour than almost anything else on this list.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Biology looks like the recall subject and is marked like a precision subject. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance questions are answered in the student's own words and marked against specific terms. The command terms - describe, explain, suggest, compare - carry the difference, and a tutor who makes the student write to the term is worth more than one who re-teaches the content.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: One grade across all three sciences, a reduced subject content and fewer papers. Students here are often carrying a weak strand that drags the single grade, and the useful tutoring is diagnostic: find which of the three strands is costing marks, fix it, and leave the other two alone. Buying three subjects' worth of support for one combined grade is a common overspend.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: Two grades from three sciences, widely entered in British-curriculum schools around Emirates Living because it keeps an option open without filling three slots on the timetable. The tutoring question is the same as the subject's design question: which strand is the ceiling? Session planning should follow the strand, not the timetable.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Two written papers, with practical skills assessed inside them rather than in a separate component. Question stems and mark-scheme habits differ from Cambridge enough that mixed practice confuses candidates. A student entered for 4PH1 should practise 4PH1 papers, and a tutor should be able to say which paper a given question came from without looking.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Calculation-heavy, with quantitative chemistry threaded through both papers. The commonest loss is arithmetic presentation: a right method with no working, or an answer given to the wrong number of significant figures. These are cheap marks to recover and they are recovered by marking, not by explaining.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: Extended-writing questions carry more weight than many candidates expect, and the practical-skills questions inside the written papers reward students who have actually handled the apparatus. Where a school's practical programme has been thin, written practice on method, variables and error is the substitute that earns marks.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Included because science grades are frequently limited by maths. Rearranging formulae, standard form, ratio and graph work appear inside physics and chemistry questions, and a student who stalls there loses science marks that look like science ignorance. A short maths block is sometimes the cheapest science intervention available.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Environmental Management 0680
subjects.description: Taken alongside the sciences in some schools in the belt between Al Barsha and Dubailand. Case-study recall and data-response technique matter more than content volume. Sessions here are best spent on structuring answers to the mark allocation, which is a transferable skill that also lifts Biology extended writing.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE science tutor in The Views actually costs
paragraphs: Market rates for IGCSE science tuition reaching The Views run from about AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 for a premium named tutor, as published by providers in October 2026. The band most families here transact in is AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and AED 200 to 450 and above for a subject specialist. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500, with the drive inside the rate.

Those figures are the market, not an IB Gram price list. They are set out because three of the six competitor pages researched for this cluster publish no price at all, and one of them asks the price question in its own FAQ and then declines to answer it. A family comparing offers in Emirates Living deserves the bands in the currency they pay school fees in, with the provider that quoted each one named and the month of the quote stated.

The spread is not a quality ladder. A tutor at AED 450 may be a Physics specialist who has marked hundreds of Paper 4 scripts, or may simply be scarce in that subject at that hour. A tutor at AED 150 may be a current teacher doing two evenings a week. What separates them in practice is whether they can name the component your child is losing marks in before you book, and whether they will mark written work to the scheme rather than discuss it.

Read the table below as a map of the market rather than a recommendation. The useful column is the last one: what the hour usually contains. Two providers quoting the same number can be selling a content re-teach and a marked past paper respectively, and only one of those moves a grade in the eight weeks before a series.

sections.heading: Three sciences, three mark schemes: what you are buying per subject
paragraphs: The single biggest driver of total spend is how many sciences a candidate is entered for and at what tier. Three separate Extended-tier sciences is three syllabuses, three sets of past papers and three practical components. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is two grades from the same three strands, and Combined Science 0653 is one. A family budgeting for science support should start from the entry, because the entry decides how much work exists.

At Extended tier a Cambridge science candidate sits a multiple-choice paper worth 30% of the grade, a structured theory paper worth 50%, and a practical component worth 20% - either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, depending on what the school enters. Those shares are set in the current syllabus and should be confirmed on cambridgeinternational.org before any plan is built on them, because a syllabus revision changes the arithmetic.

The practical component is where the costing goes wrong most often. Twenty per cent of the grade sits in apparatus, method, tables, graphs and sources of error, and it is the component least covered by general revision. Three to five focused hours on graph scales, anomalous points and the suggest-one-improvement question type is usually the highest-return block available, and it is almost never what a family asks for when they first call.

Pearson's International GCSE sciences distribute practical skills inside the written papers instead of a separate component, so the same student needs the same skills assessed differently. That is why board confirmation precedes everything. A term of Cambridge past papers bought for a 4PH1 candidate is money spent on the wrong question stems, and it is a mistake that is invisible until the mocks come back.

sections.heading: Where the money goes to waste
paragraphs: Almost every overspend on science tuition in Emirates Living comes from one of five decisions, and all five are made before the first lesson. The first is buying hours before a diagnosis. A parent who says the child is weak at Physics is reporting a symptom; the mark scheme reports a cause, and the cause is usually a single component. Twelve hours of general Physics is a reasonable-sounding purchase that frequently leaves the Paper 6 problem untouched.

The second is paying for proximity. An in-home rate of AED 300 against an online rate of AED 220 for an equivalent tutor is a 36% premium for a drive, and from The Views that drive is twenty to forty minutes each way at school-run hour. The third is buying a group class to save money on a problem that is individual. Group pricing is genuinely lower per student, and it buys a shared pace, which is useful for broad revision and close to useless for one student's specific weakness.

The fourth is starting late. Rates do not formally rise before a series, but availability tightens, and a family looking for a Chemistry specialist in April is choosing from whoever is left rather than from whoever is best suited. The fifth is paying for content delivery when the student already knows the content. A candidate scoring well on recall and badly on structured questions needs marking and timing, which is a cheaper intervention than re-teaching and is the one most often skipped.

There is a sixth, less visible: not asking the school first. Several schools near The Views run their own after-school science clinics inside the fees already paid. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in private-school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. The fee line is fixed; the tutoring line is the variable one, and it should be the last thing bought, not the first.
