sections.heading: Costing a block of sessions against the paper it has to fix
paragraphs: The useful unit of purchase is not the hour, it is the block that clears one named problem. A block has a target component, a number of sessions, a piece of written evidence at the end, and a price that can be compared against doing nothing. Framed that way, science tuition stops being an open-ended subscription and becomes a series of decisions a family in The Views can say no to.

The table below prices blocks at AED 200 an hour, which sits inside the published market band for a qualified subject tutor online. It is used as an arithmetic anchor, not as a quoted price. The point is the relationship between the problem and the hours: a graph-and-error problem is four hours, a cannot-finish-the-paper problem is six, and a whole-subject grade shift across a year is a different order of commitment entirely.

Reading the last row honestly matters. Two sciences at one hour a week across a full academic year, at the mid band, is a five-figure commitment in AED. That is a real number and most families should see it before they start, because the alternative - six to ten well-targeted hours in the spring - often does more for a candidate whose knowledge is sound and whose technique is not. The expensive plan is sometimes right. It should never be the default.

Every figure in this table is indicative market arithmetic. Actual hours vary with the student, the starting point and how much written work gets done between sessions, which is the single largest variable nobody prices. A student who completes the marked work between sessions needs roughly half the hours of one who does not, and that is worth more than any discount a provider will offer.

sections.heading: The practical component when the practical is not the problem
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of an Extended-tier Cambridge science grade sits in a practical component, and families reasonably assume that a component about apparatus cannot be supported over video. The assumption is wrong in a specific and useful way. The alternative-to-practical paper is a written paper. It asks a candidate to read a method, complete a results table, plot and interpret a graph, identify an anomalous point, name a source of error and suggest one improvement. None of that requires a bench.

What it requires is practice at the particular register the scheme rewards. A candidate who writes that the experiment was inaccurate earns nothing; one who writes that the thermometer was read to the nearest degree and the temperature change was small earns the mark. That distinction is taught on paper, by marking, and it is one of the few places in IGCSE science where a handful of hours reliably converts into whole marks.

Where the school enters the practical test rather than the alternative paper, the hands-on work belongs to the school and should stay there. What tutoring adds is the surrounding technique: recording to the right precision, laying out a table before starting, deciding in advance how many readings to take and at what intervals. Those decisions are made before any apparatus is touched, and they are what distinguishes a finished script from an unfinished one.

For Pearson candidates there is no separate practical paper, and the same skills appear inside the written papers as method and data questions. The work is identical in substance and different in where it turns up. In both cases the honest statement is that a screen is not a limitation here, because the component being assessed is written reasoning about experiments rather than the experiments themselves.

sections.heading: Tuition spend in context for a The Views household
paragraphs: Tutoring is one line in a bigger education budget, and it reads differently next to the others. Dubai's private-school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curriculum schools accounting for 37% of enrolment and the International Baccalaureate 7%. That is the market a family in The Views is buying inside, and it is the reason the tutoring market here is both deep and unevenly priced.

The fee side of the budget is fixed for the coming year. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Dubai's 2026-27 intake also adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%.

Against a fixed fee line, tutoring is the variable the family controls. Monthly packages visible in the market run at AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

The last row of the table is the one most families forget. A candidate entered privately rather than through a school pays an entry fee set by the exam centre, not by the board and not by a tutor. Ask the centre directly, early, because the deadline for a June series entry sits in the preceding autumn and a late entry is a separate cost again.

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group: the arithmetic from Emirates Living
paragraphs: This is the comparison that decides most of the budget, so it is worth doing with the actual geography. The Views sits inside Emirates Living with The Greens to one side and The Meadows and The Lakes to the other. At school-run hour the drive to Al Barsha or Al Sufouh is twenty to forty minutes each way; Emirates Hills is closer but larger, and the internal drive adds minutes a map does not show. A tutor driving to a 4pm slot is committing ninety minutes to deliver sixty.

That commitment is priced. In-home rates in Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate, against AED 150 to 300 for an equivalent qualified tutor working online. The premium is the drive, and it also narrows the choice: a family paying for proximity is choosing from the tutors willing to drive to Emirates Living at that hour, not from the tutors who know Chemistry 0620 best.

IB Gram delivers tuition for families in The Views as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, and in-person tutoring in Dubai is not something IB Gram sells; in-home teaching is a service we run only in India. The reason to be blunt about that is that the online format is the stronger answer for a science subject anyway, and a page that hedges on delivery is hiding the part the parent most needs to know.

The gain is specificity. A Year 11 candidate losing marks on Paper 6 graph work needs someone who has marked that paper, and the chance that such a person is both free at 4pm and willing to drive to The Views is much lower than the chance that they are simply free at 4pm. Screen-shared past papers, a document camera for working, and marked scripts returned between sessions cover everything the component actually assesses.

sections.heading: What a science tutor may and may not do, and how to check the permit
paragraphs: Two things are worth knowing before money changes hands, and neither appears on most competitor pages. The first is the legal position of the person teaching. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anybody. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. That is the page to check, and a tutor who cannot discuss it is telling you something.

A second constraint applies in Abu Dhabi and is worth knowing even from Dubai: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported and should be verified against the current policy document, but the direction is clear and it rules out the arrangement some families ask for first.

The second thing is the academic boundary. A tutor teaches, explains, sets practice and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not produce assessed work, and no reputable provider offers to. For IGCSE science that means practical write-ups, coursework where a school sets it, and any investigation submitted for assessment remain the student's own work from first word to last. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments; that is a malpractice trigger for the student and it is the clearest signal available that a provider should be avoided.

sections.heading: Starting without overspending, and what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The sequence that wastes the least money is short. Ask the school what support is already included. Get the board and syllabus code for each science, and the tier entered. Collect the last two marked scripts. Then buy a diagnostic rather than a term, and let the diagnosis name the component and the hours. A free trial lesson - one per family, with no card details taken - is the right place to test whether a tutor can read those scripts and say something specific about them.

What a diagnostic should produce is a written plan naming the component, the number of sessions, what the student will do between them and how progress will be measured. If the output is a vague promise about confidence, that is a sign the sessions will also be vague. Paper scores are the measurement that matters, and they are available because official past papers exist and the schemes are published by the boards on their own sites.

Availability is the part most providers conceal, so here it is plainly. Specialist cover is not uniform across subjects and hours. Chemistry and Physics at Extended tier in the 4pm to 6pm Gulf Standard Time window are the tightest slots in the week, because every family in Dubai wants them. If no specialist is free for the hours a family in The Views needs, the honest answers are a different time slot, a short wait, or a tutor whose specialism is adjacent rather than exact - and the family should be told which of the three applies before paying anything.

Finally, review on a timetable rather than on a feeling. Four sessions in, look at the paper scores and the marked work. If the target component has moved, extend. If it has not, change the component, change the tutor, or stop. A plan that cannot be stopped at a review point is not a plan, it is a subscription, and subscriptions are how a reasonable AED 200 an hour becomes a number nobody examined.

process.title: Confirm board, code and tier
process.description: Before anything is priced, find out which board each science is entered with, which syllabus code, and whether the entry is Core or Extended. The school's head of science can confirm all three in one message. This single step prevents the most expensive mistake in the market, which is buying past-paper practice for the wrong board.

process.title: Send the last two marked scripts
process.description: A mock paper with the examiner's or teacher's marks on it tells a specialist more than an hour of conversation. It shows which component is leaking, whether the losses are knowledge or technique, and whether the candidate is finishing. Scripts and the school report comments are the whole of the useful input.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One free trial lesson per family, with no card details taken beforehand. Use it as an interview rather than a lesson: ask the tutor to name the component that is costing marks and to say what the first four sessions would target. A specific answer is the thing being tested.

process.title: Buy a diagnostic block, not a term
process.description: Two or three sessions whose output is a written plan with a component, a session count and a measurement. This costs less than a month of weekly sessions and it is the step that decides whether the eventual spend is four hours or forty. Families who skip it almost always buy more hours than they needed.

process.title: Work between sessions and mark it
process.description: The variable that halves or doubles the total hours is whether written work gets done and marked between lessons. Set it, do it, return it marked to the scheme. A student completing timed questions each week needs roughly half the sessions of one who only turns up, and no discount available anywhere matches that saving.

process.title: Review on paper scores at session four
process.description: At the fourth session compare paper scores on the target component against the starting point. Extend, change or stop on that evidence. A review point that is written into the plan in advance is what separates a costed intervention from an open-ended monthly payment nobody audits.

whyPoints.title: The price is on the page, in AED
whyPoints.description: Market bands are published here with the provider that quoted each one and the month of the quote. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this cluster publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. A family in The Views comparing offers should be able to see the range before making a call.

whyPoints.title: No drive inside the rate
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video, so none of the hour is spent on Sheikh Zayed Road and none of the rate pays for it. From Emirates Living the school-run drive to Al Barsha or Al Sufouh is twenty to forty minutes each way, which is the premium in-home pricing exists to cover.

whyPoints.title: Matched to a component, not a postcode
whyPoints.description: The useful question is not who is nearby but who has marked the paper your child is losing marks on. Choosing by component rather than by distance widens the pool to every specialist free at that hour, which is the practical argument for the online format in a subject with three distinct mark schemes.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes, not subject labels
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0610, 0620, 0625, 0653 and 0654 and Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 behave differently in question stems and mark schemes. Work is planned against the code the candidate is entered for, and past papers come from that code, which is the difference between practice and busywork.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary is stated
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, explains, sets practice and gives feedback on the student's own work. Nothing assessed is produced for a student, ever. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments, which is a malpractice trigger for the candidate, and the boundary is worth saying out loud rather than leaving implied.

whyPoints.title: Availability is disclosed before payment
whyPoints.description: Specialist cover varies by subject and by hour, and the 4pm to 6pm Gulf Standard Time window is the tightest in the week. If no exact specialist is free for the slot a family needs, that is said before anything is paid, with the alternatives named. Concealed coverage limits are a cost that arrives later.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE science tutor for The Views cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Market rates reaching The Views run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 for a premium named tutor, as published by providers in October 2026. Most families transact between AED 150 and 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and AED 200 to 450 or more for a subject specialist. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500, with the drive inside the rate. Those are market bands rather than an IB Gram price list. What varies inside a band is whether the hour contains marked written work or only conversation, and that difference matters more than the number.

faqs.question: Is one tutor for all three sciences cheaper than three specialists?
faqs.answer: It is usually cheaper per hour and often more expensive per mark. Biology, Chemistry and Physics at Extended tier are three syllabuses with three mark schemes, and few tutors mark all three to examiner standard. Where a candidate has one narrow problem in each subject, a single tutor on alternating weeks can work and halves the weekly cost. Where one science has a broad problem, that subject needs its own specialist. The honest test is to ask the tutor to name the component costing marks in each of the three. A tutor who can do that for all three is rare and worth keeping.

faqs.question: Do triple-award candidates need more tutoring hours than double-award?
faqs.answer: Yes, roughly in proportion to the papers sat. Three separate sciences means three multiple-choice papers, three theory papers and three practical components, so there is simply more assessed material. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 produces two grades from the same three strands and Combined Science 0653 produces one, which concentrates the work. With a combined award the efficient approach is diagnostic: identify which strand is dragging the single grade and spend the hours there. Buying three subjects' worth of support for one combined grade is one of the commonest overspends in this market.

faqs.question: Is a group science class in Barsha Heights better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Per hour, clearly yes. Per problem, usually not. A group class is sold at a lower per-student rate and delivers a shared pace across a syllabus, which suits broad revision before a series. It does not suit one candidate's specific weakness, because the weakest topic for your child is rarely the topic the group needs that week. A reasonable sequence is a group class for syllabus coverage if the school is not already providing it, plus a short one-to-one block aimed at the component the mock paper identified. Paying group prices to solve an individual problem is a false economy.

faqs.question: How many sessions does it take to fix electricity and magnetism?
faqs.answer: For a candidate who understands the rest of Physics and loses marks on circuits, six sessions is a realistic block: roughly one per sub-topic, plus retrieval practice and two timed papers. At the mid market band of AED 200 an hour that is around AED 1,200 of indicative arithmetic, not a quoted price. The variable that changes it most is whether the student completes and submits the written work between sessions. A candidate who does needs about half the hours of one who does not, which is a bigger saving than any rate negotiation will produce.

faqs.question: Does paying more per hour buy a better science tutor?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. The published spread in Dubai is roughly fourteenfold for what is advertised as the same service, and a high rate can reflect scarcity in a subject at a particular hour rather than method or experience. The checkable signals are different: can the tutor name the component your child is losing marks in before being booked, will they mark written work against the published scheme rather than discuss it, and do they know the syllabus code rather than just the subject. Those three questions separate tutors more accurately than price does, and all three can be tested in a trial lesson.

faqs.question: When in Year 10 is the cheapest time to start science support?
faqs.answer: The cheapest intervention is usually the earliest small one. A short diagnostic in the first term of Year 10, once the tier entry is known, costs a few hours and prevents a weak strand becoming a whole-subject problem by the mocks. Waiting until the spring of Year 11 does not raise rates formally, but it narrows availability sharply, and a family looking for a specialist in April chooses from whoever is left. Early also means the work can be spread, and spread hours are both cheaper per month and more effective than the same hours compressed.

faqs.question: Do science tutoring rates in Dubai rise before the June series?
faqs.answer: Published rates do not generally move, but effective cost does. As a series approaches, demand concentrates in the 4pm to 6pm Gulf Standard Time window, specialists in Chemistry and Physics fill first, and families accept adjacent rather than exact specialisms or less convenient slots. That is a quality cost rather than a price rise. Some providers do sell intensive exam-term packages at higher monthly totals because the session count is higher. The practical conclusion is to book the specialist and the slot early, even if the sessions themselves start later in the year.

faqs.question: What should I ask about price before the first science lesson?
faqs.answer: Six questions settle it. Is the rate per clock hour or per lesson, and how long is a lesson? Is marking of written work between sessions included or extra? Is there a minimum block, and can we stop at a review point? What happens to unused sessions? Is the rate per subject if two sciences share a slot? And does the quoted figure include VAT? Ask them in writing and keep the reply. Most disputes in this market come from the gap between an hourly rate and what the hour included, not from the rate itself.

faqs.question: Are the AED rates quoted per hour or per session?
faqs.answer: Both conventions exist in Dubai, which is exactly why comparison is hard. Some providers quote a clock-hour rate; others quote per session, where a session may be fifty, sixty or ninety minutes. A few quote monthly packages with a stated session count, such as the AED 799 a month for eight online sessions visible in the market. Convert everything to a cost per sixty minutes of teaching before comparing, and ask separately whether marking between sessions is inside that number. Two quotes that look twenty per cent apart are sometimes identical once normalised.

faqs.question: Can the alternative-to-practical paper be taught over video?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the better uses of an online hour. The alternative-to-practical paper is a written paper: read a method, complete a results table, plot and interpret a graph, spot an anomalous point, name a source of error, suggest one improvement. All of that is paper technique and responds to marking. Where a school enters the practical test instead, the hands-on work belongs to the school, and tutoring supports the surrounding decisions - table layout, precision, how many readings and at what intervals. Those are made before any apparatus is touched.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge or Pearson science cheaper to get tutoring for?
faqs.answer: The rate is the same; the availability is not. Cambridge syllabuses are more widely entered in Dubai, so the pool of tutors who know 0610, 0620 and 0625 well is larger and easier to fill at awkward hours. Pearson's 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 need a tutor who works from the Pearson specification and Pearson past papers, and that pool is smaller. The real cost difference appears if a family buys the wrong board's practice. Confirm the board per subject rather than per school, because some schools enter a mixture.

faqs.question: How do I check a private science tutor may legally teach in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. Ask any individual tutor whether they hold the permit and check the official page yourself. Anyone quoting you a fee for it, or a fine amount, is working from something that is not published.

faqs.question: What happens to the money if the first science tutor is the wrong match?
faqs.answer: Ask before you pay, in writing, and prefer arrangements with a review point rather than a long prepaid block. A sensible structure is a free trial lesson first, then a short diagnostic block, then a review at the fourth session against paper scores on the target component. If the component has not moved, the right move is to change the tutor or the target, not to extend. Avoid any arrangement that ties a refund to an exam outcome; outcomes depend on the student's own work and no honest provider prices them.

faqs.question: What if no Physics specialist is free for the hours we need?
faqs.answer: That happens, most often in the 4pm to 6pm Gulf Standard Time window during an exam term, and the honest answer is one of three. A different slot, sometimes a morning at a weekend, which is usually the best of the three. A short wait for the right specialist, which is reasonable in autumn and risky in April. Or an adjacent specialism - a Chemistry teacher strong on quantitative work covering the calculation side while Paper 6 technique waits. Which one applies should be said before any payment, not discovered afterwards.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-views.closingHeading: Price the problem, then buy the hours
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-views.closingBody: The useful order is cheap first: ask the school what is already included, confirm the board, code and tier for each science, collect the last two marked scripts, then test a tutor on a free trial lesson by asking them to name the component that is costing marks. Buy a diagnostic rather than a term, write down the component, the session count and the measurement, and review on paper scores at the fourth session. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which keeps the drive out of the rate and widens the choice to every specialist free at that hour. intro.heading: Three comparisons before you compare tutors
paragraphs: Science at IGCSE is not one qualification but several, and a family hiring a tutor without knowing which one their child sits is guessing. Separate sciences means three IGCSEs with three sets of papers. Cambridge Combined Science 0653 is a single award across all three sciences. Cambridge Co-ordinated Science 0654 is a double award. The Pearson Edexcel Science Double Award 4SD0 is a different double award again. Content volume, paper structure, reporting and sixth-form access all differ.

So this page makes three comparisons before discussing teaching. The awards, compared on what they actually cover and what they open afterwards. The two boards, compared on how they assess practical skills, which is the difference that most affects an online-tutored student. And the three sciences, compared on how each one has to be revised, because a method that works for biology is close to useless for physics.

Tilal Al Ghaf is a good place to make the award comparison because the choice is genuinely live. The community has a British-curriculum school inside its boundary and DAMAC Hills, Dubai Sports City and Motor City all have their own provision nearby, and across those schools both awarding bodies and several award structures are in use. A pupil here may be on a combined award while a neighbour two streets away sits three separate sciences, and the two families will exchange advice that does not transfer.

The practical question is the one most often asked of an online provider, and it deserves a direct answer early. In Cambridge sciences a candidate sits either a practical test in the school laboratory or an alternative-to-practical written paper, depending on what the centre enters. In Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences there is no separate practical paper and experimental skills appear inside the two written papers. For the written versions a tutor on a screen is not disadvantaged at all; for apparatus familiarity the school is the only source and we say so.

One scheduling advantage is worth using here. Because Tilal Al Ghaf has a school inside the community and its neighbours do too, pupils are often home before four, so an early weekday session is realistic. In science that matters most for the quantitative work, where a tired pupil makes arithmetic errors rather than conceptual ones, and for full timed papers, which need an alert candidate to be a fair test.

IB Gram delivers science tuition to Tilal Al Ghaf as live one-to-one lessons over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Practical work happens in your child's school laboratory in either case, which this page treats as a fact rather than an obstacle to be talked around.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-tilal-al-gh.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE science topics Tilal Al Ghaf families ask about, with the revision method each actually responds to. The method differs by science, which is why a single revision plan across all three usually underperforms.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Responds to worked problems rather than to notes, because circuit reasoning holds current, potential difference and resistance together. Marks go to candidates who state which quantity is constant in a given arrangement before calculating anything.

subjects.name: Forces and motion
subjects.description: Responds to graph practice. Candidates read values correctly and then cannot say what the gradient or the area under the line physically represents, which is where the explanation marks sit rather than in the arithmetic.

subjects.name: Waves, light and sound
subjects.description: Responds to drawing practice. Refraction and ray diagrams are marked on construction lines and on measuring from the normal rather than the surface, so repeated drawing beats reading about it every time.

subjects.name: Moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: Responds only to volume of worked calculations. It recurs through titration, yield and gas-volume questions and compounds, and unit discipline between moles per cubic decimetre and per cubic centimetre costs more across a paper than conceptual gaps do.

subjects.name: Qualitative analysis
subjects.description: The one topic in all three sciences where memorisation is the correct method. Tests for cations, anions and gases with their observations are learned content, cheap marks, and reliably skipped in revision because they feel like rote work.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and rates
subjects.description: Responds to explanation practice. Rate questions want collision-frequency reasoning rather than a restatement of the trend, and candidates lose marks describing what happens to the rate instead of explaining why particles collide more often.

subjects.name: Transport and respiration
subjects.description: Responds to terminology drilling. Diffusion, osmosis and active transport are distinguished in the mark scheme and conflated under time pressure, so the method that works is precise definition practice rather than reading.

subjects.name: Inheritance and variation
subjects.description: Responds to one technique change: drawing the genetic cross rather than reasoning in prose. Candidates who state a correct ratio without the cross lose the method marks, and the fix is a single session followed by repetition.

subjects.name: Enzymes and photosynthesis
subjects.description: Responds to data-interpretation practice, since these topics generate most of the graph questions. The answer wanted is the limiting factor producing the graph's shape, not a description of the shape itself.

subjects.name: Experimental skills
subjects.levels: Cambridge Papers 5 and 6; within Edexcel written papers
subjects.description: Responds to question-type practice, because it follows a formula: name the independent, dependent and controlled variables, justify repeats, handle an anomaly, choose apparatus with appropriate resolution, name a specific source of error. The most predictable marks in the subject.

subjects.name: Calculations and units across the sciences
subjects.description: Responds to volume and to enforced visible working. A science problem is frequently a mathematics problem in disguise, which is why a diagnostic has to test the quantitative handling separately from the content knowledge.

subjects.name: Command terms in science answers
subjects.description: Responds to marked-and-rewritten practice rather than to being explained. 'State', 'describe', 'explain', 'suggest' and 'compare' carry different expectations, and teaching a candidate to answer the verb recovers marks across every topic at once.

sections.heading: Separate sciences or a combined award: the real comparison
paragraphs: This is the decision that shapes a pupil's options at sixteen and it is frequently made on timetable convenience. The four structures in use are not interchangeable: separate sciences gives three IGCSEs, Cambridge Co-ordinated Science 0654 and the Pearson Edexcel Science Double Award 4SD0 each give a double award, and Cambridge Combined Science 0653 gives a single award. Content volume per science descends across that list and so does what it opens afterwards.

The first thing to be clear about is what a combined award is not. It is not an easier version of the same assessment. Content per science is reduced, but the papers are marked to the same standard with the same command-term precision and the same calculation discipline. Families told the course is lighter frequently conclude it is easier, and then find that a pupil who was going to find three sciences hard finds a combined award hard too, just across less material.

The second is what it costs in options. A Level and IB Higher Level sciences commonly assume separate-science content, and a pupil arriving from a combined award has a genuine content gap rather than a pacing problem. That is bridgeable with a block before Year 12, but it has to be planned rather than discovered. Ask the school directly what their own sixth form expects, because the answer is specific to the school and is usually more precise than any general advice.

The third is the honest case for a combined award, which is real. A pupil who would carry three sciences badly, at the cost of their other subjects, is better served by one or two awards done well. Three separate sciences at the higher tier is a substantial load, and a pupil whose intended route needs no science beyond sixteen gains nothing from carrying it. The mistake is not choosing a combined award; it is choosing one without checking what it closes.

sections.heading: The two boards compared on practical assessment
paragraphs: This is the comparison that most affects a family considering online tutoring, so it deserves precision rather than reassurance. The two awarding bodies assess experimental skills in genuinely different ways, and that changes what a tutor can and cannot contribute.

In Cambridge sciences a candidate sits either a practical test, conducted in the school laboratory under exam conditions, or an alternative-to-practical written paper in which experimental skills are examined on paper. Which one depends on what the centre enters, so ask the exams officer. The alternative-to-practical paper is a written paper and a tutor on a screen is not disadvantaged by it at all; in fact it is among the most teachable papers in the whole qualification, because the question types follow a formula.

In Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences there is no separate practical paper. Experimental skills appear inside the two written papers, woven among the content questions. That is easier to prepare for incidentally and harder to target deliberately, because there is no single paper to practise. The consequence for tutoring is that experimental-skills work has to be threaded through the year rather than treated as a block before the exam.

The practical test is the only version where a screen genuinely loses something, and the loss is apparatus familiarity rather than knowledge. A candidate who knows before walking in that they will record readings to a consistent precision, tabulate with units in the headings and plot with a sensible scale will score better than one discovering those expectations during the exam, and that preparation is talk and marked practice. What a tutor cannot supply is the feel of a burette or the look of a failed reaction, and the school provides that in either case.

sections.heading: The three sciences compared by how they must be revised
paragraphs: Families apply one revision plan across all three sciences and then conclude that revision does not work. The plan is the problem. The three sciences reward different methods, and a method that produces results in biology produces almost nothing in physics.

Physics has the lowest content volume and the highest reasoning demand, so it responds to worked problems and to drawing practice rather than to notes. A pupil who reads a physics textbook chapter has learned very little; the same pupil who works twenty circuit problems has learned a great deal. Making notes is close to the least efficient physics revision available, which is unfortunate because it is the most popular.

Chemistry is quantitative and sequential, so it responds to volume of worked calculations with visible working. The mole concept recurs through titration, yield, gas volumes and rates, and fluency there carries everything downstream. The one chemistry topic where memorisation is the correct method is qualitative analysis, which is pure learned content and the cheapest marks on the paper, and which pupils skip precisely because it feels like rote work.

Biology has the highest content volume and the lowest mathematical demand, and it responds to terminology drilling and data-interpretation practice. Diffusion, osmosis and active transport are separated in the mark scheme and conflated under pressure, and precise definition practice fixes that. Inheritance responds to one technique change — drawing the cross rather than reasoning in prose — and enzyme and photosynthesis questions respond to graph work. Biology is also the science where flashcards genuinely earn their place, which is not true of the other two.

sections.heading: Reading the mock by paper, not by grade
paragraphs: A single science grade hides the information you need. In Cambridge sciences a candidate sits a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a practical or alternative-to-practical paper, and the losses are frequently concentrated in one of them rather than spread across the subject. A grade reports the sum and tells you nothing about which.

The pattern we see most often is a concentrated loss on the alternative-to-practical paper, because it is the paper nobody revises. A family reading a single grade concludes the science is weak and buys a term of content teaching, which does not touch the paper the marks were lost on. A family reading the papers separately buys three sessions on variables, repeats, anomalies and apparatus resolution and recovers most of it.

The second common pattern is a weak multiple-choice performance against a reasonable theory paper, which usually means the content is thin but the written technique is fine. The reverse — strong multiple choice, weak theory — usually means content is secure and extended answers are not, which is a command-term problem and responds to marked-and-rewritten practice within weeks.

So the request to make of the school is specific: not the grade but the mark on each paper, and ideally the question-level breakdown. Most schools will provide it if asked. That single piece of information frequently changes what a family should buy, and it costs nothing. Doing this is also why an honest first session sometimes ends with us saying that three sessions will do rather than a term.

sections.heading: Comparing the bridge into A Level and into IB sciences
paragraphs: Both sixth-form routes are available within a reasonable drive of Tilal Al Ghaf, and the bridging requirement differs, which is worth knowing before the summer after the series disappears unused. In both cases the summer block is the cheapest intervention available at that point and the one almost nobody books, because the exams are over and nothing feels urgent.

Into A Level sciences, the gap is depth and mathematical pace. A Level physics and chemistry go considerably further than IGCSE within the same topics, and both assume algebraic fluency from the first week. Practical work is assessed through a separate practical endorsement across many activities rather than one piece of coursework, so a candidate who sat an alternative-to-practical paper has laboratory expectations to learn but no single high-stakes piece to prepare.

Into IB Higher Level sciences, the gap is depth plus the investigation. Every IB science requires an individual scientific investigation marked out of 24 across four criteria and worth 20% of the grade, and an IGCSE candidate who only ever sat an alternative-to-practical paper has never designed anything. Teaching variables, controls, uncertainty and evaluation before Year 12 begins means their first investigation is not also their first attempt at the skills it needs.

Either way the content gap is larger for a pupil arriving from a combined award than from separate sciences, and it is a genuine content gap rather than a matter of pace. Six to eight sessions covers the separate-sciences case; a pupil from a combined award needs longer and should plan for it rather than discovering it in October. Ask the receiving school what they assume, because they will tell you and it is more precise than anything a tutoring page can say.

sections.heading: What the awards cost to support
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figures rather than the hourly ones, because an award is a year-long commitment and no family buys a single science hour. Bestimate's Dubai estimates, read in October 2026, run AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, each of those per subject supported rather than per child. The hourly ladder sitting behind those bands, taken the same month from the providers' own published pages, climbs steeply: Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52, EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65, Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE, TutorChase at AED 270, BartyED at AED 650. Bestimate's table also puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. For a Tilal Al Ghaf family the spread matters less than the multiplier, and the multiplier was fixed when the award was chosen.

The award structure changes the arithmetic more than anything else, which is rarely mentioned when the award is chosen. A pupil on three separate sciences who needs support in two is a two-subject commitment: at the mid band, roughly AED 1,200 to AED 2,400 a month for weekly sessions in each. A pupil on a combined or double award is a single commitment, because one tutor can cover the reduced content across the sciences in that award. For a family where budget is a real constraint, that is a legitimate consideration in the award decision and nobody raises it at the time.

The second arithmetic point is the practical paper. Where the award sets an alternative-to-practical paper, three sessions on variables, repeats, anomalies and apparatus resolution covers it, which is a small, fixed and well-defined purchase. That is one of the best-value blocks in IGCSE science and it is almost never bought, because it is not a topic and therefore does not appear on anyone's list of things to revise.

The market band lets you judge any quote including ours, and the first lesson is free. In it, ask the tutor which papers your child's award sets and how practical skills are assessed on that board. A specialist answers both immediately.

sections.heading: Which science to drop, if one has to go
paragraphs: Year 9 option blocks sometimes force a choice, and the decision is often made on which teacher a pupil likes. Two better criteria exist and neither takes long to apply.

The first is the destination. If any intended sixth-form or degree route needs a particular science, that settles it, and the requirement is published by schools and universities rather than inferred. Medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and veterinary routes commonly want chemistry, frequently with biology. Engineering and physics routes commonly want physics with mathematics. Life sciences generally want biology with chemistry. A pupil dropping chemistry while aiming at medicine has usually made the wrong trade and will discover it at sixteen.

The second is load capacity against profile. Physics has the lowest content volume and the highest reasoning and mathematical demand, so it suits a pupil who reasons well and dislikes memorising. Chemistry is quantitative and sequential, so it suits a pupil who is organised and precise with numbers, and punishes a weak foundation more than the others because so much sits downstream of the mole concept. Biology has the highest content volume and the lowest mathematical demand, so it suits a pupil with a strong memory and written discipline.

Where the destination leaves a genuine choice, matching the profile produces a better grade than following a preference for a teacher, and a better grade in two sciences usually serves a pupil better than three mediocre ones. That is the conversation to have in Year 9 rather than Year 11, and it is one a tutor should be willing to have even when the honest answer reduces the number of subjects they might be asked to teach.

sections.heading: Permits, papers and the claims to distrust
paragraphs: This heading promises claims to distrust, and the first is the one nobody states out loud: that the person you are about to hire is lawfully permitted to teach your child. Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-regulated, and eligibility is far broader than parents assume. It covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students, so the useful question is never whether a tutor could hold a permit but whether they actually do. The instrument is Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its app, website and e-services. No fee and two working days means a provider who has not applied has decided not to, and that single fact filters a shortlist faster than any claim about which science award they specialise in.

The penalty for going without one is where the internet starts inventing. What the law actually says is that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and that is the whole of it. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and the figure circulating online could not be verified, which is why no dirham amount appears anywhere on this page. Read a provider who prints a penalty figure the way you would read one who puts a number on next June's result: both offer a precision that has been invented to create urgency, and neither has a published source standing behind it.

On materials, the limit is firm. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement. A tutor works through questions from legitimately obtained material and teaches the candidate to read a mark scheme themselves, which matters in science because the marks sit in named variables, units and construction lines rather than in the final figure.

Two further claims to treat sceptically. Examiner status, which we do not use as a selling point for anyone whose current status cannot be evidenced and which gives no access to marking, boundaries or unseen papers. And any promise about a specific result, which we will not make because nobody controls it. What we will give you after a mock read paper by paper is a categorised account of where the marks went and an honest view of what the remaining weeks can close. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson.

process.title: Establish the award, not just the subject
process.description: Email the exams officer for the award structure, the awarding body, the syllabus code and the tier, plus whether the centre enters a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. Those answers determine the whole plan, and in a neighbourhood where several structures are in use they cannot be assumed from a neighbour's experience.

process.title: Ask for the mock marks paper by paper
process.description: Not the subject grade but the mark on each paper, and the question-level breakdown if the school has it. Losses in Cambridge sciences are often concentrated in one paper rather than spread, and very often in the alternative-to-practical paper, which no amount of content teaching would have touched.

process.title: Match the method to the science
process.description: Physics by worked problems and drawing, chemistry by calculation volume with working shown, biology by terminology drilling and data interpretation. A single revision plan across all three is why so much revision produces so little, and the fix costs nothing but a change of approach.

process.title: A free first lesson with the named tutor
process.description: One full lesson, no charge, with the person who would continue. Ask them which papers your child's award sets and how practical skills are assessed on that board. A specialist answers instantly. Then watch whether they found where the marks actually went.

process.title: Put the quantitative work early
process.description: Tilal Al Ghaf pupils are often home before four, so a four-thirty start is realistic here. That matters for chemistry calculation and physics problem work, where a tired pupil makes arithmetic errors rather than conceptual ones, and for full timed papers, which need an alert candidate to be a fair test.

process.title: Reassess by paper at each mock
process.description: Each mock is read paper by paper and compared with the last, so the plan follows evidence rather than habit. If one paper has moved and another has not, the hours get reallocated. If a science is secure we say so and stop rather than rolling a session forward with no target.

whyPoints.title: The award comparison made before the hours are sold
whyPoints.description: Four structures are in use and they differ in content, in reporting and in what they open at sixteen. We set out the honest case for a combined award as well as against one, because a pupil who would carry three sciences badly is better served by fewer done well.

whyPoints.title: Practical assessment explained board by board
whyPoints.description: Cambridge sets a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper; Edexcel assesses experimental skills inside the written papers. That distinction decides what a tutor can contribute, and the alternative-to-practical paper is among the most teachable papers in the whole qualification.

whyPoints.title: Revision method matched to the science
whyPoints.description: Note-making is close to the least efficient physics revision available and among the most useful for biology. Applying one plan across all three sciences is the commonest reason revision produces nothing, and changing it costs a family nothing at all.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis paper by paper, not by grade
whyPoints.description: A single science grade is a sum that hides where the marks went. Reading the mock paper by paper regularly shows a concentrated loss in the paper nobody revised, which turns a term of content teaching into three well-aimed sessions.

whyPoints.title: The bridging block named in advance
whyPoints.description: A pupil arriving at A Level or IB Higher Level sciences from a combined award has a genuine content gap, and an alternative-paper candidate going into the IB has never designed an investigation. Both are cheap to fix in the summer and expensive to discover in October.

whyPoints.title: Clear about the limits
whyPoints.description: Practical work stays at school. No home visits in the UAE. No distribution of awarding-body papers or mark schemes. No examiner claims we cannot evidence. No promises about results. No approval or accreditation from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, because we hold none.

faqs.question: Do the papers get marked more gently on a combined award?
faqs.answer: No — the award is lighter in volume and identical in standard, which is a distinction families regularly miss. Content per science is reduced, but the papers are marked with the same command-term precision and the same calculation discipline, so a pupil who would find three sciences hard will find a combined award hard too, across less material. The real difference is what it opens at sixteen: A Level and IB Higher Level sciences commonly assume separate-science content, so a bridging block may be needed.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science award gives the best sixth-form access?
faqs.answer: Separate sciences, directly, because A Level and IB Higher Level courses commonly assume that content. Cambridge Co-ordinated Science 0654 and the Pearson Edexcel Science Double Award 4SD0 are each double awards with substantial content and are often sufficient, while Cambridge Combined Science 0653 is the most reduced and more often needs bridging. Ask your own school's sixth form what it assumes, because the answer is specific to the school and more precise than general advice.

faqs.question: How are practical skills assessed in each board's IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: Cambridge sets either a practical test in the school laboratory under exam conditions or an alternative-to-practical written paper, depending on what the centre enters, so ask the exams officer which. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences have no separate practical component and assess experimental skills inside the two written papers. That changes tutoring: the Cambridge alternative paper is a highly teachable block, while Edexcel's experimental questions have to be threaded through the year.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram offer in-home science tutoring in Tilal Al Ghaf?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE tuition is delivered live and one-to-one over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we run only in India. Practical laboratory work happens at school in either case, so no tutor in any format substitutes for apparatus familiarity. For the written and practical-skills papers a screen costs nothing, because the work is marked questions, worked calculations with visible steps and annotated diagrams on a shared display.

faqs.question: Why does my child's revision not move their science marks?
faqs.answer: Most often because one method is being applied to three sciences that reward different ones. Note-making is close to the least efficient physics revision available, because physics has low content volume and high reasoning demand and responds to worked problems. Chemistry responds to volume of calculations with visible working. Biology, with the highest content volume and lowest mathematical demand, is the one science where flashcards genuinely earn their place. Changing the method costs nothing.

faqs.question: Should I ask for the mock marks paper by paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the single most useful request you can make. A subject grade is a sum that hides where the marks went, and in Cambridge sciences the losses are frequently concentrated in one paper rather than spread. The commonest pattern is a heavy loss on the alternative-to-practical paper, because it is the paper nobody revises, and a term of content teaching would not have touched it. Three well-aimed sessions often recovers most of it instead.

faqs.question: Which science should my child drop if the option block forces a choice?
faqs.answer: Start with the destination, which is published rather than inferred: medicine, dentistry and pharmacy routes commonly want chemistry, often with biology; engineering and physics want physics with mathematics; life sciences generally want biology with chemistry. Where the destination leaves a genuine choice, match the profile — physics for reasoning over memorising, chemistry for precision with numbers, biology for memory and written discipline. Two sciences done well usually serve a pupil better than three done poorly.

faqs.question: What is the alternative-to-practical paper and how do you prepare for it?
faqs.answer: A Cambridge written paper examining experimental skills on paper rather than in a laboratory, sat where the centre enters it instead of the practical test. It follows a formula: identify the independent, dependent and controlled variables, justify repeat readings, spot and handle an anomaly, choose apparatus with appropriate resolution, name a specific source of error rather than human error, and read a scale or graph accurately. Three sessions covers it, which makes it among the best-value blocks in IGCSE science.

faqs.question: How does the award structure change what tutoring costs?
faqs.answer: More than anything else, and nobody mentions it when the award is chosen. Three separate sciences with two weak subjects is a two-subject commitment, roughly AED 1,200 to AED 2,400 a month at the mid market band read in October 2026. A combined or double award is a single commitment, because one tutor can cover the reduced content across the sciences in that award. For a family where budget is a genuine constraint, that belongs in the award decision.

faqs.question: What should my child do in the summer after IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: A bridging block, and the shape depends on the destination. Into A Level sciences the gap is depth and mathematical pace, so six to eight sessions from separate sciences usually suffices. Into IB Higher Level sciences there is the investigation as well: every IB science requires an individual investigation marked out of 24 and worth 20% of the grade, and a candidate who only ever sat an alternative-to-practical paper has never designed anything. A pupil from a combined award needs longer in either case.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all three sciences on a combined award?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and that is one of the practical advantages of a combined or double award. Content per science is reduced, so a single competent science tutor can cover the whole award rather than a family needing three specialists. On three separate sciences at the higher tier the opposite applies: the content depth in each makes a specialist worth having, particularly in chemistry where the quantitative work is unforgiving and in physics where the explanation demand is highest.

faqs.question: Why does session timing matter for IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: Because the quantitative work is precision work. A tired pupil makes arithmetic errors rather than conceptual ones, and in chemistry a rounding decision at the first step of a multi-step calculation survives to the final answer. Full timed papers are also only a fair test with an alert candidate. Tilal Al Ghaf has a school inside the community and neighbours with their own provision, so pupils are often home before four and a four-thirty start is genuinely available here.

faqs.question: Which exam series does a Tilal Al Ghaf science candidate sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs June and November, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Those are what UAE candidates use. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any UAE-facing page quoting a February window is describing a different country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise.

faqs.question: Will a tutor provide past papers for the sciences?
faqs.answer: No. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement. A tutor works through questions from legitimately obtained material and teaches your child to read a mark scheme themselves. In science that matters particularly, because the marks sit in named variables, units and construction lines rather than in the final figure, and a candidate who sees that writes differently next time.

faqs.question: What licensing applies to a science tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, so be sceptical of pages quoting amounts. Ask to see the document rather than accepting an assurance.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-tilal-al-gh.closingBody: Two requests to the school decide most of this. Ask for the award structure, the awarding body, the syllabus code, the tier, and whether the centre enters a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. With those in hand you can judge any tutor in two minutes, and you may well find that three well-aimed sessions do what a term of content teaching would not. intro.heading: Which practical route is your child entered for?
paragraphs: Ask a Town Square parent which board their child's science department uses and most can find out. Ask which practical assessment route the school entered and almost nobody knows, which is a problem, because that single decision changes where a substantial share of the marks sit and therefore what tutoring should be aimed at.

The two broad possibilities are a written Alternative to Practical paper, used on many Cambridge science entries, or assessed laboratory work at school. They are not variations on a theme. The written route tests experimental understanding on paper — reading an instrument to a sensible precision, spotting that a method cannot answer the question it was set, identifying an uncontrolled variable, building a results table with correct headings and units, plotting and interpreting a graph, judging whether a conclusion is supported. All of that responds directly to one-to-one work, and it is reliably where students lose the most marks relative to the effort of preparing.

The laboratory route puts the assessed technique at school, where it belongs and where no tutor substitutes for it. A provider implying otherwise is overselling, and it is worth treating as a signal. What tutoring adds in that case is the reasoning around the bench — predicting the expected result, handling an anomaly rather than discarding it, simple uncertainty treatment, writing up to the expected standard — which is still a meaningful share of the credit.

Both routes sit on top of the entry question. Separate sciences, Cambridge Coordinated Sciences 0654 and Cambridge Combined Science 0653 cover different amounts of content and award different numbers of grades, so a tutor teaching separate-science depth to a coordinated student spends sessions on material that will not be examined. One email to the school office returns the entry, the board, the syllabus codes and the practical route together.

Town Square's geography matters too. It is a Nshama community off Al Qudra Road, populated recently by younger families, and Dubai's tutoring supply clusters around the older school corridors rather than the newer Dubailand ones. The subset of tutors willing to work out here is smaller before specification is considered, and a recently settled community has not yet built the neighbour network that vets tutors elsewhere.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. That widens the pool from whoever will drive to Al Qudra Road to anybody who has prepared students for your child's specific practical component, which is the variable that actually decides the marks.

A last framing point before the detail. In a triple-award week the limiting resource is not money but hours, and three sciences generate three sets of homework on top of a long school run. That is why most of this page argues for buying the shared layer once rather than buying three weekly tutors: scientific calculation, command terms, data handling and practical reasoning are examined in effectively the same way across all three subjects, so one block lifts three grades and leaves the week breathable.

subjects.name: Biology, separate science
subjects.description: Recall volume plus command-term precision. Describe, explain and suggest want different answers, and a knowledgeable student writing the wrong one scores low. Experimental design and data-interpretation questions reward structured weekly practice over re-reading notes.

subjects.name: Chemistry, separate science

subjects.name: Physics, separate science
subjects.description: Precise definitions, units carried through every step, and rearranging a formula under pressure. Electricity, waves and energy transfer recur as weak topics. Graph work and reading instruments to a justified precision are examined directly.

subjects.description: All three disciplines in one qualification with reduced content in each, awarding two grades. Teaching separate-science depth to a coordinated student spends sessions on content that will not be examined, which is a specific and common mismatch.

subjects.name: Combined Science
subjects.description: A single grade across all three disciplines at further reduced depth. Often misidentified as triple award by a new tutor, because the school may still timetable three teachers and three sets of lessons regardless of the entry.

subjects.name: The Alternative to Practical paper
subjects.description: A written paper assessing experimental understanding rather than bench skill. Taught last in most schools and where the most marks sit relative to preparation effort, which makes it the single most efficient thing a three-science family can target.

subjects.name: Assessed laboratory work
subjects.levels: Where the school enters that route
subjects.description: Bench technique taught and assessed at school, which no tutor replaces. What one-to-one work contributes is prediction, anomaly handling, simple uncertainty treatment and writing up to the expected standard, which is still a real share of the credit.

subjects.name: Scientific calculation
subjects.description: Rearrangement, units, standard form and percentage work. The clearest shared weakness: it appears in chemistry stoichiometry, physics formulae and biology data questions alike, so fixing it once improves three grades.

subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest, compare and evaluate each want a different structure, and the distinction decides more marks than content recall does. Rarely taught explicitly because departments are busy covering content.

subjects.name: Data handling and graph work
subjects.description: Tables with correct headings and units, plotting, lines of best fit, reading values back and stating whether data supports a conclusion. Transfers across all three sciences at once, which makes it efficient to teach.

sections.heading: The practical assessment route, and why it decides what to prepare
paragraphs: This is the question to put to the school office first, and it is the one almost no family asks. How is the practical component assessed in each science: by a written Alternative to Practical paper, or by assessed laboratory work? The answer changes where the recoverable marks sit and therefore what a tutor should spend sessions on.

On a written route, the whole assessed task is a document — and that is excellent news for one-to-one online work, because the entire exercise is reading, annotating and marking a document together. What it tests is specific: reading a measuring instrument to a precision the instrument justifies, recognising that a described method cannot answer its question, identifying which variable needed controlling and was not, constructing a results table with correct headings and units, plotting points and drawing a line of best fit, reading a value back from the graph and saying what it means, and judging whether a stated conclusion is supported by the data shown.

On a laboratory route, the assessed technique happens at school and no tutor substitutes for it. That limitation is real and we state it rather than working around it. What one-to-one work adds is everything surrounding the bench: predicting what the experiment should produce before it runs, deciding what to do with an anomalous result rather than silently dropping it, calculating a simple percentage uncertainty from the apparatus and judging whether the effect exceeds it, and writing up so the assessment criteria are actually addressed.

The written papers in both cases also carry experimental questions that ask a student to evaluate a method rather than perform one, which is examinable reasoning and the same skill set. The table sets out the routes and what each means for preparation.

sections.heading: Which of the three sciences should you work on first?
paragraphs: In a triple-award household the honest answer is almost never all of them, so the choice matters. And the subject a student names is frequently not the subject where marks are most recoverable, which is why this decision should rest on a diagnostic rather than on a preference.

Students name the science they dislike or find most confusing. That is real information about how they feel and poor information about where a grade can move. The subject with the best return per hour is usually the one where content is nearly there and only the technique is missing — where a student understands the material and loses marks on command terms, on unshown method, or on data questions. Those faults move in weeks. A subject where a year of content is genuinely absent does not move in a term, whatever anybody sells you.

There are diagnostic signals for each. In chemistry, if multi-step conversions fail under time pressure, that is a quantitative fault and inexpensive to fix. In physics, if definitions are loose and units get dropped, that is technique. In biology, if answers are knowledgeable and the wrong shape, that is command terms, and it is the cheapest grade movement available in the subject. Conversely, a student who cannot explain a basic mechanism in chemistry or cannot rearrange a formula at all in physics is showing a content or foundation gap that needs more time than a final term provides.

The table sets out the signals against what they mean and what the work is. Read it alongside a marked paper rather than a report, because a report grade cannot distinguish a technique fault from a content gap and the whole decision rests on that distinction.

sections.heading: The shared layer: what all three sciences examine identically
paragraphs: This is the most efficient purchase available to a Town Square three-science family, and almost nobody sells it because it is a smaller sale than three weekly tutors.

Four things are examined in effectively the same way across biology, chemistry and physics. Scientific calculation: rearranging a formula, carrying units through a multi-step calculation, standard form at speed, percentage work. Command terms: state, describe, explain, suggest, compare and evaluate each demanding a different structure of answer. Data handling: tables with correct headings and units, plotting, lines of best fit, reading values back, judging whether data supports a conclusion. And practical-paper reasoning, which on a written route is an entire paper and on a laboratory route still appears in theory-paper experimental questions.

Because those are shared, a six to ten session block aimed at them lifts three grades rather than one. The arithmetic is straightforward: at published mid-band Dubai rates, three separate weekly science tutors run to roughly AED 1,800-3,600 a month, while a single shared block occupies one slot and is finished with a defined endpoint. For most families the sensible sequence is the shared block first, then one science weekly if the diagnostic still warrants it.

It also solves the week problem. Three weekly sessions plus the homework three sciences generate plus a long Al Qudra Road school run leaves a student no independent study time, and independent practice is where science grades are actually made. A shared block plus one weekly subject leaves the week breathable, which is a condition of any of it working.

sections.heading: The entry route still has to be established
paragraphs: Even once the practical route is known, the entry decides how much content is examined, and it is not visible from the timetable. A student can have three science teachers and three sets of lessons and still be entered for a single coordinated qualification.

Separate sciences, the triple-award route, means biology, chemistry and physics as independent qualifications with three grades, each covering the full syllabus — Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625, or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Cambridge Coordinated Sciences 0654 covers all three disciplines in one double-award qualification with reduced content in each, awarding two grades. Cambridge Combined Science 0653 is the single-award version at further reduced depth, awarding one.

The mismatch this creates is concrete. A tutor assuming triple award and teaching separate-science depth to a coordinated student spends sessions on content that will not be examined. A tutor assuming coordinated and teaching reduced depth to a triple-award student leaves the top of each syllabus uncovered. Both look entirely satisfactory week to week, and neither becomes visible until a paper arrives.

The entry also has a post-16 consequence families learn latest. A Level sciences and IB Higher Level sciences generally expect separate-science grades at a good standard, so the coordinated route can narrow which options are straightforwardly available at sixteen. If a chemistry-requiring or physics-requiring degree is anywhere in view, that decision in Year 9 or Year 10 matters more than any individual grade does. Ask the school what would be required to change entry route, and by when, because the answer is usually a date rather than a refusal.

Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, and budget online tutoring at AED 33-65 an hour, Tutopiya at AED 33-52 and EdFlik at AED 45-65. All of those were read from provider pages in October 2026. The band matters less than one question asked inside it: only a tutor who can tell you what an alternative-to-practical paper demands that a practical-endorsement route does not is being paid to prepare the papers your child will actually sit.

For a three-science household the monthly multiple is the number that matters, and it is the reason the shared-skills block exists. Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 a month for one weekly hour at the budget band, AED 600-1,200 mid-tier and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Multiply by three for three separate weekly tutors and the mid band alone reaches AED 1,800-3,600 a month, for an arrangement that also consumes the student's entire week.

There is a quieter cost too. Paying specialist rates for separate-science depth when the child is entered for coordinated sciences is paying for content that will not be examined, and paying for the wrong practical route's preparation is paying for a paper the student will not sit. Neither is visible on an invoice, and both are prevented by one email before the first session.

Every figure belongs to the provider named beside it.
