sections.heading: The June series, the November route, and the series not available here
paragraphs: A correction first, because it circulates among UAE parents constantly and acting on it costs a term. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. If anybody has told you a March resit is available for your child, they are describing another country's provision.

The part of the Cambridge calendar that catches a separate-science candidate is the zone rather than the series. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Three separate sciences means six or more science papers sitting inside that timetable, so there are six or more opportunities to read the wrong zone's version, and a Town Square family whose child travels out to a campus in another community cannot infer the zone from where they live. Ask the school which zone it sits in rather than downloading a timetable found by search. The series themselves are settled: Cambridge runs its International GCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.

On the Pearson side, the question a three-science family actually needs answered is when a result lands rather than when a paper is sat. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. A November entry returns its result in January: the November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026, late enough to matter for a few post-16 deadlines and early enough for most of them. A summer entry returns in August, with June 2026 results reaching centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. The sitting window itself is autumn, the November 2026 final timetable having run from late October to 19 November 2026, which means the revision block for one re-entered science falls across the first term of the following school year and competes with that year's work. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, so work from the live official PDF rather than any date restated on a tutoring site.

For a three-science family the November route is strategically useful rather than a consolation prize. A student who did well in two sciences and poorly in one re-enters that single subject, works a narrow fixed-scope block over the summer and first term, and has a January result in time to update post-16 applications. That is a better outcome than attempting to lift three grades simultaneously in the spring of Year 11, and it costs considerably less.

sections.heading: Is the science tutor you find permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: The heading asks a question, and it is one you can check rather than one you have to take on trust. Private tuition here is a permitted activity rather than an unregulated one, and most parents have never been told. The permit a science tutor needs was created by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. On MoHRE's own system the service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Because it costs nothing and takes two working days, lacking one is a choice rather than an obstacle. Eligibility is wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, and Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the amounts, so any figure circulating informally should be disregarded.

The permit's code of conduct bars a tutor from serving students affiliated with their own school, and press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes the same prohibition for Abu Dhabi school staff. In science this closes off the arrangement families most want in a specific way: the person who knows exactly which practical route your child's department entered is your child's own science teacher, and that is the one person who may not be engaged privately.

One further distinction, because Town Square sits close enough to several tuition centres that a parent will be offered premises and sometimes a lab bench. An individual needs the MoHRE permit. An organisation running tutoring from premises anywhere in Dubai needs something else entirely: a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That renewal date is worth asking about, because a centre that lets it lapse part-way through a series is a centre your child loses in the middle of a practical block. IB Gram is in neither position. We hold no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership, claim none, and have no UAE office or centre.

sections.heading: What we will not claim about science grades
paragraphs: No guarantee of a grade, a tier change or an improvement in any of the three sciences, and no suggestion that tutoring is required for Ministry of Education equivalency, university admission or school progression. That last point is a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process, and it is worth noticing whenever anybody makes it.

No statistics without a sample size, a date and a method, which in practice means none. No average science grades achieved by students we have taught, no percentage improved, no satisfaction figure, no self-generated star rating. Competitors publish such numbers routinely, sometimes in two conflicting versions on the same page, and almost never state how any of them was produced. Self-asserted review markup also breaches Google's structured-data policy.

No awarding-body material hosted or supplied. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson; we cite and link them rather than distributing them, and a provider charging a materials fee for them deserves a question. No examiner descriptions either, because current examiner status is not something we can evidence.

And no three-tutor recommendation where a shared block plus one weekly subject would serve better, even though three sessions is a larger sale. What we will do instead is diagnose all three sciences, name the one with the most movement per hour, recommend the shared layer where it is better value, and tell you plainly when three grades cannot all be lifted in the time remaining.

faqs.question: How do I find out how my child's science practicals are assessed?
faqs.answer: Ask the school office directly, per science. The two broad possibilities are a written Alternative to Practical paper, used on many Cambridge entries, or assessed laboratory work at school. Almost no family has been told which, and it matters because the answer changes where the recoverable marks sit. On a written route the whole assessed task is a document, which responds directly to one-to-one work. On a laboratory route the assessed technique happens at school and no tutor substitutes for it.

faqs.question: What skills does the written practical paper put marks on?
faqs.answer: Experimental understanding on paper rather than handling skill. Reading a measuring instrument to a precision the instrument justifies. Recognising that a described method cannot answer the question it was set. Identifying which variable needed controlling and was not. Building a results table with correct headings and units. Plotting points, drawing a line of best fit, reading a value back and saying what it means. Judging whether a stated conclusion is supported by the data shown. All of it is teachable one-to-one, and it is taught last in most schools.

faqs.question: Which science should a Town Square family work on first?
faqs.answer: The one with the most movement available per hour, which is frequently not the one the student complains about. Students name the science they dislike; a marked paper shows where marks are recoverable. A technique fault — knowledgeable answers in the wrong shape, right answers with no working, data questions guessed — moves in weeks. A genuine content gap, where a student cannot explain a basic process or rearrange a formula at all, does not move in a final term whatever anybody sells you.

faqs.question: Is it worth buying one block for all three sciences?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is what we recommend most often. Four things are examined effectively identically across biology, chemistry and physics: scientific calculation, command terms, data handling and practical-paper reasoning. A six to ten session block aimed at those lifts three grades rather than one, occupies a single slot in the week, and finishes with a defined endpoint. Three separate weekly tutors reach roughly AED 1,800-3,600 a month at published mid-band rates and consume the student's whole week.

faqs.question: Why does buying three science tutors usually backfire?
faqs.answer: Because of the week rather than the money, though the money is real too. Three weekly sessions plus the homework three sciences generate plus a long Al Qudra Road school run leaves a student no independent study time — and independent practice is where science grades are actually made. The student ends up with shallow coverage of all three subjects and too little energy to use any of it. A shared block plus one weekly science leaves the week breathable, which is a condition of any of it working.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether Town Square schools entered triple or coordinated science?
faqs.answer: Triple award means biology, chemistry and physics as three independent qualifications covering their full syllabuses, awarding three grades — Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625, or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Cambridge Coordinated Sciences 0654 covers all three disciplines in one double-award qualification with reduced content, awarding two grades. Combined Science 0653 is a single-award version at further reduced depth. The timetable does not reveal which: a student can have three science teachers and be entered for one qualification.

faqs.question: Does the science entry route affect A Level or IB options later?
faqs.answer: It can, and this is the consequence families learn latest. A Level sciences and IB Higher Level sciences generally expect separate-science grades at a good standard, so the coordinated or combined route can narrow which post-16 options are straightforwardly available. Check the published entry requirements of the schools and programmes your child may move into rather than relying on general advice. If a chemistry-requiring or physics-requiring degree is in view, the Year 9 entry decision matters more than any single grade.

faqs.question: Which syllabus codes should I ask the school for?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge separate sciences: 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics. For Cambridge combined routes: 0654 Coordinated Sciences double award or 0653 Combined Science single award. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE: 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1. Ask per subject rather than assuming one answer covers everything, because Dubai departments make independent board decisions and a household can genuinely have biology on one board and physics on another. Ask for the practical route in the same email.

faqs.question: Can online tutoring help if the school assesses practicals in the lab?
faqs.answer: Partly, and we are specific about which part. Bench technique — handling, precision, following a method — is taught and assessed at school and no tutor replaces it, in person or online. What one-to-one work adds is everything around the bench: predicting what the experiment should produce before it runs, deciding what to do with an anomalous result rather than dropping it silently, calculating percentage uncertainty from the apparatus and judging whether the effect exceeds it, and writing up so the criteria are addressed.

faqs.question: Is there a science tutor near Town Square who knows our route?
faqs.answer: General science tutors, plenty. Tutors who have prepared students for your specific practical component and entry route, far fewer, and the drive narrows the pool before any of that is considered. Dubai's tutoring supply clusters around the older school corridors rather than the newer Dubailand communities, and Town Square is recently settled so the neighbour network that vets tutors elsewhere is thin. Online matching removes the proximity filter, which was never the variable that decided the marks.

faqs.question: What should a three-science family in Town Square expect to spend?
faqs.answer: At published Dubai rates read in October 2026, one weekly hour runs AED 240-600 a month at the budget band, AED 600-1,200 mid-tier and AED 1,000-2,000 or more at the specialist exam-year band. For three separate weekly tutors, multiply: AED 720-1,800, AED 1,800-3,600 and AED 3,000-6,000 or more respectively. Those are the providers' published figures, not ours. The shared-skills block occupies one slot and covers all three, which is why we recommend it before anything else.

faqs.question: Can my child resit one science in February or March?
faqs.answer: Not in the UAE. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, and UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The belief circulates widely here and planning around it costs a term, so confirm with your school. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For a three-science family the November route is genuinely strategic: re-enter the single weak subject, work a narrow block over the summer and first term, and the January result still updates post-16 applications.

faqs.question: My child is weak in all three sciences after mocks. What now?
faqs.answer: Triage, honestly. Three grades cannot all be lifted substantially in a final term, and a provider implying otherwise is selling rather than advising. After a diagnostic we would normally propose the shared layer first — calculation, command terms, data handling, practical-paper reasoning — because it touches all three at once, plus focused weekly work on whichever single science shows the most movement per hour. For another subject, a November entry with a narrow summer block is frequently the better outcome.

faqs.question: Does a science tutor in Dubai need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Any individual charging for private tuition in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE listing a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website or e-services. Eligibility covers school and sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Since it costs nothing and takes two days, lacking one is a choice. Ask to see it and verify with MoHRE.

faqs.question: Could we just ask my child's own science teacher to tutor them?
faqs.answer: No, and in science this is particularly frustrating, because the person who knows exactly which practical route and entry the department chose is precisely the person who may not be engaged privately. The MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars a tutor from serving students affiliated with their own school, and press reporting on Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules describes the same prohibition there. What you can do is ask the department for additional support within school, naming the component specifically rather than asking generally.

intro.heading: Three sciences, two boards, and a tiering decision nobody explains
paragraphs: IGCSE Science is not one thing. A Year 10 student in Dubai might be sitting three separate sciences, each with its own syllabus code and its own set of papers. Or they might be sitting Co-ordinated Sciences as a double award, which compresses the three into two GCSE-equivalent grades. Or Combined Science as a single award. Or Pearson Edexcel's Science Double Award, which is structured differently again. The first question any competent tutor should ask is which of those your child is entered for, and the honest answer from many parents is that nobody has told them.

The syllabus code settles it. Cambridge IGCSE Physics is 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 and Combined Science 0653. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics is 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1 and Science Double Award 4SD0. Those codes appear on the statement of entry and on every past paper. Across an entire cluster of competing pages for these searches, exactly one syllabus code appears anywhere, which tells you how specific the advice on offer generally is. Ask the school office for the codes if the statement of entry is not to hand; it takes one email and it prevents a term of misdirected revision.

The second thing that matters more than anything else on this page is tiering. Cambridge single sciences are entered at either Core or Extended. A Core entry is assessed for grades C to G. An Extended entry is assessed for grades A* to E. That means a Core entry places a hard ceiling on the grade before the student has sat anything, and a student moved down to Core in Year 11 to protect a pass has given up the top four grades in exchange. Whether that trade is right depends on the student, but it should be a decision taken with the numbers in front of you rather than by default.

Umm Al Sheif has no secondary school inside its boundary. Students here commute to the Jumeirah, Al Safa, Al Sufouh and Al Barsha schools, so the board, the tier, the practical route and the internal deadlines all belong to a school elsewhere. A tutor's usefulness depends on knowing those, not on living nearby. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Teaching for Umm Al Sheif students is delivered one-to-one over live video.

The rest of this page is the detail: how the two boards structure the same science differently, what the Core and Extended decision actually costs, what Paper 5 and Paper 6 demand and what Edexcel does instead of either, the mark-scheme traps common to all three sciences, a past-paper method that serves three subjects at once, the Dubai rate bands with their published sources, and the June and November series read backwards from the paper.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-umm-al-shei.programmesIntro: IGCSE sciences sit in the middle of a long sequence, and the decisions taken at 14 shape what is possible at 18. These are the stages an Umm Al Sheif family is working through and what each needs from a tutor.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10-11
programmes.description: Two years, three sciences or one double award, and a board that the school chooses rather than the family. Cambridge single sciences weight the multiple-choice paper at 30%, the theory paper at 50% and the practical component at 20%. Pearson Edexcel splits its sciences across two written papers of unequal length and assesses practical skills inside them. Tiering applies to the Cambridge route and is the single most consequential decision of the two years.
programmes.countryNote: Umm Al Sheif students sit IGCSE sciences at the Jumeirah, Al Safa and Al Sufouh schools, most of which run the British curriculum and enter candidates through a Dubai examination centre. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone timetable must be used, because it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper after reading the wrong version.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, Years 7-9
programmes.description: The three years before the syllabus starts, and the place where most IGCSE science problems are created. The specific things that matter later are unit handling, rearranging a formula with three variables, reading a scale to a sensible precision, and the difference between a prediction and a conclusion. None of these are hard; all of them are assumed from the first week of Year 10.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Umm Al Sheif student is in Year 9 and already struggling with science, the efficient intervention is here rather than in Year 10. A term of work on algebraic rearrangement and measurement precision in Year 9 removes the problem that otherwise recurs in every calculation question for two years and shows up as a tiering conversation in Year 11.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma, Years 12-13
programmes.description: What the IGCSE grades buy. A Level sciences and IB Diploma Higher Level sciences both normally expect a strong Extended-tier IGCSE grade in the same subject, which is the practical reason the tiering decision matters: a Core entry capped at C may close the Higher Level route before the student has chosen subjects. Schools set their own entry requirements and they differ.
programmes.countryNote: In this part of Dubai a student may do IGCSE at one school and move for sixth form, and the receiving school's entry requirement is the one that governs. Asking what grade the intended post-16 route requires, before the tier is confirmed in Year 11, is the most useful question a parent in Umm Al Sheif can put to the school.

programmes.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
programmes.ageRange: All year groups in Dubai private schools
programmes.description: These run alongside whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for. They are not optional and they occupy real timetable hours. Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies must be taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, and combined classes are prohibited.
programmes.countryNote: The reason this belongs on a science page is arithmetic. A Year 11 student in Dubai carries three sciences, mathematics, English, the mandatory subjects and usually two options. The week is full before any tutoring is added, which is why we ask for the actual timetable before proposing a session count rather than recommending a number that sounds reassuring.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-umm-al-shei.subjectsIntro: IGCSE science tutoring is rarely for one subject alone. These are the codes we teach and what each one is actually assessed on, because the paper structure differs more between boards than most parents are told.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Multiple choice at 30%, theory at 50%, practical at 20%. Marks go missing in the required practical techniques, in formula rearrangement, and in questions asking for an explanation where a student supplies a description. Electricity and magnetism is the topic Umm Al Sheif students most often name as the point where the subject stopped making sense.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Same 30-50-20 structure. The recurring losses are state symbols omitted from equations, moles treated as a formula rather than a counting unit, and qualitative analysis tests learned as a list without the reasoning. Organic chemistry at Extended tier is where the gap between Core and Extended becomes most visible.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Terminology volume is the challenge rather than the mathematics. The subject punishes imprecise language: diffusion described without a concentration gradient, or osmosis described without water potential, scores nothing. Required practical work on enzymes and on osmosis appears reliably in the practical component.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: The three sciences compressed into a double award with two grades. Content breadth is slightly reduced but the paper structure is the same, and students often underestimate it because the word co-ordinated sounds easier than separate. It is not; it is three subjects' worth of concepts examined in two grades' worth of papers.

subjects.name: Combined Science (Cambridge 0653)
subjects.description: The single-award route, producing one grade for all three sciences. Suitable where a student is not continuing with science post-16 and the timetable is full. Worth checking against post-16 entry requirements before committing, because some sixth forms will not accept it for an A Level science.

subjects.name: Physics (Pearson Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Two written papers of unequal length rather than Cambridge's three-component structure, with no separate practical examination. Practical skills are assessed inside the written papers, which changes revision substantially: a student cannot treat practical technique as a separate paper to prepare for near the end.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Pearson Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Also two written papers with practical skills assessed within them. Edexcel's question style leans more heavily on extended written answers than Cambridge's, so the same student can be well prepared on content and badly prepared on the format. Past papers from the correct board are not optional.

subjects.name: Biology (Pearson Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: Two written papers, practical skills assessed within them. The specification detail differs from Cambridge in places, so a student using the wrong board's revision guide will learn material that is not examined and miss material that is. Checking the code on the statement of entry prevents a term of misdirected work.

subjects.name: Science Double Award (Pearson Edexcel 4SD0)
subjects.description: Edexcel's equivalent of Co-ordinated Sciences, producing two grades. Structured around separate biology, chemistry and physics papers, so the revision load is best organised by subject rather than by paper. A useful route where a student needs two science grades without three subjects' worth of timetable.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Included because science grades depend on it. A student who cannot rearrange a formula with three variables or handle standard form will lose marks in Physics and Chemistry regardless of how well they understand the science. Repairing the mathematics often raises two or three subject grades at once.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-umm-al-shei.modesIntro: Three ways an IGCSE science student in Umm Al Sheif can work with us, all over live video. Which fits depends on whether the problem is one subject, all three, or the paper technique that affects all of them at once.

modes.title: Single-subject weekly sessions
modes.description: One science, one fixed slot a week, following the school's teaching order. This is the right mode when one subject is clearly behind the other two, which is the most common pattern. Sessions are 60 minutes at this level, the past-paper questions are set from the correct syllabus code, and the whiteboard file is saved.
bullets: Lesson tied to the school's current unit rather than a generic sequence
Questions pulled from the right board's papers, not a mix
Marking against the published scheme so the student sees each mark
A short note after each session naming the specific error type

modes.title: Three-science rotation
modes.description: A rota across Physics, Chemistry and Biology, usually two sessions a week with the third subject picked up in alternate weeks. Suited to a Year 10 student who is broadly behind rather than failing in one place, and it allows shared skills such as graph work and formula rearrangement to be taught once and applied three times.
bullets: Shared skills taught once: units, rearrangement, graphs, precision
Subject-specific sessions rotated against the school's test calendar
Priority shifted to whichever subject has the nearer assessment
A single plan rather than three unconnected tutors

modes.title: Paper-technique block before the series
modes.description: A compressed run in the weeks before June or November, built on timed papers rather than new content. The multiple-choice paper, the theory paper and the practical component are drilled separately because they fail for different reasons, and command-term work is done once for all three sciences.
bullets: Multiple choice under full time pressure, then error-pattern analysis

Command-term drill: state, describe, explain, suggest, calculate

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel for the same science
paragraphs: The two boards examine the same science in structurally different ways, and a student revising from the wrong board's material will be well prepared for an examination they are not sitting. This is the most common avoidable error in IGCSE science preparation, and it is entirely preventable: the syllabus code is printed on the statement of entry.

Cambridge single sciences use three components. A multiple-choice paper worth 30%, a theory paper worth 50%, and a practical component worth 20% which is sat either as a laboratory practical test or as a written alternative. The tier, Core or Extended, determines which version of the multiple-choice and theory papers the student sits and therefore which grades are available.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences use two written papers of unequal length with no separate practical examination. Practical skills are assessed inside those written papers. That difference is larger in practice than it sounds, because it removes the option of leaving practical technique until a dedicated revision block near the end: with Edexcel it has to be embedded in ordinary topic revision from the start.

Question style differs too. Edexcel leans more heavily on extended written responses; Cambridge spreads marks across a greater number of shorter items. A student who is strong on content and weak on sustained written explanation will find Edexcel harder than Cambridge at the same level of understanding, and the fix is format practice rather than more content. The practical instruction is simple: find the code, then buy or download only that board's past papers and specification, and ignore everything else.

sections.heading: Core and Extended: the decision that caps the grade
paragraphs: On the Cambridge route, every single science is entered at either Core or Extended. A Core entry is assessed for grades C to G. An Extended entry is assessed for grades A* to E. The consequence is blunt: a Core candidate cannot be awarded a B, an A or an A*, no matter how well they perform, because those grades are not available on the papers they sat.

Schools move students between tiers for defensible reasons. A student who is genuinely at risk of failing an Extended entry may be better served by a secure C on Core than by an E or a U on Extended. That is a real trade and sometimes the right one. What makes it a problem is when it happens quietly, as a departmental default in Year 11, without the family being shown what is being given up.

The questions a parent in Umm Al Sheif should ask are specific. Which tier is my child currently entered for, in each science separately? What does the intended post-16 route require? When is the last date the entry can be changed? And what would need to improve, in which topics, for an Extended entry to be viable? A school can answer all four, and the answers turn a vague worry into a plan.

Where the tier is already set at Core and the post-16 route needs better, the useful work is topic-specific rather than general. The Extended-only content in each science is identifiable: it is marked as supplement material in the syllabus. A student working towards a tier change needs that content plus the harder question styles, which is a different programme from general science support.

sections.heading: The practical component, and what it actually tests
paragraphs: On the Cambridge route the practical component is 20% of each single science, and it is sat either as a laboratory practical test or as a written paper that substitutes for it. Schools choose which, and the choice changes what a student needs to practise. A laboratory test requires apparatus handling under time pressure. A written alternative requires describing apparatus handling in words, which is a different skill and in some ways a harder one.

What both versions test is the same underlying set of ideas: identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables; choosing a measuring instrument with appropriate precision; recognising sources of error and distinguishing random from systematic; reading and plotting data correctly; and drawing a conclusion that the data supports. None of that requires a laboratory to teach. All of it can be taught from a student's own data and from past-paper practical questions.

Pearson Edexcel takes a different route and assesses practical skills inside the written papers. This removes the separate component and distributes the same skills across ordinary topic questions. It also removes the possibility of a late dedicated practical revision block, which is how students on the Cambridge route often recover that 20%. With Edexcel, practical reasoning has to be built into topic revision from the beginning.

The recurring losses in practical questions are consistent across all three sciences and both boards. Students describe what they did rather than why. They name a variable without saying how it was controlled. They quote a reading to a precision the instrument does not support. And they offer improvements that amount to being more careful, where the scheme wants a change to the method or the apparatus.
bullets: Variables named and the method of control stated, not just listed
Instrument precision matched to the quantity being measured
Random error distinguished from systematic error, with a reason
Improvements expressed as method or apparatus changes, not as taking more care
Conclusions limited to what the data actually supports

sections.heading: Mark-scheme traps that cost marks in all three sciences
paragraphs: Mark schemes reward particular wording, and a student who knows the science without knowing the scheme loses marks that more content revision will never recover. The traps below appear across Physics, Chemistry and Biology, which means fixing them once pays three times.

Command terms come first. State wants an answer with no working. Describe wants what happens. Explain wants why, with a cause named. Suggest wants a plausible answer applied to an unfamiliar context. Calculate wants the working shown. Students who describe when asked to explain write correct science and earn nothing for it, and this is the fastest-paying correction available in the final weeks.

Units and precision come second. A numerical answer without a unit is usually incomplete, and a correct calculation rounded mid-working or quoted to the full calculator display loses the precision mark. The rule is to carry full precision through and round once at the end, to the precision of the least precise measurement in the question.

Subject-specific traps follow the same pattern. In Chemistry, state symbols omitted from equations. In Biology, a process named without its driving mechanism, such as diffusion described with no reference to a concentration gradient. In Physics, a formula quoted without rearranging it correctly, or a graph gradient read as a number with no physical interpretation attached. Each of these is a habit rather than a gap, and habits respond quickly to deliberate practice. A single session spent reading a marked script against the published scheme, mark by mark, usually changes more behaviour than a fortnight of further content revision.

sections.heading: A past-paper method that serves three sciences at once
paragraphs: Past papers are the most recommended and least planned part of IGCSE revision. Working through them in date order and marking them loosely produces a score and very little change. The version that works is organised by skill, uses the correct board's papers, and attaches analysis to every attempt.

Begin with topic question sets rather than whole papers, pulled from the correct syllabus code and done untimed with the specification open. Mark them against the published scheme line by line, including the parts the student got right, because seeing where a mark was awarded teaches the scheme as effectively as seeing where one was lost. The output of this stage is a short list of recurring error types, not a percentage.

Then separate the components. The multiple-choice paper is practised under full time pressure, because its failure mode is pacing. The theory paper is practised in sections with the longer questions planned on paper before being written, because its failure mode is structure. The practical component is practised on its own, because its failure mode is vocabulary. Treating all three as one block of revision conceals which is actually costing the grade.

Only then move to whole papers, and only two or three of them, with analysis between. A paper sat and analysed is worth more than three sat consecutively. For a student taking three sciences, the shared skills found in the first stage are the highest-value target: units, rearrangement, graph interpretation and command terms appear in all three papers, so one session on each repairs marks in three subjects.

sections.heading: What IGCSE science tuition costs in Dubai
paragraphs: Three sciences changes the cost conversation, because the natural instinct is to book three tutors and the natural consequence is a bill nobody can sustain. The useful first question is whether the problem is actually three subject problems or one shared skill problem showing up three times, because the second is much cheaper to fix.

The Dubai market bands as follows. Budget online tuition is published at AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. A qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to AED 300, and Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate quoting AED 200 to AED 450 upwards. Premium named tutors reach AED 500 to AED 650, with BartyED at AED 650.

In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 including travel, with Bestimate at AED 180 to AED 350. Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle. Advertised packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those figures belong to the providers named beside them.

A note on context worth having. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. For a family already paying Dubai school fees, tutoring is an additional line on top of a fixed one, which is why we would rather establish what is actually needed in a free trial lesson than sell a three-subject package by default.

sections.heading: Online lessons against a tutor driving to Umm Al Sheif
paragraphs: In-home tutoring earns its premium in some situations and it is worth saying which. A younger child concentrates better with an adult present. A student who will not start work without supervision benefits from someone in the room. Nothing needs setting up. Where supervision is the product being bought, in-home is a reasonable purchase.

IGCSE science is a different case because the requirement is specific. You need a tutor who knows whether your child sits 0625 or 4PH1, which tier they are entered for, and whether the practical component is a laboratory test or a written alternative. Requiring that person to also live within a short drive of Umm Al Sheif and be free on a weekday afternoon shrinks the available pool sharply, and the specificity is what gets lost.

The format differences are modest and some favour video. Working is written on a shared whiteboard that is saved and can be revisited before a test, which a page in an exercise book cannot be. Past-paper scripts are annotated on screen with the mark scheme beside them, so the student watches each mark being awarded or withheld. Graph work is done on screen where the plotting can be corrected point by point. A document camera handles anything on paper.

To be explicit, because this market is not: IB Gram does not make home visits in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run only in India. Every IGCSE science lesson for an Umm Al Sheif family is one-to-one over live video, and the trial lesson exists so the format can be tested on your own child before any commitment.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards
paragraphs: Almost nothing in this market is written about examination sessions, which is odd, because the calendar decides whether help arrives in time to be useful. The method is to count backwards from the paper. Every task has a latest useful date, and most of those dates fall months earlier than families expect.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series. UAE candidates sit those two. Cambridge also operates a February and March series, but it is offered to India only, so it is not a route available from Dubai and should be ignored in any Dubai planning. Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct version of the timetable for the zone must be used, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and in November. Backward-looking dates make the pattern checkable: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That January arrival is the reason a November resit is a slow route, since the result lands most of a term after the paper.

Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and they can be revised, so the practical instruction is to open the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than relying on any restatement, including the figures above. For a Year 11 student, the two dates that matter most are the school's final entry deadline, after which the tier cannot be changed, and the mock window, which is the last honest diagnostic before the real paper.

sections.heading: KHDA, the regulator map and the Year 11 timetable squeeze
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the emirate regulator's role goes beyond inspection.

Scale for context: Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with UK programmes at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. Seven new private schools were announced for the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places. Six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%.

An inspection band is context rather than a prediction for one student. A school rated Outstanding can still have a Year 11 Chemistry set in which several students are losing marks on state symbols. Read the subject-level commentary in the inspection report if you want something that bears on a decision about science tutoring.

The timetable point is the one that affects planning most directly. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed for, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Separate classes are required for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. A Year 11 student with three sciences, mathematics, English, the mandatory subjects and two options has a full week before any tutoring is added, which is why we ask for the real timetable before recommending a session count.

process.title: Send the syllabus codes and the tier
process.description: The statement of entry carries both. Physics 0625 Extended, Chemistry 0620 Core, Biology 0610 Extended tells us exactly what to teach and what grades are in play. Without the codes a tutor guesses the board, and a term of practice from the wrong board's papers is a real and common waste.

process.title: A free trial lesson used as a diagnostic
process.description: The trial is a working session. The tutor sets short questions across the sciences and watches where the reasoning breaks, then sends a written note. The common finding is that one shared skill, usually formula rearrangement or command terms, is costing marks in all three subjects.

process.title: Decide between one subject and a rotation
process.description: If one science is clearly behind, a single weekly session on it beats spreading time thinly. If all three are drifting, a rotation with shared-skill work is more efficient and cheaper. We say which we think applies and why, based on the trial rather than on what sells more hours.

process.title: Build the plan around the school's dates
process.description: We ask for the mock window, the final entry deadline and the school's internal assessment calendar, then sequence backwards. The entry deadline matters most because the tier cannot be changed after it, and a tier conversation is far easier to have before that date than after.

process.title: Weekly notes, and change the tutor if needed
process.description: Each session ends with a short written note on what was covered and what went wrong. If the match is not working after two or three sessions, say so and we move the student. Persisting with a poor fit costs weeks that the June series will not give back.

whyPoints.title: We teach to the code, not to the subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are both IGCSE Chemistry and they are not the same examination. We ask for the code before the first lesson and set practice from the correct board, which prevents the most common and most expensive preparation error in this qualification.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IGCSE Core and Extended, and does it matter?
faqs.answer: It matters more than almost anything else in the two years. On the Cambridge route each single science is entered at Core or Extended. A Core entry is assessed for grades C to G; an Extended entry for A* to E. A Core candidate cannot be awarded a B or above, because those grades are not available on the papers they sit. Schools sometimes move a student to Core to protect a pass, which can be the right call, but it should be a decision taken with the post-16 entry requirements in front of you. Ask which tier your child is entered for in each science separately, and the last date it can be changed.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel science?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry carries the syllabus code, and the code settles it. Cambridge Physics is 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 and Combined Science 0653. Pearson Edexcel Physics is 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1 and Science Double Award 4SD0. This is worth five minutes of your time, because the two boards structure the same science differently and a student revising from the wrong board's guide learns material that will not be examined while missing material that will. The school office can confirm the codes if the statement is not to hand.

faqs.question: If lessons are on video, how does my child prepare for the practical component?
faqs.answer: The apparatus work stays at school; the reasoning is what tutoring addresses. On the Cambridge route the practical component is 20% of each single science and is sat either as a laboratory test or as a written alternative, depending on what the school enters. Pearson Edexcel assesses practical skills inside its written papers instead. What is examined in all cases is variable identification and control, instrument precision, classifying errors as random or systematic, plotting and reading data, and proposing genuine method improvements. All of that is taught from past-paper questions and from the student's own recorded results.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science do students in Dubai struggle with most?
faqs.answer: Physics, most often, and usually for a mathematical reason rather than a physical one. A student who cannot confidently rearrange a formula with three variables or handle standard form will lose marks across the whole paper regardless of how well they understand the concepts. Chemistry comes second, where the mole concept learned as a formula rather than a counting unit undermines every calculation question. Biology is third and fails differently: not through mathematics but through imprecise language, where a process is named without the mechanism that drives it. The mathematical repair is usually the highest-value intervention because it lifts two subjects at once.

faqs.question: My child takes all three sciences. Do we need three separate tutors?
faqs.answer: Often not, and starting there is how families end up with an unsustainable bill. The first question is whether this is three subject problems or one shared skill problem appearing three times. Units, formula rearrangement, graph interpretation and command terms are assessed in all three sciences, so a single habit can cost marks across the whole set. Where the trial lesson shows that pattern, one tutor working on shared skills plus the weakest subject is both cheaper and faster. Where the sciences genuinely diverge, a rotation across two sessions a week usually works better than three separate weekly commitments.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE science exams held for students in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. Cambridge also operates a February and March series but it is offered to India only, so Dubai families should disregard it entirely in their planning. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone version of the timetable must be used, because it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper after reading the wrong one. Always open the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

faqs.question: How long does a November resit take to produce a result?
faqs.answer: Longer than most families expect, which is why it should be planned rather than assumed as a safety net. Taking Pearson's published pattern as the example: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. June results move faster, with June 2026 results reaching centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. A November entry therefore delivers its outcome most of a term after the paper, which can be too late for some sixth-form admission timelines. Check the receiving school's deadline before relying on it.

faqs.question: What does my child actually lose by being entered for Core?
faqs.answer: The top four grades. A Core entry is assessed for C to G, so B, A and A* are not available on the papers sat. Beyond the grade itself, the practical loss is in post-16 options: A Level sciences and IB Diploma Higher Level sciences usually expect a strong Extended-tier grade in the same subject, and a C from Core may not meet the requirement even though it is a pass. The Extended-only material is identifiable in the syllabus as supplement content, so a student working towards a tier change has a defined body of work rather than a vague instruction to improve.

faqs.question: Which mark-scheme habits cost the most marks across the sciences?
faqs.answer: Four, and all four are habits rather than knowledge gaps. Answering describe when the question says explain, which produces correct science that scores nothing. Omitting units from numerical answers. Rounding mid-calculation or quoting the full calculator display instead of rounding once at the end to the least precise measurement. And in Chemistry specifically, leaving state symbols off equations, which is the cheapest loss available in the subject. Because these appear in all three sciences, correcting them is the highest-return work in the final weeks before a series, ahead of any further content revision.

faqs.question: How should we use past papers so the time is not wasted?
faqs.answer: By skill rather than by date. Start with topic question sets from the correct syllabus code, untimed, with the specification open, marked against the published scheme line by line including the parts that were right. The output should be a named list of recurring errors, not a percentage. Then separate the components: multiple choice under full time because its failure mode is pacing, theory with the long answers planned first because its failure mode is structure, and practical questions on their own because their failure mode is vocabulary. Whole papers come last, two or three of them, with analysis between each.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE science tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures, each attributed to whoever published it. Budget online tuition runs AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. A qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. IGCSE and A Level specialists are published at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home one-to-one including travel is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle for weekly sessions.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class a reasonable option for three sciences?
faqs.answer: For broad coverage at a lower cost per head, often yes, and several centres sit along Al Wasl Road and in Al Barsha within reach of Umm Al Sheif. The trade-offs are specific. A group class works to the group's pace, so a student whose problem is one particular topic may sit through material they already hold. The class may teach to one board while your child sits the other. And the family travels, on a fixed timetable. Group classes suit a student who needs the whole syllabus covered again; one-to-one suits a student who needs one identified gap closed.

faqs.question: Does online teaching work for a 15-year-old who gets distracted easily?
faqs.answer: Honestly, it depends on the student, which is why the trial lesson exists. Some students focus better one-to-one on screen than in a room, because there is nowhere to look except the shared whiteboard and the tutor can see when attention goes. Others genuinely need an adult physically present, and for those students in-home tuition is the better product even at the higher market rate. We would rather you test the format on your own child in a free trial than take a general claim about effectiveness from a page like this one.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help if my child has already been moved down to Core?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the work splits into two questions. First, whether a move back to Extended is still possible, which depends on the school's final entry deadline and should be asked about in writing now rather than later. Second, what the best achievable outcome is on the current entry, since a secure C on Core is a real qualification and better than an E on Extended. Where a tier move is in play, the target is defined: the supplement content marked in the syllabus plus the harder Extended question styles. That is a specific programme rather than general science support.

faqs.question: Does the school's KHDA inspection rating tell me whether my child needs a tutor?
faqs.answer: Not really, and it is a poor proxy. Dubai's private schools are inspected by KHDA on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and a school in the top band can still have a Year 11 set where several students are losing marks on units and command terms. What is worth reading is the subject-level commentary inside the report, which sometimes names science attainment specifically. For a decision about tutoring, your child's own marked papers and the mock result are far better evidence than any whole-school band.

intro.heading: What is left of a school day, and which science marks live there
paragraphs: Science is the subject where the school holds something a tutor cannot replicate. Laboratories, equipment, a technician, a teacher watching twenty-eight students heat a liquid safely. That is real, and any page claiming otherwise is selling something. But it is also a much smaller part of the qualification than parents assume, and conflating practical science with the practical marks is how families in Umm Suqeim end up believing their child's science grade is out of reach in the evening.

Here is the division that matters. In Cambridge IGCSE Biology, Chemistry and Physics, the multiple-choice paper carries 30% of the grade, the theory paper carries 50%, and the practical component - either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper - carries 20%. Pearson's International GCSE sciences do it differently, assessing practical skills inside the written papers rather than in a separate component. In both systems, the marks awarded for practical work are awarded for written answers: identifying the independent variable, explaining why a result was repeated, labelling a table with units, reading a graph correctly, saying what the data does and does not support. None of that requires a bench.

Which is why the evening is where the science grade is actually decided. A student who gets home to Umm Suqeim at about 3:40pm after a 3:15pm release, eats, and has ninety usable minutes can do the single most valuable science task there is: take a marked past-paper question and work out why the mark scheme awarded three marks where they wrote four lines and got one. That is not laboratory work. It is writing, and it is teachable over live video.

This page is organised around that evening. It sets out which science route your child is on and what it costs them, the component structure for each board so you can see where the marks sit, what the alternative-to-practical paper rewards and why it is the most neglected fifth of the qualification, the specific topics where students in this part of Dubai lose marks, and a realistic plan for fitting science work into the hours between a school-run arrival and bedtime. It also explains why three sciences rarely means three tutors.

On delivery: IB Gram teaches Umm Suqeim students one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. For science specifically that matters less than for any other subject, because the work is written, the student's own paper is the material, and a shared screen is a better way to annotate an answer than a kitchen table. It also widens the pool, which in science matters at the edges: separate sciences at the top grades, and the handful of students in this area sitting a less common board, are the requests that a locally-bounded search fails to fill at all. Dropping the drive keeps those requests answerable, and keeps the whole of the evening window available to the lesson rather than to a journey.

sections.heading: Which science marks need a laboratory and which need an evening
paragraphs: An IGCSE science tutor in Umm Suqeim cannot give your child bench time, and should say so in the first conversation. What the school provides - equipment, supervision, the experience of actually doing an experiment badly and seeing why - is not replaceable. What the school frequently does not provide, because there is no time in a crowded scheme of work, is deliberate instruction in how practical work is written up for marks. That gap is where a tutor is most useful, and it is the opposite of what families expect.

The arithmetic makes the case. In Cambridge IGCSE Biology, Chemistry and Physics the multiple-choice paper carries 30%, the theory paper carries 50% and the practical component carries 20%. The practical component is either Paper 5, a practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative-to-practical paper, and in both cases the marks are awarded for written responses. Pearson's International GCSE sciences take a different route, assessing practical skills within the written papers rather than separately, which means the same written technique matters and there is no separate practical paper to revise.

So of the whole qualification, the portion that genuinely requires a laboratory is the hands-on experience that informs the writing - and even students who have done every practical in the scheme routinely lose those marks, because nobody showed them that 'repeat the experiment' earns a mark only when paired with a stated reason. Everything else is reading, reasoning and writing: command words, chains of explanation, calculations, graph interpretation, and the discipline of answering the question asked.

The practical conclusion for a family in Umm Suqeim is reassuring and slightly deflating. Your child's science grade is decided largely in the evenings, by work that happens on paper. The school is doing the part a tutor cannot do. The part the school has least room for - deliberate, slow, mark-scheme-level attention to how an answer is written - is exactly what one hour a week over live video is good for.

sections.heading: Three sciences, double award or single: the choice behind the timetable
paragraphs: The science route is usually chosen on an option form in Year 9, and usually framed as a matter of interest and workload. It is also a decision about what will be available at 16 and 18, and that half of it is rarely explained at the time. The table below sets out the routes with their real consequences, so a parent in Umm Suqeim can have the conversation with the school before the form goes in rather than after.

The practical difference between the routes is content volume against doors kept open. Three separate sciences is the heaviest load and the most conventional route into A Level sciences and into medicine, engineering and dentistry applications. Co-ordinated Sciences as a double award reduces content substantially and produces two grades, which suits a student carrying ten subjects or one whose strengths are elsewhere; whether it is accepted for A Level science entry varies between schools, so ask the specific school. Combined Science as a single award is lighter still and closes most A Level science routes.

Tiering sits on top of this. Cambridge tiers these specifications into Core and Extended, with Core papers graded C to G and Extended papers graded A* to E, and the entry is made by the school to the board's deadline. A student on a Core entry cannot be awarded a top grade regardless of performance or tuition, which is worth knowing in Year 10 rather than in February of Year 11.

Where tuition changes this decision rather than following it: a student who is capable of three sciences but is currently weak in one is sometimes pushed towards a double award on evidence that a term of focused work would have changed. That is the one case where buying tuition in Year 9 or early Year 10 has a structural rather than a marginal return, because it keeps a route open rather than improving a grade inside a route already chosen.

sections.heading: Where the marks sit: component structure by board
paragraphs: You cannot plan science revision without knowing what each paper is worth, and most families never see the numbers. The table below gives them for the specifications common around Umm Suqeim. Read it once and the priorities reorder themselves immediately: a student spending most of their revision time on multiple-choice practice is optimising 30% of the grade while the theory paper at 50% and the practical component at 20% go untouched.

The theory paper deserves most of the attention, and not because it is the largest. It is the paper where the marks are awarded for extended written answers, which means it is the paper where technique compounds. A student who learns how a six-mark explanation is structured gains marks on every subsequent question of that type, in all three sciences, for the rest of the course. A student who memorises more content gains marks only on the questions that happen to ask about what they memorised.

The practical component is the most neglected 20% in the whole British-curriculum system. Students assume it is easy because the science content is familiar, then lose marks on independent and dependent variables, on why a result was repeated, on table headings that need units in the header rather than beside each value, on axis choices and best-fit lines, and on conclusions that overstate what the data shows. None of these are hard. All of them are specific, and almost none of them are revised.

For Pearson's International GCSE sciences the structure differs: practical skills are assessed inside the written papers, so there is no separate practical component to schedule. The written technique is the same, but the revision plan has to be built differently, which is another reason to confirm the specification code before any tutor starts teaching.

sections.heading: The alternative-to-practical paper, taught without a bench
paragraphs: This is the section worth reading twice if your child sits a Cambridge science. The alternative-to-practical paper, or the practical test where a school enters students for it, is worth a fifth of the grade and consists almost entirely of transferable written skills. A tutor working over video can teach every one of them using past-paper questions and the official mark scheme.

What the paper rewards, concretely. Identifying the independent, dependent and controlled variables in an unfamiliar experiment. Explaining why a measurement was repeated and what is done with the repeats. Constructing a results table with the quantity and its unit in the column heading, consistent significant figures and no units repeated in the body. Choosing axes that use most of the grid, plotting accurately, and drawing a line of best fit rather than joining points. Identifying anomalous results and saying what to do about them. Naming a specific source of error rather than writing 'human error'. Stating a conclusion that the data actually supports, and saying where it does not.

Each of those is a rule with a mark attached, and each is checkable. A student who can be handed an unfamiliar method and reliably produce those elements will score well on this paper regardless of whether they happened to do that particular experiment in school. A student who did the experiment and writes 'we repeated it to be accurate' will lose the mark, because the scheme wants the reason - to identify anomalies, or to calculate a mean - and 'to be accurate' is not it.

The practical argument for doing this work in the evening with a tutor rather than in school is time. A scheme of work has to cover the content, and practical write-up technique gets taught in passing when a practical happens to be on. An hour spent deliberately on ten past-paper practical questions, marked against the scheme and corrected, typically returns more marks than an hour of content revision at any point in Year 11.

sections.heading: Topic by topic: where science marks actually disappear in Years 10 and 11
paragraphs: The losses are consistent enough to predict. In Chemistry, moles calculations go wrong because students learn one formula triangle and meet a question phrased the other way round; electrolysis loses marks because half-equations are written without balancing charge; organic chemistry loses marks because reaction conditions are learned as a list rather than as a reason; and rates questions lose marks because gradients are described rather than calculated.

In Physics the pattern is reasoning rather than recall. A student knows that increasing resistance decreases current, writes the conclusion, and loses two of three marks because the chain - voltage constant, resistance up, therefore current down by the relationship - was never written down. Units and prefixes cost marks under pressure, particularly milli and kilo conversions inside a multi-step calculation. Moments, thermal physics and circuit analysis with two resistors are the usual casualties.

In Biology the volume of content hides a technique problem. Transport in plants, enzyme action, inheritance diagrams and homeostasis all require sequenced explanations, and the mark scheme awards each step. Students who know the biology write a paragraph that contains three of the five steps in no particular order and score three. Students who have been taught to write in steps score five with the same knowledge. Genetics questions additionally lose marks to careless Punnett squares and to answers that give a ratio without naming the phenotypes.

Across all three sciences the largest single avoidable loss is command words. 'State' wants a fact with no explanation. 'Describe' wants what happens. 'Explain' wants why. 'Suggest' wants a reasoned inference about something unfamiliar. 'Compare' wants both sides in each sentence. 'Calculate' wants working shown. A correct answer written in the wrong shape earns nothing, and this is diagnosable from any marked paper in about twenty minutes.

sections.heading: Fitting science into the evening after a 3:15pm gate
paragraphs: A plan that assumes five clear evenings will be abandoned by October. Build it around three. The gates nearest Umm Suqeim release secondary year groups between roughly 2:50pm and 3:30pm, the beach road and Al Wasl Road absorb all of it at once, and a child is home between about 3:30pm and 4:25pm depending on which section of Umm Suqeim and which gate. Food and changing take until about 4:30pm. Concentration is genuinely available from roughly 4:45pm to 6:30pm and declining after that.

Inside that window, different science tasks need different amounts of a student. Learning new content and working through a hard calculation need the front of the window. Past-paper practical questions need moderate energy and benefit from being done in short batches. Marking yesterday's answers against the mark scheme, flashcard recall and reading back a corrected explanation can be done at the tired end, and are the right things to put there.

Then subtract the fixtures. A sports commitment in Al Quoz or Al Barsha removes that evening entirely, not partially, because of the double journey. Arabic and Islamic Education homework are real and non-negotiable, since both subjects are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA's guidance stating those requirements must be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. A week with three usable science evenings is a normal week, not a failure.

It assumes one tutored session, two independent evenings and a weekend morning, which is a realistic rather than aspirational load - and it puts the practical-skills work in the slot where it belongs, because those questions reward precision rather than energy.

sections.heading: What science tuition costs, and why three sciences is rarely three tutors
paragraphs: Start at the top of the market and work down, because the top is where the assumption that more money buys more marks is strongest. Premium named or examiner-led tutors in Dubai publish AED 500-650 and upwards, with BartyED at AED 650. IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists sit at AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's guidance putting specialists at AED 200-450 or more. A qualified subject tutor working online runs AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home one-to-one with travel included runs AED 180-500, Bestimate quoting AED 180-350. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52.

For science specifically, the band that matters is the middle one, and the reason is the practical component. A tutor at AED 150-300 who can mark an alternative-to-practical answer against the official scheme will recover more marks per hour than a tutor at AED 650 teaching content the student largely knows. The premium bands are worth paying for a short diagnostic or for a genuinely rare specification, not for the weekly hour where most of the work gets done.

Monthly, the market shows AED 240-600 at the budget end for a weekly hour, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with advertised packages at AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Multiply any of those by three for three sciences and the number stops being sensible, which brings us to the practical point.

Three sciences rarely needs three tutors. Two of the three largest sources of lost marks - command words and practical write-up technique - are common across all three sciences, and the third, mathematical handling, is shared between Chemistry and Physics. One tutor working on those three things in a single science usually lifts the other two without touching them. Where separate specialists are genuinely justified is at the top end, where a student aiming at a 9 in all three needs content depth in each. For everyone else, one well-chosen tutor and a parent who understands the component weightings is a better purchase than three weekly sessions. All figures above are other providers' published rates read in October 2026, quoted as market context rather than as an IB Gram price list.

sections.heading: Starting from Umm Suqeim, and the honest limits of science tuition
paragraphs: Send four things: which sciences, which specification codes, which tier if Cambridge, and the most recent marked science paper. We confirm the codes, match a tutor who teaches those specifications, and you take a full-length trial lesson at no cost worked through that paper. Sessions then run weekly in Gulf Standard Time, placed against your gate's release time, usually 4:45pm or 5:00pm. Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing and weekend mornings are available for extended work.

What tuition cannot do, stated plainly. It cannot provide laboratory experience; the school does that and should. It cannot make up for content never learned in Year 9 in the four weeks before a series - at that point the honest service is to protect the marks that are still reachable. It cannot change a tier entry, which belongs to the school and the board's deadline. And it cannot fix a situation where all three sciences are weak alongside three other subjects, because that is a load or wellbeing problem and more sessions make it worse.

What it does well is narrow and valuable: it teaches the written technique that carries the practical component, it fixes command-word discipline across all three sciences at once, it marks a student's own work against the official scheme until the student can predict the marks, and it tells you honestly which of the three sciences is actually costing the grade. Those four things are available in one hour a week and they are the reason most families see movement within a term rather than a year.

The fixed limits apply here as everywhere on this site. No home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. No claimed approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, because IB Gram holds none. No reproduction or supply of specifications, past papers or mark schemes - we link the official sources and work from your school's own copies. No coursework written or completed. No grade promises, and no statistics about our own outcomes without the sample, date and method that would make them meaningful.
