faqs.question: Can my child really improve an IGCSE science grade without extra laboratory time?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the marks are written. In Cambridge IGCSE Biology, Chemistry and Physics the multiple-choice paper carries 30%, the theory paper 50% and the practical component 20%, and the practical component awards marks for written responses about variables, repeats, tables, graphs, errors and conclusions. Pearson's International GCSE sciences assess practical skills inside the written papers instead. Bench experience informs that writing and belongs to the school, but the marks themselves are recovered on paper. Deliberate work on practical write-up technique is usually the highest return per hour available in IGCSE science.

faqs.question: Which science component do students in Dubai most often leave unrevised?
faqs.answer: The practical component, which in Cambridge sciences is worth 20% of the grade. Students assume it is easy because the underlying science is familiar, then lose marks on precise things: naming the independent and controlled variables, justifying repeats by purpose rather than by the word accuracy, putting the unit in a table heading instead of beside each value, using most of the grid when choosing axes, drawing a line of best fit rather than joining points, and naming a specific source of error rather than writing human error. Each has a mark attached and each is learnable in a session or two.

faqs.question: Should my child take three separate sciences or Co-ordinated Sciences?
faqs.answer: It depends on where they are heading, and the decision is usually made on timetable arithmetic in Year 9 rather than on that. Three separate sciences is the heaviest load and the conventional route into A Level sciences and into medicine, engineering and dentistry applications. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 reduces content and produces two grades, which suits a loaded timetable - but whether it is accepted for A Level science entry varies between schools, so ask the specific school before the option form goes in. Combined Science as a single award is lighter again and closes most A Level science routes.

faqs.question: Does one tutor cover Biology, Chemistry and Physics, or do we need three?
faqs.answer: One tutor covers two comfortably in most cases and three only at the top end. The reason is that the biggest sources of lost marks are shared: command-word discipline applies identically across all three sciences, practical write-up technique is the same paper skill in each, and mathematical rearrangement is shared between Chemistry and Physics. Fixing those in one science usually lifts the others without separate sessions. Where three specialists are genuinely justified is a student aiming at the top grade in all three and needing content depth in each. For everyone else, three weekly sessions is more cost than benefit.

faqs.question: When in the evening should a science session be scheduled in Umm Suqeim?
faqs.answer: Put the teaching session at 4:45pm or 5:00pm depending on which gate your child leaves. Secondary release around Umm Suqeim, Al Safa and Al Sufouh runs roughly from 2:50pm to 3:30pm, the beach road and Al Wasl Road take all of it at once, and a child is home between about 3:30pm and 4:25pm. Food and changing take until roughly 4:30pm, and real concentration is available from about 4:45pm until 6:30pm. Save marking and review for the tired end of the evening and keep full timed papers for a weekend morning.

faqs.question: My child knows the science but writes poor answers. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly command words. 'State' wants a fact with no explanation, 'describe' wants what happens, 'explain' wants why, 'suggest' wants a reasoned inference about unfamiliar material, 'compare' wants both sides in each sentence, and 'calculate' wants the working shown. A correct answer in the wrong shape earns nothing, and a student who writes a good paragraph containing three of five required steps in no order scores three. This is diagnosable from any marked paper in about twenty minutes and is fixable in a few weeks, which makes it the single best-value thing to work on.

faqs.question: How do we revise for a practical paper if the school has not done the experiment?
faqs.answer: You revise the rules rather than the experiment, because the paper is designed to present unfamiliar methods. A student who can reliably identify the independent, dependent and controlled variables in any described experiment, justify repeats, build a correctly headed table, plot and draw a best-fit line, spot anomalies, name a specific error source and state a conclusion the data supports will score well whether or not they have met that particular practical. Working through ten past-paper practical questions against the official mark scheme teaches those rules faster than doing three more experiments would.

faqs.question: Does the tier entry affect how we should plan science tuition?
faqs.answer: Substantially. Cambridge science specifications are tiered, with Core papers graded C to G and Extended papers graded A* to E, and the entry is made by the school to the board's deadline on the basis of internal performance. A student on a Core entry cannot be awarded a top grade whatever the tuition. So the useful conversation, in Year 10 rather than February of Year 11, is which tier your child is heading for in each science and what would change it. A child on the tier boundary has far more to gain from a term of work than one comfortably inside either tier.

faqs.question: Which science is usually the quickest to improve?
faqs.answer: Chemistry, because it is the most procedural. Moles calculations, electrolysis half-equations, rates gradients and organic reaction conditions are rule-governed, and a student who drills them with a tutor marking to the mark scheme tends to see movement within a half term. Physics takes longer because the losses are in reasoning that has to be written out rather than in facts. Biology takes longest because the content volume is highest, although the technique fix - writing sequenced explanations that match the mark scheme steps - often produces a quick partial gain before the content work is finished.

faqs.question: What should we spend on science tuition for one child in Year 11?
faqs.answer: The mid-market online band of AED 150-300 an hour is where science tuition belongs, because the skill that recovers the most marks is marking an answer against the official scheme rather than teaching content the student mostly knows. Published Dubai figures put specialists at AED 200-450 and upwards with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named tutors at AED 500-650 with BartyED at AED 650. Monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 600-1,200 mid-market. The premium bands are worth a short diagnostic, not the weekly hour where most of the work happens.

faqs.question: How does the Arabic and Islamic Education requirement affect a science revision plan?
faqs.answer: It removes time that most plans assume is free. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's guidance states the requirements must be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Those subjects set homework, and it is not optional. A Year 11 student taking three sciences plus the mandatory subjects has fewer free evenings than a revision timetable suggests, so plan around three usable science evenings a week rather than five.

faqs.question: Can a science tutor help with the maths inside physics and chemistry?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is often the better place to fix it. Rearranging equations, standard form, significant figures, percentage change, gradients and areas under graphs account for a disproportionate share of lost science marks, and a student who meets them inside a physics question learns them in the context they will be tested in. Three sessions on algebraic rearrangement inside a physics session frequently return more than the same time in a general maths session, because the student stops treating the formula as a triangle to memorise and starts treating it as a relationship to manipulate.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start science tuition eight weeks before the June series?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is enough to change technique and to recover the highest-mark topics, and it is not enough to learn content never taught. What works in that window: practical-skills questions worked against the mark scheme, command-word discipline, the two or three heaviest topics in each science by mark allocation, and timed papers in the final three weeks. What does not work is a sweep through the whole specification. If the content was genuinely never learned, the honest plan is to protect the marks still reachable rather than to attempt everything, and we will say that rather than sell a rescue.

faqs.question: How will we know the science tuition is working before results come out?
faqs.answer: By recounting categories of lost marks on a fresh marked paper every six to eight weeks rather than by asking whether lessons feel useful. Separate the losses into content never learned, command word misread, practical technique, calculation error and ran out of time, and track whether the targeted category has shrunk. Grades move in steps and lag technique by a term, so a category count is the more honest early signal. If the targeted category has not moved after a full block, the sensible responses are a change of focus, a change of tutor, or stopping.

faqs.question: Do you provide past papers and mark schemes for IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: No, and no provider should. Specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the boards' copyright material, and reproducing or distributing them is infringement. We reference them, link the official Cambridge and Pearson sources, and work from the papers your school has issued to your child - which are the right ones anyway, because they match the exact specification and tier your child sits. A provider offering a library of downloadable board material is offering something they are not entitled to distribute.

intro.heading: Three sciences, one grade, and the wrong thing usually gets bought
paragraphs: Villanova is a townhouse community off Al Qudra Road in the Dubailand belt, and its Year 10 and 11 students are split across at least six IGCSE science routes. Some take three separate sciences. Some take Coordinated Sciences as a double award. Some take a single-award combined course. Some sit Cambridge, some Pearson Edexcel. The phrase 'science tutor' covers all of it and distinguishes none of it.

That matters for money because of one structural fact: in a combined or coordinated course, a single weak discipline drags the whole grade. A student who is strong in biology, adequate in chemistry and lost in physics does not get a mid grade in each. They get one grade, pulled down by physics. The efficient purchase is support in physics. The common purchase is support in all three, which costs three times as much and moves the grade by roughly the same amount.

On separate sciences the arithmetic reverses. Three subjects, three grades, three sets of papers, and a weak discipline damages only its own grade. Here the decision is which of the three matters most for the post-16 plan, and whether the student is better served by securing two grades well than by stretching across three.

Published Dubai rates for a qualified subject tutor run AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Budget online tuition starts at AED 33 to 65, per Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel, per Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Those are market figures from the parties named, not our price list.

IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses: home visits are a service we offer only in India. Villanova students are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which removes the travel premium that in this belt sits at the top of the AED 50 to 150 per hour range. For the sciences there is one honest limitation, discussed properly below: the laboratory stays at school, and no screen replaces handling apparatus.

Everything that follows is about getting the money in the right place: the route your child is on, the discipline that is actually costing the grade, the paper structures and practical components, the topics that repay tutoring quickly, and the entry and resit costs that arrive after the tutoring budget has gone. Every figure is attributed, so you can check it rather than take it on trust, and where a decision depends on your child's specific entry we say to confirm it with the school's exam office rather than guessing from a page.

subjects.description: Moments questions and density calculations produce predictable errors around unit conversion and taking moments about the wrong point. Cheap to address, and the questions are structurally similar year to year, which makes practice transfer unusually well.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: The calculation block that separates grades at the upper tier. The problem is fluency under time pressure rather than understanding, so timed calculation practice rather than re-explanation is what works. Three to five sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry: qualitative analysis and tests
subjects.description: Ion tests, gas tests and observation wording. Highly learnable, directly examined, and frequently left to last-minute memorisation. One or two sessions of strict marking on the expected wording recovers a specific and predictable set of marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic chemistry
subjects.description: Narrow at IGCSE and rule-governed, which makes it the fastest available gain in the chemistry component for a Year 11. A student who learns the homologous series properly and the handful of reaction types can bank these marks in a fortnight.

subjects.name: Biology: enzymes and transport
subjects.description: Enzyme graphs and transport in plants produce the widest mark spread in the biology component. Marks go to explanation of mechanism rather than description of the observation, which is a command-term habit rather than a content gap.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Punnett squares and ratio reasoning are reliably available marks for a student who practises the layout, and reliably lost by one who improvises it. A low-cost, high-certainty target in the final weeks before a series.

subjects.name: Required practical skills
subjects.description: Assessed either through a practical examination or an alternative-to-practical written paper depending on board and entry. Method description, variable control, graph plotting and improvement suggestions are all written skills, examined in writing, and almost never practised deliberately.

subjects.name: Graph and data skills
subjects.description: Plotting accurately, reading a gradient, choosing scales and interpreting an unfamiliar data set. Shared across all three disciplines, which makes it the one topic where paying for cross-discipline work genuinely pays: one session improves marks in three places.

subjects.name: Command terms in science
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest and compare carry different expectations and different ceilings. Answering 'explain' with description is the most common silent loss in the whole science component, and it is correctable in a single session with a marked paper in front of the student.

sections.heading: Which route your child is on, and what it costs to support
paragraphs: Before any money is spent, establish the route and the board from the school's entry statement. The six combinations in the table below carry different paper structures, different numbers of grades at stake, and therefore different sensible spending levels. Families regularly buy support for the wrong structure, which is invisible for weeks because the content looks similar.

The crucial distinction is how many grades are at risk. On separate sciences a weak physics performance damages the physics grade and nothing else, so the spending decision is about which subject matters for the post-16 plan. On coordinated or single-award routes all three disciplines feed one or two shared grades, so the weakest discipline sets the ceiling and support aimed anywhere else is close to wasted.

That single fact changes the arithmetic dramatically. In a double-award course, four to eight sessions on circuits may lift both grades. The same budget spread evenly across biology, chemistry and physics produces three partial interventions, none of which reaches the discipline that was dragging the result. We have watched families spend AED 6,000 this way and get a smaller movement than AED 1,500 would have delivered if aimed properly.

So the first conversation about cost is really a conversation about structure. Get the entry statement, identify the route, then read the marked papers by discipline. Only then does the number of hours become a sensible question. The whole exercise costs a phone call to the exam office and ten minutes with a marked paper, which is a better return than any hour you will buy afterwards.

sections.heading: What the hours cost, case by case
paragraphs: Here are honest session estimates by diagnosis, priced at the qualified-tutor band of AED 150 to 300 an hour that most IGCSE science work sits in. The spread between the cheapest and most expensive case is close to tenfold, which is why an hourly rate on its own tells a parent nothing useful.

Read it alongside the route table. A circuits block in a double-award course is four to eight sessions and lifts two shared grades: that is the best value purchase available in IGCSE science and it costs AED 600 to 2,400. A genuine content deficit across a separate-science subject is twenty to thirty sessions and AED 3,000 to 9,000, and it lifts one grade. Both are legitimate; they are simply not the same decision.

The pattern with delay is worth noting because it differs between categories. Technique and habit problems — command terms, graph skills, practical method wording — stay cheap almost until the exam, so a family short of funds in April should spend them there. Content deficits get steadily more expensive and, in the last term, become damage limitation rather than repair. A DP-bound Year 10 with a content gap should spend now; a Year 11 in March should spend on technique.

Our own first session exists to place a student in one of these rows and say so, including when the honest row is 'four sessions and then stop'. That happens often enough in science that we would rather be known for saying it than for selling a weekly year.

sections.heading: Which of the three sciences to actually pay for
paragraphs: This is the question that decides whether a science budget works, and it has a factual answer available from the marked papers rather than an opinion answer available from the student.

Take the most recent marked paper or mock and separate the lost marks by discipline. In a coordinated course the papers mix the three, so this takes ten minutes with a pen. In our experience of Dubai cohorts the loss concentrates in physics more often than in anything else, with the chemistry calculation block second. Biology losses tend to be distributed and command-term driven rather than concentrated, which is why biology is usually the wrong place to spend first even when it feels like the hardest subject to a student facing a lot of content.

Then check one thing before committing: whether the loss is content or technique. A discipline where whole questions are blank is a content problem. A discipline where answers are started, partially right, and marked down is a technique problem — and technique problems are cheaper, faster and available in every discipline at once through the command-term and graph work described above.

The result for most Villanova families on a coordinated route is a specific plan: four to eight sessions on the physics weakness, three on cross-discipline graph and command-term skills, and nothing on the two disciplines that were already functioning. That is roughly AED 1,000 to 3,000 rather than AED 6,000, and it is aimed at the thing that was setting the ceiling.

sections.heading: Paper structures and the practical component
paragraphs: Science papers differ by board and route, and the practical element differs most of all. Confirming it matters because the practical component is assessed in writing in most entries, and written practical skills are a distinct thing to prepare for.

Depending on board and school entry, practical skills are assessed either through a practical examination taken under supervision or through an alternative-to-practical written paper on unseen experiments. Either way, the examined skills are largely written: describing a method precisely, identifying and controlling variables, tabulating results, plotting and interpreting graphs, discussing uncertainty and suggesting specific improvements. Those are teachable without apparatus, and they are rarely taught deliberately.

That produces a clear and cheap opportunity. Three to five sessions on the written practical skills addresses a component most students have never practised, and the marks are available whether the entry is a practical examination or an alternative paper. Compare that with the same money spent on a general content sweep across three disciplines and the choice makes itself.

Confirm the structure against the board's current specification for your child's entry year, because paper counts and practical routes are revised between specification versions. Those documents are free on the board's own site, and any tutor worth paying works from them. Nobody should be charging you for them. One practical note for Villanova parents comparing notes: because departments inside a single Dubai school sometimes enter different boards, two children at the same school can be on different practical routes, and the recommendation that suited one will not automatically suit the other.

sections.heading: Topics that repay tutoring in each discipline
paragraphs: Once the discipline is chosen, the topic choice inside it decides how fast the money works. These are the targets we would pick first in each science, ordered by marks recovered per session.

In physics: circuits first, every time. It is the largest reliable loss in UAE cohorts and it responds to question-led teaching — what happens to the rest of the circuit when this component changes — rather than to re-reading notes. Then moments and density, where errors cluster around unit conversion and taking moments about the wrong point, both of which are correctable in a session.

In chemistry: qualitative analysis wording and organic chemistry, because both are narrow, rule-governed and directly examined. A student who learns the expected observation wording for the standard ion and gas tests banks a predictable set of marks for an hour or two of work. Moles and stoichiometry come next, treated as a fluency problem with timed practice rather than as a comprehension problem with more explanation.

In biology: genetics and inheritance, where the Punnett square layout is worth practising until it is automatic, and then command-term discipline on enzyme and transport questions, where students describe the observation instead of explaining the mechanism. Biology rewards precision of language more than any other discipline at this level, and precision is cheaper to teach than content. Across all three disciplines, the cheapest work of all is graph and data skills, because the same hour improves answers in biology, chemistry and physics at once and the questions that test it appear on every paper regardless of route.
bullets: Physics: circuits, then moments and density unit handling
Chemistry: qualitative analysis wording and organic, then moles fluency

sections.heading: Online or in-home for science, and the laboratory question
paragraphs: The fair question from any science parent: can this subject be taught properly without apparatus in the room? The honest answer splits the work and is more useful than a reassuring generality.

The apparatus work stays at school. That is where the equipment, the technician and the safety framework are, and it is where your child builds the circuit, times the reaction and records the readings. No online session substitutes for handling equipment, and any tutor who claims otherwise is overselling. For families whose children are entered for a practical examination, the procedural rehearsal happens with the school's teacher and the school's apparatus.

What online teaching covers is the written part of practical assessment, which is where most practical marks actually sit: method description, variable control, tabulation, graph plotting and interpretation, uncertainty and specific improvements. It also covers every other part of the course. On a shared screen, graphs can be plotted live, a data table annotated in a second colour, and the marked work saved so both the tutor and the student keep the record.

The cost difference is real. In-home visits to this belt run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against AED 150 to 300 for the same qualified tutor online, and Villanova sits at the top of the in-home range because the drive out is long. Over a twenty-session block the travel component commonly adds AED 1,000 to 3,000. That premium buys presence, which is the right purchase for a child who genuinely cannot work on a screen. IB Gram does not offer it anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are an India-only service.
bullets: Apparatus work stays at school, with the school's equipment and supervision

sections.heading: Where science tutoring money gets wasted in this belt
paragraphs: Five patterns, each common enough in Dubailand enquiries to be worth naming, and each avoidable with one question asked before the first payment.

First and largest: buying support in all three disciplines when the marked papers show the loss concentrated in one. In a coordinated course this triples the cost for roughly the same grade movement, because the ceiling was set by the weak discipline and the other two sessions were spent maintaining things that already worked. Second: buying content teaching when the problem is technique. A student whose answers are started and marked down needs command-term and graph work, not more topics.

Third: buying group science classes to fix an individual gap. A group delivers one pace to everyone, which suits consolidation and cannot reach a specific circuits problem. Monthly packages in this market are advertised from around AED 799 for eight sessions, which looks cheap until the mismatch and the drive from Villanova to Motor City are counted.

Fourth: practising the wrong board's papers because nobody confirmed the codes, which makes every hour less effective without anyone noticing for weeks. Fifth: spending the whole budget before results, leaving nothing for a resit entry in the November series if one subject goes wrong. A realistic plan keeps a reserve, because a second entry fee is a real cost that no tutoring quote includes. The through-line in all five is the same: money committed before the marked paper was read, when the marked paper was free and already in the house.
bullets: Paying for all three sciences when one discipline set the ceiling

sections.heading: Entries, series and the costs that arrive after the tutoring
paragraphs: Exam administration is the cost that catches families out, and it is driven by the calendar rather than by choice. For a Villanova household, getting the series right is a budget decision as much as an academic one.

Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to a candidate sitting in the UAE, so advice built around a February window belongs to a different country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school's exam officer which zone applies.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. Checkable reference points: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables for later series that may be revised, so work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

The money consequence: a resit is a second entry fee, quoted by the exam centre rather than by any tutor, plus whatever further hours you decide on. For a science student on a coordinated route the decision is more complicated than for a single subject, because the shared grade means the whole award is re-sat rather than one discipline. Ask the exam office what that involves before results day rather than after it.

process.title: Send the route, the codes and a marked paper
process.description: The entry statement gives the route and the syllabus codes; the marked paper shows where the loss is. With both, we can tell you which discipline is setting the ceiling and roughly how many sessions it takes. Without them, the first exchanges are spent establishing what your child is actually sitting.

process.title: Diagnosis by discipline, then a price
process.description: We separate the lost marks by discipline and by cause before quoting, because the honest answer ranges from two sessions to thirty. A rate quoted before anyone has read a paper is a figure set for the seller's convenience rather than an estimate of what the job needs.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the matched tutor
process.description: A genuine lesson with the person who would continue, no card required. It tests the diagnosis and the fit together: whether the losses are content or technique, and whether the pair of them work well. If the pace or style does not suit your child, say so and we match again.

process.title: A plan in spending order, with a finish date
process.description: The plan names the discipline block first, the cross-discipline skills work second, and nothing for the disciplines that were already functioning. Each item carries a session count and an end date set against the school's mocks and the board entry deadline, rather than running on indefinitely.

whyPoints.title: One discipline, not three
whyPoints.description: In coordinated and single-award courses the weakest discipline sets the shared grade, so support aimed at it lifts the whole result. Spreading the same budget evenly across three sciences produces three partial interventions and leaves the ceiling where it was.

whyPoints.title: Technique before content, where the papers say so
whyPoints.description: Blank questions mean a content gap; partially right answers marked down mean a technique gap. Technique is cheaper, faster and improves all three disciplines at once through command-term and graph work, which almost nobody teaches deliberately.

whyPoints.title: Codes and route confirmed first
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0654 and Pearson 4SD0 are not interchangeable, and neither are the separate-science codes. Practice on the wrong board's papers is wasted money that goes unnoticed for weeks, so the specification is confirmed before the first session rather than after a term.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the laboratory
whyPoints.description: Apparatus work stays at school. What online teaching covers is the written practical skills — method, variables, tabulation, graphs, improvements — which is where most practical marks sit and which is almost never practised deliberately.

whyPoints.title: Figures with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here names who published it and is presented as the market rather than our price. We publish no statistic without a source, no promises about final grades, no resold board material, and no self-awarded ratings.

faqs.question: Should I pay for all three sciences or just one?
faqs.answer: In a coordinated or single-award course, almost always one — the discipline the marked papers show as the concentration of lost marks, which in Dubai cohorts is most often physics. Because all three feed one or two shared grades, the weakest discipline sets the ceiling and support aimed elsewhere maintains what already worked. Spreading the budget evenly triples the cost for roughly the same movement. On separate sciences the logic differs: each grade stands alone, so choose by which subject matters for the post-16 plan.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE science tutoring cost in the Dubailand belt?
faqs.answer: A qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Budget online tuition starts at AED 33 to 65, per Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel, and Villanova sits at the top of that range because the drive is long. The useful number is the total: a four-session circuits block is AED 600 to 2,400, while a year of weekly sessions in one subject is AED 4,500 to 9,000.

faqs.question: How do I find out which science route and codes my child is on?
faqs.answer: Ask the exam office for the entry statement, which names the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject. It takes ten minutes and it settles three things at once: whether the route is separate, coordinated or single award, how many grades are at stake, and which board's past papers are worth the hour. Departments within one Dubai school sometimes differ, so check discipline by discipline rather than assuming the school uses one board throughout.

faqs.question: Which science topic is the best value to tutor first?
faqs.answer: Circuits, in almost every case. Electricity is the largest reliable loss across UAE science cohorts, it responds to question-led teaching rather than re-reading notes, and in a coordinated course it lifts the grade all three disciplines share. Four to eight sessions typically does it. The next best buys are cross-discipline: graph plotting and interpretation, and command-term discipline, both of which improve answers in biology, chemistry and physics simultaneously for a handful of sessions.

faqs.question: Villanova lessons are online - so who supervises the practical work?
faqs.answer: The apparatus work stays at school, where the equipment, the technician and the safety framework are, and where your child builds the circuit and records the readings. Online teaching covers the written practical skills, which is where most practical marks sit: describing a method precisely, identifying and controlling variables, tabulating, plotting and interpreting graphs, discussing uncertainty and suggesting specific improvements. Those are examined in writing whether the entry is a practical examination or an alternative-to-practical paper, and they are rarely practised deliberately.

faqs.question: Is biology, chemistry or physics the hardest for Dubai students?
faqs.answer: Physics produces the largest concentrated losses, chemistry the most calculation-driven ones, and biology the most distributed ones. That is not the same as hardest: biology feels hardest to many students because of the content volume, but its losses tend to be command-term driven — describing an observation where an explanation of mechanism was asked for — which is a language habit rather than a content gap. Physics losses tend to be genuinely conceptual, which is why physics is usually where a limited budget should go first.

faqs.question: Will a science tutor come to our house in Villanova?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram teaches UAE students one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we run only in India, so no tutor will arrive at a Dubailand address. Independent in-home science tutors work in this belt at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Villanova at the top of that range. Over twenty sessions the travel element commonly adds AED 1,000 to 3,000, and it buys presence rather than better teaching of circuits or moles calculations.

faqs.question: Are group science classes at a centre worth it?
faqs.answer: For consolidation, yes; for a diagnosed gap, no. A group delivers one pace and one sequence to everyone, which suits a student broadly on track who needs more exposure and practice. It cannot reach an individual circuits problem or a chemistry calculation weakness. Monthly packages in this market are advertised from around AED 799 for eight sessions, which looks inexpensive until you add the drive from Villanova to Motor City — twenty-five to forty minutes each way plus waiting — and the mismatch between the class plan and your child's actual loss.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 11 and the mock was poor across all sciences. What now?
faqs.answer: Separate the lost marks by discipline and by cause before buying anything, which takes ten minutes with the marked paper. A poor result across all three usually turns out to be one content gap plus a technique problem that was costing marks everywhere. In that case the efficient plan is a four to eight session block on the weak discipline and three sessions on command terms and graph skills, which is roughly AED 1,000 to 3,000 rather than the AED 6,000 that three separate arrangements would cost.

faqs.question: Does the science route affect MoE equivalency?
faqs.answer: It affects the subject count. For the British track, Gulf Today reported the Ministry's clarification that five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates are needed at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from those five, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. A double-award science contributes two subjects to that count while a single award contributes one, which is worth knowing at option time. Verify current requirements on moe.gov.ae, and note that no tutoring is required for equivalency.

faqs.question: Can a single tutor handle all three sciences for a Villanova Year 11?
faqs.answer: Someone will offer to, and for a single-award or coordinated course at a mid grade it can work adequately. For a targeted intervention it is usually weaker than a specialist in the one discipline that matters. The compromise most families land on is a specialist for the weak discipline and school support elsewhere, plus a short cross-discipline block on graphs and command terms where a generalist is genuinely fine. Depth beats convenience when a specific grade is at stake.

faqs.question: What does a science resit cost if June goes badly?
faqs.answer: A second entry fee quoted by the exam centre, plus whatever further hours you decide on. For a coordinated or double-award route it is more involved than for a single subject, because the shared grade means the award rather than one discipline is re-sat, so ask the exam office exactly what a resit entails before results day. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates and Pearson runs May/June and November, so there is a route each year. Keeping a reserve in the budget is sensible.

faqs.question: Is the quoted price per hour or per lesson, and does it include materials?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get it in writing before the first paid session, along with the cancellation notice period and whether an hour means sixty minutes. On materials: nobody should be charging you for Cambridge or Pearson specifications, past papers or mark schemes. Those are published free by the boards and should be cited and linked, not resold as a resource pack. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition as a general fact, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than an opinion.

faqs.question: Is a permit needed to tutor science privately in Dubailand?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years according to u.ae. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, through MoHRE's Private Tutor Licensing service. Since the permit is free no tutor should pass on a licensing cost, and because no fine schedule is published, treat any penalty figure quoted at you as unverified.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-villanova.closingHeading: Find the discipline, then spend the money
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-villanova.closingBody: The most useful ten minutes a Villanova family can spend on IGCSE science costs nothing: get the entry statement so you know the route and the codes, then go through the last marked paper separating lost marks by discipline and by cause. That turns a vague three-subject worry into one targeted block and one short skills block, which is usually a quarter of the spend. Send us both documents and you will get an honest session count and a rate quoted after the free trial lesson. Teaching is live, one-to-one and online; the laboratory stays at school.

dubai/igcse-summer-tuition.tutorsIntro: The tutors below hold the IGCSE specifications your child actually sits, not a general maths or science brief. Each works from the Cambridge or Pearson subject content for the current series, marks to the published mark scheme wording rather than a private rubric, and reports back in the grade language your school uses. Pick one, or send the syllabus codes and a shortlist comes back.

intro.heading: What a Dubai summer actually buys you
paragraphs: The Dubai school year closes in the first week of July and opens again in the last days of August or the first week of September, depending on whether a school runs a British or an IB calendar. That leaves roughly eight to nine clear weeks. For an IGCSE student the arithmetic is unusually favourable. A two-year course taught at four or five lessons a fortnight loses nothing in that window, while a student who uses thirty of those hours properly can arrive in Year 11 having already closed the three topics that would otherwise sit unresolved until the February mock.

Summer tuition is not term tuition moved sideways. During term a tutor is permanently one week behind a school scheme of work, patching whatever was taught on Tuesday afternoon. In July nothing is being taught, so the agenda belongs entirely to the student. That changes what a session can be. A whole hour can go on simultaneous equations with no competing deadline. A second hour can revisit the same topic two days later, which is the spacing that moves recall rather than comprehension, and term-time scheduling almost never allows it.

The second thing the break buys is a clean read on where the marks went. Most Dubai families arrive in July holding a June report card with a letter on it and no information underneath. A report says grade 5. It does not say that the 5 came from scoring well on routine calculation and badly on anything beginning with the command term explain. One timed paper, marked against the published mark scheme in front of the student, produces that split inside ninety minutes and turns a vague worry into a list.

Travel is the constraint everyone underestimates. Dubai empties in July. Families move between the UAE, the United Kingdom, India, Egypt, Lebanon and Pakistan, often more than once, and a tutor who can only meet in a Dubai living room loses the student for five of the nine weeks. Lessons delivered over live video follow the student instead. A session booked for 17:00 Gulf Standard Time becomes 13:00 in London and 18:30 in Mumbai, and the schedule holds because the fixed points are the tutor and the student, not a car.

The last thing to settle before July is whether the summer is remedial, preparatory or a resit campaign, because those are three different plans. A Year 10 student closing gaps works topic by topic. A student entering Year 11 works forward into the first term's content so that September becomes revision rather than first contact. A student entered for the Pearson November series is on a fixed countdown and needs past-paper volume from week one. Mixing the three is the most reliable way to watch a summer dissolve into pleasant, undirected conversation.
bullets: Eight to nine clear weeks between the July close and the late-August return
Thirty taught hours is a realistic block at two or three sessions a week

dubai/igcse-summer-tuition.programmesIntro: Summer work splits by where a student sits on the British curriculum ladder, not by age. These are the four entry points Dubai families book in July, with what each should have produced by the last week of August. A Year 9 student choosing options needs something different from a November resit candidate, and the only reason the two get planned identically is that nobody asked the question in June.

programmes.name: Pre-IGCSE: the options summer
programmes.description: Year 9 ends with a subject-choice form and very little information behind it. A July block here is diagnostic rather than remedial: enough algebra, enough chemical calculation and enough extended writing to tell whether triple science and Extended maths are a sensible load or an expensive mistake. The output is a short written view on each candidate subject, with the specification content the student has not yet met named topic by topic.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai complicates this because option blocks differ sharply between schools in the same community. A Jumeirah school may run triple science against a second language, while a school ten minutes away runs them in parallel. Settling the question in July, before the form is returned in September, is cheaper than discovering in Year 11 that Chemistry 0620 was never going to fit alongside Additional Mathematics 0606.

programmes.name: Year 10 gap closure
programmes.description: The most common July booking. One year of the course has been taught, roughly half the specification is covered, and the June report has produced a grade nobody can explain. Work runs topic by topic against the published subject content, with a timed section of a past paper every second session so that progress is measured in marks rather than in how the student felt about the hour.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Year 10 students lose a disproportionate number of marks in the first half of the specification because it is taught in Year 9 and never revisited. Number, units and the mole, and the practical-skills paper content all fall into that trap. A summer block that goes back to the earliest taught topics, rather than forward, usually produces more mark movement than any amount of new content.

programmes.name: The September bridge into Year 11
programmes.description: This block runs forward. Four or five weeks of work on the content a school will teach in the autumn term turns September from first contact into revision, which matters enormously in a year where the February mock sets predicted grades for university applications. It suits a student who is already reasonably secure and whose risk is volume rather than understanding.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools set their Year 11 mocks earlier than UK schools do, often in January or early February, because UCAS and UAE university deadlines arrive sooner for the cohort sitting A-Levels or the IB Diploma afterwards. A student who spent the summer four weeks ahead walks into that mock having seen the material twice. One who did not sees it once, three weeks before.

programmes.name: The November resit campaign
programmes.description: A fixed countdown with no room for topic tourism. Past-paper volume starts in week one, marked and logged, and the plan is built from the error log rather than from the syllabus order. The student needs to know which paper, which tier and which board before the first session, because the Cambridge and Pearson versions of the same subject award marks differently.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE exams in May or June and again in November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Entry is made through a centre, and private candidates in Dubai need to secure one early. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is the realistic point at which a Dubai sixth-form place can be confirmed on a repaired grade.

dubai/igcse-summer-tuition.subjectsIntro: Nine subjects account for most July bookings in Dubai. The syllabus code matters more than the subject name, because Cambridge and Pearson split content, papers and tiers differently for the same nominal course. Send the code from your child's exam entry or statement of entry and the planning starts from the right document rather than from an assumption.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher tiers
subjects.description: Marks concentrate in algebraic manipulation, trigonometry beyond the right-angled triangle, and the long multi-step questions at the back of Paper 4. Summer work normally starts with indices, surds and rearranging formulae, because nearly every later topic quietly depends on them and the dependency is invisible in a school report.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure (0606, 4PM1)
subjects.description: Calculus, matrices, logarithms and kinematics arrive with no gentle introduction, and students who coped with 0580 by pattern-matching run out of patterns. July is the natural moment for this subject because it rewards uninterrupted blocks of practice rather than one lesson a week squeezed against everything else.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism produce the widest spread of marks, and the practical-skills questions produce the most avoidable losses: axes unlabelled, a line of best fit drawn through the origin for no reason, a conclusion that restates the data. Both are fixable in a summer with no competing homework.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: The mole dominates. Students who cannot move confidently between mass, moles, concentration and volume lose marks across half the paper, not just in the calculation questions. Organic chemistry and the qualitative-analysis tables are the other two reliable gaps, and both reward memorisation with structure behind it.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem rather than difficulty. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance carry most of the lost marks, usually because an answer describes when the command term asked the student to explain. Summer work here is as much about answer construction as about recall.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Science (0653, 0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into two GCSE grades, which means the specification cuts content unpredictably and students revise topics they will never be asked about. The first useful summer hour is spent mapping what the double award actually includes, against the single-science syllabus the online revision sites assume.

subjects.name: English Language (0500, 0990, 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response carry the marks, and both are assessed on a band descriptor rather than a tick list. A student who has never read the band descriptors is guessing. Summer work pairs one timed response a week with line-by-line marking against the published criteria.

subjects.name: English Literature (0475, 0992, 4ET1)
subjects.description: Closed-text examination means quotation accuracy matters, and Dubai students who changed school mid-course sometimes carry notes on a text they are no longer being examined on. July is the moment to confirm the set texts for the series and build a quotation bank around the assessment objectives.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (0455, 0450, 4EC1, 4BS1)
subjects.description: Both subjects are lost on evaluation rather than knowledge. A definition earns one mark; a judgement supported by a chain of reasoning earns four. Summer sessions here work almost entirely on paragraph structure, with the content treated as raw material rather than as the thing being learned.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First and Additional Language (0508, 0544)
subjects.description: Dubai students sit Arabic alongside an international curriculum because KHDA requires the subject regardless of the licensed curriculum. The IGCSE version is a separate examination with its own specification, and summer support has to distinguish between school Arabic lessons and the Cambridge assessment they do not automatically prepare for.

dubai/igcse-summer-tuition.regionsIntro: Area matters less for delivery than it used to, because the sessions run over live video, and more for scheduling. These are the seven Dubai communities that generate the most July enquiries, with what the summer actually looks like in each. The pattern of who leaves and when decides whether a thirty-hour block fits into six weeks or nine.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Safa
regions.note: Heavy British-curriculum catchment and the earliest July departures, with many families away for the whole of August. Blocks here usually compress into the first five weeks, running three sessions a week rather than two, and finish before the family travels.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JBR and Dubai Harbour
regions.note: Apartment living and shorter trips. Students are often in Dubai for most of the break but share a desk with a sibling and a parent working from home, so sessions are timed to the quietest part of the day rather than the conventional late afternoon.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, Mudon and Dubailand
regions.note: Villa communities where a tutor visit once meant a thirty-minute drive each way from the city. Online delivery removes that entirely, which is why mid-morning sessions are common here in July, a slot that was never practical during term.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Khawaneej
regions.note: Large family households with several IGCSE-age children and a strong preference for consecutive sessions. Two students back to back on the same subject at different tiers is the usual pattern, with one on Core and one on Extended.

regions.name: Al Barsha, Dubai Hills Estate and Al Quoz
regions.note: The densest cluster of British-curriculum schools in the city, which produces the widest spread of exam boards in a single community. Confirming Cambridge against Pearson before the first session matters more here than almost anywhere else.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai, Business Bay and DIFC
regions.note: Short breaks and working parents, so July bookings skew towards evening sessions and towards resit candidates rather than Year 10 gap closure. Students here are often already in a sixth form elsewhere and repairing one grade.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle, Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Price-sensitive and well informed, with families who have already compared four providers before making contact. Published market rates and a clear statement of what a block excludes matter more to this group than any other.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: Long-established British-curriculum schools running IGCSE at 16 before splitting into A-Levels or the IB Diploma. Families in this cluster usually know their exam board but rarely know the tier their child has been entered at, which is the first thing a July diagnostic settles.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Dubai Hills and Al Quoz
schoolClusters.note: The highest concentration of British-curriculum provision in Dubai, with a mix of Cambridge and Pearson entries across schools a few minutes apart. Students who move between these schools mid-course are the ones most likely to be revising the wrong specification.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Dubai Festival City
schoolClusters.note: Larger year groups and a broader attainment spread, so Core and Extended entries sit side by side in the same household. Summer plans in this cluster more often involve two children than one, on different tiers of the same subject.

dubai/igcse-summer-tuition.modesIntro: Four shapes of summer booking cover almost every enquiry. The difference between them is not the number of hours but what the hours are pointed at, and choosing the wrong shape is why some summers produce a visible grade shift and others produce a pleasant set of conversations and no mark movement at all.

modes.title: The thirty-hour block
modes.description: Two or three sessions a week across six to nine weeks, planned as one course rather than as separate lessons. Week one is diagnostic. Weeks two to seven work the error log in priority order. The final week is a timed full paper under exam conditions, marked and returned with a written handover for the autumn term.
bullets: Timed diagnostic in session one, marked against the published mark scheme
Written plan with a named output for every week
A marked past-paper section every second session
Handover note at the end, written for the student and the parent

modes.title: Resit countdown
modes.description: For a student entered for a November or later series. Past papers from week one, worked under timed conditions, with the plan rebuilt every fortnight from what the marking shows rather than from the syllabus order. The board and tier are confirmed before the first session, because Cambridge and Pearson reward different answer structures for identical content.
bullets: Board, paper and tier confirmed from the statement of entry
Weekly timed paper with full mark-scheme annotation

Entry logistics discussed, with the centre and deadline named

modes.title: September bridge
modes.description: Four to five weeks spent forward of the school, covering the content the autumn term will teach. Suits a secure student whose risk is volume rather than understanding, and it changes the February mock from a first full encounter with the specification into a second one. Pace is deliberately brisk and the material is revisited in September anyway.

modes.title: Two students, one timetable
modes.description: Common in Dubai villa communities where two or three siblings sit IGCSE in consecutive years. Sessions run back to back with separate plans, separate diagnostics and separate reporting, which keeps the convenience of one timetable without the compromise of teaching two different tiers in the same hour.

sections.heading: What IGCSE summer tuition in Dubai costs, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Three of the six agency pages ranking for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote United States dollars, a currency Dubai families do not transact in. Here is the market in dirhams. Budget online tutoring, usually a university student working straight from the textbook, sits around AED 45 to 150 an hour: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online runs AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150.

An in-home visit is the expensive option, and the premium is travel rather than teaching. Bestimate's Dubai rate table for 2026 puts home tutoring at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500. A tutor who drives from Mirdif to Arabian Ranches for a 17:00 session has spent ninety unpaid minutes in a car, and that time is priced into the hour whether or not anyone itemises it. Specialist IGCSE and A-Level tutors run AED 200 to 450 and upwards, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor.

Summer moves the number in one direction only: volume. A thirty-hour block bought in July almost always carries a lower effective hourly rate than six single lessons bought in February, because the tutor is planning one course rather than six separate rescues. Monthly packages visible across the Dubai market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour home visits. IB Gram publishes no rate card on these pages: the free trial lesson and the conversation after it are where a quote comes from, and the figures above are the market you are quoting against.

sections.heading: The eight-week plan, written backwards from the September return
paragraphs: A summer plan written forwards fills the available hours. A summer plan written backwards from the first week of September decides what has to be true on the last Sunday of August and works out what each week must deliver to get there. The difference shows up in week six, when the forward plan is still working through the syllabus in order and the backward plan has already spent two weeks on the three topics that were costing the most marks.

The sequence below assumes thirty hours across eight weeks at two sessions a week, which is the most commonly booked shape in Dubai. It survives interruption reasonably well. A family that disappears for a fortnight in the middle loses weeks four and five, and the plan absorbs that by compressing the consolidation block rather than by abandoning the final timed paper, which is the one component that must not move.

Two outputs make this plan auditable rather than aspirational. The first is the error log, a running list of every dropped mark classified by topic and by command term, which replaces the tutor's memory as the planning document and is shared with the family rather than kept in a notebook. The second is the weekly named deliverable in the right-hand column of the table below. If a week ends and the deliverable does not exist, the plan has slipped, and the next session opens with that rather than with new content. Both are deliberately boring, which is the point: a summer plan that can be checked halfway through is the only kind that gets corrected in time.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Almost nobody loses IGCSE marks because a topic was never taught. Marks go missing because an answer does the wrong thing with the content it has. A student who knows the mechanism of osmosis perfectly and writes a description when the paper asked for an explanation has lost two marks on knowledge they possess. Repeat that across a paper and a grade 7 becomes a grade 5 without a single genuine gap in understanding.

Command terms are the mechanism. Each one has a mark-scheme shape behind it, and the shapes are not interchangeable. Calculate wants working and a unit. Explain wants a causal chain, usually two linked statements. Compare wants both sides in the same sentence, not two paragraphs side by side. Suggest wants a plausible application of principle to an unfamiliar context and is marked generously if the reasoning is visible. None of this is secret and none of it is on the specification.

The second mechanism is arithmetic about time. A Cambridge Extended paper allocates roughly one mark a minute, and a student who spends twelve minutes on a four-mark question has borrowed eight minutes from somewhere later. The fix is not speed, it is triage, and it is learned by sitting timed sections with a clock visible and reviewing what the clock cost rather than only what the answers scored. July is the only time of year with room to practise that properly, because a timed section costs an hour of a session that is not also carrying this week's homework.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier decision Dubai families leave too late
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is examined at two tiers. Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 and can be awarded grades C to G. Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 and can be awarded grades A* to E. The decision is made by the school, usually in Year 10 and sometimes as late as the autumn of Year 11, and it sets a hard ceiling on what the student can be awarded no matter how well the paper goes.

Families frequently discover the tier only when the statement of entry arrives. By then a student capable of a grade 6 may be entered for Core, where a grade 6 does not exist, and a student who is genuinely struggling may be entered for Extended, where the paper is written for a different attainment range and the experience is demoralising rather than instructive. July is the right moment to look at the question honestly, because a tier change requested in September is a conversation and one requested in January is a problem.

The right-fit signal is not the report grade. It is how the student performs on the harder half of the tier above, under time. A student who scores respectably on Paper 4 questions from the first half of the specification belongs on Extended even if the school is hesitant. A student who finds Paper 2 uncomfortable and Paper 1 straightforward is better served by a Core entry with a secure grade C than by an Extended entry and a grade E. Both conversations are easier with a marked script in hand.

sections.heading: Resit routes, and why the entry deadline sits months before the paper
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a Dubai family can learn in July is that exam entry is a separate process from exam preparation, with its own calendar and its own failure mode. Pearson Edexcel offers International GCSE in a May or June series and again in November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Cambridge International runs exactly two series a Dubai centre can enter a candidate for: June and November. The February and March sitting is offered to India only, and the March, May and October dates a parent may stumble across online belong to Checkpoint, which is a Primary and Lower Secondary assessment rather than IGCSE. That leaves a clean piece of July arithmetic. A student revising this month is either about fifteen weeks out from the first November paper or about eleven months out from the next June one, and in both directions the entry closed or will close long before the revision starts to feel urgent. The exact entry day for your series sits on the centre's statement of entry, not on a tutoring page.

One operational detail catches private candidates every year. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so the only safe reference is the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than any date restated on a tutoring page, including this one.

sections.heading: How the lessons are actually delivered, and why nobody arrives at a Dubai address
paragraphs: Every session on this page is one-to-one and runs over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors into homes anywhere in the United Arab Emirates; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India, and that is true in July as it is in term time. The reason is not logistics. It is that the pool of people who can teach Cambridge 0620 organic chemistry to a grade 8 standard and who also happen to live within a twenty-minute drive of Arabian Ranches in August is close to empty, while the pool who can teach it over a shared screen is not.

What the video session gives up is physical presence. What it gains is specification match. A Dubai family choosing an in-home tutor is choosing from whoever is available locally and free at 17:00; a family choosing an online specialist is choosing from everyone who teaches that paper. In a subject where the difference between a Cambridge and a Pearson answer structure is worth a grade, that trade is not close.

Practically, a session uses a shared whiteboard, a document camera or phone stand so handwritten working is visible both ways, and the actual past-paper PDF annotated live. Sessions are recorded, which turns the summer into a revision archive the student still has in February. Handwritten scripts are photographed and returned marked. None of this requires anyone to be in a car during a Dubai August, which is its own argument.

sections.heading: KHDA, the Dubai calendar and the mandatory subjects that do not pause
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. The scale is worth knowing before you plan a summer: Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum accounting for 37 per cent of that enrolment, Indian 26 per cent, US 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate 7 per cent.

Two KHDA facts shape a July plan. The first is money: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is therefore being added to a flat school-fee base this year rather than a rising one, which changes how a thirty-hour block looks in a household budget. The second is capacity: the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools and 16,846 places, four of them UK curriculum.

The third thing that does not pause is the mandatory UAE subject requirement. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. A summer that ignores these subjects ignores part of the September timetable.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: the five-subject rule that decides which summer subjects matter
paragraphs: If your child will apply to a UAE university, the Ministry of Education equivalency rules decide which IGCSE grades count, and the British-track requirement is specific. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that changes summer planning is the exclusion. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. A student holding seven IGCSEs of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education has five that count, with no margin. One ranking competitor publishes the claim that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the rule says, and a family planning around that number is planning around an error.

Two cautions belong with this. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs and verifies, not something a tutoring service performs, promises or accelerates, and nothing on this page should be read as a route around it. And no IB points threshold for equivalency is published here, because the figure circulating online could not be verified against moe.gov.ae. Check the current requirement on the Ministry's own page or with the attestation authority in your emirate before you plan a subject load around it.
