Verify on the Ministry's own page
No figure published here; the circulating number is unsourced

sections.heading: Academic honesty in a summer with no teacher watching
paragraphs: July is when the boundary gets tested, because school coursework deadlines sit in the autumn and the person supervising is on holiday. The position here is not negotiable. A tutor teaches, questions, models technique and gives written feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not author assessed work, does not supply finished answers for submission, and does not edit a draft to the point where the voice and the judgements are no longer the student's own.

This is a live problem in this market rather than a theoretical one. One site ranking for these queries sells finished Internal Assessments outright. Buying one is an academic-integrity breach that puts the student's own certification at risk, and no amount of tutoring hours makes it a sensible purchase. The honest version of coursework support is narrower and more useful: teaching the skill the task assesses, reading a draft the student wrote and naming what the criteria would reward, then handing it back.

The same boundary applies to materials. Board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and they are referenced and linked rather than reproduced or redistributed. Where a session works through a past paper, it works through the official document on screen. That is both the lawful position and, incidentally, the only version in which the student is looking at the real thing rather than at somebody's retyped approximation of it.
bullets: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work
No assessed work is authored, supplied or edited to completion
Board materials are cited and linked, never reproduced as downloads
Feedback is written down, so what was said can be checked later

process.title: Send the syllabus codes and the June report
process.description: Three things make the first session useful: the statement of entry or exam timetable showing the board and tier, the June report card, and one piece of recent marked work. Without the codes, planning starts from an assumption about which specification your child sits, and in Al Barsha that assumption is wrong about as often as it is right.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then a timed diagnostic
process.description: The trial is a real lesson, not a sales call, and no card details are needed to book it. If the match works, session one is a timed section of a past paper from the correct tier, marked against the published mark scheme while the student watches. That produces the error log everything else is planned from.

process.title: A written plan with one named output a week
process.description: You receive the sequence before the hours are booked: which topics, in which order, with what existing at the end of each week. A plan with named weekly outputs can be audited mid-summer. A plan that says revision and consolidation cannot, which is how six weeks disappear without anything measurable changing.

process.title: Fortnightly marked paper and a short note to you
process.description: Every second session ends with timed questions, marked and annotated. The note that follows is short and specific: what moved, what has not, and what the next fortnight targets. It is written so a parent who does not teach the subject can still tell whether the block is working.

process.title: Handover into September
process.description: The final session is a full paper under exam conditions, followed by a one-page handover naming the topics that are now secure, the ones still at risk and the command terms to watch. It is written for the student to take into the autumn term and, if the school asks, to show a teacher.

whyPoints.title: The diagnostic comes before the teaching
whyPoints.description: No topic is taught in week one. A timed section of the correct paper is sat and marked first, because the gap a parent describes and the gap the marks show are different often enough that starting from the description wastes the first fortnight of a nine-week window.

whyPoints.title: Specification, not subject
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are not the same course, and 0625 Physics is not 4PH1. Tutors are matched to the paper your child sits, and the first session confirms it from the statement of entry rather than from what the school is assumed to use.

whyPoints.title: Marked to the published mark scheme wording
whyPoints.description: Scripts are marked against the board's own criteria rather than a private rubric, and the mark scheme language is shown to the student. A student who has read what the examiner is paid to reward stops guessing what a four-mark answer looks like.

whyPoints.title: The schedule follows the family
whyPoints.description: July in Dubai means travel. Sessions run over live video anchored to Gulf Standard Time, so a block booked in June survives three weeks in London and a fortnight in Kerala without being rescheduled into nothing. The only fixed points are the tutor and the student.

whyPoints.title: Honest limits on what a tutor touches
whyPoints.description: Coursework and assessed work stay the student's own. Teaching, questioning and written feedback on a draft the student wrote are inside the line; authoring, supplying or finishing assessed work is outside it, and saying so plainly is a genuine difference in this particular search result.

whyPoints.title: Coverage disclosed, including the fallback
whyPoints.description: Some subject and tier combinations have thin availability in a UAE time zone during August. Where that happens you are told before booking, offered a specialist in another time zone with the session times that implies, or told to wait. No competitor page in this cluster discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: How many hours of IGCSE summer tuition does a Dubai student actually need?
faqs.answer: Thirty hours across the break is the most commonly booked block, which is two sessions a week for eight weeks with a little slack for travel. For a single weak topic, eight to ten hours is enough. For a student repairing two subjects, sixty hours is realistic and needs three sessions a week from the first week of July. The number that matters more than the total is the spacing: two sessions a week on one subject beats four sessions in one weekend, because the gap between them is where retention happens. Any provider quoting a fixed package without seeing a marked script is guessing.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting in July if my child only goes into Year 10 in September?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, but for a different reason than most families expect. A pre-Year 10 block is diagnostic rather than remedial. The useful question is whether the subject combination on the options form is a sensible load, and that is answered by seeing how the student handles early algebra, chemical calculation and extended writing under time. The output is a short written view on each candidate subject. That is worth more in Year 9 than content teaching, because the subjects chosen in September decide two years of work and the form is usually returned before anyone has tested the assumptions behind it.

faqs.question: We leave Dubai for six weeks in summer. Can the lessons continue from London or Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the main practical reason the sessions run over live video rather than in person. The schedule is anchored to Gulf Standard Time and converted for wherever the student is, so a 17:00 Dubai slot becomes 13:00 in London or 18:30 in Mumbai. What the student needs is a laptop, a stable connection and about forty minutes of quiet, which a hotel room supplies as well as a villa study. Sessions are recorded, so a week genuinely lost to a family event is recoverable rather than simply gone from a block you have already paid for.

faqs.question: Can my child resit an IGCSE in November rather than waiting a whole year?
faqs.answer: Pearson Edexcel offers International GCSE in a May or June series and again in November, so a November resit is a real route. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is the point a sixth-form place can be confirmed on a repaired grade. The constraint is entry, not teaching: entries go through a centre and close well ahead of the papers. Confirm the live timetable and the entry deadline on the board's own site, because provisional timetables are revised and a date restated on any tutoring page can be out of date.

faqs.question: What does summer IGCSE tuition cost per hour in Dubai this year?
faqs.answer: The Dubai market in October 2026 runs roughly like this. Budget online tutoring sits at AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to 300, and Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 because travel is priced into the hour. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Those are market figures from published sources, not an IB Gram price list; a quote follows the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry or the exam timetable the school issues carries the board name and the syllabus code, and that document is the only reliable source. School websites often name the board for the whole key stage while individual departments enter differently. Cambridge codes are four digits, such as 0580 for Mathematics or 0625 for Physics. Pearson codes start with a digit and two letters, such as 4MA1 or 4PH1. The distinction is not cosmetic: the papers differ in structure, tiering and the answer shapes the mark schemes reward, so revising the wrong one costs real marks in a real examination.

faqs.question: Should my child move from Core to Extended over the summer?
faqs.answer: The decision belongs to the school, but the summer is when the evidence for it can be gathered. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 awards grades C to G at Core and A* to E at Extended, so a Core entry caps the outcome regardless of how well the student prepares. The signal to look for is performance on Paper 4 questions drawn from topics already taught, under time. Respectable marks there argue for Extended even when the school is hesitant. Difficulty with Paper 2 alongside comfort on Paper 1 argues the other way, and a secure Core grade C beats an Extended grade E on any application.

faqs.question: Does summer tuition cover the IGCSE science practical papers?
faqs.answer: It covers the assessment, which is what carries the marks. Cambridge and Pearson both examine practical skills through a written paper rather than through observed laboratory work for most international candidates, and the lost marks are predictable: axes without units, a line of best fit forced through the origin, a conclusion that restates the readings instead of interpreting them, an evaluation that names an error without saying what it does to the result. All of that is teachable over a shared screen using the real past paper and real data. What a session cannot replace is the school laboratory time itself.

faqs.question: My child got a grade 4 in the June mock. Can that realistically move by next June?
faqs.answer: A two-grade movement over a full year is common when the starting point is technique rather than absent knowledge, which a marked script shows within one session. A grade 4 built on reasonable content knowledge and poor answer construction moves faster than a grade 4 built on three untaught topics. No honest tutor promises a specific grade, and anyone who does should be asked how they propose to control an examination they do not mark. What can be promised is measurement: timed questions every fortnight, marked to the board's criteria, so the trajectory is visible by October rather than guessed at in May.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Dubai families book most often in July?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first, by a wide margin, then Chemistry, Physics and English Language in roughly that order, with Biology and Additional Mathematics behind them. The pattern reflects where the specifications are least forgiving rather than where teaching is weakest. Mathematics punishes gaps from two years earlier, Chemistry punishes anyone shaky on the mole, Physics punishes weak algebra in disguise, and English Language punishes students who have never read a band descriptor. Economics and Business Studies arrive later in the year, usually in the term before the examination, because their problem is evaluation technique and that can be fixed faster.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit to teach my child over the summer?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, with its own service page titled Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help with my child's coursework while school is closed?
faqs.answer: Within a clear boundary, yes. A tutor teaches the skill the task assesses, explains what the published criteria reward, reads a draft the student has produced and names what is missing in writing. A tutor does not author assessed work, supply finished answers for submission, or edit a draft until the judgements stop being the student's own. That line matters in this market because at least one site ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments, which is an integrity breach that puts the student's own certification at risk. Written feedback on the student's own work is the version that is both lawful and useful.

faqs.question: For a UAE university application, how many of my child's IGCSE grades actually count?
faqs.answer: Five. The British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five, which catches families out, because a student with seven certificates of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education has exactly five that count. One competitor page states that six subjects are required, which does not match the rule. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae before planning a subject load.

faqs.question: Is online summer tuition genuinely as useful as having someone in the room?
faqs.answer: For IGCSE work it is a straight trade, and the trade favours video. What you lose is physical presence. What you gain is the specification match: instead of choosing from whoever lives nearby and is free at 17:00 in August, you choose from everyone who teaches that exact paper. Sessions use a shared whiteboard, a document camera so handwritten working is visible both ways, and the real past paper annotated live. They are recorded, which turns July into a revision archive the student still has in February. For a subject where a Cambridge answer differs from a Pearson one, that is not a close call.

faqs.question: What happens in the first session, and what should we send beforehand?
faqs.answer: Send three things: the statement of entry or exam timetable showing board and tier, the most recent report, and one piece of marked work. The first paid session is then a timed section of a past paper from the correct tier, marked against the published mark scheme while the student watches, which produces an error log classified by topic and command term. That log, not the report card, is what the written plan is built from. The free trial lesson sits before all of this and is a real lesson with a real tutor, booked without card details.

dubai/igcse-summer-tuition.closingHeading: Book the July block before the calendar fills
dubai/igcse-summer-tuition.closingBody: Dubai summers are short and awkwardly shaped: nine weeks on paper, five once travel is subtracted, and the specialists for Extended Mathematics and Chemistry 0620 are committed by the middle of June. Send the syllabus codes, the June report and one marked script, and the free trial lesson can be sat the same week. You will get a written plan with a named output for each week, a timed diagnostic marked against the board's own mark scheme, and a one-page handover in late August that tells your child exactly what September needs to address. Sessions run one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, from wherever the family happens to be.

dubai/igcse-to-ib-transition-course.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach both sides of this move: the IGCSE specification a student has just left and the Diploma course they are entering. Each profile names the subject, the Diploma level and whether the tutor works on Internal Assessment drafts, because the first IA is where this transition is usually won or lost.

intro.heading: The gap is not the content
paragraphs: Students arriving in the first Diploma year from IGCSE are rarely short of knowledge. They have sat externally marked written papers, they know how to revise, and in the sciences and mathematics they have covered a good deal of what the Diploma assumes. What they have not met is the shape of the qualification. Six subjects rather than nine. Three of them at a level with sixty per cent more published teaching hours. An internally assessed piece of work in every subject. A four thousand word independent essay. A course about knowledge itself. And a service and activity requirement with written reflections.

That list is the transition, and none of it is on an IGCSE specification. A student who scored well across nine IGCSEs by learning content and practising mark schemes meets, in the first term of the Diploma, a set of tasks that reward independence, planning and written judgement. The grades usually dip. Families interpret the dip as the student struggling with harder content, and spend money on content, and the dip persists because the content was never the problem.

A bridge block that works is built around the four new demands and one subject bridged hard, usually mathematics or a Higher Level science. It is short, six weeks is typical, and it should be bought for what it leaves behind rather than for reassurance. By the end there should be a marked task at genuine Diploma difficulty in the bridged subject, a draft research question for the Extended Essay, one criterion-marked piece of work so the student has seen criterion marking applied to their own writing, and a written note of the school's internal deadlines for the year.

That last item sounds administrative and is the single most valuable output. Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge deadlines are set by the school and fall long before the written papers, and families who do not have them written down discover them one at a time as crises. Asking for them in the first fortnight costs nothing and restructures the whole year.

The second thing a bridge block should test is the Higher Level choice. Levels are selected before any Diploma content has been taught, on IGCSE evidence that does not map cleanly onto Higher Level demand. A marked task at the real level, early in the first term, is the evidence a school will weigh if a change is needed, and schools run their own deadlines for level changes which pass quietly. A student who waits for the end-of-year internal examinations has usually waited too long.

Sessions are delivered online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, since that is an India-only service. For a transition block the online format has a specific advantage: comments on a first Internal Assessment draft are typed into the student's own document and stay there, which is both better feedback and a visible record of what support was given if the school asks.

Criterion marking replaces the mark scheme the student knows
The school's internal deadlines, written down in the first fortnight

dubai/igcse-to-ib-transition-course.programmesIntro: This move spans three points in a student's school career, and the useful work differs at each. These are the stages a Dubai family is buying for.

programmes.name: The IGCSE examination year, before the move
programmes.description: The cheapest point to prepare for the Diploma, and almost nobody uses it. Two things transfer directly: the habit of writing method and reasoning out in full, and an early look at what criterion marking means. Both are built in a handful of sessions and both pay across two years.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools confirm Diploma subject and level choices during Year 11, frequently before IGCSE results arrive. A marked task at Diploma difficulty in the candidate Higher Level subjects is better evidence for that choice than an IGCSE predicted grade.

programmes.name: Between the two qualifications
programmes.description: A short, narrow block works here and a content course does not. The useful content is the mathematical or scientific technique the Diploma assumes, plus one honest introduction to what an Internal Assessment is. Reading ahead through a Diploma textbook is usually wasted effort at this stage.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's long summer break and the number of families travelling make a fixed slot harder to hold than during term. Four sessions spread across the break, with work set between them, holds better than an intensive week that nobody completes.

programmes.name: The first Diploma year
programmes.description: Where the transition actually happens and where the dip appears. The first Internal Assessment, the first criterion-marked essay and the Extended Essay question all land in this year, alongside the school's level-change deadline. Support placed here changes submitted marks rather than revision feelings.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools run internal examinations towards the end of the first Diploma year, and those results are the first honest measurement. By then the level-change window has usually closed, which is why a marked task in the first term matters more than it sounds.

dubai/igcse-to-ib-transition-course.subjectsIntro: Below, each subject is described by what the Diploma adds to what an IGCSE student already holds, which is the only comparison that helps when planning a bridge block.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Builds directly on IGCSE Extended or Higher tier algebra and then goes much further into calculus and proof. An IGCSE student who worked mentally and wrote one line will lose method marks immediately, and the non-calculator paper demands fluency that IGCSE revision rarely builds.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Closer to IGCSE in computation and much further in statistics and modelling. The new demand is writing: stating what a result means in context, what the model assumes, and where it breaks. IGCSE mathematics asks for none of that.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content overlap with IGCSE is substantial and the assessment changes shape. Data-based questions carry more weight, extended responses require the accepted terminology, and the Internal Assessment demands an investigation designed by the student rather than a prescribed practical.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms go well beyond IGCSE, and Higher Level considerably further again. The practical element changes from an alternative-to-practical paper to a designed investigation assessed against criteria, which is a different task entirely.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The content step is manageable; the mathematical step is not always. Diploma physics assumes algebraic confidence that an IGCSE Core or Foundation route does not build, which is why a student's mathematics tier matters more for physics than their physics grade does.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Frequently new subjects at Diploma level, taken by students who did not sit them at IGCSE. That is usually fine, because the content starts from the beginning, but the evaluation demand is immediate and unfamiliar to anyone trained on IGCSE knowledge questions.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The source skills from IGCSE transfer well and the essay demand does not. Diploma essays require an argument sustained across an answer rather than a sequence of accurate paragraphs, and Higher Level adds a depth study and a further written component.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: An IGCSE First Language English student arrives with directed writing and reading analysis, and meets unseen guided analysis, comparative essay writing and an Individual Oral. The last of those is wholly new and is the component students most often underprepare.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: No IGCSE equivalent exists, and together they carry up to three of the forty-five points. Both are internally deadlined in the first Diploma year, which means they compete with settling into six new courses. Starting the Extended Essay question early is the cheapest intervention available.

dubai/igcse-to-ib-transition-course.regionsIntro: What location changes here is when a bridge block can realistically run, because the move happens across a long summer and into a busy first term. These notes cover the pattern across the city.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and Dubai Hills
regions.note: Large cohorts moving from IGCSE into the Diploma inside the same school group, so the level-choice window falls in the same weeks for many families. Weekend slots for a marked Diploma-difficulty task book out early in the first term.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: A high share of students moving from a British-curriculum school into an IB school elsewhere in the city, which means a new school as well as a new qualification. The internal deadline list matters doubly when nobody in the family knows the school yet.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Barsha Heights
regions.note: Short commutes make a weekday 16:30 session realistic, which suits a six-week bridge block in the first term. That is the period when the block is most useful and the slot least likely to be cancelled.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Long eastern commutes mean a first-term evening session finishes late and tired. A weekend block for the marked task plus a short midweek check on an Internal Assessment draft works better than two full weekday sessions.

regions.name: Downtown, Business Bay and Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Central towers close to two continuum IB schools, where students often arrive into the Diploma from an IGCSE route in a different emirate or country. Establishing which syllabus they actually sat is the first task rather than an assumption.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Sports City
regions.note: Many mid-year and mid-phase arrivals, so a student may be entering the Diploma without a settled IGCSE profile behind them. That changes a bridge block from technique work into genuine content work, and it should be said plainly.

sections.heading: The four demands an IGCSE student has never met
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an Internal Assessment: a piece of work produced by the student, marked against published criteria, contributing to the final grade. An IGCSE student may have met coursework in one or two subjects and has almost certainly never met six of them running simultaneously, each with its own criteria and its own school deadline. The first one arrives in the first Diploma year, and the mark it earns is banked before any revision begins.

The Extended Essay is four thousand words of independent research with a supervisor, a reflection requirement and a submission date in the first half of the final year in most schools. Nothing in an IGCSE programme prepares a student for a piece of work of that length chosen by themselves. The commonest failure is not writing it badly; it is choosing a question too broad to research and discovering that fact in month four.

Theory of Knowledge is a course about how knowledge is made and justified, assessed through an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. Students trained to answer questions with content find it disorienting, because there is no body of facts to learn. Together with the Extended Essay it contributes up to three points of the forty-five, which makes it worth more than most families assume.

CAS, the creativity, activity and service requirement, is a completion requirement rather than a graded one, with reflections recorded over the programme. It consumes time rather than marks, and students who leave the record until the final term create an administrative problem in the middle of examination preparation. The table below sets out all four with their deadline position and what late work costs.

sections.heading: Criterion marking against the mark scheme they know
paragraphs: An IGCSE student has been trained on mark schemes, and mark schemes are generous in a specific way: they list acceptable answers, and a student who produces one of them earns the mark. The relationship is transactional and learnable, which is why IGCSE revision rewards practice so directly. Criterion marking works differently. A criterion describes a quality of work at several levels, and the marker judges which description the work as a whole best fits.

The practical consequence is that a student cannot collect criterion marks point by point. An Internal Assessment with four correct results and no evaluation does not earn most of the available marks, because the criterion that rewards evaluation has nothing to judge. Conversely, a modest piece of work that addresses every criterion deliberately scores better than an impressive one that addresses three of them. Students find this unfair the first time and manageable the second.

The bridge is mechanical and takes one session. Give the student a criterion descriptor, in plain language, and a short piece of work, and ask them to decide which band it sits in and why. Then show them a band above and ask what would have to change. After doing that twice, a student reads their own draft differently, and that single shift is worth more than any amount of content teaching in the first term.

The second half of the bridge is the habit of writing against criteria rather than writing and hoping. Before producing a draft, list the criteria, write one line under each describing how the work will satisfy it, and keep that list visible while writing. It is unglamorous, it takes ten minutes, and it is the difference between a first Internal Assessment that reflects the student's ability and one that does not.

sections.heading: The subject-by-subject gap, mapped
paragraphs: Content overlap between IGCSE and the Diploma is larger than families expect in the sciences and mathematics, and smaller than they expect in the essay subjects. In biology and chemistry a great deal of IGCSE content reappears and is then extended, particularly at Higher Level. In mathematics the Extended or Higher tier is a genuine foundation and the Core or Foundation tier is not, which is the single most consequential piece of IGCSE history for a Diploma plan.

In the essay subjects the overlap is in skills rather than content. IGCSE history source handling transfers directly into Diploma source papers, and IGCSE First Language English directed writing transfers partially into Diploma written work. What does not transfer is the demand for a sustained argument: Diploma essays reward a line of reasoning held across an answer, where IGCSE often rewards accurate paragraphs in sequence.

Several Diploma subjects are new to most students, including economics, business management, psychology and environmental systems. That is usually not a problem, because the courses start from the beginning. The hidden cost is the evaluation demand, which arrives in the first term in all of them and is unfamiliar to a student trained on knowledge-recall questions.

The table maps the common routes with the gap and the realistic amount of support. The last column is deliberately modest: most of these gaps are weeks of work, not terms, provided they are named early rather than discovered in the mock results.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE grade does and does not predict
paragraphs: Families use IGCSE results to choose Diploma levels because they are the only evidence available, and they predict some things well and others badly. They predict content security reliably: a student with a strong grade in IGCSE Chemistry has the foundation that Diploma Chemistry assumes. They predict examination technique reasonably: a student who performed well under timed conditions will probably do so again.

What they do not predict is tolerance for independent work. The Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge all reward a student who can define a task for themselves, plan it and stick to a schedule nobody enforces daily. Nothing in an IGCSE programme measures that, and students with excellent grades frequently struggle with it while students with middling grades sometimes flourish.

They also do not predict the mathematics tier effect, which is the most mechanical and most ignored signal available. A student who sat Core or Foundation tier mathematics has not covered content that Diploma mathematics and Diploma physics both assume, and no amount of enthusiasm substitutes. That is a scheduling fact to plan around, not a judgement about ability, and it argues for either Applications and Interpretation or a substantial early block in mathematics.

The honest use of IGCSE results, then, is as one of three inputs. The second is a marked task at genuine Diploma difficulty in the candidate Higher Level subjects. The third is an honest conversation about independent work, which parents are usually better placed to assess than schools. Levels chosen on all three hold up considerably better than levels chosen on grades alone.

sections.heading: The six-week bridge block, week by week
paragraphs: A bridge block is short by design, because the purpose is to change habits and settle decisions rather than to pre-teach a two-year course. Six weeks is the shape that works in practice, and the value is in what exists at the end rather than in the hours spent. Each week should produce something a parent can look at without knowing the subject.

The first fortnight is diagnosis and administration. A marked task at genuine Diploma difficulty in one subject, which gives a baseline and a level signal, and a written list of every internal deadline the school has set for the year. The second of those is free and routinely skipped, and it is the item that most changes how the year runs.

The middle fortnight is criterion marking and the Extended Essay question. One piece of the student's own work marked against criteria so they have seen it applied to themselves, a session spent judging bands on somebody else's short piece, and a research question narrowed until it is small enough to actually investigate. A broad question is the single most common Extended Essay failure and it costs months.

The final fortnight is the bridged subject proper, with two marked tasks under timing so that movement is measurable rather than asserted. The block then ends. If the raw marks moved and the deadlines are written down and the Extended Essay question is settled, the transition has been bought properly, and whether to continue into weekly subject support becomes a separate decision made on evidence.

sections.heading: The level decision, tested while it can still change
paragraphs: Higher Level choices are made before any Diploma content has been taught, which means they are made on IGCSE evidence and on ambition. Schools then set their own deadlines for level changes, usually within the first Diploma year, and those deadlines pass without announcement. A student who finds Higher Level Chemistry unmanageable in October and waits for the end-of-year internal examinations to prove it has usually waited past the point of choice.

The evidence that works in that conversation is a marked task at genuine Higher Level difficulty, sat under timing, with the losses classified. A school can act on that. It cannot easily act on a parent's impression or a student's discouragement, both of which are common in the first term for reasons that have nothing to do with level fit. Producing that script in the first half of the first term is the whole point of testing early.

Where a change is appropriate, the arithmetic is often better than families fear. A candidate carrying a Higher Level at grade 4 with content unsecured may well reach grade 6 at Standard Level, which improves the point total, reduces load across the other five subjects, and costs less to support because Standard Level sits in a cheaper band. The exception is where a university offer names that subject at Higher Level, in which case a change satisfies the Diploma and fails the application.

Where a change is not appropriate or not possible, the plan changes rather than ending. Concentrate funded hours on the recoverable marks: written method, command terms, the Internal Assessment and the extra component Higher Level adds. Those produce movement regardless of whether the level was the ideal choice, and they are the marks a bridge block is best placed to reach.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with the first Internal Assessment
paragraphs: This is the part of the transition where boundaries matter most, because it is the first time an IGCSE student encounters assessed work produced outside examination conditions and the first time anybody offers to help with it inappropriately. Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work, and the IB treats submitted work that is not as malpractice, with the consequence falling on the student rather than on whoever was paid.

Inside that boundary a tutor can do a great deal, and it happens to be the part students find hardest. Explaining what a criterion descriptor actually asks for, in plain language, with an example drawn from a different topic. Questioning whether a research question can be investigated at the required depth. Pointing out that a control variable is not controlled, or that a measurement's uncertainty undermines the conclusion. Commenting on a draft by naming the criterion, the band it currently sits in, and what the band above requires.

What a tutor cannot do is write, rewrite or complete any part of it. One site competing for UAE coursework searches advertises completed Internal Assessments for a fixed fee, which is not tutoring and is a risk transfer running entirely the wrong way. A family paying for that buys a malpractice finding, and the student loses the qualification rather than the money.

Stating the boundary explicitly helps rather than restricts, and it is the main reason written comments in the student's own document are better than a verbal call. The comments are honest feedback, they are a visible record of what support was given, and your child's supervisor is entitled to ask. An answer that is comfortable to give is a good sign about the arrangement.

sections.heading: What this costs, and what to refuse
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates give the arithmetic. A qualified online subject tutor sits at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB work is quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, TutorChase at AED 270, and BartyED's premium named tier at AED 650. A six-week bridge block of six sessions therefore runs roughly AED 900 to 2,700, and a four-session Internal Assessment block around AED 800 to 1,800. Those are market figures, not IB Gram's; our rate is quoted after the free trial lesson with the session length and marking inclusion stated.

Refuse a transition course sold as a term of content across several subjects. The gap is not content, and a plan that treats it as content will bill for a term and leave the four new demands untouched. If a provider cannot name which artefacts the block produces, they are selling attendance at a Diploma-shaped lecture.

Refuse any offer to supply IB past papers, mark schemes or subject guides as downloads. Those belong to the International Baccalaureate, and privately circulated copies are frequently from superseded guides. The school's Diploma coordinator and the IB's own store are the routes, and for a transitioning student the coordinator is the better one anyway, since they also hold the deadlines.

Insist on three outputs in writing: the marked task with a raw mark and a date, the internal deadline list, and a statement of what the block will not reach. No success rate, average point score or satisfaction figure appears on this page, because none could be produced with a sample size, a date and a method, and no tutor can promise a Diploma score.

process.title: Find out which IGCSE the student actually sat
process.description: Board, syllabus code and tier for mathematics and the sciences specifically. The mathematics tier is the most consequential single fact for a Diploma plan, because Core or Foundation tier leaves content that Diploma mathematics and physics both assume, and no enthusiasm substitutes for it.

process.title: Collect every internal deadline in the first fortnight
process.description: Ask the Diploma coordinator for the Internal Assessment deadlines in all six subjects plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, and put them on one calendar. It costs an email and restructures the year before any habits have set.

process.title: Produce one marked task at real Diploma difficulty
process.description: In the candidate Higher Level subject, under timing, marked against the published standard, with the losses classified as content, command term, method or time. That script is the baseline, the level signal and the evidence a school will weigh if a change is needed.

process.title: Bridge criterion marking, then the Extended Essay question
process.description: One session judging bands on somebody else's short piece, one with the student's own work marked against criteria, and one narrowing the Extended Essay question until it could genuinely be investigated in four thousand words. Three sessions, three artefacts.

process.title: Close the block on a second marked task
process.description: Same subject, same conditions, same length as the first, with the two raw marks side by side. Then stop and decide separately whether weekly subject support is warranted, on the evidence rather than on momentum. A block that rolls on without that decision is a subscription.

whyPoints.title: We treat the gap as structural, not academic
whyPoints.description: Six subjects, criterion marking and four new assessed demands are the transition; content is largely continuous in the sciences and mathematics. A block aimed at content will bill for a term and leave the actual gap untouched, which is what most transition courses do.

whyPoints.title: The deadline list is a deliverable
whyPoints.description: Every internal deadline across six subjects and the core, written on one calendar in the first fortnight. It costs nothing, it is skipped by almost everyone, and it is the single change that most alters how a first Diploma year runs.

whyPoints.title: The level choice is tested while it can change
whyPoints.description: A marked task at genuine Higher Level difficulty in the first half of the first term, because the school's change deadline passes quietly and a parental impression is not evidence a coordinator can act on.

whyPoints.title: Criterion marking is taught, not described
whyPoints.description: The student judges bands on a short piece, then sees criteria applied to their own writing. Two sessions of that changes how they read every draft afterwards, which is worth more in the first term than any amount of pre-teaching.

faqs.question: What actually changes between IGCSE and the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: The structure, far more than the content. Six subjects instead of eight or nine, three of them at a level with sixty per cent more published teaching hours, an internally assessed piece of work in every subject, a four thousand word Extended Essay, a course about knowledge itself, and a service and activity requirement with written reflections. Content in the sciences and mathematics is largely continuous and then extended. Families who treat the move as a content problem spend on content and the difficulty persists, because the content was never the issue.

faqs.question: Does a strong set of IGCSE grades predict a strong Diploma score?
faqs.answer: Partly. They predict content security well and timed examination technique reasonably. They predict tolerance for independent work hardly at all, and that is exactly what the Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge reward. Students with excellent IGCSE results sometimes struggle with work nobody enforces daily, while students with middling results sometimes flourish. Use the grades as one input of three, alongside a marked task at real Diploma difficulty and an honest view of how the student handles self-directed work.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects map onto which Higher Level choices?
faqs.answer: Extended or Higher tier mathematics maps reasonably onto Analysis and Approaches; Core or Foundation tier does not, and that single fact also constrains Diploma physics, which assumes algebraic confidence. IGCSE Biology and Chemistry map onto the same subjects at either level, with real content extension at Higher Level. IGCSE History and Geography transfer their source skills and not their essay style. Several Diploma subjects such as economics and psychology are new to most students, which is fine because they start from the beginning.

faqs.question: What are the four new components my child has never met?
faqs.answer: The Internal Assessment in each of six subjects, marked against published criteria with a school deadline in each. The Extended Essay, four thousand words of independent research with a supervisor and a reflection requirement. Theory of Knowledge, assessed through an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title, which with the Extended Essay carries up to three of the forty-five points. And CAS, a completion requirement with recorded reflections that consumes time rather than marks. All four are internally deadlined before the written papers.

faqs.question: Should a bridge block run over the summer or in the first term?
faqs.answer: The first term, for most families. Over the summer the useful work is narrow: the mathematical or scientific technique the Diploma assumes, and one honest introduction to what an Internal Assessment is. Almost everything else needs the school's actual deadlines, the real subject teachers and real tasks, none of which exist in August. The first term also coincides with the school's level-change window, which is the decision a block can most usefully inform while it is still open.

faqs.question: What evidence should a transition course produce each week?
faqs.answer: Something a parent can look at without knowing the subject. A marked script with a raw mark, a date and the conditions it was sat under. A band judgement the student wrote themselves. Comments on a draft naming the criterion letter and the band. A written deadline list. A research question that could genuinely be investigated in four thousand words. If a week produced only a conversation about settling in, that is worth one week and should not be the pattern across six.

faqs.question: How is criterion marking different from a mark scheme?
faqs.answer: A mark scheme lists acceptable answers, so a student who produces one earns the mark; the relationship is transactional and learnable, which is why IGCSE practice works so directly. A criterion describes a quality of work at several levels, and the marker judges which description the work as a whole best fits. The practical consequence is that criterion marks cannot be collected point by point: an Internal Assessment with correct results and no evaluation loses the marks that reward evaluation, because that criterion has nothing to judge.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's first Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Within a boundary worth stating plainly. A tutor can explain what a criterion descriptor asks for, question whether a research question can be investigated at the required depth, point out an uncontrolled variable, and comment on a draft by naming the criterion, the band it sits in and what the band above needs. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or complete any part of it. The work must be the student's own, and the consequence of breaching that falls on the student rather than on whoever was paid.

faqs.question: Is it worth preparing for Theory of Knowledge in advance?
faqs.answer: A little, and not in the way families expect. There is no content to pre-learn, so reading a textbook achieves nothing. What helps is one session on the kind of question the course asks, so a student arriving from a content-driven qualification understands that answers are arguments about how claims are justified rather than recollections of facts. Beyond that, the useful preparation is the Extended Essay question, because the two compete for the same weeks and the essay has the harder deadline.

faqs.question: My child took Core tier IGCSE mathematics. Can they do Diploma mathematics?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the realistic route is Applications and Interpretation, usually at Standard Level, unless a substantial early block closes the algebra gap. Core tier omits content that Analysis and Approaches assumes from the first weeks, and the same gap constrains Diploma physics, which is why the mathematics tier matters more for the physics grade than the physics grade does. This is a scheduling fact rather than a judgement, and naming it before levels are confirmed prevents two difficult years.

faqs.question: Do you run transition sessions at our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, since that is an India-only service, and all sessions are delivered online over live video. For a transition block that is genuinely the better format. Comments on a first Internal Assessment draft are typed into the student's own document and stay there, which is both clearer feedback and a visible record of what help was given if the supervisor asks. Marked scripts and raw marks also accumulate in one place across the block.

faqs.question: How long should a bridge block be, and what does it cost?
faqs.answer: Six sessions is the shape that works, aimed at one subject plus criterion marking and the Extended Essay question. At published Dubai bands of AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified online tutor and AED 200 to 450 and above for a specialist, that is roughly AED 900 to 2,700. A separate four-session Internal Assessment block runs about AED 800 to 1,800. Those are market figures from Unitors, TutorChase and Bestimate rather than ours, and any quote should state session length and whether marking is included.

faqs.question: Should my child read ahead through a Diploma textbook over the summer?
faqs.answer: Mostly no. Reading ahead without tasks, feedback or a teacher produces familiarity rather than capability, and in criterion-assessed work familiarity earns nothing. The summer is better spent on two narrow things: the algebraic or scientific technique the Diploma assumes and the student may not have, and the habit of writing method and reasoning out in full rather than working mentally. Both are small, both transfer directly, and both are worth more in September than fifty pages of pre-reading.

faqs.question: What if the Higher Level choice turns out to be wrong?
faqs.answer: Act while the school's change window is open, which is usually within the first Diploma year and passes without announcement. Produce a marked task at genuine Higher Level difficulty so the school has evidence it can act on, and check whether any university route names that subject at Higher Level before changing anything. Where no offer names it and content is the real problem, moving to Standard Level can raise the point total, reduce load across five other subjects and cost less to support at the same time.

faqs.question: Is an IGCSE student at a disadvantage against a classmate from the MYP?
faqs.answer: They start with different strengths rather than a deficit. An IGCSE student arrives with stronger externally examined technique: timed writing, mark scheme awareness, revision discipline. An MYP student arrives having been criterion-marked for several years and is more comfortable with internally assessed work and with reflection. Over two years both gaps close. The IGCSE student's gap closes faster if criterion marking is bridged deliberately in the first term rather than learned slowly through disappointing Internal Assessment marks.

dubai/igcse-to-ib-transition-course.closingHeading: Buy the block for what it leaves behind
dubai/igcse-to-ib-transition-course.closingBody: A transition block is worth paying for when it produces four things: a marked task at genuine Diploma difficulty with a raw mark and a date, a written list of every internal deadline the school has set for the year, one piece of the student's own work marked against criteria so they have seen the shift, and an Extended Essay question narrow enough to research. Book the free trial lesson, bring the IGCSE board and tier for mathematics and the sciences, and ask which of those four the block will deliver and by when. Then close it on a second marked task and decide what comes next from the two raw marks.

dubai/igcse-tuition.tutorsIntro: Each of these tutors works to a named specification rather than a subject label, because a Cambridge paper and an Edexcel paper on the same topic reward different things. Tell us the code on the entry form and the match follows from it.

intro.heading: Two boards, one subject name, and the mistake that follows
paragraphs: A Dubai parent who asks for IGCSE Maths tuition has given a tutor roughly half the information needed. Cambridge International runs Mathematics as syllabus 0580, tiered Core and Extended, with its own paper structure and its own house style of question. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE Mathematics as specification 4MA1, tiered Foundation and Higher, with a different paper split and a different relationship between the formula sheet and the recall expected. Both appear on Dubai school reports as IGCSE Maths. A tutor who prepares a student for the wrong one will teach correct mathematics and waste a term.

This happens more in Dubai than in most cities, for a structural reason. The emirate licenses 17 different curricula across its private schools, and British-curriculum provision is the largest single block by enrolment. Within that block, schools choose boards subject by subject. A single Year 11 can be entered for Cambridge sciences, Edexcel Mathematics and a Cambridge first-language English, and nothing on a termly report makes that obvious. The information lives on the options form and the exam entry letter.

So the first job of this page is to make the board map legible. The second is to translate it into the two decisions that follow: which tier to sit, and which subjects to count. Both have consequences well beyond the exam. Tiering sets a grade ceiling that sixth-form admissions read. Subject selection interacts with the Ministry of Education's equivalency rule, which on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, and which excludes Arabic and Islamic education from that count.

The third job is to be clear about what tuition can and cannot do inside that structure. It can teach a specification properly. It can convert a score into a cause and attack the cause. It cannot change a tier the school has entered, it cannot promise a grade, and it cannot shortcut an equivalency process run by a ministry. Any service that suggests otherwise is selling something other than teaching.

IB Gram arranges this as one-to-one tuition delivered live over video, timed to Gulf Standard Time and scheduled around a Dubai school week. We do not operate home visits in Dubai or elsewhere in the UAE - that is a service we run only in India. The practical consequence for a family is that board specialism beats proximity: a Cambridge 0620 Chemistry teacher is matched to a household in Al Qusais on exactly the same terms as one in Jumeirah, because nobody is driving anywhere.

What follows is arranged as a reference rather than a pitch. There is a table comparing the two boards across the subjects Dubai schools enter most, a table separating the three different grade thresholds a family has to track, and a table setting out retake windows against the deadlines that govern them. Between them sit the sections on subject count, on arriving mid-course from another system, and on what a tutor may and may not do with a coursework component. If you read only one part, read the first section, because knowing which board your child is entered for changes every decision after it.

dubai/igcse-tuition.programmesIntro: Three programme structures account for nearly every IGCSE entry in Dubai. They differ in how units are banked, when retakes are possible, and how much of the grade is decided on a single morning.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, linear entry
programmes.description: All papers in a subject sat in one series, with the grade decided across that set. Subjects carry four-digit codes and most sciences and mathematics are tiered Core and Extended, with Core capping the grade available. Cambridge offers a June series and a November series to UAE centres - the February and March sitting is an India-only option that a Dubai candidate cannot take - and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai centres sit June as the main series, with November used chiefly for retakes and private candidates. Because Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used, the school's own published timetable is the only version a Dubai family should plan against.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, including modular routes
programmes.description: Identified by codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1, with Mathematics tiered Foundation and Higher. Several specifications are available in a modular structure, so units can be sat and banked across series rather than everything resting on one window. Exams run in May/June and November, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series.
programmes.countryNote: Modularity is the practical argument for Edexcel in a transient city. A student arriving in Dubai mid-course, or one whose first attempt at a unit went badly, can bank a result and re-sit a component without re-sitting the subject. The November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, which is a real window for a Dubai Year 12 needing one grade lifted.

programmes.name: Mixed-board entry across one student's subject set
programmes.description: Not a programme the boards publish, but the arrangement many Dubai schools actually use: Cambridge for the separate sciences, Edexcel for Mathematics, and either board for English depending on the cohort. It is a reasonable choice by a school optimising for each department's strengths, and it creates a planning problem for the family because two sets of entry deadlines, two grading conventions and two timetables apply at once.
programmes.countryNote: The fix is administrative rather than academic: one page listing each subject, its board, its code, its tier and its series, taped inside a folder. Most of the avoidable chaos in a Dubai Year 11 comes from nobody having written that page down.

programmes.name: What IGCSE grades are for: A Level and IB Diploma entry
programmes.description: Dubai sixth forms set subject-specific IGCSE bars, commonly a grade 6 or 7 in the same subject before A Level, with IB Diploma Higher Level pitched similarly. Those bars are published by the school rather than by the board, and they are the reason tiering matters: a capped grade can be a perfectly good result and still fall below an entry requirement.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. More sixth-form capacity does not loosen subject bars; it widens the choice of where to meet them.

dubai/igcse-tuition.subjectsIntro: The subject notes below are written around the board difference, because that is where Dubai families lose time. Each one names what changes between Cambridge and Pearson and what a tutoring hour should therefore be spent on.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The tier names differ and so do the papers. Cambridge Extended runs two papers with a heavier emphasis on structured multi-step questions; Edexcel Higher splits across two papers with its own formula provision. Working shown line by line earns method marks on both, and that single habit is worth more than any topic revision in either specification.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge tiers the subject and sets an Alternative to Practical paper; Edexcel's structure handles practical skills differently and weights its papers differently. Electromagnetic induction and circuit analysis are where marks go in both. A tutor should be able to say which paper carries what percentage before the first session.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations with limiting reagents and percentage yield sit in the Extended and Higher content rather than the Core. The qualitative-analysis tables differ in presentation between boards, which trips students who revise from the wrong board's notes - a common failure in Dubai, where sibling sets often sit different boards.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Very similar content, materially different question style. Cambridge rewards precision against its own syllabus statements; Edexcel asks more extended-response application. A student revising from the other board's past papers will meet unfamiliar phrasing in the exam and read it as unfamiliar content, which costs confidence as well as marks.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Both assess reading and directed writing, with mark tariffs attached to content points on the summary tasks. Cambridge 0500 and the Edexcel specification differ in text provision and coursework options, and some Dubai schools enter a coursework route while others do not. Timing discipline moves these grades faster than vocabulary work.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A separate specification with its own mark profile, entered by Dubai schools according to the cohort rather than the individual. Students moved from 0510 to 0500 part-way through a course - frequent in a city with this much school transfer - meet a reading paper that assumes practice they have not had, and that gap is the whole tutoring brief.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Data-response and case-study questions carry the marks on both boards. The standing loss is a correct definition applied to no particular firm. Evaluation marks need a judgement with a reason attached, which is a writing habit rather than knowledge, and it is teachable inside a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the quiet mark-earner: axes labelled, curves named, the shift shown and the new equilibrium marked. Students who can explain the economics verbally and draw it loosely lose marks they never notice losing. Gulf-relevant examples make the application marks easier to reach.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: The written papers test pseudocode to the board's own convention, trace tables and data representation rather than coding fluency. A student fluent in Python will still drop marks writing pseudocode the wrong way. Dubai schools sometimes enter Computer Science and ICT with different boards, which changes the practical component entirely.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study recall is necessary and insufficient. The top band requires the source or figure interrogated and a conclusion that answers the question set. Fieldwork and skills components differ between boards, so a tutor needs to know which paper your child sits before promising anything about preparation.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because expectations and the language of instruction differ. IGCSE Arabic is a separate examination sitting alongside that requirement, and the two are regularly confused on a report.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.levels: Single tier, entered by a minority of schools
subjects.description: Calculus and series arriving two years early, taken by students heading for A Level Maths or Further Maths. This is the clearest case where the pool of tutors who have actually taught the specification is small in any one part of Dubai, and where matching over video rather than by neighbourhood is the only way to reach one.

dubai/igcse-tuition.regionsTitle: Where the families asking about IGCSE tuition in Dubai live
dubai/igcse-tuition.regionsIntro: These districts are listed because their school mix shapes which board questions come up, not because a tutor sits in any of them. Delivery is over video, so the match is made on the specification.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Muhaisnah
regions.note: A dense mixed-curriculum belt where British, Indian and Ministry-curriculum schools share the same streets. Households here frequently have children on two different boards at once, which is where the mixed-entry confusion is most acute.

regions.name: The Springs, The Meadows and The Views
regions.note: Established villa communities feeding a small number of long-standing British-curriculum schools. Requests here cluster around tier decisions in Year 10 rather than emergency Year 11 work.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: Short distances but severe single-road congestion at school-run times. Families here are unusually willing to schedule late evening sessions, which suits tutors working from other time zones.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens and The Gardens
regions.note: Apartment districts with a high proportion of mid-year arrivals. Students joining a two-year IGCSE course in its second year are the typical case, and board familiarity rather than content is usually the gap.

regions.name: Town Square and Remraam
regions.note: Newer outlying communities where the school commute is the longest part of the day. Sessions realistically start after 6:30pm, and Friday morning blocks are more popular here than anywhere else in the city.

regions.name: International City and Al Nahda
regions.note: Price-sensitive districts where the published market range for tutoring matters most. Families here ask about session length and frequency before they ask about tutor credentials, which is a reasonable order.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis
regions.note: Schools and universities adjacent to each other, with households already comfortable with screen-based learning. Computer Science and ICT board differences come up here more than elsewhere.

regions.name: Al Khawaneej and Mirdif
regions.note: Villa districts on the eastern edge, where the drive to a tutor in central Dubai was historically the deciding objection. Removing the journey changes the economics of weekly tuition entirely.

schoolClusters.city: Deira, Al Qusais and the eastern districts
schoolClusters.note: A long-established schooling belt with the widest board mix in the emirate. Students we support from these catchments most often arrive with a Cambridge science entry and an Edexcel mathematics entry, and no clear record of which is which.
schools: GEMS Our Own English High School

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Living, Motor City and Sports City
schoolClusters.note: Villa and townhouse communities built around their schools, with settled cohorts and published sixth-form entry bars. Tier conversations in Year 10 dominate the requests from this cluster.

schoolClusters.city: Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens and Jebel Ali
schoolClusters.note: High residential turnover and a steady flow of students joining courses part-way through. Board familiarity, past-paper style and mark-scheme convention are the recurring requests rather than new content.

dubai/igcse-tuition.modesIntro: Three session patterns cover the board-specific work families ask for. All of them run as live video lessons; none involves a tutor attending a UAE address.

modes.title: Specification-matched weekly tuition
modes.description: One or two fixed slots a week on a single named specification. The tutor works from the board's published syllabus and past papers for that code, not from a generic subject plan, and the session note records which syllabus statements were covered. This is the format for a student on a two-year course who wants the grade secured rather than rescued.
bullets: Tutor confirmed against the specification code before the first lesson
Session notes reference the board's own syllabus statements
Past-paper practice drawn from the correct board and series
Tier review once a term with the marked evidence attached

modes.title: Board-transfer catch-up
modes.description: For students who have changed school, country or board mid-course - the single most common Dubai scenario. The work is a mapping exercise first: what the new specification contains that the old one did not, which topics are assessed differently, and which revision material the student now has to stop using.
bullets: Gap map between the two specifications, written down
Question-style retraining on the new board's past papers
Explicit list of old material to set aside
Realistic timeline, including when a series change is the better answer

modes.title: Retake and modular planning
modes.description: Where a single grade needs lifting for a sixth-form condition, the planning question comes before the teaching question: which series, which board, which components, and what the entry deadline is. Pearson's modular routes sometimes allow a component re-sit rather than a whole-subject repeat, and that distinction changes the workload completely.
bullets: Series and deadline identified before any teaching is booked
Component-level rather than subject-level planning where the board allows it
Private-candidate entry route explained, with the centre's own rules checked
Honest assessment of whether the available weeks are enough

sections.heading: How to find out which board your child is actually entered for
paragraphs: Three documents answer this, and the school report is the least reliable of them. The options form signed in Year 9 names the subjects but often not the board. The termly report usually says 'IGCSE Mathematics' and stops there. The document that settles it is the exam entry statement issued before final entries close, which lists each subject with its code, its tier and its series. Ask the exams officer for it by name; every Dubai centre produces one.

Failing that, the codes are recognisable on sight. Cambridge uses four digits: 0580, 0620, 0625, 0610, 0500, 0510, 0450, 0455, 0460, 0478. Pearson Edexcel uses a digit, two letters and a digit: 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1, 4EA1, 4BS1, 4EC1, 4GE1. If a textbook cover, a worksheet header or a past paper in your child's folder carries one of those strings, you have your answer for that subject - though not necessarily for the others, because mixing boards across a subject set is normal in this emirate.

It is worth doing this before you book anything. A tutor who is told 'IGCSE Physics, Year 11, Dubai' will prepare competently for whichever board they know best. A tutor told '0625 Extended, June series, mocks in February' will plan the term around the right papers. The difference between those two briefings is the difference between a useful term and a pleasant one, and it costs one email to the exams officer.

The same document resolves the tier question, which parents often do not realise has already been decided. Entries are made at a tier, and by the time the entry statement exists the school has committed. If you want that revisited, the conversation has to happen before the final entry deadline, and for a Dubai candidate that deadline belongs to a June or a November series. Cambridge entries close months ahead of the first paper - in the spring for the June papers, and before the autumn term is properly under way for November - which is why a tier conversation opened in the second term of Year 11 is usually a conversation opened too late. The exact closing date for your series is printed on the centre's statement of entry, and it is worth reading the moment it arrives rather than the week of the first exam.
bullets: Ask the exams officer for the exam entry statement by name
Cambridge codes are four digits; Edexcel codes read like 4MA1
Mixed boards across one student's subjects are normal in Dubai
Tier is fixed at entry, so any challenge must precede the entry deadline

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel, subject by subject
paragraphs: The two boards are not harder or easier than one another in any way a parent can act on, and anyone who tells you otherwise is guessing. What they are is different in structure: in how many papers a subject carries, in how tiering is named and handled, in how practical skills are assessed, and in whether components can be banked across series. Those differences change what a tutoring hour should contain.

The table below compares the subjects Dubai schools enter most. Read it as a planning document rather than a league table. The useful column is the last one, because it names the thing a tutor should be doing differently depending on which paper your child will open in the exam hall.

One structural difference deserves emphasis for Dubai specifically. Pearson's modular availability in some specifications means a unit can be sat, banked and re-sat without repeating the whole subject. In a city where families relocate mid-course and students arrive in Year 11 having done Year 10 somewhere else, that flexibility is worth real money. Cambridge's linear structure, by contrast, concentrates everything into one series, which is simpler to plan for and less forgiving of a bad fortnight.

The second difference worth a parent's attention is how practical skills reach the paper. Cambridge sets an Alternative to Practical paper in the tiered sciences, which assesses experimental method in writing: naming the independent and dependent variables, identifying controls, reading instruments, spotting anomalies and proposing improvements. That is a distinct skill with its own vocabulary, and it is taught explicitly or not at all. Pearson distributes practical assessment differently across its science papers. A tutor who has prepared students for one and not the other will teach the right science in the wrong register, and the marks will show it.

Tiering is the third. Cambridge's Core and Extended split applies across several subjects and caps the grade available at Core; Pearson tiers Mathematics as Foundation and Higher and runs most other International GCSE subjects at a single tier. A family comparing two children, or comparing a current report with an older sibling's, is often comparing a tiered entry with an untiered one and reading a difference in grades that reflects structure rather than ability.

sections.heading: Reading the grade: 9-1, A*-G and what a Dubai sixth form asks for
paragraphs: Two grading scales are in circulation and Dubai families see both. Several specifications report on a 9 to 1 numeric scale; others still report A* to G. A school may use one scale for some subjects and the other for the rest, depending on board and specification. Parents comparing a sibling's results from three years ago to a current report are frequently comparing two different scales without realising it.

What matters practically is the entry bar on the other side. Dubai sixth forms publish subject-specific IGCSE requirements - commonly a grade 6 or 7, or the equivalent letter, in the same subject before A Level, with IB Diploma Higher Level pitched similarly. Those bars are set by the school, not by the board, and they are the only figure that should drive a tiering decision. Ask for them in writing before Year 10 entries are finalised.

The third number in the picture is the Ministry of Education's equivalency threshold, which is far lower than people assume and serves a completely different purpose. On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement; the sourced rule says five.

So a student can clear equivalency comfortably and still miss a sixth-form entry bar by two grades. These are separate processes with separate purposes, and conflating them is how families end up either complacent or panicked for no reason. Equivalency is administered by the Ministry; verify your own case through the Ministry's own channel rather than through any tutoring service.
