dubai/igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Dubai families meet international GCSEs through two awarding organisations and occasionally a third qualification alongside them. The differences are not cosmetic: codes, papers, tiering and grading scales all vary, and so does the exam calendar.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The most widely taught international GCSE in this market. Subjects carry four-digit syllabus codes, several are tiered into Core and Extended with different papers and different available grades, and the sciences offer either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. Results are reported on the A* to G scale internationally.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs a June and a November series and allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, warning that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A Dubai parent should know which zone their school sits in before they plan anything around a published timetable.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes begin with a 4, such as 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1 for Physics and 4EA1 for English Language A. Mathematics A is tiered into Foundation and Higher, most other subjects are untiered so one paper set serves the whole ability range, and results are reported on the 9 to 1 scale. Assessment is predominantly or wholly examined in the subjects Dubai schools run most often.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE examinations in May or June and in November each year. Its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so plan against the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level
programmes.description: Still offered in some subjects and still taken in parts of this region, usually where a school has a long-established pathway. Papers and grading differ from the IGCSE equivalent, so a tutor matched for an IGCSE syllabus is not automatically the right match for the O Level version of the same subject.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs O Level examinations in the same June and November series as the IGCSE. If a Dubai school enters candidates for O Level in a subject, ask for the specific syllabus code, because the specimen material and mark schemes a tutor should be working from are different documents.

programmes.name: The post-16 step
programmes.description: Not an IGCSE qualification, but the destination for a large share of Dubai IGCSE candidates and the reason tier and grade decisions at sixteen matter. International A Level subjects assume specific IGCSE content, most sharply in mathematics and the sciences, and a Core-tier entry can close a route without anyone saying so.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no lower than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five.

dubai/igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Dubai schools run a recognisable core of IGCSE subjects, and tutoring demand concentrates in a short list of them. Syllabus codes matter here: they decide which papers a student sits and which specimen material a tutor should be teaching from.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 · Cambridge International Maths 0607
subjects.description: The highest-demand subject in this market by a clear margin. Cambridge 0580 Core sits on Papers 1 and 3, Extended on Papers 2 and 4, with different available grades. Most marks are lost on method presentation and on questions that require translating a sentence into an equation.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main maths syllabus by students heading for A Level Mathematics or Further Mathematics. A genuinely thin specialist market in Dubai, which is one of the few places at IGCSE where scarcity moves a quote noticeably.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0625 offers a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, and the alternative paper is its own skill rather than a softer option. Electricity and the quantitative questions carry the heaviest losses; unit handling and rearrangement account for a surprising share of them.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic chemistry are the recurring difficulties. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards precision about apparatus and about what an observation does and does not show, which is teachable and routinely untaught.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Deceptively content-heavy, and the subject where students most often mistake familiarity for knowledge. Extended-response questions on transport, respiration and genetics reward sequencing and command-term precision over volume of recall.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Single-award and double-award routes that cover all three sciences in less depth. These are a sensible choice for many students and a quiet constraint for a few, because certain post-16 science routes assume separate-science content. Worth checking before Year 10 rather than after.

subjects.name: English First Language
subjects.description: Reading and directed writing rather than literature. Marks are lost on reading questions where candidates summarise instead of selecting, and on writing tasks where register and audience are ignored. The fastest-moving English component with a weekly reader.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: 0510 carries a speaking endorsement reported separately; 0511 counts the speaking component into the grade. Which code a school enters matters to a student's final certificate, so establish it before planning any speaking preparation.

subjects.name: Literature in English
subjects.description: Set-text work where essays rise or fall on quotation integration and on answering the question asked rather than the question rehearsed. The subject most improved by a tutor who marks writing weekly rather than discussing texts.

subjects.name: Business Studies, Economics and Accounting
subjects.description: Heavily taken across Dubai schools and heavily tutored. Application and evaluation carry the marks: candidates who define terms accurately and then fail to apply them to the case material plateau in the middle bands regardless of how much they know.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Two different subjects frequently confused when a family books help. Computer Science is algorithmic and includes pseudocode and problem decomposition; ICT is applied and practical. Matching to the wrong one wastes a block of hours.

subjects.name: Arabic, Geography and History
subjects.description: Arabic as a first language and as a foreign language are separate syllabuses with separate codes, and KHDA requires Dubai schools to stream Arabic provision by group in any case. Geography and History reward case-study specificity, which is exactly what thin revision notes remove.

dubai/igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: In a cost conversation, geography matters for one reason: it decides how much of an in-home hour is actually teaching. The communities below differ sharply on that, and the difference is money rather than convenience.

regions.name: Emirates Hills, The Meadows and The Lakes
regions.note: Low-density villa communities with long internal roads and limited through-traffic. A visiting tutor loses the most time here, and in-home quotes in these communities sit towards the upper half of the published Dubai band as a result.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JBR and JLT
regions.note: Apartment-dense with a large resident tutor pool, so in-home rates are more competitive here than almost anywhere else in the emirate. The constraint is parking and building access rather than drive time.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
regions.note: Established eastern family districts with heavy Year 10 and 11 populations and strong demand for Arabic first language alongside maths and the sciences. Quotes here are typically lower than in the western villa communities.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, Dubai Hills Estate and Mudon
regions.note: Family villa communities with schools inside or beside the gate. Session timing is set by after-school activities rather than traffic, which pushes demand into a narrow 16:30 to 18:00 window and makes those slots the most expensive to book.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle, Jumeirah Village Triangle and Al Furjan
regions.note: Fast-growing mid-market communities with large Year 10 and 11 cohorts and the highest sensitivity to price in the emirate. This is where monthly package pricing is marketed hardest and where converting it to a per-hour figure pays off most.

regions.name: Business Bay, Downtown Dubai and Dubai Creek Harbour
regions.note: Central apartment districts where parents commute late, so evening slots after 19:00 are more commonly requested than elsewhere. Later slots attract a premium from in-home providers and none from online ones.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Mixed housing beside a school and university cluster, with a resident pool of postgraduate students. This is where the lowest advertised rates in the emirate turn up, and where checking what the hour actually contains matters most.

regions.name: Jebel Ali, Dubai Investments Park and Dubai South
regions.note: The longest internal commutes in Dubai. An in-home tutor crossing to these communities at 17:00 is adding a substantial unbilled or half-billed journey, which is why providers either decline the area or price it at the top of the band.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: Long-established British-curriculum secondaries running IGCSE at sixteen before splitting into A Level or the Diploma. Tutoring demand from this cluster concentrates in Extended-tier maths and the separate sciences, which is the more expensive end of the subject mix.

schoolClusters.city: Academic City, Dubai Festival City and the eastern corridor
schoolClusters.note: A mix of Cambridge and Pearson centres, which is why families in this cluster are the most likely to arrive not knowing which board their child is entered with. Establishing the awarding organisation and the syllabus code is the first thing any quote should depend on.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha South, Motor City and Dubai Sports City
schoolClusters.note: Newer and mid-market secondaries with large year groups, where students commonly sit nine or ten subjects. This is the cluster where the which-two-to-fund question is sharpest, because the subject count makes funding everything impossible on any normal budget.

dubai/igcse-tutor.modesIntro: What a family buys at IGCSE should follow the stage of the course rather than a standard weekly template. A Year 10 autumn gap and a Year 11 February emergency are different purchases at different prices.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one in one subject
modes.description: The default and usually the right starting point. Sixty minutes a week in the single subject carrying the most available marks, taught against the named syllabus code and its specimen papers. Each session ends with marked work and a specific instruction for the week, which is what separates teaching from supervision at this level.
bullets: One subject, one syllabus code, one named weakness
Timed question practice marked against the published mark scheme
A weekly note so a parent can see what moved
Reviewed at six weeks against the diagnostic from the trial

modes.title: A ten-hour diagnostic and repair block
modes.description: Bought as a finite block rather than an open subscription, usually when a mock result has arrived and nobody knows what it means. The first hour is diagnosis, the next eight are the two or three highest-value repairs it identified, and the last reviews against a fresh timed paper. Then the family decides again.

Prioritised by available marks rather than by topic order
A defined end, so the spend does not drift
Suits Year 11 from January onwards

modes.title: Two subjects in alternate weeks
modes.description: A way of covering two subjects on one subject's budget, and the right answer less often than families hope. It works where both gaps are narrow and well diagnosed. It fails where either subject needs weekly marked writing, because a fortnight between pieces is long enough for the habit not to form.

Not suitable for English or Literature writing work
Costs the same as one weekly subject
Reviewed at eight weeks rather than six

modes.title: A final-stretch block before the series
modes.description: Concentrated work in the weeks before the June or November papers, built around the specific components with the most recoverable marks and timed under real conditions. Scheduled against the live official timetable for the school's Cambridge zone or Pearson series rather than against a restated date.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE tutor in Dubai costs per hour
paragraphs: An IGCSE tutor in Dubai costs between roughly AED 33 and roughly AED 650 an hour according to published figures read in October 2026, and the useful bands inside that spread are narrower than the extremes suggest. A qualified subject teacher working online publishes rates in the region of AED 150 to AED 300. A tutor travelling to a Dubai address is quoted between about AED 180 and AED 500 once the journey is inside the number. The low thirties to sixties band is almost entirely university students, and the top of the range is aimed at examination candidates at post-16 level rather than at Year 11.

Three of the six most visible competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and two of the ones that do quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family transacts in. One publishes an hourly figure in its page copy that contradicts the price range in its own structured data. That is why this table exists. Each row names the provider that published the figure and the month it was read, and nothing in it is an IB Gram price.

Where IGCSE sits inside that spread is specific. It is generally quoted below Diploma and A Level work by the same providers: one agency publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, which is a reasonable indication of the gap. The exceptions are the scarce syllabuses, principally Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Maths, and the Arabic first-language stream, where the thin specialist pool pushes quotes up regardless of level.

We do not publish an IB Gram price list on this page. That is a deliberate position rather than an evasion: a figure printed before anyone knows the subject, the syllabus code, the tier, the session length and the number of weeks would be a guess with a currency symbol in front of it. The free trial lesson and the written plan that follows it are where a real number comes from, and that plan arrives before any payment is taken.

sections.heading: Nine subjects, one budget: the arithmetic nobody does
paragraphs: A Dubai student in Year 11 is typically entered for eight to ten IGCSE subjects. At published market rates, funding weekly tuition in all of them would cost more per year than the school fees do. Nobody attempts it, but almost nobody does the arithmetic either, which is how families end up funding the subject that worries them rather than the subject where the money works.

Do it explicitly. Write the subjects down with the current working grade beside each, the awarding organisation and the tier where one applies. Then mark each one with how many marks are realistically recoverable and how quickly. A student two marks below a grade boundary in Chemistry and fifteen below in History has a cheap gain and an expensive one, and the cheap one is not the subject they complain about. Boundaries move between series and are published after the event, so treat this as a ranking exercise rather than a calculation.

Three patterns recur in this market. The first is a student whose maths is sound and whose written subjects are collapsing, usually because nobody has read their writing in months; that is one weekly reader in one subject, not three. The second is a student entered for Core who could hold Extended, where the highest-value spend is a short block before the entry deadline rather than a year of general support. The third is a student whose problem is examination technique across every subject at once, which is a single skill bought once and applied nine times.

The table below works three realistic Dubai budgets against the published bands and shows what each buys. The point of it is not the totals, which are illustrative rather than quoted. It is that the shape of the spend matters more than the size: at every budget level, two subjects done properly beats four done thinly, and one subject plus examination technique beats two subjects without it.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE syllabuses carry a premium in Dubai, and why
paragraphs: At Diploma level, subject scarcity moves a quote considerably. At IGCSE it moves it less, because the common subjects are taught in every school in the emirate and the supply of people who can teach them is correspondingly deep. There are real exceptions, though, and they are worth knowing before you accept that a high quote reflects quality rather than availability.

Additional Mathematics, Cambridge 0606, and Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 are the clearest. They are taken by a small, able fraction of each cohort, usually heading for A Level Mathematics or Further Mathematics, and the pool of tutors who can teach them confidently is genuinely thin in this market. Arabic as a first language, Cambridge 0508, is the second: it needs a specialist in a stream that Dubai schools are required to timetable separately from Arabic as a foreign language, and the available teaching population is smaller than demand.

Two more sit a step below. Computer Science 0478 is scarcer than ICT 0417 because the algorithmic content and pseudocode require a different background, and families routinely book one when they need the other. Accounting 0452 is thinly supplied relative to Business Studies 0450 for similar reasons. Everything else at IGCSE level, including the separate sciences and both main maths routes, is well enough covered in Dubai that a high quote should be justified by something other than rarity.

The useful move is to ask directly. How many tutors do you have for this exact syllabus code, and when could the second one start if the first does not suit? A provider with depth answers immediately. A provider with one person answers vaguely, and the premium you are being quoted is the premium of a single point of failure rather than the premium of expertise.

sections.heading: Core or Extended changes the hours before it changes the rate
paragraphs: Several Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered. A candidate is entered for either Core or Extended, the two tiers sit on different papers, and the range of grades available differs: Core is generally reported in the lower part of the scale while Extended reaches the top of it. Confirm the exact papers and available grades for your child's syllabus in the current Cambridge syllabus document, because they vary by subject and are revised between editions.

This is the most consequential decision in a Dubai Year 10, and most parents do not know it has been taken. It is usually made by the school, on the basis of internal assessment, somewhere between the middle of Year 10 and the entry deadline in Year 11. A student entered for Core is working towards a ceiling. If that ceiling is below what a post-16 route requires, the problem is not a tutoring problem at all; it is an entry problem, and it has a deadline.

The cost consequence runs the opposite way from what families expect. Teaching a student to the top of the Core tier is usually a short job, because the content is bounded and the papers are predictable. Moving a borderline student from Core to Extended is a longer job, because the additional content is real and the papers ask different kinds of question. And supporting an Extended candidate who is struggling is longer still, since the difficulty is rarely one topic. The rate does not change across those three; the number of hours changes by a factor of three or four.

Pearson works differently and this is worth knowing before comparing quotes. Its Mathematics A syllabus is tiered into Foundation and Higher, but most other Pearson International GCSE subjects are untiered, so one paper set serves the whole ability range and there is no tier decision to make or to reverse in those subjects. That removes an entire category of risk in most of the timetable, and it is one of the few structural differences between the two boards that changes what a family should buy.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Pearson cost the same to teach and not the same to plan
paragraphs: The two awarding organisations that dominate international GCSE in Dubai charge similar market rates for tutoring, because the labour is the same. What differs is everything a plan depends on: the syllabus codes, the paper structures, the tiering, the grading scale and the calendar. A tutor who starts work without establishing the board is teaching from the wrong specimen papers, and that is not a small inefficiency at AED 200 an hour.

Grading is the most visible difference and the one that confuses Dubai families most. Cambridge reports IGCSE results internationally on the A* to G scale. Pearson reports International GCSE results on the 9 to 1 scale. A student taking subjects from both boards can finish Year 11 holding one certificate in letters and another in numbers, and there is no official conversion a parent should rely on for comparison. Ask the school which scale applies to which subject.

The calendars differ too, and the published dates matter because entry deadlines sit months before examinations. Cambridge runs June and November series. It also allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson runs May or June and November series, and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each one, so every plan should be built against the live official timetable rather than a date someone has restated.

Pearson's published dates for the November 2026 International GCSE series make the deadline gap vivid. The final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and the results do not reach students until the new year: the November 2025 series reported to students on 22 January 2026. Entries for a November series close in the preceding summer, months before the first paper, and the exact date is the one printed on your centre's statement of entry rather than anything worth restating here. Cambridge's June and November series run on the same logic, with entries closing well ahead of the papers. Whichever board your child sits, the shape is the point: the tier decision and the subject list are settled long before anybody feels urgent about them, which is why a tutoring plan that starts in the term before the series is already working inside a fixed entry list.

sections.heading: If you can only buy ten hours, buy them in this order
paragraphs: Ten hours at the mid online band is a real purchase for most Dubai families and a small one against a nine-subject timetable. Spent in the right order it moves a grade. Spent in the usual order, which is weekly general support in whichever subject feels worst, it mostly produces reassurance. The ordering below is the part of this page worth more than the rate table.

Hour one is diagnosis and nothing else. A full past paper, done under time, marked properly against the published mark scheme by somebody who knows the syllabus. Not a conversation about how things are going. The output is a list of components and error types, which is what the remaining nine hours get spent on. Families resist this hour because it feels like paying for an assessment, and it is the single highest-value hour in the block.

Hours two to four go to examination technique on whichever component the diagnosis identified, because technique transfers. A student who learns to read the command word, allocate time by marks and show method in a way a marker can follow applies that in nine subjects, not one. Hours five to eight go to the two highest-yield content gaps, defined as the ones with the most marks closest to reach. Hour nine is a second timed paper. Hour ten reviews it and decides whether to buy another block.

What not to buy first, in order of how commonly it is bought first: general weekly homework supervision, which is the easiest thing to purchase in this market and the least likely to change a grade; a full syllabus sweep, which spends the budget on content the student already holds; and the premium tier, since the published AED 500 to AED 650 band in Dubai exists for post-16 candidates and no provider offers a reason to apply it to Year 11. Free moves matter too: past papers from the official site, marked against the published scheme, plus one specific conversation with the subject teacher, reduce the hours you need to buy.
bullets: Hour one: a timed past paper, marked against the published scheme
Hours two to four: examination technique, because it transfers across subjects
Hours five to eight: the two gaps with the most marks closest to reach
Hours nine and ten: a second timed paper and an honest decision about continuing

sections.heading: The permit, and why it belongs in a price conversation
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and a family comparing quotes should know that the cheapest rates in this market frequently come from people who have not obtained one. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

MoHRE's own service for it is called Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Because it is free and fast, there is no cost argument for not holding one. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone.

Two further points belong in a Dubai price conversation. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal object from an individual tutor: it requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. Those are two different documents, and a provider conflating them is telling you something. In Abu Dhabi, separately, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

What this means practically is one question, asked once, before money moves: do you hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and may I see it? The permit is free, so a refusal is not about cost. And the related temptation should be named: your child's own subject teacher, privately, is the arrangement the rules are designed to prevent, and it puts a teacher's position at risk as well as a student's.

sections.heading: Why these hours run over live video, with the travel priced out
paragraphs: This page is about cost, so the format question is a cost question. An in-home hour in Dubai is quoted between roughly AED 180 and AED 500 by the published sources read in October 2026, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject teacher working online. The difference is not teaching. It is a journey, and in this city at 17:00 the journey is not short.

The journey also distorts the product. A tutor who has driven forty minutes needs the session to be worth the drive, which is why in-home lessons in Dubai are typically sold at ninety minutes rather than sixty. For a Year 11 working on examination technique that extra half hour has some value. For a Year 10 doing weekly content work it mostly has the value of being easy to sell. The format quietly sets the session length, and the session length is a cost.

IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai. We do not run in-person lessons anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson described here is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We state that before an enquiry rather than after one, because two providers in this market route UAE families to numbers outside the UAE without disclosing it, and one shows a Dubai footer address on an Abu Dhabi page. Disclosure costs nothing and is the cheapest trust signal available.

The honest accounting includes what the format gives up. Nobody is in the room to notice a phone, close a door or tidy a desk. Handwritten working needs a document camera or a phone propped over the page, which takes a setup conversation once. Practical science has a real limit: the Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper can be taught thoroughly over video because it is a written paper about practical work, but a practical test sat in a school laboratory needs the laboratory. We say that rather than talking around it.

sections.heading: What the money cannot buy at any rate in this market
paragraphs: A page about cost should be clear about the limits of spending, because the providers who are vague about them are the ones who sell the most hours. No rate in this market buys a grade. Grade boundaries are set by the awarding organisation after each series and published afterwards, they move between series, and nobody teaching your child knows where they will fall. Any provider promising a particular grade, a promised number of marks, or money back tied to a result is offering something they cannot control.

Nor does money buy syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as a package. Those belong to Cambridge and Pearson, they are available through official channels, and a provider supplying them as downloads is reproducing material it does not own. We reference them and link to the official source, which is both the lawful position and the more useful one, since the official version is current and a copied one is not.

Money does not buy assessed work either. Where an IGCSE subject carries a non-examined component, the submission must be the student's own, and a tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on what the student has produced. A tutor who offers to supply content for an assessed piece is offering the student a malpractice finding, and that risk sits with the student rather than with the provider that sold it. The same applies to the Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies streams Dubai schools are required to run, where KHDA prohibits the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission.

Finally, money cannot buy back a missed entry deadline. Entries on both boards close months before the papers, tier decisions are made before that, and a family that discovers in March that a child was entered for the wrong tier has a problem no amount of tutoring resolves. The cheapest intervention available in this entire market is a fifteen-minute conversation with the school in Year 10 to establish, in writing, which board, which syllabus codes and which tier each subject has been entered for.

process.title: Send the board, the code and the tier
process.description: One message with the awarding organisation, the syllabus codes and whether each subject is Core or Extended is worth more than a long description of the student. If you do not know those, ask the school in writing first; it is free and it changes the entire plan.

process.title: A free trial lesson that produces a diagnosis
process.description: One trial lesson per family, nothing to pay and no card required. For an IGCSE student the trial works best with a marked piece of work or a past-paper question in front of it, so the hour produces a list of components and error types rather than a general impression.

process.title: A written plan with a number in it
process.description: After the trial you get a plan naming the subject, the components to target, the session length and frequency, the expected number of weeks and the cost of that block. That is where an IB Gram figure comes from, and it arrives before any payment is taken.

process.title: Weekly sessions that leave marked work
process.description: Each session ends with the student's own work marked against the published mark scheme, a note of what moved, and one specific thing to attempt before the next session. Unmarked practice rehearses the error, so marking is the part we do not skip.

process.title: A six-week review against the diagnostic
process.description: At six weeks we re-run a timed component and compare it with the trial diagnosis. If marks have not moved we change the tutor, change the target component, or tell you to stop buying hours. Continuing unchanged and hoping is not one of the options.

process.title: A calendar check before every series
process.description: Before each June or November series we check the plan against the live official timetable for your centre's Cambridge zone or your Pearson series, because entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers and a restated date is not a source.

whyPoints.title: Prices attributed, not asserted
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was read. None of them is our price. We would rather publish somebody else's number honestly than our own number vaguely, which is what most of this market does.

whyPoints.title: Taught to a syllabus code, not a subject name
whyPoints.description: 0580 is not 0607, 0478 is not 0417, and 4MA1 is not 4PM1. We establish the awarding organisation and the code before the first session, because a tutor working from the wrong specimen papers is expensive at any rate.

whyPoints.title: The tier question raised early
whyPoints.description: Core and Extended carry different papers and different available grades, and the decision is usually taken by the school in Year 10. We raise it at the first conversation rather than discovering it in February, because by then it is an entry problem rather than a teaching one.

whyPoints.title: Marked work every session
whyPoints.description: Timed questions marked against the published mark scheme, with the marks visible to the parent. Practice that is not marked rehearses the mistake, and a session that leaves nothing behind cannot be audited by anybody.

whyPoints.title: A defined block with an end
whyPoints.description: We quote blocks with a stated number of sessions and a review point rather than open-ended weekly support. Spend that drifts is the most common quiet failure in this market, and a block with an end date prevents most of it.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram makes no home visits in Dubai and holds no centre, office or branch anywhere in the UAE, and we say so on the page rather than in an email after your enquiry.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE tutor in Dubai cost per hour in AED?
faqs.answer: Published rates read in October 2026 span roughly AED 33 to AED 650 an hour across the UAE market. The band most IGCSE work actually sits in is AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject teacher working online; one agency publishes IGCSE from AED 150 against IB from AED 200, which gives a sense of the gap between levels. A tutor travelling to a Dubai address is quoted roughly AED 180 to AED 500 with the journey inside the number. Those are other providers' figures. We quote after a free trial lesson, because subject, tier and session count change the total more than the rate does.

faqs.question: Why do two Dubai tutors quote completely different prices for the same subject?
faqs.answer: Because they are selling different products under one word. Format accounts for most of it: an in-home hour carries a journey across Dubai and is usually sold at ninety minutes to justify it. Session length, frequency and whether the hour includes marking all move the figure. Syllabus scarcity moves it for Additional Mathematics, Further Pure Maths and Arabic first language, and for very little else at this level. Paperwork moves it a little and is worth paying for. What should not move it is a credential claim nobody will put in writing.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should we actually fund tutoring in?
faqs.answer: One, usually, and two at most. A Dubai Year 11 is typically entered for eight to ten subjects, and funding all of them would cost more annually than school fees. The useful exercise is to list the subjects with the working grade, the board and the tier, then rank them by how many marks are realistically recoverable and how fast. The cheap gain is rarely the subject the student complains about. At every budget level, two subjects done properly with marked work beats four done thinly, and one subject plus transferable examination technique beats two without it.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Core and Extended, and does it change the cost?
faqs.answer: In several Cambridge subjects a candidate is entered for one tier or the other, the tiers sit on different papers, and the available grades differ, with Core reaching a lower ceiling than Extended. Confirm the exact papers and grades in the current syllabus document. It changes the hours rather than the rate, and by a large factor: teaching to the top of Core is a short job, moving a borderline student up to Extended is three or four times longer and has an entry deadline attached, and supporting a struggling Extended candidate is longer still. Most Pearson subjects are untiered, so this decision does not exist there.

faqs.question: Does the price change depending on whether my child sits Cambridge or Pearson?
faqs.answer: Not materially, because the teaching labour is the same. What differs is everything a plan depends on. Cambridge uses four-digit codes such as 0580 and 0625, tiers several subjects into Core and Extended, and reports results on the A* to G scale internationally. Pearson codes begin with a 4, such as 4MA1 and 4PH1, Mathematics A is tiered into Foundation and Higher while most other subjects are untiered, and results are reported on the 9 to 1 scale. The calendars differ too. A tutor who starts without establishing the board is working from the wrong specimen papers, which is expensive at any hourly rate.

faqs.question: Is an online IGCSE tutor cheaper than one who comes to the house in Dubai?
faqs.answer: On the published figures, yes, and the gap is mostly the journey. Online qualified-teacher rates run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour; in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 with travel folded in. The second effect is less obvious and matters more: in-home lessons in Dubai are usually sold at ninety minutes because a tutor who has driven across the city needs the session to be worth the drive, so the format sets the length and the length is a cost. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai; our lessons are one-to-one over live video.

faqs.question: How much do IGCSE exam entries cost for a private candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Entry fees are set by the examination centre rather than by the awarding organisation, they differ between centres in this emirate, and we will not publish a figure we have not verified. Ask two or three centres in writing for the per-subject fee, the late-entry surcharge, the deadline, and whether practical components can be accommodated. Do it well before the deadline rather than near it. The Pearson November 2026 timetable runs to 19 November 2026 and entries for that series closed in the preceding summer, and Cambridge entries for a June series close months ahead of the first paper in the same way. On both boards the entry window shuts long before the exam feels close.

faqs.question: Should we book in October or wait until the mock results come back?
faqs.answer: October, if you already know a subject is in trouble. Demand rises and availability falls as the series approaches, which has the same effect on what a family can actually book as a price rise would. The practical consequence is not a higher advertised rate so much as the disappearance of the useful slots: by February, the 16:30 to 18:00 window in the family villa communities is largely gone, and the specialists in scarce syllabuses are committed. The same block of hours bought in October buys more teaching than it does in March, partly because it is easier to schedule and mostly because there is time left to act on what the diagnosis finds.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to find a tutor for in this emirate?
faqs.answer: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 and Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1, because a small able fraction of each cohort takes them and the teaching pool is correspondingly thin. Arabic as a first language, 0508, is the next, since it is a separately timetabled stream in Dubai schools and demand outruns supply. Computer Science 0478 is scarcer than ICT 0417 and the two are frequently confused when families book. Everything else at this level, including the separate sciences and both main maths routes, is well covered, so a high quote there needs an explanation other than rarity.

faqs.question: How do I compare a Dubai monthly package against an hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Convert the package to a cost per minute of one-to-one contact before deciding anything. A published online package in this market of AED 799 a month for eight sessions works out near AED 100 a session, which looks strong against the hourly bands until you check the session length and what the provider counts as a session. In-home monthly packages advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits are eight contact hours and four journeys inside one number. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for exam-year specialist work. Compare on minutes of one-to-one contact.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor in Dubai need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's service is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time through its app and e-services. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount as unverified. Since it is free, ask to see it.

faqs.question: Can I hire my child's own subject teacher privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement the rules are built to prevent, and it puts the teacher at risk as well as your child. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the ADEK position as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document. Practically, the conflict of interest is obvious: the person who teaches the class should not also be paid to compensate for it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor guarantee my child a grade 7 or an A for the money?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone who offers it is selling something they do not control. Grade boundaries are set by the awarding organisation after each series and published afterwards, and they move between series, so nobody teaching your child knows where the line will fall. What can honestly be promised is a diagnosis, marked work against the published mark scheme, a named target component and a review date. A provider promising a particular grade, a promised number of marks, or money back tied to a result is making a claim no rate in this market supports.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE equivalency process actually count?
faqs.answer: Five. On the British track, a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Beyond that, one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, is required. One ranking competitor in this market publishes a requirement of six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule. Verify the current position on moe.gov.ae, and note that equivalency is a Ministry process no tutoring provider performs or accelerates.

faqs.question: What is the single cheapest thing we can do to improve an IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, in writing, which awarding organisation each subject is entered with, which syllabus code, and which tier. It costs nothing and it resolves a surprising share of problems, because a child entered for Core when they could hold Extended has a ceiling problem with a deadline rather than a teaching problem. After that, past papers from the official site done under time and marked against the published mark scheme, plus one specific conversation with the subject teacher about where the marks went. All of that is free and it reduces the hours you need to buy.

dubai/igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Get a real number after a free trial, not before it
dubai/igcse-tutor.closingBody: Send the awarding organisation, the syllabus codes and the tier for each subject you are considering, plus the most recent marked paper if you have one. The trial lesson is free, one per family, with nothing to pay and no card required, and for an IGCSE student it works as a diagnosis: a timed question, marked against the published scheme, producing a list of components rather than an impression. The written plan that follows names the target component, the session length, the number of weeks and the cost of that block. If the honest answer is that a conversation with the school will do more than a block of hours, the plan will say so.

dubai/igcse-tutor-cost.heroSubtitle: The IGCSE tutor cost in Dubai that matters is not the hourly rate. It is the rate divided by the marks it moved on comparable papers, which is a number almost nobody calculates. This page sets out how to measure it: what evidence a paid hour should produce, how to read a ten-week mark trend, when to review spending, and the three situations in which buying more hours is the wrong decision. Tuition is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/igcse-tutor-cost.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE one-to-one online across Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel specifications. What each should be asked for is the same: a diagnosis from marked timed work in week one, an hour estimate they will stand behind, and comparable papers at week ten.

intro.heading: A rate is an input, not a cost
paragraphs: Families in Dubai compare tuition on the hourly rate because it is the only number on offer. It is also the number least related to what the spending achieves. AED 150 an hour that produces no marked work and no measurable movement is more expensive than AED 300 an hour that moves a candidate from a 5 to a 7, because the cheaper arrangement bought nothing and the dearer one bought a grade. The useful figure is cost per mark moved on comparable papers, and the reason nobody quotes it is that calculating it requires evidence most arrangements never produce.

The published market bands are the starting point. A qualified subject tutor working online with a Dubai family charges roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour at October 2026 rates: Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150, TutorChase quotes AED 270, and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tier. Those are market figures attributed to their publishers, not IB Gram's prices.

What this page adds is the denominator. A paid hour should leave a trace: a timed question set marked against the published criteria, annotations at the point of loss, a short written note on what changed, and at intervals, a paper comparable to the one sat in week one. With those, ten weeks of tuition produces a mark trend, and a trend divided into a total spend is a cost you can actually judge. Without them, you have a feeling about whether things are better, which is what most tuition decisions in this market are made on.

The discipline this requires is unglamorous and cheap. Comparable means the same difficulty, timed the same way, marked to the same criteria. A tutor who sets easier work as the term progresses produces a rising line that measures nothing, and families reading that line conclude the money is working. Equally, a child who is given more help during a session scores higher on the work done in it, which is why the measurement has to be on unaided timed work rather than on anything completed together.

IB Gram is an independent IB and IGCSE tutor-matching platform, with no affiliation to Cambridge International, to Pearson, or to any Dubai school named here. Tuition for families in the UAE is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video; IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visiting is offered only in India. That matters to the cost question in one direct way: the travel line disappears from the fee, and the tutor pool is set by the clock rather than by a twenty-minute radius, which is what makes a specification specialist affordable for a family in Dubai South rather than only for one in Jumeirah.

dubai/igcse-tutor-cost.programmesIntro: The same hourly rate buys different amounts of movement at different stages, which is the single biggest reason two Dubai families paying the same figure get very different value from it.

programmes.name: Years 8-9, before the course begins
programmes.description: The highest return per dirham in the whole sequence, and the hardest to measure, because there is no past paper to sit. The proxy is a short topic test repeated after a month on the same content. Movement here prevents a Year 11 problem rather than fixing one, which is why the cost looks like insurance and behaves like it.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools admit new arrivals across the year, so Year 9 classes hold children from CBSE, American and different British schemes. Where a gap is a specific untaught topic rather than general weakness, six hours often closes it and twenty would be waste. A diagnostic that names the topics is therefore the first purchase, not a term of weekly sessions.

programmes.name: Year 10, first teaching
programmes.description: The best measurable value, because school assessments provide a natural comparable series and the work is alongside first teaching rather than on top of it. Movement shows up within a term, and the hours needed for a given gain are roughly half what the same gain costs in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Year 10 is also when the tier decision is live. Dubai entries are submitted months ahead of the papers, so an evidenced opinion on Core versus Extended in the autumn term can change what the certificate is capable of showing. That is a use of tuition money with a discrete, checkable outcome rather than a general one.

programmes.name: Year 11, the examination year
programmes.description: The most measurable stage and the dearest. Past papers give genuinely comparable instruments, so a ten-week block produces a readable trend. Rates also peak here: specialist exam-year work in this market runs AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and the scarce tutors are scarcest at exactly the moment demand arrives.
programmes.countryNote: Because Dubai centres enter candidates across Cambridge's March, June and November series and Pearson's May/June and November series, the ten-week window before a child's own papers can fall at very different points in the year. Booking a named specialist a series ahead costs less and matches better than booking one eight weeks out.

programmes.name: Resits and private candidates
programmes.description: The clearest cost calculation available, because the previous attempt is the baseline. You know the mark, you know the paper, and a comparable paper under timed conditions tells you where the candidate now stands. The complication is logistics rather than teaching: entries, centres and deadlines that a school would ordinarily handle.
programmes.countryNote: For a Dubai candidate the retake route is the November series rather than a spring one, because Cambridge offers its February and March series in India only. November is therefore the earliest sitting after a June result, and Cambridge entries for it close in the preceding summer. Pearson runs May/June and November as well, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026 and results reaching students in January. Entry deadlines, not teaching time, are what usually decide a resit plan.

dubai/igcse-tutor-cost.subjectsIntro: Cost per mark differs sharply by subject, because the marks available to recover differ. These notes say where the recoverable marks sit in each subject and therefore how quickly spending should show up in a trend.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The fastest subject to show movement, because method marks are recoverable immediately. A candidate who starts writing one line of working before each answer gains marks on the next paper they sit, which makes a ten-week trend here unusually readable.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Two distinct mark pools. The practical paper's losses are checklist-fixable and show up within weeks; the quantitative theory topics take longer and move more slowly. A good plan targets the practical pool first because the evidence arrives sooner.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole fluency is the single lever. It is slow to install and then moves marks across several papers at once, which produces a flat trend for three or four weeks followed by a step. Families who stop at week four because nothing moved often stop just before it would have.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Mostly command-term discipline, which is a rule rather than content, so movement is quick and cheap. This is often the subject where the lowest spend produces the clearest trend, and where a long weekly commitment is poor value compared with a short block.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 / 0510)
subjects.description: Reading-response marks are among the most teachable on any paper and show movement within a few weeks. Writing marks move more slowly. Measure the two components separately or the trend will look flat when half of it is rising.

subjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Nearly all recoverable marks sit in the long questions, in application and evaluation. Because those marks are large and few, individual paper scores are noisy, so a trend needs more data points here than in Maths before it means anything.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Paper 2 pseudocode marks are recoverable quickly once the published conventions are learned, which produces a sharp early step. Paper 1 theory vocabulary responds to structured recall testing and moves steadily rather than suddenly.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: The slowest and most expensive to move, because the losses sit in prerequisite fluency rather than in the topic being examined. Expect a longer flat period and budget more hours; a ten-week trend may show little even where the work is correct.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (0654, 0653)
subjects.description: Measure by discipline rather than overall, because one weak strand of three drags the aggregate and hides movement in the other two. Reporting a single score here is the commonest way a working plan looks like a failing one.

subjects.name: Geography (0460) and History (0470)
subjects.description: Case-study specificity and arguing from the source are the recoverable pools. Both respond to marked written work rather than to lesson time, so a plan weighted towards marking rather than teaching usually produces a better trend per dirham.

dubai/igcse-tutor-cost.regionsIntro: Delivery is online, so the area a Dubai family lives in does not change the rate. What it changes is whether sessions actually happen at a workable hour, and a ten-week trend built on seven sessions is not a ten-week trend.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JBR and Bluewaters
regions.note: Late school-bus arrivals push a realistic start to 17:00, and high relocation turnover means mid-year starts. A mid-year start needs a sharper week-one baseline, because there is less runway for a flat period before the evidence has to speak.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle, Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Afternoon journeys across Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road make 17:30 the earliest honest start. The main threat to a readable trend here is cancelled sessions rather than ineffective ones, which is an argument for two shorter slots a week.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Mizhar
regions.note: Schools close by and children home early, so 16:00 holds and attendance is consistent. Large IGCSE cohorts mean plenty of school assessment data to use as comparable instruments alongside past papers.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Families here often run two subjects in one evening, which makes the review conversation easier because both have the same number of sessions behind them. Watch for the second subject being measured less carefully than the first.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1, 2 and 3
regions.note: The earliest feasible starts in the city, often competing with swimming and music commitments that already own the early evening. Where the evening is full, a thirty-minute marking review plus a shorter session often beats one long slot.

regions.name: Business Bay, Downtown and DIFC
regions.note: Tower living where the binding constraint is a quiet room rather than a journey. Timed work completed in a noisy space is not comparable work, so where to sit the measurement paper is part of the plan rather than a detail.

regions.name: Deira, Bur Dubai and Al Qusais
regions.note: Strong IGCSE Maths and science demand, with sessions timed around Maghrib and family dinner. Ramadan shifts the slot again, and a plan that does not anticipate that loses two or three weeks from its own trend.

regions.name: Dubai South, Mudon and Town Square
regions.note: The thinnest local pool for scarce specifications, which matters to cost rather than to scheduling: online delivery is what makes an 0606 or 0478 specialist available here at the same rate as in a central community.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving Marina, Al Barsha and Tecom
schoolClusters.note: Large IGCSE cohorts with frequent internal assessment, which gives families a free supply of comparable instruments alongside past papers. Students we support attend schools in this cluster; the names are market context only.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
schoolClusters.note: British and Indian-curriculum provision side by side with heavy Maths and science demand, and reporting cycles that make a term-by-term comparison straightforward for parents who ask for the mark rather than the comment.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving Dubai Hills, the Ranches and Al Qudra
schoolClusters.note: Wide catchments and campuses running both post-16 routes, so the target grade a family measures against depends on which route they intend. Ask the school for its published per-subject entry requirements before setting one.

dubai/igcse-tutor-cost.modesIntro: Each format produces evidence at a different speed, and the cost question is really a question about which evidence you need and how soon.

modes.title: A bounded diagnostic block
modes.description: Four to six sessions at an agreed total, bought to establish what is wrong and how many hours would fix it. The cheapest way to find out whether tuition is the right spend at all, and the only format that can honestly end in a recommendation not to continue.
bullets: A fixed total agreed before anything starts
Week one is a marked timed paper used as the baseline
Ends with named causes and an hour estimate in writing
No obligation to continue when the block finishes

modes.title: A ten-week measured block
modes.description: Weekly sessions with timed work marked at consistent difficulty between them, and a comparable paper at week ten against the week-one baseline. This is the shortest arrangement that produces a trend rather than a reading, and it is the format this page is built around.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE tutor cost in Dubai should produce for the money
paragraphs: Each band in this market should produce a different kind of evidence, and knowing which is which prevents most disappointment. At AED 33 to AED 65, the published rates of two providers here, you are buying supervision: a student is kept on task and questions get answered. That is a real service and it leaves almost no trace, so there is nothing to measure. Expecting a mark trend from it is a category error rather than a complaint.

At AED 150 to AED 300, the band a qualified subject tutor occupies, you should be getting marked written work between sessions, annotations at the point of loss, a short written note per session and a diagnosis in week one. That is enough to build a trend. At AED 200 to AED 450 and above, the specialist and exam-year band, you should additionally be getting paper-level knowledge: which of the available marks this candidate is leaving behind, on which component, and in what order they will be recovered.

The table below sets that out band by band. Use it to judge a quote rather than to haggle. A provider charging mid-band rates who produces no marked work between sessions is charging specialist prices for a supervision product, and that mismatch is the commonest overpayment in this market. Equally, a budget provider doing exactly what budget providers do is not failing, and asking them for a marked paper trend is asking for something that was never in the price.

sections.heading: Cost per mark moved: a worked ten-week example
paragraphs: The calculation is simple once the evidence exists. Sit a comparable paper in week one and again at week ten, under the same timing and marked to the same criteria. Divide the total spend by the difference in marks. The result is a number you can compare across subjects, across providers and across years, and it is the only figure in this market that reflects what the money did rather than what it cost.

The table below works through a single illustrative case: a Year 11 candidate on Cambridge Extended Chemistry, ten weekly hours at AED 220, with a timed Paper 4 section as the instrument at both ends. The numbers are an example of the method rather than a claim about outcomes; no provider can promise a particular movement, and a flat result is a possible honest outcome of a well-run block. What the table shows is how the arithmetic reads in both the good case and the bad one.

Two warnings about using it. First, marks on a single paper are noisy, so a difference of two or three marks is not a trend; it is weather. That is why a mid-point reading at week five matters, and why Economics needs more data points than Maths before anything can be concluded. Second, the instrument has to be unaided. A paper completed with help, or one the student has seen before, measures the help and the memory rather than the learning, and a tutor who supplies the measurement paper should not also have worked through it in a session.

sections.heading: Comparable marked work, and how to tell when it is not
paragraphs: Comparability is the whole technique, and it fails quietly. The commonest failure is drift in difficulty: a tutor choosing question sets that suit what has just been taught, which is good teaching and terrible measurement. The second is timing: work done at leisure at the kitchen table is not comparable with work done in twenty-five minutes. The third is assistance, which includes the subtle kind, where a tutor sitting alongside asks a leading question at the moment the student stalls.

The fix is to separate the two functions explicitly. Practice work can be anything: scaffolded, discussed, revisited, as helpful as the tutor can make it. Measurement work is unaided, timed, from a paper the student has not seen, marked to the published criteria, and used only to answer the question of where they now stand. Agreeing with a tutor that one set a month is measurement and the rest is practice costs nothing and makes the whole trend legible.

Parents can audit this without subject knowledge. Ask to see the week-one instrument and the week-ten instrument side by side and ask one question: are these the same difficulty. Ask whether the second was timed and whether anyone was present. If the answer to the first is no or the answer about assistance is unclear, the trend is not evidence, and the honest position is that you do not yet know whether the money worked. That is a better place to be than a confident wrong conclusion.

sections.heading: When to review the spending, and what to decide
paragraphs: Review cadence does more for the cost of tuition than negotiating the rate ever will. Most money wasted in this market is wasted slowly, by arrangements that run without a point at which anybody asks whether they are working. A schedule fixes that, and it has to be set at the start, because setting it later feels like an accusation and tends not to happen.

Four points are enough. At session one, you should receive named causes and an hour estimate. At week five, a mid-point reading that tells you whether anything is moving, with the decision being either continue or revise the diagnosis. At week ten, a comparable paper and a cost per mark. And once a year, usually in September, a whole-budget review against the rest of the household's education spending, which is where the question of how many subjects to support actually belongs.

Each review point needs a stated consequence, or it is a report rather than a decision. Flat at week five means the diagnosis changes or the arrangement does. Flat at week ten after a revised plan means tuition is probably not the intervention this child needs, and a tutor willing to say that is worth more than one who is not. The three honest outcomes are continue, change the plan, and stop, and a provider who only ever reaches the first is not reviewing anything. Put the dates in your own calendar rather than relying on the tutor to raise them, and send a one-line message a week beforehand asking for the comparable set to be ready. That small piece of administration is what turns a cadence on paper into one that actually happens.

sections.heading: Why the cheapest hour is often the dearest
paragraphs: A budget tutor at AED 50 an hour who meets a child weekly for a year costs roughly AED 1,500 to AED 2,500 and, if no written work is marked and no diagnosis was made, may move nothing at all. A specialist at AED 300 who runs a bounded ten-week block costs AED 3,000 and moves a grade. The second is dearer per hour and cheaper per result, and the first is the version families regret, because it feels prudent throughout and produces nothing to point at.

The mechanism is diagnosis. A child achieving grade 5 in Chemistry has usually met every topic on the specification and has two or three recurring, specific failures. Re-teaching the content does not touch them, because the child believes they answered correctly. Supervision keeps them working and leaves the failures in place. What changes the grade is someone reading the working, naming the cause and teaching that, and that is the skill the price difference between the bands is actually buying.

The opposite error is also real. Paying specialist rates for a Year 8 child building algebraic fluency is paying for paper-level knowledge that nothing in the work calls on. A strong general teacher is sufficient and sometimes better there. The test is whether the problem is content or assessment: content problems respond to good teaching at any price point, assessment problems respond only to someone who knows how these specific papers award marks.

sections.heading: Three stop rules worth agreeing in advance
paragraphs: Buying more hours is sometimes the wrong purchase, and the situations in which that is true are predictable enough to name before you start. The first is a flat trend after a revised plan. If the diagnosis has already been changed once and comparable work has still not moved across ten weeks, further hours are unlikely to be the answer, and the next conversation should be with the school rather than with a tutor.

The second is a scheduling failure disguised as a teaching failure. A plan of ten sessions that delivered six, because the slot sat at 18:30 after a long school run and the child arrived exhausted, has not been tested. More hours at the same hour will not help. The fix is a different time, a shorter session, or a different day, and it costs nothing. Dubai evenings are crowded, and this accounts for a surprising share of arrangements that appear to be failing.

The third is a mismatch between what is wrong and what tuition can do. Where the barrier is attendance, an unaddressed learning difference, or a subject the child does not need and will drop at 16, the honest recommendation is to spend the money elsewhere or not at all. A provider willing to say so in week five is a provider whose week-ten advice is worth taking. Where IB Gram cannot find a tutor who covers a specification at a workable hour, it says so rather than offering a substitute.

sections.heading: The exam calendar counted backwards, and what it does to cost
paragraphs: Timing moves tuition costs more than negotiation does, and the reason is that the calendar is fixed and demand is not. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and those are the only two a Dubai candidate can sit, because Cambridge offers its February and March series in India only. Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests do run in March, May and October, but those are not IGCSE and should never be read as an extra sitting. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. Each of those series has an entry deadline that sits months before the papers.

The clearest worked example is the Pearson November 2026 series, because its dates are published and precise. The final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and the results do not land until the new year: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson's summer series is the mirror image, with June 2026 results going to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Cambridge works on the same logic across its June and November series, with entries closing months ahead of the first paper, but the exact entry date belongs to your centre's key dates and the correct zone timetable rather than to a figure anyone should restate from memory. Either way the cost consequence is identical. The decisions that commit money, meaning the tier, the subject list and how many specialist hours are bought, are all made a term or two before anybody sits down in the hall.

One administrative detail is worth more than it sounds. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and it is essential that the correct version of the timetable for that zone is used, because Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which can be revised, so any plan should be built against the live official timetable rather than a restated date. Dates for IB sessions are not published on this page because they could not be verified from the IB directly, and any IB date should be confirmed with the school's coordinator.

sections.heading: Cost by starting point: three Dubai households
paragraphs: Abstract bands are less useful than cases, so here are three, drawn as composites rather than as real families. The first is a Year 10 student in Mirdif at grade 6 in Extended Maths whose school reports say effort is fine. The cause turns out to be unwritten working, the plan is ten weekly hours, and the trend shows in three weeks because method marks are recoverable immediately. The spend is modest and the cost per mark is the lowest of the three.

The second is a Year 11 student in Jumeirah Village Circle at grade 5 in Chemistry, eight weeks from the papers. There is no time to rebuild, so the plan is triage: mole conversions and one other high-mark topic, two shorter sessions a week, everything built on timed questions marked beforehand. The hourly rate is at the top of the range because the specialist and the season are both scarce, and the evidence arrives fast because real papers are the instrument.

The third is a Year 9 student in Dubai South with gaps from a mid-year arrival from a different curriculum. The cause is a handful of untaught topics rather than weakness, the plan is a six-session diagnostic block followed by eight focused hours, and the instrument is a repeated topic test rather than a past paper. Cost per mark cannot be calculated meaningfully at this stage, which is worth saying out loud rather than inventing a number for.

sections.heading: What online delivery does to the cost-evidence link
paragraphs: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; tuition for UAE families runs online, one-to-one, over live video, and home visiting is a service offered only in India. For a page about cost measured against evidence, the format matters in three specific ways rather than as a general preference.

The first is that the travel line leaves the fee, so more of the hourly rate is teaching and marking. The second is that the session length follows the student rather than a journey, which means a sixty-minute slot is available where sixty minutes is what the child can sustain, and the measurement work is not padded to justify a drive. The third is the pool: a specification specialist for 0606 or 0478 becomes available to a family in Dubai South at the same rate as to a family in Jumeirah, because the constraint is the clock rather than a twenty-minute radius.

One thing online delivery makes easier is the record itself. Written work exchanged digitally, marked and returned with annotations, accumulates into exactly the trail this page asks for, without anyone needing to keep a folder. The honest limitation is also worth stating: a tutor in the room can hold the attention of a younger or very distractible child in a way a screen has to work harder at, and that is a real consideration for families with children at the younger end of the IGCSE course.

process.description: The first working session is an unaided timed paper, used as the instrument you will measure against later. Keep it. A plan without a week-one baseline cannot produce a cost per mark at week ten, however good the teaching is.

process.description: A mid-point reading at week five with the decision being continue or revise, a comparable paper at week ten, and a stated consequence at each. Ten minutes of agreement at the start is what makes the spending reviewable later.

process.title: Calculate the number at week ten
process.description: Total spend divided by marks moved on comparable unaided work. Compare it against the next ten weeks' target rather than against another family's hourly rate. Three outcomes are honest: continue, change the plan, or stop.
