faqs.question: What is a reasonable IGCSE tutor cost in Dubai for weekly one-to-one sessions?
faqs.answer: A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour at October 2026 published rates: Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase quotes AED 270, while Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Across thirty teaching weeks that is roughly AED 4,500 to AED 9,000 for one subject. Whether it is reasonable depends on what the hour produces. At that band you should be receiving marked timed work between sessions, annotations at the point of loss and a written note after each session.

faqs.question: How do I work out whether tuition spending is actually achieving anything?
faqs.answer: Divide what you have spent by the marks moved on comparable unaided work. Sit a timed paper in week one and a comparable one at week ten, both unseen, both marked to the published criteria, with nobody sitting alongside. The difference in marks is the numerator's partner, and the resulting figure is the only number in this market that reflects what the money did. A difference of two or three marks on a single paper is noise rather than a trend, which is why a mid-point reading at week five matters as much as the end point.

faqs.question: What makes two question sets comparable enough to measure against each other?
faqs.answer: Four things: the same difficulty, the same timing, a paper the student has not seen, and marking to the same published criteria without assistance during the attempt. Comparability fails quietly. The commonest failure is drift, where a tutor picks sets suited to what has just been taught, which is good teaching and useless measurement. The practical fix is to separate the functions: practice work can be as scaffolded as the tutor likes, while one unaided timed set a month is reserved purely for measurement and is never worked through in a session first.

faqs.question: Why has our tuition produced nothing visible after four weeks?
faqs.answer: Three explanations are common and they need different responses. In Chemistry, mole fluency is slow to install and then moves marks across several papers at once, so a flat four weeks followed by a step is the normal shape and stopping at week four means stopping just before the gain. Alternatively the instrument is wrong: work done with help, or sets of drifting difficulty, will not show movement that is actually happening. Or the diagnosis was wrong, which is what the week-five decision point exists to catch. Ask which of the three it is.

faqs.question: Is a cheap IGCSE tutor in Dubai a false economy?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the mechanism is specific. At AED 33 to AED 65, the published rates of two providers here, you are buying supervision: a student is kept on task and questions get answered. That is a real service that leaves no measurable trace, so a year of it can cost AED 2,000 and move nothing. A grade 5 candidate has usually met every topic and has two or three recurring specific failures, and only someone reading the working and naming the cause changes that. Judge a budget provider on what budget providers do, and do not ask it for a mark trend.

faqs.question: When should we decide to stop paying for IGCSE tuition?
faqs.answer: Three situations justify stopping rather than buying more hours. A flat trend after the diagnosis has already been revised once, where the next conversation belongs with the school. A plan that delivered six of ten sessions because the slot was too late in a Dubai evening, which has not been tested and should be rescheduled rather than extended. And a mismatch between the barrier and what tuition can address, such as attendance or an unaddressed learning difference. A tutor willing to name any of these in week five is one whose week-ten advice is worth taking.

faqs.question: How far ahead of the IGCSE series should we book to keep the cost down?
faqs.answer: A series ahead. Demand for specification specialists peaks from January into the May and June papers, and it spikes a second time in the autumn, when November candidates and June resitters compete for the same few people, so the scarce tutors are scarcest exactly when families start looking. Booking in September for a June series costs less and produces a better match than booking in February. The deadline that really bites is administrative rather than academic: Cambridge entries for a June series close in the spring, months before the first paper, and the Pearson November 2026 timetable ran to 19 November 2026 with its entries shut since the preceding summer.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects show movement fastest for the money?
faqs.answer: Mathematics, because method marks are recoverable immediately: a candidate who starts writing one line of working before each answer gains marks on the next paper they sit. Biology next, since much of the loss is command-term discipline, which is a rule rather than content. Physics practical skills respond to a checklist within weeks. Chemistry moves in a step after a flat period while mole fluency installs. Additional Mathematics 0606 is slowest, because the losses sit in prerequisite fluency rather than in the topic being examined, so budget more hours and expect a longer flat stretch.

faqs.question: Should I measure my child's progress by school reports instead?
faqs.answer: Use them, but not alone. School assessments are a useful free supply of comparable instruments, particularly in Dubai schools with frequent internal testing, and asking for the mark rather than the comment makes them usable. Two cautions. Report comments describe effort and attitude, which are not what tuition was bought to change. And internal assessments vary in difficulty between terms for reasons nobody documents, so a term-on-term fall can be an instrument effect. A past paper under timed conditions remains the cleanest instrument available in Years 10 and 11.

faqs.question: Does paying more per hour get a better IGCSE result?
faqs.answer: Only where the extra buys something the problem calls on. Specialist rates buy paper-level knowledge: which available marks this candidate is leaving behind, on which component, and in what order to recover them. For a Year 11 candidate weeks from a paper, that is the whole value. For a Year 8 child building algebraic fluency it is knowledge nothing in the work uses, and a strong general teacher is sufficient and sometimes better. The test is whether the problem is content or assessment. Families routinely buy the expensive version for content problems and the cheap one for assessment problems.

faqs.question: What does a resit cost us in time as well as money in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Less time than families assume, because the calendar offers two sittings a year rather than one. Cambridge runs June and November, and Pearson runs May/June and November, so a June candidate can often sit again in the autumn instead of waiting a full year. What a Dubai family cannot use is the February and March series, which Cambridge offers in India only. The constraint is entry deadlines rather than teaching: November entries close over the summer, before a June result has been fully digested, which is why the resit framework has to exist before results day. A resit is also the cleanest cost calculation available, since the previous result is a ready-made baseline and a comparable unseen paper tells you immediately where the candidate now stands.

faqs.question: Can online tuition be measured as reliably as sessions in our home?
faqs.answer: More easily, in practice. Written work exchanged digitally, marked and returned with annotations, accumulates into exactly the record a cost calculation needs without anyone maintaining a folder. The travel line also leaves the fee, so more of the hourly rate is teaching and marking, and session length follows the student rather than a journey, which keeps measurement work from being padded. The honest limitation is attention: a tutor in the room holds a younger or very distractible child more easily, and that is worth weighing for children at the younger end of the course.

faqs.question: Why do Dubai providers quote such different prices for the same IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: Because the hour contains different things and the word tutor spans a twentyfold range here. Published figures run from AED 33 to AED 65 at the budget end up to AED 650 for one provider's premium named tier. Scarcity moves it too: Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 pseudocode work and Arabic as a first language have thin pools and price accordingly, while Extended Maths and English are competitive. Season matters as well, with rates rising from January as the series approaches. Ask what the hour includes rather than comparing headline numbers.

faqs.question: What should I ask for in writing before the first paid session?
faqs.answer: Four things, and they take one message. Named causes from the diagnosis, specific enough to be re-tested in a fortnight. An estimated hour count from someone willing to be shown wrong. The review cadence, with week five as a decision rather than a report. And confirmation of what written work will be marked between sessions and what note you will receive afterwards. A provider who supplies all four is quoting a product you can later evaluate; one who supplies only an hourly rate has given you a figure and nothing to judge it by.

faqs.question: Does a Cambridge exam zone really affect our planning in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It affects which timetable you work to, which matters more than it sounds. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for that zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your child's exams officer which zone the centre sits in and work from that timetable. Pearson publishes provisional timetables that can be revised, so build any plan against the live official document rather than a restated date.

dubai/igcse-tutor-cost.closingHeading: One number, calculated once a term
dubai/igcse-tutor-cost.closingBody: Sit an unaided timed paper in week one and keep it. Agree a mid-point reading at week five with a decision attached, and a comparable paper at week ten. Then divide what you spent by the marks that moved. That single calculation, done once a term, tells you more than any comparison of hourly rates across Dubai providers, and it makes the three honest outcomes available: continue, change the plan, or stop. A free trial lesson comes first, with no card details and no commitment, and the diagnosis that follows should arrive in writing.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me.tutorsIntro: Every tutor below is matched to a named Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel specification and a tier rather than to a postcode. Tell us the code on the entry form and the two time windows that work, and the shortlist follows from those.

intro.heading: Distance is the wrong filter, and Dubai makes that unusually obvious
paragraphs: A proximity search is a sensible instinct applied to the wrong problem. It makes sense for a dentist, a barber or a car service, where the thing you need is interchangeable and the journey is the only real cost. It makes much less sense for IGCSE support, because the thing you need is not interchangeable at all. A tutor who has taught Cambridge 0620 Chemistry at Extended tier for six years and a tutor who did A Level Chemistry themselves are both 'a chemistry tutor', and they are not substitutes.

Dubai sharpens the point. The emirate has 227 private schools running 17 different curricula, and families routinely live in one district while their child attends school in another. A household in Mirdif may send a child to a school in Al Barsha; a family in Dubai Marina may be at a school in Nad Al Sheba. There is no stable relationship between where you live, where your child studies and where a competent tutor for one specific specification happens to sit. Searching by distance filters on the one variable that has the least to do with the outcome.

The cost of insisting on proximity is measurable, and it is paid in minutes. A round trip across Dubai at five in the afternoon is routinely forty to ninety minutes depending on the pair of districts involved. Over a school year of weekly sessions that is between twenty-five and sixty hours spent in a car, by either the tutor or the student. Somebody pays for that time - it is the main reason in-home visits are advertised at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor working online.

There is a second, less obvious cost. A proximity-first search narrows the pool before the subject is even considered, which means the binding constraint becomes 'who is nearby and free' rather than 'who has taught this paper'. For well-staffed subjects that is survivable. For Additional Mathematics, Further Pure Mathematics, Computer Science at the top end or a less commonly entered language, it produces either nobody or somebody unsuitable, and the family concludes that no help exists when what does not exist is a nearby version of it.

IB Gram arranges UAE tuition as one-to-one lessons delivered live over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to addresses in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. This page is not an argument that proximity never matters - for some children the presence of an adult in the room is the whole intervention, and that is a real preference. It is an argument that in Dubai, for IGCSE specifically, distance is the variable to drop first.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: What a family should be searching for changes with the stage, because the scarcity of suitable tutors changes. These are the four points at which Dubai parents start looking.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before the IGCSE course starts
programmes.description: The easiest stage to staff locally, because the content is widely taught and almost any competent mathematician or scientist can deliver it. If proximity genuinely matters to your household, this is the stage where insisting on it costs you least in quality. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October give the first external signal.
programmes.countryNote: This is also when Dubai's mid-year arrivals surface. A student joining a British-curriculum school from another system in Year 8 or 9 usually has the content and not the written-examination convention, and that gap is cheap to close now and expensive to close in Year 11.

programmes.name: IGCSE Core and Foundation tier
programmes.description: Reasonably well staffed across the city, since the content subset is narrower and the question styles are more predictable. A family here has genuine choice and can weigh preference about format against specification experience without one of the options vanishing.
programmes.countryNote: Worth knowing before you choose a tutor on convenience: the lower tier caps the grade available on tiered specifications. If the sixth-form plan needs a top grade in that subject, the conversation to have is with the school about tier, not with a tutor about hours.

programmes.name: IGCSE Extended and Higher tier
programmes.description: Where the local pool thins noticeably. Extension content - vectors and transformations in mathematics, limiting reagents and yield in chemistry, induction in physics - needs a tutor who has taught it to examination standard rather than one who met it at school. The honest search term is the specification code, not the district.
programmes.countryNote: In practice this is the tier at which Dubai families who insisted on proximity come back having had two unsatisfactory terms. The second search is usually by subject, and it succeeds.

programmes.name: Thinly entered specifications
programmes.description: Additional Mathematics, Further Pure Mathematics, the top end of Computer Science, and languages entered by a handful of schools. These cannot be staffed by district in any city, let alone one community within it. There may be a small number of people in the whole UAE who have taught the paper, and they will not be within a twenty-minute drive of most households.
programmes.countryNote: This is the clearest case for dropping distance entirely. If your child is entered for one of these, the question is not who is nearby but whether anyone at all is free, and we will give you a straight answer including when the answer is no.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: Each note states how deep the local pool tends to be in Dubai and what that means for a family searching by area. Availability, not difficulty, is the variable here.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The deepest pool in the city at both tiers, which is why a proximity search usually succeeds here and why families generalise from it. Note the board difference: a tutor fluent in 0580 is not automatically fluent in 4MA1 paper structure, and that distinction survives however close they live.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Good general availability, thinner once the Alternative to Practical paper is specified. Ask any candidate tutor what that paper rewards before anything else; the answer sorts the pool faster than any credential check and is independent of location.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Reasonable availability at Core, noticeably thinner at Extended where mole calculations with limiting reagents and percentage yield sit. A family in an outlying community searching by distance at Extended tier will often find nobody and conclude wrongly that nobody exists.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Wide availability across Dubai. The useful filter is not proximity but whether the tutor teaches command-term discipline, since that is where most of the marks go in this subject rather than in content recall.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: The scarcest IGCSE specification in the market. Entered by a minority of Dubai schools, taught to examination standard by very few people, and essentially impossible to staff within one district. Any family searching for this by area is searching for something that is not there.

subjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: Equally thin, and frequently confused with Additional Mathematics by both parents and tutors. Confirm the specification code before accepting a match, because a tutor who prepared students for one will not necessarily know the paper structure of the other.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Very wide availability and the widest variation in actual usefulness. A proximity search here returns many people, most of whom teach writing rather than the mark tariffs on the summary and directed-writing tasks. Ask which, because only the second moves the grade.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Strong availability in Dubai, with the practical issue being whether the tutor knows the 0510 and 0511 task shapes rather than general language teaching. Students transferred between 0510 and 0500 mid-course need the specific reading-paper work, which is a narrower skill.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Good availability, and unusually portable: the application and evaluation habits these subjects need are the same wherever the tutor sits. Economics diagram conventions are the one thing to check, since they are drilled rather than discussed.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Plentiful at first glance and thin where it matters. Programmers are everywhere in Dubai's technology districts; tutors who can teach the board's own pseudocode convention and a ruled trace table are not. Verify the second, and ignore where they live.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Demand is structural because KHDA requires Arabic in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Evening slots are the binding constraint rather than geography, and they go early in the term.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Moderate availability. The skill to check is source interrogation and provenance use rather than case-study knowledge, since that is where the upper bands are awarded. It is also entirely teachable on a shared screen with the resource on it.

regions.note: Eastern districts where a drive to a tutor in Jumeirah or Al Barsha is forty minutes outbound at five in the afternoon. Proximity searches here return general tutors and almost nothing at Extended tier in the sciences.

regions.note: Low-density villa communities with few commercial services inside them, so any in-person arrangement means a drive in both directions. The subject requests are typically Extended maths and separate sciences.

regions.note: Outlying communities where the nearest cluster of tutors is twenty-five minutes away without traffic and considerably more with it. Younger cohorts, so requests skew to Years 9 and 10.

sections.heading: The commute arithmetic, in minutes rather than adjectives
paragraphs: The cost of proximity is normally discussed as convenience, which hides it. Put it in minutes and it becomes a number a family can weigh against the alternative. A weekly session with a twenty-minute drive each way costs forty minutes per session - a little over twenty-five hours across a school year of thirty-eight weeks. The same session with a forty-five-minute crawl along Sheikh Zayed Road or Al Khail Road at five in the afternoon costs ninety minutes, which is nearly sixty hours.

Those hours are not evenly distributed either. They land precisely in the window where a Year 11 is least able to afford them: between the end of the school day and the point where concentration gives out. A student who arrives at a session having spent forty-five minutes in a car is not the same student who starts a session from their own desk, and the first twenty minutes of the lesson are often spent recovering rather than working.

Someone pays for the tutor's half of the journey too, and the market prices it openly. Qualified subject tutors working online are advertised at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour. In-home one-to-one visits with travel included run approximately AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's Dubai rate guide putting them at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200-500. The difference between those bands is substantially the car.

The table below sets out realistic early-evening journey times between Dubai district pairs that come up constantly in this search. They are indicative rather than measured, and any Dubai resident will have their own worse example. The point is the order of magnitude: the travel component of an in-person arrangement is usually larger than the teaching component of the problem it was meant to solve.

sections.heading: Pool by area against pool by subject
paragraphs: Two different pools are involved in any tutoring search and conflating them is what makes a proximity search feel disappointing. The first pool is geographic: who teaches privately within a reasonable journey of your community. The second is technical: who has taught the specific specification and tier your child is entered for, anywhere. For common subjects the two pools overlap enough that the distinction never surfaces. For the rest, the overlap is close to empty.

The table below sets out roughly how deep each pool runs by subject, based on which specifications Dubai schools enter and how widely each is taught. Read the final column as the practical consequence of filtering by distance first - in several rows the result is not a worse tutor but no tutor, followed by a family concluding that help is unavailable.

What makes this worth writing down is that the subjects most likely to need help are disproportionately in the thin rows. A student struggling in Year 10 Biology has a wide choice. A student struggling with Additional Mathematics has, in any one Dubai district, essentially none - and that student is also the one for whom a term of unsuitable teaching does the most damage, because the content moves fast and the gap compounds.

The honest version of availability includes saying when it runs out. Mathematics, the three separate sciences, English in both specifications, Business Studies, Economics and Geography are well covered at both tiers and on both boards. Additional Mathematics, Further Pure Mathematics, upper-end Computer Science and the less commonly entered languages are thin everywhere, and in those cases the options are a wait for the right person, a different session pattern, or a recommendation to look elsewhere.

sections.heading: How to check that a tutor may legally teach privately in the UAE
paragraphs: This is the question almost nobody in the search results answers, and it is one of the few that has a documented answer. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

The application route is MoHRE's own: the service is listed as 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' on mohre.gov.ae, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time and no fees. Because it is free and quick, a tutor has no good reason not to hold one, and asking to see it is a reasonable request rather than an accusation.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published - press reporting on the rules notes that the ministry did not specify amounts or detail the penalties - so a specific figure quoted at you online has not been verified and should not be relied on. The relevant fact for a parent is simply that the permit exists and is checkable.

One further point applies to teachers. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. That is press-reported and worth verifying against the current policy document, but the direction is clear enough that 'your child's own teacher, privately' is a request a family should not make.

sections.heading: Scheduling around the Dubai school run, traffic and the week
paragraphs: Dubai's school day starts early - a 7:20 or 7:30am register is common - and secondary students in outlying communities are on a bus before seven. That sets the limit on how late a session can usefully run, and it is the reason a 9pm slot is a bad idea in February however convenient it looks in the diary.

The other constraint is the afternoon. Between about 4:30pm and 6:30pm the main corridors are at their worst, and in several communities the student is still in transit. For a household in Serena, Town Square or Mudon the realistic start is 7pm. For an apartment family in Dubai Marina or Business Bay with a short school run, 4:30pm works and is often the better slot because the student is not yet tired.

The weekend shape matters too. With Friday part of the weekend in Dubai, a Friday morning session is a genuinely good option for timed-paper work: the student is rested, there is no school day on either side, and a full ninety minutes under exam conditions is possible in a way it never is on a Tuesday evening. Families rarely consider it and those who do tend to keep it.

Ramadan reshapes everything for a month. The school day shortens, routines move, and the slot that worked in January becomes the worst available. The practical answer is a post-Iftar window, slightly shorter sessions, and treating the fortnight around Eid as consolidation rather than new content. Because the session is delivered over video, moving the slot costs nothing more than a message - which is not true of an arrangement built around someone's drive.

sections.heading: When your child's school is nowhere near your home
paragraphs: A substantial share of Dubai families drive past two or three schools to reach the one their child attends. That is a rational outcome of choosing a school on curriculum, inspection record, sibling places or availability rather than on distance - and it quietly breaks the logic of a proximity search, because the relevant community is arguably the school's, not the home's.

It also means the useful local knowledge a tutor might have is about the school rather than the neighbourhood. Which board the school enters for each subject. When its mock windows fall. Whether it runs coursework components. What its sixth form requires at IGCSE before admitting a student to a given A Level or Higher Level course. None of that requires living nearby; all of it requires asking the family the right questions at the start.

The questions worth bringing to a first conversation are therefore school-specific rather than area-specific: the name of the school, the board and code per subject, the tier, the mock dates, and the sixth-form entry bars if the family has them in writing. A tutor who takes those down and plans against them is doing the thing people imagine a 'local' tutor does automatically, and most local tutors do not.

There is one genuinely local factor that matters, and it is the commute, which the previous section covered in minutes. If your child spends fifty minutes on a bus each way, their available study time is materially smaller than a classmate's who walks, and a plan that ignores that will fail for reasons nobody will diagnose correctly.

sections.heading: Safeguarding: who is in the room and what a parent can see
paragraphs: Families comparing an in-person tutor with an online one often raise supervision, and it deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. With a video session, a parent can be present without being in the way: the room is your own, the door can be open, the audio is audible from the next room, and nothing about the arrangement requires an adult the family has not met to be inside the house.

The practical standards worth insisting on from any provider, in either format, are the same. Sessions happen on a named platform rather than a personal messaging app. The tutor's identity is known to the provider, not merely to a marketplace listing. Communication with the student goes through the platform or through the parent rather than through private channels. And there is a clear route to raise a concern that does not involve messaging the tutor.

Session notes contribute here too. A dated written note after every lesson gives a parent a continuous, reviewable account of what happened without sitting in. That is a stronger form of oversight than occasional presence in a living room, and it is the main reason we treat notes as part of the service rather than a courtesy.

Data matters as well. Lead forms for tutoring collect personal information about a minor, and the UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection sits behind that. A provider should be able to tell you what is collected, why, how long it is kept and how to have it deleted, and should not be asking for a child's school, grades and photograph without a stated purpose. Ask; the answer is informative either way.

sections.heading: What the first session covers when there is nothing to send
paragraphs: Ideally a family arrives with a marked mock paper and an exam entry statement. Frequently they arrive with neither, because the search began at eleven at night after a bad report. That is a workable starting point and it changes the shape of the first session rather than its usefulness.

Without prior work, the session begins by generating some. Twenty to thirty minutes of timed questions from a real past paper on the correct specification, chosen to span the topics the student should have met by this point in the year. The tutor says nothing during it. Then the marking happens on screen, strictly to the published scheme, with every lost mark labelled by cause rather than simply counted.

What comes out is the same deliverable a marked mock would have produced: a ranked list of what is costing marks, and a first target. For a parent, the value is that it is specific - not 'needs to work on algebra' but 'eleven marks lost, five to unwritten method, three to command terms, two to units, one to a named topic gap'. That is actionable with or without further sessions.

The reason this is easy over video and awkward in a living room is mundane. On screen, the paper, the mark scheme, the annotation and a visible timer occupy one window, and the whole thing is saved as a dated file that can be compared with the next one in six weeks. A sheet of paper handed over at the end of a visit does not get compared with anything.

sections.heading: Getting started, and what happens if the match is wrong
paragraphs: Send four things: the school, the subject with its board and syllabus code, the tier, and two time windows that genuinely survive a Dubai school week. If you have a marked mock script, send that too and it will do more work than anything you write. Nothing on that list is your home district, which is the point of this page.

Then take the free trial lesson, and use it to test specification knowledge rather than warmth. Ask what the papers are worth on that code, where candidates lose marks on the particular paper your child sits, and what the first four weeks would attack. Someone who has taught the paper answers in particulars. Someone who has taught the subject answers in generalities.

If the match is wrong, say so early and we will change it. The commonest reason a match fails is not competence but pace or manner, and a fifteen-year-old usually knows within two sessions. A provider that makes changing a tutor awkward is optimising for its own diary. Ask about the replacement policy before you book rather than after, and get the answer in writing with the cancellation terms.

To be unambiguous about delivery: these are live one-to-one video sessions on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, and home visits are a service we provide only in India. The trade is explicit - you give up a person in the room, and you gain a person who has actually taught the paper your child will open in the exam hall, with no part of the hour spent on Al Khail Road.

faqs.question: Why does searching for an IGCSE tutor near me in Dubai return so few genuine matches?
faqs.answer: Because the search filters on distance, which is the variable least connected to the outcome. Dubai has 227 private schools across 17 curricula, families routinely live in one district and study in another, and there is no stable relationship between your postcode and where someone who has taught Cambridge 0620 at Extended tier happens to live. For well-staffed subjects the two pools overlap enough that you never notice. For Extended-tier sciences, Additional Mathematics or upper-end Computer Science, filtering by area first returns nobody, which parents reasonably misread as no help existing.

faqs.question: Does living close to a tutor actually make any difference to an IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: Not to the grade, in our experience, though it can matter to the child. Proximity buys the presence of an adult in the room, which for some students - particularly younger ones, or those who genuinely cannot start work without supervision - is the whole intervention. What it does not buy is specification knowledge, mark-scheme literacy or familiarity with the Alternative to Practical paper, and those are what move marks. If presence is the need, say so and choose accordingly. If marks are the need, drop distance first.

faqs.question: How long is the round trip to a tutor across Dubai at five in the afternoon?
faqs.answer: Commonly between fifty and a hundred and ten minutes depending on the district pair. Mirdif to Al Barsha is typically thirty-five to fifty minutes outbound; Al Qusais to Jumeirah can be fifty-five. Over a thirty-eight week school year a weekly cross-city session costs somewhere between twenty-five and seventy hours in a car, and those hours land in the exact window between the school day and the end of useful concentration. A student arriving from forty-five minutes of traffic also spends the first part of the lesson recovering.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are genuinely hard to find a tutor for in my part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Mathematics are the clearest cases - entered by a minority of schools, taught to examination standard by very few people, and effectively impossible to staff within one district. Extended-tier Chemistry is thin outside the dense districts of Al Barsha and Tecom. Physics with the Alternative to Practical paper is thinner than it looks, because many tutors know the content and not that paper. Upper-end Computer Science is thin for a related reason: programmers are plentiful, teachers of the board's pseudocode convention are not.

faqs.question: How can I check that a tutor in Dubai is legally permitted to teach privately?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is MoHRE's own service, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', with a two-working-day completion time and no fees. Since it costs nothing and takes two days, there is no good reason for a UAE-based tutor not to hold one.

faqs.question: My child's school is in a different part of Dubai from our home - how should we time sessions?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from the bus rather than from the school bell. A student on a fifty-minute bus each way has materially less usable study time than a classmate who walks, and a plan that ignores that will fail for reasons nobody diagnoses correctly. For outlying communities such as Serena, Town Square or Mudon, 7pm is the realistic start. For short school runs in apartment districts, 4:30pm is usually better because the student is not yet tired. Friday mornings are the best slot in a Dubai week for timed-paper work.

faqs.question: Is hiring a teacher from my child's own school as a private tutor a good idea?
faqs.answer: No, and in parts of the UAE it is prohibited. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi bar paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat the ADEK position as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document, but the direction is unambiguous. Beyond the rules, it creates an obvious conflict around internal assessment decisions that no family benefits from.

faqs.question: What should I be able to see or hear during an online tutoring session?
faqs.answer: Everything you want to. The room is your own, the door can stay open and the audio is audible from the next room, so supervision is available without an adult you have not met being inside the house. Insist on the same standards in either format: sessions on a named platform rather than a personal messaging app, the tutor's identity known to the provider, contact with the student routed through the platform or through you, and a clear route to raise a concern that does not involve messaging the tutor.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same household share one tutoring arrangement?
faqs.answer: Yes, in two ways. Back-to-back individual slots on the same evening is the usual arrangement and keeps each child's session directed by their own error log. A genuinely paired session works where both children are on the same specification, the same tier and roughly the same standing, and it brings the per-student cost down materially in exchange for roughly half the direct attention each. It works well for timed-paper practice and badly where the two have different gaps, which is the more common case with siblings.

faqs.question: We are moving from Dubai to Abu Dhabi mid-course - does the tutoring arrangement survive?
faqs.answer: The tutoring does, because nothing about it is tied to an address. The same tutor, the same slot and the same error log continue, which is not true of any arrangement built around someone's drive. What changes is the school context: Abu Dhabi private schools are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge rather than KHDA, the new school may enter a different board for a subject, and its mock windows and sixth-form entry bars will differ. Send the new entry statement as soon as you have it and the plan is adjusted to it.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor be matched once I send the details?
faqs.answer: For well-covered subjects - Mathematics, the three separate sciences, English in both specifications, Business Studies, Economics, Geography - a match on the correct specification is usually possible within a few working days once we have the code, the tier and two workable time windows. For thin specifications it takes longer and sometimes it cannot be done at all in the window you need. You will be told which of those applies rather than offered a nearby alternative who has not taught the paper.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have tutors living in my area of Dubai?
faqs.answer: That is not how the match works, and it is deliberate. IB Gram delivers UAE tuition as live one-to-one video sessions on Gulf Standard Time, and does not send tutors to addresses in Dubai or anywhere else in the country - in-home tutoring is a service we operate only in India. Tutors are selected for the board, syllabus code and tier your child is entered for, which is why a household in Dubai Creek Harbour or Al Mizhar gets the same access to a specialist as one in Al Barsha, where the local pool is deepest.

faqs.question: What does a first session cover if we have no marked work to send?
faqs.answer: It generates some. Twenty to thirty minutes of timed questions from a real past paper on the correct specification, spanning the topics the student should have met by that point in the year, with the tutor saying nothing while the clock runs. Then the marking happens on screen, strictly to the published scheme, with every lost mark labelled by cause. The output is the same as a marked mock would have given you: a ranked list of what is costing marks and a first target, specific enough to act on with or without further sessions.

faqs.question: Can sessions be scheduled around prayer times, Friday and Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they should be. With Friday part of the Dubai weekend, a Friday morning session is the best slot in the week for a full timed paper - the student is rested and there is no school day either side. Around prayer times the slot is simply set to avoid them. During Ramadan the school day shortens and routines move, so sessions shift to a post-Iftar window, run slightly shorter, and the fortnight around Eid becomes consolidation rather than new content. Moving a video slot costs nothing beyond a message.

faqs.question: What happens if the first tutor turns out not to be the right match?
faqs.answer: Tell us early and we change it. Most failed matches are about pace or manner rather than competence, and a fifteen-year-old usually knows within two sessions. The thing to establish before you book - with us or anyone else - is the replacement policy in writing, alongside the cancellation window in hours and whether the quoted rate is per hour or per lesson. A provider that makes a tutor change awkward is optimising for its own diary rather than for your child's term.

intro.heading: The nearest tutor may be teaching the wrong specification
paragraphs: A proximity search has a hidden failure mode in this part of Dubai, and almost nobody warns parents about it. Al Barari is a villa community off Al Ain Road with no school inside its own gates, so every pupil commutes out — some north into Nad Al Sheba, some west towards Motor City and the Arabian Ranches, some further into Dubailand. Those schools do not all use the same awarding body. Two children from neighbouring villas can both be preparing for 'IGCSE Chemistry' and be preparing for different qualifications with different paper structures.

So the tutor who lives closest is not necessarily the tutor who knows your child's course. Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry is syllabus 0620. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry is 4CH1. They cover similar chemistry and examine it differently, and the tiering rules are not the same. A tutor who learned one specification well and is handed a student sitting the other will teach competently for a term and leave the child unprepared for the actual paper. That is a more expensive mistake than paying a higher hourly rate.

This page therefore compares Al Barari with its neighbouring communities honestly and then shows that the comparison does not change the answer. The commutes differ, the school mix differs, and the board mix differs. What does not differ is that selecting by syllabus code produces a better tutor than selecting by distance, in every one of these communities equally.

There is a second reason the proximity instinct misleads here. What parents actually want from a nearby tutor is accountability: someone who can be identified, who will not be swapped out, and who will still be there in eight weeks. Distance is a weak proxy for all three. A named tutor, a written note after every session and a free first lesson in which you watch the teaching happen deliver them directly, and they do not require anybody to drive down Al Ain Road at five o'clock.

The one place where distance genuinely counts is the youngest end. A pupil who needs an adult physically present to stay on task is poorly served by a screen, and we will say so rather than argue a family into a format that cannot work for their child. For Year 10 and Year 11 work, though, a session means worked questions, a marked past paper and a conversation about where the credit went, and none of that requires anyone to be in the room.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE tuition to Al Barari as live one-to-one lessons over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. What follows is the board comparison, the community comparison, the Dubai market rates in dirhams with their sources, the grading scales set side by side, and the permit rules that govern anyone you hire in this emirate.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-barari.programmesIntro: An IGCSE tutor near Al Barari is being asked for at one of three points, and the job is different at each. These are the stages, with what is still changeable at each one.

programmes.name: Year 9, before the course starts
programmes.description: The least common booking and the most efficient. Work at this point is about securing algebraic fluency, written stamina in the sciences and reading-response technique, all of which the IGCSE specification assumes rather than teaches. It also gives a family evidence to use in the subject and tier conversation at the end of the year.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this stage coincides with option choices, and the question families underuse is what each sixth-form route in their own school requires. Schools near Al Barari split at sixteen into A Levels, the IB Diploma or both, and those routes assume specific IGCSE subjects at specific tiers.

programmes.name: Year 10, building the grade
programmes.description: The year in which the grade is actually made. A tutor consolidates content as the school teaches it, builds method, units and command-term discipline before questions get harder, and can flag a mismatched tier entry while it can still be changed. The effort required per mark is lower here than at any later point.
programmes.countryNote: Al Barari commutes make a five o'clock weekday start realistic, so Year 10 families often do better with a weekend morning slot. Dubai school holidays also allow four or five sessions a week, which closes content gaps that a single weekly slot cannot reach.

programmes.name: Year 11, after the mocks
programmes.description: The most common booking. A marked mock paper is evidence, and the first session reads it question by question to establish whether marks went to content, method, units, command terms or timing. Teaching then follows the mark distribution rather than the syllabus order, usually at two sessions a week to the series.
programmes.countryNote: The series matters here. Cambridge runs June and November for UAE candidates and Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November, with entries closing months in advance through the centre. A resit decision taken after results must be entered for the next series rather than taken at a convenient moment.

programmes.name: After IGCSE, into A Level or the Diploma
programmes.description: The destination that should have shaped the tier decision two years earlier. A Level and IB Higher Level courses assume the Extended or Higher tier content in mathematics and the sciences, so a child entered for Core in a subject they intend to continue arrives with a genuine content hole rather than a confidence gap.
programmes.countryNote: For a UAE university application the Ministry of Education's British-track equivalency requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own channel.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-barari.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Al Barari families ask about, with both boards' codes. The codes are the point: a tutor matched to the subject but not the specification is a term wasted.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two papers on each board. Method marks are forfeited by unshown steps even where the final answer is right, which penalises exactly the pupils who calculate quickly in their heads. Rounding and units cost more across a paper than any single topic does.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main course by pupils heading for A Level Mathematics or IB Higher Level Maths AA. Introduces calculus, logarithms and trigonometric identities early. Differentiation is usually where fluency and genuine understanding separate.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Bonding, moles, rates, organic chemistry and qualitative analysis. Mole calculations decide the grade because they recur and compound: an early unit error survives to the final answer. Analysis recall is pure learned content and the cheapest marks available.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, electricity, waves, thermal physics and magnetism. Electricity is the reliable weak spot because circuit reasoning requires holding three relationships together rather than recalling one formula. Practical questions reward naming the controlled variable.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Large content load with exact terminology. Marks go to pupils who answer the command term rather than writing everything they know, and to precise diagram labelling. Inheritance rewards drawing the cross rather than reasoning in prose.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Science
subjects.description: One or two awards covering all three sciences, common where a pupil takes a broader subject spread. Content is reduced per science but the paper still demands the same command-term precision, which catches out pupils who assume it is a lighter course.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing, marked on comprehension, summary skill and control of register. The summary question is the most coachable task on the paper: it rewards selection and compression rather than style.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and, where entered, speaking. Text types are assessed on format and register, so an email, report or article each carry conventions. Confident speakers often underperform here because nobody taught them the conventions explicitly.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study assessment where context carries the marks. Answering with textbook theory and never referring to the business in the stimulus is the standard loss. Costs, revenue and ratio calculations are easy marks routinely skipped under time pressure.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Markets, the macro economy and trade. A mislabelled diagram axis undermines every sentence built on it. Evaluation marks require an explicit stated judgement, which pupils omit even after writing a strong explanation.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Systems, data representation, algorithms and programming. Binary, hexadecimal and logic gates are learnable in a handful of sessions and recur every series. Hand-tracing pseudocode is the missing skill, because pupils learn to run code rather than predict it.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: First language and additional language, plus mandated strands
subjects.description: Compulsory in Dubai private schools alongside the licensed curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and tutoring splits along the same line.

sections.heading: Why your neighbour's tutor may be no use to your child
paragraphs: Recommendation is how most tutoring in villa communities gets arranged, and in a community like Al Barari it carries a specific risk. The family three doors down has a child at a different school, possibly sitting a different awarding body, and their excellent tutor may have no working knowledge of the specification your child will be examined on. This is not a hypothetical. In the Dubailand belt, Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel are both widely used, sometimes within a few kilometres of each other.

The difference is not cosmetic. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 tiers as Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1 tiers as Foundation and Higher. The grade ceilings, the paper structures and the content boundaries differ. In the sciences, Cambridge Physics 0625 and Edexcel 4PH1 treat practical skills differently in the written papers. A tutor who teaches one as though it were the other will cover material that is not examined and skip material that is.

The fix costs one email. Ask the school's exams officer for the awarding body, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject your child takes, and get it in writing rather than relying on what the child believes. Pupils frequently do not know, and a textbook cover is not evidence. Once you have the codes, any tutor can be assessed in two minutes: ask them to describe the papers for that code and the answer is either specific or it is not.

This is also the strongest practical argument for ignoring distance when you choose. The pool of tutors who know Cambridge 0620 well is a different pool from the one who know Edexcel 4CH1 well, and neither pool is distributed by neighbourhood. Filtering by syllabus code gives you the right pool; filtering by postcode gives you whoever is nearby from both.

sections.heading: Al Barari against the communities next door
paragraphs: Here is the comparison the proximity search implies and never shows. These communities sit within a short drive of one another, share roads and school runs, and differ in ways that affect scheduling rather than supply. The useful conclusion is the one in the right-hand column: the sensible answer is the same in every row.

Commute length is the real difference. A Nad Al Sheba pupil may be home by half past three and can start a session at half past four. An Al Barari pupil commuting out, or an Arabian Ranches 3 pupil on shared transport, may not be settled until half past four or five. That hour decides whether a weekday evening slot survives a term or whether the household should be looking at a weekend morning instead. Tired sessions produce very little, and families tend to blame the tutor.

Board mix is the second difference, and it is the one that makes local recommendation unreliable in this belt. Because the communities feed several school clusters, two neighbouring households can be on different specifications in the same subject. A tutor shared between them is teaching one of the two children the wrong paper structure, and nobody notices until a mock.

What does not differ between these communities is specialist supply. The number of tutors in Dubai who know a specific syllabus code at the higher tier is a fixed, fairly small number, and it is not distributed by neighbourhood. In-home rates rise with distance from the centre while the available pool does not improve, so the further out you live the worse the value of a proximity search becomes.

sections.heading: What the travel premium actually buys
paragraphs: Most pages comparing online and in-home tuition argue about effectiveness. The more useful question is narrower: when you pay the in-home premium, what are you buying with that specific money? Market figures read in October 2026 put in-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. Published monthly packages show AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits against around AED 799 for eight online sessions.

So the premium is substantial and it buys exactly three things. It buys an adult physically in the room, which is a real intervention for a young or distractible child. It buys a session that does not depend on a connection. And it buys the absence of a screen, which some families value for its own sake. Those are legitimate purchases and this page is not going to argue a family out of them.

What the premium does not buy is better teaching, a wider choice of tutor, or more reliable attendance. On the contrary: it narrows the pool to people who will drive to a villa community off Al Ain Road at five on a weekday and hold that slot weekly for a term, and it introduces traffic as a cancellation risk on both legs of the journey. Two lost weeks in a Year 11 spring term is two weeks removed from a fixed countdown to the series.

IB Gram does not offer in-home tuition anywhere in the UAE, so the comparison here is not neutral and should be read with that in mind. The figures, though, are the market's own published numbers, and the three things the premium buys are stated as plainly as we can state them. If one of those three is what your child needs, the right provider is one who offers it, and that is not us in this country.

sections.heading: Grading scales, tiers and ceilings, side by side
paragraphs: Parents in Dubai deal with two IGCSE grading scales at once and frequently do not realise it. Cambridge reports some syllabuses on A* to G and others on 9 to 1, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on 9 to 1. A child may therefore come home with an A in one subject and a 7 in another from the same series, and comparing them requires knowing which scale each sits on. Ask the school which scale each of your child's subjects uses, because the answer affects how you read a mock result.

The second thing to understand is the tier ceiling. On Cambridge, a Core entry caps the grade that can be awarded regardless of how well the paper is answered. The Extended tier reaches the full range. Edexcel's Foundation and Higher tiers work the same way. This is the single most consequential administrative decision in the two years, and it is usually made quietly in Year 10 on the basis of a school assessment.

If your child is on the lower tier in a subject they intend to continue at A Level or IB Higher Level, raise it with the school now rather than after the mocks. Whether the entry can still move depends on the school and on how close the entry deadline is, and entries close months before papers are sat. A tutor's useful role here is evidential: a marked past paper at the higher tier is a more persuasive document in that conversation than a parent's opinion.

The table sets the scales and ceilings next to each other. Treat it as a structural guide and confirm your child's specific subjects with the school, because awarding bodies revise which syllabuses sit on which scale and the current specification is the authority.

sections.heading: A revision routine that works in a commuting household
paragraphs: The most common reason IGCSE tutoring underperforms is not the tutor. It is that the set work between sessions does not get done, and in a commuting household with a five o'clock arrival home there is a real reason for that. So the routine has to be designed around the week that exists rather than the week a revision guide assumes.

What works is small and specific. One past-paper question set per subject per week, timed, rather than an hour of open revision. Timed is the operative word: a student who knows the material but spends fourteen minutes on a six-mark question will not finish the paper, and unanswered questions score nothing. Twenty minutes with a clock running teaches more than ninety minutes without one, and it fits in a household where the evening starts late.

The second element is marking against the published scheme rather than against a sense of whether the answer was right. This is the habit that changes results, because it shows the student where credit is actually awarded: a method step, a unit, a named variable, a stated judgement. Students who learn to read a mark scheme start writing for the marker instead of writing what they know. A tutor's job in the session is largely to build that habit and then check it.

The third is sequencing by weakness rather than by syllabus order. Revision guides work front to back, which means a student spends week one on content they already know. A marked diagnostic paper tells you which three or four topics are producing most of the lost marks, and those go first. In a household with limited evening hours, that ordering is the difference between a term of revision that moves a grade and a term that confirms one.

sections.heading: The school's regulator and the tutor's permit
paragraphs: Two different regimes apply here and parents routinely merge them. Your child's school is regulated by the emirate. In Dubai that is KHDA, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, inspecting annually across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. Dubai had 227 private schools and 387,441 pupils in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum accounting for 37% of enrolment, which is why IGCSE provision in the Dubailand belt is so broad.

The tutor is regulated federally. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE is subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

No fine amount appears on this page. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and the figure circulating online could not be verified, so printing it would be guesswork dressed as information. Nor is IB Gram approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes operating premises in Dubai, and nobody should imply otherwise without a permit number.

The useful thing about knowing all this is that it gives you three questions that sort a market quickly. Do you hold a MoHRE private tuition permit? Which awarding body and syllabus code do you teach? Do you work at a school my child attends? The last one matters because ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid tutoring of their own enrolled pupils and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar.
