sections.heading: Three English qualifications with one name, and the misplacement that follows
paragraphs: English is where Al Barsha South families most often discover their child is sitting a different exam from the one they assumed. Cambridge IGCSE English First Language exists as 0500, graded A*-G, and as 0990, graded 9-1. Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language runs as 0510, 0511 and 0993. Pearson offers English Language A as 4EA1. These are not difficulty levels of the same course; they are separate qualifications with separate papers.

The placement decision is usually made by a school in Year 9 on the basis of a reading assessment, and it is rarely revisited. A child who arrived in Dubai with limited English in Year 7 and is fluent by Year 10 may still be sitting ESL, which caps what universities and the Ministry of Education will later treat the qualification as demonstrating. The reverse happens too: a student placed on First Language who cannot yet access the reading passages loses marks across every paper.

For tutoring, the practical consequence is that the preparation diverges early. First Language rewards a directed-writing response with controlled register and a reading response that quotes precisely and comments on effect. ESL rewards accurate retrieval of detail and a narrower range of writing forms, with speaking assessed separately. A tutor teaching essay craft to an ESL candidate is teaching skills the mark scheme will not pay for.

The check is quick. Ask the school which code is on the entry, and ask to see one specimen paper. Ten minutes with the specimen tells a parent more about whether the placement is right than a term of reports will.

sections.heading: A past-paper sequence that is actually worth doing
paragraphs: Most students do past papers badly: open a paper, answer the questions they can, check the answers, feel reassured. That produces a measurement rather than a gain. The sequence below produces a gain, and it is the structure our tutors use for the final two terms of an IGCSE course.

The core idea is that a paper is worth doing three times in three different ways. Once untimed and open-book, to learn the question types. Once timed and closed, to measure. Once as a marking exercise on somebody else's script or your own, to learn what the examiner is paying for. Students who do five papers properly outperform students who do twenty-five badly, and the second group is much larger.

Official material only. Cambridge, Pearson and the schools themselves publish past papers and mark schemes, and those are what we work from. We do not reproduce or distribute syllabus documents, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we cite them and link the official source so a family can open the current version themselves. Third-party question banks that paraphrase real papers teach the paraphrase.

The sequencing below is counted in weeks before the paper rather than in calendar dates, because the series your child sits depends on the school. For a UAE candidate, that is the Cambridge June series or the Pearson May/June series, with November as the resit route. The February/March Cambridge series is offered to India only and is not available to a Dubai centre.

sections.heading: What a syllabus specialist costs around Al Barsha South
paragraphs: Published rates in this market cluster into recognisable bands, and a parent can check most of them in ten minutes of searching. The cheapest advertised online tuition starts low: EdFlik lists from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, which puts the budget online tier somewhere between AED 45 and 150. Those tutors are frequently university students, and for arithmetic fluency drills that can be the correct purchase.

Move up one step and you are paying for somebody who knows the specification rather than the subject. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, which maps onto a qualified-subject-tutor band of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour online. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tutors run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table showing 200 to 450 plus. At the top, BartyED advertises AED 650 for a premium named tutor.

In-home visits sit between those two bands and on a different logic. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, with travel built into the hour. Monthly packages advertised in Dubai include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support.

Those are market figures published by other providers with the date and source stated, not an IB Gram price list. What they show is that the premium for a true specification specialist is real but bounded, and that the premium for travel buys travel. For a family in Al Barsha South deciding between a nearby generalist at AED 180 and an online 0620 specialist at AED 250, the second is the cheaper way to buy a chemistry grade. Our own model starts with a free trial lesson and a quoted rate for the subject and level before anything is paid.

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor your child in Dubai, and how you check
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and the permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

An individual tutoring without that permit is, in the u.ae wording, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount can honestly be quoted; a figure circulating online could not be verified against any ministry source. The useful point for a parent is that the permit costs the tutor nothing, which removes the only excuse for not holding one.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal. That requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and makes no claim to one: we are an independent online tutor-matching platform with no UAE office, centre or branch, and no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

One more rule worth knowing. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than verbatim policy and check the current document. Either way, a parent should never be offered their child's own class teacher privately, and an offer like that is a reason to walk away.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Barsha South, and the parts we will not promise
paragraphs: A useful enquiry from Al Barsha South contains four things: the syllabus code, the tier, the papers already sat and the specific thing going wrong. With those, a match is a short conversation. Without them, the first lesson is spent finding them out, which is a lesson you paid for to establish facts that were written on the entry confirmation.

The first lesson is free and diagnostic. The tutor works through recent script evidence if there is any, establishes which specification statements are insecure, and separates content gaps from question-reading gaps. At the end you get a written summary naming the papers, the topics and the mark types being lost. If the honest answer is that your child needs a better revision timetable rather than a tutor, we will say that; it costs us a sale and saves you a term.

Where we will not stretch the truth: lessons to Al Barsha South, Arjan and Dubai Science Park are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and no tutor will arrive at a Dubai address. We publish no guaranteed grade, no score improvement figure and no satisfaction statistic, because none of those can be evidenced on a page. A tutor teaches, explains and gives feedback on your child's own work, and never writes the coursework or the investigation that must be the student's own.

On availability, the honest version is that a common combination such as 0580 Extended or 0620 is usually matched within a few days, and a narrow one such as 0607 Extended with the investigation paper, or a minority-language specification, can take longer or occasionally cannot be covered at all. We say so at the point of enquiry rather than matching you to whoever is free. The enquiry form collects the student's year group, school, subject, specification and a contact for the parent; it is used to make the match and nothing else, and you can ask for it to be deleted at any time.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE specification my child in Al Barsha South is sitting?
faqs.answer: Look at the exam entry confirmation the school issues, or the top line of any past paper the department has handed out. You are looking for a four-digit Cambridge number such as 0580 or 0620, or a Pearson code beginning with 4, such as 4MA1. If neither is to hand, the school's exam officer can tell you in one email, and heads of department expect the question. The code also tells you the tier of entry, which is the figure that sets the maximum grade available, so it is worth having in writing before any tutoring conversation starts.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who lives in Al Barsha South better than one teaching from a screen?
faqs.answer: Only if they happen to specialise in the same specification, which is unlikely in a residential district of this size. Al Barsha South has no resident expert in Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 Paper 6 simply by virtue of being a neighbourhood. Choosing by distance selects from whoever is within a twenty-minute drive; choosing by specification selects from everyone qualified. For Al Barsha South, Arjan and Dubai Science Park families, IB Gram delivers lessons online over live video, and the reason is this one: the pool of people who genuinely know your child's papers is much larger than the pool who can reach your door.

faqs.question: Which command terms lose Al Barsha South students the most IGCSE marks?
faqs.answer: A command term is the instruction verb at the start of an exam question, and every mark scheme is written around it. Describe wants observable features. Explain wants a reason linked with a because. Analyse wants a connected chain of consequences. Evaluate wants a judgement with support. A student who writes a good description in answer to an explain question scores nothing for it, however accurate the content. Four command terms learned properly lift marks across every subject at once, which makes this the highest-return hour of teaching available to a Year 10 student.

faqs.question: Can my child move from Core to Extended, and when is it too late?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and the deadline is set by the exam entry rather than by the teaching. The tier is fixed when the school submits entries, which happens months before the papers. A Core entry caps the grade at C, so a student who improves through Year 11 can be sitting a paper that cannot award what they now deserve. The conversation to have with the head of department is in the autumn term of Year 11. Ask directly when entries close and whether the tier can still be changed; schools answer that question routinely.

faqs.question: Does Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 really have a non-calculator paper now?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under the current syllabus, 0580 Extended candidates sit a non-calculator Paper 2 and a calculator Paper 4, each two hours and 100 marks. Core candidates sit the equivalent pair as Paper 1 and Paper 3. That means roughly half the written marks depend on hand arithmetic, surds, indices and fraction work under time pressure. Dubai cohorts are often weak here because calculators are permitted in school assessments from early secondary. Ten minutes of daily mental arithmetic from Year 9 is worth more than a revision course in April, and it costs nothing.

faqs.question: My child is on Pearson 4MA1 Higher. Is the preparation different from Cambridge?
faqs.answer: Substantially. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A Higher permits a calculator on both papers, so the risk moves away from hand arithmetic and towards over-reliance on the machine: a value typed in wrongly and accepted because no estimate was made first. The grading is 9-1 throughout rather than Cambridge's A*-G in older syllabuses. A tutor who assumes a Cambridge structure will teach non-calculator fluency your child does not need and skip the estimation discipline they do, which is why the specification code belongs in the first message you send.

faqs.question: What is the difference between English First Language and English as a Second Language at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: They are separate qualifications, not difficulty levels. Cambridge runs First Language as 0500, graded A*-G, and 0990, graded 9-1, with a reading response and directed writing at the centre. English as a Second Language runs as 0510, 0511 and 0993, with speaking assessed separately and a reading paper rewarding precise retrieval of detail. Placement is usually decided in Year 9 and rarely revisited, so a child who was new to English at eleven and fluent at fifteen may still be entered for the wrong one. Ask the school which code is on the entry.

faqs.question: How should my child actually use past papers rather than just doing them?
faqs.answer: Do fewer papers, three ways each. First untimed with the syllabus open, to learn the question types. Then timed and closed, to measure honestly. Then as a marking exercise, where the student marks their own script against the official mark scheme while the tutor challenges every decision. That third pass is the one almost nobody does and the one that changes grades, because it shows the student what the examiner is paying for. Five papers worked properly beat twenty-five answered and glanced at.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE exams happen for a candidate sitting them in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE centres, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only and is not available to a Dubai centre, so ignore any plan built around it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, so use the one your child's school publishes.

faqs.question: How quickly do November results arrive if we need a retake decision?
faqs.answer: For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is the pattern to plan around rather than a promise about a future series. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. That January gap matters for a family weighing a retake, because it leaves limited time before the following summer series. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each session, so open the live official timetable PDF rather than relying on a restated date from any page, including this one.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to our villa in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons for families in Al Barsha South, Arjan, Dubai Science Park and Jumeirah Village Circle are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. The market for in-home visits is real and priced between roughly AED 180 and 500 an hour by other providers, with travel inside the rate. We quote that honestly rather than matching it, because the money a Dubai family spends on a tutor's commute buys a commute.

faqs.question: What does a genuine specification specialist cost compared with a general tutor?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates group into bands. Budget online tuition starts low, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online sit around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table showing 200 to 450 plus. Those are other providers' published figures with their sources, not ours. The step from generalist to specialist is one band; the step to a premium named tutor is several.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Dubai need a permit, and can I check it?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day turnaround. Ask any tutor directly whether they hold it. Because the permit costs nothing, there is no honest reason for a working tutor not to have one.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's IGCSE coursework or science investigation?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the method, explain the assessment criteria, question a plan and give feedback on a draft the student has written. No tutor should write, redraft to completion or produce any part of assessed work, and we will not. Schools and awarding bodies treat that as malpractice, and the consequences land on the student rather than on the tutor. If anyone offers to supply a finished investigation or essay, that is the point to stop the conversation. The honest version of coursework support is slower and it is the only version that is safe.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE grades does the Ministry of Education actually count for equivalency?
faqs.answer: The British-track requirement published for secondary certificate equivalency is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor states six subjects, which is wrong. Equivalency is handled by the Ministry rather than by any tutoring provider, so verify the current rule on the official channel before acting on it.

faqs.question: Do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies still apply if my child sits IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Those lessons occupy timetable space, which is worth factoring into how much homework capacity a Year 11 student realistically has.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-barsha-s.closingHeading: Start with the code, then the lesson
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-barsha-s.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, make it the four-digit number. A parent in Al Barsha South who can say "0580 Extended, Paper 2 is the problem, here is last term's script" will get a better tutor, faster, at a lower cost than a parent describing a general worry, and that holds whoever they buy from. Send the code, the tier and the papers already sat, and the first lesson is free and diagnostic. You will finish it with a written account of which specification statements are insecure and which mark types are being dropped, delivered online over live video, and an honest answer about whether a tutor is the right purchase at all.

intro.heading: Proximity is easy to verify. Syllabus knowledge is not.
paragraphs: A search for a tutor near you returns distance, and distance is the one thing about a tutor that does not affect a grade. What a parent in Al Furjan actually needs to know is whether the person on the other end of the enquiry has taught the specific syllabus their child is entered for, can name the papers, knows which tier caps which grade, and has marked work against the board's own conventions. None of that is visible from a listing or a community group recommendation.

This matters more in Al Furjan than in some other parts of Dubai, because the local pool is small. The community sits between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Yalayis Road, residential rather than academic, with Discovery Gardens to the north and Dubai Investments Park to the south. The tutors who will drive into the villa districts for a 17:00 start are a limited group, and choosing from a limited group means accepting whoever is in it.

The failure mode is quiet. A competent tutor teaches good lessons on the wrong board's material. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is syllabus 0580 and the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE equivalent is 4MA1; the tier names, paper structure, formula provision and mark-scheme conventions differ. Six weeks in, the student is still underperforming and nothing in the lessons looks wrong. That is a term lost to a question nobody asked at the start.

So this page is a verification guide rather than a sales page. It gives you five questions to put to any tutor, in Al Furjan or anywhere else, and tells you what a good answer sounds like. It describes the categories of people who make up the Dubai IGCSE tutor pool and what each is genuinely good for. It explains why knowing a syllabus means knowing a mark scheme. And it says plainly where the honest answer is that nobody available covers your subject.

IB Gram's own position: we match on the board and syllabus code you give us, name the tutor and their components before the first lesson, and deliver every UAE session one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30. No tutor attends a UAE address, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. If physical presence is what you need, this is the point to stop reading rather than after a phone call.

One practical instruction before the detail. Ask the school's exams officer for your child's entry list. It shows the board and the code for every subject, and several schools in this corridor enter different boards in different departments. That single document turns a vague search into a specific one, and it is free. Everything else on this page is easier once you have it in front of you.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-furjan.programmesIntro: Verification looks different at each stage, because the evidence available changes. These are the three stages either side of the Year 11 papers and what you can actually check at each.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: No external assessment, so there is nothing to verify a tutor against except their explanation of what they are building. What they should be building is narrow and checkable: algebraic fluency, formula rearrangement without guessing, and paragraphs that answer the question asked. A tutor who cannot name the specific skills they are developing at this stage is working on generalities.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Furjan this is the stage where verification is easiest to skip and most useful. Year 8 and 9 students are home before 16:30, so a session fits earlier in the afternoon than any Year 11 slot. It is also when the school decides tier recommendations, and a tutor who can read marked work against the Extended tier requirement is giving you information the report card does not.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE, Years 10 to 11
programmes.description: Two years, terminal written papers, and a grade largely decided by mark-scheme compliance rather than by knowledge. A tutor who knows this syllabus can name the paper numbers, state what each is worth, describe the tiering, and explain the difference between describe, explain and evaluate in that board's wording. That is the whole verification test, and it takes five minutes.
programmes.countryNote: This is where nearly every Al Furjan enquiry sits. Year 11 students in this corridor reach home between 15:40 and 16:30, later with a school revision clinic, so a 17:00 or 17:30 start is normal. Verification matters most here because there is no second chance within the two years: the terminal papers arrive once, and the November series is the only other route.

programmes.name: Advanced Level or IB Diploma afterwards
programmes.description: The Year 11 grade profile decides which post-16 routes stay open. Most British-curriculum schools want grade 6 or 7 in a subject before accepting it at Advanced Level, and IB Diploma Higher Level entry usually asks the same. A tutor who understands this talks about tier and target grade together rather than treating them as separate conversations.
programmes.countryNote: Al Furjan families moving from IGCSE into the IB Diploma generally change schools, because full Diploma provision in the Jebel Ali corridor is thinner than further north. The widest gap in the whole transition is mathematics: Extended IGCSE builds procedure, while Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level expects calculus notation and sustained proof from the first term.

programmes.name: The November series and resit route
programmes.description: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. A resit is worth entering when the paper-level breakdown shows a near miss on one component in a subject needed for an offer, and is usually the wrong answer when marks were spread evenly below target across every paper.
programmes.countryNote: The November route is the easiest time of year to verify and secure a specialist, because demand across Dubai collapses after August results. For an Al Furjan family that means a genuine choice of tutor rather than whoever is left, and sessions running through the UAE summer when nothing else is competing for the evening.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-furjan.subjectsIntro: What counts as syllabus knowledge differs by subject. For each of these, the note names the specific thing a tutor should be able to tell you in the first conversation.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Ask which tier your child is entered for and what grade it caps at. A tutor who knows this subject talks about method marks before answers, and can explain why a correct final answer with no working scores below a wrong answer with sound method in a multi-step question.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: Ask how much calculus the paper examines and how it differs from the main entry. This is the best bridge into Advanced Level or Diploma mathematics and the most under-taught subject in this corridor, so a tutor who has actually taught it is worth holding onto.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Ask whether the entry carries a laboratory paper or the alternative-to-practical written paper. A specialist will then talk about gradients, unit conversion and naming control variables, because that is where the marks go, rather than about which topics are hardest.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Ask how they teach the chemical tests. The right answer involves observations and conclusions rather than a memorised list, because the paper asks what you would see and what it shows. Mole calculations are the other reliable source of lost marks across every cohort.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Ask what makes an answer about an increase score zero. A specialist will say immediately that naming the mechanism and the direction is required and that vague cause-and-effect answers earn nothing. Genetic crosses and required practical technique are the other two recoverable areas.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: Ask which award the school entered, because double and single award differ in content and in what they allow afterwards. A weakness in one discipline is carried into every paper here, so a tutor needs to be credible across all three rather than strong in one.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Ask what a reading question rewards. The answer should be selective quotation with precise explanation of effect, not summary. A tutor who talks about writing everything the student noticed is describing the commonest way marks are lost in this paper.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Ask how they mark a timed essay. The grade depends on argument structure and embedded quotation rather than plot recall, and the only intervention that moves it is repeated timed writing with marked feedback, which is labour-intensive and therefore a useful honesty test.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Ask them to distinguish explain, analyse and evaluate in that board's wording. Students who write the same paragraph shape for all three cap out around grade 6, and a tutor who cannot separate them cannot fix it.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Ask about pseudocode conventions. Confident coders routinely lose marks writing pseudocode that does not follow the board's own notation, which is a narrow and quickly closed gap but only if the tutor knows the convention exists.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Ask what a source question expects. Content recall without mark-scheme awareness is the standard failure in both subjects, and a tutor who talks only about case studies has not seen enough marked scripts.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic to all pupils under KHDA rules, in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Ask which entry your child sits, since first language and additional language are different qualifications, and support works from the school's own prescribed material.

sections.heading: What a search for a tutor near you actually returns
paragraphs: A proximity search ranks by distance and by who has paid to appear, and neither correlates with teaching the right syllabus. What comes back is a mix of agencies with managed rosters, international marketplaces listing tutors in other time zones, freelance tutors advertising in community groups, and tuition centres selling group courses. Each of those is a different product and a different risk, and the listing does not distinguish them.

The second thing a proximity search hides is time-zone and location reality. Two of the most visible competitor pages in this market route UAE parents to Indian phone numbers, and one shows a Dubai footer address on a page written for Abu Dhabi. A page can appear local without anything behind it being local, and the only reliable test is asking directly who will teach, from where, and in which time zone.

The third is the board. Nothing in a listing tells you whether the tutor teaches Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, and in Dubai both are common. Several schools in this corridor enter Cambridge in one department and Pearson in another, so even a tutor who teaches at your child's school may know the wrong set of papers for the subject you need. That is not incompetence; it is a mismatch nobody checked.

What replaces proximity as a useful filter is the syllabus code. Get the entry list from the school's exams officer, which names the board and code for every subject, and use it as the first question in every enquiry. IB Gram matches on that code and names the tutor and their components before any lesson. The lesson itself runs one-to-one over live video; no tutor attends a UAE address.

sections.heading: Five questions that separate a specialist from a generalist
paragraphs: Verification takes about five minutes if you ask the right things. The questions below are not technical tests of the tutor; they are tests of whether they have taught this specific qualification to this specific board recently enough to remember how it is marked. A tutor who has will answer all five without hesitating. A tutor who has not will answer in generalities that sound reasonable.

The pattern to listen for is specificity about assessment rather than about content. Anyone can say that electricity is a hard topic in Physics. A specialist says that students lose marks on gradient calculations because they read coordinates off the plotted points rather than from the line of best fit. The first is a topic observation; the second is a mark-scheme observation, and only the second changes a grade.

Watch for one particular evasion. Asked which board they teach, a weak answer is that the syllabuses are broadly similar. They are not, in the ways that matter: tier names, paper counts, formula provision and mark-scheme conventions all differ between Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel for the same subject. A tutor who treats that as a detail is telling you they work from generic material.

Finally, ask what they will not do. A tutor who volunteers that they teach technique and give feedback on the student's own work but do not write or rewrite assessed work is describing the correct boundary unprompted. In a market where at least one provider openly sells completed coursework, that answer is informative about everything else in the arrangement.

sections.heading: Who is actually in the Dubai IGCSE tutor pool
paragraphs: The pool is not one group of people and the differences are practical rather than snobbish. School teachers tutoring privately bring current classroom and marking experience, but they are constrained: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. So the appealing option of hiring your child's own teacher is the one specifically excluded.

Recent graduates and university students are the budget end of the market, and published rates reflect it: Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 per hour. They are genuinely useful for structured homework support and for keeping a capable student moving. They are not usually the right choice for a tiering decision, a coursework boundary question or a mark-scheme diagnosis, because they have never marked to a published scheme.

Career tutors and agency rosters sit in the AED 150 to 450 band, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase AED 270. This is where board-specific experience concentrates, and it is the group worth putting the five questions to, because within it the range of actual syllabus knowledge is wide. The examiner-experienced end of the market, where BartyED publishes AED 650, is rarely necessary before the final two terms.

Then there are overseas online tutors, who may be excellent and may be teaching a different qualification under a similar name. GCSE and IGCSE are not identical, and a tutor trained on the English domestic GCSE may not know the International GCSE papers your child sits. Ask the question directly. All rates quoted here are published market figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices.

sections.heading: Knowing the syllabus means knowing the mark scheme
paragraphs: Parents reasonably assume that a tutor who knows the subject knows what the exam wants. At IGCSE those are different bodies of knowledge. The subject is the content; the exam is a set of conventions about how that content must be expressed to earn a mark. A graduate chemist can explain a reaction mechanism beautifully and still not know that the paper awards a mark for the observation and a separate mark for the conclusion.

The clearest example is command terms. Describe, explain, compare and evaluate each require a different shape of answer, and the boards publish what each one means. A student who writes a description when the paper asked for an explanation loses the marks regardless of how accurate the description is. A tutor who knows the syllabus corrects that in the first session; a tutor who knows only the subject may never notice it.

The second example is method marks in mathematics. In a multi-step question, a wrong final answer with sound working often scores more than a correct answer with no working. Students who do everything on the calculator lose marks they have genuinely earned. This is not a content gap and no amount of topic revision fixes it, which is why topic-based tutoring can run for a term without moving a grade.

The third is practical skills in science. Whether the entry carries a laboratory paper or the alternative-to-practical written paper, the marks go to specific behaviours: units in the table heading, a scale that fills the grid, a named control variable with a method for controlling it, an explained anomaly rather than a circled one. Those are trainable in a handful of sessions, and they are where a specialist earns their rate.

sections.heading: What a tutor should be able to tell you about the papers
paragraphs: A short test that works well on a first call: ask the tutor to describe the assessment structure of the subject without looking anything up. Not the content, the structure. How many papers, roughly what each is worth, what tier applies, and whether there is a practical or coursework component. Someone teaching that qualification this year will do it immediately. Someone working from generic material will offer to send details later.

The reason this works is that structure is what planning depends on. If a student is losing marks predominantly on one component, the revision plan should weight that component, and that is impossible to design without knowing what each is worth. A plan that treats every paper as equal is a plan written by someone who does not know which paper matters most for this student.

Boards differ here in ways that matter. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel structure the same subject differently, assess practical skills by different routes, and provide different formula support in the exam room. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge runs June and November and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating that it is essential to use the correct zone timetable and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

One caution on documents. We do not reproduce or distribute board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, and nor should any tutor. The correct practice is to cite and link the official source and work from material the school has issued to the student. A tutor offering you a folder of downloaded papers and mark schemes is offering something that is not theirs to give.

sections.heading: How a parent in Al Furjan verifies the permit and the claims
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the facts are simple enough to check in a single question. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The ministry's service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and runs through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule has been published this page quotes no amount.

Then verify the claims rather than the credentials. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, which means school licensing and inspection, not tutor approval. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a separate licence issued to training institutes operating premises in Dubai. So a claim of KHDA endorsement for an individual tutor describes something that does not exist in that form. IB Gram holds no such approval and does not claim one.

Be equally careful with examiner claims and review scores. Describing a tutor as a current examiner is only meaningful with evidence of current status, and examiner status does not give anyone access to marking, boundaries or paper content. On reviews, one competitor shows two different star ratings and review counts on the same page. A rating you cannot trace to countable, dated reviews is a marketing figure.

sections.heading: Try the free options before you pay for anything
paragraphs: Two useful things in this market cost nothing, and a family that tries them first buys tutoring more intelligently afterwards. The first is the school's own subject clinic or support session. The teacher who set the assessment is the person best placed to explain the marking of it, and in most Dubai schools that time exists and is under-used. It is limited and rarely diagnostic across a whole subject, but it is free and immediate.

The second is the KHDA inspection report for your child's school. KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes the reports, which name subject-level strengths and weaknesses rather than giving a single verdict. For an Al Furjan parent deciding whether a weak mathematics result is a child problem or a department problem, that document answers the question before any tutor is hired.

Third, ask for the paper-level breakdown of your child's last mock. Schools hold it and often do not send it out. A grade 5 that came from one weak component is a different problem from a grade 5 spread evenly across every paper, and the two need opposite plans. This is also the document that makes a trial lesson useful rather than conversational.

Only after those three does a paid tutor become a well-specified purchase: you know the subject, the component, the pattern of lost marks and whether the school can address it. That is what we ask for at the start, and it is why our free trial is built around a marked paper you provide rather than around a general conversation about how your child is finding school.

sections.heading: When the honest answer is that nobody available covers it
paragraphs: Every tutoring page in this market implies a bottomless roster. The truthful position is that some subjects at some times are not available, and an Al Furjan family deserves that answer before paying rather than after. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English at IGCSE are usually matched within a few days. Additional Mathematics, Further Pure Mathematics, Arabic as a first language, Computer Science and the smaller humanities entries take longer.

Timing compounds it. In the four weeks of study leave before the June series, every Year 11 family in Dubai is looking at once, and specialists in the common subjects fill first. In the summer and autumn, when November-series candidates are the only demand, the same specialists have space. So the same request produces a different answer depending entirely on the month in which it is made.

When the right specialist is not free for your slot, we give one of three answers: a different time with the correct tutor, a short wait with a date attached, or a straight recommendation to look elsewhere. We will not put a tutor who teaches the other board on the call, and we will not describe a generalist as a specialist. That substitution is the exact failure this page exists to help you avoid.

The free trial is where all of this gets tested, by you rather than by us. Bring the marked paper, ask what pattern connects the lost marks, and judge the answer. Nothing is paid, and if the match is wrong you say so and we try once more or stop. Treating that hour as an interview is the single most useful thing an Al Furjan parent can do in this process.

faqs.question: Is there anyone in Al Furjan who genuinely knows my child's IGCSE syllabus?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and the way to find out is the entry list rather than a community recommendation. Al Furjan is residential rather than academic, so the number of subject specialists within a short drive is small, and smaller still once you require a specific board. Get the board and syllabus code from the school's exams officer, then ask any tutor to state the paper structure for that code from memory. Someone teaching it this year answers immediately. That question filters the local pool faster than anything else available to you.

faqs.question: Why does the exam board matter so much if the subject is the same?
faqs.answer: Because the exam is not the subject. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 and the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE equivalent is 4MA1, and between them the tier names, paper count, formula provision and mark-scheme conventions all differ. A tutor working from the wrong board's material teaches good lessons that aim at the wrong target. Nothing about those lessons looks wrong, which is why the mistake survives for a term. Several Dubai schools also enter different boards in different departments, so one student can need two sets of papers.

faqs.question: Can I just hire a teacher from my child's own school privately?
faqs.answer: That is the one arrangement the rules specifically exclude. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. A teacher from a different school is a different matter, and brings current marking experience with them. What your child's own teacher can legitimately give is time in the school's subject clinic.

faqs.question: What single question best exposes a tutor who does not know the papers?
faqs.answer: Ask where students lose marks in this subject, and listen to whether the answer is about a topic or about the mark scheme. A topic answer, such as electricity being difficult, is something anyone could say. A mark-scheme answer, such as students reading gradients from plotted points instead of the line of best fit, or writing a description where the paper asked for an explanation, can only come from someone who has marked scripts. Only mark-scheme errors are quickly recoverable, so only the second answer is useful to you.

faqs.question: Does a university student tutor at AED 50 an hour ever make sense?
faqs.answer: For structured homework support and keeping a capable student moving, yes, and published Dubai rates at that end run AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik. What that tier cannot usually do is diagnose a mark-scheme pattern, advise on a tiering decision, or hold a coursework boundary, because nobody in it has marked to a published scheme. Spending AED 50 an hour on the wrong task costs more than spending AED 200 on the right one. Match the tier to the problem rather than to the budget.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether an online tutor teaches International GCSE or the English GCSE?
faqs.answer: Ask outright, because the qualifications are not identical and a tutor trained on the English domestic GCSE may not know the International GCSE papers your child sits. Follow it with the code question: name the syllabus, and ask them to describe the components. A specialist in Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1 will do it without checking. This matters particularly for overseas online tutors, who may be excellent teachers of a qualification with a similar name and a different paper structure.

faqs.question: What does the KHDA inspection report tell an Al Furjan parent before hiring anyone?
faqs.answer: Whether the problem is your child or the department. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes reports that name subject-level strengths and weaknesses rather than giving one overall verdict. If mathematics attainment is flagged across the school, a tutor is addressing a structural issue and should be briefed accordingly. If the department is strong and your child is not, the diagnosis is individual. The report is free and public, and almost nobody reads it before buying tutoring.

faqs.question: My child got a grade 5 in the mock. What should I ask the school for?
faqs.answer: The paper-level breakdown, which schools hold and often do not send out. A grade 5 produced by one weak component is a different problem from a grade 5 spread evenly across every paper, and the two need opposite plans: targeted component drilling in the first case, broad consolidation in the second. Without that breakdown any tutoring plan is guesswork. It is also the document that turns a trial lesson into a diagnosis rather than a conversation about how your child is finding school.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give me past papers and mark schemes to work through at home?
faqs.answer: A tutor should not be distributing them, and one offering a folder of downloaded board material is offering something that is not theirs to give. IB Gram cites and links official sources and works from material the school has issued to the student. Reproducing syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables is a copyright matter, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure for the student. Ask the school what it can release; most will share past papers for the student's own entry.

faqs.question: How quickly can a verified IGCSE specialist actually start in this corridor?
faqs.answer: For Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English, usually within a few days. Additional Mathematics, Further Pure Mathematics, Arabic as a first language, Computer Science and the smaller humanities entries take longer at any time of year. Availability tightens sharply during the four weeks of study leave before the June series, when every Year 11 family in Dubai is looking at once, and is at its widest in the summer when November-series candidates are the only demand. The same request gets a different answer in different months.

faqs.question: Should I trust a tutoring site that advertises a 4.9 star rating?
faqs.answer: Only if the reviews are countable, dated and attributable. One competitor in this market displays two different ratings and review counts on the same page, and another shows a perfect score from twenty reviews next to a student count it cannot support. Self-asserted rating markup is against Google's structured-data policy and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, carries consumer-protection exposure. This page carries no rating, no satisfaction percentage and no student count, because we cannot produce the underlying data for any of them.

faqs.question: What should a first session look like if the tutor really knows the syllabus?
faqs.answer: It should start with your child's marked work rather than with a syllabus overview. Within twenty minutes the tutor should be naming a pattern: command-term errors in extended response, method marks lost to calculator-only working, units misplaced in practical tables. By the end you should have a stated number of sessions and a specific first target. A first session spent on introductions, a diagnostic quiz and a general plan is a sales call, and you have learned nothing you could not have read on a website.

faqs.question: Is online tuition a compromise for a Year 11 student in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: For Year 10 and Year 11 work it is usually the better option, because what decides the grade is the match on board and component rather than physical presence. A session is largely a marked paper, a mark scheme and a discussion of specific answers, all of which share to a screen cleanly. It also removes the travel constraint that keeps the Al Furjan in-home pool small. The honest exception is children under eight, who are easier to hold in a room than on a call.

faqs.question: Which boards do UAE candidates sit, and when?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only and must not be used to plan a UAE entry. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct zone timetable, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. Get the zone timetable from your school.

faqs.question: Does my child still take Arabic alongside IGCSE at a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, and states that combined classes are strictly prohibited. Ask which Arabic entry your child sits, since first language and additional language are separate qualifications, and support works from the school's own prescribed material.

faqs.question: What happens if I decide after the trial that the tutor is not right?
faqs.answer: You say so and nothing is owed. No payment is taken for the trial lesson and there is no obligation afterwards. We will either try one more tutor or tell you honestly that we cannot cover your subject and slot, which happens with the scarcer entries and during study leave. Families in Al Furjan who treat the trial as an interview, with a marked paper and a prepared question, make this decision confidently in one session instead of discovering a mismatch six weeks into a monthly commitment.

intro.heading: Nobody in Al Garhoud goes to school in Al Garhoud
paragraphs: Al Garhoud is a small neighbourhood between Dubai International Airport, the Creek and the bridge named after it. It has one well-known school inside its boundaries and a population of secondary students who travel out of it every morning — across the water to Dubai Festival City, down to Oud Metha, or east towards Al Qusais. A search for a tutor near me therefore asks for something the geography does not supply, and the honest response is to stop solving for distance and start solving for the week.

Here is what the week already contains for a Dubai IGCSE student. Eight to ten subject entries. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies, which are mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever curriculum it is licensed to teach, calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit with KHDA advising at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Two or three afternoons of revision clinics, sport or music. Homework that arrives in clusters around assessment weeks rather than evenly. Friday and Saturday as the weekend. Count honestly and most Year 11 weeks contain two weekday evenings that are genuinely available.

That number is the whole planning problem. A family who books three weekly sessions into a two-evening week is not buying more teaching; they are buying three half-attended hours and a plan that collapses by the fourth week. A family who books one session into one protected evening, and uses a Friday morning for timed paper practice, generally gets through the term with the arrangement intact. The second family spends less and gets more, which is an unusual thing to be able to say about tutoring.

Before any of that, there is free provision to use. Most Dubai secondary schools run subject clinics, catch-up sessions or revision classes at no charge, and they are routinely under-attended because they are not advertised to parents. A student who attends two of those a week and takes one paid session is better supported than a student who takes three paid sessions and skips the clinics. Ask the head of year what exists before you ask anybody for a quote.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. On this page that matters for a practical reason rather than a philosophical one: the only way to place a session at 5:35pm on a Tuesday, move it to Wednesday during mock week, and shift it to an early afternoon through Ramadan is to take the car out of the arrangement entirely. Everything else on this page follows from that one constraint: the week decides the slot, the slot decides whether the arrangement survives, and an arrangement that survives the spring term is the only kind that changes a grade in June.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-garhoud.programmesIntro: Three things shape the week an IGCSE student lives in: the number of subject entries, the board those entries sit with, and what the school already provides free of charge. All three should be established before a tutor is chosen.

programmes.name: Year 9, before the entries are made
programmes.description: The year when subject choices and tier placements are decided. Workload is lower than Year 10 and the week has room, which makes it the cheapest year in which to fix an underlying gap. Algebraic fluency and written explanation quality are the two things that decide how heavy Years 10 and 11 feel.
programmes.countryNote: Garhoud families often start tutoring here specifically to protect the Extended-tier option in Mathematics and the sciences, since a school may place a student on Core on the basis of Year 9 attainment. One session a week in Year 9 frequently removes the need for three in Year 11.

programmes.name: Year 10, the content year
programmes.description: Content is delivered across eight to ten subjects and the first serious internal assessments appear. The week tightens noticeably. Tutoring here is best spent keeping pace in one subject rather than catching up in three, because content gaps opened in Year 10 are what make Year 11 revision impossible.
programmes.countryNote: This is the year when Dubai students most often add a second language or drop a subject, and when after-school clinics begin in earnest. Check the clinic timetable before booking anything, since the free session and the paid one frequently land on the same evening.

programmes.name: Year 11, the examination year
programmes.description: Mocks, entries, coursework deadlines and the series itself. The week is at its fullest and the margin for a collapsed arrangement is smallest. One protected weekday slot plus a weekend paper session is the shape that holds; anything more ambitious usually degrades within a month.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the June series, with November available as a resit route. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that using the correct zone timetable is essential, so ask the school which zone it sits in and work from that timetable.

programmes.name: The mandatory UAE subjects alongside
programmes.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies run in every Dubai private school regardless of curriculum. They occupy timetable periods, appear on reports, and carry their own homework. Any weekly plan that ignores them has under-counted the load by several hours.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes are strictly prohibited. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five required IGCSE subjects.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-garhoud.subjectsIntro: The list below is ordered by how much weekly time each subject tends to demand of a Dubai IGCSE student, because that is the figure a family needs when deciding which one gets the protected slot.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The heaviest weekly homework load of any subject and the grade that gates the most post-16 options. It is also the subject where a single protected weekly session shows the clearest return, because method-mark discipline is a trainable habit rather than a body of knowledge. If the week holds only one session, this is usually where it goes.

subjects.name: Separate sciences: Physics, Chemistry, Biology
subjects.description: Three subjects' worth of content and three sets of homework, which is why students taking all three feel the week most acutely. Supporting all three weekly is not possible inside a Dubai timetable; the realistic approach is one at a time, chosen by which is weakest at Extended tier.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.description: One or two awards covering all three sciences, common where a student takes nine or ten subjects. Lighter in weekly homework than the separate sciences but easy to under-prepare, because students revise from separate-science material and cover topics they will never be examined on.

subjects.name: English First Language
subjects.description: Moderate weekly load, heavily front-loaded by reading. The sessions that help most are short and frequent rather than long, because analytical writing improves through repeated short pieces marked quickly. Good candidate for a Friday morning slot alongside paper practice.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A separate qualification with its own mark scheme and, in some variants, a speaking component. Weekly demands are lower but the entry decision matters: students are sometimes entered here when First Language was achievable, which is worth raising with school in Year 10.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Low weekly homework, high marginal return from a short block near the examinations, because the marks sit in diagram accuracy and judgement rather than content volume. These are the subjects most sensibly left until a six-week push rather than supported all year.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: ICT carries a substantial practical coursework element that occupies weeks of the year in bursts; Computer Science is theory and pseudocode with steadier homework. Families frequently confuse the two, so confirm which is on the timetable before booking anybody.

subjects.name: Arabic and modern foreign languages
subjects.description: Steady weekly vocabulary and speaking preparation that is easy to let slide because it rarely has a deadline attached. Short frequent sessions work far better than a long one, and for the mandatory Arabic provision any support stays inside the school's prescribed curriculum.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and further options
subjects.description: Taken by stronger students, often as a tenth subject, and the first thing to drop when the week stops working. Before paying for support here, check whether the entry is actually required for post-16 plans or was added because a timetable slot existed.

sections.heading: What a radius search actually costs you
paragraphs: The near-me filter feels like it is saving time, and in this part of Dubai it is spending it. The question is not how far away a tutor lives but how much of your evening their journey consumes, and in a neighbourhood ringed by a Creek crossing, an airport road and a bridge, those are different numbers at different hours.

Work it through for a 60-minute session. A tutor travelling from Oud Metha at 5pm is committing perhaps twenty minutes each way, which they price into the hour whether or not they itemise it. From Mirdif it is closer to forty. From the Jumeirah side, more. The parent sees an hourly rate and assumes it reflects teaching; a meaningful portion of it reflects a car. That is the mechanism behind the travel premium of roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour that separates in-home rates from online ones in the published Dubai figures.

There is a second cost that nobody prices at all: the sessions that do not happen. A fixed arrival time is fragile on these roads, and a visiting tutor who is twenty minutes late on a 5pm booking has turned a sixty-minute lesson into a forty-minute one at full price. Over a term, three or four such evenings plus one or two outright cancellations is a material share of what you paid. An online slot does not have this failure mode, which is less exciting than a pedagogical argument and matters more.

The table puts the journeys side by side so a family can see what they would be buying. It is not an argument that in-home tutoring is bad; it is an argument that the near-me filter is the wrong one to optimise.

sections.heading: Designing the week: nine subjects, five weekdays
paragraphs: Write the week out before you book anything. Five weekday afternoons, each with a school commitment or not, each with a homework load, and Friday and Saturday as the weekend. The exercise takes fifteen minutes and it is the only reliable way to find out how much tutoring the week can hold, which is nearly always less than a family assumes and almost never more.

The pattern that emerges in most Dubai Year 11 households looks like this. Two afternoons are taken by school clinics, sport or music, finishing at 4:15pm or later, which rules them out for a session entirely. One afternoon carries the heaviest homework of the week, usually the day after Mathematics and a science fall together, which rules it out on grounds of capacity. That leaves two evenings. One of them is where the protected slot goes. The other should be left empty on purpose, as the shock absorber that lets the week survive a bad day.

The weekend is where the long work belongs. A full past paper sat to time takes ninety minutes plus marking, which is impossible on a school evening and straightforward on a Friday morning. Fortnightly is usually sufficient, and it produces the diagnostic evidence that makes the weekday session useful: without a timed paper, a tutor is working from impressions rather than from data.

Two practical notes. Put the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies homework on the chart as well, because it is real work that families routinely omit from their mental arithmetic. And revisit the chart after mocks, since the shape of the week changes once coursework deadlines pass.

sections.heading: Everything your school gives away before you pay anybody
paragraphs: This section exists because it is the one piece of advice in this market that costs a provider money to give. Dubai secondary schools run a substantial amount of free academic support and most parents do not know the detail of it, because it is communicated to students rather than to families and students do not always pass it on.

The usual inventory: subject clinics at lunchtime or after school, examination-technique sessions in the run-up to mocks, coursework catch-up sessions, past-paper packs and mark schemes available on the school's learning platform, and a head of year who can tell you exactly which topics your child's class is weakest on because they have the data. None of it is charged for. All of it is run by the people who will set and mark the mocks, which gives it an information advantage no external tutor can match.

What free provision cannot do is sit with one student for fifty minutes and work out why they lose four marks on every six-mark explanation question. Clinics are group settings, teachers are managing a class, and a student who is quiet in a clinic gets nothing from it. That specific diagnostic work is what a paid one-to-one hour is for, and the sensible order is therefore: use everything free, identify what remains, and buy only that.

A family who follows that order typically ends up buying one weekly session instead of three, and getting more from it, because the free provision is covering the content work while the paid hour does the diagnosis. The table lists what to ask for.

sections.heading: If the week only holds one session, which subject gets it?
paragraphs: Mathematics, most of the time, and for three reasons that are worth stating because they are not obvious. The grade gates more post-16 options than any other IGCSE result. The subject carries the heaviest weekly homework load, so help there relieves pressure across the whole week. And the thing being taught — method-mark discipline, showing working a marker can follow, not abandoning a multi-step question halfway — is a habit that transfers directly into the sciences.

The second candidate is whichever science is both weakest and entered at Extended or Higher tier, because Extended is where multi-step reasoning and unfamiliar-context questions live and where a generalist's help runs out. If your child is taking the separate sciences, pick one rather than rotating between three; rotation produces three shallow improvements and no grade change.

Some subjects are better left for a short block closer to the examinations. Business Studies and Economics reward six focused weeks on diagram accuracy and judgement far more than a year of weekly sessions. English First Language improves through frequent short marked pieces, which a Friday morning handles better than a Tuesday evening. ICT coursework needs help in the weeks the coursework is actually running and nothing at all outside them.

The decision should be revisited after every set of mocks, not held for the year. A family that moves the protected slot from Mathematics to Chemistry in January because the mock evidence pointed there is using the arrangement properly. A family still tutoring the subject they chose in September because that is what was booked is not.

sections.heading: Mock season, and the only hour that produces real evidence
paragraphs: Mocks are the most valuable thing in a Dubai IGCSE year and the most wasted. They produce marked scripts against real mark schemes, which is the only honest diagnostic a family gets before the series itself, and in most households the scripts come home, get looked at for ninety seconds, and go in a drawer.

The hour that changes outcomes is the one spent going through a mock script question by question, sorting every lost mark into one of three bins: content not known, method not shown, or question not read properly. Those three failures need completely different responses, and a student who does not know which one is costing them marks cannot fix it by revising harder. Most students discover that the largest bin is the second or third, which is good news, because both are faster to fix than missing content.

During the mock fortnight itself the sensible move is to relocate the weekly session rather than cancel it, ideally to the evening before the paper that matters most, and to use it for timing strategy rather than new content. Teaching anything new in that week is wasted; rehearsing the order in which a student will attempt the paper is not.

Afterwards, the plan should change. Mock evidence is the point at which the protected slot should move subject if the numbers say so, and the point at which a family can honestly decide whether to continue, stop, or change tutor. Any arrangement that does not have a review built in at this moment is not being run properly.

sections.heading: What this costs in Al Garhoud, by the month
paragraphs: Families budget monthly, so take the Dubai market monthly. Bestimate's rate work for Dubai estimates AED 240 to 600 a month for a weekly one-hour session at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 a month at the mid range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month for specialist examination-year support. Advertised packages tell the same story from the other direction: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, against AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Converted to hours, the published bands run as follows. Online generalist tutoring from roughly AED 33 to 52 an hour at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik. Qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate, and up to AED 500 for independent home tutors. Premium named tutors at AED 650, published by BartyED. All read in October 2026, each attributed to its publisher, and none of them ours.

The monthly view makes one thing obvious that the hourly view hides: the single protected weekly session this page recommends costs between AED 600 and AED 1,800 a month depending on band, which is a planned household line rather than an open-ended commitment. Three sessions a week at specialist rates is a different kind of number and is the pattern that leads families to stop abruptly in February having spent more than they intended and achieved less.

IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson, one per subject before any payment, against a written plan with a term total on it. We publish the market bands rather than a flat rate so that a Garhoud parent can screen any quote, including ours, against something checkable.
