sections.heading: Sleep, screens and the 7pm question
paragraphs: Parents ask whether a 7pm session is acceptable, and the honest answer is that it depends entirely on what time the student gets up. A Dubai school day that starts at 7:30am means leaving home around 6:45am, which means a student who needs eight hours is asleep before 10pm. A session that finishes at 8pm leaves time for food, a shower and some decompression. A session that finishes at 8:30pm, followed by homework, does not, and the cost appears two weeks later as concentration that has quietly disappeared.

The practical rule we would offer is that the last session of the evening should finish at least two hours before the student's actual bedtime, and that no session should be the fourth consecutive hour of academic work. A student who has done school, a clinic, homework and then a tutoring hour is not learning in the fourth hour; they are present in it. That is a waste of money as well as of the child.

On screens, the common worry is that an online lesson is one more hour in front of a device at the end of a screen-heavy day. It is a fair concern and the mitigation is straightforward: an online session should involve the student writing on paper and holding it up, working on a shared whiteboard with a stylus, and talking far more than reading. A tutor whose session is a slideshow is doing it badly, in any format.

The last consideration is the weekend. Friday and Saturday mornings are the best academic hours a Dubai student has all week and families frequently protect them for rest, which is reasonable. The compromise most households land on is one weekend morning used fortnightly for a timed paper and the other left genuinely free, which is both sustainable and more productive than four tired weekday evenings.

sections.heading: Siblings, shared school runs and two timetables
paragraphs: Garhoud households often have two or three children at different schools with different finishing times, and the tutoring arrangement has to survive that rather than ignore it. The common failure is booking two children into adjacent slots on the same evening because it suits an adult's logistics, and then discovering that one of them is arriving home in the middle of the other's session.

Two patterns work. The first is different evenings for different children, which costs nothing extra and removes the collision entirely. The second, for siblings in the same year group or the same subject, is genuinely sharing a session — not a group class, but two children with the same tutor working on the same topic, which some families negotiate at a reduced combined rate. That works when the two are close in attainment and badly when they are not, because the weaker child becomes an audience.

The school-run share is a separate variable. Families in this part of Dubai frequently split the run with neighbours, which means arrival times vary depending on whose turn it is. An online slot absorbs that; a visiting tutor's fixed arrival does not. If your arrival time changes week to week, say so when booking, because a session set to the earliest possible arrival will fail on the weeks when it is the latest.

One final piece of household arithmetic: if two children both need support, the budget rarely stretches to specialist rates for both. The sensible split is usually specialist help for the examination-year child and school clinics plus budget-band supervision for the younger one, revisited when the younger reaches Year 10.

sections.heading: Why we do not drive to Al Garhoud, and what that solves
paragraphs: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. We put that in the opening section of every UAE page rather than the footer, because the phrase a parent searches is often a home-tutor phrase and nobody should learn the format after paying for it.

The reason is the whole content of this page. A visiting tutor's slot is fixed by their route; your slot is fixed by your child's. Those two cannot be reconciled reliably across a thirty-week Dubai term on roads where arrival home varies by half an hour, and the thing that gets sacrificed is always the paid hour. An online slot can be 5:35pm, can move to Thursday during mocks, can shift to an early afternoon through Ramadan when schools shorten the day, and can run while a family is away for a long weekend.

The second reason is supply. Matching on syllabus code rather than postcode means a student entered for 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences gets somebody who has taught 0654 rather than somebody who has taught the separate sciences and will cover material that is not on the paper. Across eight to ten subjects and two boards, the chance that the right specialist for each lives within a sensible drive of Al Garhoud is small.

Where a tutor in the room is genuinely better — a young child who will not settle on screen, a household with no quiet corner, a student who needs apparatus handled — the Dubai market supplies it at the rates in the table above and a family should use it. We are simply not that provider, and would rather say so plainly than be vague about it.

process.title: Write the week out first
process.description: Before contacting anybody, chart five weekday afternoons with what is already in them, including mandatory-subject homework. Tell us which two evenings are genuinely free. That single piece of information does more for the success of the arrangement than the choice of tutor.

process.title: Exhaust the free provision
process.description: Ask the school in writing for the clinic timetable, the mock scripts with mark schemes, and the head of year's view on class weak topics. Come back with what is left over. We would rather place one well-aimed session than three that duplicate what your school already runs for nothing.

process.title: Free trial at the proposed time
process.description: One free trial lesson per subject before any payment, taken at the slot you are considering so you can see whether that hour works for your child in practice. Bring the most recent marked paper and the syllabus code from the entry form.

process.title: One protected slot, written down
process.description: The plan names the subject, the evening, the start time measured from arrival home, the weeks it will not run, and what evidence will show it worked. It also names the empty evening we are deliberately not using, because that is the week's shock absorber.

process.title: Review at the mocks
process.description: Mock scripts are the review point. We go through them sorting lost marks into content, method and question-reading, and the protected slot moves subject if the evidence says so. Every review is also a clean exit point with nothing outstanding.

whyPoints.title: We plan the week before selling the hour
whyPoints.description: The commonest reason tutoring fails in this neighbourhood is a slot placed on an evening that was never free. We ask for the week first and will tell you if the honest answer is one session rather than the three you were considering.

whyPoints.title: Free school support named explicitly
whyPoints.description: Clinics, mock scripts, mark schemes and the head of year's data are all free and routinely under-used. Pointing at them costs us revenue and improves outcomes, which is the correct trade and the reason that section is on the page at all.

whyPoints.title: Slots set from arrival, not dismissal
whyPoints.description: In a neighbourhood ringed by a Creek crossing and the airport road, dismissal time predicts very little. We set the session from when your child genuinely walks in, and because lessons are online the time can be changed permanently when a route changes.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the syllabus code
whyPoints.description: 0580 and 4MA1 are different papers; 0654 is not the separate sciences. We ask for the code from the entry form before matching, because past-paper work is most of the value of a session and the wrong board's papers train habits your child cannot use.

whyPoints.title: Monthly numbers, with sources
whyPoints.description: Market bands on this page are published Dubai figures, dated October 2026, with the publisher named and given monthly as well as hourly, because that is how a household budgets. We quote our own figure after a free trial, with a term total.

whyPoints.title: A plan that survives February
whyPoints.description: Resilience is the point. One protected slot plus a fortnightly weekend paper survives mocks, illness, Ramadan and a bad week, and a plan that survives is the only kind that can produce a result. Three ambitious sessions a week rarely reach half term.

faqs.question: How many tutoring sessions can a Dubai Year 11 week actually hold?
faqs.answer: Usually one weekday session and one weekend paper slot. Count what the week already contains: eight to ten subject entries, mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies lessons, two or three afternoons of clinics, sport or music, and homework that clusters around assessments. Most Year 11 weeks have two genuinely free weekday evenings, and one of those should be left empty as a shock absorber. Booking three sessions into that week does not buy more teaching; it buys three half-attended hours and an arrangement that collapses by the fourth week.

faqs.question: What should I ask my child's school for before paying a tutor?
faqs.answer: Four things, all free. The subject clinic timetable in writing, because it is communicated to students and often never reaches parents. The mock scripts with their mark schemes, which are the only honest diagnostic available before the real series. The examination-technique sessions that run before mocks. And the head of year's view on which topics your child's class is weakest on, since the school holds that data. A family who uses all four typically ends up buying one session rather than three.

faqs.question: Which evening is the best one to book an IGCSE session on?
faqs.answer: The one with nothing after school, which in most Dubai timetables is a Tuesday or a Thursday. Avoid the day after Mathematics and a science fall together, because that evening carries the heaviest homework of the week and a session on top of it produces a tired student doing a fourth consecutive hour of academic work. Avoid any day with a clinic or a fixture finishing at 4:15pm or later; move the session to another evening rather than pushing it to 6:30pm.

faqs.question: Is a 7pm tutoring session too late for a Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: It depends on wake-up time. A Dubai school day starting at 7:30am usually means leaving home around 6:45am, so a student needing eight hours is asleep before 10pm. A session ending at 8pm leaves room for food and decompression; one ending at 8:30pm followed by homework does not, and the cost shows up two weeks later as lost concentration. The working rule is that the session should finish at least two hours before actual bedtime and should never be the fourth consecutive hour of academic work.

faqs.question: What does one weekly IGCSE session cost per month in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Using published Dubai figures read in October 2026: roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget band, AED 600 to 1,200 at the qualified band, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support, per Bestimate's monthly estimates. Advertised packages run near AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are market numbers, not ours; we quote after a free trial lesson with a term total so the figure is plannable rather than open-ended.

faqs.question: Does it matter that no tutor actually lives in Al Garhoud?
faqs.answer: Less than the near-me search implies. Almost no secondary student in Al Garhoud attends school in it, so the neighbourhood is a place families return to rather than a catchment. What matters is whether the session fits the evening and whether the tutor has taught the exact syllabus code on your child's entry form. A tutor fifteen minutes away who teaches a different board's papers is a worse match than a specialist who is not in Dubai at all, because past-paper practice is most of the value.

faqs.question: How should we use the week after mock exams?
faqs.answer: On the scripts, not on new content. Go through every lost mark and sort it into one of three bins: content not known, method not shown, or question not read properly. Those need completely different responses, and most students find the largest bin is the second or third, which is good news because both are faster to fix than missing content. This is also the moment to move the protected slot to a different subject if the numbers point there, and the natural review point for whether to continue at all.

faqs.question: Can two siblings share one tutoring session?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it works only under one condition: they are close in attainment and working on the same topic. Where that holds, some families negotiate a reduced combined rate and both children benefit from the discussion. Where it does not, the weaker child becomes an audience and pays for the privilege. The safer arrangement for siblings in different year groups is different evenings, which costs nothing extra and removes the collision between one child arriving home and the other mid-session.

faqs.question: Our school run is shared and arrival time changes weekly. Does that break the plan?
faqs.answer: Not if you say so when booking. A session set to the earliest possible arrival will fail on the weeks when it is the latest, which is the commonest avoidable scheduling error in this neighbourhood. Tell us the range rather than the best case, and we will set the slot to the later end or arrange a time that tolerates the variation. Because lessons are online there is no tutor journey to coordinate, so a slot can also be moved permanently if the rota changes.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a centre in Al Qusais a reasonable alternative?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is dismissed too readily. A small group taught by somebody who knows the syllabus, at well below one-to-one rates, generally beats a cheap one-to-one hour with a generalist, because teaching quality matters more than ratio once the group is small. Al Qusais and Al Nahda have the highest concentration of centres near Al Garhoud. What a group cannot do is identify why one student loses four marks on every explanation question, which is exactly what a specialist one-to-one hour is for.

faqs.question: Should a Year 9 student have tutoring at all?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest year in which to fix something, because the week has room and because tier placements in Mathematics and the sciences are decided on Year 9 and Year 10 attainment. A single weekly session in Year 9 aimed at algebraic fluency or written explanation quality frequently removes the need for three sessions in Year 11. The thing to ask the school is when the tier decision is made and what attainment it rests on, then work backwards from that date rather than waiting for a report.

faqs.question: Which subjects are better left until closer to the exams?
faqs.answer: Business Studies and Economics, where the marks sit in diagram accuracy and justified judgement rather than content volume, and which respond better to six focused weeks than to a year of weekly sessions. ICT coursework needs help in the weeks the coursework actually runs and nothing outside them. English First Language improves through frequent short marked pieces, which suits a weekend slot. Mathematics and the sciences are the opposite: they are cumulative, so support there is worth more early than late.

faqs.question: What happens to the weekly slot during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: It moves, and the move should be agreed before the period begins. Dubai schools shorten the day and reduce after-school activities, which frees the early afternoon — the only time in a normal term when a student is both awake and unburdened. The alternative is a post-Iftar slot for older students who have adjusted their sleep. Both work online. The failure to avoid is a session that quietly stops for a month and is never rebuilt, costing six weeks of momentum in the half of the year when revision should be building.

faqs.question: Will an online session just be another hour staring at a screen?
faqs.answer: It should not be, and that is a fair thing to check during the free trial. A well-run session has the student writing on paper and holding it up, working on a shared whiteboard, and talking considerably more than reading. If the tutor's session is a slideshow with the student watching, that is bad teaching in any format and you should say so. Ask your child afterwards how much of the hour they spent writing or speaking; if the answer is under half, the format is not the problem.

faqs.question: How quickly will we know whether the arrangement is working?
faqs.answer: Fit shows in two or three sessions; effect shows at the next marked assessment. Those are different questions and both need asking. If your child cannot say what the last session was about, that is a fit problem and should be raised immediately rather than left until a report. If the fit is fine but the next marked paper has not moved, the review decides whether to change the target, the method or the tutor, and we will say which of the three we think it is.

faqs.question: Can we pause over the summer and pick up again in September?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for many families that is the right decision. The exception is a student entering Year 11 with a known content gap, where four or five sessions across the summer break is the cheapest repair available, because the week has no competing demands and a morning slot is possible. Pausing entirely is sensible for Year 9 and most of Year 10. What does not work is pausing in the spring term of Year 11, which is the period the whole year has been building towards.

intro.heading: Two towers, one canal, and four different exam timetables
paragraphs: Al Habtoor City is a compact place with an uncompact school map. The three residential towers sit on the Dubai Water Canal where Sheikh Zayed Road meets Al Safa, and the children in them attend schools in Al Safa, Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim, Mohammed Bin Rashid City and Al Barsha. That spread has a consequence that catches parents out: in one lift lobby you can find a Year 11 student on Cambridge IGCSE, another on Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and a third on the IB Middle Years Programme with no IGCSE at all. Three assessment systems, three timetables, three sets of past papers.

So a search for an IGCSE tutor near me in Al Habtoor City runs into a problem before distance even comes up. The nearest competent tutor to your front door may teach the wrong board. A Cambridge 0580 Extended mathematics candidate and a Pearson 4MA1 Higher tier candidate are covering overlapping content in different paper structures with different mark schemes, and the second half of that sentence is where the marks are. Hiring on proximity means hiring on the one attribute that does not predict whether the tutor knows your child's papers.

This page is therefore built as a comparison. It puts Al Habtoor City next to Al Safa, Business Bay, Jumeirah 1 and Al Wasl, looks at which schools each feeds, what time a child actually gets home, and what the local tutor supply looks like in each. Then it does the arithmetic that follows from the comparison, which is that the available pool of genuine subject specialists for any one board and code is small everywhere, and gets smaller the tighter the radius you draw. The neighbourhood you live in changes your commute. It does not change which Physics teacher can explain the 0625 Paper 4 mark scheme.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition as one-to-one lessons over live video. There is no in-home visiting service in Dubai or anywhere else in the Emirates; that service exists only in India. Said plainly so you can weigh it: if what you want is an adult physically present with a thirteen-year-old who will not sit down, this is not that product. If what you want is somebody who has taught Cambridge 0620 Chemistry through several June series and can mark your child's Paper 4 the way the examiner will, removing the drive from the equation is how you get them.

One factual note that shapes everything on the timing side. UAE candidates sit Cambridge IGCSE in the June and November series. The February and March series runs in India only, so any plan built around it belongs to a different country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Both boards publish live timetables, and Cambridge warns that every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Work from the copy your school's exams officer issues, never from a forum post.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-habtoor-.programmesIntro: Al Habtoor City families reach IGCSE by several routes, and the route determines what a tutor has to fix first. The four below cover nearly every case seen on this stretch of the canal.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Typically eight to ten subjects examined at the end of Year 11, graded 9 to 1 or A* to G depending on the syllabus. Many subjects offer Core and Extended routes with different papers and different grade ceilings. Assessment is almost entirely by written examination, with practical science assessed either by a timed practical paper or by the alternative-to-practical written paper.
programmes.countryNote: The dominant route in Dubai's British-curriculum schools, which hold the largest share of private-school enrolment in the emirate. Candidates sit June and November series only; the February and March window is an India-only offering. Each centre works to one of six Cambridge zone timetables, and the exams officer holds the correct one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The same qualification level under a different board, with its own codes such as 4MA1 for mathematics and 4PH1 for physics, and Foundation and Higher tiers in place of Core and Extended in several subjects. Some subjects allow modular entry across sessions rather than a single terminal sitting, which changes revision planning substantially.
programmes.countryNote: Used by a significant minority of Dubai schools, sometimes alongside Cambridge in the same building for different subjects. Pearson publishes International GCSE series in May/June and November; the November final timetable in the most recent cycle ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The alternative at the same ages, assessed against four lettered criteria per subject group with levels out of 8 rather than examined grades. No IGCSE is sat at all in most MYP schools. Students finish with the Personal Project and, in some schools, eAssessment in selected subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Several IB continuum schools within a short drive of Al Habtoor City run MYP to Year 11, which is why a neighbour's child may have no IGCSE exams at all. Families who transfer between MYP and IGCSE mid-stream are the most frequent mid-year tutoring request on this side of the canal.

programmes.name: What IGCSE leads into
programmes.description: Either A Level or the IB Diploma Programme, and the Year 11 grades gate both. A Level sciences and the IB Diploma's Higher Level sciences both assume secure algebra and secure practical understanding from the IGCSE years, which is why a grade 6 in a science with a weak Paper 4 is a different risk from a grade 6 with a weak Paper 2.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students from this area split roughly between A Level routes at the British schools in Al Safa and Al Sufouh and IB Diploma routes at the continuum schools in Jumeirah, Al Barsha and Mohammed Bin Rashid City. The choice is usually made in Year 11, mid-examination year, which is unhelpful timing and a reason to have the conversation in Year 10.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-habtoor-.subjectsIntro: Subject requests from Al Habtoor City and the streets immediately around it concentrate in mathematics and the three separate sciences, with English language and economics behind them. Each entry names the levels and the specific places marks go.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Number, algebra, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, vectors, statistics and probability. Extended and Higher candidates lose most marks in algebraic manipulation under time pressure and in multi-step problems where no method is written down, so a correct final answer still scores partially.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: A bridging course taken by students heading for A Level or Diploma mathematics, covering calculus, functions and series beyond the standard syllabus. The marks go in the calculus questions, where students who can differentiate still cannot decide what to differentiate.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Motion, forces, energy, thermal physics, waves, electricity, magnetism and atomic physics. Electricity is the reliable casualty: circuit reasoning requires holding three quantities in mind at once, and students who have only learned the formulae cannot do it when the circuit is unfamiliar.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: States of matter, atoms and bonding, stoichiometry, electrochemistry, energetics, rates, organic chemistry and analysis. Moles are where the grade is decided, because almost every calculation question in Paper 4 routes through them and a shaky mole concept caps the whole paper.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, transport, nutrition, respiration, coordination, reproduction, inheritance and ecology. The content is learnable and the marks still go missing, almost always on command terms and on questions requiring data interpretation rather than recall.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Science
subjects.description: Physics, chemistry and biology compressed into one or two award-bearing courses. Suits students who need science without three full syllabuses, but it narrows later options, so the decision deserves a conversation in Year 9 rather than a shrug in Year 10.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0500 and 0990 first language; 0510 and 0991 second language
subjects.description: Reading comprehension and directed writing, plus composition. The directed-writing task is the reliable mark loss: students who can write well still ignore the audience, form and purpose the question specifies, which is where most of the available credit sits.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Set texts examined by essay and extract question. Marks depend on quotation precision and on answering the question asked rather than the one revised for, which is why timed essay practice against the real mark scheme beats rereading the novel.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Basic economic problem, allocation of resources, microeconomic decision makers, government and the macroeconomy, and international trade. Diagram accuracy is the cheapest available mark and the most frequently lost, usually through unlabelled axes or a curve shifted the wrong way.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Business activity, people in business, marketing, operations and finance, assessed partly through case-study analysis. The failure pattern is describing a concept rather than applying it to the case material, which scores in the lowest band however accurate the description.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Data representation, hardware, networks, security, algorithms and programming. Students who code confidently often lose marks on the theory paper, particularly on binary, hexadecimal and network topics that feel too simple to revise.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools alongside the licensed curriculum. KHDA sets the weekly time and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, so a child's stream follows their registered category rather than their actual fluency level.

sections.heading: Al Habtoor City against Al Safa, Business Bay and Jumeirah 1
paragraphs: Put four neighbourhoods side by side and the comparison stops being sentimental. What differs between them is the school map and the clock. What does not differ is the number of people within a short drive who have taught Cambridge 0620 Chemistry Extended through multiple June series and can mark a Paper 4 the way the examiner does. That number is small in every one of these neighbourhoods, and it does not grow because you moved from Jumeirah 1 to Al Safa.

The clock differences are real though, and they matter for scheduling. A child at a school in Al Safa can be home by a quarter past three, so a four o'clock lesson is a four o'clock lesson. A child living in Al Habtoor City but attending a campus in Al Sufouh is unlikely to be settled before five, and on a Sunday with roadworks on Al Wasl Road, later. A Business Bay family with both parents in the towers often prefers seven in the evening because that is when an adult is home to see that the lesson is actually happening. None of those constraints are solved by a tutor who lives nearby; they are solved by a start time that does not depend on traffic.

The school map differences are larger and less obvious. Jumeirah 1 sends a meaningful share of its children to an IB continuum school where no IGCSE is sat at all. Al Safa sends most of its to British-curriculum schools running Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE. Mohammed Bin Rashid City, five minutes east, sends to schools that do the same but with a different mix of boards by subject. A parent asking a neighbour for a tutor recommendation across that boundary is asking somebody whose child is sitting a different qualification.

Which is the whole argument of this page in one line: the comparison tells you about commutes, not about competence. Draw a tighter radius and you shrink the pool without improving it. Remove the radius and match on the syllabus code instead, and the pool becomes everybody who can teach that code at that tier in a compatible time zone.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: establish the board before you buy anything
paragraphs: This is the step most parents skip and the one that most often wastes the first month. Ask your child which exam board they sit and a surprising number cannot say. Ask which syllabus code and almost none can. The information is easy to get: it is on the statement of entry the school issues, and the subject teacher or exams officer will confirm it in a sentence. Get it before you hire anybody, because a tutor teaching the wrong board is teaching the wrong paper structure to the right content.

The practical differences are not cosmetic. Cambridge splits many subjects into Core and Extended with different papers and different grade ceilings; Pearson more often uses Foundation and Higher tiers, and in some subjects allows modular entry across sessions rather than one terminal sitting. Cambridge mathematics is 0580 with Core and Extended variants; Pearson's is 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher. Physics is 0625 against 4PH1, chemistry 0620 against 4CH1, biology 0610 against 4BI1. Practical science is handled differently too, which is covered further down this page.

The timing differs as well. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series. In the most recent cycle Pearson's November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those dates are quoted because they are past and therefore checkable; for a future series, work from the live timetable the board publishes.

A warning on one specific error, because it has consequences. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates do not sit it. A revision plan built around a February exam window is a plan for the wrong country, and a provider that offers one has not understood where you live.

sections.heading: Core and Extended, and the grade ceiling nobody mentions at parents' evening
paragraphs: In several Cambridge subjects a student is entered for either the Core papers or the Extended papers, and the two are not the same examination with different difficulty. They carry different grade ranges. A Core entry has a ceiling, and that ceiling can sit below what a sixth-form or Diploma course will later ask for. Pearson's Foundation and Higher tiers in mathematics work the same way. The decision is usually made by the school in Year 10 on the basis of Year 9 attainment, and it is frequently communicated to parents in a sentence that does not mention the ceiling at all.

The honest version of the conversation has three parts. First, what is the ceiling on the route my child is entered for, in grade terms. Second, what grade does the next stage need, which for A Level and Diploma Higher Level sciences and mathematics is usually well above a pass. Third, if the two numbers do not meet, what would have to change for a tier move to be realistic, and by when does that decision have to be made. Schools answer all three readily when asked directly. They rarely volunteer them.

Tutoring has a specific role here and it is a narrow one. Moving a student from Core to Extended, or Foundation to Higher, is not a matter of extra practice. It requires the content only the higher route covers, plus the fluency to handle it under time. That is a Year 10 project, not a Year 11 one, and anybody promising it in the term before the papers is misrepresenting the arithmetic. Where tutoring genuinely earns its fee is in making the decision evidence-based: a timed higher-tier paper, honestly marked, tells you more in two hours than a term of opinions.

There is a related trap in science. A student can be entered for Extended and still be working at Core level in one topic, usually electricity in physics or moles in chemistry. The entry says Extended; the performance says otherwise. That shows up as a grade two or three below the rest of the paper profile, and it is the single most fixable thing in a Year 11 science. Finding it needs a marked Paper 4, not a conversation.

sections.heading: Why the answer comes out the same on both sides of the canal
paragraphs: Having run the comparison, it is worth stating the conclusion rather than implying it. Al Habtoor City, Al Safa, Business Bay, Jumeirah 1 and Al Wasl differ in school destinations and in what time a child gets home. They do not differ in the thing you are buying. A chemistry teacher who knows the 0620 Paper 4 mark scheme is equally useful to a student in a tower on the canal and a student in a villa in Al Safa, and equally unavailable to both if the search radius is drawn at two kilometres.

Think about the supply side for a moment, because it explains the whole market. The people who can teach a named IGCSE syllabus well are mostly current or former subject teachers. Those people work in schools, which means they are available in the late afternoon and evening, which means a travelling tutor can serve perhaps two or three students a day with driving between them. An online tutor can serve five or six in the same window. That capacity difference is why online rates in Dubai sit lower than in-home rates for equivalent qualifications, and it is also why the specialist you actually want is far more likely to be teaching over video than circling for parking.

The second reason the answer converges is scheduling risk. An in-home arrangement has a failure mode that a video lesson does not: the tutor is late, or does not come, or arrives from the previous student with twenty minutes lost. Over a term that is not an occasional nuisance, it is a predictable percentage of what you paid for. Families on Palm Jumeirah experience this most acutely because of the single access road, but anybody on this stretch of Sheikh Zayed Road recognises the pattern.

None of which means in-home tuition is wrong for everybody. For a younger child who needs an adult physically present, it is the better buy and it is sold at AED 180 to 500 an hour in this market according to published Dubai rate comparisons. For a Year 10 or Year 11 student working through past papers on a shared screen, the comparison favours online on pool, on price and on reliability at the same time, which is unusual and worth noticing.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs here, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Most pages in this market start at the premium end, which flatters the seller. Start at the other end instead. The cheapest real option is the school's own after-school support, which is already inside the fees you pay and which KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 would not rise in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year under an economic incentives package reported at AED 1.5 billion. Ask what subject clinics run and when before buying anything. The second cheapest is a group class, which works for content revision in a subject where the student's problem is coverage rather than diagnosis.

Above that sit the paid one-to-one options, and here are the published Dubai figures read in October 2026. Budget online tutors, generally university students, advertise from AED 33 to 150 an hour: Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Qualified subject tutors working online run AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits with travel included are quoted at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's Dubai table at AED 180 to 350 and home-tutor agencies at AED 200 to 500. IB and IGCSE specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650.

The monthly view is the one that predicts whether an arrangement survives. Bestimate estimates weekly one-hour tutoring at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Advertised packages in this market include roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. None of those are IB Gram prices; our fee is quoted after the free trial lesson, with the trial carrying no card requirement and no obligation.

What a parent can actually verify is the useful test here. Three of the six strongest-ranking Dubai tutoring pages publish no price at all, and two of the ones that do quote in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays in. A provider who will state a rate in AED, say what it includes, and name the cancellation terms is giving you something checkable. A provider whose own FAQ asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer is telling you something too.

sections.heading: Practical science, and the private-candidate route nobody explains
paragraphs: Parents ask a version of this constantly: if lessons are online, how does my child do the practical work. The answer separates two different things. Teaching practical skills and sitting a practical assessment are not the same activity, and only one of them happens in a school laboratory.

Cambridge assesses practical science either through a timed practical examination taken at the centre or through the alternative-to-practical written paper, depending on the syllabus and the centre's arrangements. The alternative-to-practical paper is written, and it tests exactly the things that can be taught over a shared screen: reading a measuring instrument correctly, identifying the dependent and independent variables, spotting the uncontrolled one, criticising a method, drawing a graph to the mark scheme's standard, and calculating a value from somebody else's data. Those are examinable skills and they are where candidates lose a predictable band of marks every series.

The laboratory work itself belongs to the school and should be done there. A tutor's useful contribution is before and after: making sure the student understands the method going in, and making sure they can analyse what came out. Students who can perform an experiment but cannot process the results score badly on both the practical and the alternative-to-practical routes, because both reward analysis over dexterity.

The private-candidate question comes up for families who have moved mid-year or whose school does not offer a subject. Candidates can be entered through an approved examination centre rather than their own school, and several centres in Dubai accept private candidates. The practical implications are real: entry deadlines sit months before the papers, fees are paid to the centre, and for some science syllabuses a centre may only offer the alternative-to-practical route. That is a conversation with a centre and with the board, not with a tutor, and the boards' own pages are the place to check what each syllabus allows.

sections.heading: The five-subject equivalency rule, and the ranking page that gets it wrong
paragraphs: Families planning on a UAE university, or on anything that requires a UAE-attested school certificate, eventually meet Ministry of Education equivalency. It is worth understanding in Year 10 rather than in the week results arrive, because it constrains subject choice.

For the British track the requirement, as reported when the UAE clarified equivalency for secondary certificates, is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. The detail that changes subject planning is that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. So a student taking five subjects of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education does not have five that count.

This is also a point where accuracy is a competitive matter rather than a pedantic one. One provider ranking for Dubai IGCSE searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The sourced figure is five, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education. If a page gets that wrong, a parent planning around it makes a worse decision than they would have with no page at all.

Two cautions. IB Gram does not perform, process or guarantee equivalency or attestation; it is a Ministry of Education process and the Ministry and the emirate attestation authority are the only places to confirm current requirements. And no IB points threshold for equivalency appears on this page, because the figure circulating for it could not be read on an official Ministry source, and publishing an unverified threshold about a regulatory process is exactly the error worth not making. For the American track the sourced requirements are an IELTS academic score of 5, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, plus at least 450 in SAT Mathematics.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and the one request that tests a tutor
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE sits inside a permit system, and knowing how it works protects you. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The application runs through the MoHRE service called Issuance of a New Work Permit, Private Tutor Licensing, via the MoHRE app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Two things follow. Anyone offering private lessons in the UAE without that permit is outside the rules, and the government portal states that such individuals are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published anywhere official, so a specific amount quoted at you is not a fact. Separately, a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is issued to a named entity at a named address. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE centre or office, and describes itself using no regulator's name. Any provider calling itself regulator-approved should be asked for a permit number.

On academic honesty the line is the same in IGCSE as it is in the Diploma, even though there is less coursework. A tutor teaches, marks, explains and gives feedback on the student's own work. A tutor does not write the coursework, produce the assignment or supply answers to be submitted. One site ranking for these searches sells completed internal assessments to Diploma students; that is a different transaction with consequences that land on the student, and it is worth knowing it exists in this market so you can recognise it.

Which brings the page to its most useful single suggestion. Before paying anyone, send them one page of your child's actual marked work and ask them to tell you where the marks went and why. A tutor who knows the board and the tier will answer with specifics: this is a method mark lost for no working, this is a command-term miss, this answer is right and unmarkable because the unit is missing. A tutor who does not will answer with encouragement. That one request costs nothing and tells you nearly everything, in any neighbourhood on either side of the canal.

process.title: Confirm the board, the code and the tier
process.description: Before anything else, get the syllabus code and route from the statement of entry or the subject teacher. Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson 4MA1 Higher are not interchangeable, and a tutor matched without this works from the wrong past papers. It takes one email to the school and it saves the first month.

process.title: Send one page of marked work
process.description: A recent marked paper with the teacher's comments still on it is the most informative thing you can provide. It shows where marks are actually going, which is rarely where the student believes, and it lets a tutor diagnose in one session rather than three.

process.title: Match on the syllabus, not the map
process.description: A tutor is proposed who has taught that specific code at that tier, with the number of series they have taught it through stated. Where no specialist is free for that exact code, you are told so and told when one is expected, rather than being offered a neighbouring subject.

process.title: Free trial lesson, terms stated upfront
process.description: One lesson at no cost, no card details taken, no obligation to continue. It is a teaching session rather than a sales call, and the thing to judge is whether the tutor can read your child's marked work accurately and say something you did not already know.

process.title: A plan with an end date and a dropped-topics list
process.description: After the trial, the tutor writes out the session sequence against the school's own dates: what is covered when, what the student practises alone, and which topics are deliberately being left. The dropped list is part of an honest plan, particularly inside the final term.

process.title: Mid-point review that can end the arrangement
process.description: Halfway through a block there is a direct conversation about whether this is working, including the version where the right answer is a different tutor, a different subject or no tutoring at all. A review that can only conclude in favour of continuing is not a review.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code, not by postcode
whyPoints.description: The tutor is chosen because they have taught Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4MA1 at the right tier, not because they can reach the canal by half past four. In a city where neighbouring children sit different boards for the same subject, that distinction is the one that decides whether the hour is useful.

whyPoints.title: Rates in AED with a named source
whyPoints.description: Every figure on this page is attributed to the provider that published it and dated to when it was read. Three of the strongest-ranking Dubai pages publish no price and two quote in US dollars, so a sourced AED band is something you can actually check against the market.

whyPoints.title: A start time that does not depend on Al Wasl Road
whyPoints.description: A video lesson begins when it is scheduled. No portion of what you pay for is lost to the drive from Al Barsha, nothing is shortened because the previous student overran, and the arrangement does not break the week a road closes. Over a Year 11 that reliability is a measurable share of the value.

whyPoints.title: The exam calendar stated correctly for the UAE
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit Cambridge in June and November; the February and March series is an India-only offering and does not appear in any plan here. Pearson dates are quoted from the board's own timetable with the series named, and future series are named by month so the page does not go stale.

whyPoints.title: The work stays the student's own
whyPoints.description: Marking, explanation and feedback on work the student has done. Nothing written, completed or supplied for submission. One site ranking in this market sells finished assessed work, and knowing that it exists is part of being able to avoid it.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits said out loud
whyPoints.description: If no tutor is free for a specific code at a specific tier, that is stated along with when one is expected, rather than filled with a near-enough match. The commonest instance is a separate science at Extended level in the weeks before a June series.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tutor living in Al Habtoor City who could visit?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. All UAE lessons run one-to-one over live video, and home visits are offered only in India rather than anywhere in the Emirates. Al Habtoor City is three residential towers on the canal with no school inside the development, so the local pool of people who have taught your child's specific syllabus code at the right tier is very small. Matching over video replaces that radius with a different question: who has taught Cambridge 0620 Extended or Pearson 4CH1 through several series and can mark a paper the way the examiner will.

faqs.question: How do I check which board and code my child is entered for near Al Safa?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer, or read the statement of entry the school issues, which lists the board and the syllabus code for every subject. Do this before hiring anyone. It is common in Dubai for one school to use Cambridge for some subjects and Pearson Edexcel for others, so a single answer for the whole timetable may be wrong. The code matters more than the board name: Cambridge mathematics is 0580 with Core and Extended variants, Pearson's is 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher tiers, and the papers are structured differently.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether we live in Al Habtoor City or Al Safa when choosing a tutor?
faqs.answer: It changes your commute and your realistic start time, and almost nothing else. A child at a school in Al Safa can be home by a quarter past three, so a four o'clock lesson is genuinely four o'clock. A child in Al Habtoor City travelling back from Al Barsha is unlikely to be settled before five. What the neighbourhood does not change is how many people within reach have taught your child's syllabus code at the right tier, which is a small number everywhere and gets smaller the tighter the radius you draw.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between Cambridge Core and Extended papers?
faqs.answer: They are different examinations with different grade ranges rather than the same paper at two difficulties. A Core entry carries a grade ceiling, and that ceiling may sit below what an A Level or IB Diploma Higher Level course later requires. Pearson's Foundation and Higher tiers in mathematics work the same way. Schools usually set the route in Year 10 from Year 9 attainment. The three questions worth asking are what the ceiling is in grade terms, what the next stage needs, and by when a tier move would have to be decided.

faqs.question: Which series can a Dubai IGCSE candidate actually sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, plus Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered in India only, so any plan built around a February exam window belongs to another country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable, so use the copy the exams officer issues.

faqs.question: My child is entered for Extended but keeps scoring like a Core candidate. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Usually one topic is dragging the whole profile. In physics it is almost always electricity, where circuit reasoning requires holding several quantities in mind at once rather than recalling a formula. In chemistry it is moles, because most Paper 4 calculation questions route through them and a shaky mole concept caps the paper regardless of how well the rest is known. This pattern is the most fixable thing in a Year 11 science, and finding it needs a marked Paper 4 rather than a conversation about confidence.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE tutor cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Starting at the cheapest end: the school's own subject clinics are already inside the fees, which KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 would not rise in Dubai for 2026-27. Published paid rates read in October 2026 run from AED 33 to 150 an hour for budget online tutors, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65; AED 150 to 300 for qualified online subject tutors, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits; and AED 500 to 650 at the premium end, BartyED at AED 650. Those are market figures, not ours.

faqs.question: Why would an online tutor cost less than the same person coming to the villa?
faqs.answer: Because capacity differs. A travelling tutor crossing Dubai in the late afternoon can teach perhaps two or three students in the window when students are available; working over video the same person can teach five or six. That capacity gap is why Dubai online rates for equivalent qualifications sit below in-home rates, which published comparisons put at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online. The remainder of the in-home premium is travel time and the scheduling risk that comes with it, neither of which is teaching.

faqs.question: If lessons are online, how does my child handle the science practicals?
faqs.answer: The laboratory work belongs to the school and should happen there. What a tutor can teach over a shared screen is the examinable part: reading instruments, identifying variables, spotting the uncontrolled one, criticising a method, plotting a graph to the mark scheme's standard, and calculating from supplied data. Cambridge assesses practical science either by a timed practical paper at the centre or by the alternative-to-practical written paper, and the second is entirely written. Candidates lose a predictable band of marks on analysis rather than on technique, every series.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE require for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. The UAE's clarification of equivalency for secondary certificates requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus either one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One provider ranking for Dubai IGCSE searches states six subjects, which is wrong and would distort a family's subject planning. Confirm current requirements with the Ministry of Education; IB Gram does not process or guarantee equivalency.

faqs.question: Where is the line on IGCSE coursework help for a Year 11 student here?
faqs.answer: Yes, within the same boundary that applies to any assessed work. A tutor may explain what the task is asking, teach the skills it requires, mark a draft the student has written and explain where credit is being lost against the criteria. A tutor must not write the coursework, complete the assignment or supply material for submission. The work has to be the student's own, and the consequence of a breach falls on the student rather than the tutor. That limit is worth confirming with any provider before you pay them.

faqs.question: Does a tutor teaching an Al Habtoor City student need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, if they are providing private lessons in the UAE. The private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is free for two years. Eligible applicants include school and government employees, private-sector staff, unemployed residents, university students, and students aged 15 to 18. The UAE government portal states that tutoring without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, but publishes no amounts, so any figure quoted at you is unverified.

faqs.question: What should I ask a prospective IGCSE tutor before paying anything?
faqs.answer: Two questions and one request. Ask which syllabus code and tier they have taught, and through how many series. Ask what the grade ceiling is on your child's current route. Then send one page of your child's marked work and ask where the marks went. A specialist answers with specifics: a method mark lost for no working, a command term missed, a correct answer made unmarkable by a missing unit. A generalist answers with encouragement. That request costs nothing and is the most informative thing you can do.

faqs.question: Should an Al Habtoor City family start IGCSE support in Year 10 instead?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is cheaper per mark gained, because the fixes available then are structural. Algebraic fluency, mole arithmetic and command-term discipline underpin every later paper, and there is time to embed them rather than patch them. Year 10 is also when the Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher decision is live, and an honestly marked higher-tier paper at that point is worth more than a term of discussion about readiness. By the final term of Year 11 the work is necessarily triage: timed papers, mark-scheme discipline and deciding what to abandon.

faqs.question: Could an Al Habtoor City student sit IGCSE papers as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: In many subjects, yes, through an approved examination centre rather than their own school, and several Dubai centres accept private candidates. The practicalities matter: entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, fees are paid to the centre, and for some science syllabuses a centre may offer only the alternative-to-practical route rather than the timed practical. That changes which papers your child sits and how they should prepare. It is a conversation with the centre and with the board's own guidance rather than with a tutor.

faqs.question: What if my child is on MYP rather than IGCSE at a school near Jumeirah 1?
faqs.answer: Then the tutoring question is a different one, and hiring an IGCSE tutor would be a mismatch. The Middle Years Programme assesses against four lettered criteria per subject group with levels out of 8 rather than examined grades, and most MYP schools sit no IGCSE at all. This happens often near Jumeirah 1, where an IB continuum school sits among British-curriculum neighbours. Confirm which system your child is actually in before anything else, because a recommendation from a neighbour may be for a different qualification entirely.

With those answers in hand, the neighbourhood question answers itself: Al Habtoor City, Al Safa, Business Bay and Jumeirah 1 differ in commute and in school destination, not in who can teach Cambridge 0580 Extended. Bring the codes and one page of marked work to a free trial lesson, with no card details taken, and a tutor who has taught that code will tell you inside an hour whether the problem is content, technique or tier.

intro.heading: One search phrase, six different businesses
paragraphs: Type "IGCSE tutor near me in Al Jaddaf" and the results look homogeneous. They are not. Behind the similar wording sit at least six distinct business models: a managed agency that places and replaces tutors, an international marketplace that lists them and takes a commission, an independent freelance tutor working alone, a tuition centre running group classes from premises, an online platform with no geography, and the school's own paid support sessions. Each prices differently, carries a different permit position, and fails in a different way when something goes wrong.

Comparing brands is unhelpful and, in this market, frequently misleading. Comparing models is useful, because the model determines what you can expect. An agency can replace a tutor and charges for that capability. A marketplace cannot, and is cheaper for the same reason. A freelance tutor is the cheapest one-to-one option and carries all the single-point-of-failure risk. A centre group class is cheaper per hour than anything one-to-one and buys you less attention per student. None of these is wrong; they are different purchases.

The permit question cuts across all six and is the one most families never ask. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Because the permit is free, no model can cite permit cost as a reason for a higher rate.

IB Gram sits in the online one-to-one category and does not pretend otherwise. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Al Jaddaf or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we operate only in India. That is a limit worth stating on a page whose whole purpose is model comparison, because a reader deserves to know which column we occupy before reading our account of the others.

Al Jaddaf makes the comparison concrete because the district is compact and its school options are not. Swiss International Scientific School Dubai sits inside Al Jaddaf. Everything else Al Jaddaf families use is elsewhere: Dubai Festival City across the Creek, Sobha Hartland and Nad Al Sheba south along Al Khail Road. A freelance tutor advertising nearby may be minutes away and still be the wrong board. A centre group class may be convenient and be taught to the other specification in the room.

What follows compares the six models on the things that differ, sets out what happens when no specialist covers a subject, lays out the permit categories so a parent can actually ask the right question, names the regulator in each emirate, and gives the honest version of how to start. Every AED figure belongs to the provider that published it and was read in October 2026.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Assessed by written papers at the end of a two-year course, entered at Core or Extended in many subjects, with Core carrying a grade ceiling. Syllabus codes identify the content: Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, First Language English 0500 or 0990, Additional Mathematics 0606.
programmes.countryNote: Relevant to a model comparison: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable each, and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. A centre group class drawn from several schools may contain candidates in different zones, which is one reason a group timetable cannot substitute for the school's own issued one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Tiered Foundation and Higher in mathematics, with Specification A coded 4MA1 and sciences coded 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. Science practical skills are assessed inside the written papers rather than through a separate practical examination, so apparatus and variable-control questions are a written skill.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official PDF rather than a restated date is what we plan from.

programmes.name: Households with two boards
programmes.description: Al Jaddaf households frequently have children at two schools on two boards, because the district feeds several clusters. One child may sit Cambridge Extended and another Pearson Higher, which means two specifications, two tier systems and two sets of past papers in one home.
programmes.countryNote: This is where a group class or a single generalist tutor breaks down fastest, and where parents most often discover they have bought one solution for two problems. Our scheduling answer is two separate one-to-one sessions placed back to back on one evening, which keeps the rest of the week clear and keeps a parent supervising once rather than four times.

programmes.name: After IGCSE
programmes.description: Al Jaddaf's feeder schools split after Year 11 into Cambridge or Pearson A Level or the IB Diploma. Tier ceilings matter, because A Level Mathematics, Physics and Economics and IB Higher Level sciences assume the Extended or Higher tier content.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. A ranking competitor states six, which does not match the sourced rule. Verify your own case with the Ministry; IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees equivalency.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-jaddaf.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects Al Jaddaf families ask for most, with a note on which provider model tends to serve each one adequately.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The most requested subject. At Core or Foundation a group class or a budget tutor can genuinely work. At Extended or Higher the gap is usually unclaimed method marks, which needs somebody who has read the published scheme, and that is a one-to-one job.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Mechanics, electricity, waves and atomic physics. Pearson candidates need apparatus and variable questions drilled on paper. A group class mixing boards is a poor fit here, because the practical-skills route differs between the two specifications.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, bonding, electrochemistry and organic chemistry. Moles arithmetic decides the grade, and it is a skill that benefits from immediate correction, which is what one-to-one provides and a group of eight cannot.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Wide content, precise marking on named structures and processes. The subject where a budget tutor or a well-run group class most often suffices, because the work is recall discipline rather than technique correction.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Science (0653 / 0654)
subjects.description: Two or three sciences in a smaller award. Broad per paper and shallow per topic, so revision must rotate. Group classes serve this reasonably when all students share the board and the tier, which is less common than centres imply.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Reading response, directed writing and composition. Marks move when evidence is selected for an argument rather than summarised. Written feedback on a student's own work is the mechanism, so this is poorly served by group delivery.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0993)
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and an optional speaking endorsement. Speaking practice benefits from one-to-one time; the reading and listening papers respond well to structured independent work at a lower cost.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (0455 / 0450)
subjects.description: Data response and case-study application decide the marks. A generic answer earns knowledge credit and stops. Anchoring to the named firm or dataset in the stem is teachable quickly and transfers between the two subjects.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Data representation, networks, hardware and software, and algorithm design with pseudocode. A minority subject, so local coverage in any one district is thin and this is where a geography-bounded model fails first.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Calculus, binomial expansion and advanced trigonometry alongside 0580. The clearest example of a subject where the available model matters more than the price: a freelance tutor nearby who has not taught it is not a substitute for one who has.

sections.heading: Six provider models, compared on what differs
paragraphs: This is the table that should exist on every page in this market and exists on none of them. Competitors compare themselves against an unnamed category of other platforms, which tells a reader nothing. A model-level comparison tells you what you can reasonably expect from each kind of business and where each one breaks, and it lets you price the difference instead of guessing at it.

The headline price differences are real and explainable. A tuition centre group class is cheapest per hour because the cost is divided across a room. A freelance independent tutor is the cheapest one-to-one option because there is no organisation behind the rate, and that is also the whole of the risk: no replacement, no cover for illness, no second opinion. A managed agency charges more because replacement capability costs money to maintain. An international marketplace is cheaper than an agency and typically quotes in a currency other than dirhams, which is itself a signal about who the page was written for.

The permit position differs by model too, and it is the question a parent should ask of whichever one they choose. An individual providing private tutoring needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, applied for through MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service. A tuition operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

One model is worth treating separately. The school's own paid support sessions sit inside the school's governance, which is an advantage, but a teacher taking paid private work with students enrolled at their own school is a different matter. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from exactly that, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Ask the school which arrangement a support session falls under before assuming it is the same thing.

sections.heading: When a group class is the right purchase, and when it is not
paragraphs: A tuition centre group class is the cheapest format per hour in this market, because the cost of a teacher is divided across a room. That is a genuine saving and it is the right purchase in specific circumstances, which is worth saying on a page published by a one-to-one provider. Where a student needs exposure to more worked examples, structured time to practise, and the discipline of a fixed appointment, a well-run group class delivers that at a fraction of one-to-one cost.

It stops working when the room is mixed. A class advertised as IGCSE Mathematics may contain Cambridge Core candidates, Cambridge Extended candidates, Pearson Foundation and Pearson Higher candidates at once, because centres draw from several schools. The content overlaps enough to make the class deliverable and differs enough to make it imprecise, and the student who most needed correction gets the least, since a teacher managing eight students cannot interrupt one of them mid-error.

For an Al Jaddaf family there is also a practical scheduling problem. Tuition centres cluster in commercial districts, and a class time fixed at 17:00 suits a student who finished school nearby and not one who arrives home from Nad Al Sheba at 17:15. Travel to a centre adds the journey back into an evening that online delivery had already removed it from, which is a cost in time rather than money and is frequently the reason a centre arrangement lapses by the middle of term.

The honest rule of thumb. If the problem is practice volume and a student who works better with others around, a group class is the better value. If the problem is an error pattern that needs catching as it happens, immediate correction is the entire value and a room of eight cannot provide it. Diagnose first, then choose the format, rather than choosing the format and hoping it fits the problem.

sections.heading: What happens when nobody covers your subject
paragraphs: No competitor page in the research behind this site discloses a coverage limit. Several route UAE parents to a non-UAE phone number without saying where delivery actually happens. We take the opposite approach, because a disclosed limit is more useful than an implied capability, and because the subjects where coverage is thin are predictable rather than random.

Thin coverage concentrates in three places. Minority subjects first: Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478, and Pearson Specification B rather than Specification A. Second, particular tier and board combinations at the top end, where a specialist has to have taught that exact paper through to a series. Third, time: the eight to twelve weeks before a June or November series, when every school's cohort reaches the same point simultaneously and demand across Dubai peaks in the same fortnight.

Our rule is to say so rather than to place somebody adjacent. If no tutor with the right specification has a slot in your window, you get told that, given a realistic wait, and offered the nearest honest alternative: a different time slot, a shorter weekly commitment with a specialist whose availability is limited, or paper-technique and command-term work while the subject slot remains pending. What you do not get is a general tutor presented as a specification match, which is the failure that shows up at mock time with no runway left.

There is one more disclosure worth making plainly. Where a UAE-based tutor is unavailable for a niche subject, delivery may come from a specialist based outside the UAE, online and on Gulf Standard Time. That is stated rather than concealed, because concealing it behind a local-looking listing is precisely the trust failure we were built to avoid. sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is the question with the clearest answer and the one least often asked. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. The eligible categories are deliberately broad, which is why a parent should ask which category applies rather than whether a permit exists in the abstract.

Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, listed with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. That is the official channel and the one to point any tutor towards.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published. A figure circulating in this market could not be verified against any official source, and the ministry was reported as not having specified the amounts or detailed the penalties, so no amount appears here and any amount quoted to you should be treated as unverified.

One important distinction. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is not an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That permit belongs to institutes with premises. IB Gram does not hold one and does not need one, because we have no UAE premises, no UAE office and no UAE branch, and we say so rather than implying otherwise.
