sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why it is not your tutor
paragraphs: A parent searching near me in Al Jaddaf is in Dubai, so the regulator is KHDA. But families move between emirates, and households with children at schools in two emirates are common, so the whole map is worth having. Five bodies cover private schools across the seven emirates, and only one of them is named by most pages in this market. ADEK, which regulates Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, is named by none of the competitors in the research behind this site.

What each body does is more than inspection. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval sits with the emirate regulator rather than federally. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The federal baseline is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

The point for a tutoring decision is a negative one, and it is important. None of these bodies approves, accredits or licenses tutors or tutoring platforms. A KHDA inspection rating judges a school. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson. Any provider implying regulator endorsement is making a claim worth checking before money moves.

The Dubai context is worth one paragraph because it explains the market. KHDA reported 227 private schools serving 387,441 students in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with UK curricula at thirty-seven per cent of enrolment, Indian at twenty-six, US at fourteen and the International Baccalaureate at seven. Seven new private schools join for the 2026-27 intake creating 16,846 places, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that fees would not rise for that year under Dubai's second economic incentives package.

sections.heading: Materials, coursework and the lines a legitimate provider holds
paragraphs: Two of the six models in this market routinely cross lines that a parent should know about, and both are visible before you pay. The first is materials. Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are copyright works. They should be referenced and linked from the board's own site, not reproduced or supplied as downloads. A provider advertising a library of papers is offering something a legitimate operation would not, and it is reasonable to wonder what else they are relaxed about.

The second is coursework. IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than the IB Diploma, but where it exists the boundary is identical: a tutor teaches, explains, models technique and gives feedback on work the student produced. A tutor does not write, complete, substantially rewrite or supply it. There are providers in this market selling completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. The consequence of that falls on the candidate as a malpractice matter, not on the seller, which is the part the advertising omits.

A third line is quieter and worth naming. Lead forms collect personal data about minors, and UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection applies. A form that asks for a child's school, grades and photograph without stating what the data is for, how long it is kept and how to have it deleted is a form worth not completing. A privacy link should be present on every page that collects anything.

What we do instead of supplying material is show the student where the official source lives, which is a transferable skill. A student who can locate a current syllabus on cambridgeinternational.org or a timetable on qualifications.pearson.com can also check a claim a tutor has made, including one of ours. That is a better outcome than a folder of files, and it costs nothing.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Jaddaf, with the limits stated
paragraphs: Send four things: the board, the specification code, the tier, and two evening windows that genuinely work from Al Jaddaf after the school run. If 0606 or Pearson Specification B is involved, say so, because those change the match time and we would rather tell you the wait up front than discover it after you have committed. We then match a specification specialist and run one free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep.

One trial per student, nothing charged beforehand, and no card details required to book it. The tutor writes a short note on what they found and what they would address first. That note is the thing to judge us on, because a note that names a specific weakness and the evidence that would show it moving is what makes the next term affordable. A general note means nobody has diagnosed anything yet.

Al Jaddaf scheduling has one genuine advantage worth using. The district is compact and minutes from the Creek crossings, so a student at a school inside Al Jaddaf or across in Dubai Festival City is often home in time for a 16:30 start, which is earlier than most Dubai neighbourhoods manage. For mathematics and the sciences, which lose more to fatigue than reading subjects do, that is worth real money across a term. Where the school is further out, a weekend morning is the better slot and it also widens the choice of tutor.

Finally, the limits. Nobody can promise a grade and this page does not. Nothing here implies that tutoring is required for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission or for school progression; those are regulatory and institutional processes with their own published rules, and the authority rather than any tutoring provider is where to verify them. And where a UAE-based specialist is unavailable for a niche subject, delivery may come from a specialist based outside the UAE, online and on Gulf Standard Time, which we state rather than conceal.

faqs.question: What kinds of business come up when I search for an IGCSE tutor near me in Al Jaddaf?
faqs.answer: Six, behind similar wording. A managed agency that places and replaces tutors; an international marketplace that lists them and takes a commission; an independent freelance tutor working alone; a tuition centre running group classes from premises; an online one-to-one platform with no geography; and your school's own paid support sessions. Each prices differently and fails differently. Replacement capability is the main thing an agency or platform charges for, and the main thing a freelance tutor, however good, cannot provide.

faqs.question: Which model is cheapest per hour, and what does the saving cost?
faqs.answer: A tuition centre group class, because the cost of a teacher divides across the room. The saving is real and so is the trade: a class advertised as IGCSE Mathematics may contain Cambridge Core, Cambridge Extended, Pearson Foundation and Pearson Higher candidates at once, since centres draw from several schools. A teacher managing eight students cannot interrupt one mid-error, so the student who most needs correction gets the least. If the problem is practice volume rather than error correction, a group class is the better purchase.

faqs.question: How do I check whether a tutor is legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask which MoHRE category applies and whether the permit is current. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service, with no fee and a stated two working days. Because it is free, there is no cost reason for a tutor not to hold one.

faqs.question: Are there fines for tutoring in the UAE without a permit, and how much?
faqs.answer: Individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published. A figure circulating in this market could not be verified against any official source, and the ministry was reported as not having specified the amounts or detailed the penalties. So no amount appears on this page, and any specific figure quoted to you by a provider should be treated as unverified, which is itself a useful signal about their other claims.

faqs.question: Does a tuition centre in Dubai need a different licence from an individual tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the two are separate legal positions. An individual needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds neither a centre permit nor any UAE premises, office or branch, and we say so rather than implying a local presence we do not have.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates my child's school if we move emirate?
faqs.answer: Five bodies cover the seven emirates. KHDA regulates Dubai. ADEK handles licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates Sharjah and the Department of Knowledge regulates Ras Al Khaimah, and both approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. None of these bodies approves, accredits or licenses tutors or tutoring platforms, which is the point most relevant to choosing one.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor covers my child's subject and tier?
faqs.answer: We tell you, give a realistic wait, and offer the nearest honest alternative rather than placing somebody adjacent. Thin coverage is predictable: Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478, Pearson Specification B, and the eight to twelve weeks before a June or November series when every Dubai cohort reaches the same point at once. The alternatives are a different slot, a shorter commitment with a specialist whose availability is limited, or command-term and paper-technique work while the subject slot stays pending.

faqs.question: Could my child end up being taught by a tutor who is not in the UAE?
faqs.answer: For a niche subject, possibly, and we state it rather than conceal it. Where no UAE-based specialist is available, delivery may come from a specialist based elsewhere, online and scheduled on Gulf Standard Time so the session still fits an Al Jaddaf evening. Several providers in this market conceal non-UAE delivery behind a local-looking listing or a non-UAE contact number, which is a trust failure rather than a logistics detail. If where the tutor sits matters to you, ask before booking and expect a straight answer.

faqs.question: Is an independent freelance tutor in Al Jaddaf a bad idea?
faqs.answer: Not at all, and it is usually the cheapest one-to-one option available. The trade is single-point-of-failure risk: no replacement if they are ill, no cover if they relocate or change jobs, and no second opinion if the match is not working. In Year 10 that risk is tolerable. In the final term before a series it is the expensive part, because a local replacement takes weeks to find. Ask what happens if they become unavailable, and treat a vague answer as the answer.

faqs.question: Does a tutor advertising in Al Jaddaf actually know my child's board?
faqs.answer: Ask, because proximity carries no information about it. Al Jaddaf is compact but its school catchment spans several clusters on both sides of the Creek, and those schools do not share one examination board. A tutor minutes away may be experienced in Cambridge 0580 Extended while your child sits Pearson 4MA1 Higher, where the paper structure, tier system and formula support all differ. Confirm the board, the specification code and the tier before any lessons, using the statement of entry.

faqs.question: Is paying a subject teacher from our own school for private lessons allowed in the UAE?
faqs.answer: You should not, and a professional teacher will decline. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Beyond the rules it creates a conflict: the person teaching the class and marking its assessments should not be separately paid by one family in it. Ask the school which arrangement a paid support session falls under.

faqs.question: Why do some tutoring sites quote prices in dollars rather than dirhams?
faqs.answer: Because they were written for a different audience and localised afterwards, if at all. Of the strongest pages researched for this market, three publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. Alongside that, two route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers. None of that makes a provider incompetent, but it does tell you how much of the page was written with a Dubai parent in mind, which is reasonable information to weigh when comparing.

faqs.question: Will a provider give me past papers and mark schemes to keep?
faqs.answer: Some offer it, and a legitimate one should not. Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are copyright works to be referenced and linked from the board's own site rather than reproduced or redistributed. A provider advertising a library of papers is offering something outside the rules, which raises a fair question about what else they are relaxed about. We work from the official source in the session and show the student where to find it themselves.

faqs.question: Should I be cautious about a form asking for my child's grades and photograph?
faqs.answer: Yes, unless the purpose is stated. Lead forms collect personal data about minors and UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection applies. A form asking for a child's school, grades and photograph without saying what the data is for, how long it is kept and how to have it deleted is one to leave incomplete. A privacy link should appear on every page that collects anything, and a provider unwilling to explain its data handling before you enrol has answered a different question.

faqs.question: How early in the evening can an IGCSE session realistically begin in this district?
faqs.answer: Often 16:30, which is earlier than most Dubai districts manage. Al Jaddaf is compact, sits beside Dubai Healthcare City Phase 2 and is minutes from the Creek crossings, so a student at a school inside the district or across in Dubai Festival City is frequently home in time. Pupils travelling to Sobha Hartland sit better at 17:00 and those commuting to Nad Al Sheba at 17:15 or later. Mathematics and the sciences lose more to fatigue than reading subjects, so the earlier slot is worth taking.

intro.heading: A belt of new communities with old-fashioned school geography
paragraphs: The Dubailand belt is unusual in Dubai. Al Khail Gate, Town Square, Mudon, DAMAC Hills and the Ranches extensions were built faster than the schools serving them, so families here commute in several directions and the nearest good option for one household is not the nearest for its neighbour. That makes a near-me search behave oddly: the results are not wrong, they are simply answering a question that does not map onto how this part of the city actually works.

The second feature is churn. Communities in this belt fill with families who have moved within Dubai, often from the older districts or from the Marina corridor, and school places move with availability rather than preference. A student who changes school in Year 10 or Year 11 may change exam board at the same time, and that is a far bigger disruption than changing neighbourhood. Cambridge and Pearson examine similar content through different papers with different grading, and a term spent practising the wrong board's style is a term lost.

Third, school supply here is changing quickly. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating around sixteen thousand eight hundred places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent across the sector. For a Year 9 or Year 10 family in this belt that means the school landscape in two years will not be the one they are looking at now.

So the comparison this page makes is two-layered. The first layer is district against district: what each community actually offers, how long the run is, which boards dominate nearby and whether the local tutoring market differs at all. The answer to that last question is no, consistently, and the reasons are worth seeing laid out rather than asserted.

The second layer is board against board, which is the comparison that genuinely changes what a student should be doing on a Saturday. Cambridge IGCSE tiers into Core and Extended with four papers in several subjects plus a practical paper; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1, tiers mathematics into Foundation and Higher, and runs untiered sciences with longer question stems. Knowing which one is on the statement of entry is worth more than knowing which tutor lives closest.

There is a third comparison families in this belt ask about and rarely get answered: school inspection bands against individual subject grades. A KHDA rating describes a whole school across many measures and is a poor predictor for one Year 11 set. The useful comparison for a parent is between a student's timed-paper mark and their target grade, which takes an afternoon to establish and tells you something a report cannot.

sections.heading: Six Dubailand communities compared on what actually matters
paragraphs: Set Al Khail Gate beside Motor City, Dubai Sports City, Arabian Ranches, Dubai Hills and the newer communities further out and three variables genuinely differ. School supply differs sharply: Dubai Sports City has schools inside it, Al Khail Gate has none, and Town Square and Mudon have newer and fewer. The commute differs by up to an hour each way depending on direction and interchange. And the dominant exam board differs by school, which in this belt means by household.

What does not differ is the supply of individual subject specialists resident nearby. Tutoring supply in Dubai concentrates where tutors live and where demand has been established longest, and the Dubailand belt is newer than that pattern. A family in Al Khail Gate who widens its search to Motor City and then to the Ranches is widening the radius without meaningfully widening the pool, and the names that do appear are increasingly constrained by how far they will drive.

The belt does have one real local option worth naming: the newer communities have attracted learning centres and group classes alongside their retail, and for a student whose problem is that no work happens unsupervised at home, a nearby group class at a lower hourly rate can be a sound purchase. It buys structure and syllabus coverage rather than diagnosis of one student's mark losses, and that distinction is the thing to be clear about before paying.

The comparison therefore ends where the Al Muteena version of this question ends, by a different route. Choose on board, tier and marking practice rather than on distance, use a local group class if structure is the binding problem, and accept that the individual specialist will not be a neighbour. In a belt where neighbours attend four different schools on two different boards, that is less of a loss than it sounds.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson: the comparison that changes revision
paragraphs: This is the comparison worth spending an evening on. Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examine similar content and present it differently, and the differences are concentrated in exactly the places where marks are won. Grading scales differ: Cambridge uses A* to G on most science and mathematics syllabuses while Pearson grades 9 to 1, which means a parent comparing two children's reports is comparing two scales. Paper counts differ: Cambridge mathematics runs four papers across two tiers, Pearson two.

Tiering differs in structure as well as name. Cambridge Core and Extended split both content and papers, so a Core candidate is not taught several topics at all. Pearson mathematics splits Foundation and Higher, while Pearson sciences are untiered, meaning one paper set covers the whole grade range and there is no ceiling to argue about. For a family comparing two schools, that single fact can matter more than an inspection band.

Question style is the third difference and the one students notice. Cambridge Extended papers tend to be tightly structured with short multi-part questions and precise command terms. Pearson stems run longer with more data to interpret before the question begins. Neither is harder; they reward different reading habits, and a student trained on one who sits the other will feel the paper is unfamiliar even where every topic is known.

The practical rule that follows is narrow and important: use past papers from the board the student is entered for, and nothing else. Cross-board practice looks efficient because the content overlaps, and it is the commonest reason a diligent student arrives at a mock feeling the paper was strange. The statement of entry names the board and the code; everything on a revision desk should match it.

sections.heading: Moving house inside Dubai mid-IGCSE: what it actually costs
paragraphs: Relocation within Dubai is common in this belt, and a school change in Year 10 or Year 11 carries a cost families consistently underestimate because they measure it in the wrong units. The social adjustment is visible and usually survivable. The academic cost is invisible and specific: a different exam board, possibly a different tier placement, a different set of past papers, and a different assumption about what was covered in Year 9.

The board change is the largest component. A student taught Cambridge for a year and entered for Pearson, or the reverse, knows most of the content and none of the paper. They will have practised the wrong formula conventions, the wrong question style and in the sciences possibly the wrong practical expectations. Four to six focused sessions on specification differences usually closes it, which is far cheaper than the general tutoring families often buy instead.

The tier placement is the second. A new school will place a student on the evidence it has, which after a move is thin, and a cautious placement on Core or Foundation can follow a student to results day. The response is the same as anywhere: timed higher-tier papers marked honestly, presented to the new head of department before entries close. After a move, that conversation should happen in the first term rather than when the first report arrives.

The third is coverage. Schools sequence topics differently, so a student arriving in Year 11 may have missed a unit entirely while repeating another. Asking the new school for its Year 10 scheme of work, and comparing it with the previous school's, identifies the genuine gaps in an hour. Doing that rather than assuming the curriculum is interchangeable is the difference between four sessions and a term of general catch-up.

sections.heading: New school supply in this belt, and what it changes
paragraphs: Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curricula at thirty-seven per cent of enrolment, Indian at twenty-six, US at fourteen and International Baccalaureate at seven. That mix explains the shape of tutoring demand in the city: IGCSE requests far outnumber Diploma requests even though the Diploma attracts more discussion.

The supply picture is moving. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating around sixteen thousand eight hundred new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. For families in this belt, where supply has lagged housing, that is the most consequential comparison of all: the school map in two years is not the one on screen today.

What it means practically for a Year 9 or Year 10 family is that a decision taken now on the basis of current availability may be reversible later on better terms, and that a place accepted reluctantly because it was the only one available is worth revisiting. It also means more Diploma capacity within reach of this belt specifically, since three of the seven additions are International Baccalaureate schools.

A fee note belongs with this. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a household weighing a school move alongside a tutoring budget, a flat fee year makes both decisions easier to plan in the same conversation.

sections.heading: Comparing an inspection band with a subject grade
paragraphs: Families in this belt compare schools constantly, and inspection bands are the metric most readily to hand. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the judgement covers the whole institution across many measures. It is genuinely useful information about a school and close to useless as a prediction for one Year 11 subject set.

The reason is statistical rather than critical. A school judged Very Good contains departments of varying strength, cohorts of varying ability and individual sets with individual teachers. A parent wanting to know whether their child is on track for a grade 7 in mathematics learns nothing from a whole-school band, because the band is an average across a whole student body and dozens of subjects.

The comparison that does answer the question takes an afternoon. Have the student sit one full past paper from their own board and tier under timed conditions with no notes, mark it against the published scheme without generosity, and compare the raw mark against the target grade. That single number tells a parent more than every report and inspection document combined, because it measures the thing that will actually be measured in the hall.

It is worth adding what the regulators do and do not cover, because the assumption that one body oversees everything is common. Dubai private schools fall under KHDA; Abu Dhabi and Al Ain under ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation; Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority; Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge; and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the Ministry of Education. None of them regulates private tutoring, which sits with MoHRE through the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years.

sections.heading: Four formats compared for the same student
paragraphs: The last comparison is between delivery models, and it is worth doing with the same student in mind rather than in the abstract. A Year 11 student in Al Khail Gate losing method marks on Cambridge Extended mathematics could be helped by a group class at a local centre, by an in-home tutor, by the school's own support sessions, or by one-to-one online. Those four do genuinely different things.

A group class provides structure, a fixed time, a supervised room and syllabus coverage at the lowest cost per hour, and cannot spend twenty minutes on why this student in particular does not write their working. The school's own sessions know the internal timeline and the teacher's expectations, which nothing else does, and are also paced for a group. An in-home tutor provides individual attention plus physical presence at a published AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel. One-to-one online provides individual attention plus selection by board and tier at a published AED 150 to 300, with specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above.

There is one constraint on school support worth knowing about rather than discovering. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the ADEK detail as press-reported and verify the current policy, but the direction across the UAE is clear: do not go looking for your child's own teacher privately.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address in Al Khail Gate or anywhere else in the Emirates. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. A family that wants a different format should buy it from somebody who sells it, with the published bands above as the benchmark.

sections.heading: The same eight hours, costed four ways
paragraphs: Comparing hourly rates across formats is misleading because the formats deliver different things per hour. A fairer comparison fixes the contact hours and looks at what each option costs and includes. Eight contact hours in a month is the unit most families end up buying, and the published Dubai figures make the comparison straightforward.

At the budget end, Tutopiya advertises online tutoring from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, which puts eight hours somewhere between roughly AED 264 and 520. Qualified subject tutors working online are published at AED 150 to 300, so roughly AED 1,200 to 2,400, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, so roughly AED 1,600 to 3,600. In-home is AED 180 to 500 with travel included, so roughly AED 1,440 to 4,000, and monthly in-home packages in the market sit at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions against about AED 799 for eight online sessions.

What those numbers do not show is what each hour contains. A group hour is shared, so the attention per student is a fraction of the hour. An in-home hour includes the tutor's travel in the price but not in the hour. An online specialist hour is a full hour of attention from somebody who teaches that exact paper. For a student whose problem is specific, the cost per useful minute diverges far more than the cost per hour suggests.

The monthly framing matters for a household decision too. Bestimate's estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-band, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Set against a flat school-fee year in Dubai, that is a line a family can plan deliberately rather than improvise under pressure in the final term, which is when the same help costs most and achieves least.

sections.heading: What the comparison concludes, and what we claim
paragraphs: Laid out across six communities, two exam boards, four formats and a fixed number of contact hours, the comparison resolves consistently. Distance does not discriminate between tutors in this belt, because specialist supply is thin in every community here. Board does discriminate, sharply, and it is knowable from the statement of entry. Tier discriminates and is contestable with evidence before entries close. Format discriminates according to what the student's actual problem is, not according to which is better in general.

That gives a family a short, usable sequence. Find the board and codes. Replace all practice material with that board's papers. Sit one full timed paper and compare the raw mark with the target. Decide whether the problem is structure, coverage or diagnosis, and buy the format that addresses that. Ask any provider which board and tier they teach and how they will mark the work.

What we claim is narrow. Tutors teach a named board at a named tier, mark student work against the published scheme in the session, and send a short note afterwards naming the topic, the marks and the next target. There is a free trial lesson before any payment is taken, and it functions as a diagnosis. If the honest conclusion is that a local group class or the school's own sessions would serve better, that is what gets said.

What we do not claim: IB Gram holds no permit, licence, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no office, centre or branch in the UAE. We publish no statistics about our own outcomes, no star ratings and no student counts, because we cannot produce the underlying data. Every AED figure on this page is a published market rate credited to the provider or study that published it.

faqs.question: Why does the nearest school differ for every family in Al Khail Gate?
faqs.answer: Because the Dubailand belt was built faster than its schools. Al Khail Gate has no school on its doorstep, so households commute in several directions depending on where a place was available when they needed one. Dubai Sports City has schools inside it; Motor City and Arabian Ranches have established provision a short run away; Town Square, Mudon and DAMAC Hills have newer and fewer. The practical consequence is that neighbours often attend four different schools on two different exam boards, which is why board matters more than postcode here.

faqs.question: Which is better for my child, Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Neither is better; they are different, and the difference matters for revision rather than for difficulty. Cambridge grades A* to G on most science and mathematics syllabuses, tiers into Core and Extended, and runs four papers in several subjects plus a practical paper. Pearson grades 9 to 1, tiers mathematics into Foundation and Higher, runs untiered sciences with two papers, and asks longer data-led questions. The practical rule is to use past papers only from the board your child is entered for, because cross-board practice is the commonest reason a mock feels unfamiliar.

faqs.question: We moved house and schools inside Dubai mid-IGCSE. How much ground has my son lost?
faqs.answer: Less content than you fear and more technique than you expect. The largest cost is usually a board change: a student taught Cambridge and entered for Pearson, or the reverse, knows most of the content and has practised the wrong paper style, formula conventions and in the sciences possibly the wrong practical expectations. Four to six focused sessions on specification differences typically closes it. The second cost is a cautious tier placement made on thin evidence, which should be contested in the first term with timed higher-tier papers.

faqs.question: How do I find out which exam board my child's new school uses?
faqs.answer: Ask the school directly and get it in writing, then check the statement of entry when it is issued. The board and the four-character syllabus code appear on that document for every subject, along with the tier. Do not infer the board from the textbook, because schools sometimes teach from one publisher's material and enter candidates with the other board. Once you have the codes, every past paper and revision guide on the desk should match them, which is the single most useful piece of housekeeping available.

faqs.question: Is a group class in Motor City or Sports City worth considering?
faqs.answer: Genuinely, for the right problem. A group class provides a fixed time, a supervised room, peers working the same syllabus and the lowest cost per hour, and for a student whose real issue is that no work happens unsupervised at home that combination can beat individual diagnosis. What it cannot do is spend twenty minutes on why one particular student does not write their working, or adapt when students in the room are on different boards and tiers, which in this belt is common.

faqs.question: Does a Dubai school's inspection rating predict my child's IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: Hardly at all. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, judging the whole institution across many measures and a whole student body. It is useful information about a school and a poor predictor for one Year 11 subject set. The measurement that does predict a grade is one full past paper from the right board and tier, sat under timed conditions and marked against the published scheme without generosity. That takes an afternoon and answers the question directly.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send a tutor to Al Khail Gate or Town Square?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address anywhere in the Emirates. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and delivered live over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper and published mark scheme shared on screen. The published Dubai in-home band is AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 online, and that is the benchmark if in-home delivery is what you want.

faqs.question: How much do eight hours of tutoring a month cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: At published rates, roughly AED 264 to 520 at the budget end, where Tutopiya advertises from around AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65; roughly AED 1,200 to 2,400 from a qualified online tutor, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150; roughly AED 1,600 to 3,600 or more at specialist rates; and roughly AED 1,440 to 4,000 in-home, where travel is included in the rate. Monthly packages seen in the market are around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

faqs.question: Are more schools opening near the Dubailand communities?
faqs.answer: Yes. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating around sixteen thousand eight hundred new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. For families in this belt, where housing has outpaced school supply, that means a place accepted reluctantly because it was the only option may be worth revisiting, and that Diploma capacity within reach of these communities is widening rather than static.

faqs.question: Can we hire a teacher from my daughter's own school for private lessons?
faqs.answer: It is restricted and best avoided. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the ADEK detail as press-reported and verify the current policy document, but the direction across the UAE is consistent. A teacher from a different school carries no conflict and knows the specification equally well.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a UAE permit, and can I check it?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with applications through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: Which subjects should we prioritise if the budget only covers one?
faqs.answer: The one closest to a grade boundary on a timed paper, not the one that feels worst. Rank the subjects by the gap between the raw mark on a properly sat past paper and the target grade, then spend the hours at the top of that list. Untiered subjects such as Business Studies and Economics keep the whole grade range open throughout, which sometimes makes them a better late investment than a tiered science where the ceiling has already been fixed by the entry.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE exams happen for students in this belt?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series and UAE centres sit those two; the February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable per zone, stating that using the correct one is essential and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise, so the timetable to trust is the one your school's exams officer issues.

faqs.question: Should we switch tutor if the first three weeks produce nothing?
faqs.answer: Check what is being measured before switching. Three weeks of raw timed-paper marks is a fair test for a technique problem and too short for a content gap, so the first question is which problem was diagnosed at the start. If the diagnosis was technique and the marks have not moved, change something: the tutor, the subject priority or the diagnosis itself. If the diagnosis was a content gap, the honest expectation was always longer, and that should have been stated before any payment was taken.

faqs.question: How do we compare two tuition providers fairly?
faqs.answer: Fix the contact hours and ask the same five questions of both. Which board and tier do you teach and have you taught that code this year? How will my child's work be marked? What will I receive after each session? How will we measure this in three weeks? And what will you refuse to do with assessed coursework? Written answers to those five, set against a fixed number of hours at a quoted rate, make two providers genuinely comparable in a way testimonials and student-count claims never do.

intro.heading: The question underneath 'near me'
paragraphs: A parent in Al Khawaneej who searches for a tutor nearby is almost never worried about the drive. The worry is competence, and specifically whether anyone within reach knows the exact qualification their child is sitting. That worry is well founded. The word IGCSE on a school report covers several different qualifications from several different boards, and the schools this community feeds do not all use the same one. Two Year 11 students living on the same street can be sitting different syllabuses in the same subject, with different papers and different practical arrangements.

Local adverts rarely resolve it. A notice in a community group offering IGCSE science tuition is making a claim about a subject, not about a syllabus, and the gap between those two things is where a term gets wasted. A tutor who learned the content on one board teaches the chemistry competently and prepares the student imperfectly for the paper, because the question styles, the command-term conventions and the way practical skills are assessed are not identical between boards.

There is a second reason local supply is thinner than it looks. The people who know a particular syllabus best in this part of Dubai are employed full time teaching it, which means the ones available on a weekday evening are a small subset, and for a less commonly taught subject or a particular board the subset can be empty. That is not a criticism of anybody. It is arithmetic, and it explains why a family can search diligently for a fortnight and find only approximate matches.

This page answers the question honestly rather than flattering it. It sets out how the boards differ, gives five questions that establish in one phone call whether a tutor knows your child's syllabus, explains what a parent can verify about a tutor's legal standing in the UAE, and describes what a syllabus specialist does that a generalist cannot. It also states plainly what IB Gram does: matching is on the board and the code, and teaching happens one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because in-home visiting is a service offered only in India.

The useful consequence of teaching over video is precisely the one this page is about. Once the hour does not require anybody to drive to Al Khawaneej, the question stops being who is nearby and becomes who teaches this syllabus. For a family that has spent two weeks looking for a local specialist in a particular board and code, that is not a sales argument. It is the difference between finding one and not. Everything below is written so you can use it on any provider, including this one.

sections.heading: The boards are not interchangeable
paragraphs: Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both award international GCSE qualifications, other awarding bodies operate in the UAE as well, and the schools around Al Khawaneej do not all use the same one. Treating them as a single qualification called IGCSE is the mistake that makes a local search feel successful and then disappointing. The content overlap is genuinely large, which is why a mismatch is not obvious in week one. The differences live in the papers.

Specifically: the structure and number of papers differs, the tiering arrangements and the language used to describe them differ, practical skills in the sciences are assessed by different means, the modular or linear arrangement of assessment can differ, and the mark-scheme conventions about what earns an explanation mark are not identical. A student practising to the wrong conventions will write answers that would score on another board's scheme, which is a particularly cruel way to lose marks.

The table below gives the comparison a parent can actually use, with the proviso that board arrangements are revised and the board's own current documentation is the authority. The practical instruction is simple: establish the board and the code from the statement of entry, then ask every prospective tutor which board and which code they teach. A specific answer is a good sign. A general answer about IGCSE experience is, for this purpose, a no. Ask the same question of the school as well, because a school occasionally moves board between year groups and the Year 11 answer is not always the Year 10 answer.

sections.heading: Five questions that settle it in one phone call
paragraphs: You do not need to understand a syllabus to find out whether somebody else does. Five questions, asked in order, separate a syllabus specialist from a competent generalist in about four minutes, and they work whether the person is around the corner or teaching from another city.

Ask which board and which syllabus code they teach for this subject. A specialist answers with the code. Ask how the practical or non-written component is assessed on that syllabus, because a tutor who has prepared candidates will describe it without hesitation. Ask what the commonest reason is that students lose marks on a specific paper in that subject, and listen for whether the answer is about mark-scheme behaviour or about students not working hard enough. Ask what they would want to see before the first session; the right answer involves a marked script. And ask what they will not do, which should produce a clear statement about coursework and assessed work.

The table lays out what a good answer sounds like against a weak one. The point is not to catch anybody out; plenty of good tutors are generalists and will say so, which is itself a useful answer. The point is that a family in Al Khawaneej spending real money for a term deserves to know which they are buying before the first invoice rather than in the eighth week. Asking them of a tutor already working with your child is also legitimate, and the answers explain a great deal.

sections.heading: Why the nearby pool is smaller than it looks
paragraphs: Al Khawaneej sits at the eastern edge of the city. The community holds primary provision and a Dubai Schools campus, and its secondary students travel out to Mirdif, Al Warqa, Al Qusais or further. The people in this part of Dubai who know a particular IGCSE syllabus well are, for the most part, the people teaching it at those schools, and they are employed full time.

Work the arithmetic through for a specific case. A family needs a tutor for a particular science syllabus on a particular board, able to teach at Extended tier, available on a weekday evening, and willing to be in or near Al Khawaneej. Each condition removes most of the remaining candidates. By the end of the list the set is often one person, and sometimes none, which is exactly the experience families report after two weeks of asking in community groups.

This is why local searches in this catchment end in approximate matches. The alternatives on offer are a tutor who knows the subject but not the board, a tutor who knows the board but is only free at a time nobody can attend, or an undergraduate at the budget end who sat the qualification recently and has never read a mark scheme as a marker. None of those is dishonest. They are what a distance filter leaves behind. Removing the distance filter is the only move that genuinely enlarges the set, and that is what teaching over live video does.

sections.heading: What a parent can verify about a tutor's standing in the UAE
paragraphs: Beyond syllabus knowledge there is a legal question, and it has a clear answer that most families never hear. The UAE regulates private tutoring through a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the Ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, with no fee stated and a two-working-day completion time. The permit is granted free of charge and lasts two years.

The categories eligible to hold it are published and broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone providing private tutoring without the permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so a figure quoted to you as a deterrent is unverified and should be treated that way rather than repeated.

The table turns that into something a parent can use. Two further points belong here. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a separate instrument with its own process and renewal; an individual's work permit is not that, and nobody should describe themselves as KHDA approved on the strength of one. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, has no UAE premises and makes no such claim. And press reporting on Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules indicates school staff there may not take paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with the permit's code of conduct pointing the same way; verify current wording with the authority before relying on it, and in any case do not arrange for your child's own teacher to tutor them for money.

sections.heading: What a syllabus specialist does that a generalist cannot
paragraphs: The difference shows up in the detail of a marked script. A generalist reads a wrong answer and explains the correct content. A specialist reads the same answer and says that the content was right, the command term was not addressed, and the scheme awards nothing for a description where it asked for an explanation. The student in the second case has learned something transferable; the student in the first case has learned the answer to one question.

Three further things belong to the specialist. Knowing which topics are heavily weighted on this board's papers and which appear rarely, so revision time goes where the marks are. Knowing the conventions, such as how many distinct differences a two-mark comparison needs or whether a unit is required in a particular style of answer. And knowing the tier boundary well enough to say whether a student entered at the lower tier is being limited by the entry rather than by their ability.

None of this requires the specialist to be nearby. All of it requires them to know the specific syllabus. That is the whole claim of this page, and it is why IB Gram matches on board and code and teaches over live video rather than recruiting whoever is willing to drive east on a Tuesday. A shared whiteboard with the student's own script on screen covers everything this kind of work needs, and the hour starts when your child is ready rather than when a car arrives.

sections.heading: Private candidates, centres and the questions only a centre can answer
paragraphs: Some Al Khawaneej families need a paper their child's school is not entering them for: a resit, an extra subject, or a qualification taken outside the school timetable. The teaching for that is ordinary tutoring. The administration is not, and it is worth being clear about which parts a tutoring provider can and cannot do.

Entry for a private candidate is made through a registered examination centre, and the centre sets the deadlines, charges the fees and administers the papers. A tutoring provider does not arrange entries, cannot influence them and should not imply otherwise. The questions to take to a centre are which series it accepts private candidates for, what the entry deadline is, which syllabuses and components it can offer, and how practical or non-written components are handled for a candidate who is not taught there. Boards publish centre information on their own sites and that is the right starting point.

Timing is the part families get wrong. An entry deadline sits months before the paper, so a decision about a resit has to be made a long way in advance of the point at which it feels urgent. Cambridge International runs June and November series for international candidates, with an additional early-year series offered to India only, so a UAE candidate plans around June and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November; its November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Provisional timetables are published ahead of each series and can be revised, so work from the live official timetable rather than from any date restated here.

sections.heading: Starting, and the coverage we disclose by syllabus
paragraphs: Send three things and the first conversation is a real one. The statement of entry, giving the board, the syllabus code and the tier. The most recent marked script with the teacher's comments intact. And the realistic weekday time your child is able to work, which for a student travelling home across eastern Dubai is later than families expect.

Then a free trial lesson, one-to-one over live video. Use the five questions on this page during it. Ask the tutor to work through the marked script against the board's own conventions and name what is costing marks. A specific answer, grounded in the scheme rather than in general advice about revision, is what you are paying for and you should be able to hear it inside an hour. If the match is wrong, say so in week one.

The disclosure, stated before you ask. Coverage is held per board and per syllabus code, not per subject name, and there are genuinely weeks when no UAE-based specialist in a particular code holds an evening slot that fits an Al Khawaneej timetable. Where that happens you will be told, and offered a specialist based elsewhere teaching the same syllabus over the same live video on Gulf Standard Time. What will not happen is a tutor for one board being presented as a specialist in another, because that is the exact failure this page exists to prevent. No competitor page reviewed for this project discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: Is there anyone in Al Khawaneej who teaches my child's exact IGCSE syllabus?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and the honest answer is that the set is small. The community holds primary provision and a Dubai Schools campus rather than a large secondary entry, and the people in this part of Dubai who know a specific syllabus well are mostly teaching it full time at schools in Mirdif, Al Warqa or Al Qusais. Add a board, a tier and a weekday evening requirement and the available set often reduces to one person or none. Removing the distance condition is the only move that genuinely enlarges it.

faqs.question: How do I check whether a tutor really knows the syllabus my child sits?
faqs.answer: Ask five questions. Which board and syllabus code do you teach for this subject. How is the practical or non-written component assessed on it. Where do students most often lose marks on that paper. What do you want to see before the first session. And what will you not do. A specialist answers the first with a code and the third with mark-scheme behaviour rather than a comment about revision. It takes about four minutes and it works on anybody, including us.

faqs.question: Does it really matter whether a tutor knows Cambridge or Edexcel?
faqs.answer: The content overlap is large, which is why a mismatch is not obvious early. The differences live in the papers: their number and structure, the tiering arrangements and what they are called, how practical skills in the sciences are assessed, whether assessment is linear or modular, and the mark-scheme conventions about what earns an explanation mark. A student practising to the wrong conventions writes answers that would score on another board's scheme, which is a particularly unkind way to lose marks in a real paper.

faqs.question: Where do I find my child's syllabus code?
faqs.answer: On the statement of entry the school issues, on the entry confirmation, or on the front page of any past paper the school has given your child. If none of those is to hand, email the school's exams officer rather than the class teacher; it is the exams officer's record and they can answer in a line. Ask in the same email which tier your child is entered for where the syllabus is tiered, because that answer is not reversible once the series has been sat.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Dubai need a licence, and can I check it?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. You can ask a tutor directly whether they hold it. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can my child's own schoolteacher tutor them privately for money?
faqs.answer: Treat it as something to avoid. Press reporting on Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff there may not provide paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the Ministry permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify current wording with the relevant authority before relying on the detail. The practical position for a Dubai family is straightforward enough: do not arrange it, however convenient the familiarity appears.

faqs.question: Is a nearby generalist better than a syllabus specialist teaching online?
faqs.answer: For most families in this catchment, no, and the reason is what each can see in a marked script. A generalist reads a wrong answer and explains the correct content. A specialist reads the same answer and reports that the content was right, the command term was not addressed, and the scheme gives nothing for a description where it asked for an explanation. The second is transferable to every future paper. Proximity adds nothing to that, and in this catchment it subtracts the evening a tutor would spend driving.

faqs.question: My child wants to resit one IGCSE subject. How does that work?
faqs.answer: Entry for a candidate sitting outside their school's arrangement is made through a registered examination centre, which sets the deadlines, charges the fees and administers the papers. A tutoring provider does not arrange entries and cannot influence them. Ask a centre which series it accepts private candidates for, what the entry deadline is, which syllabuses and components it offers, and how non-written components are handled. The boards publish centre information on their own sites, and the entry deadline sits months before the paper.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE series should an Al Khawaneej candidate plan around?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs June and November series for international candidates, with June the main sitting and November available as a resit route. Its additional early-year series is offered to India only, so it does not apply here. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with a different timetable version each, and its guidance states that using the wrong zone timetable is the centre's risk. Your exams officer holds both facts.

faqs.question: What should I listen for in a trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Specificity about the mark scheme. A tutor working through your child's marked script should be able to say which convention cost the mark, not simply what the right answer was. Listen also for what they ask for: a request to see marked work before the session is a good sign, and an offer to start at the beginning of the syllabus usually means no diagnosis has happened. You should finish able to repeat the finding to your child in two sentences.

faqs.question: Why did a local tutor seem fine for six weeks and then stop helping?
faqs.answer: The usual explanation is a board mismatch that only becomes visible under exam conditions. Content teaching goes well because the content overlaps, and the problem surfaces when timed papers begin and the student meets question structures and conventions they have not practised. The second common explanation is that no diagnosis was ever done, so the sessions covered what the student already half knew. Both are preventable with the five questions on this page, asked before the first invoice rather than in week eight.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need to know my child's set texts as well as the board?
faqs.answer: In literature, yes, and it is worth asking separately. Schools choose set texts from the board's list, so two centres on the same board can be teaching different texts. A tutor who knows the board but not the texts is of limited use in the final year, when the work is detailed quotation and argument on specific material. Ask which texts they have taught and when. In most other subjects the board and the code are sufficient to establish a real match.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover a subject if my child changes board mid-course?
faqs.answer: It happens, usually with a school move, and it needs care rather than panic. The content largely transfers; the practice does not. The work is a deliberate audit of what differs, paper structure, tiering, practical arrangements and conventions, followed by timed practice on the new board's papers rather than the old ones. A tutor who teaches both boards is ideal. A tutor who teaches only the previous board is the specific risk this situation creates and is worth replacing rather than persevering with.

faqs.question: What should an Al Khawaneej family send before an IGCSE trial lesson?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry showing board, syllabus code and tier. The most recent marked script with the teacher's comments intact, which is where any real diagnosis comes from. And the realistic weekday time your child can work, measured rather than estimated, since a student travelling home across eastern Dubai is ready later than families assume. With those three things the trial hour does work instead of making introductions, and you can judge the tutor on something specific.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-mamzar.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE subjects to students living in Al Mamzar, Hor Al Anz, Al Nahda and Al Qusais. Each is listed by board and syllabus code, because that is the detail that decides whether a term of work produces marks.

intro.heading: Supply is not the problem here. Precision is.
paragraphs: There is a version of this search that deserves a pessimistic answer and a version that deserves an optimistic one, and IGCSE gets the optimistic one. UK curriculum schools account for 37 per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment, the largest single share in a sector of 227 private schools and 387,441 students. Tutors follow that market. So unlike a family hunting for a Higher Level Diploma specialist, a family in Al Mamzar looking for IGCSE help is not facing genuine scarcity.

What they are facing is imprecision, and it costs more than scarcity does because it is invisible. 'IGCSE tutor' is not a specification. There are two boards in common use in Dubai, Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel, with different syllabus codes, different paper structures, different tier names and different question styles. Cambridge tiers maths and the sciences into Core and Extended; Pearson tiers maths into Foundation and Higher. A tutor who is fluent in one and working with a student entered for the other will teach real content and produce very few extra marks.

The second imprecision is the tier itself. On Cambridge, a Core entry caps the attainable grade. On Pearson 4MA1, Higher tier covers grades 9 to 4 and Foundation covers 5 to 1. Those caps are applied at entry, months before the examination, and a surprising number of families in this catchment do not know which applies to their child. Buying tutoring to chase a grade that the entry has already excluded is the most expensive mistake available in this subject, and nobody discovers it until results day.

The third is the subject beneath the subject. A student losing marks in physics, chemistry and maths at once usually has one quantitative problem rather than three subject problems. A tutor hired for physics will teach physics. A tutor who tests the rearrangement of an unfamiliar formula first will find the real issue in five minutes, and fixing it lifts all three. The difference between those two tutors is not knowledge; it is whether they diagnose before they teach.

Al Mamzar's own geography adds a practical layer. The neighbourhood sits against the Sharjah border, the schools immediately around it predominantly teach CBSE or the Ministry curriculum, and British-curriculum families here commute towards Al Qusais, Al Garhoud or across the creek. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Mamzar or anywhere else in the UAE; a tutor attending a student's address is a service we run only in India. Every lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, matched on the code rather than on the drive.

The sections below are ordered to be used rather than read. The first names the four mismatches that account for most wasted tutoring money in this market, with a column on how to detect each one before paying. The second writes out the Cambridge and Pearson code pairs so a parent can settle the question in a single email to the school office. The third gives three questions to ask in a free trial lesson that will separate a precise tutor from a vague one, with no subject expertise required. After that: the local tuition-centre option assessed fairly, what this district's tutoring market is genuinely strong at, rates read as a monthly number, and the regulator position for a neighbourhood that sits five minutes from a different emirate's authority.

subjects.description: Common across this part of Dubai, where many households use Arabic, Malayalam, Urdu, Tagalog or Hindi at home. The listening component and the note-making exercise need timed practice rather than vocabulary drilling.

subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading summary carry the volatile marks. Students lose marks for not shaping a response to the stated audience and purpose, which is a mark-scheme habit rather than a comprehension gap.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Arabic is mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. In this neighbourhood the first-language pathway is more common than the city average, and local tutoring supply for it is strong.

subjects.name: Accounting and Business Studies
subjects.description: Both popular in a district where many parents work in trade, logistics and accountancy around Deira and Al Hamriya. Accounting loses marks to layout and presentation conventions; Business Studies loses them to answering the topic rather than the command term.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and command-term discipline decide more marks than the economics content does. An evaluate question answered as a description sits in the lower band however accurate the description is.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables need deliberate practice; the practical ICT components need fluency against a specific software version, which is one of the few cases where the tutor's own software setup genuinely matters.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure
subjects.description: Extension qualifications taken alongside the main maths syllabus by students heading for A Level maths. Usually timetabled into an option block with fewer hours than the content needs, which is where strong mathematicians underperform.

sections.heading: What you asked for, what you might get, and how to tell the difference
paragraphs: The honest risk in this search is not that nobody competent is available. It is that the person you hire is competent at something adjacent. Four mismatches account for most of the wasted money in this market, and all four are detectable in a free trial lesson if you know to look for them. None of them involves a bad tutor; they involve a tutor pointed at the wrong target.

The first is board mismatch. A tutor fluent in Cambridge 0580 working with a Pearson 4MA1 candidate will teach correct mathematics using the wrong question styles and the wrong past papers. The second is tier mismatch: teaching Extended content to a Core candidate wastes the hours, and teaching Core content to an Extended candidate leaves the upper marks unreachable. The third is a GCSE rather than IGCSE background, which overlaps heavily but differs in coursework arrangements and in some content.

The fourth is the subject-versus-cause mismatch, which is the costliest because it looks like success. A tutor hired for physics teaches physics competently for a term, and the grade does not move because the actual problem was equation rearrangement under time pressure. The student concludes they are bad at physics, the parent concludes tutoring does not work, and both conclusions are wrong. A five-minute test with an unfamiliar formula would have found it in session one.

The table below sets out each mismatch, how to detect it and what it costs. It is written to be used before paying rather than afterwards, which is why the detection column is the important one. Every item in it is something a parent with no subject expertise can check.

sections.heading: The code pairs, written out, so you can check them in one email
paragraphs: This is the part a parent can settle in a single message to the school office, and it removes most of the risk above. Ask for the examination board and the syllabus code for each subject, and the tier where one applies. Write the answers down and keep the list; it is the document that makes every later decision about revision material, tutoring and resits straightforward instead of guesswork.

A mixed entry is more common than families expect. Departments choose boards independently, so a student can sit Cambridge papers in maths and Pearson papers in physics at the same school, and a student who transferred mid-course sometimes keeps the board they started on. So the question is not 'which board are we' but 'which code is each subject entered under'.

Tier names are the other source of confusion, because the two boards use different words for related ideas. Cambridge tiers maths and the sciences into Core and Extended. Pearson tiers Mathematics A into Foundation and Higher, with Higher covering grades 9 to 4 and Foundation covering 5 to 1, and runs most other subjects as a single tier. A parent told 'he's on Higher' and a parent told 'she's on Extended' have both been told their child is on the upper tier, in different vocabularies.

One administrative point worth collecting at the same time: which of Cambridge's six administrative zones the centre sits in. Cambridge allocates every centre to a zone, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The school holds that answer, and a timetable downloaded from a search result is not a safe substitute.

sections.heading: Three questions that expose a mismatch in a free trial lesson
paragraphs: A parent does not need to understand the subject to test whether a tutor is pointed at the right target. Three questions in a trial lesson will do it, and all three are reasonable things to ask without appearing difficult. The point is not to catch anybody out; it is to find out before paying rather than in March.

The first question is about the code. Ask which syllabus code they are going to teach and which board's past papers they will use. A tutor who answers '0580 Extended, and I'll use Cambridge papers from the last four series' has told you they work precisely. A tutor who answers 'IGCSE maths' has told you they will work out the details later, and the details are the whole job.

The second question is about the tier ceiling. Ask what the student's tier caps and what it would take to move it. A tutor who knows that Pearson Foundation tops out at grade 5 and that Cambridge Core cannot reach the top grades will tell you straight away whether the grade you are hoping for is available at all. That is the single most valuable thing anybody in this market can tell you, and it takes thirty seconds.

The third question is diagnostic. Hand over a marked paper and ask what the pattern of lost marks indicates, and what the first three sessions would therefore do. A tutor who distinguishes content gaps from unwritten method, misread command terms and running out of time has demonstrated the skill that makes the hours worth buying. One who proposes to work through the syllabus from the start has told you the sessions will be a lottery, however pleasant they are.

sections.heading: The local option: tuition centres and group classes in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: Al Mamzar, Hor Al Anz and Al Qusais have a real tuition-centre market, and it deserves a fair assessment rather than a dismissal. Centres offer structure, a fixed routine, supervision, a peer group and a price per student that one-to-one cannot match. For a student who works better with external structure than with self-discipline, that is genuinely valuable, and for a family with two or three children it can be the only affordable arrangement.

The limitations are also real and specific. A group has to share a level and a board to be taught efficiently, and in a district where IGCSE is a minority curriculum the group is often mixed in both respects - some Cambridge, some Pearson, some Core, some Extended. Teaching that group means teaching the overlap, which is content everybody half-knows rather than the specific gap any individual has. The student who needs qualitative analysis tables drilled does not get them.

The second limitation is diagnostic. A centre working with twelve students cannot categorise one student's lost marks by cause and build three weeks around the result. That is not a criticism of centres; it is arithmetic. It does mean that a centre is a good place to acquire routine and a poor place to fix a specific, identified failure pattern eight weeks before the papers.

The honest recommendation is therefore split by need, which the table sets out. Routine and structure through Year 10: a centre or a group is often the better value. A specific diagnosed gap in Year 11: one-to-one, matched by code. A tier question: one-to-one, because it needs a timed upper-tier paper marked strictly and a written view, which no group setting produces.
