sections.heading: What this neighbourhood's tutoring market is genuinely good at
paragraphs: It would be dishonest to write a page about local supply and only describe its weaknesses. Al Mamzar, Hor Al Anz, Al Nahda and Al Qusais have a strong and well-established tutoring market, and for several needs the best option really is somebody nearby. Supply follows demand, and the demand in this district is concentrated in places that do not overlap with Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses.

Arabic as a first language is the clearest example. This neighbourhood has a far higher proportion of Arabic-first-language students than the Dubai average, and the supply of capable Arabic tutors here is correspondingly deep. Since KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies - because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ - matching a tutor to the correct pathway matters, and locally that match is easy to make.

CBSE support is the second. Indian-curriculum schools are 26 per cent of Dubai's enrolment overall and a much larger share here, so for a family with one child on IGCSE and another on CBSE, the sensible arrangement is often a local tutor for the CBSE child and an online code-matched tutor for the IGCSE one. Insisting on a single arrangement for both children is how families end up with a compromise that serves neither.

The third is Ministry-curriculum and Islamic Education support, where local knowledge of the school's own materials matters. KHDA requires schools to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach them, and for the mandatory subjects the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. Support in those subjects therefore has to track the school's own scheme closely, and proximity to the school community genuinely helps.

sections.heading: Rates, read as a monthly number, with the group trade included
paragraphs: Hourly rates are the least useful way for a household to think about this. Published market figures for Dubai put monthly spend for a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 for a mid-market qualified tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are the numbers to compare against a school fee, an activity cost or a group-class package.

Translated to the hour, the ladder is identifiable. Tutopiya publishes online rates from around AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, which generally means a university student. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270 for specialist work and Bestimate's specialist band runs AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home one-to-one sits at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the price.

The group comparison is the one families in this district actually make, because centres here are a real alternative rather than a theoretical one. A term package at a centre will usually come in below a weekly one-to-one session, and for Year 10 consolidation that can be the better buy. The crossover point is diagnosis: once a marked paper has identified a specific, narrow failure pattern, group teaching cannot address it and the one-to-one hour becomes the cheaper option per mark gained.

IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page, because a figure quoted without knowing the board, the tier and the frequency is a number rather than information. The trial lesson and the consultation are free, and the figures above are other providers' published rates rather than ours. For budgeting context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

sections.heading: What a tutor may not do, and the one thing you can verify
paragraphs: Several IGCSE subjects carry coursework or practical components, and those are where the honesty line gets tested. A tutor may teach content, explain what the mark scheme rewards, model a technique on a different question, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, finish or edit a piece of assessed work to completion - including when it is described as polishing or proofreading beyond clarity.

The consequence is asymmetric, which is the part worth understanding. The school signs an authentication that the work is the candidate's own, and if that is untrue the sanction falls on the student. One site ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments at a published price; the seller keeps the money and the candidate carries the entire risk. Recognising that trade for what it is matters more than any rule.

Materials work the same way. We reference Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes, cite them, and link out to the boards. We do not reproduce them or supply them as downloads, because they are the boards' copyright and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure in themselves. A tutor who offers a folder of mark schemes has told you something about how they operate.

The thing you can verify in one question is the permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing'. Tutoring without a permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted penalty figure as unverified.

sections.heading: Two regulators, five minutes apart
paragraphs: Al Mamzar is one of the few Dubai neighbourhoods where the regulator question is a live practical matter rather than background information. Private schools in Dubai are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Five minutes up the road, Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority instead.

The difference is more than the name on the inspection report. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods - so curriculum and fee approval, not only inspection, sits with the emirate regulator. A family in Al Mamzar with one child at a Dubai school and another across the boundary is dealing with two different approval frameworks, two different inspection systems and two different sets of published reports.

For completeness, the rest of the map matters to families who move within the country. In Abu Dhabi the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate; in Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge regulates private education; and the Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Those five bodies are the complete regulator map, and ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages researched in this market.

Within Dubai, the mandatory UAE subjects apply regardless of the licensed curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated against a forty-minute lesson unit, separate classes are required for Arab and non-Arab students in several of those subjects, and additional or different content needs prior permission from the Ministry of Education.

process.title: Email the school for board, code and tier
process.description: One message, three answers, for every subject. It is the step that prevents the four mismatches on this page, and it costs nothing. Write the answers down and keep the list - it governs every later decision about material, tutoring and resits.

process.title: Send a marked script
process.description: A marked paper distinguishes content gaps from unwritten method, misread command terms and running out of time. A report grade distinguishes none of them, and those four need entirely different first sessions.

process.title: Use the free trial to test the match
process.description: Ask which code and which board's papers, ask what the tier caps, and hand over the marked script for interpretation. Ten minutes of that tells you more than any credential list, and nothing has to be unwound if the answers are vague.

process.title: Decide whether a group is the better buy
process.description: For Year 10 routine and consolidation, a local centre or a small group is often better value, and we will say so. For a specific diagnosed gap in Year 11, one-to-one is cheaper per mark gained. The crossover is diagnosis.

process.title: Pick the slot by arrival reliability
process.description: A creek crossing at 3pm varies by twenty-five minutes; a Green Line commute from Abu Hail does not. We will usually recommend the slot that depends on no road at all, which in this catchment means the evening.

process.title: Review against whole papers
process.description: Every few weeks a timed paper of the correct board and tier, marked strictly, with lost marks categorised and compared against the previous one. That is the measure that tells you whether to continue, change tutor or stop.

whyPoints.title: Matched by code, not by subject name
whyPoints.description: The booking records the board, the syllabus code and the tier. That one administrative habit prevents the most expensive and most invisible waste in this market - a competent tutor pointed at the wrong target.

whyPoints.title: The tier question asked first
whyPoints.description: Cambridge Core and Pearson Foundation both cap the grade at entry. We establish which applies before building any plan, because chasing a grade the entry has excluded is money spent against a wall nobody mentioned.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before teaching
whyPoints.description: Three sciences failing at once is usually one quantitative problem. We test rearrangement and proportion with no subject attached before selling subject hours, because fixing that lifts every science at once.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the local alternatives
whyPoints.description: This district has a real tuition-centre market and deep Arabic and CBSE supply. For several needs the best option is somebody nearby, and we say which ones rather than arguing against every alternative.

whyPoints.title: No travel, so no travel premium
whyPoints.description: In-home rates run roughly AED 180-500 an hour with the journey inside the price, and the journey to Al Mamzar is longer than average. Online delivery removes the cost rather than discounting it.

whyPoints.title: Three tests you can run yourself
whyPoints.description: Code and papers, tier ceiling, and interpreting a marked script. A parent with no subject expertise can separate a precise tutor from a vague one in ten minutes, and the free trial exists for exactly that.

faqs.question: Are there enough IGCSE tutors near Al Mamzar, or will we struggle?
faqs.answer: Supply is not the problem for IGCSE. UK curriculum schools are the largest group in Dubai at 37 per cent of private-school enrolment, and tutors follow that market, so competent IGCSE tutors are not scarce the way Higher Level Diploma specialists are. The risk here is precision instead: two boards, four tier names and dozens of syllabus codes mean a competent tutor can be pointed at the wrong target, teach real content for a term and produce very few extra marks.

faqs.question: What exactly should I ask the school office before hiring anyone?
faqs.answer: Three things per subject: the examination board, the syllabus code, and the tier where one applies. Cambridge codes look like 0580, 0625 and 0620; Pearson codes look like 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1. Also ask which of Cambridge's six administrative zones the centre sits in, because Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct timetable for your zone and cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Write it all down and keep it.

faqs.question: Can my child be on Cambridge for one subject and Pearson for another?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is more common than families expect. Departments choose boards independently, so a student can sit Cambridge papers in mathematics and Pearson papers in physics at the same school, and a student who transferred mid-course sometimes keeps the board they started on. That is why the right question is not which board the school uses but which code each subject is entered under. A revision guide bought on the wrong assumption is a term of misdirected work.

faqs.question: My daughter's tutor seems good but her grade has not moved. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Four possibilities, and three of them are mismatches rather than competence problems. Wrong board: correct content taught with unfamiliar question styles. Wrong tier: either unreachable material or a ceiling nobody mentioned. GCSE rather than IGCSE background: mostly right with persistent small gaps. Or the subject was hired and the cause untreated - a physics tutor teaching physics while the real problem is rearranging equations under time pressure. Ask for a marked paper to be categorised by cause; that distinguishes all four.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in Al Qusais a reasonable alternative to one-to-one?
faqs.answer: For some needs, yes, and we would rather say so than pretend otherwise. Centres offer routine, structure, supervision, a peer group and a lower cost per student, which suits Year 10 consolidation well. The limitation is that a group has to share a board and a tier to be taught efficiently, and in this district the group is often mixed in both, so the overlap gets taught. Once a marked paper identifies a specific narrow gap, a group setting cannot address it.

faqs.question: Will someone come to our home in Al Mamzar for IGCSE lessons?
faqs.answer: Not from us. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Mamzar, in Dubai, or anywhere else in the UAE - a tutor attending a student's address is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In-home tutoring does exist in this market at published rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, and that travel is longer to Al Mamzar than to most districts because Cambridge and Pearson tutors cluster nearer the schools that teach those syllabuses.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Extended and Higher tier?
faqs.answer: Mostly vocabulary. Cambridge tiers mathematics and the sciences into Core and Extended; Pearson tiers Mathematics A into Foundation and Higher, with Higher covering grades 9 to 4 and Foundation covering 5 to 1. So a parent told their child is on Higher and one told their child is on Extended have both been told the upper tier. What matters is that the lower tier in either system caps the attainable grade at entry, months before the examination, and that cap is invisible unless somebody asks.

faqs.question: Our neighbours all use the same local tutor. Why would that not work for us?
faqs.answer: Often it would - for the right subject. This district has deep local supply in CBSE subjects and in Arabic as a first language, because that is where local demand sits, and for those needs a nearby tutor is usually the better choice. Where it breaks down is Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses, which are a minority curriculum in Deira and Al Qusais. A household with one IGCSE child and one CBSE child frequently needs two different arrangements rather than one compromise.

faqs.question: How much should we budget monthly for one subject?
faqs.answer: Published market figures for Dubai put a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 for a qualified subject tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A term package at a local centre will usually come in below the one-to-one figure. Those are other providers' published rates rather than ours. Our trial lesson and consultation are free, and a quote depends on board, tier and frequency.

faqs.question: My son is losing marks in physics, chemistry and maths. Do we need three tutors?
faqs.answer: Probably one, and probably not in any of those three subjects first. Proportion, equation rearrangement, standard form and graph reading are examined inside every one of them, and a weakness there loses marks everywhere while looking like three separate problems. The test takes five minutes: hand over an unfamiliar formula and ask for a given symbol to be made the subject, with no subject content attached. If that is slow, fix it and all three grades move together.

faqs.question: Can we still change tier if we ask now?
faqs.answer: It depends where in the two years you are. Year 10 into very early Year 11 is the realistic window, and it moves on evidence rather than argument - a timed upper-tier paper sat cold, marked strictly, with a topic-level breakdown and a realistic estimate of the weeks needed to close the gap. Schools respond to that far better than to parental conviction. By the spring of Year 11 the entry is made, and the remaining question is how high a grade is reachable inside the cap.

faqs.question: What time of day works for a student commuting back from Oud Metha?
faqs.answer: Realistically the evening. A school finishing between 2.30pm and 3.15pm across the creek means a journey of thirty to fifty minutes back to Al Mamzar at that hour, and the arrival time varies by twenty-five minutes or more week to week. A 5pm booking against that variance becomes a forty-minute session with ten unproductive minutes at the start. A 7.30pm session depends on no road, which is why it holds through a term in this catchment.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with coursework in subjects that have it?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits. A tutor can teach the content, explain what the assessment criteria reward, model a method on a different question, and comment on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write, finish or edit assessed work to completion, including when it is described as polishing. The school signs an authentication that the work is the candidate's own, and if that is untrue the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever helped, which is the asymmetry to keep in mind.

faqs.question: What if we need a subject or tier you cannot cover?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting someone approximate. Some combinations are genuinely thin - Pearson Further Pure 4PM1 at short notice, a specific Cambridge syllabus version mid-revision, or practical-paper technique in the fortnight before the papers. When that happens you get three straight answers: how long a match realistically takes, whether a closely related specialist can cover part of the need, and whether a local centre or the school's own department is the better route for now.

intro.heading: Work out the clock before you look for a tutor
paragraphs: Every family that hires a tutor and then quietly stops after six weeks has the same story, and it is almost never about teaching. The lesson was set for 4pm because that is what the school timetable said. The bus arrived at 4.35pm on three Tuesdays out of four. The child walked in hungry, sat down at 4.45pm, and the first fifteen minutes of a sixty-minute session went on settling. Then the tutor was late once because Umm Suqeim Street was closed, and once more because of rain, and by half-term the whole arrangement had become a weekly argument. The tutoring did not fail. The scheduling did.

Al Manara makes this worse than average because of where it sits. It is an inland villa community along Al Wasl Road and Umm Suqeim Street, almost exactly between two school clusters. Seaward, five to twelve minutes in clear traffic, are the Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah campuses. Inland, across Sheikh Zayed Road, twelve to twenty-five minutes off-peak, is the dense Al Barsha and Al Quoz cluster. Children from the same street go in opposite directions, and in late-afternoon traffic those drive times stretch considerably. A household with two children at two schools has two different arrival times to plan around.

Add the things that are already in the week. School buses do not run direct; they loop, which is why a 3.15pm departure becomes a 4.15pm or 4.45pm arrival depending on where your villa sits on the route. After-school clubs push one or two days later still. Dubai private schools also run KHDA's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies lessons alongside the international curriculum, with instructional time counted in 40-minute units, so the school day is fuller than the subject list implies and homework starts late.

So the first useful question is not "who is near me" but "what time does my child actually walk through the door, on a normal Tuesday, in term time". Answer that honestly - including the bad days, not the best one - and the rest of the plan becomes simple. This page maps the school-run geography around Al Manara, works out the earliest slot that holds rather than the earliest slot that looks possible, and sets out how many sessions a real Year 10 or Year 11 week can absorb.

It also deals with the tutoring question properly: the Dubai market rates in AED with the source attached to each figure, the difference between Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE routes, and the exam calendar for UAE candidates counted backwards. On delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India. For an Al Manara family, lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.
That matters more for scheduling than for anything else. A lesson that depends on nobody's drive is a lesson that starts when your child is ready, and moves when the week does.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-manara.programmesIntro: An Al Manara IGCSE enquiry sits in a British-curriculum pathway with a decision at each end. Knowing where your child is in it determines how much of the week needs protecting.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 into IGCSE
programmes.description: The years before the IGCSE course begins, and the cheapest point at which to fix anything. Algebraic fluency, scientific method, extended writing and reading stamina all get built here, and all of them are assumed by the IGCSE syllabuses. A Year 8 with shaky negative numbers becomes a Year 10 who loses marks on every rearrangement in physics.
programmes.countryNote: Scheduling is easiest at this stage because the day ends earlier and clubs are lighter, which makes a 5pm slot genuinely workable for most Al Manara households. It is also the stage at which families are least inclined to buy support, which is the opposite of what the arithmetic suggests.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years of examined courses sat as a June or November series. Cambridge subjects carry four-digit codes - 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English - with many tiered into Core and Extended. Pearson Edexcel codes read differently - 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1 - with Mathematics A tiered Foundation and Higher.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage most Al Manara enquiries concern, and Year 11 is when the week is fullest: mocks, coursework deadlines where subjects have them, and the longest school days of the pathway. Protecting one reliable weekly hour is worth more than booking three that keep collapsing.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The most common next step for Al Manara's British-curriculum students. Cambridge runs International A Levels in the same June and November series as IGCSE. The step up assumes algebraic fluency and independent practical reasoning, which is why a student who reached a strong IGCSE grade through recall often finds the first A Level term hard.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education British-track equivalency the published requirement is one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route, offered by the IB World Schools in Al Manara's inland radius. Six subjects across Higher and Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, with an internally assessed component in every subject and grades on a 1-7 scale.
programmes.countryNote: Relevant at IGCSE stage because the choice is made in Year 11 and the two routes reward different IGCSE habits. Students heading for the Diploma benefit from understanding rather than memorising their IGCSE content, because internal assessment and command terms arrive immediately in Year 12.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-manara.subjectsIntro: With a limited number of protected weekly hours, subject choice matters. These are the IGCSE subjects Al Manara families ask about, with the thing one hour a week can realistically move.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: The highest-yield subject for a single weekly hour, because the skills compound and feed physics and chemistry too. Extended reaches into functions, vectors and transformations. Marks go on unshown working and premature rounding, both of which are habits rather than knowledge and respond quickly.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two equally weighted papers with a calculator permitted throughout, which shifts the balance of skills against some Cambridge components. Higher tier assumes confident algebraic manipulation, and the most common loss is a correct method abandoned mid-question under time pressure.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves absorb most of the lost marks, and the failure is usually arithmetic rather than conceptual - a unit unconverted or a slip in rearrangement. Graph and gradient technique is quick to teach and rarely taught, which makes it good value for a single hour.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry decide the grade and benefit from weekly rather than occasional practice. Marks are lost on state symbols, significant figures and answers that describe an observation instead of explaining it. Electrolysis questions punish vague electrode reasoning.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: A volume subject, which makes it the hardest to move with one hour a week - the content has to be learned rather than explained. Where an hour does pay is terminology precision and data interpretation, since near-miss vocabulary earns nothing against the mark scheme.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Two or three sciences compressed into fewer qualifications, common among Dubai students not carrying all three forward. The content is shallower but exam technique demands are identical, and students often arrive with weaker practical reasoning from fewer laboratory sessions.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing carry the paper. The highest-return work in one hour is timing discipline and task-type awareness - audience, form, purpose - rather than vocabulary. Students lose marks summarising a passage where the task asks them to select and analyse.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Listening, reading and writing with a specified text type for each writing task. A confident speaker can plateau because register and text-type conventions were never taught explicitly, which is a fast fix. Listening practice needs quiet, which is itself a scheduling point.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and case-study application decide the grade. A correctly labelled and shifted diagram with the new equilibrium marked earns marks prose cannot recover, and tool-based answers that never name the business in the case are capped however fluent.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and data representation in Computer Science; practical application skills in ICT. Trace table marks go to rushing rows, and theory marks go to giving an example where the command term asked for a definition or a comparison.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger candidates heading for A Level Mathematics and genuinely useful preparation for it. The algebraic demand jumps sharply from the main syllabus, so students who coped with 0580 Extended by pattern recognition tend to stall here first.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: Dubai students often carry an IGCSE Arabic entry alongside KHDA's mandatory Arabic lessons, which have their own content. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs with combined classes prohibited, so the two strands are genuinely different work.

sections.heading: What time does your child actually walk in?
paragraphs: This is a question with a real answer and most families have never written it down. Take a normal term-time Tuesday, not the best day of the week. Note the timetabled finish. Add the bus loop if your child takes a bus, which for an Al Manara villa on an Al Barsha route is commonly thirty to sixty minutes rather than the fifteen the map suggests. Add the walk from the drop-off point. Then add the twenty minutes a fourteen-year-old needs to eat something and stop being a passenger.

Do that honestly and the 4pm slot that looked obvious usually turns out to be a 5pm or 5.15pm slot. That is not a failure; it is a plan. A session that starts when the student is ready uses its full hour. A session scheduled against the timetable loses its first quarter every week to arrival, food and settling, which over a term is the equivalent of three lessons thrown away.

There are two complications specific to Dubai worth building in. First, the school day is fuller than the international curriculum suggests. KHDA's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies lessons run in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and KHDA advising at least 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. Those sit inside the timetable, so finish times run later than parents sometimes expect.

Second, arrival times differ by sibling. An Al Manara household with one child seaward in Umm Suqeim and one inland in Al Barsha has two different clocks, and a tutor who travels can only serve one of them. sections.heading: Why the 4pm slot fails and the later slot works
paragraphs: The 4pm lesson is the single most common scheduling mistake in Dubai tutoring, and it fails for four reasons at once. The student is not home. If the student is home, the student is hungry. If the student has eaten, the student has been in a vehicle for forty minutes and is in no state to think about simultaneous equations. And the tutor, if the tutor travels, is in the same traffic the bus was in, arriving flustered or late.

A later slot fixes all four. The student has arrived, eaten and changed. The adrenaline of the school day has dropped. A slot set after the worst normal arrival time is a slot that does not need renegotiating every week, and a tutoring arrangement that needs renegotiating is one that ends. The pattern to aim for is boring: same day, same time, same tutor, enough margin that a bad traffic day costs nothing.

There is a limit at the other end, which is worth being honest about. Past roughly 7.30pm most Year 10 and Year 11 students are producing diminishing work, and a session that eats into sleep is a false economy during a term with mocks in it. The usable window for an Al Manara family is therefore narrower than it looks: roughly 4.30pm to 7.30pm on weekdays, with the start depending on which direction the school run comes from.

Where the week genuinely does not contain a usable hour - long inland commute, two clubs, a sibling's schedule - the honest answer is a weekend slot rather than a weekday one squeezed in against the evidence. A Friday or Saturday session with a rested student does more than a Tuesday session with an exhausted one, and it survives term after term. Families are often reluctant to give up weekend time and then relieved once they have.

sections.heading: How many sessions a real Year 11 week can hold
paragraphs: Parents in the exam year often want three or four weekly sessions and the week cannot take them. A Year 11 student in a Dubai school has a full timetable including mandatory UAE subjects, homework in eight or nine subjects, coursework or practical components in some, mock preparation, and the commute this page has already described. Adding four tutoring hours to that produces a tired student doing worse work in everything, which is the opposite of the intention.

The realistic arithmetic is one protected hour per subject that genuinely needs it, to a maximum of two or occasionally three across the whole week, with the understanding that homework for those sessions has to fit somewhere too. A tutor who sets forty minutes of practice between lessons is adding to the load as well as to the learning, and that is correct - but it has to be counted.

Choosing which subjects get the hours is the real decision, and it should be made on where the marks are rather than on which subject feels worst. Mathematics usually earns its hour first because the skills compound and feed physics and chemistry too. A subject where the loss is pure content volume - biology, often - is the hardest thing to move with one weekly hour and may be better served by a holiday block. A subject where the loss is technique - unshown working, command terms, timing - moves fastest of all.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the Dubai academic calendar
paragraphs: Scheduling in Dubai has to account for a year that does not look like a European one, and no competitor page in this search result mentions it. During Ramadan school days shorten, timings shift, and the afternoon is the least useful part of the day for concentrated work. For many households a post-Iftar slot works considerably better than the usual late-afternoon hour, and for others the honest answer is to pause weekly sessions and resume afterwards rather than run them badly.

The practical point is that a tutoring arrangement which cannot move is an arrangement that breaks during Ramadan and often never restarts. One that moves easily - because nobody is driving anywhere and the slot is a calendar entry rather than a journey - simply shifts for a month and continues. That is a small operational detail with a large effect on whether support survives a whole academic year.

The same logic applies to the rest of the Dubai calendar. Long summer breaks, with many families travelling, are where a weekly arrangement usually collapses; over live video on Gulf Standard Time it can continue or shift to another time zone. Winter and spring breaks are natural points for a concentrated block on a content-heavy subject, which is exactly the thing a single weekly hour cannot deliver.

Then there are the school's own fixed points to plan around: mock weeks, coursework and practical deadlines where subjects have them, parent consultations, and the series itself. The useful habit is to put the school's published calendar and the tutoring slot in the same place, so a mock week becomes a reason to change the focus of a session rather than a reason to cancel it.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to a candidate in Dubai, which matters because a page quoting the wrong window to a UAE parent causes real harm to a real revision plan.

One Cambridge detail deserves its own sentence. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your child's exams officer which zone your centre is in, in writing, before building anything around a date you found online.

For Pearson, International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why any plan should work from the live official timetable rather than from restated dates - including the ones on this page.

Counted backwards the shape is the same whichever board: entries close months ahead, the mock round is the last honest diagnostic, the final weeks belong to timed papers, and results arrive on a known date with a resit series available. The table adds the column most calendars leave out, which is who actually owns each deadline.

sections.heading: What a lost twenty minutes costs, in AED
paragraphs: Scheduling is a money question as well as a logistics one, and this is the arithmetic nobody does. Take a mid-market rate: a qualified subject tutor online is quoted around AED 150-300 an hour across Dubai, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. If a session set too early loses its first twenty minutes every week to arrival and settling, you are discarding a third of the hour. Over a thirty-week school year that is ten hours of tuition paid for and not received.

Now add the travel premium, because it compounds the same problem. In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are quoted at AED 180-350 by Bestimate's 2026 rate table, with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33-52; named specialists are quoted AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, with premium rates reaching AED 650 at BartyED. The in-home premium is the price of a car, not of better teaching.

The monthly packages make the trade visible. Around AED 799 a month buys roughly eight online sessions; AED 1,599-1,799 a month buys four two-hour in-home visits. For a Year 10 student building exam technique, eight shorter contacts produce eight cycles of work and feedback where four produce four - and the four are the ones that get cancelled when a road closes.

What the in-home premium genuinely buys deserves saying fairly: a person in the room, supervision, and a working environment that is not competing with the laptop. For a younger or easily distracted student that is worth paying for, and plenty of Dubai providers deliver it well. IB Gram is not among them. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and for an Al Manara family lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. One figure for context: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

sections.heading: Making the slot survive the whole year
paragraphs: A tutoring arrangement that lasts an academic year is worth more than a better one that lasts six weeks, and survival is mostly about design rather than willpower. The first design choice is the margin already described: set the start after the worst normal arrival, so the lesson does not need defending every Tuesday. The second is consistency - same day, same time, same tutor - because a slot that moves around gets displaced by whatever else wants the evening.

The third is what happens when something interrupts, and here the rule should be reschedule rather than cancel. A school trip, a mock week, a family event: a lesson moved to Thursday is a lesson kept, while a lesson cancelled is a week of momentum gone and the beginning of the slow fade that ends most tutoring arrangements by half-term. Because nobody is driving, moving a session is a calendar change rather than a logistical negotiation.

The fourth is honesty about load. If a student has mocks, a coursework deadline and two clubs in the same fortnight, the right move is often to reduce to one session and change its purpose - exam technique rather than new content - rather than to push through the usual plan. A tutor who insists the plan is the plan regardless of the student's week is not managing a real child's year.

The last is measurement, because an arrangement nobody evaluates drifts. Judge it against the school's own marking: the next assessed piece, the next mock, the next report. If the mark moved, the slot is earning its place. If it did not after a fair run, the diagnosis was wrong and should be revised rather than repeated. That review conversation is worth putting in the calendar too, once a term.

sections.heading: Checking the tutor and the boundaries
paragraphs: Two checks, both free, both worth making before the first paid hour. The permit first. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted at you by anybody.

MoHRE's own service page is "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and runs through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. There is also a rule worth knowing: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

The second check is the coursework boundary, which applies wherever an IGCSE subject carries an assessed component. A tutor may teach the skill, explain the assessment criteria, mark practice attempts and give written feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of a submission, supply data, or edit a draft to completion. In the adjacent IB market one provider openly sells completed Internal Assessments; the risk in buying anything of that kind falls on the student rather than the seller.

One clarification, since the phrase circulates widely in Dubai: no individual tutor is KHDA-approved, because that status does not exist for individuals. KHDA regulates and inspects Dubai private schools and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises in the emirate. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no premises in the UAE and claims no regulator or board accreditation of any kind.

sections.heading: What to send so the first lesson is not wasted
paragraphs: Four pieces of information turn a first session from an introduction into a diagnosis, and they take ten minutes to gather. The board and syllabus code from your child's school entry confirmation - Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, 0620 or 4CH1 - because the two are different qualifications with different papers. The tier, where the subject is tiered, since Core and Foundation cap the grade available.

Then the most recent marked paper, with whatever annotations the teacher made. A specialist reads a marked script diagnostically: which topics, which command terms, whether the loss is content, technique or timing. That document is worth more than any amount of description, and a plan proposed without it is guesswork however confident it sounds.

And finally the clock: the real arrival time on a normal Tuesday, the days that already have clubs, and the date of the next thing that matters - a mock, a coursework deadline, a series. With those, a slot can be set that holds rather than one that has to be renegotiated in October.

The free trial lesson is where all of this gets tested rather than taken on trust. One lesson at no cost, with the marked paper on screen, at a time chosen from the real arrival rather than the timetable. By the end you should know which topics and command terms are costing marks and roughly how many hours the fix needs. If the answer is no, nothing is owed and no block has been bought.

process.title: Write down the real arrival time
process.description: Before anything else, work out when your child walks in on a normal term-time Tuesday - timetabled finish, plus the bus loop, plus the walk, plus twenty minutes to eat. That number, not the school timetable, is what the weekly slot should be built on, and it is the single biggest predictor of whether the arrangement lasts.

process.title: Send the code and the marked paper
process.description: The board and syllabus code from the school's entry confirmation, the tier, and the last marked paper with its annotations. That combination lets a specialist name the topics and command terms losing marks in the first session rather than the third.

process.title: See the proposed tutor and the available slots
process.description: You get a named tutor with the boards and codes they have taught, and the slots they can hold against your arrival time. If the right subject teacher cannot cover your window, you are told rather than quietly offered somebody adjacent.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson at the real time
process.description: One lesson at no cost, deliberately scheduled at the time you would actually use, so the test includes the clock and not just the teaching. If the slot is wrong you will know in week one rather than in week six.

process.title: Lock the slot and protect it
process.description: Same day, same time, same tutor, with enough margin that a late bus costs twenty minutes rather than the session. When a mock week or a school trip interrupts, the lesson moves rather than cancelling, because nothing depends on a drive across Al Wasl Road.

process.title: Review once a term against the school's marks
process.description: Progress is judged on the next assessed piece and the next mock, not on an internal report nobody else uses. If the mark moved, the slot has earned its place. If it did not after a fair run, the diagnosis gets revised rather than repeated.

whyPoints.title: The slot is built from the arrival time
whyPoints.description: Al Manara children travel in two directions and arrive home anywhere from 4pm to past 5.30pm depending on route and bus loop. Setting the session after the worst normal arrival, rather than after the timetabled finish, is what stops a third of every paid hour disappearing into settling.

whyPoints.title: Nobody is in the traffic
whyPoints.description: A late bus moves the lesson by twenty minutes instead of wasting it, and a closed road on Umm Suqeim Street cancels nothing. Over a thirty-week year that difference is worth more than the hourly rate gap between any two providers in this market.

whyPoints.title: Two shorter sessions cost no more to arrange
whyPoints.description: Because there is no travel in the rate, splitting an hour into two shorter weekly slots does not double an overhead. For a Year 10 building exam technique, two feedback cycles a week beat one longer session almost every time.

whyPoints.title: Rates come with their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to whoever published it - Unitors, Bestimate, EdFlik, Tutopiya, TutorChase, BartyED - with no invented IB Gram price list. Three of six researched competitor pages publish no price at all and two quote in a currency UAE families do not use.

whyPoints.title: Exam dates come from the boards
whyPoints.description: Cambridge runs June and November for UAE candidates and allocates each centre to one of six zones; Pearson's November 2026 timetable ran to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The India-only February/March series is named as such rather than quoted at Dubai parents.

whyPoints.title: Delivery is stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service we run only in India. Tutor location is disclosed rather than hidden behind a local-looking number, and the free trial lesson tests the slot as well as the teaching before any hours are agreed.

faqs.question: Is a 4pm IGCSE lesson realistic for a child bussing back into Al Manara?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and this is the most common reason a tutoring arrangement quietly dies. School buses loop rather than running direct, so an Al Manara villa on an Al Barsha route commonly sees arrival forty to sixty minutes after the timetabled finish, and even the short seaward routes from Umm Suqeim add twenty to thirty minutes. Add the walk from the drop-off and the twenty minutes a teenager needs to eat and stop being a passenger. A 5pm or 5.30pm start that holds every week is worth far more than a 4pm start that needs renegotiating.

faqs.question: How late in the evening can a session still be useful?
faqs.answer: For most Year 10 and Year 11 students the work produced falls away after about 7.30pm, and a session that eats into sleep during a mock term is a false economy. That gives an Al Manara family a usable weekday window of roughly 4.30pm to 7.30pm, with the start depending on which direction the school run comes from. Where the week genuinely has no hour in that window - a long inland commute plus two clubs - a weekend slot with a rested student does more work than a weekday one squeezed in against the evidence.

faqs.question: Do two children at two different schools need two different tutoring times?
faqs.answer: Almost always, because Al Manara sits between two clusters and siblings often travel in opposite directions. A child at an Umm Suqeim campus may be home thirty minutes after the bell while a sibling on an Al Barsha route arrives an hour later. A tutor who drives can realistically serve one of those arrival times, not both, which is one of the quieter advantages of video delivery: two slots an hour apart cost no extra travel and need no second journey arranged.

faqs.question: What happens to our lesson when a road closure or rain disrupts the afternoon?
faqs.answer: The lesson shifts by twenty minutes or moves to another evening, because nobody is in a vehicle. That is a small operational difference with a large cumulative effect: an in-home arrangement loses the session to a late start with no refund, or loses the week entirely because there is no substitute tutor inside the driving radius. Over a thirty-week school year those lost weeks add up to more than the hourly-rate gap between most providers in this market, and they tend to land in the weeks that matter most.

faqs.question: How many tutoring hours can a Year 11 week in Dubai actually absorb?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families want. A Year 11 student carries a full timetable including KHDA's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies lessons, homework across eight or nine subjects, mock preparation, any coursework or practical components, and the commute. One protected hour per subject that genuinely needs it, to a maximum of two or occasionally three across the week, is the realistic ceiling - and the practice a tutor sets between lessons has to fit somewhere too. Four hours of tuition on top of that produces worse work everywhere.

faqs.question: Which subject should get the one hour we can protect?
faqs.answer: Usually mathematics, because the skills compound and feed physics and chemistry as well. After that, choose on where the marks are rather than on which subject feels worst. Where the loss is technique - unshown working, misread command terms, timing - one weekly hour moves it fastest. Where the loss is pure content volume, biology most often, a single hour struggles and a concentrated holiday block does more. A marked mock script tells you which of those you are dealing with; a percentage does not.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan rather than stopping altogether?
faqs.answer: Yes, and moving is much better than stopping. School days shorten during Ramadan, timings shift and the afternoon becomes the least productive part of the day, so a post-Iftar slot often works better than the usual late-afternoon hour. Because nobody is driving anywhere, changing the time is a calendar entry rather than a renegotiation. The arrangements that break during Ramadan are the ones that cannot move, and in practice they rarely restart afterwards - which is how a year of planned support becomes five months of it.

faqs.question: Should we keep lessons running through the Dubai summer break?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject and the year. For a student going into Year 11, the summer is the best available window for content-heavy catch-up - biology, combined sciences, anything where volume rather than technique is the problem - because term time cannot provide concentrated hours. For a student who has just finished a series, a genuine break has value. Travel is not an obstacle: lessons over live video can continue on Gulf Standard Time or shift to whichever time zone the family is in.

faqs.question: Which sitting does an Al Manara candidate get entered for?
faqs.answer: The June series or the November series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to a candidate in Dubai. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. Always plan from the live official timetable on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com rather than any restated dates, including those here, because provisional timetables get revised.

faqs.question: Why might my child's Cambridge timetable differ from a friend's at another school?
faqs.answer: Because of administrative zones. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. That means two candidates sitting the same syllabus can face different dates and times. It is one question to your child's exams officer, and the answer belongs in writing before any revision plan is built around a particular date.

faqs.question: What does a session starting twenty minutes late actually cost us?
faqs.answer: A third of the hour, every week. At a mid-market Dubai rate - a qualified subject tutor online is quoted around AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 - that is roughly ten hours of tuition paid for and not received across a thirty-week school year. The fix costs nothing: set the start after the worst normal arrival time instead of after the timetabled finish. It is the cheapest improvement available to any tutoring arrangement and almost nobody makes it deliberately.

faqs.question: Why is in-home tuition in Dubai quoted so much higher than online?
faqs.answer: Because an hour of teaching takes about two and a half hours to deliver. Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online. The gap is the price of a car: a tutor driving into Al Manara from Al Barsha or Umm Suqeim in late-afternoon traffic, finding parking, and driving back. What it buys is physical supervision, which genuinely helps some students. What it does not buy is better subject teaching.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to a house in Al Manara?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and nobody is sent to a UAE address. For an Al Manara family, lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing so the marked paper, the specimen paper and the mark scheme are visible to both sides and the annotated script stays with the student. For a scheduling-driven problem that is the point rather than a compromise: a lesson that depends on no journey is a lesson that starts when your child is ready and moves when the week does.

faqs.question: What should we send before the first IGCSE session so it is not wasted?
faqs.answer: Four things, ten minutes of work. The board and four-character syllabus code from the school's entry confirmation - 0580 or 4MA1, 0620 or 4CH1 - because those are different qualifications. The tier, where the subject is tiered, since Core and Foundation cap the grade available. The most recent marked paper with the teacher's annotations. And the real arrival time on a normal Tuesday plus the days clubs already own. With those, the first lesson is a diagnosis rather than an introduction.

faqs.question: How do we know after a term whether the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: By the school's marking, not the tutor's. Judge it on the next assessed piece, the next mock and the next report, because those are the marks that follow your child and feed predicted grades. A provider reporting progress only against their own internal tests is reporting on themselves. Put a review in the calendar once a term: if the mark on the same component moved, the slot has earned its place; if it did not after a fair run, the diagnosis was wrong and should be revised rather than repeated more loudly.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-mankhool.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE subjects for students at the Bur Dubai, Al Mankhool and Karama schools. Each one works to a specific code and tier rather than to a subject label, because the paper your child sits is determined by that code and so is every mark scheme the hours should be aimed at.

intro.heading: The four digits that decide whether the hours work
paragraphs: There is a number on your child's school entry statement that matters more than anything in this search result. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580. Cambridge International Mathematics is 0607, a different course with different papers. Physics is 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, Co-ordinated Sciences 0654, English as a Second Language 0510, English First Language 0500. Pearson Edexcel uses a different scheme entirely: Mathematics A is 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1. Two students living in the same Al Mankhool block can be sitting different papers in the same subject.

Almost nothing in the local tutoring market is organised around that fact. A tutor advertises IGCSE Physics, a parent books it, and the sessions proceed on whichever syllabus the tutor knows. For six weeks everything looks fine, because the physics is the physics and most of the content overlaps. Then a mock paper arrives in a question style the student has not practised, with a mark scheme that rewards something slightly different, and the gap between what was taught and what is examined becomes visible at the worst possible moment.

Codes are not the only thing a subject-led approach cares about. Each paper has its own geography of lost marks, and those are remarkably consistent across cohorts. In the sciences it is the six-mark extended response, where a student who knows everything writes a list of correct facts and scores three. In mathematics it is unwritten method, where a correct approach done mentally earns nothing after one arithmetic slip. In English it is writing about what a passage says rather than how the writer achieves an effect. In Economics and Business it is a definition where an evaluation was demanded.

None of those is a content gap, and that is the useful part. They are all trainable patterns, visible in a marked script within minutes, and fixable in a handful of sessions rather than a term. A family in Al Mankhool who brings one marked paper to a first conversation gets a far better plan than one who brings a report card, because the script shows where the marks are going and the report card only shows that they went.

It is worth adding that the code question is not pedantry invented by a tutoring company. Receiving schools and universities state their entry requirements in named qualifications, not in general subject terms, and the certificate your child eventually holds names the board and the syllabus. A parent who has never seen the entry statement is effectively unaware of what their child is being certified in, which is a strange position to be in while paying for support in it.

So the sections below work through the subjects rather than the neighbourhood. The code directory first, so you know what you are buying support for. Then the extended-response question that decides science grades. Then how practical science is examined when nobody is standing at a bench. Then the English decision, which quietly affects university and equivalency paperwork. Then a subject-by-subject map of mark-scheme traps, and finally which subjects actually reward past-paper practice and which still need content.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-mankhool.programmesIntro: Three qualification families are sat across the schools near Al Mankhool, plus the IB alternative. Each uses a different code scheme, and knowing which one your child is in is the first step in every plan below.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Four-digit codes, many subjects tiered Core and Extended, and a June and November series for UAE candidates. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge also runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which is a separate thing from the IGCSE series and is sometimes confused with it in local tutoring material. For an Al Mankhool family the operative point is that the authoritative timetable comes from the school's entry statement and the board's live timetable, not from a search result.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: A different code scheme - 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology - with its own tiering and a distinct question-building style. Exams are available in May/June and November each year, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series.
programmes.countryNote: Dates worth knowing because they show the shape of the calendar: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Always work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level
programmes.description: Still sat in some schools in this part of Dubai, particularly where a school's history runs through a different system, and examined in the same June and November series as IGCSE. Content overlaps substantially with IGCSE but assessment structures differ, so past-paper practice must come from the correct qualification.
programmes.countryNote: Families sometimes discover a child is on O Level rather than IGCSE only when a tutor brings the wrong papers. The entry statement settles it in one line. It matters for progression too, since receiving schools and universities state requirements in terms of specific qualifications rather than general equivalents.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The alternative route to sixteen at the IB continuum schools near this district, assessed against four criteria per subject group on a 1-8 scale with no terminal papers in most schools. Support looks nothing like IGCSE past-paper work and should not be bought as though it were.
programmes.countryNote: Where a household has one child on IGCSE and another on MYP - which happens often in Al Mankhool, since siblings sometimes attend different schools - the two children need genuinely different kinds of help. Buying the same weekly pattern for both wastes money on one of them.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-mankhool.subjectsIntro: Below are the IGCSE subjects students around Al Mankhool most often need, each with its code and the specific mark-scheme habit that costs marks in it. These are patterns rather than content gaps, which is why they are quick to fix.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: The trap is unwritten method. A four-mark question typically awards two or three for a correct approach, so working mentally and writing one line forfeits them after any arithmetic slip. Across a paper this costs more than any topic weakness.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Same subject, different question architecture: parts build on one another in a particular way and the paper rewards following that build. A student drilled on Cambridge papers reads the question stems slightly wrong and loses time before losing marks.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism produce the biggest losses, usually on explain questions answered as descriptions. The scheme wants a mechanism - charge, field, force, consequence - in a linked chain, and a correct but unlinked set of statements scores low.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations and organic chemistry take the hours, but the recoverable marks are in the extended response, where a list of true statements about a reaction scores less than a shorter answer that connects cause to effect in order.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: The subject that punishes revision-by-reading hardest. Students feel prepared and then lose marks on data interpretation and on definition precision. Describing a process step by step, in the right order, is the single most profitable thing to practise.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: All three sciences in a double award, which limits depth. Worth confirming before paying for three separate science tutors, and worth checking against what a post-sixteen science course at the receiving school expects.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510)
subjects.description: Counts toward the five subjects MoE equivalency recognises on the British track. Marks are won on reading-comprehension technique and on the controlled writing tasks, where following the rubric exactly matters more than vocabulary range.

subjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the analysis of unseen passages. Students write about what the passage says; the scheme rewards writing about how the writer produces an effect. That shift is a technique fix of roughly six to eight sessions, not a year of reading.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Definitions and diagrams get a student to the middle of the range and no further. The upper marks sit in the evaluation questions, which require a judgement with its limits stated, and students who revise content exclusively never reach them.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Application to the specific case given in the paper separates the bands. A correct general answer about a concept scores below a shorter answer that uses the named business's actual circumstances, and that discipline is quick to teach.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Theory plus algorithms and programming problem-solving. Students fluent in Python still lose marks by writing Python where the scheme expects the syllabus pseudocode conventions, which is a presentation habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Calculus, logarithms and matrices taken alongside 0580 Extended by students heading toward A Level or Higher Level Mathematics. Demanding in pace: it stretches a student with secure algebra and overwhelms one without it.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-mankhool.regionsIntro: This is a dense part of old Dubai where neighbours rarely share a syllabus. The notes below are about what each area's school mix means for finding somebody on the right code, rather than about the length of a drive.

regions.name: Al Mankhool
regions.note: Apartment living with a mixed intake across British, Indian and IB provision. A recommendation passed between two families in the same building frequently points to a tutor on a different board entirely, which is why the code question has to be asked every time.

regions.name: Bur Dubai and Al Fahidi
regions.note: The historic core with long-established schools, several of which split entries between Cambridge and Pearson by subject. A single student can therefore sit one board in mathematics and another in a science, which surprises parents more often than it should.

regions.name: Karama
regions.note: Dense, close and home to the cheapest word-of-mouth tuition in the city. That market is largely generalist, which is adequate for consolidating a Core-tier subject and poor for an Extended-tier science where the extended response decides the grade.

regions.name: Al Satwa and Al Hamriya
regions.note: Mixed residential with students travelling in several directions. Because the school mix is wide, this is where families most often end up buying tuition for the wrong qualification - O Level practice for an IGCSE entry, or the reverse.

regions.name: Al Jafiliya and Za'abeel
regions.note: Toward the Trade Centre, with working-parent households and sessions that drift late. For essay subjects an evening hour is fine; for the non-calculator mathematics paper and for timed science practice, fatigue costs accuracy first.

regions.name: Oud Metha
regions.note: The adjacent school belt a short drive east, with several large schools running to sixteen. Families here and in Al Mankhool compare notes constantly, which is useful about schools and misleading about tutors.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf and Dubai Healthcare City
regions.note: Newer towers and the nearest IB continuum option, so some students here are on MYP rather than IGCSE. Different assessment model, different support, and the two should not be bought as the same product.

regions.name: Deira and Al Garhoud
regions.note: Across the creek with its own school cluster. Students travelling that way lose the afternoon to the crossing between four and six, so their sessions realistically start later than a family in Al Mankhool itself would plan.

schoolClusters.city: The Al Mankhool and Bur Dubai schools
schoolClusters.note: Long-established schools running Cambridge, Pearson and in places O Level provision to sixteen, with an Indian-curriculum presence alongside. The board split within and between these schools is the practical reason the code matters more than the postcode.

schoolClusters.city: Where this belt's students go at sixteen
schoolClusters.note: The post-sixteen provision reachable from Al Mankhool, running A Level, the Diploma or American-curriculum routes. Their entry requirements are stated in named qualifications, which is another reason the code on the certificate matters.

sections.heading: The code directory, and what changes between boards
paragraphs: The first thing to establish is which qualification, which code and which tier. It is one line on the school's entry statement, the school will send it on request, and it determines every past paper, every mark scheme and every question style that the sessions should use. Without it, a tutoring plan is a guess dressed as a syllabus.

What actually differs between the boards is less about content than about architecture. Cambridge papers and Pearson papers ask about the same physics and the same algebra, but they build questions differently, phrase stems differently and reward slightly different things in the extended responses. A student who has practised fifty Cambridge papers reads a Pearson stem a fraction wrong, spends longer deciding what is wanted, and runs short at the end of the paper. The content was never the problem.

Tiering is the other axis. Many Cambridge subjects are tiered Core and Extended; Pearson Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher. The lower tier caps the grade available, which makes it the most consequential fact in the whole plan and the one least often discussed openly at a parents' evening. Confirm it, and if there is doubt about whether the tier is right, raise it with the school while a change is still practical.

sections.heading: The six-mark question is where science grades are decided
paragraphs: In IGCSE science papers there is one question type that separates students who know the material from students whose grades show it: the extended response worth five or six marks. It asks for an explanation or an evaluation of a process, and it is marked by the presence of specific linked points rather than by the volume of correct information.

The typical answer from a well-taught student is a list. Every statement in it is true, several of them are relevant, and the mark comes out at about half. The reason is that the scheme awards marks for a chain - this happens, which causes this, which means this - and an unordered set of facts does not form a chain. The student is being penalised for structure, not for knowledge, and nobody has told them.

The fix is mechanical and fast. Identify the chain the question wants, write it in order, use connective language that makes the causation explicit, and stop. Three sentences that link properly outscore eight that do not. Students find this counterintuitive because it means writing less, and they need to see it marked against the real scheme two or three times before they believe it.

This is the highest-return thing to work on in Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610, and it transfers between all three. It is also almost never taught in a weekly tuition hour, because the hour defaults to content and the extended response is not content. Ask any prospective tutor how they would teach a six-mark explain question, and the answer will tell you a great deal.

sections.heading: How practical science is examined when nobody is at a bench
paragraphs: Parents considering online science tuition reasonably ask about practicals, and the honest answer is more reassuring than expected, because of how the boards assess practical skills. Depending on the centre's entry, practical ability is examined either through a practical examination or through an alternative-to-practical written paper. Either way the student is being tested on practical reasoning - method design, variable control, measurement precision, sources of error, reading apparatus diagrams, interpreting results - rather than on manual dexterity.

That reasoning is a written skill and it is taught well on paper. The alternative-to-practical paper in particular is a distinct discipline with its own recurring question types: identify the independent variable, explain why a particular control matters, state a source of error and how to reduce it, read a scale correctly, suggest an improvement. Students lose marks on it consistently and schools often cover it late, because laboratory time goes to the practical work itself.

What a school provides and a tutor cannot is the laboratory: the apparatus, the supervision and the experience of handling equipment. That belongs inside the school day and nothing bought outside replaces it. What a tutor adds is the written reasoning layer on top - which is, as it happens, where the examined marks are.

sections.heading: The English decision, and why it reaches further than the grade
paragraphs: English at IGCSE involves a choice that affects more than a single grade, and in this district it is frequently made by default rather than deliberately. English as a Second Language 0510 and English First Language 0500 are different qualifications with different papers, different demands and different consequences downstream, and a student who could succeed at either is sometimes entered for the one the school happens to run for their group.

On the First Language paper the central skill is writing about how a writer achieves an effect, not about what a passage says. Students arrive able to summarise fluently and lose marks because summary is not what is being rewarded. Directed writing adds a second demand: producing a specific text type for a specific audience, where the conventions carry marks independently of the quality of the prose. Both are technique, and both move within a handful of sessions once named.

On the English as a Second Language paper the marks sit in reading-comprehension precision and in following the controlled-writing rubric exactly. Fluent speakers underperform here surprisingly often, because fluency is not the thing being measured and an answer that reads well but ignores the rubric scores badly. Practising against the rubric rather than practising English is the whole of the fix.

The downstream point is worth knowing. MoE equivalency on the British track requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among the five. Receiving schools and universities set their own requirements and sometimes name a specific English qualification. Ask the receiving institution what it expects before the entry is made, not afterwards.
