sections.heading: Which subjects reward past papers and which still need content
paragraphs: There is a question families should ask before buying a weekly hour: is this subject's problem content or technique? The answer differs by subject and it changes what the hour should contain. Buying content teaching for a technique failure is the most common waste in this market, and buying past-paper drilling for a genuine content gap is the second.

Mathematics at Extended or Higher tier usually has both, and the proportions shift across the two years: content in Year 10, technique and timing in Year 11. The sciences are typically content-heavy in the first year and almost entirely technique in the second, because the extended response and the practical-skills paper dominate the recoverable marks. English is overwhelmingly technique at both stages - there is very little content to learn and a great deal of method. Economics and Business sit in between: a modest content base and then evaluation technique that decides the band.

The practical test is the marked script again. If the student is getting whole questions wrong because they do not recognise the topic, that is content. If they are getting partial marks on questions they clearly understand, that is technique, and no amount of re-teaching will move it. A tutor who cannot make that distinction in the first session will spend the term on the wrong side of it.

sections.heading: Coursework, controlled assessment and where a tutor stops
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than it once did and less than the IB Diploma, but where a component is assessed internally or completed as controlled work, the line between teaching and producing it is a line with consequences. The same line governs the Diploma internal assessments and the Extended Essay that many of these students will meet in two years.

What a tutor may do: explain what the assessment criteria reward, teach the technique the component requires, model an approach on an entirely different task, read the student's own draft and question reasoning that does not hold, and point out where a section fails to address what it is supposed to. What a tutor may not do: write, draft, rewrite, edit to completion or supply any part of it. IB Gram tutors do not produce assessed work, and we state it rather than leaving it implied, because this search result contains operations that sell completed assessed work outright.

The materials question belongs here too. We do not reproduce or supply Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. Those are published and owned by the boards; your child's school holds the current versions and the boards publish what is openly available. A tutor's work is to teach against a mark scheme and mark the student's own answers honestly against it. If a provider advertises a downloadable library of board material as a feature, ask who holds the copyright in it.

There is a practical as well as an ethical argument here. The hours that actually buy marks on an internally assessed component are hours spent on the student's own reasoning. A polished document shaped by somebody else teaches the student nothing and carries all the risk, and the risk sits with the child rather than with whoever was paid.

sections.heading: What the wrong code costs, and what the right one costs
paragraphs: Think about price as a function of match rather than of rate, because in this subject the cost of a mismatch dwarfs the difference between bands. A term of weekly sessions on the wrong board's papers costs whatever was paid plus a term of the two years available, and the second part is the expensive half. That is the risk the budget end of this market carries: not that the tutor is weak, but that nobody checked the code.

The published bands, for reference, each belonging to the provider that published it and read in October 2026. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts qualified online tuition at AED 150 to 300, in-home one-to-one including travel at AED 180 to 350, and specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level provision at AED 200 to 450 or more. TutorChase publishes AED 270. BartyED publishes AED 650. Home tutors are quoted up to AED 500 an hour including travel. None of those is an IB Gram price.

Where the bands genuinely matter is the type of job. A three-session block fixing the six-mark extended response needs a specialist who knows that scheme, and because it is short the hourly rate is a small part of the decision. A year of consolidating a Core-tier subject that is already stable needs competence rather than specialism and should be bought accordingly. Spreading the specialist band thinly across seven subjects is the standard way an IGCSE budget disappears without a grade moving.

Monthly comparison is cleaner. One Dubai provider publishes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, roughly AED 100 an hour. In-home monthly packages are advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits, roughly AED 200 to 225 for the same eight hours of teaching. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India, and sessions for Al Mankhool students run one-to-one over live video.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and the mandatory UAE subjects
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit, and a parent can check it directly. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the smart app, website and e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time. Because the permit is free, no part of a quoted rate is a permit fee, and operating without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so nobody should be quoting an amount.

The school side divides by emirate. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and publishes inspection reports on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs a different instrument again: a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, no regulator accreditation and no UAE office, and does not describe itself as approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Where a page in this search result does claim otherwise, ask it for the permit number.

Alongside the IGCSE timetable sits a block that is not optional. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA's requirements due from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 where the year begins in April. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises at least twenty-five minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs are required for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are strictly prohibited. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which limits what any tutor can legitimately offer in them.

process.title: Ask the school for the entry statement
process.description: One line, already in the school's records, naming the board, the four-digit or alphanumeric code, the tier and the practical route for each subject. Everything in a sensible plan follows from it, and without it the plan is a guess about which papers to practise.

process.title: Send one marked script with it
process.description: The most recent marked paper, even a bad one. It shows whether whole questions are being missed - a content gap - or partial marks are being dropped on questions the student clearly understood, which is technique and needs an entirely different hour.

process.title: Free trial lesson on the correct code
process.description: A full one-to-one session at no charge with a specialist on that exact code and tier, built around a question the student has already attempted. The output should be a named pattern rather than a general impression that things went well.

process.title: The plan follows the pattern
process.description: A named trap - the six-mark explain question, unwritten method, the alternative-to-practical paper, directed writing - is usually three to five sessions. Genuine content gaps need a term. We would rather sell the short thing that fixes it than the long thing that postpones it.

process.title: Papers, then review against school marks
process.description: In the final year the work is timed papers on the correct code, marked against the official scheme, with losses categorised each time. Progress is judged on school assessments and mocks, and if those are not moving the plan changes or the tutor does.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the code, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: 0580 and 4MA1 are different papers. 0625 and 4PH1 are different papers. 0607 is not 0580. We match on what the entry statement says, because a mismatch costs a term of the two years available and the term is the expensive part.

whyPoints.title: The extended response taught deliberately
whyPoints.description: In IGCSE science the six-mark explain question is where grades are decided, and it rewards a linked causal chain rather than a volume of correct facts. It transfers across all three sciences and it is almost never taught in a weekly content hour.

whyPoints.title: Practical skills treated as an examined paper
whyPoints.description: Variable control, sources of error, reading scales and suggesting improvements are written skills with recurring question types. The laboratory stays with the school; the examined reasoning layer is what an hour outside it can genuinely add.

whyPoints.title: Content and technique told apart
whyPoints.description: Whole questions missed is a content gap; partial marks dropped on understood questions is technique. The two need different hours, and buying the wrong one is the most common waste in this market. We make the call from a marked script in the first session.

whyPoints.title: Short blocks where short blocks are the answer
whyPoints.description: A named pattern is three to five sessions. We scope from the script, fix the pattern, and stop - rather than converting every problem into a term-long weekly commitment that is easier to sell and slower to work.

whyPoints.title: Nothing claimed that cannot be evidenced
whyPoints.description: No regulator approval, no UAE office, no grade guarantees, no board documents supplied, and every dirham figure attributed to the provider that published it with the month it was read. Ask any provider claiming more to show the paperwork.

faqs.question: Why does the syllabus code matter more than finding someone nearby in Al Mankhool?
faqs.answer: Because the code decides which papers your child sits. Cambridge Mathematics is 0580, Cambridge International Mathematics is 0607 and Pearson Mathematics A is 4MA1 - three different courses with different question architecture and different mark schemes. In a district this dense, plenty of tutors are nearby; the one who helps is the one working from the right paper set. A mismatch is invisible for about six weeks because the content overlaps, then a mock exposes it. Ask the school for the entry statement before you pay for anything.

faqs.question: My child knows the science but only gets half marks on the long questions. What is happening?
faqs.answer: They are writing a list where the scheme wants a chain. A six-mark extended response is marked by the presence of specific linked points - this happens, which causes this, which means this - so eight true but unordered statements score about half, while three properly connected sentences score well. Students find it counterintuitive because the fix means writing less. They need to see it marked against the real scheme two or three times before they believe it, and then it transfers across Physics, Chemistry and Biology.

faqs.question: How can an online tutor help with science practicals?
faqs.answer: By teaching the part that is actually examined. Depending on the centre's entry, practical ability is assessed through a practical examination or through an alternative-to-practical written paper, and both test practical reasoning - variable control, measurement precision, sources of error, reading apparatus diagrams, suggesting improvements - rather than manual dexterity. That is a written skill with recurring question types, and it is taught well on paper. The laboratory, the apparatus and the supervision stay with the school, where they belong and where they are already paid for.

faqs.question: Should my child be entered for English First Language or English as a Second Language?
faqs.answer: Ask the receiving school or university what it expects before the entry is made, because the two are different qualifications with different downstream consequences and the decision is often taken by default. First Language 0500 rewards analysing how a writer creates an effect, plus directed writing in a specified text type. English as a Second Language 0510 rewards precise comprehension and following the controlled-writing rubric exactly, and is tiered Core and Extended. Either can count among the five subjects MoE equivalency recognises on the British track.

faqs.question: Is my child's problem content or exam technique?
faqs.answer: A marked script answers it in minutes. If whole questions are being missed because the topic is not recognised, that is content and needs teaching. If partial marks are being dropped on questions the student clearly understood, that is technique and no amount of re-teaching will move it. Across subjects the balance differs: English is almost entirely technique, Biology is content-heavy in the first year and technique in the second, mathematics shifts from content in Year 10 to timing and method in Year 11.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we actually buy support in?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families start with. Spreading a budget across seven subjects is the standard way to spend it without moving a single grade, because nothing receives enough hours to change. Work backwards from what the next stage names: MoE equivalency on the British track counts five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, and receiving schools state their own requirements in named subjects. Fund those properly and let the school's own provision carry what is already stable.

faqs.question: Can the Core tier hold my child's grade down no matter what we spend?
faqs.answer: Yes, which makes the tier the most consequential fact in the plan. Many Cambridge subjects are tiered Core and Extended; Pearson Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher. The lower tier caps the grade available, so hours spent reaching for a grade the tier cannot award are wasted hours. One or two diagnostic sessions on past papers from each tier will show which one the student is genuinely working at, and the conversation with the school is free to have while a change is still practical.

faqs.question: What is the alternative-to-practical paper and how do we prepare for it?
faqs.answer: A written paper testing practical reasoning where a centre has not entered candidates for the practical examination route. It has recurring question types: identify the independent, dependent and controlled variables; explain why a particular control protects the conclusion; name a specific source of error and its effect; propose a concrete method or apparatus change; read a scale with appropriate precision; suggest an improvement addressing a named limitation. Each has a right shape of answer, and schools often cover it late because laboratory time goes to the practical work itself.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child sit, and can a bad result be retaken?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. So a subject that goes wrong in the summer can usually be retaken in the autumn, with a second entry fee and a short concentrated block of work. Decide early, because entry deadlines sit months ahead of the exams. Note the results gap too: Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

faqs.question: Should we be revising toward a February or March exam window?
faqs.answer: No. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only - UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Cambridge's Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October, which is a different thing and is sometimes confused with the IGCSE series in locally written tutoring material. If any plan has your child in Al Mankhool working toward a February or March examination, it is using the wrong country's calendar, and that is worth treating as a signal about the rest of its detail.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge mention six administrative zones?
faqs.answer: Because the timetable differs between them. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The practical instruction for a family here is to take dates from the school's entry statement and the board's live timetable rather than from a PDF found through a search engine, and to link the official timetable rather than trusting a restated date.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE specialist cost around Al Mankhool and Bur Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates start at AED 33 to 65 an hour - Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 - which typically buys a university student. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts qualified online tuition at AED 150 to 300, in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 including travel, and specialist provision at AED 200 to 450 or more. TutorChase publishes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650. All read October 2026, all belonging to the provider named rather than to us.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our building in Al Mankhool?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Sessions for Al Mankhool students run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For code-matched work that is the point rather than a compromise: the pool becomes every specialist on your child's exact syllabus and tier rather than the few qualified people prepared to drive into this district at a fixed hour, and marked scripts sit on a shared screen both people can annotate.

faqs.question: Will you give us past papers and mark schemes to work from?
faqs.answer: No, and no provider should. Those documents are published and owned by Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and reproducing or redistributing them is copyright infringement. Your child's school holds the current versions and the boards publish what is openly available. A tutor's job is to teach against a mark scheme, show exactly how marks are allocated in a specific question, and mark the student's own written answers honestly against it. If a provider advertises a downloadable library of board material as a feature, ask who holds the copyright.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and should it affect the price?
faqs.answer: They need one and it should not affect the price. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Since it costs the tutor nothing, no part of any quoted rate is a permit fee being recovered. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: What if nobody is available on our exact code and tier?

intro.heading: The same request means different things in September and in March
paragraphs: A parent in Al Mizhar typing "IGCSE tutor near me" in late September is asking a different question from one typing it in March, even though the words are identical. In September there is a whole year, the tier is still open, content can be repaired and a habit can be built. In March the entry is submitted, the tier is fixed, the mocks have happened and the only work left is converting what the student already understands into marks they are not currently collecting.

Almost nobody writing about tutoring in this market acknowledges that, which is why so many families buy the wrong thing at the wrong time. A weekly general-subject hour started in April is too slow to reach a June paper. An eight-week intensive bought in October wastes the one year of the course that has genuine slack in it. The purchase should follow the calendar, and the calendar in Dubai has its own shape.

There is a second calendar effect that is specific to searching locally. Availability in these villa communities is seasonal. After mocks, every competent local tutor's evening slots are taken, and the subset willing to drive out past Mirdif to Al Mizhar for one hour is smaller again. In the summer the same people have space. A family searching in the busiest fortnight of the year by distance is searching the thinnest possible market, which is a large part of why "near me" returns disappointing results in February and reasonable ones in July.

IB Gram's delivery removes the travel half of that problem. Lessons for Al Mizhar families are one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service offered only in India, so nobody is scheduling a drive out past Mirdif at four in the afternoon. The scarcity that remains is real and seasonal, and we will tell you about it rather than pretend otherwise.

One more calendar fact deserves saying early, because it is the one that costs families most. The deadline that decides a grade ceiling is not an examination date at all. It is the entry, submitted by the school months ahead of the first paper, and it fixes both the tier and the series. A parent who has the tier conversation in Year 10 is having a conversation with options in it; a parent who raises it in February is being told, politely, that the decision was made in the autumn. Nobody sends a reminder about this.

What follows is the year, month by month, with what each part of it can deliver. Then the three diagnostics a school year hands a parent, which most never ask for. Then the entry and tier conversation and when it has to happen. Then tutoring cost set against the actual cost of schooling in Dubai, which is a comparison nobody publishes. And then the honesty boundary, which does not move whatever the month is.

programmes.name: Year 9: the year before the clock starts
programmes.description: Nothing here is examined for a certificate, which makes it the cheapest possible place to act. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests sit in March, May and October and give schools an external read on a cohort. The work that pays is fluency: index laws, fractions without a calculator, rearranging a formula, and writing a precise scientific explanation.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Al Mizhar from Mirdif and Al Warqa use Year 9 outcomes to stream Year 10 into Core and Extended routes. A Core placement quietly closes the route to A Level in that subject two years before university comes up, so this is the term to ask which tier your child is heading for and on what evidence.

programmes.name: Year 10: the only year with slack
programmes.description: The examined course begins, and this is the single year in which content can be repaired properly rather than patched. Examination technique can be built as a habit over months instead of drilled in a panic, and the tier decision is still genuinely open. A weekly hour started here is worth considerably more than the same hour started in the spring of Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Mizhar families this is also the year to settle when a lesson can happen, because the bus routes from Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais run long and a slot improvised in Year 11 rarely survives. Fix the hour in Year 10 and it still works in the examination year.

programmes.name: Year 11: counted in weeks
programmes.description: Every decision becomes a calendar decision. Entry deadlines fall months before the papers and fix the tier and the series. Mocks arrive in the term before the live series and are the best diagnostic a family will get all year. From the mock onwards the work is almost entirely past papers marked against the published scheme, with specific errors named and tested.

That is why the choice of which subject receives the tutoring hours has to be deliberate rather than reactive.

programmes.name: After results: resit or move on
programmes.description: A June result that misses a sixth-form requirement opens a short window. The November series is the resit route, entry runs through a centre on the board's own deadline, and the work is technique and targeted content because the syllabus was covered once already. The alternative is adjusting the post-16 plan, which is sometimes the better answer.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-mizhar.subjectsIntro: Which subject to fund changes with the month, because subjects respond to a short window at very different speeds. These are the ones Al Mizhar families ask about.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The fastest-responding subject on the timetable at any time of year, because most losses are procedural: sign errors, method not written down, multi-step questions abandoned. In Year 10 the same hour also closes genuine content gaps, which is why starting early compounds here more than anywhere.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Two jobs on different clocks. Circuits is conceptual and needs weeks, so it belongs in Year 10 or early Year 11. The practical or alternative-to-practical component is a written skill learned from past questions in days, which makes it the right choice late.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic is pure repetition and therefore fits any window, including a short one. Equilibrium reasoning does not compress and belongs earlier in the course, which is a good example of why the month matters as much as the subject.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Responds least well to a late window, because its volume tempts a thin pass over everything and that is the wrong work in April. Early in the course the right work is precise terminology on fewer topics; late, it is extended-response structure only.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Directed writing has finite task types and responds well at any point in the year, because the marks go to answering the specific brief with the right form, audience and register. Reading comprehension technique improves quickly with marked practice.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A separate qualification from First Language with its own structure and a speaking component. The speaking element is the single most under-rehearsed thing on many timetables and the easiest to improve in a fortnight, which makes it a good late purchase.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the evaluation marks at the end of structured questions are both finite and quick to drill, so this subject stays available to a short window. A correctly labelled diagram with the shift in the right direction earns marks no prose can replace.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus rather than recall of theory, which is a habit rather than a body of content. Eight weeks of marked practice forcing every point back to the case material is well spent even late in Year 11.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 / 0984)
subjects.description: Data representation marks on the theory paper are mechanical and recoverable in days. The algorithm paper demands pseudocode in the board's own conventions, which fluent Python coders still lose marks on, and which is learnable quickly.

subjects.name: ICT (Cambridge 0417)
subjects.description: Practical papers on specific software tasks under timed conditions, where the gap is procedural speed rather than understanding. One of the best fits for a short intensive block, because a student who has done each task six times finishes in time.

subjects.name: Examination technique across the timetable
subjects.description: Reading the mark allocation, showing method so partial credit survives, answering the command term, and abandoning a question rather than sinking ten minutes in it. The best purchase available in the final two terms, because it lifts marks in every subject at once.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside IGCSE in every Dubai private school. KHDA states that using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited, so tutoring follows the school's own approved material.

sections.heading: The Dubai academic year, month by month
paragraphs: A Dubai school year has a shape, and tutoring that ignores it loses weeks nobody budgeted for. The year opens in the autumn with a settling period, runs through a first assessment round, breaks for winter, picks up with the heaviest teaching term, meets mocks, and then runs into the examination window with Ramadan somewhere in the mix depending on the year.

The table below is the version we plan from. It is not a school calendar, because every school's dates differ and yours will tell you its own; it is a map of what each part of the year can realistically deliver. Read it with the actual month in mind rather than with a vague sense of there being time, because the gap between those two is where terms disappear.

Two periods are worth calling out as opportunities rather than obstacles. The summer between Years 10 and 11 is the single best-value window in the cycle: availability is at its widest, nothing competes for an evening, and the work can be properly remedial. The winter break is the second, particularly for a Year 11 student who can spend three or four concentrated sessions on one paper rather than keeping a weekly slot limping along while the family travels.

One period is worth avoiding as a starting point. The fortnight after mocks is when every household in this cluster reaches the same conclusion at the same time, and it is the worst moment to begin a search by distance. If you are reading this in that fortnight, the useful move is to book quickly and to widen the search beyond who will drive out past Mirdif.

sections.heading: The three diagnostics a school year gives you, free
paragraphs: Most parents judge a child's progress from a report, which is the least informative document the school produces. A report compresses a term into a grade and a sentence. What is actually useful is marked work, and a school year hands a family three good opportunities to get it, at no cost.

The first is the autumn assessment round. Ask not for the grade but for the marked paper, and look at where the marks went rather than how many there were. The second is any mid-year internal examination, which is closer to the real thing in format and therefore more revealing about timing and technique. The third is the mock, which is the best single diagnostic a family will ever get and which an alarming number of households never see the actual paper from.

What to look for requires no subject knowledge. Are the marks lost in the long questions or the short ones? Is the method written down? Are the last two questions unattempted, which is a timing problem rather than a knowledge one? Does the same type of error appear three times? Those four questions identify the work to be done more accurately than any teacher comment, and they take ten minutes at the kitchen table.

Also worth asking for: the school's own view of which tier your child should be entered at, with the evidence behind it. That conversation has a deadline, because the entry fixes the tier and falls months before the first paper. Schools will usually discuss it willingly and rarely raise it unprompted.

sections.heading: Entry, tier and the series: the dates that cannot be moved
paragraphs: Entry is the deadline that matters and the one families discover late. A school submits entries months before the first paper, and that submission fixes both the tier and the series. After it, moving tier for that series is difficult and often impossible, whatever is bought afterwards.

The series question has a clear answer. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in those two series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, which matters because plans built around a March window have reached UAE parents elsewhere, and a date a family acts on being wrong for their country is a genuine cost. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

For dated worked examples, Pearson's published record is checkable. The Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are past dates, which is why they are safe to use as a shape rather than as a promise. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so open the live official timetable rather than relying on any restated date, this page included.

The practical sequence for a parent is short. Get the statement of entry, which names the board, code, tier and series for every subject. Open the board's live timetable. Count the weeks, subtracting Ramadan, the school break and any trip already booked. Then decide what to buy against that number.

sections.heading: Does tutoring get more expensive closer to the exams?
paragraphs: Parents ask this, and the honest answer has two parts. Published hourly rates do not move much with the calendar. What moves sharply is availability, and availability near a deadline behaves like a price: the people still free in the fortnight after mocks are not usually the people you would have chosen in October.

The published Dubai bands, each read on the provider's own page, are these. EdFlik advertises budget online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya's published panel starts lower again. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Named IGCSE specialists run roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai table reaching the top of that band. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500, with the travel inside it.

What does change late in the year is the shape of the spend rather than the rate. A weekly hour costs what it costs; an intensive of three sessions a week for eight weeks costs three times as much per week, which is where families feel the increase. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour tutoring run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or above for exam-year specialist support, and that last band is the one most households meet in Year 11.

So the real saving is temporal, not commercial. The same money spent in Year 10, or in the summer between the two years, buys remedial work at ordinary intensity instead of rescue work at three sessions a week. None of these figures is an IB Gram rate and we publish no rate card on these pages; the number for your child comes out of the free trial and the conversation after it.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost set against what schooling in Dubai actually costs
paragraphs: Nobody in this market puts tutoring spend in context, so here is the context. Dubai's private school sector had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the UK curriculum accounting for thirty-seven per cent of enrolment, Indian twenty-six, US fourteen and the International Baccalaureate seven.

On fees, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion out of AED 2.5 billion in total. That is a useful anchor for a family budgeting tutoring, because it means the school line in the household budget is not rising this year even if the tutoring line is.

Capacity is also expanding. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four following a UK curriculum and three the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. For a family in these eastern communities that matters mostly as context for school choice rather than for tutoring, but it does mean the market a parent is reading about this year is not the market of three years ago.

Set against those numbers, the tutoring decision looks different. A weekly mid-tier hour at AED 600 to 1,200 a month is a real commitment and a small fraction of what a Dubai private education costs over two years, and the version of it bought in Year 10 is substantially cheaper than the version bought in the spring of Year 11. Tutoring is also not required for Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and anybody implying otherwise is making a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process.

sections.heading: Ramadan, breaks and travel inside a two-year plan
paragraphs: Over two years a family in these communities will lose weeks to Ramadan, to school breaks and to travel, and the only question is whether those weeks were planned or merely lost. Planned, they cost nothing and sometimes gain something. Unplanned, they are the difference between seventy sessions across the Diploma-length run of an IGCSE course and fifty.

During Ramadan school days are shortened and household routines move towards the evening, so the usual slot shifts to after iftar. Because no tutor is travelling anywhere, that change costs a message rather than a renegotiation. Families who agree it before Ramadan begins keep continuity through it; families who improvise typically lose three or four weeks and restart from a worse position in a busier term.

School breaks are an asset if used deliberately. A winter or spring week with no homework competing is the best place in the year for three or four concentrated sessions on one paper, and for a Year 11 student that can be the most productive stretch of the term. What wastes a break is keeping a weekly slot limping along while the family is away.

Travel is a standing feature out here. Online lessons follow a student to another time zone if the slot is adjusted, which no arrangement tied to a villa address can do. Send the dates in advance and sessions move rather than vanish. The thing to avoid is letting a trip become a four-week gap, because in a cumulative subject the restart costs more than the sessions missed.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do, in any month
paragraphs: The honesty boundary does not move with the calendar, and it is tested hardest when a deadline is close, which is why it belongs on a page about timing.

A tutor may teach the method, work a comparable example, question a student about their own attempt and point out where the reasoning does not hold. A tutor may not write, complete, redo or edit to completion any piece of work the student submits. The practical test requires no subject knowledge: feedback that arrives as questions your child must go and answer is correct, feedback that arrives as sentences they could copy in is not.

It is worth knowing what is on sale in this search result. One page in the researched competitor set advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. That is an academic-integrity breach and an examination malpractice trigger, and the student carries it through appeals, applications and sometimes a whole qualification while the seller carries none of it. Any offer of that kind should end the conversation.

We also decline to reproduce or supply board material. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson and reach you through them or through the school. That matters practically as well as legally, because official material is current while a folder circulating in a school parent group is frequently from a superseded specification and will send a student to question styles that no longer appear.

sections.heading: Starting, whatever month you are reading this in
paragraphs: Send four things: the syllabus code and tier from the statement of entry, the series your child is entered for, a photograph of the most recent marked paper, and the time your child is realistically through the door on a bad traffic afternoon. With those, the right purchase for the month you are in is a single conversation rather than a guess.

The free trial lesson runs about forty minutes on a past question from your child's own code, with your child working and the tutor teaching. Afterwards you receive a written read on the biggest recurring loss and the weeks it implies, which is also the honest answer to whether the window you have is long enough for what you want.

Availability is seasonal and we will tell you where you are in that cycle. In the summer and the autumn, most requests are matched quickly. In the fortnight after mocks, late-afternoon and early-evening Gulf Standard Time slots fill first, weekend mornings next, and a resit specialist in an unusual subject at short notice may genuinely not exist. We give a realistic match time rather than filling an hour with a generalist.

Notice what the list above asks for and what it does not. A photograph of the marked paper, yes - that is the diagnostic. A photograph of your child, no, and we will not ask for one. Matching an Al Mizhar family needs six things and stops there: board, code, tier, series, the school if you want its sequence followed, and a contact for scheduling. We do not need a full grade history across every subject, a previous tutor's reports, or anything about a sibling. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs the data we do hold, and the privacy link on this page sets out what is kept, for how long, and how to have it removed.

process.title: Work out which month you are actually in
process.description: Autumn with a year left, spring with a term, or the fortnight after mocks. The month decides whether you are buying content repair, a sustained habit, or technique and triage, and buying the wrong one for the month is the commonest waste in this market.

process.title: Get the statement of entry and the live timetable
process.description: The statement names the board, code, tier and series. The board's own site carries the live timetable. UAE candidates sit June and November, and the Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only.

process.title: Ask for the marked paper, not the grade
process.description: A school year gives three good diagnostics: the autumn assessment, the mid-year internal and the mock. Ask for the paper each time. Ten minutes at the kitchen table identifies the work more accurately than any report comment.

process.title: Count the weeks with the deductions
process.description: From today to the paper, minus Ramadan, minus the school break, minus the trip already booked. Families routinely believe they have twelve weeks and discover they have seven, which is how an eight-week plan gets attempted in five.

process.title: Set a slot the whole year can hold
process.description: Al Mizhar students on Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais routes arrive home late, so choose the hour that works on the worst afternoon. A slot fixed in Year 10 still works in Year 11; one improvised in Year 11 usually does not.

process.title: Take the free trial, then review on the right cycle
process.description: Forty minutes on a past question from the right code. Review at six lessons in a weekly arrangement, and weekly in an intensive one, because in an eight-week plan there is no time to discover in week six that the approach was wrong.

whyPoints.title: The advice changes with the month
whyPoints.description: A weekly general hour started in April cannot reach a June paper, and an eight-week intensive bought in October wastes the only year with slack in it. We ask what month you are in before recommending a shape, because the calendar decides more than the subject does.

whyPoints.title: We name the seasonal availability problem
whyPoints.description: Local supply in these villa communities collapses in the fortnight after mocks and reopens over the summer. That is why a search by distance disappoints in February and works in July, and we will tell you where in the cycle you are rather than imply constant capacity.

whyPoints.title: The right series, stated plainly
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit June and November. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only, and plans built around a March window have reached UAE parents elsewhere. We also point you at your centre's administrative zone, because Cambridge warns the wrong zone timetable is the family's risk.

whyPoints.title: Cost put in real context
whyPoints.description: Dubai had 387,441 private school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, and KHDA confirmed no fee increase for 2026-27 under a package worth AED 1.5 billion. Set against that, the saving available from acting a year earlier is larger than any saving available from haggling over an hourly rate.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure is attributed
whyPoints.description: Each rate here was read on the provider's own public page and credited to them, and none is an IB Gram price. Three of the best-ranking pages on these searches publish no price at all, and a number you can go and check is worth more than a reassurance.

whyPoints.title: No false urgency about regulation
whyPoints.description: Tutoring is not required for Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. We explain what the authorities actually require and link to their own pages, and IB Gram holds no approval or licence from KHDA, the Ministry of Education or the MoHRE.

faqs.question: Is it harder to find a tutor near Al Mizhar at certain times of year?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the swing is large. In the fortnight after mocks every household in this cluster reaches the same conclusion at once, local evening slots fill, and the subset of tutors willing to drive out past Mirdif for a single hour is smaller again. Over the summer the same people have space. That seasonality is most of the reason a search by distance disappoints in February and works in July, and it is a reason to widen the search beyond who can reach your villa.

faqs.question: When in the two-year course is tutoring money best spent?
faqs.answer: Year 10, and the summer between Years 10 and 11. Year 10 is the only year with genuine slack, so content can be repaired properly rather than patched, technique becomes a habit over months, and the tier conversation happens with evidence while it is still open. The summer is the best-value window in the whole cycle: availability is at its widest, nothing competes for the evening, and the work can be remedial. The same money spent in the spring of Year 11 buys triage instead.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Dubai rise closer to the exams?
faqs.answer: The published rates do not move much; what changes is availability and the number of sessions a week you need. A weekly hour costs the same in October and in April, but an intensive of three sessions a week costs three times as much per week, which is where families feel the increase. Bestimate's Dubai monthly estimates run AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-tier weekly tutoring and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or above for exam-year specialist support. The saving is temporal rather than commercial.

faqs.question: What should we do with the summer between Years 10 and 11?
faqs.answer: Buy six to ten sessions on the weakest topic in the weakest subject and finish before term starts. It is the only part of the cycle where tutoring can be genuinely remedial without competing against homework, assessments or fatigue from a long bus route. Local availability is at its widest, so the choice of tutor is real rather than whoever is left. For a student who struggled in Year 10, this fortnight changes how the examination year begins more than any equivalent spend later does.

faqs.question: What are the three diagnostics a school year gives us?
faqs.answer: The autumn assessment round, the mid-year internal examination and the mock, and in each case the useful thing is the marked paper rather than the grade. Ask whether marks are lost in long or short questions, whether the method is written down, whether the last two questions were unattempted, which is a timing problem, and whether the same error appears three times. Those four questions take ten minutes at a kitchen table and identify the work more accurately than any report comment does.

faqs.question: Why does the entry deadline matter more than the exam date?
faqs.answer: Because the entry fixes the tier and the series, and it is submitted months before the first paper. A family who discovers in February that their child is entered at Core or Foundation has discovered it too late for that series, and the lower tier caps the available grade, which can close the route to A Level in the same subject. The tier recommendation conversation belongs in Year 10 and again early in Year 11, with marked mock papers as the evidence rather than a report comment.

faqs.question: Which series will my child sit, and where do I check the dates?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, and the statement of entry names which. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only, so ignore any plan built around a March window. For dated shape, Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and November 2025 results on 22 January 2026. Always open the board's live timetable, because provisional versions are revised.

faqs.question: Which subjects respond well to a late start and which do not?
faqs.answer: Mathematics responds best at any point, because most of its losses are procedural: sign errors, method not written down, multi-step questions abandoned. ICT is next, since its practical papers are a speed problem. Economics and Business Studies do well late because diagram accuracy and application to stimulus are finite habits. Biology responds worst late, because its volume tempts a thin pass over everything and the right late work there is extended-response structure on fewer topics, not more coverage.

faqs.question: How does the Ramadan period affect a two-year tutoring plan?
faqs.answer: It costs weeks if it is not planned and nothing if it is. School days are shortened and household routines move towards the evening, so the usual slot shifts to after iftar; because no tutor is travelling anywhere, moving it is a message rather than a renegotiation. Families who agree the shift before Ramadan begins keep their continuity. Families who improvise typically lose three or four weeks and then restart from a worse position in a busier term, which is the expensive version.

faqs.question: Is a school break a good time for tutoring or a waste of money?
faqs.answer: A good time, if it is used as a block rather than as a limping weekly slot. A winter or spring week with no homework competing is the best place in the year for three or four concentrated sessions on a single paper, and for a Year 11 student it can be the most productive stretch of the term. What wastes it is keeping a weekly hour alive while the family is travelling. Decide before the break whether it is a block or a pause, and either is fine once chosen.

faqs.question: How much of our household budget should tutoring be?
faqs.answer: That is yours to judge, and here is the context nobody publishes. Dubai had 387,441 private school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for 2026-27 under an incentives package worth AED 1.5 billion of AED 2.5 billion in total. Against a two-year school bill, a mid-tier weekly hour at AED 600 to 1,200 a month is a real but modest line, and the version bought in Year 10 is cheaper than the version bought in Year 11.

faqs.question: Is tutoring necessary for Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: No, and anybody implying otherwise is making a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Equivalency is a process the ministry runs. Verify every requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority rather than from a tutoring page.

faqs.question: We missed the mock. Is the plan still workable?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the diagnosis has to come from somewhere else, and that costs a session. Ask the school for the most recent marked class tests and for the subject teacher's written read on where marks are being lost. Failing that, the first tutoring session becomes the diagnostic: a past question under timed conditions, marked against the published scheme, with the recurring errors named. It is a reasonable use of an hour and it is still cheaper than guessing for six weeks about what the problem is.

faqs.question: Can a tutor finish coursework if the deadline is days away?
faqs.answer: No, and the date makes no difference to that. A tutor may teach the method, work a comparable example, question your child about their own attempt and point out where the reasoning does not hold. A tutor may not write, complete, redo or edit to completion anything your child submits. One page in this search result sells completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price, which is an examination malpractice trigger, and the student carries it through appeals and applications while the seller carries nothing at all.

faqs.question: What should we send, and does the month change that?
faqs.answer: The same four things in any month: the syllabus code and tier from the statement of entry, the series your child is entered for, a photograph of the most recent marked paper, and the time your child is realistically through the door on a bad traffic afternoon. What the month changes is the recommendation that comes back, not the information needed to make it. We do not need a photograph of your child or a full grade history; UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs what is held.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-mizhar.closingHeading: Ask what month it is before you ask what it costs
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-mizhar.closingBody: The useful question for an Al Mizhar family is not which tutor is nearest but where in the year you are standing. Send us the code, the series, a marked paper and the time your child gets home, and take the free trial lesson. We will tell you what this month can realistically deliver.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-muteena.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE subjects to Dubai students over live video. The list is organised by subject and board rather than by location, because location is the one variable this page argues you can stop optimising for.

intro.heading: Why widening the radius does not widen the shortlist
paragraphs: A near-me search behaves as if tutoring supply were distributed like supermarkets. It is not. Tutors cluster where demand clusters and where tutors themselves live, which in Dubai means the newer western communities rather than the older northern grid. An Al Muteena parent who widens the search to Hor Al Anz gets largely the same names, widens again to Deira and gets tuition centres rather than individuals, and widens again to Karama and Al Qusais and gets a longer list of people whose commute has become the deciding constraint on when they can teach.

This is not a reason to accept worse. It is a reason to change the variable being optimised. The things that actually predict whether tutoring moves an IGCSE grade are specific: does the tutor teach the student's exact board and tier, do they mark against the published scheme, will they take a session at the hour the student is genuinely free, and can the family tell within three weeks whether it is working. None of those four correlate with distance in any useful way.

There is a second reason the radius question misleads. Sixty per cent of what a parent is buying in the lowest-cost local arrangements is not teaching at all. In-home rates include travel, group sessions at a centre include room and overhead, and an individual who drives to three districts an evening is pricing the car. The published Dubai gap between in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 an hour and comparable online work at AED 150 to 300 is almost entirely that.

The third reason is practical and specific to this part of Dubai. Students in Al Muteena attend schools across the Deira grid and south into Al Garhoud and Bur Dubai, and the school bus decides when the day ends. A tutor who has to travel can offer a window; a tutor on video can start when the student walks in. Over a full exam term that difference is a dozen sessions that happened rather than were rearranged.

So the comparison in this page is deliberate. It sets Al Muteena against its neighbours on local school stock, arrival times, centre availability and tutor supply, and finds that the sensible answer is identical in each. Then it does the more useful work: comparing provider models, pricing the travel premium, setting out what the MoHRE permit means, and giving six questions a parent can ask before paying anybody anything.

One point to hold throughout. Nothing here argues that in-home tutoring is bad. It argues that it is a format with a published price, a real benefit for some students and a real cost in hours, and that a family should choose it knowing the trade rather than by default because the search box asked where they live.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher

subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or untiered Pearson

subjects.description: Generates steady demand around moles, ionic equations and organic naming. Families usually arrive after a mock where a calculation chain collapsed, which is almost always traceable to one unbalanced equation earlier in the question.

subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or untiered Pearson
subjects.description: Deceptive because it looks learnable from notes. The requests that arrive tend to be from students with strong recall and middling marks, where the gap is command-term discipline rather than knowledge.

subjects.name: English, first and second language
subjects.description: Heavy demand in this district, where many students are academically strong but not first-language English speakers. The placement question between the two qualifications is often more consequential than any amount of tutoring within one of them.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Case-study papers where marks follow application to the firm or economy in the stem. Popular subject choices in Dubai and a common source of plateau, because definitions learned thoroughly do not earn application marks.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Growing demand, often from students who code competently and lose marks on written theory papers and on the precise terminology the scheme requires. A short technique block usually does more than further programming practice.

subjects.name: Arabic as a second language
subjects.description: Requested alongside IGCSE subjects because Dubai schools must deliver Arabic regardless of curriculum. Students placed into a stream above their level carry that gap for years, and it is worth addressing separately from the examined subjects.

subjects.description: Smaller cohorts, which is exactly where a local near-me search fails hardest: a district may contain nobody teaching the subject while an online pool contains several people teaching it weekly.

sections.heading: Al Muteena against Hor Al Anz, Deira, Karama and Al Qusais
paragraphs: Put the five districts side by side on the variables that actually differ and the pattern is immediate. Local school stock differs: Deira has the most, Al Garhoud the strongest international provision, Al Muteena and Hor Al Anz very little of their own. Arrival times differ by up to ninety minutes depending on whether a student attends locally or is bussed south. Tuition centre density differs sharply, with Deira and Karama carrying the heaviest concentration in the city.

What does not differ is the pool of individual subject specialists resident in the district. Dubai's tutoring supply is concentrated where tutors live and where demand is wealthiest, which is the newer western communities. An Al Muteena family who widens its search to Hor Al Anz is searching the same market. Widening to Deira or Karama substitutes centres for individuals, which is a change of product rather than a longer list.

That makes the comparison useful in an unexpected way. If the answer is the same from every address in this cluster, the family can stop spending evenings on the geography question and spend them on the questions that do discriminate: board and tier, marking practice, availability at the right hour, and whether there is a way to tell in three weeks whether it is working. Those are answerable by asking, and the answers vary enormously between providers.

The one genuine local variable worth respecting is the tuition centre option. For a student who needs structure and company more than individual diagnosis, a Deira or Karama centre at a lower hourly rate can be the right call, and a family nearby can actually use it. That is a real choice this page is not arguing against. It is a different product, priced differently, with different things it can and cannot do.

sections.heading: The travel arithmetic, priced honestly
paragraphs: The published Dubai in-home band is AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, from Bestimate's rate work at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Comparable qualified subject tutors working online are published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Monthly packages show the same shape: around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions.

Read the second of those pairs carefully, because it is the most instructive number on the page. Four two-hour in-home sessions is eight contact hours a month. Eight online sessions at an hour each is also eight contact hours. The in-home figure is roughly double for the same hours, and the difference is a car in Dubai traffic between four and seven in the afternoon.

The travel also costs the student something that does not appear in any price list. A tutor crossing the city can usually offer one window per evening, and if the school bus is late or a mock runs long, the session is lost rather than moved. Over a twelve-week exam term a family that loses one session a fortnight to logistics has lost six hours, which at specialist rates is a significant sum spent on nothing.

What the premium does buy is real for some students: a person in the room, a parent able to overhear, and a younger child who will not settle at a screen alone. Those are legitimate reasons to pay it, and a family choosing in-home for them is making a reasonable decision. The unreasonable version is paying it by default because the search box asked for a location, without ever seeing what the same budget buys in specialist hours online.

sections.heading: Provider models compared, with their own published prices
paragraphs: Every tutoring provider compares itself favourably with an unnamed competitor. A more useful comparison is between models, because the model determines what the arrangement can and cannot do regardless of who is running it. There are six in this market: the tuition centre with premises, the agency that matches and manages tutors, the international marketplace, the independent freelance tutor, the school's own after-hours support, and the online platform.

A tuition centre offers structure, supervision and a lower hourly rate because the cost is shared across a group. It cannot easily diagnose one student's specific mark losses, because the session is paced for the room. An agency offers vetting and a replacement if the match fails, at a higher rate that covers the management. A marketplace offers the widest choice and the least mediation, so the parent does the vetting themselves. A freelance tutor is often the best value and the hardest to replace if it goes wrong mid-term.

School-run support has an advantage nothing else can match, which is that the teacher knows the student's own assessment timeline, and a limitation worth knowing about. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported and check the current policy, but do not go looking for your child's own teacher privately.

The online platform model, which is what IB Gram runs in the UAE, trades physical presence for selection. The pool is not limited by who will travel, so a student needing one specific board at one specific tier gets a specialist rather than a generalist. The honest limitation is that a student who will not work without someone in the room is not fixed by the format, and a family in that position should know it before buying.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is the question almost no competitor page answers and every parent is entitled to ask. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any figure quoted at you is unverified.

Eligibility is broad rather than narrow, which is why the permit is a reasonable thing to expect rather than an obstacle. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and the application runs through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system.

A separate thing entirely is a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai, which needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. That process requires initial approval first, allows a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and requires annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. This is the specific permit that the loose phrase KHDA approved refers to, and it applies to institutes with premises rather than to individual tutors or online platforms.

IB Gram holds no such permit and makes no accreditation claim of any kind, from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. What a parent can reasonably do is ask an individual tutor whether they hold the MoHRE permit, ask a centre to show its KHDA permit number, and treat a provider that describes itself as approved without naming the permit as having answered the question.

sections.heading: Six questions that discriminate between tutors, and one that does not
paragraphs: Location does not discriminate between tutors in this market. These six questions do, and every one of them can be asked in a message before any money changes hands. First: which board and tier is my child entered for, and have you taught that exact syllabus this year? A tutor who answers with the code has demonstrated something a reference cannot.

Second: how will you mark my child's work? The answer should involve the published mark scheme, not an impression. Third: what will you send me after each session? A line naming the topic, the marks scored and the next target is enough, and a provider unwilling to commit to that is telling you how the sessions will be run. Fourth: how will we know in three weeks whether this is working? The only usable answer involves timed papers and raw marks.

Fifth: what will you not do? A straight answer here covers assessed coursework. A tutor who teaches, questions and feeds back on a student's own work is doing the job; a tutor who offers to write or complete an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or any coursework is offering something that puts the student at risk, and there are operations in this market that do exactly that. Sixth: do you hold the MoHRE private tuition permit?

The question that does not discriminate is how far away the tutor lives, and the one that discriminates least usefully is how many students they have taught. Scale claims are unverifiable and every provider makes them. A tutor who can name the syllabus code, describe the marking process and commit to a three-week measurement has given you four checkable facts, which is more than any volume of testimonial provides.

sections.heading: Group classes and one-to-one: a real comparison, not a straw man
paragraphs: Deira and Karama carry the densest tuition-centre provision in Dubai, and for a family in Al Muteena a centre is genuinely reachable. The honest case for it is strong for certain students. A group class provides a fixed time, a room without distractions, peers working on the same paper and a lower hourly cost because the room is shared. For a student whose problem is that no work happens at home, that combination can be worth more than individual diagnosis.

The limitation is structural rather than a matter of quality. A group session is paced for the group, which means it cannot spend twenty minutes on the specific reason one student loses method marks on Paper 4. It also cannot easily adapt when one student is on a different board or tier from the others, which in a mixed Deira cohort is common. A family paying for a group class should know they are buying structure and coverage, not diagnosis.

One-to-one, in any format, buys the opposite: full attention on one student's actual mark losses, a plan that changes when the evidence changes, and work on the specific paper that student sits. It costs more per hour and it does nothing about a student who will not work between sessions. Many families end up using both, with a centre for structure and a one-to-one for the subject where a boundary is in play.

The useful decision rule is to look at the most recent marked paper. If the losses are spread evenly across topics and the student is broadly lost, group coverage of the syllabus helps. If the losses are concentrated in a pattern, method marks unwritten, command terms misread, time running out, then a group cannot address it and the money is better spent on one-to-one hours, however few.

sections.heading: Who regulates what across the UAE, and what that means for a tutoring decision
paragraphs: The regulator map is worth knowing because almost nobody publishes it and parents assume one body covers everything. Dubai private schools fall under KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The emirate regulators do more than inspect. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval sits with the emirate rather than only at federal level. At federal level, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations, which is the rule underlying every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement.

For an Al Muteena family the practical consequences are two. If your child attends a Sharjah-side school, which happens from Al Nahda and Al Mamzar, the regulator and some calendar details differ even though the Cambridge or Pearson qualification is identical. And KHDA's school-level judgements, on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, tell you about the institution rather than about one subject set, so they are a poor proxy for whether a particular student is on track.

There is also a fee-context point worth knowing. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a household already stretched by school fees, a flat year is the window in which a recurring tutoring line becomes affordable to plan rather than improvise.
