faqs.question: Why does searching for a tutor near Al Muteena return so few names?
faqs.answer: Because tutoring supply in Dubai clusters where tutors live and where demand is wealthiest, which is the newer western communities rather than the older northern grid. Widening the search to Hor Al Anz returns largely the same people; widening to Deira or Karama substitutes tuition centres for individuals, which is a different product rather than a longer list. The variables that actually predict whether tutoring works, board and tier knowledge, mark-scheme marking, availability at the right hour and a way to measure progress, do not correlate with distance.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in Deira or Karama a better buy than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: For some students, genuinely yes. A centre provides a fixed time, a room without distractions, peers working the same paper and a lower hourly cost because the room is shared. If the real problem is that no work happens at home, that combination can beat individual diagnosis. What a centre cannot do is spend twenty minutes on why one student loses method marks on a specific paper, or adapt when students in the room are on different boards and tiers. Look at the marked paper: evenly spread losses suit a group, patterned losses do not.

faqs.question: How much more does in-home tutoring cost than online in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Roughly double for the same contact hours, on the published figures. Monthly packages circulating in the market show around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is eight contact hours, against about AED 799 for eight one-hour online sessions, also eight contact hours. Hourly, Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500 with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for comparable online work. The gap is the car, not the teaching.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and can I ask to see it?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and applications run through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: What does KHDA approved actually mean when a tutoring provider says it?
faqs.answer: Usually nothing specific. The real thing it could refer to is a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, issued to operations with premises in Dubai, requiring initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. If a provider uses the phrase, ask for the permit number. IB Gram holds no such permit and makes no accreditation claim from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

faqs.question: Can we hire my child's own schoolteacher for private lessons?
faqs.answer: It is specifically discouraged and in Abu Dhabi restricted. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the ADEK detail as press-reported and verify the current policy document, but the direction is clear across the UAE. A teacher from a different school carries no such conflict and knows the curriculum equally well.

faqs.question: Which questions actually separate one Al Muteena tutor from another?
faqs.answer: Six things, all answerable in a message. Which board and tier is my child entered for, and have you taught that syllabus code this year? How will you mark their work? What will you send me after each session? How will we know in three weeks whether this is working? What will you refuse to do with assessed coursework? And do you hold the MoHRE private tuition permit? Written answers to those six eliminate most shortlists in a day, and they are far more informative than how many students a provider claims to have taught.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram offer home tutoring anywhere in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and delivered live over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper and published mark scheme shared on screen. We also have no UAE office, centre or branch. Those statements are on the page deliberately, because a family deciding between formats should know what each provider actually sells before a booking rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: How quickly should I expect to see a change in marks?
faqs.answer: Judge it in three weeks on raw timed-paper marks, not on confidence. Technique problems, unwritten method, misread command terms, running out of clock, often move within two or three marked papers because nothing new is being learned. Content gaps take longer because the material has to be taught. What should not happen is three months of sessions with no measurement. No tutor can promise a grade, and a provider that offers one is telling you something about its standards rather than its teaching.

faqs.question: My son drifts off unless somebody is sitting with him. Does an online session work?
faqs.answer: The format does not fix motivation and nobody should pretend otherwise. A student who will not work without a person in the room does not become self-directed because the lesson is on video. For that student, a nearby tuition centre with a fixed time and a supervised room, or in-home work if the budget allows, may genuinely be the better structure. What online delivery does is remove distance as a constraint on who teaches a student who is willing to work, which for a specific board and tier is usually the binding constraint.

faqs.question: How many pupils and schools are in the Dubai private sector?
faqs.answer: Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curricula at thirty-seven per cent, Indian at twenty-six, US at fourteen and International Baccalaureate at seven. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating around sixteen thousand eight hundred new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. Those figures explain why IGCSE tutoring demand in the city far exceeds IB demand.

faqs.question: Which body regulates my child's school, and does it regulate tutoring?
faqs.answer: For Dubai, KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the Ministry of Education. None of them regulates private tutoring providers; that sits with MoHRE through the private tuition work permit. So a school inspection band says nothing about a tutoring arrangement either way.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai school-fee freeze change when we should start tutoring?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a household already stretched by fees, a flat year is the practical window in which a recurring tutoring line becomes something to plan rather than improvise. It is also the reason a monthly figure, rather than an hourly one, is the right frame for the decision.

faqs.question: Should we book a term of sessions up front to secure a good tutor?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider pushing for it is worth questioning. Three sessions and three timed papers produce evidence; a term bought in advance commits money before any evidence exists. Any tutor confident in the match will accept being measured over three weeks on raw marks. If the marks move, extend and keep measuring. If they do not, the right response is to change the tutor, the subject priority or the diagnosis, which is much harder to do once a term has been paid for.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor turns out to be the wrong match?
faqs.answer: Ask about replacement before you start rather than after, because the answer varies by model. An agency usually offers a managed replacement, which is part of what the higher rate covers. A marketplace leaves the parent to start again. An independent freelancer is the hardest to replace mid-term, which is the hidden cost of the better rate. With us, a mismatch means a different tutor with a handover of the student's paper plan, so the new tutor starts from the evidence rather than from scratch.

faqs.question: Can one provider cover two children on different curricula in the same household?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is common in this district, where families often have one child on an Indian curriculum and one on IGCSE. Practically it means two separate plans rather than one shared arrangement, because the boards, the assessment and the calendars differ. Online delivery makes the scheduling easier, since two sessions can run back to back in the same room on the same laptop without anybody travelling. What it should not mean is one generalist covering both; the subject and board specialism is the thing being bought.

Before you book, find the codes on your child's examination timetable and send them, because the same subject on two boards needs two different practice regimes and a tutor should be able to say which they teach.

intro.heading: Does anyone near me know my child's actual specification?
paragraphs: This is the right question and the one most tutoring pages avoid, so here is a direct answer. IGCSE is not one qualification. It is a family of specifications from different boards, each with its own code, tier structure, paper pattern, grade scale and calculator rules. A tutor who says they teach IGCSE mathematics has told you almost nothing. A tutor who says they teach Cambridge 0580 Extended, including the non-calculator paper, and can explain how that differs from Pearson 4MA1 Higher, has told you something you can act on.

Al Nahda makes this sharper than most neighbourhoods. The area sits across the Dubai-Sharjah boundary, with Dubai-side schools regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority and Sharjah-side schools by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves curricula and assessment methods as well as regulating quality. Within a few minutes' drive the catchment contains Indian-curriculum, British-track and IB schools. Two neighbours in the same block can be sitting Cambridge papers, Pearson papers and a CBSE paper in the same year group.

So the honest supply position is this. Finding somebody near Al Nahda Pond Park who can teach general secondary mathematics or biology is easy. Finding somebody nearby who knows that Cambridge restructured 0580 so that both tiers now sit a non-calculator paper, or who can say whether your child's centre sits a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, is considerably harder - not because Dubai lacks such people but because the ones who exist are distributed across the city rather than concentrated in one neighbourhood. The people who hold that knowledge are spread across Dubai in ones and twos, and no search radius brings them closer to Al Nahda Road.

The cost of getting this wrong is specific rather than vague. A student drilled for a calculator-permitted paper who sits a non-calculator one loses straightforward marks. A student prepared for a practical test who sits the alternative paper has practised the wrong skill for a term. A student on a tier that caps their grade cannot be tutored past the cap. None of those failures is visible until a mock paper arrives, which is why the test questions on this page are worth ten minutes before any money changes hands. Ten minutes of specific questions costs nothing and protects a term of effort, which is why they are set out in full further down this page.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE tuition to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time, matched by syllabus code and tier. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Where we cannot match a specification properly, we say so at the match stage with the alternatives and a date rather than filling the slot with someone adjacent and letting a term pass before the next mock explains it.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-nahda.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Al Nahda families most often ask about, each with the specification detail that a tutor needs to know and that a generalist usually does not.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Cambridge sets a non-calculator paper on both Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator on both of its two-hour papers. Same content, two different practice regimes. Ask a tutor which they teach and listen for whether they volunteer the difference unprompted.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 Extended by stronger cohorts, with calculus and more advanced algebra. Scarce to staff and frequently confused with the main syllabus, so confirm whether your child is entered for it before assuming a maths tutor covers it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge splits core and extended across multiple-choice and theory papers and adds either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. Pearson assesses practical skills inside its two written papers. The difference decides a term of preparation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same practical split as physics on the Cambridge side. The quantitative spine - moles, limiting reagents, yield, concentration - is where marks concentrate on both boards, and it drills well in short frequent sessions rather than long ones.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Marks are lost to written imprecision more than to understanding on either board. Describe against explain, named structures, and answers that stop one clause short of the mark point. Drilling against the published scheme is the fix and it works quickly.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson: the differences that actually change teaching
paragraphs: Board differences are often presented as trivia. They are not, because each one changes what a student should be practising this week. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is syllabus 0580, tiered Core, graded C to G, and Extended, graded A* to E, with both tiers now sitting a non-calculator written paper alongside a calculator one. Pearson's International GCSE in Mathematics Specification A is 4MA1, tiered Foundation reaching grade 5 and Higher running 9 to 4, with two papers of two hours and a calculator permitted on both. Specification B is 4MB1, structured with a shorter first paper and a longer second.

In the sciences, Cambridge offers Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 as separate sciences with Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 as a double award and Combined Science 0653 as a single award. Practical skills on the Cambridge separate sciences are assessed either through a practical test in the laboratory or through an alternative-to-practical written paper, and which applies is a centre-level arrangement. Pearson's separate specifications - 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 - assess practical skills within the written papers, with Science Double Award under 4SD0.

Grade scales differ, which matters when a sixth form states an entry requirement. Cambridge reports in letters, with the tier setting the ceiling and the floor. Pearson reports on the 9 to 1 numeric scale. A school asking for a grade 6 and a student holding a Cambridge B are not speaking the same language, and the mapping is a question for the sixth form rather than for a tutor. Establish it in writing before results day rather than after it.

Series and logistics differ too. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates and the February and March series is offered to India only, so no Al Nahda family should plan around a March examination. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson runs May/June and November, its November final timetable having run from late October to 19 November 2026.

sections.heading: Eight questions that show whether a tutor knows your child's board
paragraphs: Put these to anyone you are considering, nearby or online, including us. None requires you to know the subject. You are listening for specificity, for whether the tutor volunteers information you did not ask for, and for whether they say plainly when something is outside what they teach.

Start with identification. Which specification code do you teach for this subject? What tier is my child entered for, and how would you check? For Cambridge mathematics, how do the two tiers differ in grade range and in the papers sat? A tutor working from real knowledge answers these in sentences with numbers in them. A tutor working from general experience answers in adjectives.

Then move to the differences that catch people out. Does my child's maths paper allow a calculator, and how does that change what we practise? For the sciences: does my child's centre sit a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, and how do you prepare differently for each? Those two questions eliminate most generalists on their own, because the answer requires knowing something specific about a specification rather than about the subject.

Finish on process and honesty. Will you mark a past paper against the published scheme and send me the list of named weaknesses? What happens in week four if nothing has shifted? And do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit - it is granted free of charge for two years, so there is no financial reason for a working tutor to be without one. A tutor who answers seven of the eight well and says plainly that they do not teach the eighth is a better bet than one who answers all eight smoothly and vaguely.

sections.heading: Tiering: the decision stack that caps or releases a grade
paragraphs: Tier entry is the most consequential thing in IGCSE and the thing families nearest to it know least about. Cambridge 0580 Core is graded C to G; Extended is graded A* to E. Pearson 4MA1 Foundation reaches grade 5; Higher runs 9 to 4. In the Cambridge sciences a student may be entered on core or extended routes with different paper numbers. In each case the entry sets both a ceiling and a floor, and the entry is made by the school rather than by the family.

What follows is an arithmetic that no amount of tutoring changes. A student on Cambridge Core cannot be taught to a B, because the papers do not contain those marks. A family paying for weekly tutoring in pursuit of one is buying something the examination cannot produce, and a tutor who does not say so is either uninformed or dishonest. Equally, a borderline student pushed onto Extended can lose a secure C and finish with an E, which is its own expensive error.

The decision stack is worth writing out because it is rarely presented clearly. First, which subjects are tiered at all - not all are. Second, which tier is your child provisionally entered for in each. Third, when does each entry become final. Fourth, what evidence is the decision resting on. Fifth, what does the destination sixth form actually require, in that board's own grade language. Answer those five in writing with the school and most of the tutoring question answers itself.

The cheapest intervention available is one marked paper at each tier for any subject genuinely in doubt, sat before the entry closes. Two hours of tutoring to settle a decision that governs two years of effort and spending is the best value purchase on this page, and almost nobody sells it as a standalone product. We will, and we will tell you when the answer is that the current tier is correct and no further hours are needed yet.

sections.heading: If the school will not enter a subject: the private candidate route
paragraphs: Some students need a qualification their school does not offer, or want to resit a subject outside the school's arrangements. The route for that is private candidacy: the student sits the examination at an approved centre that accepts private candidates rather than through their own school. It is a real and reasonably common option in the UAE, and it is poorly documented in tutoring content, which is why families often conclude wrongly that it is impossible.

The sequence runs in a specific order and the order matters. First establish that a centre near you accepts private candidates for that board and that subject - not all do, and the arrangements for subjects with practical components are more limited. Second establish the entry deadline, which sits months before the examination. Third make the entry and pay the centre's fees, which are separate from any tutoring cost and set by the centre. Only then does the teaching plan matter.

Two cautions. Subjects with a practical component are the most constrained, because a private candidate may need the alternative-to-practical route or may not be accommodated at all for that specification at a given centre. And a resit carries a retention problem: the content has to be held across an additional period while new sixth-form work begins, which usually means timed practice from the outset rather than content teaching followed by revision.

IB Gram does not make entries, hold a centre, or administer examinations, and we would not describe tutoring as a requirement for any of this. What a tutor can do is teach the specification once the logistics are settled, and tell a family honestly when the timetable they are proposing is not achievable. Confirm every date and arrangement with the centre and the board's live official timetable rather than with any restated figure.

sections.heading: Verifying a nearby tutor: permit, references and the arrangement to avoid
paragraphs: If a family does choose a tutor from the immediate neighbourhood, the verification steps are the same as for anyone else and most of them are free. The permit first: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

MoHRE's service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the smart app, website and e-services system, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published - Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties - so disregard any figure circulating as the penalty.

The arrangement to avoid is paying your child's own classroom teacher privately, however convenient a nearby colleague seems. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct has been reported as barring the same. Verify the current wording against the authority's own policy document; the principle holds across the Emirates.

A tuition centre is a different category again. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson. Where those bodies appear here it is to explain what they do.

sections.heading: What it costs, and what you can check about every figure
paragraphs: A page that asks you to audit tutors should let you audit its own numbers, so each figure here is attributed and dated. The published Dubai market rate for a qualified subject tutor working online is roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB tuition from AED 200. Named exam specialists are quoted higher, roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table placing specialist exam-year support in that region. BartyED published AED 650 at the premium end.

At the budget end, platforms staffed largely by university students advertise from the low double digits: Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. For IGCSE that band is not automatically a bad buy - supervised practice and homework help have value - but it is unlikely to come with specification knowledge, which is the thing this page argues matters. In-home visits in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel, with Bestimate showing AED 180 to 350 and independent tutors asking AED 200 to 500.

Monthly comparisons are easier to budget against. Market packages show around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits, and Bestimate estimates weekly one-hour sessions at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000-plus for specialist exam-year support. All of those were read in October 2026 and belong to the providers that published them.

What you can check: each of those providers publishes its figures, so a parent can verify any number above by visiting the source. What you cannot check anywhere in this market is a satisfaction percentage, a star rating or a student count, which is why we publish none. Research into these queries found pages showing two different review scores in the same document. We do not print a rate card either, because the honest number depends on the specification, the tier and the weeks remaining - the free trial lesson exists so the tutor can be judged before the fee is discussed.

sections.heading: Getting started, and what we say when a specification is outside our coverage
paragraphs: Send four things: the examination timetable with the codes visible, the tier for each tiered subject, which emirate the school sits in, and the two time windows that work on a school night. Arrival in Al Nahda runs from roughly 15:00 to 15:45 and later for cross-boundary journeys, so a 15:45 start is workable for some households and not for others, and that detail decides whether a schedule survives.

The first lesson is a free trial with the matched tutor - one lesson, one tutor, with the fee discussed afterwards. Use the eight questions on this page during it, and ask the tutor to work a question from your child's actual paper rather than a generic one. If the fit is wrong, say so and we match again. Fit failures usually have nothing to do with competence and everything to do with pace and manner, which is why they are worth discovering in week one.

Coverage, stated honestly. Common specifications - Cambridge 0580, 0610, 0620, 0625, 0654 and the main Pearson equivalents - are comfortably staffed. Less common ones, such as Cambridge Additional Mathematics, Cambridge International Mathematics, Pearson Specification B and some of the humanities and language specifications, are tighter. If your child's specification falls in the tighter group, you are told at the match stage with three options: a different slot with the right person, adjacent expertise starting now, or a wait with a date attached.

And the standing limits. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. We operate no office, centre or branch in the Emirates. Where a specification includes coursework, a tutor may teach the criteria, question a plan and mark a draft against the descriptors, but may not write it, redraft it to completion or supply the content - the work has to be the student's own.

faqs.question: How do I know whether an IGCSE tutor near me actually knows my child's specification?
faqs.answer: Ask for the code rather than the board. A tutor who teaches your child's course answers with 0580, 4MA1, 0620 or 0654 and can say what the tier does to the grade range. Then ask two specification-level questions: does my child's maths paper allow a calculator, and does the science centre sit a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper. Those two eliminate most generalists, because answering them requires knowing something about a specification rather than about the subject in general.

faqs.question: Why does it matter which board my child's school uses?
faqs.answer: Because the practice regime differs. Cambridge 0580 now sets a non-calculator written paper on both Core and Extended, while Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator on both of its two-hour papers. Cambridge separate sciences add either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper; Pearson assesses practical skills inside its written papers. Grade scales differ too, with Cambridge reporting A* to G and Pearson 9 to 1. The same child, on the same content, needs different preparation depending on which applies.

faqs.question: Two children on our street sit different IGCSE papers. How is that possible?
faqs.answer: Al Nahda spans the Dubai-Sharjah boundary and the catchment contains Indian-curriculum, British-track and IB schools within a few minutes of each other. Dubai-side schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Sharjah-side schools to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves curricula and assessment methods as well as regulating quality. So neighbours can be on Cambridge, Pearson and CBSE papers in the same year group. Never infer a board from a neighbourhood, and never copy a neighbour's tutoring plan without checking your own codes.

faqs.question: Can tutoring lift my child above the grade their tier allows?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge 0580 Core is graded C to G, so grade C is the ceiling the papers can produce; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation reaches grade 5. Hours bought in pursuit of a higher grade on a capped entry are hours spent on something the examination cannot deliver, and a tutor who does not tell you that is either uninformed or not being straight with you. The conversation to have is with the head of department about the entry, supported if necessary by one marked paper at the tier above.

faqs.question: What is the single best-value thing to buy before committing to weekly tutoring?
faqs.answer: A specification audit and a marked paper. The audit takes the examination timetable, identifies every code and tier, establishes the practical arrangement where one applies and sets out what each paper demands. The marked paper then gives a written list of named weaknesses with the marks attached. Together those often change what a family buys next, and sometimes show that the problem is three topics and a wrong practice regime rather than the subject. Almost nobody in this market sells either as a standalone product.

faqs.question: Does my child's centre sit a practical test or the alternative paper?
faqs.answer: That is a centre-level arrangement rather than a student choice, so ask the school's examinations officer. It matters because the preparation is genuinely different. A practical-test candidate needs apparatus familiarity, repeat readings and tabulating discipline, much of which happens in the school laboratory. An alternative-to-practical candidate needs to read a described method, identify the controlled variable and the error that actually matters, complete tables, plot from given data and propose a real improvement - which is highly trainable online and usually left untouched.

faqs.question: Our school does not offer a subject my child needs. What are the options?
faqs.answer: Often yes, as a private candidate at an approved centre that accepts them. The order matters: confirm that a centre near you takes private candidates for that board and subject, establish the entry deadline, which sits months before the examination, make the entry and pay the centre's fees, and only then plan the teaching. Subjects with a practical component are the most constrained. IB Gram does not make entries, hold a centre or administer examinations; we teach the specification once the logistics are settled.

faqs.question: Is a nearby tutor ever the better choice for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Yes, in two cases we would not argue with. A younger student who needs company and supervision while they work, where presence does most of the useful work, and a household whose broadband cannot carry a reliable video lesson. In both, buy presence and accept the published premium of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel, plus the lower session frequency that follows. For a Year 11 whose problem is a specification mismatch, proximity does nothing to help.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE specifications are hardest to find a tutor for in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge Additional Mathematics and Cambridge International Mathematics, Pearson Specification B in mathematics, and several of the humanities and language specifications. The common routes - 0580, 0610, 0620, 0625, 0654 and the main Pearson science and maths equivalents - are comfortably staffed. If your child's specification falls in the tighter group you should expect to hear that at the match stage, with the alternatives and a date, rather than after a payment has been taken.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we buy IGCSE tutoring for at once?
faqs.answer: Two or three at most. A student sits eight to ten subjects and, in this neighbourhood, has two usable study windows on a school night once bus arrival between roughly 15:00 and 15:45 and the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies homework are counted. Spreading hours across five subjects produces a plan nobody can keep. Diagnose first, then aim the hours at the subjects where marks are genuinely recoverable, and accept that some subjects get nothing this term.

faqs.question: What should a marked IGCSE paper actually produce?
faqs.answer: A written list of three to six named weaknesses with the marks lost beside each, plus a view on whether the current tier is right. Marked against the published scheme, not ticked - which means someone explaining why an answer that looks correct earned nothing, usually because a method line was missing or a command word was ignored. You keep that document whether you continue with that tutor, take it elsewhere or decide no weekly tutoring is needed yet. It is the cheapest useful purchase in this market.

faqs.question: Do you send IGCSE tutors to homes anywhere in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson we arrange is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we operate only in India, stated the same way on every UAE page here. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the Emirates. The Dubai market does supply in-home tutors at published rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel; this page sets out what that premium buys so the trade can be made deliberately.

faqs.question: Should I ask a nearby tutor about their tutoring permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and there is no reason for an evasive answer. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing, a working tutor has no financial reason to lack one. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: How should we handle an IGCSE resit in the November series?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a route rather than a safety net, because the content has to be carried across an extra period while sixth-form work begins. That argues for timed practice from the outset rather than content teaching followed by late revision. Confirm the entry route first: whether through the school or as a private candidate at an approved centre, and the entry deadline, which sits well before the examination. Work from the board's live official timetable rather than any restated date, including anything on this page.

intro.heading: Comparing Al Quoz with the district next door, and finding the comparison does not matter
paragraphs: Parents who search for an IGCSE tutor near me in Al Quoz are usually running a comparison in their heads. Al Barsha has more schools. Al Safa and Jumeirah feel better served. Al Quoz is mostly warehouses and showrooms, so perhaps there is less here. The comparison is reasonable and the conclusion is wrong, because the thing being compared has almost nothing to do with the thing that decides your child's grade.

Here is what genuinely differs between these districts: the number of schools inside them, the length of the school run, and therefore the earliest hour a weekday session can start. Al Quoz 1, 2 and 3 hold the housing, between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road, and children travel outwards in several directions, so the realistic start is 5pm to 5.30pm. In Al Barsha, with several schools in the district itself, 4.30pm works. That is the whole of the difference.

Here is what does not differ: whether your child sits Cambridge 0625 Physics or Pearson Edexcel 4PH1, which paper the marks are being lost on, and whether the person teaching them holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit that Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 requires of individuals offering private lessons. None of those three is a property of a district. All three are properties of a tutor, and the first two are properties of your child's school.

That is why this page compares the things that are actually comparable. It sets Al Quoz against the neighbouring districts on school supply and session timing, then puts Cambridge against Edexcel subject by subject with the codes, then compares the provider models in this market on price and verifiability, then explains how a parent checks whether a tutor is legally permitted to teach in the UAE. Those are decisions a family can act on, unlike a postcode.

It is worth saying why the district comparison feels so convincing. Al Quoz Industrial 1 to 4 dominate the district by land area, so a map search centred there returns showrooms, workshops and the Alserkal Avenue arts spaces alongside a thin list of tutors, while the same search in Al Barsha returns schools. The visual difference is real. It is a land-use difference, not a measure of who can teach your child Edexcel 4CH1 on a Tuesday evening.

The premise, stated plainly: IB Gram delivers one-to-one IGCSE tuition into Al Quoz homes as live online video sessions, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. The practical consequence is that an Al Quoz family and an Al Barsha family are selecting from exactly the same pool of board specialists, and neither is limited by what a car can reach at half past five.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-quoz.programmesIntro: An IGCSE student in the Al Quoz cluster sits one of two boards, sometimes a mix across subjects, and arrives from one of several lower-secondary routes. Each is described below by what it changes for a family choosing support.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Four-digit syllabus codes identify every subject and determine the paper structure. Many subjects are tiered Core and Extended, with the Core tier capped below the top grades, and papers are set per tier. The practical implication is that past-paper practice has to match the entered tier precisely, because a Core candidate practising Extended papers is learning content that will not appear.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong timetable. So the timetable that counts for an Al Quoz child is the one the school's exams officer holds.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Different codes and a different structure: 4MA1 Mathematics tiered Foundation and Higher, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology. Assessment is wholly written in most subjects with practical skills examined on paper, and some subjects are offered modularly, so units can be sat across series instead of all at the end.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so plans belong against the live official document. Checkable results reference points: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: Mixed-board timetables
programmes.description: Plenty of UAE schools enter candidates with Cambridge for some subjects and Edexcel for others, usually because departments choose independently. A student can therefore sit 0580 Mathematics and 4CH1 Chemistry in the same year, with two different paper conventions, two sets of command term habits and two timetables.
programmes.countryNote: This is the single most common reason an Al Quoz family ends up with a tutor working from the wrong past papers. Check the code on the school's assessment paperwork for each subject separately rather than assuming the school uses one board throughout.

programmes.name: What IGCSE feeds into
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum schools in Dubai run IGCSE to 16 then split into A Level or the IB Diploma. Year 10 tier decisions constrain that choice: a Core-tier or Foundation-tier Mathematics candidate is not positioned for A Level Mathematics or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches, whatever grade they achieve within the capped tier.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in the Al Quoz and central corridor clusters offer both post-16 routes, which makes the Year 10 tier decision more consequential here than in a school with a single pathway. It is worth raising with the subject teacher before the school's confirmation deadline rather than after.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-quoz.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Al Quoz families ask about, with both boards' codes where they exist, and the component where the marks actually go. A tutor who cannot name the code cannot build the right practice set.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The two boards cover similar ground with different paper structures and tier language. Most lost marks are procedural rather than conceptual: unshown working forfeits method marks, and premature rounding breaks otherwise correct multi-step answers.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by stronger cohorts as a bridge to A Level or Higher Level IB. It introduces calculus and formal function work. A student fluent in 0580 Extended who struggles here usually has a speed and fluency gap rather than a conceptual one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and waves cost Extended and Higher candidates the most. Practical skills are examined on paper in both boards, which means a student must describe a method precisely enough for a stranger to repeat it, and that is a trainable writing skill.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, stoichiometry and organic chemistry account for most dropped marks. Answers that name a correct substance without the balanced equation or the units score nothing in most schemes, which is why practice has to be marked against the scheme rather than against intuition.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Students revise it as a memory subject and are marked on command terms. Describe, explain, suggest and compare each demand a different response shape, and a correct fact in the wrong shape earns nothing, which is a four-session fix rather than a term-long one.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: One or two grades covering all three sciences for students not taking the separates. Breadth is wide and depth shallower, so revision has to be scheduled; the predictable failure is running out of time on whichever science was taught first.

subjects.name: English
subjects.description: Reading questions reward precise selection and close inference. Writing is marked on structure and control as much as content, and the dominant error is an answer that retells the passage instead of analysing how it achieves its effect.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and application to the stimulus decide the grade. Evaluation has to reach a judgement rather than list two sides, and a generic answer that never touches the case study in front of the student loses the application marks outright.

subjects.name: ICT and Computer Science
subjects.description: ICT carries practical components with strict output requirements, where presentation errors cost marks unrelated to understanding. Computer Science rewards pseudocode in the board's own conventions rather than in whichever language the student happens to know.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Required alongside the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. These sit on top of a full IGCSE load, which is a genuine and often unexamined cause of Year 11 underperformance.

sections.heading: What a proximity search returns for IGCSE in Al Quoz
paragraphs: An IGCSE tutor near me in Al Quoz search ranks by distance. IB Gram meets the need behind it differently: one-to-one IGCSE teaching delivered into Al Quoz homes as live online sessions on Gulf Standard Time, matched on board, subject code and tier. No tutor is sent to a UAE address, because home visits are a service we run only in India.

The reason distance is the wrong sort first becomes obvious when you look at what a result list contains. Tuition centres with fixed group timetables, nurseries, general homework tutors and a handful of subject teachers, in a district whose land area is mostly warehouses and showrooms. None of those results tells you whether the tutor has taught Edexcel 4CH1 or only Cambridge 0620, and that is the difference between useful practice and plausible-looking practice.

There is a verification problem too, and it is specific to how this market is built. Individuals offering private lessons in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, and those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. A proximity search surfaces nothing about permit status, and most parents never ask.

So this page compares the things that are comparable and verifiable: school supply and timing across districts, the two boards subject by subject, the provider models by price and transparency, and the permit position by tutor category. Everything else about choosing an IGCSE tutor follows from those four.

sections.heading: District by district: what really changes around Al Quoz
paragraphs: The table below is the comparison a parent is running, filled in with the two variables that genuinely differ: how many schools sit inside the district, and what that does to the earliest workable session time. Both are real. Neither tells you anything about teaching quality.

Read the last column carefully, because it is the point of the exercise. In every row the answer to what changes for tutoring is the same: the hour, and only the hour. More schools in a district means a shorter drive to school, not a deeper pool of Edexcel Chemistry specialists. Al Barsha's advantage over Al Quoz is thirty minutes of evening, which is worth having and is not worth choosing a tutor over.

There is one genuine asymmetry worth naming, and it runs the other way. Districts with schools inside them are where school staff tend to live, which looks like better local supply. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a comparable code of conduct, so that apparent supply is not always available to you anyway.

If you take one thing from the table, let it be the planning use rather than the comparative one. Find your district, read the realistic start time, and build the week around it. That is the part of a tutoring plan that geography actually decides.

One practical consequence for Al Quoz specifically. Because the start time is around 5pm rather than 4.30pm, a household that needs two sessions a week in the run-up to a series usually has to put one of them at the weekend. Deciding that in advance is better than discovering it in week three and quietly dropping to one session, which is the point at which an eight-week block stops working.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Edexcel, subject by subject
paragraphs: This is the comparison that changes outcomes, and across the researched competitor pages for this market exactly one syllabus code appeared in an entire seven-page cluster. Yet the code decides the paper structure, the tier language, how practical skills are assessed and which past papers are useful. A tutor working from the wrong board's papers is wasting your child's revision time with complete sincerity.

The content overlap between the two boards is large, which is why the error survives. A student revising Cambridge 0620 material for an Edexcel 4CH1 paper will recognise most of the chemistry and still be surprised by the paper. In Mathematics the tier vocabulary differs outright: Cambridge sets Core and Extended, Edexcel sets Foundation and Higher, and a parent translating between them in conversation can easily agree to the wrong entry.

Check this per subject rather than per school. Departments choose independently, so a single student can sit Cambridge Mathematics and Edexcel Chemistry in the same year. The code is printed on the school's assessment paperwork and the subject teacher will confirm it in one sentence, which is a better use of an email than almost anything else a parent can send.

Both boards publish provisional timetables ahead of each series and revise them, so use the official live document for dates. The checkable reference points for Pearson are that June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and that November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

The price columns are other providers' own published figures as at October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. Budget online provision starts at EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 per hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. The verification columns are where the market is weakest. sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE, and how do you check?
paragraphs: Only one researched competitor in this market touches licensing at all, in a single heading. It is the most practical question a parent in Al Quoz can ask, and it has a clear answer. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws.

The permit is granted free of charge for two years, which is worth knowing because it removes the usual excuse. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two working day completion time and no fees listed.

A separate permit covers organisations rather than individuals. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which involves initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That is why the phrase about being approved by KHDA is the most misleading claim available in this market: it describes a premises permit and is used to imply something about teaching quality.

No fine amount appears on this page. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and a figure circulating publicly could not be verified, so quoting one would be inventing a number. What a parent can do is ask directly, ask which category the tutor applied under, and treat a vague answer as the answer.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and what that means
paragraphs: Every Al Quoz school is regulated by KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Most families know that much. Far fewer know the rest of the map, which matters the moment a family moves emirate or compares a school in Dubai with one in Sharjah or Abu Dhabi.

Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which u.ae says supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education there. Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in those emirates. ADEK is named by none of the competitors researched for this market and SPEA by one.

The powers differ in ways that affect families directly. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval sit with the emirate regulator rather than only inspection. In Dubai, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package.

The federal baseline sits underneath all of it: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule behind every emirate's mandatory subject requirement, including the ones your child is sitting alongside IGCSE.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies on top of IGCSE
paragraphs: Here is the one item that is genuinely identical in Al Quoz, Al Barsha, Al Safa and Jumeirah, and it is what the district comparison at the top of this page should have been about. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in every Dubai private school regardless of which international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, so a British-curriculum pupil living beside a warehouse strip and an American-curriculum pupil in a Jumeirah villa carry precisely the same additional load. KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Not one competitor page in any cluster researched for this market carries a section on it, which is why most parents meet it as a surprise on a published timetable rather than as a fact they could have planned around.

Two of those rules govern who may stand in front of the class, which connects straight back to the verification section above. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education must hold appropriate KHDA approval, and that is a requirement on a school's own staffing rather than a credential a private tutor can hold, so treat the phrase as a check on the school and not as a line on a tutor's profile. The classes themselves may not be merged: KHDA requires separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for Arabs and non-Arabs are strictly prohibited, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ between the two groups. The language rules are what that difference amounts to in a classroom. Standard Arabic is the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students. Non-Arabs are taught in the school's licensed-curriculum language, which around Al Quoz usually means English.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools free to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and a recommendation that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Content is tightly controlled: KHDA states that using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited.

For an Al Quoz family the practical consequence is timetable arithmetic. These subjects sit on top of a full IGCSE load, so a Year 11 student who seems to be underperforming across the board is sometimes simply out of hours, and the right intervention is a schedule rather than a tutor. Where support is appropriate, it works inside the school's own material rather than around it.

sections.heading: Getting started from Al Quoz, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: The sequence is short. Send the board and code for each subject, the tier, the school, and the last two marked papers. A specialist reading those can usually name the failing pattern in a sentence. The trial lesson is free, comes before any payment, and exists to produce that diagnosis rather than to sell a term.

Here is what will not be claimed on the call. No grade promise, because nobody can make one honestly. No suggestion that tutoring is required for equivalency, university admission or school progression, because that is a false claim about a regulatory process. No regulator or board approval: IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no UAE office or centre. And no invented statistics, which is why you will not find a satisfaction percentage anywhere on this page.

There is also a limit worth stating in advance. Narrow requests at popular hours are genuinely constrained in the weeks before a series, when much of Dubai's Year 11 cohort wants the same early-evening slot. When it happens you are told, offered the nearest workable alternative, and given a realistic view of when the slot opens. A generalist is never quietly substituted for the specialist you asked for.

On data, one practical note: enquiry forms collect information about a child, so only what is needed is asked for, the purpose is stated, and a privacy link sits on every page. We do not ask for a child's photograph, and you can ask for the enquiry record to be deleted.

faqs.question: Are there fewer IGCSE tutors available in Al Quoz than in Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: Locally, probably yes, because Al Quoz is mostly warehouses and showrooms by land area with housing in Al Quoz 1, 2 and 3, while Al Barsha has several schools inside the district. But it makes no difference to what your child can access. Lessons through IB Gram are delivered live online, so both families select from the same pool of board specialists. The real difference between the two districts is about thirty minutes of weekday evening, which affects scheduling and nothing else.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our Al Quoz address for IGCSE lessons?
faqs.answer: Not through us. IB Gram teaches IGCSE one-to-one into Al Quoz homes over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and sends no tutors to UAE addresses; in-person home visits are an India-only service for us. Other Dubai providers do offer them, at market rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour with travel included, according to Bestimate's 2026 cost table. We work online because it lets us match the board and code your child actually sits rather than the nearest available person.

faqs.question: Where is the syllabus code written down if we do not know the board?
faqs.answer: The code is printed on the school's assessment paperwork, and the subject teacher will confirm it in one sentence. Check it per subject rather than per school, because departments choose independently and a single student can sit Cambridge 0580 Mathematics alongside Edexcel 4CH1 Chemistry. This is the most common reason a tutor ends up working from the wrong past papers, which looks like diligent revision and is not.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE close enough that the board does not matter?
faqs.answer: The content overlaps heavily and the papers do not, which is exactly why the error persists. Structure, mark allocation, command term conventions and the way practical skills are examined all differ, and Mathematics tiering differs in name as well: Cambridge sets Core and Extended, Edexcel Foundation and Higher. In Year 9 the distinction barely matters. In a Year 11 block built on past papers it matters a great deal, because the wrong papers teach the wrong habits.

faqs.question: How can I check that a private tutor in Dubai is permitted to teach?
faqs.answer: Ask directly, and ask which category they applied under. Individuals offering private tuition need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service. A centre's KHDA permit covers premises, not the individual teaching your child.

faqs.question: Does a centre being permitted by KHDA mean its tutors are vetted?
faqs.answer: Not in the sense most parents assume. A KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute is issued to an organisation with premises, involving initial approval, up to six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. It is a premises and operating authorisation. It says nothing directly about whether the person teaching your child holds an individual MoHRE private tuition work permit, so that remains worth asking separately.

faqs.question: Which regulator covers my child's school if we move to Sharjah or Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Dubai schools sit with KHDA. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and both approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education. The powers differ, so fee and curriculum questions go to different places in different emirates.

faqs.question: What should I actually compare when choosing between tutoring providers?
faqs.answer: Four things you can check rather than four things you can feel. Whether a rate is published at all and in which currency. Whether the provider states a position on the MoHRE tutor permit. Whether a free trial exists and what condition is attached to it. And whether the tutor can name the board and syllabus code your child sits. Across the researched competitor pages in this market, three publish no price, two quote in US dollars and only one mentions licensing anywhere.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in Al Safa better than an online specialist?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is wrong. A centre group class teaching a fixed syllabus on its own timetable is reasonable value for broad coverage, and it is poor value for repairing one component, because the class cannot stop for your child's specific error. Add two car journeys per session from Al Quoz and the real cost is higher than the headline. If the problem is one paper or one topic, a board-matched specialist working one-to-one will get there in fewer hours.

faqs.question: My child sits Cambridge for Maths and Edexcel for Science. Do we need two tutors?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is worth the extra scheduling. The subjects are different, the boards are different, and a tutor stretched across both is compromising on at least one. What a single provider can do is sequence the sessions so one evening is not overloaded and keep one point of contact for the household. If a tutor is strong in Cambridge 0580 but vague about 4CH1 paper structure, two specialists serve your child better than one convenient diary.

faqs.question: Do you publish an hourly rate for IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Not as a list, because the plan determines it: subject, level, how many sessions a week and for how long. What this page does publish is the market, attributed and dated to October 2026, so you can judge any quote against it. Budget online runs AED 33 to 65, qualified online subject tutors AED 150 to 300, specialists AED 200 to 450 or more, in-home visits AED 180 to 500 including travel. faqs.question: Why does Al Quoz feel short of options when it is so central?
faqs.answer: Because the district's land area is dominated by Al Quoz Industrial 1 to 4: warehouses, workshops, showrooms and the Alserkal Avenue arts spaces. Housing sits in Al Quoz 1, 2 and 3, so the residential population is smaller than the map footprint implies, and the number of qualified subject teachers who both live nearby and are free at 5pm is smaller still. A proximity search reflects the land use, not your child's options, which is the flaw in using one.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons affect IGCSE results?
faqs.answer: Indirectly and significantly, through the timetable. They are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. So they sit on top of a full IGCSE load, and a Year 11 student underperforming across several subjects at once is sometimes out of hours rather than out of ability.

faqs.answer: Two emails and one decision. Email the subject teacher to confirm the board, code and tier for each subject that is causing concern. Ask for the last two marked papers, or photograph them at home. Then decide which single component matters most, because a plan aimed at one component works and a plan aimed at a whole subject usually does not. intro.heading: Three facts your child's school may never have put in writing
paragraphs: The first is the board. Dubai schools run Cambridge International or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and sometimes both in the same building for different subjects. The syllabus, the paper structure and the grading scale differ between them. A parent who buys past-paper practice without checking the code can easily hand a Cambridge 0580 student a Pearson 4MA1 paper, which is an honest mistake that wastes a term of revision.

The second is the tier. Cambridge Mathematics splits into Core and Extended; Pearson Mathematics A splits into Foundation and Higher. The decision is not cosmetic. A Cambridge Core entry caps the available grade at C, and a Pearson Foundation entry caps it at 5. Children are entered for a tier by the school, often provisionally in Year 10, and parents discover the cap when a university prerequisite collides with it two years later.

The third is the calendar. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate never sits it, no matter what a generic revision website says. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, which is why a decision taken late is a decision taken for you.

Al Quoz 4 adds a local complication on top of all three. This is a villa pocket between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road where virtually nobody attends school locally. Year 10 and Year 11 students travel to Al Barsha South, Al Safa, Nad Al Sheba or Al Jaddaf, and come back on a bus that threads two or three sub-communities. The day they get home with homework and a coursework deadline is a shorter day than it looks on paper.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; in-home tutoring is an India-only service. What we deliver to Al Quoz 4 is one-to-one teaching over live video, matched by specification code, scheduled around the actual bus arrival rather than the theoretical bell. The rest of this page is the detail: codes, tiers, dates counted backwards, the subjects worth tutoring out of nine, the Ministry of Education equivalency rule, and what the market charges.

A word on how to use all of it. None of these three facts requires a tutor to discover. The board and code take one email to the school office. The tier takes the same email with a second sentence attached. The series your child sits is published on the board's own site, by administrative zone, and your school knows which zone it belongs to. Gather those answers first and you will be able to judge every provider you speak to, including this one, on whether they ask for them before quoting a price. The ones who quote first and ask later are selling hours rather than teaching.

sections.heading: Which board your child sits, and why nobody told you
paragraphs: Open any past paper your child has brought home and look at the top right corner. A four-digit number starting with a zero is Cambridge International. A code beginning 4 followed by two letters and a 1 is Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. That single check answers a question most Al Quoz 4 parents have never been asked to answer, and it changes which resources, which mark schemes and which tutor are useful.

The two boards are not interchangeable. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 Extended candidates sit a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper. Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1 permits a calculator on both of its papers, which changes how arithmetic fluency is practised. In the sciences the gap is wider: Cambridge assesses practical skills through a practical test or the Alternative to Practical paper, while Pearson International GCSE assesses them inside the written papers instead.

Grading scales differ too, which is where parents get confused comparing siblings. Cambridge reports A* to G, with Core entries capped at C and Extended reaching A*. Pearson International GCSE reports 9 to 1, with Foundation tier capped at 5 and Higher tier starting at 4. A child with a 6 and a child with a B are not easily compared, and a school report that mixes both boards across subjects makes the comparison harder still.

Ask the school, in writing, for the board and code for every examined subject. It is a reasonable request, it takes an administrator two minutes, and it is the foundation for every revision decision you make for the next two years.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: Tiering is the least discussed and most consequential decision in the IGCSE years. A Cambridge Core entry in Mathematics means the student sits Paper 1 and Paper 2 and cannot be awarded above a C, whatever they write. An Extended entry means Paper 3 and Paper 4, with A* available and a real risk of a low grade if the student was not ready. Pearson works the same way with Foundation and Higher.

Schools make the provisional decision from Year 10 performance, which is reasonable, and they are usually right. The problem is that the decision is often communicated as administration rather than as a choice, so a family finds out at the point entries are confirmed. By then a student who has worked hard through Year 10 may have outgrown a Core entry and have no simple route to move.

The downstream effect is the part that stings. Post-16 courses in the Al Barsha and Nad Al Sheba corridor set subject entry grades, and a Mathematics grade ceiling of C can remove A Level Mathematics, Physics, Economics and Chemistry from the options in one stroke. No one hides this; it simply never gets said out loud while there is still time to change it.

If your child is in Year 10 now, ask three questions this term. Which tier are they provisionally entered for in each subject, what grade does that cap them at, and what is the last date a change can be made. A tutor cannot make that decision for you, but two sessions on current attainment against the Extended specification will tell you whether the question is worth pressing.

A student from an extended-day school in the Al Barsha corridor can be walking through the door at 16:20 with eight subjects of homework behind them.

The practical result is that the 16:00 slot most agencies default to does not exist for a Year 11 student here. What does exist is 19:30, after the meal and the first push at homework, and Saturday morning. Dubai schools finish between 12:00 and 12:30 on a Friday and the weekend runs Saturday and Sunday, so a 10:00 Saturday session catches a student rested for the only time in the week.

There is one more window worth naming. Mock season in Dubai British-curriculum schools typically runs in the winter term, and schools often release students for parts of it. Those are the single most productive tutoring days in the whole year, because a student is already in exam mode and the marked script is fresh. Families who book a short intensive across mock fortnight get more out of four sessions than out of twelve in October.

When you contact us, give the school name, the year group, the finish time and the actual bus arrival. That sentence does more to produce a workable schedule than any amount of discussion about preferred times.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate never sits it. Any revision site that hands you a February entry deadline is describing a different country's calendar, and acting on it would cost a series.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Results dates give a sense of the real rhythm: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The November route therefore functions as a repair series, with a result in the following January rather than the same summer.

There is a Cambridge administrative detail worth knowing because it has real consequences. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your school which zone it sits in and use that timetable, not a generic one found online.

Always check the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than relying on any restatement, including this one; Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and they can be revised.

sections.heading: Nine subjects, and the three worth paying for
paragraphs: A typical Dubai IGCSE student carries eight to ten subjects. Almost no family can fund or sustain tutoring in all of them, and almost none should try, because the limiting factor at this age is the student's remaining hours rather than money. The question is which three subjects buy the most, and it is answerable with the mock script rather than with instinct.

Rank by three criteria. First, which grades are furthest below the post-16 entry requirement the student actually needs, not the one they vaguely want. Second, which subjects have the steepest marginal return, usually mathematics and the sciences, where method is teachable and a repeated error can be removed in a fortnight. Third, which subject is eating morale, because a child losing confidence in one subject underperforms in the others.

What usually does not justify one-to-one tutoring is a subject where the student is already at or near their target, or a subject where the issue is volume of recall rather than method. Those respond better to a changed revision routine than to a weekly hour. A good tutor will tell you that in the first session rather than sell you a second subject.

The honest version of availability also belongs here. For common subjects we can usually arrange a trial within days. For a narrow combination, a less common language or a specific evening hour, it can take longer, and occasionally we have nobody suitable free. We will say so rather than put a generalist in front of a Year 11 student eight weeks from a paper.
