sections.heading: Five subjects at grade E: the Ministry of Education equivalency rule
paragraphs: Families planning to use a UAE university, or to keep the option open, eventually meet certificate equivalency. For the British track, the published requirement is that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail most often got wrong is which subjects count. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. One competing site ranking for these queries tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the published rule says. Getting this right matters because it changes the subject list a Year 10 student should be entered for.

For the American track the requirements are different again: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test. No IB points threshold for equivalency has been read on a Ministry source, so this page publishes none; a figure invented for a landing page is worse than no figure.

Equivalency is a process the Ministry of Education runs, not something a tutoring service performs or guarantees. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own site or with the attestation authority before you act on it, and treat any provider claiming to secure equivalency for you as a reason for caution rather than confidence.

sections.heading: What the hour costs in Dubai, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Most pages in this market either refuse to publish a price or quote in US dollars, which is a currency UAE families do not transact in. Here is the Dubai market in dirhams, from the cheapest real option upward, with the source of each band named so you can check it. None of this is an IB Gram price list; it is the market you should measure any quote against.

At the bottom sit university-student tutors online, advertised from around AED 45 to 65 an hour by EdFlik and from around AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya on their own published pages. For Key Stage 3 fluency work or homework supervision this is good value and nobody should pretend otherwise. It is the wrong purchase for Chemistry 0620 eight weeks before a paper, where the tutor needs to know how the qualitative analysis marks are allocated.

The middle band is a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase quotes around AED 270. In-home one-to-one sits higher at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, per Bestimate's Dubai rate table and published home-tutor rates, with monthly in-home packages seen at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits.

Set that against the wider cost picture. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is therefore the variable line in a Dubai education budget this year, which is an argument for spending it deliberately on two or three subjects rather than thinly across nine.

sections.heading: Science practicals when the lessons are on video
paragraphs: This is the fair objection to online science tutoring and it deserves a direct answer. A tutor on video cannot run a titration with your child. What a tutor on video can do is teach the thing the practical papers actually assess, which is not manual dexterity. Cambridge's Alternative to Practical paper tests experimental design, reading instruments, recording data to the right precision, plotting, and identifying sources of error. All of that is paper skill.

Pearson International GCSE takes a different route, assessing practical skills inside the written papers rather than through a separate component. The effect for tutoring is similar: the examinable material is the method and the analysis, not the execution. A student who can explain why a repeat was taken and what a systematic error does to a gradient scores where a student with excellent lab technique and no vocabulary does not.

Where school practical work is genuinely missing, say because a student joined late or changed schools mid-course, the gap is real and a tutor should say so rather than paper over it. The honest response is to raise it with the school, which holds the equipment and the responsibility, and to use sessions to secure the analysis skills that carry the marks in the meantime.

One practical advantage of video that parents do not anticipate: graph work. A shared whiteboard with a plotted axis, marked points and a drawn line of best fit, saved and sent afterwards, is a better revision artefact than the same thing sketched in a notebook and never looked at again.

process.title: Send the code, not just the subject
process.description: Tell us 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher rather than maths. If you do not know, photograph the top corner of a past paper or ask the school in writing. Two minutes here prevents a term of revision against the wrong specification, which is the most common avoidable error in this market.

process.title: Send the last mock script
process.description: A marked paper is worth more than any description of the difficulty. We read it for pattern rather than total: marks lost in the last question of every paper, in one command term, or in unshown working each point at a different fix, and each fix takes a different number of weeks.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One per family, booked before payment and with no card details taken. It is a real lesson on your child's own material. The question afterwards is simple: did your child explain something back that they could not explain an hour earlier, and did the tutor name a specific thing to change.

process.title: Agree the slot and the eight-week target
process.description: Pick the hour that survives a busy week, usually 19:30 or Saturday morning in Al Quoz 4. Then agree what eight weeks should produce: a grade boundary crossed in mocks, a paper technique fixed, a topic rebuilt. A checkable target beats an open-ended arrangement.

process.title: Review on marked work, then adjust
process.description: At eight weeks we look at a new marked piece. If the lost marks have moved, continue. If they have not, we change the tutor, the format or the diagnosis rather than adding hours. Re-matching costs nothing and keeps the work already done.

whyPoints.title: Matched by specification, not by subject
whyPoints.description: A Cambridge 0625 student and a Pearson 4PH1 student need different teachers and different papers. We match on the code, which is why the first thing we ask for is the code. Nobody is given a generic physics tutor and left to discover the practical component works differently.

whyPoints.title: The tier conversation happens early
whyPoints.description: Core and Foundation entries cap the grade, and the cap closes post-16 doors quietly. We raise it in Year 10 while there is still time to act, with the current attainment held against the Extended specification, and give you a written summary to take to the school.

whyPoints.title: A schedule built on the bus, not the bell
whyPoints.description: Session times are chosen around when your child genuinely gets home to Al Quoz 4, which for an extended-day school can be 16:20. Because teaching is on video, a 19:30 weekday or a 10:00 Saturday is as easy to staff as any other hour.

whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit the June and November series with Cambridge and May, June and November with Pearson. We name the series by month rather than by year so the page stays true, and we point at the board's own live timetable rather than restating dates that get revised.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my Al Quoz 4 child sits Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Look at the top right corner of any past paper they have brought home. A four-digit code beginning with zero, such as 0580 or 0625, is Cambridge International. A code of the form 4MA1 or 4PH1 is Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. If no paper is to hand, email the school and ask for the board and syllabus code for every examined subject; it is a routine request. Schools in the Al Barsha and Nad Al Sheba corridor sometimes use different boards for different subjects, so check each one rather than assuming.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE tutor near me in Al Quoz 4 have to be physically nearby?
faqs.answer: No, and in this area it works against you. Al Quoz 4 sits between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road, where the 15:30 to 17:00 crossing is the slowest part of the day. A tutor who drives can only offer the hours their route allows, which clusters around 16:00 to 18:00, and for a Year 11 student off an extended-day bus at 16:20 that window barely exists. Online delivery removes the drive, opens 19:30 and weekend mornings, and widens the pool to every specialist teaching that code.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to a villa in Al Quoz 4?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Lessons for Al Quoz 4 families are one to one over live video, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own school material on screen. We state this plainly because parts of this market do not: several providers imply a visit and then connect families to tutors who are not in the country. If someone in the room is what you want, you want a different provider.

faqs.question: Is a Core entry in Cambridge Mathematics a problem for my child?
faqs.answer: It is a ceiling rather than a problem in itself. A Cambridge Core entry means Paper 1 and Paper 2 and a maximum grade of C; Extended means Paper 3 and Paper 4 with A* available. For a student heading to a vocational or humanities route, Core can be the right fit and reduces the risk of a poor grade. For anyone who might want A Level Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry or Economics, a C ceiling can close those doors. Ask the school which tier, what cap, and the last date it can change.

faqs.question: When do UAE students sit their IGCSE exams, and is there a February sitting?
faqs.answer: There is not, for candidates in the UAE. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series for UAE centres; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The November route works as a repair series with results arriving the following January, as happened when November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Check your school's zone timetable on the board's own site.

faqs.question: What is the Cambridge administrative zone, and why should I care?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and the exam timetable differs between them. Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Parents who download a timetable from a search result are at genuine risk of planning around the wrong dates. Ask your child's school which zone it is in, then use only that timetable for revision planning.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does the Ministry of Education count for equivalency?
faqs.answer: The published British-track equivalency rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, together with one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. At least one site ranking for these searches states six subjects, which does not match the published rule. Verify the current requirement with the Ministry of Education before acting on any version of it.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE tutor cost in Dubai right now?
faqs.answer: Taking published Dubai market figures rather than our own, university-student tutors online advertise from around AED 33 to 65 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, and an IGCSE or IB specialist sits at AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. Those bands come from Tutopiya, EdFlik, Unitors, TutorChase and the Bestimate Dubai rate table. Measure any quote you receive, including ours, against them.

faqs.question: Can science be tutored properly over video when there is no lab?
faqs.answer: The examinable part can, because the papers assess method and analysis rather than manual skill. Cambridge's Alternative to Practical tests experimental design, instrument reading, precision, plotting and sources of error. Pearson assesses the same skills inside its written papers. All of that is teachable on a shared whiteboard, and graph work is arguably better on screen because the plot can be saved and reread. If a student has genuinely missed school practical work, that is a conversation with the school, and a tutor should say so.

faqs.question: My son is in Year 11 with eight subjects, so which should we tutor?
faqs.answer: Usually two or three, never eight. Rank by distance from the post-16 entry grade he actually needs, then by marginal return, which is generally steepest in mathematics and the sciences where method is teachable and a repeated error can be removed in a fortnight, then by whichever subject is costing him confidence. A subject already near target rarely justifies a weekly hour; that one responds better to a changed revision routine. A good tutor will tell you that in the first session.

faqs.question: Which evening slots actually work for Year 11 students in Al Quoz 4?
faqs.answer: 19:30 on a weekday and 10:00 on Saturday, in that order. Bells across the schools this area feeds fall between 14:30 and 15:45, and the Al Quoz bus loop adds twenty-five to forty minutes, so an extended-day student can walk in at 16:20 with eight subjects of homework ahead of them. A 16:00 start catches them on the road. Dubai schools finish around midday on Friday, which makes Saturday morning the one hour in the week a Year 11 student is genuinely rested.

faqs.question: Is mock fortnight a good time to start tutoring or a bad one?
faqs.answer: It is the best fortnight of the year to start, for two reasons. The student is already in exam mode, so timed practice feels normal rather than imposed, and the marked script arrives fresh with every lost mark visible. Four sessions built from a real mock paper usually achieve more than twelve sessions built from a syllabus checklist in October. Schools in Dubai often release students for parts of mock season, which is also the rare moment when a daytime session is possible.

faqs.question: Does the school have to tell me which tier my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Schools in Dubai will tell you if you ask, but many do not volunteer it, because entries are handled as administration rather than as a parental decision. Put the request in writing and ask three things: the tier for each examined subject, the maximum grade that tier allows, and the last date on which a change can be submitted. Those three answers let you decide whether to press for a move while it is still possible, rather than discovering the ceiling when results arrive.

faqs.question: Can an Al Quoz 4 tutor read a coursework draft without writing any of it?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach the underlying content, explain what the assessment criteria reward, question whether a plan is answerable, point at a weak section and say why it is weak, and model technique on a different example. No tutor at IB Gram will write coursework, draft it, or edit it into something the student could not have produced. Work submitted for assessment must be the student's own, and a service that offers otherwise puts the child at risk, not itself.

faqs.question: What if you have nobody free for my child's subject and time?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than filling the slot with a generalist. Common subjects at common hours are usually matched within a few days. Narrow combinations take longer: a specific Pearson science code at a fixed weekday hour, or a less commonly taught language, can need a week or more, and occasionally there is nobody suitable at all. Hearing that honestly is more useful eight weeks before a paper than discovering in session three that the tutor has never taught the specification.

intro.heading: Price the year, not the hour
paragraphs: Al Qusais is a corridor rather than a pocket. It runs along Damascus Street and the Green Line, through Al Qusais 1, 2 and 3 and the industrial area, with Al Nahda to one side and Al Twar and Mirdif beyond. The schools here are large - The Millennium School, The Westminster School, Dubai Scholars, Apple International, Al Diyafah High School - and the households tend to be larger than in central Dubai, with two or three school-age children rather than one. That combination changes the money question completely.

A family with one child asks what an hour costs. A family with three asks what a year costs, and whether the same budget can be made to serve more than one of them. The published hourly figure answers neither, because the hourly rate is the smallest and least informative part of an IGCSE year's spend. There are entry fees, the possibility of a resit, the question of how many subjects are being supported, and the choice between a tuition centre group class, a private tutor crossing the corridor, and one-to-one online delivery - and those choices differ in cost by multiples rather than by percentages.

Al Qusais is also unusually well supplied with tuition centres and group classes, more so than most Dubai districts. That matters because the group class is genuinely cheaper per student and is genuinely worse for some purposes, and the arithmetic of which is which is straightforward once somebody writes it down. A class of eight with one tutor for ninety minutes gives each student, at best, about eleven minutes of individual attention. For a cohort being taught new content that is fine. For a student whose problem is that they do not write method, it is almost useless.

Then there is the commute, which has a price even when nobody is paid for it. Damascus Street between four and six is slow, the run from Al Qusais across to Bur Dubai or Deira is longer than the map suggests, and a private tutor crossing that corridor is charging for the car as well as the teaching. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor, and in this corridor the travel component of that gap is real rather than notional.

Finally, the decisions that cost nothing. The tier a child is entered for caps the grade regardless of spend. The board determines which past papers are useful. The number of subjects being supported determines whether any of them gets enough hours to move. Those three are free to establish and they govern the value of every dirham that follows, which is why they come before any discussion of rates.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Four-digit subject codes, many subjects tiered Core and Extended, and a June series and a November series for UAE candidates. The tier is the single most consequential cost fact in the plan, because the lower tier caps the grade and hours spent reaching past that cap produce nothing.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, stating that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a family along this corridor, the dates come from the school's entry statement rather than from any restated version.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: An alphanumeric code scheme - 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology - with its own tiering and question style. Exams are available in May/June and November each year, so a subject that goes wrong in summer can be retaken in autumn with a second entry fee.
programmes.countryNote: The dated anchors that make the cost of a resit concrete: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. An autumn resit result does not arrive in time for a December deadline.

programmes.name: Indian curriculum provision alongside
programmes.description: Several of the large schools in this corridor run Indian-curriculum streams alongside or instead of IGCSE, which is why households here frequently have children on two different systems. The assessment model, the examination calendar and the useful past papers are all different.
programmes.countryNote: The practical cost consequence is that a single tutor cannot serve two children on two systems, and a recommendation that worked for one sibling may be useless for the other. Families who budget for two children assuming one arrangement will cover both usually end up paying twice anyway, later and under pressure.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The alternative to sixteen at the continuum schools reachable from this corridor, assessed against four criteria on a 1 to 8 scale with no terminal papers in most schools. No entry fees and no resit question, but a completely different kind of support required.
programmes.countryNote: Worth separating in a household budget because MYP support is bought in short criterion-focused blocks rather than in examination run-ins. Treating an MYP child's needs as a smaller version of an IGCSE sibling's is one of the more common ways a family's tuition money is spent on the wrong thing.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-qusais.subjectsIntro: Subjects do not cost different amounts per hour, but they need very different numbers of hours. Below are the IGCSE subjects most requested along this corridor, with an honest note on what each tends to consume.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The most requested subject and the one where a short block does most good, because the dominant loss - unwritten method - is a habit rather than a knowledge gap. Confirm the tier first: the cap on the lower tier is the whole plan.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Low content volume relative to the other sciences and high technique share of losses, mainly explain questions answered as descriptions. That makes it cheap to improve per hour and a sensible first target in a stretched budget.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Splits into mechanical calculation work, which drills quickly, and explanation questions, which need structure. Most students are comfortable on one side and avoid the other, so the first session should establish which half is costing marks.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The highest content volume of the three sciences and therefore the most expensive to repair late. Marks go on process order, definition precision and unfamiliar data, and reading notes does not move any of them.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510)
subjects.description: Counts toward the five subjects MoE equivalency recognises on the British track. Marks come from reading precision and from following the controlled-writing rubric exactly, which makes it one of the better value short-block subjects.

subjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and unseen-passage analysis. The main shift - writing about how a writer creates an effect rather than what a passage says - is a technique fix of roughly six to eight sessions and not a year of reading.

subjects.name: Accounting (Cambridge 0452)
subjects.description: Widely taken in this corridor's schools and unusually mechanical, which makes it one of the cheapest subjects to improve: the question types repeat, the formats are fixed, and accuracy under time responds quickly to drilling.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450) and Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Both cap a student in the middle of the range if only content is revised, because the upper marks sit in evaluation and in applying a concept to the specific case given. A short block on answer structure usually moves these more than content work.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Theory plus algorithms, with marks lost by writing Python where the scheme expects syllabus pseudocode conventions. A presentation habit rather than a knowledge gap, and therefore inexpensive to fix once named.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 Extended by students heading toward A Level or Higher Level Mathematics. Demanding in pace and poorly suited to a short block, so budget for it as a term rather than as a repair if it is in play.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE year actually costs, line by line
paragraphs: Almost every tutoring page in this search result quotes an hourly rate and stops. For a family along this corridor that is the least useful figure available, because the hour is one component among several and not the largest. The year contains school fees already committed, a tuition decision, examination entries, the possibility of a resit with its own entry and its own block of work, and the opportunity cost of subjects not supported.

Two anchors make the context real. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. And the entry fee, where a student sits as a private candidate, is set by the approved examination centre rather than by the board - so it varies by centre and by subject, and the only honest instruction is to get the figure in writing from the centre before the deadline rather than after it.

The tuition line itself should be read monthly rather than hourly, because that is how it is committed. One Dubai provider publishes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which is near AED 100 an hour. In-home monthly packages in the same market are advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits, near AED 200 to 225 for the same eight hours of teaching. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, read in October 2026, estimates monthly spend on weekly one-hour sessions at AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

The table below sets out the year's components. Every dirham figure in it belongs to the provider or rate table named; none is an IB Gram price, and the items without figures are the ones only your school or examination centre can supply.

sections.heading: The group-class arithmetic, worked through
paragraphs: Al Qusais is better supplied with tuition centres and group classes than most Dubai districts, so the group option is genuinely on the table here rather than theoretical. It is cheaper per student, and the useful way to compare it is not by price but by minutes of individual attention purchased.

Take a class of eight students with one tutor for ninety minutes. Even with perfect management, each student receives somewhere around eleven minutes of individual attention, and in practice less, because some of the time is whole-class teaching that is genuinely shared. For a cohort meeting new content at the same pace, that is efficient and appropriate: the teaching is the shared part, and eleven minutes of individual checking on top is reasonable value.

Now take a student whose problem is that they do not write out method. That student needs somebody watching their working, stopping them, and refusing to accept an answer without it - repeatedly, over weeks. Eleven minutes a week of that is not enough to build a habit, and the other seventy-nine minutes are spent on content they may already know. The class is cheap and, for this purpose, almost valueless. The same money spent on three one-to-one sessions would fix it.

So the rule is about what is being bought. Shared teaching of new content is well served by a group. Individual habit change, diagnosis, and anything requiring somebody to watch a specific student write, is not. The table works the comparison through on minutes rather than on price.

sections.heading: The decisions that cost nothing and change the grade
paragraphs: Before any money is spent, three facts should be established, and all three are free. They govern the value of every dirham that follows, and families routinely buy a term of tuition without having checked any of them.

The first is the tier. Many Cambridge subjects are tiered Core and Extended; Pearson Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher. The lower tier caps the available grade, which means hours spent reaching for a grade the entry cannot award are wasted hours and nobody will tell you so at the end. Ask the school which tier each subject is entered for, and if there is doubt whether it is right, raise it while an amendment is still administratively possible.

The second is the board and the code. Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 and Pearson 4MA1 are three different courses with different papers and different question architecture. A tutor working from the wrong board's papers looks entirely competent for about six weeks, because the content overlaps, and then a mock exposes it. The entry statement names the board, the code and the tier in a few lines, and it is the single most useful free document in the whole year.

The third is the subject count. A budget spread across seven subjects gives none of them enough hours to move, which is the most common way a family in this corridor spends real money and sees no change. Work backwards instead: MoE equivalency on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, and the receiving school or university states its own requirements in named subjects. Fund the two or three that are actually named and let school provision carry the rest.

sections.heading: Two or three children, one budget
paragraphs: Households along this corridor are frequently supporting more than one child at once, and the instinct is to divide the available money evenly between them. That is fair and it is usually the least effective allocation, because the children are rarely at the same point of need. One may be in Year 11 with a specific named failure pattern that three sessions would fix; another may be in Year 9 with a slow-building algebra gap that needs a term; a third may be on a different curriculum entirely and need something that does not resemble either.

The sharper approach is to ask what each child's money would buy and fund the highest-value purchases first across the household, rather than giving each child an equal share of a plan. A three-session block that fixes a Year 11 student's method writing before a series is worth more than three months of general support for a Year 9 who is coping. The Year 9's turn comes next term, and that is a defensible answer rather than a neglectful one.

There is one genuine saving available where two children are at the same stage on the same code and tier: paired tuition, where the pair gets thirty minutes of individual attention each in a sixty-minute session rather than eleven in a group. It only works where the two are genuinely at the same point - siblings two years apart on different tiers will not benefit, and one will be carried while the other is held back.

The format matters more in a multi-child household than anywhere else. Online delivery means two or three different subject specialists can run on different evenings or in consecutive hours without anybody travelling, which is simply not economic in-home across three children with three different needs. sections.heading: What the school already provides, and what duplicating it costs
paragraphs: The large schools along this corridor generally run revision clinics, after-school support sessions and departmental catch-up provision, all of it included in fees that KHDA confirmed would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year in Dubai. A substantial amount of privately bought tuition in this district duplicates that provision, which is the purest form of wasted spend because the family is paying for something they already own.

Finding out what exists takes one conversation and most parents never have it. Ask the subject teacher, not the office, what support is available outside lessons, which weekdays it runs on, and what it covers. The answers are usually more substantial than expected, and they also tell you something useful for free: if the school is running a weekly clinic on exactly the topic your child is weak in, buy something else.

What school provision reliably does not cover is individual diagnosis and individual habit change. A revision clinic is a group activity teaching content to whoever attends. It cannot watch one student write out method for six consecutive weeks, and it cannot audit one student's mock script into the four causes of lost marks. Those two things are exactly what private one-to-one buys, and they are the two things most likely to move a grade.

The school's inspection report is the other free resource. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and publishes reports on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. If the report names mathematics or science attainment as a strength, the school's own provision is probably sufficient in that area and the money belongs elsewhere. sections.heading: The Damascus Street premium, priced
paragraphs: In this corridor the travel component of a tutoring bill is unusually visible. Damascus Street between four and six is slow, the run from Al Qusais to Mirdif or across to Deira takes longer than the distance suggests, and anybody driving to a lesson here is giving up more of their evening than the clock on the appointment shows. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate putting in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor.

Decompose the gap and very little of it is teaching. A tutor who has committed to arriving in Al Qusais at five cannot teach elsewhere at five, cannot easily teach at four either, and prices the lost availability into the hour. In central districts with short drives that premium is mostly scarcity; along this corridor it is genuinely partly mileage, and either way the parent is paying for a car and a fixed arrival window rather than for better teaching.

There is a second cost that never appears on an invoice and bites in exactly the wrong week. An in-home arrangement is the hardest thing in a family's week to move, because the tutor's evening geography has to be re-solved to change it. When a school adds a late mock, or Ramadan shifts the shape of the day, the in-home session is the one that cannot flex. Families along this corridor discover that in the fortnight before a series, which is the worst possible fortnight to discover it.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Sessions for Al Qusais students run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which removes both the travel premium and the fixed arrival window. The second of those is worth more than the first in a household running sessions for more than one child.

sections.heading: Where the money goes without buying a grade
paragraphs: Five patterns account for most of the privately spent tuition money in this corridor that produces no measurable change, and all five are diagnosable in a single session. The first is duplication: paying for content teaching the school is already providing free in a weekly clinic.

The second is re-teaching. A tutor who explains a topic again, clearly, is giving the student a second version of a lesson they already sat through. If the student could follow the school's explanation and still cannot answer the question, the explanation was never the problem, and a term of better explanations will not fix it.

The third is a session where nothing is written, timed or marked. Revision that consists of talking and reading is comfortable and produces no information about whether the student can satisfy a mark scheme. A session that ends without the student having produced something marked against the official scheme has produced a pleasant hour and no diagnosis.

All three of those share one tell, and it is easy to check. Ask what the student physically produced in the last session and what happened to it. If the answer is that they wrote nothing, or wrote something nobody marked against the official scheme, the hour cannot have generated any information about whether they can satisfy an examiner - which means the next hour is being planned on the same guess as the last one.

The fourth is spreading a budget across seven subjects, so that no subject receives enough hours to change. The fifth is buying late: tuition in the final eight weeks competes with the school's own mock timetable and with everybody's fatigue, and rates across this market tend to firm up as a series approaches. The same money spent two terms earlier, on diagnosis and technique, does more per dirham and is easier to book.

sections.heading: Equivalency, the subject count and what tutoring cannot do
paragraphs: Families in this corridor are often planning toward UAE universities or toward the attestation of certificates, and the number of subjects supported should follow from what those processes actually require rather than from a general sense that more is safer. The published requirement on the British track is specific: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details matter for the budget. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects, so they are carried for other reasons and should not absorb a stretched tuition budget by default. And one competitor page currently ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published requirement - a reminder to check the authority's own channel rather than a tutoring page, including this one.

On the American track, for comparison, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test before applying. No IB points threshold for equivalency appears in the sourced material available for this project, so none is published here; check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority directly.

One thing should be said plainly because the opposite is implied elsewhere in this search result. Tutoring is not required for equivalency, for attestation or for university admission. Equivalency is a documentation process performed by the authority, not a service a tutoring platform provides or guarantees, and nobody should be selling support on the basis that a regulatory process demands it.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and the periods inside the school day
paragraphs: Two cost-relevant checks a parent can make without anybody's help. First, the permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time. Because the permit is free, no part of any quoted rate is a permit fee being passed on. Those offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so nobody should be quoting you an amount.

A tuition business with premises is a different matter, which is directly relevant in a corridor with this many centres. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific instrument and it is reasonable to ask a centre about it. IB Gram holds no such permit, no regulator accreditation and no UAE office, and does not describe itself as approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

The regulator map is worth knowing because this corridor sits close to the Sharjah boundary. Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA; Abu Dhabi and Al Ain by ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation there; Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate; Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge; and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so a family with a child at a Sharjah school is reading a different regulator's decisions.

Finally the periods that compress the study week, which is why the realistic weekly figure for additional work is smaller than a timetable implies. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements due from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes. Separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs are required for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are strictly prohibited. For those subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which limits what any tutor can legitimately offer in them.

faqs.question: What should a household in Al Qusais budget for an IGCSE year?
faqs.answer: Price it monthly and include more than tuition. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts monthly spend on weekly one-hour sessions at AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. One provider publishes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Then add examination entries where the student sits as a private candidate, with the fee set by the centre rather than the board, and the possibility of a resit entry plus an autumn block. All figures read October 2026 and all are the providers' own.

faqs.question: Are the tuition centres along this corridor good value?
faqs.answer: For one purpose, genuinely yes. A group class is efficient where a cohort needs the same new content at the same pace, and this corridor has more of that provision than most Dubai districts. The arithmetic to do is minutes rather than price: a class of eight for ninety minutes gives each student roughly eleven minutes of individual attention at best. That is fine for shared teaching and almost useless for habit change, diagnosis, or anything requiring somebody to watch one student write.

faqs.question: Which should we buy first if the budget is tight?
faqs.answer: A diagnostic block of three or four sessions whose only job is to establish what is wrong, ending in a written priority list. It is the highest-value purchase available to a household with a fixed budget, because it usually produces a shorter plan than the one the family was about to commit to - and occasionally shows that the school's own provision already covers the problem. Buying a term first and diagnosing later means paying for a guess for several months.

faqs.question: Can one tutor serve two children in the same household?
faqs.answer: Only where they are genuinely at the same stage on the same board, code and tier - then paired tuition gives each about thirty minutes of individual attention in a sixty-minute session, which is a real saving. Siblings two years apart, or on different tiers, or on different boards, will not benefit: one is carried while the other is held back, and past-paper practice has to come from the correct board anyway. Two specialists scheduled back to back is usually the better answer.

faqs.question: How should we split a fixed budget between three children?
faqs.answer: Not evenly, which is the instinct and usually the weakest allocation. Diagnose all three, then fund the highest-value purchases first across the household. A three-session block that fixes a Year 11 student's method writing before a fixed series date is worth more than three months of general support for a Year 9 who is coping, and the Year 9's turn comes next term. Equal shares feel fair and typically produce a thin layer that moves nothing for anybody.

faqs.question: Does the school already provide what we are about to pay for?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and finding out takes one conversation that most parents never have. Ask the subject teacher - not the office - what support runs outside lessons, on which weekdays, and what it covers. The large schools along this corridor generally run revision clinics and departmental catch-up provision inside fees that KHDA confirmed would not rise for 2026-27 in Dubai. If a clinic already covers your child's weak topic, buy something else: individual diagnosis and habit change are what school provision cannot give.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home tutor more expensive along Damascus Street?
faqs.answer: Because the journey is genuinely long at peak and the tutor prices the lost evening into the hour. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 including travel, with Bestimate putting in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor. The hidden second cost is flexibility: an in-home session is the hardest thing in a week to move, and it needs moving most when a school adds a late mock. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE.

faqs.question: Which free decision matters most before we spend anything?
faqs.answer: The tier. Many Cambridge subjects are tiered Core and Extended and Pearson Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher, and the lower tier caps the grade available regardless of how many hours are bought. Ask the school which tier each subject is entered for, and if there is doubt whether it is right, raise it while an amendment is still administratively possible. Hours spent reaching for a grade the entry cannot award are wasted, and nobody will point that out at the end of the year.

faqs.question: How much do IGCSE examination entries cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Where a student sits as a private candidate, the fee is set by the approved examination centre rather than by Cambridge or Pearson, so it varies by centre and by subject and no single honest figure can be published. Contact centres directly, ask for the per-subject fee in writing, and get it before the entry deadline rather than after. Where the student sits through their own school, the entry is handled by the school and its own arrangements apply - either way, settle the number before the window closes.

faqs.question: Is a November resit worth the second entry fee?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the result date against your actual deadline. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series; Pearson Edexcel exams are available in May/June and November each year. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results went to students on 20 August 2026. So an autumn resit does not meet a December deadline however well it goes. The resit block itself is usually shorter and more targeted, because the student has sat the real paper.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we actually fund support in?
faqs.answer: Two or three, chosen by what the next stage names. A budget spread across seven subjects gives none of them enough hours to change, which is the most common way real money is spent here with no result. Work backwards: MoE equivalency on the British track requires five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, and the receiving school or university states its requirements in named subjects. Fund those and let school provision carry the rest.

faqs.question: Should a stretched budget pay for Arabic or Islamic Education support?
faqs.answer: No. The published requirement on the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among those five. They are carried for other reasons and should not absorb a stretched tuition budget by default. One competitor page ranking for these searches states six subjects are required, which does not match the published rule - verify your own position on the Ministry of Education's own channel.

faqs.question: Is tutoring needed for equivalency or attestation?
faqs.answer: No, and anybody implying otherwise is making a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process. Equivalency is a documentation procedure performed by the authority, not a service a tutoring platform provides or guarantees. What tutoring can do is help a student reach the grades the process requires, which is a different statement. Check the requirements and the route on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority directly rather than relying on any tutoring page, this one included.

faqs.question: When in the year is tuition cheapest to buy?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families buy it. Rates across this market tend to firm up as a series approaches and genuine specialists on a specific code become scarce at exactly the point when every family in the city is looking. Tuition in the final eight weeks also competes with the school's own mock timetable and with general fatigue, so the same money buys less. A diagnostic block and a short technique block two terms early cost less per dirham of effect and are far easier to book.

faqs.question: Our school is in Sharjah but we live in Al Qusais. Does that change anything?
faqs.answer: It changes which regulator's decisions apply to the school, which matters when you read an inspection report or a fee decision. Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA; Sharjah's by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in that emirate and also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. It does not change the tutoring market, which is shared across the boundary, nor the tutor permit position, which is federal through MoHRE.

faqs.question: Should we ask a tuition centre whether it holds a KHDA permit?
faqs.answer: It is a fair question in a corridor with this many centres. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific instrument tied to premises. Separately, individual tutors need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free for two years - so no part of a rate is a permit fee.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-qusais.closingHeading: Three free questions, then one small purchase
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-qusais.closingBody: Before spending anything, ask the school which tier and board each subject is entered for, what support already runs outside lessons and on which weekdays, and when the mock window falls. Those three answers regularly remove a purchase and always improve the one you make. Then buy small: a diagnostic block of three or four sessions ending in a written priority list, so the plan is sized by evidence rather than by worry. In a household with more than one child, fund the highest-value purchase first and say so. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: "Is there anyone near me who actually knows this syllabus?"
paragraphs: That is the real question behind the search. A parent in Al Rashidiya types "IGCSE tutor near me" and gets a map: pins in Al Garhoud, pins in Mirdif, a tuition centre on Algeria Street, a WhatsApp number forwarded by a neighbour. What the map cannot tell you is the one thing that matters, which is whether any of those pins has taught Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 Extended, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1 Higher, all the way through to a final paper.

We think the honest answer is worth saying out loud. Proximity and specialism pull in opposite directions in a district like this one. Al Rashidiya is a compact residential area pressed between Dubai International Airport and the Dubai-Sharjah corridor, and its secondary students scatter across schools in Al Garhoud, Al Mamzar, Mirdif and Al Qusais. The number of adults living within a fifteen-minute drive of your villa who have examined, taught or even read the 0625 syllabus in detail is small. The number who have done it for the specific tier your child sits is smaller again.

So IB Gram does not try to win the distance argument. Lessons for Al Rashidiya families are delivered one to one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor chosen for the syllabus rather than the postcode. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India; there is no version of this where somebody parks outside your gate in Al Rashidiya. What you get instead is a shortlist drawn from every tutor who teaches that code, not from the few who happen to live near the airport tunnel.

The rest of this page is built to make that choice checkable rather than asked on trust. There is a table of syllabus codes so you can match a tutor's claim against your child's statement of entry. There is a table of what tutoring actually costs in dirhams, with the provider who publishes each figure named, so you can open their page and read it yourself. There is the exam calendar read backwards from results day, because the deadline that catches families out is the entry deadline, which sits months before the first paper. And there is a plain account of what a tutor may and may not touch on assessed work, because two pages ranking for this search sell finished coursework and that route ends in a malpractice panel.

If your child is in Year 10 and drifting, or in Year 11 with a mock grade that came back two bands below the target, the useful next step is a forty-minute trial with a specialist in the weakest paper. dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-rashidiy.programmesIntro: An Al Rashidiya family usually arrives at IGCSE from a British or Indian primary route, and leaves it for A Level or the IB Diploma. These are the stages we cover either side of the exam year, because the gap that shows up in Year 11 was usually opened in Year 8.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The years before the exam course, where the arithmetic fluency and the scientific vocabulary that IGCSE assumes are either built or missed. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests sit in March, May and October and give a school an external read on a cohort. The content is not examined for a certificate, which is exactly why it is the cheapest point to fix a weakness.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Al Rashidiya run Checkpoint in Year 9 and use it to stream Year 10 into Core and Extended maths. A student placed into Core at that point can find the route to an A Level sciences offer closed two years before anybody mentions it, so this is the year to ask the school which tier they are heading for and why.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE
programmes.description: The two-year examined course and the reason most families on this page are reading it. Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are separate qualifications with separate codes, separate paper structures and separate past-paper banks. A student typically sits eight or nine subjects, graded 9-1 or A*-G depending on the board and subject, with the grades going on to university applications and to the Ministry of Education equivalency file.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's UK-curriculum schools account for roughly thirty-seven per cent of private-school enrolment, which makes IGCSE the commonest exam a sixteen-year-old in Al Rashidiya sits. It also means the tuition market here is crowded with generalists. Asking for the syllabus code rather than the subject name is the fastest way to separate a specialist from somebody who taught GCSE in the UK a decade ago.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB's middle-school programme, assessed against criteria A to D rather than by paper marks, and run by the IB continuum schools in this part of Dubai. Students move from MYP into either the Diploma Programme or, occasionally, into an IGCSE year at a different school. The criteria-based habit of mind transfers badly to a timed IGCSE paper without specific work on command terms.
programmes.countryNote: Uptown International School is the nearest IB continuum option to Al Rashidiya, so a family moving from an MYP school into a British-curriculum school in Mirdif or Al Garhoud is a routine local case. The hardest part of that move is not content, it is the switch from an open-ended task to a paper that awards marks for a specific form of answer.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma entry
programmes.description: What IGCSE grades are actually for. A Level sciences and mathematics usually ask for grade 7 or above at IGCSE in the same subject, and the IB Diploma schools set their own Higher Level entry bars. The decisions made in Year 11 about tier and subject choice set the ceiling for this stage, which is why we treat IGCSE tutoring as preparation for two things rather than one.
programmes.countryNote: For a family in Al Rashidiya the practical question is often whether to stay British or cross to the IB Diploma for sixth form, since both are available within a reasonable school run. The grade profile that keeps both doors open is a strong Extended maths grade and two strong sciences, and that is worth knowing in Year 10 rather than in August of Year 11.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-rashidiy.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Al Rashidiya families ask for most often, with the part of each one where marks actually disappear. Where a syllabus code is named, ask any prospective tutor to confirm they have taught that exact code rather than the subject in general.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The tier decision dominates everything. Extended and Higher reach calculus-adjacent topics, functions and harder trigonometry that Core and Foundation never touch, and the grade ceiling on the lower tier closes off A Level maths. Marks go missing on multi-step problems where the method is right and the working is unreadable.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity, and specifically series and parallel circuits, is where this subject separates students. The second recurring loss is the practical paper: Cambridge sets an alternative-to-practical component that asks students to criticise an experiment they have not run, and that is a learned skill, not a knowledge recall.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles. Almost every chemistry grade in Year 11 is decided by whether the student can move fluently between mass, moles and concentration under time pressure. Organic chemistry and the reactivity series reward memory; stoichiometry rewards practice, and practice is the part students skip.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The content volume is the trap. Students revise the whole syllabus thinly and lose marks on the long-answer questions that want precise terminology: osmosis described without water potential, enzymes described without active site. Writing to the command term is worth more here than another pass through the textbook.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the comparative reading question carry most of the risk. Students who read widely still lose marks for not answering the specific task set, and for writing a general essay where the question asked for a letter, a speech or a report with a named audience.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language, with its own paper structure and a speaking component. The decision about which one a student should sit is made by the school and is occasionally wrong; a student placed in ESL who could manage First Language carries that on their transcript to university.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and further maths routes
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Maths or Further Maths, and a sensible investment for anyone targeting engineering. It bridges the step that otherwise lands in the first term of Year 12, covering calculus, matrices and harder trigonometric identities ahead of time.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the whole game. A correctly labelled supply and demand diagram with the shift drawn the right way earns marks that no amount of surrounding prose can recover. The evaluation marks at the end of structured questions are the second place students leave easy marks behind.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Application to the case material, not recall of definitions, is what the mark scheme rewards. Students who write a textbook answer about motivation theory without reference to the business in the stem are capped, and that pattern repeats through every paper.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 / 0984)
subjects.description: Two separate failure modes: the theory paper, where binary, hexadecimal and data representation are mechanical marks lost to carelessness, and the algorithm paper, where students who can code in Python still lose marks for pseudocode that does not follow the syllabus conventions.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and tutored against the school's own MoE-approved material rather than any alternative scheme. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

subjects.name: ICT (Cambridge 0417)
subjects.description: Practical papers set under exam conditions on specific software tasks, which means the gap is almost always procedural speed rather than understanding. Students who have done the tasks once rarely finish in time; students who have done them six times do.

sections.heading: What "near me" is really asking, and the honest answer
paragraphs: The search means two things at once. The first is practical: somebody my child can see regularly, without a forty-minute drive at the end of a school day. The second is the one parents rarely type: somebody who knows this exam well enough to be worth the hour. Those two requirements are not equally scarce in Al Rashidiya, and pretending they are is how families end up paying specialist money for general help.

Al Rashidiya is residential, compact and bordered by the airport, Al Garhoud and Nad Al Hamar. It has no concentration of secondary schools inside it, which means its IGCSE students are distributed across five or six school catchments in other districts. A tutor who lives in the district is not therefore a tutor who knows your child's school, their scheme of work, or the board they are entered for. Proximity delivers convenience. It does not deliver syllabus knowledge, and the grade is decided by the second one.

IB Gram's answer is to stop optimising for the map. Lessons are one to one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor selected for the syllabus code on the statement of entry. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that service exists only in India. What that trade buys an Al Rashidiya family is a pool measured in boards and codes rather than in kilometres, and a session that starts at the time it was booked for regardless of what Algeria Street is doing.

There is one thing a nearby tutor genuinely offers that video does not, and it is worth naming rather than arguing away: a young student who will not sit still for a screen. For a Year 7 or Year 8 child, physical presence can carry a lesson that video cannot. For Years 10 and 11, working from past papers in a named syllabus, the specialism matters far more, and a shared screen with annotated mark schemes is in several respects better than two people over a kitchen table.

sections.heading: Match the tutor to the code on the statement of entry
paragraphs: Every IGCSE candidate in the UAE has a statement of entry from the school listing, for each subject, the board and the syllabus code. That document is the single most useful thing a parent can bring to a first conversation with a tutor, and most parents have never opened it. The code is what tells you which papers your child sits, which past papers are relevant, and which mark scheme their work will be judged against.

The table below sets out the commonest pairs for the subjects Al Rashidiya families ask about. The point is not that one board is harder. It is that the two are structurally different in ways that make a tutor's experience non-transferable. A tutor who has drilled Cambridge 0625 alternative-to-practical questions for five years has a skill that does not map onto Pearson 4PH1, where practical understanding is examined inside the main written papers instead.

Use the table as a script. Ask the prospective tutor which code they teach, then ask them to describe the paper structure for it without looking. A specialist answers in one breath. A generalist asks which syllabus you mean, which is itself a fair answer if they say so honestly, and a bad sign if they bluff. Always confirm the current structure on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com, because boards revise specifications and a page is not a syllabus.

One more thing the code settles for you: which past papers your child should be working from. Families in this corridor swap revision material through school WhatsApp groups, and a well-meaning parent in Al Qusais passing on a folder of Cambridge 0580 papers to a child entered for Pearson 4MA1 has handed over hours of practice on the wrong question styles. Check the code on the top of any paper against the code on the statement of entry before your child spends a weekend on it. We do not supply past papers or mark schemes ourselves; those are the boards' property and the right place to get them is the board's own site.

sections.heading: Eight questions that separate a specialist from a generalist
paragraphs: Parents are routinely asked to judge a tutor on a profile and a price. That is not enough information, and the tuition market in Dubai knows it. What follows is a short interview a parent with no subject knowledge can conduct in five minutes, because every question has an answer that is either specific or evasive, and you can hear the difference without knowing any chemistry.

Run it on the trial lesson rather than before it. A tutor who is given a past question from the right syllabus and asked to teach it for forty minutes reveals more than any credential list. Watch for whether they refer to the mark scheme language, whether they can say what a grade boundary did last series, and whether they ask your child what they already tried before explaining.

The questions below are deliberately mechanical. They are not about warmth or rapport, which you can judge perfectly well yourself and which matters a great deal. They are about the thing that is hard to assess from the outside: whether this person has actually worked inside the examination your child is sitting.

Two answers should make you walk away rather than negotiate. The first is any version of a grade promise. No honest tutor promises a top grade, a band of improvement or a specific mark, and a tutor who offers one is either inexperienced or selling. The second is an offer to help with coursework in a way that involves producing any of it. Both are common enough in this market that a parent should expect to hear them at least once, and both are easier to refuse before money has changed hands than afterwards.

A note on credentials. A teaching qualification and years in a classroom are genuinely useful signals, and so is having taught the code recently. Examiner status is harder to verify and is often claimed loosely, so treat it as a detail rather than a deciding factor unless the person can evidence it. What you can always verify is the teaching itself, in forty minutes, with your child in the room and a past paper open.

Which topic in that syllabus loses the most marks, and what do you do about it?
What does the mark scheme reward in an extended-response question in this subject?

That is the whole point of listing them this way, because a rate you can check is worth more than a rate you are asked to believe.

Start at the bottom of the market rather than the top, because that is where the decision usually sits. A university-student tutor working online is advertised from around AED 45 to 65 an hour by EdFlik, and Tutopiya's published panel starts lower still. A qualified subject tutor working online is a different band: Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A specialist in a named IGCSE or IB subject sits between roughly AED 200 and 450 or above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table reaching the top of that range. The premium tier exists and is real: BartyED publishes AED 650.

The travel premium is the number worth staring at. In-home one-to-one in Dubai is quoted between AED 180 and 500 an hour, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor working online. The gap is not buying better teaching. It is buying a car journey, and in the eastern suburbs it is buying a car journey through the worst of the afternoon. Monthly packages seen in the market tell the same story: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, against AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four in-home sessions of two hours. sections.heading: Proximity against specialism: the trade the map forces
paragraphs: Suppose your child is entered for Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 Extended and is losing marks on circuits and on the alternative-to-practical paper. Searching by distance from Al Rashidiya gives you a set of candidates defined by geography. Searching by syllabus gives you a set defined by the exam. The two sets overlap, but not reliably, and the smaller the niche the less they overlap.

This matters most in exactly the cases where tutoring is most worth buying. A general maths tutor near the airport can help a Year 8 student with fractions, and that is a real service. A Year 11 student who needs someone to mark twenty 0625 Paper 6 questions against the published mark scheme and name the pattern in the losses needs a narrower person, and narrowing by district throws most of those people away before you start.

The table sets the trade out plainly, including the things the in-home option genuinely wins. Nobody should pretend video is better at everything. It is better at matching, at scheduling, at recording what happened, and at not losing forty minutes of a paid hour to Algeria Street at 4pm. It is worse at a restless nine-year-old, and it needs a working camera and a quiet room, which in a shared villa is sometimes the real constraint.

The quiet room is worth planning for rather than hoping about. An Al Rashidiya household with younger siblings, a grandmother visiting and a television running will not produce a useful hour at 6pm in the living room, and the lesson will be blamed when the room was the problem. A bedroom desk, a door that closes, headphones and the laptop on a stable surface rather than a lap is the whole setup. Families who sort that out in the first week get noticeably more from the same money than families who do not.

One case genuinely goes the other way. A student with a diagnosed need that requires physical prompting or hands-on support is better served in person, and we will say so rather than take the booking. IB Gram does not place tutors in UAE homes under any circumstances, so for that family the honest recommendation is a local provider and a MoHRE-permitted tutor they can verify.

sections.heading: The exam calendar read backwards from results day
paragraphs: The deadline that catches families out is not the exam. It is the entry. A school enters its candidates months before the first paper, and a decision made at that point about tier or about which series a student sits is difficult and sometimes impossible to change afterwards. Reading the calendar backwards is how you find the dates that actually require a decision from you.

Get the series right first. UAE candidates sit the June and the November series. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only, so a plan built around a March window is a plan for the wrong country, and that error has reached UAE parents on other pages. Cambridge also allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school's exams officer which zone the centre is in.

For dated worked examples, Pearson's published record is the checkable one. The Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are past dates, which is exactly why they are safe to plan against as a shape. Always open the live official timetable rather than trusting any restated date, including ours, because provisional timetables are revised.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects, and what they mean for a tutoring plan
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. That is a useful thing for a parent to know, because the KHDA inspection report for your child's school is public and specific, and it will often name the subjects where attainment is weakest. If you are deciding which single subject to tutor, that document is better evidence than a hunch.

KHDA also sets requirements that run alongside whichever international curriculum the school is licensed for. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, and KHDA's guidance states those requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

Two practical consequences follow for an Al Rashidiya family. First, your child's timetable carries more subjects than the IGCSE block alone, and tutoring time has to be budgeted against the whole week rather than the exam subjects only. Second, for the mandatory subjects the content is constrained: KHDA states that the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the MoE, is strictly prohibited. Arabic tutoring therefore works from the school's own approved material, not from an alternative scheme, and any tutor who offers you a better syllabus for Arabic is offering you something the regulator does not allow. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA and makes no such claim; we explain what the regulator requires, and link you to its own pages.
