sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and the subject count a ranking page gets wrong
paragraphs: An IGCSE certificate earned in Dubai is used for two different things: a university application, and a Ministry of Education equivalency file if the student stays in the UAE system. The second one has published requirements that a surprising number of tutoring pages either ignore or state incorrectly, and getting it wrong costs a family a year.

For the British track, as reported in July 2026, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects. One page currently ranking for UAE tutoring queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The published rule is five, and if you are planning a subject load around that number it matters.

Two cautions. There is no verified IB points threshold for equivalency available from the ministry's own pages, so no figure of that kind appears here; if your child is on the Diploma route, ask the ministry or the school's registrar directly. And equivalency is a process the ministry runs, not something a tutoring service performs, guarantees or accelerates. Tutoring is not required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. Verify every requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority before acting on it.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on assessed work
paragraphs: This section exists because of what is on sale in this search result. One page in the researched set advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. That is not tutoring. It is a route to a malpractice finding against the student, and the student carries the consequence, not the seller.

The boundary is simple to state and easy to hold. A tutor may teach the skill, explain the criteria, model the method on a different example, ask questions about the student's draft, and name where an argument is unsupported. A tutor may not write, draft, complete, rewrite or edit to completion any part of an assessed submission. For IGCSE that covers coursework components, practical write-ups, ICT practical tasks and language speaking preparation. For students moving into the Diploma it covers the Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay.

There is a practical test a parent can apply. If a tutor's feedback arrives as sentences your child can paste in, the line has been crossed. If it arrives as questions your child has to answer themselves, it has not. We also decline to supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; those belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and the right thing to do is to point you at the official page and let you download them from the source.

Parents sometimes worry that holding this line puts their child at a disadvantage against classmates who are not holding it. The honest answer is that it might, briefly, on one piece of work, and that the trade is still not close. A malpractice finding follows a student through an appeal, a university application and occasionally a whole qualification, and the people selling finished coursework bear none of that. Tell your child the line, tell the tutor the line, and ask to see the feedback rather than only the final mark.

sections.heading: Starting, and what we will tell you if nobody suitable is free
paragraphs: The first step is the statement of entry, or failing that a photograph of the most recent report and the subject teacher's comments. With the board, the code and the tier known, matching is a narrow problem rather than a broad one. Without them, a first lesson is spent working out what the student is actually entered for, which is a waste of a paid hour.

A trial lesson is free and is a real lesson, not a sales call. It runs forty minutes on a past question in the right syllabus, with the tutor teaching and your child working. Afterwards you get the tutor's written read on what the loss pattern looks like and how many weeks of work it implies, and you decide. There is no card required to book it, and no obligation attached to it.

Sometimes the answer is that nobody suitable is free. Niche combinations run short: a particular minority language, a specific ICT practical specification, a November resit in an unusual subject at two weeks' notice. When that happens we say so and give you a realistic match time rather than putting a generalist in the slot and hoping. A tutor who does not know the code will cost you the fee and the weeks, and the weeks are the expensive part in Year 11.

Data you send us is limited to what the matching actually needs: the subject, the board and code, the year group, the school if you want the scheme of work followed, and a contact for scheduling. We do not need a photograph of your child, a full academic history or a list of grades across every subject, and you should be wary of any form that asks for them without saying why. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs personal data here, and the privacy link on this page sets out what is held and how to have it deleted.

If you are weighing this up against a tuition centre or a neighbour's recommendation, the comparison worth making is not price per hour. It is whether the person in the lesson has taught the paper your child is losing marks on. Everything on this page, from the code table to the published market rates, exists so you can make that comparison yourself, with or without us.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IGCSE tutor near me in Al Rashidiya who knows my child's syllabus?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but distance is the wrong filter. Al Rashidiya has no secondary school concentration of its own, so its IGCSE students are spread across catchments in Al Garhoud, Mirdif, Al Qusais and Al Warqa. The number of people within a short drive who have taught Cambridge 0625 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher through to a final paper is small, and smaller still for a specific weak paper. IB Gram matches on the syllabus code instead and teaches one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, which widens the pool from one district to every tutor who teaches that code.

faqs.question: Where do I find the syllabus code my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: On the statement of entry the school issues ahead of each exam series. It lists, per subject, the board and the syllabus code: 0580 or 4MA1 for maths, 0625 or 4PH1 for physics, and so on. Your school's exams officer holds it and will send a copy. If the series is still some way off, the subject teacher or the head of department can confirm which board and tier the class is working towards. Bring that code to any tutoring conversation; it turns a vague request into a specific one and makes a bad match much harder.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether my child sits Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: For choosing a tutor, yes. The two are separate qualifications with different paper structures, different command-term conventions and separate past-paper banks. Cambridge Physics 0625 sets a practical or alternative-to-practical component; Pearson 4PH1 examines practical understanding inside the written papers. Pearson English works from a set anthology, Cambridge from unseen passages. A tutor fluent in one is not automatically useful in the other, and a student practising the wrong board's past papers is practising the wrong thing. Confirm the current structure on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com rather than on any third-party page.

faqs.question: Which exam series do IGCSE students in Dubai sit?
faqs.answer: The June series and the November series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in those two series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any plan built around a March exam window is a plan for a different country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between Core and Extended, and can we change tier?
faqs.answer: Extended covers more content and carries a higher grade ceiling; Core is capped, which can close off A Level routes in the same subject. The tier is fixed at entry, which falls months before the first paper, so the decision point is earlier than most families expect. If your child is borderline, the conversation to have is with the subject teacher before the entry deadline, with evidence from mock papers rather than impressions. After entry, moving tier is difficult and sometimes not possible for that series.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay an IGCSE tutor around the eastern suburbs?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai, each read on the provider's own page, run from roughly AED 45 to 65 an hour for a university-student tutor online, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to 450 or above for a named IGCSE or IB specialist, and up to AED 650 at the premium end. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, which includes the travel. None of those is an IB Gram rate; they are the market, published by others, and you can check each one yourself.

faqs.question: Why is in-home tutoring quoted so much higher than online in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the price includes a car journey, and in the eastern suburbs it is a slow one. A tutor driving from Al Garhoud or Mirdif into Al Rashidiya between 3pm and 6pm spends a significant part of the chargeable hour on Algeria Street or at the Garhoud interchange, and that time is recovered in the rate. The market gap tells the story: AED 180 to 500 in-home against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor working online. The extra is not buying better teaching, and IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE at all.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 11 with mocks already done badly. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: No, but the format has to change. A weekly general subject lesson from here is too slow. What works is an intensive block aimed at one paper: two or three sessions a week for six to ten weeks, built entirely from past questions in the right syllabus code, marked against the published mark scheme, with the loss pattern named and drilled. A mock paper that came back two bands low usually hides two or three repeating errors rather than a general lack of knowledge, and those are fixable in weeks.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the clearest cases for a specialist. That paper does not ask a student to perform an experiment; it asks them to read a described method, identify the control variables, criticise the procedure and interpret someone else's results. That is a written skill, practised on past questions with a shared screen and the mark scheme open. What online cannot do is replace the school's own laboratory work, which your child still needs and which the school provides.

faqs.question: Should I ask an Al Rashidiya tutor to show me their MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. Ask a prospective tutor directly whether they hold the permit; the official route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service.

faqs.question: Can my child's own schoolteacher tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: Treat it as off limits. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Verify the current wording against the authority's own policy document before relying on it. Beyond the rules, there is a straightforward conflict in paying the person who marks your child's work, and it is worth avoiding even where it might be permitted.

faqs.question: With eight or nine IGCSE subjects running, how many should we tutor at the same time?
faqs.answer: One, almost always, at least to begin with. A Year 11 student carrying eight or nine IGCSE subjects plus Arabic and the other mandatory subjects has limited absorbing capacity after a school day that ends with a long bus route. Two sessions a week in the weakest subject moves a grade; one session a week in four subjects usually moves none. Pick the subject where the gap is widest or where the grade blocks a post-16 route, fix that, and reassess after six lessons against marks rather than impressions.

faqs.question: What do you send us after each lesson?
faqs.answer: A short written note: what was covered, which questions were worked, where marks were lost and what to practise before the next session. It is deliberately specific enough to be checked. If the note says the student struggled with mole calculations in a titration question, you can look at the next school test and see whether that changed. Vague feedback is the easiest thing in the world to produce and tells you nothing, so the note names topics and question types rather than describing effort.

faqs.question: What happens if there is no specialist free for my child's subject?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with a realistic match time, rather than putting a generalist in the slot. The combinations that run short are predictable: minority languages, specific ICT practical specifications, and November resits requested at a fortnight's notice. If the wait is too long for your timeline we will say that too. A tutor who does not know the syllabus code costs a family the fee and, more expensively in Year 11, the weeks, so disclosure is the cheaper outcome for everyone.

faqs.question: What exactly is attached to the free IGCSE trial lesson?
faqs.answer: It is one lesson of about forty minutes, at no charge, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue. The only condition is that it is a teaching session rather than an open-ended consultation: your child works on a past question in their own syllabus code while the tutor teaches. Afterwards you receive the tutor's written read on the loss pattern and the likely number of weeks required, and you decide from there. If you do not continue, nothing is owed and nothing is charged.

intro.heading: Distance is the weakest signal in the whole decision
paragraphs: A map search answers the question it was asked. Type IGCSE tutor near me in Al Safa and you get results ranked by how close they are, which would be the right ranking for a dentist and is the wrong one for a subject specialist. The variables that actually predict whether a grade moves are whether the tutor teaches the exact syllabus code your child is entered for, whether they can read a mark scheme at component level, and whether the slot survives the school run. None of those correlates with distance.

That is worth saying carefully rather than dismissively, because the instinct behind the search is sound. Parents want somebody accountable, somebody who understands the local schools, somebody who will not cancel. Those are real requirements. The argument of this page is that proximity is a poor proxy for all three, and that there are better proxies available: a written diagnosis, a named target, a session recording, and a tutor matched on code rather than on postcode.

The second half of this page is a comparison of the neighbourhoods, because the brief for this page is comparison and because the comparison is genuinely useful. Al Safa, Al Wasl, Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim share much of one school catchment and differ in ways that change a tutoring plan: arrival times home, which schools each one feeds, what subject demand looks like, and how much slack an evening has in it. A family that understands those differences schedules better than one that does not.

The third theme is the provider models. An Al Safa parent can choose between an agency, an international marketplace, an independent freelance tutor, a tuition centre group class, the school's own after-school support, and an online platform. These are genuinely different products with different rate bands, different depth on a narrow requirement, and different positions on the permit question. Comparing models rather than brands is both fairer and more useful.

On delivery, the position is fixed and stated upfront. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we offer only in India, and the Dubai in-home market is published at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel by other providers for families who want somebody in the room. Our Al Safa lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper and mark scheme on a shared screen.

The pages beside this one in Al Safa go deeper on boards and codes, on individual subjects, and on the Diploma. This one is about the choice itself: who is actually available to an Al Safa family, what each option costs, and what questions settle it.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-safa.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects most requested across the Al Safa catchment, with a note on how each one behaves when a parent is choosing between provider models.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The most requested subject in this catchment. Tiered, so the entry decision matters, and the loss pattern is method marks never written down. Group classes rarely fix that because it requires watching an individual student's working, which is why one-to-one wins here.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: Untiered in the Cambridge sense, with longer question setups and different formula provision. The common failure is a tutor working from Cambridge material, which is a matching problem rather than a teaching one and is invisible until a mock.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity and circuit reasoning account for most Extended losses. A narrow requirement, which is exactly where a distance-ranked shortlist fails: the right specialist for circuits may be nowhere near Al Safa.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole and concentration calculations under time pressure, plus organic naming and reaction conditions. Predictable enough that a well-matched eight-week block moves marks reliably, and poorly served by broad revision classes.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Content-dense, which makes it look suited to self-study and group revision. The marks actually sit in command-term precision and in genetics layout, both of which need an individual script to be seen and corrected.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language 0510 and 0511
subjects.description: Writing tasks marked for purpose and audience as much as accuracy. Strong students lose marks writing a competent piece aimed at the wrong reader, which only shows up when somebody reads their script closely.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500
subjects.description: Directed writing, composition and reading response under tight timing. Planning for two minutes before writing is the main intervention, and it is behavioural, so it needs a tutor who will insist rather than a class that moves on.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with marks for applying a tool to the specific stimulus. Frameworks learned generically plateau around the middle grades, and the fix is a writing structure taught against marked answers.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy plus evaluation. Unlabelled axes cost marks a student does not expect, and extended answers that explain without judging forfeit the evaluation marks entirely.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Two papers each, with practical understanding examined inside the written papers. Any provider shortlist has to be filtered on board before anything else, because question phrasing differs enough to invalidate the wrong practice.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: Theory plus algorithm design, pseudocode and trace tables. A narrow specialism with fewer tutors in any given area, which is the clearest case in this list for ignoring distance entirely.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Arabic
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum in Dubai, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language and requiring Arabic teachers to hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach the subject.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-safa.regionsTitle: Al Safa against the catchments either side of it
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-safa.regionsIntro: These four communities share most of one school catchment and behave differently in practice. The differences are about timing, demand and provision rather than about housing, and they are what a comparison should actually cover.

regions.name: Al Safa 1
regions.note: Several British secondaries within walking distance, so arrival home is among the earliest in this part of Dubai. A 4pm start is workable here, which no neighbouring community can reliably match.

regions.name: Al Safa 2
regions.note: Bordering Al Quoz 1 across Sheikh Zayed Road. Runs are slightly longer, and this is where Saturday morning sessions are most heavily used because weekday evenings fill with activities.

regions.name: Al Wasl
regions.note: Inland along Al Wasl Road, sharing the Al Safa catchment almost entirely. Nearly identical timing, which is why a tutor's Al Safa slot and Al Wasl slot can sit back to back without risk.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1
regions.note: Older villa stock near the beach road. Beach Road congestion at pick-up makes anything before 4.45pm unreliable in the cooler months, which is a real difference from Al Safa rather than a marginal one.

regions.name: Jumeirah 2
regions.note: School-dense, with primaries inside the community. Younger siblings arrive home well before secondary students, so households here are the most likely to need two separate slots on the same evening.

regions.name: Jumeirah 3
regions.note: Reaching towards Umm Suqeim. Secondary students travel further, pushing a realistic first slot to 5pm, and mock-week rescheduling is noticeably more common from this stretch.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Short along the coast and slow inland at peak. Families here move sessions to Friday afternoon or the weekend in the weeks before a series more often than any other community in this comparison.

regions.name: Al Manara
regions.note: Inland of Umm Suqeim near Al Khail Road. Children spread across several school groups, so sibling bookings here commonly span two boards and occasionally two curricula.

regions.name: Al Quoz 1
regions.note: Across Sheikh Zayed Road, closer off-peak and considerably further at 3pm. Buses returning from schools on its edge are the latest arrivals in this comparison, which pushes slots past 5pm.

sections.heading: What a near me search actually returns in Al Safa
paragraphs: A distance-ranked list of tutors in Al Safa mixes together things that are not comparable. Some entries are agencies that will send whoever is free. Some are individual freelance tutors with a genuine specialism and no replacement policy. Some are tuition centres offering group classes under a one-to-one headline. Some are international marketplaces whose nearest tutor is nowhere near Dubai and whose prices are quoted in a currency UAE families do not transact in.

Sorting that list by distance tells you almost nothing about which of those you are looking at. What does tell you is a short set of questions, and they are the same questions regardless of which model a provider belongs to. Which board and syllabus code does the tutor teach? Have they taught that code in the current syllabus cycle? What happens if the match is wrong after two sessions? Is the tutor a group-class teacher being sold as a one-to-one specialist?

The second thing a distance search hides is the pool size for a narrow requirement. Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478 pseudocode is a specific thing to teach. So is circuit reasoning in Physics 0625 for an Extended candidate. The number of people in Al Safa and its immediate neighbours who can teach those well is small; the number who can teach them well and are free at 4.30pm on a Tuesday is smaller again. Accepting live video turns that small number into a large one.

None of this means the local market is bad. It means the ranking is wrong. A parent in Al Safa who asks about code, cycle, replacement policy and format will usually end up choosing a different tutor from the one the map put first, and will be able to say why.

sections.heading: Al Safa against Al Wasl, Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
paragraphs: These four communities share most of one school catchment, so the schools are not the variable. What differs is journey time, arrival home, and the way that shapes which slot a household can actually keep. A comparison that only lists schools misses the thing that decides whether a tutoring block survives to week eight.

Al Safa 1 is the best-placed of the four for early sessions, because several British secondaries sit within walking distance and students are home soonest. Al Wasl behaves almost identically, which is why a tutor can run consecutive Al Safa and Al Wasl slots without risk. Jumeirah 1 to 3 add Beach Road congestion at pick-up, which does not add much distance but adds unpredictability, and unpredictability is worse than delay for a fixed weekly slot.

Umm Suqeim is the genuine outlier. The coastal run is short and the inland run at peak is not, and it sits at the edge of a second catchment with more IB continuum provision. Families here are the most frequent users of weekend sessions in this comparison, and that is a scheduling consequence rather than a preference. Al Quoz 1, across Sheikh Zayed Road, produces the latest arrivals of all, because returning buses cross the heaviest traffic.

The conclusion is the same for all four, which is the honest version of a comparison page: because every one of them is choosing from a tutor pool constrained by travel, and because the schools are shared, the answer that works best is the one that removes travel from the equation entirely. That is not a coincidence of our business model; it is what the timing data in this catchment implies.

sections.heading: The six provider models an Al Safa parent can choose between
paragraphs: Comparing brands is unproductive and, where it involves claims about a competitor's pricing or quality, unfair. Comparing models is neither. There are six genuinely different products available to a family in this catchment, and they differ on rate, on how deep the pool is for a narrow requirement, on what happens when a match fails, and on how transparent the permit position is.

An agency recruits tutors and places them, which gives a replacement policy and a single point of contact at the cost of a margin. An international marketplace offers the widest pool and the least local knowledge, and frequently quotes in a foreign currency. An independent freelance tutor can be excellent value and carries no replacement capacity: if the fit is wrong, the family starts again. A tuition centre group class is cheapest per student and cannot watch an individual student's working. School after-school support is included in fees and limited to the school's own staff and board. An online platform trades physical presence for pool depth.

On the permit question the models differ in how easy verification is. Any individual providing private lessons needs the MoHRE private tutor work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. A parent can ask about either, and the quality of the answer is informative in itself.

What a comparison cannot do honestly is declare a winner for everybody. A Year 8 student who needs structure is well served by a group class or a budget-band tutor. A Year 11 Extended candidate eight weeks from a series with a diagnosed weakness in one topic is not. The table below is built so a parent can find their own row rather than be told a conclusion.

sections.heading: What proximity buys, and what it costs you
paragraphs: Proximity does buy real things and it is worth being precise about them. A tutor in the room can see whether a student is actually writing. They can confiscate a phone. They can notice that a child is tired rather than confused. For a younger student, or one with attention difficulties, those are not trivial advantages and no amount of screen sharing replaces them.

What proximity costs is specificity, and the cost is measured in the size of the pool. For Mathematics 0580 Extended, a large catchment like Al Safa plus Al Wasl plus Jumeirah probably contains several capable tutors. For Computer Science 0478 pseudocode, or Physics 0625 electromagnetism for a student targeting the top grades, or Pearson 4CH1 specifically rather than Cambridge 0620, the local count drops quickly. The narrower the requirement, the more expensive proximity becomes in terms of what you give up.

There is a monetary cost too, and it is checkable. Published in-home one-to-one rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, per Bestimate's 2026 table and independent home-tutor listings, while published qualified online subject tutor rates run AED 150 to 300, Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. The gap between those bands buys a car journey across Sheikh Zayed Road at pick-up, which is not teaching.

The sensible way to use this is to decide which problem you have. If the problem is that your child will not work unless watched, buy presence. If the problem is that your child does not understand functions in 0580 Extended, buy the person who teaches functions best and accept that they may live elsewhere. Most Al Safa families who state their problem precisely discover it is the second one.

sections.heading: What an Al Safa parent can verify without taking anyone's word
paragraphs: Rather than opening with a rate, open with what is independently checkable, because that is the part of this market a parent has real power over. KHDA publishes an inspection band for every Dubai private school annually, on a six-point scale, on its own site. KHDA also confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Both facts are readable at source in a few minutes.

The permit position is equally checkable in principle. MoHRE's service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and applications run through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. A tutor who is vague about whether they hold one, on a permit that is free and takes two working days, has told you something.

Now the rates, each attributed so they can be checked. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel. Specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 500 to 650, BartyED publishing AED 650.

On monthly figures, Bestimate's estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, against advertised packages of AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. None of these is an IB Gram price. We quote against a plan after a free trial, because the honest number depends on the subject, the code and how many weeks remain.

sections.heading: Availability, and what happens when nobody suitable is free
paragraphs: No competitor page we examined in this market discloses a coverage limit, which is implausible. Narrow requirements run out everywhere. The useful question is not whether a provider sometimes has no suitable tutor but what they do when that happens, and whether they tell you before taking payment.

Our answer is to say so. If no specialist covering your child's code and component is free in the window you need, we will tell you rather than placing a generalist in the slot. Where the right specialist for a narrow IGCSE code is based outside the UAE, the lesson is still one-to-one over live video, and we say upfront where the tutor is rather than concealing it behind a local-looking contact number. Two ranking competitors in this market route UAE parents to numbers in another country without mentioning it.

There is a timing dimension too. The weeks before a series are when demand concentrates, which is exactly when the narrow specialisms become hardest to staff. A family that enquires in September for a June series has a wider choice than one enquiring in March, and that is worth knowing because it is the opposite of how most households behave. Booking early does not mean buying more sessions; it means securing the right tutor for the sessions you intend to buy.

The last dimension is replacement. A single freelance tutor cannot replace themselves. An agency or a platform can, and the value of that only becomes visible when a match goes wrong in week three with six weeks to go. Ask any provider what their replacement process is before paying, and treat an unclear answer as the answer.

sections.heading: The regulator map, and why it belongs on a near me page
paragraphs: A search for somebody nearby is in part a search for somebody accountable, and in the UAE accountability for schools sits with named regulators that a parent can actually read. Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects schools annually.

The rest of the country differs, which matters if a family relocates. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there; both approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the regulator's remit extends well past inspection. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. ADEK is named by almost nobody else writing about tutoring in this market.

The mandatory subject rules also belong here, because they shape the week a tutoring slot has to fit into. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, prohibits combined classes for the two groups, calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, and requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

Dubai's scale is worth holding as context for any comparison of local options: 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with the 2026-27 intake adding seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places after six opened in 2025-26. A market that large contains good and bad provision in every model, which is why model-level and question-level comparison beats choosing by distance.

sections.heading: Questions that settle it, and the honesty boundary
paragraphs: Here is the list we would want a parent to use on us as well as on anybody else. Which board and syllabus code will you teach, and have you taught it in the current cycle? Which component is my child losing marks on, and how do you know? What will the first four sessions do, specifically? What happens if the match is wrong after two sessions? Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? Where are you based, and what time zone do you schedule in?

A provider who answers those crisply is a better bet than one who answers warmly. Note what is absent from the list: how many students they have taught, what percentage improved, and any rating. Statistics without a stated sample, date and method are not evidence, and several pages in this market publish review counts and ratings that contradict each other on the same page. A figure that cannot be sourced should not move your decision.

The academic-honesty boundary is the last question and the most important. A tutor teaches, questions, reviews and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not write, complete or dictate coursework, an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or anything else submitted for assessment. One seller in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at a published price; that is an academic-integrity breach and the consequences fall on the student.

Finally, what nobody in this market should claim and we do not. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, Ministry of Education, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation, licence or partnership. We operate no premises in the UAE. We do not perform Ministry of Education equivalency or attestation, and tutoring is not required for equivalency, admission or progression. Every one of those claims appears somewhere in this SERP, and none of them is ours to make.

process.description: Not the subject, the component. Functions in 0580 Extended, or circuits in 0625, or composition timing in 0500. A precise problem makes the shortlist short, and a short shortlist is how a family avoids choosing the first result on a map.

process.description: You get a short note naming the cause of the lost marks, the target, and what the next four sessions will do. This is what replaces physical presence as the accountability mechanism, and it is more checkable than somebody at a kitchen table.

process.title: A slot chosen for your community, not generically
process.description: Al Safa 1 can hold a 4pm start; Umm Suqeim usually cannot. We pick the slot from how your actual school run behaves, because a block that loses three sessions to traffic is not the block you paid for.

process.description: Midway through, the same question types return and the marks are compared. If nothing has moved on the diagnosed cause, the plan changes or the tutor does. Carrying on because the sessions are booked is the failure mode this step exists to prevent.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether an IGCSE tutor actually lives near Al Safa?
faqs.answer: Less than almost anything else you could ask about. What predicts a grade moving is whether the tutor teaches your child's exact board and syllabus code, whether they can diagnose which component is losing marks, and whether the slot survives the school run. None of those correlates with distance. Proximity does buy real things for a younger or easily distracted student, where somebody in the room can see whether work is actually happening. For a Year 11 student with a diagnosed weakness in one topic, the specialist who teaches that topic best is the right choice wherever they are.

faqs.question: How does Al Safa compare with Al Wasl and Jumeirah for tutoring?
faqs.answer: The schools are largely shared, so provision is not the variable; timing is. Al Safa 1 has several British secondaries within walking distance and is the best placed of the four for an early 4pm session. Al Wasl behaves almost identically. Jumeirah 1 to 3 add Beach Road congestion at pick-up, pushing a reliable slot to 4.45pm or 5pm, and the unpredictability matters more than the delay. Umm Suqeim, in the next catchment over, ends up on weekend sessions most often. Al Quoz-side bus routes produce the latest arrivals of all.

faqs.question: Which is better value in Al Safa, an agency, a freelance tutor or an online platform?
faqs.answer: It depends on the problem and the stage. A freelance tutor can be excellent value and carries no replacement capacity, so a wrong match means starting again. An agency provides replacement and a single contact at the cost of a margin, with market specialist rates quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above. An online platform trades physical presence for a much deeper pool on a narrow code. A tuition centre group class is cheapest per student and cannot watch an individual's working. For Years 7 to 9 the cheap options are often adequate; for Year 11 component work they usually are not.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor before paying anything?
faqs.answer: Six questions settle most of it. Which board and syllabus code will you teach, and have you taught it in the current cycle? Which component is my child losing marks on, and how do you know? What will the first four sessions do specifically? What happens if the match is wrong after two sessions? Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? Where are you based and what time zone do you schedule in? Crisp answers matter more than warm ones, and vagueness on a free two-year permit is itself informative.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to an address in Al Safa?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Al Safa lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper and official mark scheme on a shared screen and a recording available afterwards. We target this search because it is what parents type, then answer it honestly rather than implying a service we do not sell. The Dubai in-home market exists and publishes AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel if you prefer that.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tutors near Al Safa actually charge?
faqs.answer: Market bands, each attributed to its publisher: budget online and university-student tutors AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors AED 150 to 300, Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home one-to-one visits AED 180 to 500 including travel, Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350. Specialists AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tutors AED 500 to 650, BartyED publishing AED 650. None is an IB Gram price; we quote after the free trial against a stated plan.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class worth considering for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For broad revision before mocks it can be, and it is the cheapest option per student. What it cannot do is watch one student's working, which is where a large share of recoverable IGCSE marks sit: method marks never written down, a command term misread, a graph drawn to personal taste rather than to the mark scheme. If the diagnosis from a marked script is a narrow topic or a technique habit, a group class will not reach it. If the problem is that a whole syllabus was never covered properly, a class can help.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor be matched for a student in Al Safa?
faqs.answer: For common requests such as Cambridge Mathematics 0580 Extended, days. For narrower ones such as Pearson Edexcel 4CH1 specifically, or Computer Science 0478 pseudocode, it can be a week or more, and in the final six weeks before a series the wait is at its longest because that is when demand concentrates. If nobody suitable is free in your window we will say so rather than putting a generalist in the slot, and we will tell you where a specialist is based if they are outside the UAE.

faqs.question: How do I check that a private tutor in Dubai is permitted to teach?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school-registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: What time should a weekly session be for a family in Al Safa?
faqs.answer: If you are in Al Safa 1, take 4pm or 4.30pm. Students here are home earliest in this comparison, and a session before fatigue sets in is worth more than a longer one later. Al Safa 2 and Al Wasl work well at 4.30pm. From Jumeirah 1 to 3 start at 4.45pm or 5pm and accept it, because Beach Road at pick-up is unpredictable rather than merely slow. From Umm Suqeim or an Al Quoz-side bus route, a weekend block plus a short midweek review is usually the arrangement that survives.

faqs.question: Should I trust a tutoring page that advertises a satisfaction percentage?
faqs.answer: Not without a sample size, a date and a stated method on the same page. Pages in this market publish figures such as a rating out of five from several hundred reviews, and some show two different review counts within the same page. Self-asserted ratings in structured data that differ from the visible figure are against Google's structured-data policy and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, a consumer-protection exposure. A provider who cannot produce the underlying data has published a decoration rather than evidence, and it should not move your decision.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle two children in the same Al Safa household?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is frequently the right arrangement where both children need technique rather than deep subject content. Method writing, command terms and timed practice are the same skills across subjects and year groups. Where it breaks down is when one child needs Extended-level depth in a specific science and the other needs Year 8 structure; those are different tutors. Scheduling is the other constraint: in Jumeirah 2 a primary-age sibling is often home an hour before a secondary student, which makes two separate slots simpler than one shared one.

faqs.question: Which schools do children in Al Safa and Umm Suqeim actually attend?
faqs.answer: Al Safa, Al Wasl and the Jumeirah communities draw on a largely shared set of British-curriculum secondaries inside or close to Al Safa, which is why those communities belong in one comparison. Umm Suqeim and Al Sufouh form a second cluster with more IB continuum provision and longer runs from Al Safa. KHDA inspects every Dubai private school annually and publishes a band on a six-point scale; read the current band on KHDA's own listing rather than a rating quoted on a tutoring page, which may be two cycles old.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring a compromise or a genuine choice for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For IGCSE work it is a genuine choice and often the stronger one, because the work is document work. The past paper, the official mark scheme and the student's own script can all be on a shared screen, with the tutor pointing at the exact phrase that lost the mark. The pool argument is decisive on narrow requirements: the number of people who teach Physics 0625 electromagnetism well and are free at 4.30pm within a short drive of Al Safa is small. The exception is a student who genuinely will not work without somebody in the room.

faqs.question: How do the mandatory UAE subjects affect choosing a tutoring slot?
faqs.answer: They make the school week fuller than the IGCSE subject list suggests. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies and calculating instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit. Fewer evening hours are genuinely free than a parent expects, which is why one protected weekly slot chosen around the real school run beats an ambitious plan a household cannot keep.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor turns out to be wrong for my child?
faqs.answer: Ask every provider this before paying, because the answers differ sharply by model. A single freelance tutor cannot replace themselves, so the family restarts the search. An agency or a platform can, and that capacity only reveals its value when a match fails in week three with six weeks to the papers. With us, the free trial exists to catch a mismatch before money changes hands, and if a paid block is not working we will change the tutor rather than let the sessions run down.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-safa.closingHeading: Stop sorting by distance and start sorting by code
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-safa.closingBody: Two actions change the quality of your shortlist more than any amount of searching. Ask the exams officer for the board and syllabus code for each subject, so you can filter every option on whether it actually matches. Then name the component rather than the subject when you enquire, so a tutor has to answer with specifics instead of reassurance. After that, book a free trial lesson on a past-paper question from that component and judge the explanation yourself. Lessons run online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, at a time chosen around how your own Al Safa school run actually behaves.

intro.heading: What an IGCSE tutor actually costs a Satwa family
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible tutoring sites in Dubai publish no price at all. One of them runs an FAQ that asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer it. The two that do quote a figure quote it in US dollars, which is not the currency anybody in Al Satwa pays a tutor in. So the first job of this page is arithmetic: real AED bands, named sources, and the monthly number that is the one you will actually budget against.

Al Satwa sits between Sheikh Zayed Road and the Jumeirah coast, a dense older district of low-rise apartments and villa compounds where most households are on a salary rather than an expatriate package with an education allowance. Almost no private schools sit inside Satwa itself. Children travel out — to Al Safa, Oud Metha, Al Mankhool, Jumeirah 1, Al Barsha — which means the family is already paying for a bus seat or a daily drive before a single tutoring hour is bought. That changes the maths. An in-home tutor who adds forty minutes of Dubai traffic to each visit is charging for that traffic, and in a district with this commute pattern the premium is larger than most families expect.

Here is the honest shape of the market, before any argument about which model is better. Online tutoring at the budget end runs from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65, Tutopiya from about AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits in the AED 150 to 300 band, and Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. An in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, is quoted at AED 180 to 500 — Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts the usual range at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors asking 200 to 500. An IGCSE or A-Level specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and upward; TutorChase lists AED 270. The premium named or examiner tier starts around AED 500 and BartyED asks AED 650.

Those are market figures, attributed, not an IB Gram price list. What matters more for a Satwa household is what sits inside each band, because the bands are not selling the same thing. An AED 45 hour buys a university student who finished IGCSE four years ago and is working from a revision guide. An AED 250 hour buys somebody who knows that Cambridge Maths 0580 Extended and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different formula provision, and who can tell you which one your child is entered for after looking at a single past paper. The gap between those two hours is not politeness or presentation. It is diagnosis — whether the tutor can tell you, in week one, which three topics are actually costing marks.

The other thing nobody writes down is where the money leaks. Families in this district overspend in four reliably repeated ways: buying hours before buying a diagnosis, paying a travel premium for a tutor who is weaker than an online specialist, running group sessions for a child whose problem is specific rather than general, and starting eight weeks before the June series when the same spend across the preceding year would have bought three times the effect. Each of those is costed further down this page.

IB Gram's own model is one-to-one and delivered live online to Al Satwa, with the first lesson free so the diagnosis costs you nothing. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is a limit, stated plainly, and the comparison table below makes the case for why a Satwa family is better served by it anyway.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-satwa.programmesIntro: An IGCSE search from Al Satwa usually covers a wider age range than the acronym suggests. Children in this district sit Checkpoint tests at the end of lower secondary, start the IGCSE courses in Year 10, and then split towards A Level or the IB Diploma. Each stage costs a different amount to support, for reasons worth naming.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE courses begin, assessed internally with optional Checkpoint tests at the end of Year 9. Nothing here appears on a university application, which is exactly why it is the cheapest stage to fix and the one families skip. Algebraic fluency, proportional reasoning and scientific method are built here or not at all.
programmes.countryNote: Al Satwa children at this stage are usually at a school in Al Mankhool, Oud Metha or Al Safa, and the Year 9 subject choice conversation happens in the second term. A term of support at this point costs a fraction of a Year 11 rescue, because the same topic can be taught slowly rather than against a deadline.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, examined in a June or November series. Cambridge offers Core and Extended tiers in several subjects; Pearson's International GCSE is untiered in most but runs modular assessment in some. The syllabus code on the exam entry decides what your child sits, and it is printed on the statement of entry the school issues.
programmes.countryNote: For the Ministry of Education equivalency route, British-track students must pass five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count. That rule decides which five subjects are worth paying to protect, and a Satwa parent can read it on the official clarification rather than taking a tutor's word for it.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: The route most IGCSE students in this part of Dubai take next, with three or four subjects taken to full A Level. Cambridge and Pearson both run AS and A Level series in June and November. The jump in abstraction from IGCSE Extended to AS is the single most common reason a strong Year 11 grade becomes a weak Year 12 one.
programmes.countryNote: Equivalency on the British track also asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary at the same grade. Families in Al Satwa planning for a UAE university should read that requirement before choosing a three-subject A Level block, because it constrains what can safely be dropped.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The alternative post-IGCSE route, offered by several schools within reach of Al Satwa. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and an Internal Assessment in every subject. It costs more to support than A Level simply because there are more assessed components running at once.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's International Baccalaureate cohort is about 7% of private school enrolment against 37% on the UK curriculum, so an Al Satwa family choosing the Diploma is choosing the smaller stream. That matters for tutoring supply: specialist availability is thinner, and booking earlier costs the same but gets a better match.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-satwa.subjectsIntro: Subjects do not cost the same to support, and the reason is structural rather than arbitrary. A subject with a tiered entry, a practical component or a coursework element needs more hours than one assessed by two written papers. The grid below is ordered by how much work a Satwa family typically ends up buying.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The most-requested IGCSE subject in Dubai and the one where the tier choice has the largest financial consequence. Marks go missing in algebraic manipulation, bearings, transformations and the two-step problems that put a percentage change inside a geometry question. Pearson's 4MA1 provides a different formula sheet from Cambridge 0580, which changes what has to be memorised.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (Cambridge 0607)
subjects.description: The graphics-calculator route, taught by many IB-aligned schools as the feeder into Maths AA or AI. It assesses investigation alongside technique and includes a paper where calculator use is assumed throughout. A tutor who prepares a 0607 student on 0580 past papers is preparing for the wrong assessment.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity, moments and the practical-skills paper account for most of the lost marks. Cambridge 0625 includes an alternative-to-practical paper for candidates not sitting a laboratory exam, and answering it well is a taught skill — reading a scale, identifying a control variable, explaining an anomaly — not a by-product of knowing the physics.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations and organic reaction pathways are where grades are decided. Students who can recite a definition routinely lose marks on the three-mark calculation that follows it, because the method is unpractised rather than unknown. Qualitative analysis tables reward precise observation language.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The highest content volume of the three sciences and the lowest tolerance for loose terminology. Osmosis, enzyme graphs, genetic crosses and the human systems carry most of the marks. Extended-tier questions demand explanation rather than description, and that distinction is worth teaching explicitly.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences (0653, 0654)
subjects.description: Two different single-award and double-award routes that look alike on a timetable and are not alike on a paper. Students entered for these often get taught from separate-science resources, which wastes time on content outside their syllabus. Checking the code before buying hours saves money immediately.

subjects.name: English Language and English Literature
subjects.description: Cambridge runs First Language English and English as a Second Language as separate syllabuses with different mark schemes, and a student in the wrong one underperforms for reasons unrelated to ability. Directed writing and the extended response reward structure and register far more than vocabulary.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Data-response and case-study questions where the marks sit in evaluation rather than recall. Students who define every term and then stop lose the top band consistently. A short, repeated drill on command words — explain, analyse, discuss, evaluate — shifts grades faster than more content.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Algorithm design, pseudocode and trace tables are examined in ways that reward disciplined notation. Students who can write working Python still lose marks on a trace table because the format was never taught. Practical ICT components need software access, which an online session can screen-share through.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. It does not count towards the equivalency five, which surprises many Al Satwa parents when they first read the rule.

sections.heading: The rate ladder, cheapest tier first
paragraphs: An IGCSE tutor in Dubai costs between roughly AED 45 and AED 650 an hour depending on tier and format, as of October 2026. Most Al Satwa families end up between AED 150 and AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. The table below reads from the bottom of the market upwards, because that is the order a parent encounters these offers in — the cheap ones advertise hardest.

Reading it from the bottom has a second use. It makes visible what each step up actually adds, which is the question the price tag never answers. The step from AED 65 to AED 200 is not a step in friendliness. It is the step from a tutor who can explain the answer in the back of the book to one who can look at your child's last mock paper and name the three topics that are costing marks. For a Year 11 student eight months from a June series, that diagnosis is the whole purchase.

Every figure here belongs to the provider named beside it and was published by them. None of it is an IB Gram price list. IB Gram's own position is that the first lesson is free, so the diagnosis costs nothing before you decide whether the rest is worth buying — and the band a family lands in afterwards depends on the subject, the tier and how close the series is.

One warning about the top of the ladder. A premium rate is sometimes justified by describing a tutor as an examiner. Examiner status is only meaningful if it can be evidenced, and it gives nobody access to marking, grade boundaries or unreleased paper content. A family paying AED 500 an hour should be able to see what the extra buys in teaching terms, stated as something checkable.

sections.heading: Monthly, not hourly: the number you will actually budget against
paragraphs: Nobody manages a household budget in hourly rates. The useful figure is the monthly one, and the market publishes it rarely enough that it is worth assembling here. Packages seen in Dubai include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for in-home tuition built as four two-hour visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support.

Convert that into a Satwa household's decision and the shape becomes clear. One subject, once a week, with a qualified online tutor, lands near AED 600 to 1,200 a month. Three subjects at that intensity triples it, which is why almost no family runs three subjects weekly for a full year. What they do instead — and what works — is run one subject weekly as the anchor, and rotate the other two through short diagnostic blocks.

The in-home comparison is where the number turns sharp. A four-visit month at AED 1,599 buys eight contact hours. The same AED 1,599 at the mid online band buys somewhere between five and ten hours depending on the tutor, and at the specialist band around four to six. The in-home package looks competitive on hours until you ask what fraction of each two-hour visit is genuinely teaching, and until you notice that the tutor pool it draws from is restricted to whoever will drive to Al Satwa on a Tuesday.

The last column of the table is the one families forget. A monthly figure without a stated duration is not a budget. Eight weeks of specialist support before a series is a different commitment from eighteen months of weekly maintenance, and the second one, spread out, usually costs less per grade moved.

sections.heading: Four ways Al Satwa families waste IGCSE money
paragraphs: The first leak is buying hours before buying a diagnosis. A parent who notices a 5 in chemistry books ten sessions and asks the tutor to go through the syllabus. Ten hours later the student is better at the topics they were already decent at, because that is the order a syllabus runs in. A single properly read mock paper would have said: the definitions are solid, the mole calculations are not, and the qualitative analysis answers use the wrong observation vocabulary. Three sessions on those three things beats ten on everything.

The second is paying a travel premium for a weaker tutor. In-home visits in Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, and from a district like Al Satwa the pool willing to make that drive at 17:00 is small. A family can therefore end up paying more for a generalist than an online specialist would have charged. The premium is real — it buys presence, and for some younger students presence genuinely helps — but it should be bought knowingly, not by default.

The third is running group sessions against a specific problem. Group tuition is cheaper per student and it works when two students share a gap. A child who cannot rearrange an equation and a child who cannot interpret a graph in the same group session each get half an hour of relevance for a full hour of fee. Review the pairing after four sessions, and split it the moment the gaps diverge.

The fourth is timing. Starting eight weeks before a June series is the most expensive way to buy a grade, because content repair and exam technique have to happen at once and there is no room for the forgetting curve. The same spend across the preceding twelve months buys the diagnosis early, fixes the foundation while there is time, and then runs past papers on a student who can actually do the questions.

paragraphs: The table below is the comparison competitors in this market publish in three vague rows, done with the Satwa commute inside it. The travel column is the one that changes by district, and in a dense inner-Dubai area with no secondary school of its own, it changes a lot. A tutor driving from Al Barsha to Al Satwa for a 17:00 start is in the worst traffic window of the day in both directions.

Read the 'best for' column with your own child in mind rather than in general. Presence matters most for younger students and for those who will not open a book without somebody in the room. Specialist match matters most for a Year 11 student sitting a specific tier of a specific syllabus code, where the question is not motivation but method. Those two needs point to different rows, and it is legitimate for a family to choose the first.

What IB Gram sells is the second row only. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE — that service exists only in India — so a Satwa family choosing us is choosing specialist match over physical presence. The honest version of the argument is this: within a twenty-minute drive of Al Satwa, the number of people who can teach Cambridge 0620 Extended organic pathways well is small, and online removes the drive from the selection criteria entirely.

The 'what is included' column deserves a note. Hourly rates at the budget end usually include nothing beyond the hour. At the specialist end you should expect marked written work, a named topic plan, and a short written note after each session that a parent can actually read. If that is not included, the rate is buying less than it appears to.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier decision that costs the most money
paragraphs: No single conversation in IGCSE costs an Al Satwa family more than the Cambridge tier decision, and almost nobody writes about it in financial terms. Several Cambridge subjects run a Core and an Extended route with different papers and different grade ranges, and the entry is made by the school months before the series. A student entered for Core and then needing an Extended-range grade for a sixth-form place has a problem that money cannot fully solve in the final term.

The tiering rule itself should be read on the syllabus document for your child's specific code at cambridgeinternational.org rather than taken from any tutoring site, including this one, because codes are revised. What is stable is the shape of the consequence: the two tiers do not reach the same grades, and moving between them late is constrained by entry deadlines rather than by ability.

Where tutoring money earns its keep is before the entry is made. A diagnostic run of two or three sessions in the first term of Year 10, against the actual paper the child would sit at each tier, gives the school's subject teacher something concrete to discuss. That is three hours of spend against a decision that shapes two years. Compare it with the cost of a final-term rescue at the specialist band and the arithmetic is not close.

Pearson's International GCSE behaves differently and the difference matters for budgeting. Several Pearson subjects are untiered, and some operate modular assessment where units can be sat across series. That changes when money is best spent — modular routes reward support concentrated before each unit rather than spread evenly across two years.

sections.heading: Nine subjects, one budget: how families actually split it
paragraphs: A typical IGCSE load in this part of Dubai is eight to ten subjects. No household funds weekly one-to-one support across all of them, and no student would benefit if it did. What works is a tiered allocation, and it is worth writing down explicitly because the default — fund whichever subject produced the worst report — is close to the worst possible strategy.

Start with the equivalency five. British-track Ministry of Education equivalency requires five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among those five. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong; the correct rule is on the official clarification. Those five subjects, plus whatever a target sixth-form course requires, are the ones that carry consequences. A grade 4 in a tenth subject nobody will ever ask about is not the place to spend.

Then rank by repairability per hour. Mathematics and the sciences respond fastest to targeted work because their marks sit in identifiable methods. Essay subjects move more slowly and need marked written work between sessions rather than more contact time, so the same budget is better spent on fewer, longer-spaced sessions with homework marking attached.

Finally, protect one subject as the anchor. A single weekly slot that never moves, in the subject that matters most, does more for a student's year than three slots that all collapse in the week of a school assessment. From Al Satwa, with the commute pattern this district has, the anchor slot should be the one that survives a late bus — which usually means later in the evening than a parent first proposes.
bullets: Fund the five equivalency subjects and the sixth-form prerequisites first

sections.heading: The exam calendar read as a spending plan
paragraphs: Spending the same money at different points in the year buys very different amounts of grade. The reason is that entry deadlines sit months before exams, and the decisions that matter — tier, board, subject count, whether a resit is needed — are locked by those deadlines rather than by the exam date. A family that plans against the calendar rather than against the report card spends less and gets more.

Here is the UAE-correct version. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, with Cambridge stating it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your child's school which zone it sits in; that single question removes a real risk.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. For the June 2026 series, results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so check the live official timetable rather than relying on a restatement.

The IB Diploma side has to be handled differently and honestly. UAE schools sit the May session, but no specific IB exam or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, so none is published here. Confirm every IB date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org before you plan around it.
