sections.heading: The permit, the regulator, and what you are entitled to ask
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and a parent paying AED 250 an hour is entitled to ask about it. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

MoHRE's own service page for it is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', which lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here — and any site quoting one should be treated carefully.

The regulator question is separate and frequently muddled. In Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate; in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain it is ADEK; in Sharjah the Sharjah Private Education Authority; in Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge; and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. KHDA inspects schools. It does not accredit individual tutors, and nobody should describe themselves to you as a KHDA-approved tutor.

A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram does not hold KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation and does not claim any, and there is no IB Gram office in the UAE. One more thing worth knowing: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school — so 'your child's own teacher, privately' is not something to arrange.

sections.heading: Equivalency, and what not to pay to fix
paragraphs: Ministry of Education equivalency is the process that lets a school certificate earned on an international curriculum be recognised in the UAE, and it shapes which grades are financially worth protecting. On the British track, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That is the detail most worth knowing, because it tells an Al Satwa parent that a weak Arabic grade, while it matters to the school and to the child, is not what blocks equivalency. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five, and the official clarification is the thing to read.

On the American track the requirements are different again: English proficiency via a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT; and mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold is published here, because none has been read on a Ministry of Education source — do not let anyone quote you one without showing you the page.

Two warnings follow from this. Equivalency is not something a tutoring provider performs or guarantees; it is an official process, described here and handled through the authority's own channel. And tutoring is not required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. Anyone telling an Al Satwa family otherwise is selling urgency rather than teaching.
bullets: British track: five IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3
Arabic and Islamic Education sit outside that count of five
Plus one A Level at E, or two AS Levels at E
No IB points figure is published without a Ministry of Education source

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with coursework, and what the fee does not buy
paragraphs: Some of the money moving through this market is buying something a family should not want. One operator in this SERP sells completed Internal Assessments. That is an academic-integrity breach, it is a malpractice trigger for the student rather than for the seller, and the consequences land on the child. Knowing where the line sits is part of knowing what you are paying for.

A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain the assessment criteria in the board's own words, discuss whether a research question is answerable, model the method on a different example, give feedback on a draft the student wrote, and point out where an argument does not follow. A tutor may not write, complete, rewrite, edit to completion or supply any part of assessed work. For IGCSE coursework components and for IB Internal Assessments, Extended Essays and Theory of Knowledge essays alike, the work must be the student's own.

Nor should anyone supply you with board materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. The correct behaviour is to reference them and link the official source, which is why this page points at cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com rather than hosting anything.

If a provider's pitch promises a particular grade, a promised number of marks, or money back tied to a result, the appropriate response is to stop. No tutor can promise an outcome in an externally assessed examination, and a provider willing to claim it is telling you something about their honesty rather than their teaching.

process.title: Send the four facts that price the job
process.description: School, year group, subject list and — the one most families omit — the syllabus codes from the statement of entry. Those four lines let a match be made against the exact paper your child sits, rather than against a board name. It takes two minutes and it removes most of the guesswork from the first lesson.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic lesson
process.description: The first lesson costs nothing and its purpose is diagnosis, not teaching. The tutor works through recent written work or a past paper section and comes back with named topics. If the diagnosis is vague, that is useful information about the tutor and you have spent nothing to learn it.

process.title: Get the plan and the number in writing
process.description: Before any block is booked you should have the diagnosed topics, the number of sessions proposed, what happens between sessions, and the total cost. A monthly figure with no stated duration is not a budget. A plan that says 'go through the syllabus' is not a plan.

process.title: Fix a slot that survives a late school bus
process.description: From Al Satwa the realistic window depends on which cluster your child travels to. Pick a start time that works on the worst Tuesday of the term rather than the best one, and agree in advance what happens when the bus is twenty minutes late.

process.title: Review against the calendar, not the calendar month
process.description: Review at the points where decisions get made: subject and tier selection, the series entry deadline, the mock window, and the results release. Those four moments are where money changes outcomes. A monthly renewal cycle reviews nothing except the invoice.

whyPoints.title: The prices are on the page
whyPoints.description: Market bands in AED, attributed to the provider that published them, with the date. Three of the six most visible competitors in this market publish no price at all and two quote US dollars. A family cannot make a financial decision against a contact form.

whyPoints.title: Matched on syllabus code
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different formula provision. Cambridge 0653 and 0654 are different science routes. A tutor matched on 'IGCSE maths' is matched on an acronym. The code is on the statement of entry and it is what the match is built from.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium inside the rate
whyPoints.description: In-home visits in Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, and from Al Satwa in the afternoon window that travel is substantial. Online delivery removes the drive from the price and, more usefully, removes it from the selection criteria.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before hours
whyPoints.description: The free first lesson exists to produce a list of named topics. Buying ten hours and asking a tutor to work through a syllabus is the most common way families in this district overspend, and a diagnosis is what prevents it.

whyPoints.title: The limit is stated
whyPoints.description: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are offered only in India. If presence in the room is what your child needs, that is a legitimate requirement and this is not the right service for it.

whyPoints.title: Coursework help stops where IB and Cambridge rules stop
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criteria explanation and feedback on the student's own draft, in writing. Never writing, completing or editing assessed work to completion. One operator in this market sells finished Internal Assessments; the risk of that lands on the student, not the seller.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor near me in Al Satwa actually cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai, as of October 2026, run from roughly AED 45 to 65 an hour at the budget online end, where EdFlik advertises, and from about AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya's lower band. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and 300; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase listing AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 including travel. Those are other providers' published figures, not an IB Gram price list, and the band you land in depends on the subject, the tier and how close the series is.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to buy a monthly package or pay per session in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Per hour, a package is usually cheaper than ad-hoc booking. The risk is that you commit before you know whether the tutor can diagnose. The sensible order is a free diagnostic lesson first, then a short block against named topics, then a monthly arrangement once the match is proven. Always check the session length behind a package price, because eight thirty-minute sessions and eight sixty-minute sessions are advertised the same way.

faqs.question: Why would I pay AED 250 an hour when AED 50 tutors advertise everywhere?
faqs.answer: Because the two hours are selling different things. At AED 50 you are usually buying homework company from someone who sat these exams a few years ago and is working from a revision guide. At AED 250 you should be buying diagnosis: a tutor who reads your child's mock script and names the three topics costing marks, knows the mark-scheme language the examiner rewards, and can tell a Core paper from an Extended one at a glance. If a tutor at the higher band cannot produce that list of named topics after one lesson, you are paying the higher price for the cheaper product.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to an apartment in Al Satwa?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Lessons for Al Satwa families are one-to-one and delivered live over video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and the student's written work on screen. The trade-off is explicit: you give up physical presence in the room and you gain a tutor chosen for your child's syllabus code rather than for who is willing to drive into Satwa at five in the afternoon. For a younger child who needs somebody beside them, that trade may not be the right one.

faqs.question: How much of an in-home tutor's fee is really paying for traffic?
faqs.answer: Enough to matter. In-home rates in Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor. From Al Satwa the common school-run districts sit fifteen to forty-five minutes away in the late-afternoon window, in both directions. A tutor making that round trip for one hour of teaching has to price it in. The deeper cost is not the dirhams, though — it is that the pool of tutors willing to make the drive is small, so the travel premium can buy a weaker teacher than the online band would have given you.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects give the most grade improvement per dirham spent?
faqs.answer: Mathematics and the three sciences, generally, because their lost marks sit in identifiable methods. A student who cannot complete a three-mark mole calculation or rearrange an equation under time pressure has a fixable, teachable gap, and three focused sessions can move it. Essay subjects move more slowly and need marked written work between sessions rather than more contact hours, so the same budget there is better spent on fewer sessions with homework marking attached. That difference should shape how a family splits a fixed budget across eight or nine subjects.

faqs.question: My child's report was poor in four subjects. Can we afford support in all four?
faqs.answer: Probably not weekly, and it would not be the best use of the money anyway. Fund the subjects with consequences first: the five needed for Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, plus any prerequisite for the sixth-form course your child wants. Then keep one weekly anchor slot in the subject that matters most, and rotate the others through short diagnostic blocks of two or three sessions. Four weekly commitments in a household with a long school run tend to collapse by the second month, and a collapsed schedule costs money without producing anything.

faqs.question: Do tutoring prices in Dubai rise as the June series approaches?
faqs.answer: Demand certainly does, and specialist availability tightens in the final term, which has the same practical effect as a price rise: the tutor you wanted is booked and the one who is free costs more or knows less. The bigger cost of late booking is not the rate. It is that eight weeks before a series, content repair and exam technique have to happen simultaneously with no room for forgetting and relearning. The same money spent across the preceding year buys diagnosis early, foundation repair while there is time, and past-paper work on a student who can do the questions.

faqs.question: Should I ask whether a quoted tutoring rate in Dubai includes VAT?
faqs.answer: Yes, and ask it before the first invoice rather than after. This page does not state the VAT treatment of tuition fees as fact, because that is a Federal Tax Authority matter and any claim about it needs a citation from them. What you can reasonably ask any provider is simple and specific: is the figure you have quoted me the figure I pay, and if a tax is added, what is it and on what basis. A provider who cannot answer that clearly about their own pricing has told you something useful.

faqs.question: What should the free trial lesson produce if it is worth taking?
faqs.answer: A list of named topics, not a feeling. By the end of a useful first lesson you should have heard something like: the definitions are secure, the two-step calculations are not, and the observation language in the qualitative analysis answers is costing marks. That is a diagnosis you can price work against. A trial lesson that produces warmth, enthusiasm and an offer of ten sessions to go through the syllabus has produced nothing you can spend against. The trial is free precisely so this test costs you nothing.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same Satwa household share one tutor to save money?
faqs.answer: Only if they are on the same syllabus code and the same tier, and only if their diagnosed gaps genuinely overlap. Paired sessions are cheaper per student and they work when both students need the same thing taught. They stop working the moment one needs algebraic fluency and the other needs graph interpretation, because each then receives half an hour of relevance for a full hour of fee. Review a pairing after four sessions rather than at the end of a term, and be willing to split it when the gaps diverge.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a UAE permit, and does that cost us anything?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. It costs a family nothing, so a tutor citing permit costs as a reason for a higher rate is not describing a real expense. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so ignore any figure you see quoted.

faqs.question: Is a KHDA-approved IGCSE tutor a thing I should be looking for?
faqs.answer: No, and the phrase should make you cautious. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai; it inspects schools and it issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises. It does not accredit individual private tutors. A tutor or platform describing itself as KHDA-approved is either confusing the training-institute permit with something else or hoping you will. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation and makes no such claim. The permit to ask about is the MoHRE one.

faqs.question: How does the Dubai school fee freeze change what I should budget for tutoring?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there will be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a Satwa household that means the education line in the budget is flat rather than rising, which is the first year in a while that extra tutoring spend does not have to be found by cutting something else. It is also a reason to spend it early in the year rather than in a final-term panic, when the same amount buys considerably less.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody is free for the subject and tier we need?
faqs.answer: You get told, rather than matched to whoever is available. Specialist cover is thinner in some combinations than others, and the honest options are a short wait for the right tutor, a different weekly slot that opens a wider pool, or a tutor outside the UAE working on Gulf Standard Time for the same subject and code. What should not happen is a biology specialist taking a chemistry student because the calendar had a gap. If that is proposed to you anywhere in this market, treat it as a reason to ask who else is available.

intro.heading: What an Al Sufouh family is actually paying for
paragraphs: Al Sufouh sits between Dubai Knowledge Park and the coast, with Dubai Media City and Dubai Internet City on its inland edge and Al Barsha 1 a short run across Sheikh Zayed Road. It is a small catchment with an unusually dense school supply. Dubai College sits inside it. GEMS Wellington International School sits inside it. Within fifteen minutes in good traffic you reach the American School of Dubai, Dubai American Academy, Kings' School Al Barsha and Regent International School in The Greens. That density is why the local tutoring market is priced the way it is, and why a parent typing IGCSE tutor near me in Al Sufouh is usually quoted a number before anyone has asked which board the child sits.

The number matters less than what sits behind it. Dubai's published market bands are wide. Budget online tutoring, usually delivered by university students, advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 at EdFlik and from roughly AED 33 to AED 52 at Tutopiya. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted from AED 150 by Unitors for IGCSE. A specialist with International GCSE and A Level experience runs AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. An in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, is quoted by Bestimate at AED 180 to AED 350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to AED 500. Those are market figures from the providers named, read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

Spread across a two-term run, the gap between those bands is not small. A family paying AED 180 an hour for one weekly session spends roughly AED 720 a month. A family paying AED 400 for the same hour spends about AED 1,600. Over the eight months between September and the May/June series that is a difference of around AED 7,000 for identical contact time. The question worth answering before you pay anything is which of the two is buying more marks, and in Al Sufouh the honest answer is that format matters less than syllabus match.

Here is the part the quotes rarely mention. Cambridge IGCSE 0580 Mathematics and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE 4MA1 are different papers with different structures, and 0607 International Mathematics is a third animal again with a graphic display calculator assumed throughout. A tutor who has taught 0580 for nine years and is handed a 4MA1 candidate will spend the first three paid sessions working out the differences. You pay for those sessions. The same applies across the sciences, where Cambridge splits 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology from the combined routes 0653 and 0654, and Pearson runs 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1 and the 4SD0 Science Double Award. Matching the code first is the single cheapest decision available to you.

IB Gram's position on delivery is fixed and stated on every UAE page. Tuition for families here is one-to-one online tuition over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is not a limitation dressed up as a feature. It is the reason an online IGCSE tutor in Al Sufouh can be a 0607 specialist rather than whoever holds a free Tuesday within a twenty-minute drive of Knowledge Park, and it is the reason the travel premium disappears from the bill entirely.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-sufouh.programmesIntro: Al Sufouh's British-curriculum schools run IGCSE in Years 10 and 11 before students split towards A Level or the IB Diploma. The three programme bands below are the ones families in this catchment ask about, and the cost of support differs sharply between them because the assessment load does.

programmes.name: Cambridge Upper Secondary, IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE is the two-year block sat at sixteen, graded 9 to 1 on the reformed syllabuses and A* to G on several older ones. Most subjects carry two or three written papers, and the sciences add an alternative-to-practical paper where a centre does not enter candidates for the practical test. Core and Extended tiering in subjects such as 0580 Mathematics caps the achievable grade, so tier choice is a decision with a ceiling attached rather than an administrative detail.
programmes.countryNote: Al Sufouh's Cambridge entries are concentrated in a handful of schools, so the subject combinations repeat and the tutoring demand clusters hard around maths and the separate sciences in the autumn term. Families here often discover the tier question late, in January of Year 11, when the centre's final entries are being prepared. That is the most expensive moment to find out, because a tier change forces a different past-paper diet.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs a parallel qualification with its own codes and its own paper architecture. Mathematics Specification A, 4MA1, is two papers of equal weight with a Foundation and Higher tier. Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Biology 4BI1 each run two papers, and the Science Double Award 4SD0 compresses all three into a single double grade. Pearson publishes its own timetables, and the November series results reach students in January rather than August.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Sufouh and Al Barsha families run split entries, with maths through Cambridge and the sciences through Pearson, because the school entered them that way or because a resit was taken elsewhere. A tutor who assumes one board for every subject will teach the wrong mark scheme for part of the year, and that is paid time that produces nothing.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary, Years 7-9
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE decide how expensive IGCSE becomes. Cambridge Lower Secondary covers the algebraic fluency, proportional reasoning and scientific vocabulary that Extended-tier papers assume without teaching. Checkpoint tests are available in March, May and October and give a school a cohort benchmark rather than a certificate. Support at this stage is cheaper per hour and far cheaper per mark, because it removes gaps rather than patching them under time pressure.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Sufouh this is the band parents most often skip. A Year 9 student who cannot rearrange a formula confidently will meet that same weakness in 0580 Paper 4, 0625 Physics and 0620 Chemistry simultaneously eighteen months later, and will then need three subject tutors instead of one. The arithmetic on that is not subtle.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma entry from IGCSE
programmes.description: IGCSE grades are the entry gate to A Level and to the IB Diploma, and the two routes read those grades differently. A Level sixth forms usually set subject-specific thresholds, commonly a grade 7 or 6 in the subject to be continued. IB Diploma schools look at the spread across six subject groups, because a Diploma candidate cannot drop the weak one. Where an IGCSE grade will be used to argue for an HL place, the subject it sits in matters more than the overall count.
programmes.countryNote: Al Sufouh and the Greens sit students into both routes, with Dubai College running A Levels and GEMS Wellington International School offering the IB Diploma alongside the British pathway. A family holding offers from both is making a four-subject decision against a six-subject one, and the IGCSE profile they need differs accordingly.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-sufouh.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Al Sufouh families request most, with the syllabus codes attached. Rates do not vary much by subject in the Dubai market; what varies is how many sessions each subject needs, and that is where a monthly bill is really decided.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 · Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The most requested subject in the catchment and the one where tier choice bites hardest. Extended-tier Paper 4 carries the algebraic manipulation, trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles, and the vectors and transformations work that Core never meets. Most lost marks sit in method rather than knowledge: unsimplified surds, premature rounding, and answers given without the units the mark scheme demands.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (Cambridge 0607)
subjects.description: A separate syllabus that assumes a graphic display calculator throughout and includes a short investigation paper. Students moving from 0580 teaching materials meet unfamiliar question styles in the graphing work and lose marks for describing a sketch rather than reading values from it. A tutor who does not know 0607 exists will teach 0580 at a 0607 candidate for a term.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 · Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and the circuit-analysis questions cause the most trouble, followed by anything requiring a graph gradient to be converted into a physical quantity with units. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards experimental literacy rather than recall, so students who have only revised theory lose a predictable block of marks they could have secured in three sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 · Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tables are where marks concentrate. Organic chemistry is usually learned as a list of names rather than a set of reaction types, which is why students can recognise an alcohol and still not predict what it does. Extended-tier electrolysis questions demand half-equations written correctly, not described.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 · Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content volume is the difficulty, not conceptual depth. Marks are lost to imprecise command-term responses: describing when the paper asked for an explanation, or naming a structure without its function. Transport in plants, enzymes and the genetics crosses reward exact vocabulary, and that is trainable in a way that generic revision is not.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654 · 0653)
subjects.description: The double-award and single-award science routes compress three disciplines into fewer papers, and students often revise from separate-science resources that cover material their syllabus excludes. Knowing exactly which topics are out of scope saves a term of wasted effort, and a tutor who has the right syllabus open can mark that boundary in the first session.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 · 0990 · Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: The directed writing and composition tasks carry a band descriptor rather than a mark scheme of facts, so improvement comes from structural work and timing rather than content coverage. Reading-passage questions reward close selection of evidence. Students who write beautifully and ignore the question's command verb sit in the middle bands indefinitely.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 · 0993)
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English with different band descriptors, and often the right entry for a student schooled in another language until Year 8. The listening paper is where marks leak, usually because students write a full phrase where a single word was wanted. Exam technique here is worth more than vocabulary drilling.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 · 0450)
subjects.description: Both reward structured evaluation and are marked against levels rather than points. Students who list advantages and disadvantages without reaching a judgement cap out below the top band regardless of knowledge. Diagram accuracy in Economics, especially shifts labelled with the correct axis, is a cheap and reliable source of marks.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies run in all Dubai private schools alongside the licensed international curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited. Support has to respect which stream a student actually sits in.

regions.note: Across Sheikh Zayed Road and home to the American School of Dubai, Dubai American Academy and Kings' School Al Barsha. Families here often share tutors with Al Sufouh neighbours, and the ten-minute hop looks trivial on a map until it is attempted at 5pm on a Sunday.

modes.description: A fixed slot in the same place each week across both IGCSE years, working ahead of the school's scheme of work rather than behind it. This is the cheapest format per mark because nothing is being repaired under deadline pressure, and it is the only format in which a tutor can genuinely cover a full syllabus rather than triage it.

sections.heading: What "IGCSE tutor near me in Al Sufouh" actually buys
paragraphs: A parent searching for an IGCSE tutor near me in Al Sufouh is buying one of two things, and they cost different amounts. The first is proximity: somebody who can be in the house on a Tuesday. The second is syllabus match: somebody who has taught the exact paper your child will sit, to the exact tier, recently enough to know where the mark scheme has moved. Proximity is easy to buy in this catchment and adds between AED 50 and AED 150 an hour to the bill, based on the published gap between the online and in-home bands. Syllabus match is harder to buy locally and is the only one of the two that converts into marks.

The reason proximity is expensive here is simple geography. Al Sufouh is a narrow coastal strip, and a tutor working in-home can realistically teach two or three students a day once travel between Knowledge Park, Al Barsha and the Greens is counted. That constraint has to be priced into every hour. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to AED 350 including travel, and independently advertised home tutors run from AED 200 to AED 500. Online qualified subject tutors in the same market are quoted from AED 150, with Unitors publishing AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB. The difference is not teaching quality. It is a car.

Syllabus match behaves differently. There are a limited number of people in any twenty-minute radius who have taught Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics with the graphic display calculator paper, or who can mark a 4CH1 Chemistry response against the Pearson scheme rather than the Cambridge one. Restricting the search to people who can drive to Al Sufouh shrinks that pool to whoever is left. Removing the travel constraint entirely means the Al Sufouh student gets the 0607 specialist and the family stops paying for the drive.

IB Gram's answer is therefore not a compromise on proximity. Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one online over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are offered only in India. The practical result for a family in Al Sufouh 2 is that the tutor is chosen by paper and tier rather than by driving distance, and that the travel premium is simply absent from the invoice.

sections.heading: IGCSE tutor rates in Dubai, priced by format
paragraphs: The table below is the market, not an IB Gram price list, and every band is attributed. Dubai has no published standard rate for private tuition, so the only honest way to show cost is to show who charges what and when it was read. These figures were taken from the named providers' own public pages in October 2026. Monthly columns assume one sixty-minute session a week over four weeks, which is what most Al Sufouh families actually buy in the autumn term before stepping up before a series.

Two things stand out once the formats sit side by side. The first is that the cheapest band and the most expensive band differ by roughly a factor of ten for nominally the same hour. Budget online tutoring advertised from AED 33 to AED 65 is generally delivered by current university students, which is a legitimate product for a Year 10 confidence problem and a poor one for Extended-tier Paper 4 technique. The second is that the in-home band overlaps almost entirely with the specialist online band. A family paying AED 300 an hour for a home visit and a family paying AED 300 an hour for an online specialist are spending the same money on different things, one of which is fuel.

Group sessions look like the value option and sometimes are. A small group of two to four students at a lower per-student rate works where everyone sits the same board, the same tier and the same paper, and where the weakness is shared. In Al Sufouh that condition is rarely met, because the local cohort splits across Cambridge and Pearson and across Core and Extended. A group containing a 0580 Extended candidate and a 4MA1 Foundation candidate is two lessons being delivered badly at once.

Monthly package pricing circulates in this market too, and it is worth reading carefully. Published packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. A package is cheaper per hour and less flexible; if a child's school assessment calendar moves, unused sessions are the hidden cost.

sections.heading: Where the money goes that never reaches the mark scheme
paragraphs: Most of the waste in a Dubai tutoring budget is not overpaying per hour. It is paying the right rate for the wrong work. The commonest version in this catchment is a tutor teaching the wrong syllabus for the first month because nobody asked for the code. A Year 11 student at a British-pathway school in Al Sufouh might be entered for 0580 Extended, 0607 Extended, or 4MA1 Higher, and the three require different past-paper diets, different calculator assumptions and different question-style drilling. Four sessions spent on 0580 content for a 0607 candidate is roughly AED 800 to AED 1,200 of paid time producing nothing usable.

The second leak is unmarked practice. A student who completes six past papers and marks them himself will report that he scored well and will keep making the same method errors, because self-marking cannot catch what the candidate does not know is wrong. Marking against the published mark scheme is slow, unglamorous work, and it is where the diagnostic value sits. If a tutoring arrangement does not include marked timed papers by January of Year 11, the family is paying for teaching and not for assessment.

The third is duplication with the school. Al Sufouh schools run their own clinics, intervention groups and after-school sessions, and these are included in fees already paid. A tutor who covers the same topic the school's Thursday clinic covered is being paid to repeat free provision. Asking the subject teacher what the school is already running, before buying anything, regularly removes a weekly session from the plan without removing any support.

The fourth is scope creep. A family that engages help for Chemistry in October frequently holds three weekly sessions across three subjects by February, because each new assessment produces a new worry. Three subjects at the mid band is roughly AED 1,800 to AED 3,600 a month, and the student now has eleven commitments a week. Deciding in advance how many subjects will be supported, and accepting that the other grades will be what they will be, is a cost control measure and usually an academic one too.

sections.heading: Online against an in-home tutor in Al Sufouh, costed line by line
paragraphs: Parents in this catchment ask whether an in-home tutor is worth the premium, and the answer deserves an honest comparison rather than a sales line. An in-home tutor delivers presence. For a younger student who will not sit still at a screen, or for a household where supervision is the real requirement, presence has genuine value. That is a legitimate reason to pay more, and a family who needs it should buy it.

What presence does not deliver is subject range. The published in-home band of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour buys whoever covers your subject within driving distance of Al Sufouh at a time your child is free. For Maths and Biology that pool is reasonably deep. For 0607 International Mathematics, for Pearson 4CH1 Chemistry marked to the Pearson scheme, or for Arabic as a First Language at 0508 level, it thins quickly. The table below prices the comparison on the dimensions that actually differ.

Travel is the line item most quotes bury. A tutor crossing from Mirdif or Al Nahda to Al Sufouh for a 5pm session loses ninety minutes of working time to the round trip, and that time is recovered somewhere in the rate. It also makes the arrangement fragile: one road closure on Al Sufouh Road and the session is cancelled, rescheduled or shortened. Online sessions fail for different reasons, mostly connection problems, and those are recoverable within the same hour.

IB Gram's own position, stated plainly: lessons for UAE families are one-to-one online over live video. IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai, and tutors are not dispatched to UAE addresses. Home visiting is an India-only service. A family in Al Sufouh who specifically wants a person in the room should hire locally for that, and should still ask the five questions in the process section below before paying anything.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: the question that changes the bill
paragraphs: Before any rate is agreed, establish which board your child sits for each subject. It is written on the statement of entry the school issues, and it is the single most useful piece of information a parent can bring to a first tutoring conversation. In a catchment this small, families frequently assume one board because a neighbour's child sits it, and the assumption costs a month.

The practical differences are not cosmetic. Cambridge 0580 Mathematics runs Core and Extended tiering with separate papers and a grade ceiling on Core, while Pearson 4MA1 runs Foundation and Higher tiers with its own paper structure and two papers of equal weight. Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics assumes a graphic display calculator throughout and adds an investigation paper that has no Pearson equivalent. In the sciences, Cambridge runs an alternative-to-practical paper where candidates are not entered for the practical test, and the technique required there is specific enough that it should be taught deliberately.

Session timing differs too. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and its exams officers' guide is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, because Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and its November results reach students in January rather than the following August.

The cost consequence is straightforward. A resit decision taken in August after June results is a different financial plan depending on board, because the November turnaround and the results date differ. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026 and its November 2026 timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Those are the dates that decide whether a university or sixth-form application can use the new grade, and therefore whether an eight-week intensive block in September is worth buying at all.

sections.heading: The permit question, which is also a cost question
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and a parent in Al Sufouh who does not ask about it is accepting a risk that is entirely avoidable. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. MoHRE's own service page for it is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two consequences follow for a family comparing quotes. First, because the permit costs nothing, no tutor can justify a higher rate by reference to it, and any quote that itemises a licensing cost should be questioned. Second, individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount can be quoted here; Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and a figure circulating as a fixed sum could not be verified. The exposure is real and unquantified, which is a reason to ask rather than to guess.

A separate rule sits over school teachers. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported and should be verified against current policy, but the direction is clear enough: a family in Al Sufouh who arranges for their child's own subject teacher to tutor them privately for money is arranging something the teacher may not be permitted to do.

A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again. It requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and makes no claim to one, because it operates no premises in the UAE. Any provider describing itself as approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge should be asked to show the permit or centre number.

sections.heading: The June and November series counted backwards from today
paragraphs: Cost planning only works against a calendar, and the IGCSE calendar is published well in advance. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. The February/March series exists but is offered to India only, which matters because secondary sources routinely quote its dates to Gulf parents. Working backwards from the series your child is actually entered for turns a vague tutoring budget into a defined number of sessions.

The anchor dates that can be stated with a source are Pearson's. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including the International GCSE November sitting a long way out, and those can be revised, so the live official timetable should always be the reference rather than any restatement of it.

Cambridge publishes its own timetables per series and allocates centres to one of six administrative zones, with an explicit warning that the correct zone version must be used. A family planning an intensive block needs the school's zone timetable, not a generic one, because a paper sitting two days earlier than assumed changes the final fortnight of revision entirely. Ask the exams officer for the zone and the dated timetable in the same email.

The table below is a counted-back plan rather than a list of dates, which is what a parent can actually act on. Rates in the final column use the mid-market online band so that the plan carries a cost, and are market figures rather than IB Gram prices. A family that starts this sequence in September spends less in total than one that starts in March, because the March start has to buy intensity to replace time.

sections.heading: What a tutor may not do, and why that protects your money
paragraphs: This matters more in the UAE market than parents expect, because the local SERP contains providers selling finished work. One operator advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. That is an academic-integrity breach, it is a malpractice trigger for the student rather than for the seller, and a family who buys it has spent money acquiring a risk.

The boundary is not difficult to state. A tutor teaches, explains, models, questions and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor may discuss a topic choice, interrogate a method, point at a weak argument and explain what the criteria reward. A tutor may not write, complete, draft or produce any piece of assessed work, and should not edit a student's writing to the point where the voice is no longer the student's. IB Gram's tutors work inside that line and say so to students explicitly at the start of coursework support.

For IGCSE the assessed-work exposure is smaller than at Diploma level but real, and it sits in the coursework components some subjects still carry, in school-assessed practical work, and in anything submitted under a centre declaration. Where a school requires a signed authenticity statement, the student signs it. Nobody else can.

There is a related rule about materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. A tutor may reference them and link to the official source. Reproducing them as downloads, or supplying unreleased material, is copyright infringement and, for unreleased papers, a malpractice exposure. If a provider offers a bundle of papers as a selling point, ask where it came from.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: fees, entries and the KHDA fee freeze
paragraphs: A tutoring bill reads differently once it sits next to the rest of a Dubai education budget. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family in Al Sufouh, that freeze is the first year in a while where the tuition line did not move, which is exactly when a tutoring line tends to appear.

The market context around it is worth knowing. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose by 6 per cent. A growing UK-curriculum cohort is a growing IGCSE cohort, and the demand for 0580 and 4MA1 support in this catchment follows it.

KHDA inspects Dubai's private schools annually on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak. An inspection band is a judgement about a whole school, not about a subject department and certainly not about your child's set. A parent reading a report should look for what it says about teaching in the relevant phase and subject rather than at the headline word, because a school rated in a strong band can still have a thin year in a single subject, and that is the situation in which tutoring is genuinely useful.

Set against that, the tutoring numbers are modest or substantial depending on the plan. One weekly online session at the mid band across an academic year runs roughly AED 5,400 to AED 10,800 in market terms. An eight-week pre-series intensive at two sessions a week runs roughly AED 2,400 to AED 4,800. A single-paper diagnostic is one hour. The decision is not whether tutoring is affordable in isolation; it is which of those three a particular child actually needs, and that is answerable in one session rather than one term.

process.title: Send the statement of entry, not the subject name
process.description: The statement of entry the school issues carries the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject. Sending that one document removes the most expensive source of waste in the whole arrangement, because it means the first paid session starts on the right paper rather than discovering the right paper.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson first
process.description: One lesson, one subject, booked before any payment is taken. The point is to see whether the tutor can teach this particular child, and to get a written readout of where the marks are going. If the readout says tutoring is not the right spend, that is a useful answer and it has cost nothing.

process.title: Agree the number of subjects before the first invoice
process.description: Scope creep is the second biggest cost in a Dubai tutoring budget. Deciding in advance that one or two subjects will be supported, and writing that down, prevents the February drift into three weekly sessions. It also protects the student's week, which is usually the more important constraint.

process.title: Fix the slot against the school day and the traffic
process.description: Al Sufouh school days end between 2pm and 3.30pm depending on the school and the phase. A session at 4.30pm works for a student who walks home; a Media City household usually needs 6.30pm or later. Online slots run to 9pm and beyond, so pick the time the student will actually be functional rather than the earliest available.

process.title: Insist on marked timed papers from week eight
process.description: Teaching without assessment produces confidence without evidence. From roughly the eighth week, a proportion of each session should be a paper sat under timed conditions and marked against the published mark scheme. That is what converts a tutoring arrangement into a diagnosis, and it is what tells you whether to continue.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code, not by subject label
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 and Pearson 4MA1 are three different qualifications. Matching on the code before the first lesson is what stops a month of paid time being spent on the wrong mark scheme, and it is the cheapest quality-control step available in this market.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is an India-only service. Two ranking competitors route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without saying where delivery happens.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor near me in Al Sufouh actually cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Dubai market rates read in October 2026 split into bands. Budget online tutoring advertises from AED 33 to AED 65, usually delivered by university students. Qualified subject tutors working online are quoted from AED 150, with Unitors publishing AED 150 for IGCSE. Specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to AED 350 by Bestimate, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to AED 500. Those are the market's figures, attributed to the providers who publish them, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Is paying extra for a tutor who lives near Al Sufouh worth the premium?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what you need. Presence has real value for a younger student who will not concentrate at a screen, or where supervision is the actual requirement. The published gap between the online and in-home bands is roughly AED 50 to AED 150 an hour, and that gap buys travel rather than teaching. What proximity costs you is range: restricting your search to people who can drive to Al Sufouh at your child's free time removes most specialists in the less common syllabuses, including Cambridge 0607 and the Pearson science codes.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE board and tier my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry issued by the school carries the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject, and the exams officer can confirm it in writing. Ask for it before you agree any tutoring rate. In a catchment as small as Al Sufouh, parents routinely assume a board because a neighbour's child sits it, and the assumption costs a month of paid sessions working on the wrong mark scheme. The same email should ask for the centre's Cambridge zone and the dated timetable for the series.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE exam series do UAE candidates actually sit?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so dates quoted for it do not apply to a child in Dubai. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. Always check the live official timetable, since provisional versions can be revised.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should an Al Sufouh Year 11 student have?
faqs.answer: For one subject with a known gap, one session a week from September is usually enough to cover a full syllabus properly, stepping up to two or three in the eight to twelve weeks before the series. Buying three subjects at three sessions a week in February is the pattern that produces an exhausted student and a monthly bill of AED 1,800 to AED 3,600 at mid-market rates. Fewer subjects supported properly beats more subjects supported thinly, and the student's remaining week is a real constraint rather than a soft one.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and does it add to what I pay?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it adds nothing to the cost. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Because the permit is free, any quote that itemises a licensing charge should be questioned directly.

faqs.question: Can my child's own subject teacher at an Al Sufouh school tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: Treat this as a rule rather than a grey area. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported, so verify it against current policy before relying on it, but the direction is unambiguous. A teacher from a different school who holds the permit is a straightforward arrangement; your child's own teacher, paid privately, is not.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0580 and Cambridge 0607 maths?
faqs.answer: They are separate syllabuses with separate papers. Cambridge 0580 Mathematics runs Core and Extended tiers and is the more commonly entered route. Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics assumes a graphic display calculator throughout and includes a short investigation paper that 0580 has no equivalent of. A student entered for 0607 who is taught from 0580 materials will meet unfamiliar question styles in the graphing work and will lose marks describing a sketch rather than reading values from it. This is why the code matters more than the subject name.

faqs.question: Is a small group cheaper than one-to-one for IGCSE in this area?
faqs.answer: Per student, yes, at roughly AED 80 to AED 180 against AED 150 to AED 450 for one-to-one. The condition is that every student in the group sits the same board, the same tier and has the same weakness. Al Sufouh's cohort splits across Cambridge and Pearson and across Core and Extended, so that condition is rarely met in practice. A group holding a 0580 Extended candidate and a 4MA1 Foundation candidate is two lessons being delivered badly at once, and the saving disappears.

faqs.question: We have eight weeks before the IGCSE papers in Al Sufouh. What can that buy?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is enough to change technique and to secure the predictable marks, and not enough to teach a syllabus that was never covered. An honest eight-week plan names what is being deliberately left out and why. The realistic work is timed papers marked against the published mark scheme, alternative-to-practical technique, command-term precision and an error log that gets shorter. At two sessions a week on the mid band that is roughly AED 2,400 to AED 4,800 in market terms. Anyone promising a specific grade in that window is selling something else.

faqs.question: How does online IGCSE tuition handle the practical side of the sciences?
faqs.answer: Cambridge entries are usually for the alternative-to-practical paper where a centre does not enter candidates for the practical test, and that paper assesses experimental literacy rather than manual technique: reading a scale correctly, identifying a control variable, spotting why a result is anomalous, drawing a line of best fit that the data supports. All of that is taught better with a shared screen and a real past paper than at a bench. The hands-on work belongs to the school's laboratory, and tutoring should support it rather than attempt to replace it.

faqs.question: What should I ask a Dubai tutoring provider before paying anything?
faqs.answer: Ask six things. Which syllabus code will you teach, and have you taught it. Do you hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit. Where does delivery actually happen, and from which country. Will papers be marked against the published mark scheme or self-marked. What is your replacement policy if the match is wrong. And what exactly does the free trial include. Any provider claiming approval from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge should be asked to produce the permit or centre number.

faqs.question: Do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies still apply at an IGCSE school?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and any mandatory subject lesson is advised to run at least twenty-five minutes.

faqs.question: Will IGCSE grades be enough for Ministry of Education equivalency later?
faqs.answer: For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two accredited Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule. Verify your own case with the Ministry of Education directly.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE coursework without crossing the honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is worth stating before the work starts. A tutor can discuss a topic choice, question a method, explain what the assessment criteria reward and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write, complete, draft or produce the work, and should not edit it until the voice is no longer the student's. Where a school requires an authenticity declaration, the candidate signs it. One operator in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments, which transfers a malpractice risk straight onto the student.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is available for a rarer IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: You get told, with a timescale, rather than matched with somebody approximate. Scarce codes in this market include Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics, Arabic as a First Language at 0508 level and some of the Pearson science codes marked to the Pearson scheme. Where no UAE-timezone specialist is free, the options are a tutor in another timezone working an Al Sufouh-friendly evening slot, a short wait with a named date, or a diagnostic session with a generalist to establish what is actually needed first. Being told is cheaper than being matched badly.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-sufouh.closingBody: If you are weighing up an IGCSE tutor near me in Al Sufouh, the useful first step costs nothing. Find the statement of entry, note the board, the syllabus code and the tier for the subject that worries you, and book the free trial lesson. One subject, one hour, no payment taken beforehand. You will finish it knowing where the marks are going, how many sessions the gap realistically needs, and whether the answer is a year of weekly work, an eight-week block before the series, or nothing at all. Lessons run live online, one-to-one, timed to Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Is a nearby IGCSE tutor teaching the specification your child actually sits?
paragraphs: Most parents in Al Twar can find a tutor within fifteen minutes of their door. Far fewer can tell you which examination board their child is entered for, which specification code, and at which tier. That second set of facts determines what the papers look like, how the questions are worded, how practical skills are assessed and what the highest achievable grade is. Proximity is easy to verify and almost irrelevant; specification fit is hard to verify and decides the result.

Two boards dominate this cluster. Cambridge International runs IGCSE with Core and Extended tiering in several subjects, its own practical routes, and a timetable published separately for each of six administrative zones. Pearson Edexcel runs its International GCSE with a different paper structure, untiered in many subjects but offered at Foundation and Higher tier in Mathematics A. Schools a short drive apart around Al Twar, Al Qusais and Mirdif have made opposite choices, and a tutor who teaches one fluently can be genuinely weak on the other without knowing it. Neither board is harder than the other, and a parent is not being asked to form a view on which is better. The only thing that matters is which one appears on your child's entry, because that is the paper they will actually sit in the examination hall.

The practical consequence shows up in past papers, which is where most tutoring time is spent in Year 11. A student who spends a term on Cambridge 0580 papers and then sits Pearson 4MA1 will meet unfamiliar phrasing at the worst possible moment. The content overlap is high enough that nobody notices anything is wrong until the mock, and the mark-scheme expectations are different enough that it costs grades. This is the single most common avoidable waste in the local market, and it is entirely free to prevent.

There is a second fact worth establishing at the same time, and it is the one families discover too late: the tier. In Cambridge subjects with Core and Extended entries, the tier carries a grade ceiling. A student entered at Core cannot reach the top grades regardless of how well they are taught, and the entry is set well before the examination year. Asking for the tier in writing during Year 10 is a five-minute task that occasionally changes a child's post-16 options.

So the honest framing of what we offer. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. IGCSE tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the reason that matters here is specification fit: the tutor can be selected for teaching Pearson 4CH1 or Cambridge 0620 Extended specifically, rather than for being the available person who will drive to Al Twar on a Tuesday evening.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: the same subject, different paper
paragraphs: The boards teach similar content and examine it differently, and the difference is concentrated exactly where tutoring time goes. Question phrasing is the most visible part. Mark-scheme expectations are the most expensive part: what counts as a complete answer for a given number of marks is a convention, learned by doing that board's papers, and a student trained on the other board's conventions writes answers that feel right and score short.

Paper structure is the second difference. The number of papers, the split between calculator and non-calculator work in mathematics, the provision of a formula sheet, and the way practical skills are assessed in the sciences all vary. None of these is a secret; all of them are published on the board's own site. What they require is that somebody check which applies to your child before a term of past papers is chosen.

There is one administrative difference that catches UAE families in particular. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate version of the timetable for each. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Pearson publishes its own timetables per series, with provisional versions in advance, so the live official document is the only safe source for dates on either board.

The fix for all of this is one email. Ask the examinations officer for board, specification code and tier in each subject, plus the practical route in sciences and the Cambridge zone if it applies. Those five facts make every past paper, mark scheme and revision list used thereafter correct, and they cost nothing to obtain. We ask for them in week one for exactly that reason.

sections.heading: Core and Extended: the grade ceiling written down
paragraphs: In Cambridge subjects with two tiers, the entry decides the range of grades available. A Core entry is a narrower syllabus examined on a narrower paper set, with a ceiling below the top grades. An Extended entry covers the full content and gives access to the full range. Both are legitimate routes and for some students the Core entry is the right call, because an Extended entry a student cannot access produces a worse outcome than a Core entry they can.

What is not acceptable is a family discovering the tier in the examination year. The entry is set by the school months before the papers, and by the time a Year 11 parent asks why their child's maths grade seems capped, the decision has usually been final for some time. The remedy is to ask in Year 10, in writing, for the tier in every tiered subject, and to ask what evidence the school used. That is a reasonable question and schools answer it.

Where tutoring genuinely helps is before the entry closes. A short diagnostic engagement can establish whether a student can access Extended content, which is a different question from whether they currently are. A student who is struggling because a specific topic was missed is a different case from a student for whom the Extended demand is consistently out of reach, and only the first case justifies pushing for a tier change. Pretending otherwise sets a child up for a paper they cannot complete.

Pearson Edexcel avoids this in its untiered subjects, where every candidate sits the same papers, which is one real advantage of that route for a borderline student. It also means those papers must serve the whole ability range, so the hardest questions sit alongside the most accessible ones in the same booklet, and part of the technique to teach is deciding quickly which questions to leave until last. Mathematics A is the exception, offered at Foundation and Higher tier, so the ceiling question applies there too. That is a specification-specific skill, and it is the sort of detail that distinguishes a tutor who knows the board from one who knows the subject.

sections.heading: Five questions that reveal whether a tutor knows your specification
paragraphs: You do not need to know the specification yourself to test somebody on it. Five questions, all short, all specific, all difficult to bluff. Ask them of everyone you consider, including us, and listen for precision rather than fluency. A tutor who teaches that board weekly answers all five in under two minutes; one who teaches the subject generally will answer in generalities, and that is the whole of the test.

The first question is which board and code they teach for your subject. The right answer includes the four-digit Cambridge code or the Pearson code without hesitation. The second is how many papers your child will sit and what each covers, because a tutor planning revision must know the paper structure. The third is which practical route the sciences use, and what they have prepared students for. The fourth asks what counts as a complete answer for a four-mark question on that board, which is a mark-scheme convention question and the one generalists fail most often.

The fifth is diagnostic rather than factual: what would you check first if my child kept losing marks on the six-mark questions? A good answer names something concrete, such as whether the student is making a judgement rather than listing points, or whether they are running out of time because the earlier questions were over-answered. A weak answer proposes more practice, which is what every tutor says and tells you nothing.

Run the same five questions past the nearest available tutor and past an online specialist. If the local tutor answers better, hire the local tutor; the point of publishing the test is that an Al Twar parent should be able to decide on evidence rather than on which website seemed more convincing. What we will say is that the test is easier to pass when the tutor was selected for the specification rather than for the drive.

sections.heading: Why the right past paper beats the right postcode
paragraphs: By Year 11 most tutoring hours are spent on past papers, which makes the choice of paper the most consequential decision in the whole arrangement. A board-matched paper teaches three things at once: the content, the phrasing, and the mark-scheme convention. A mismatched paper teaches the content and quietly mis-teaches the other two, and the student has no way of knowing. They will simply find the real paper oddly worded and score below what they know.

This is why specification fit outranks proximity in a district like Al Twar. The nearby pool is drawn from whoever will drive here on a weekday evening, and within that pool the chance of a precise match on board, code, tier and practical route for two or three subjects is not high. Across the whole set of tutors who teach a specification, it is close to certain. That is an argument about outcome rather than about convenience.

There is a second, subtler benefit. A tutor working with several students on the same specification sees the same mark-scheme traps repeatedly and develops a short list of the errors that cost most on that paper. That accumulated pattern knowledge is exactly what a parent is paying for above the budget band, and it only exists where a tutor has volume in the specification. A tutor covering four boards across six subjects for a local client list does not have it, however capable they are.

IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is an India-only service. For an Al Twar family that means the question stops being who is nearby and becomes who teaches Cambridge 0620 Extended, or Pearson 4MA1, every week. That is a question with a good answer, and it is the one worth asking.

sections.heading: Reading the grade: 9-1, A*-G and what a report actually says
paragraphs: Grading in this market is genuinely confusing, and the confusion costs families money because they buy tutoring against a misread report. Cambridge IGCSE reports some subjects on a 9-1 scale and others on A*-G, depending on the syllabus variant the school entered. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on 9-1. A school may therefore issue one report containing both scales, and a parent may reasonably conclude a child has slipped when nothing has happened at all.

The second source of confusion is internal grading. Many schools report predicted or working-at grades using their own internal scale during Year 10, which may not map onto either published scale. A working-at grade of 5 in a school's internal system is not necessarily a 5 on the final scale, and the school's own explanation of its scale is the only authority on that. Ask for it in writing; it is usually a single paragraph and it changes how every subsequent report reads.

The third is the tier interaction. A Core entry in a tiered Cambridge subject carries a grade ceiling, so a child reported as working at the top of Core is not working at the top of the subject. That distinction is frequently lost in conversation, and it matters enormously for post-16 planning, because A Level and Diploma Higher Level routes have prerequisites expressed on the full scale.

For tutoring purposes the practical instruction is simple. Get three things in writing from the school: the scale each subject is reported on, the tier where applicable, and what the school's internal grades mean relative to the final scale. Then a tutoring plan can be built against the real position rather than the apparent one, and you will not be paying to fix a problem that is actually a reporting artefact.
