sections.heading: Specification coverage near Al Twar, and the fallback if nobody matches
paragraphs: No page in this market publishes a coverage limit, and that silence is doing work. Tutor supply is uneven by specification, not just by subject. Cambridge mathematics and the three Cambridge sciences at Extended are well covered. Pearson Edexcel equivalents are reasonably covered. Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics, 0478 Computer Science with its specification-specific pseudocode conventions, and first-language Arabic are thinner, and a precise match on an unusual combination can take longer.

Our rule is stated the same way on every UAE page. Where a UAE-based tutor covers the specification and tier, that is the match, because the term calendar and the time zone already align. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, we say so before you book and offer a tutor from the wider pool working Gulf Standard Time at the same band. What we will not do is place a tutor who teaches a different board and let the difference surface in a mock, which is the failure this whole page exists to prevent.

There is an Al Twar-specific version of this worth naming. Families here often hold a school place in another district, or across the Sharjah boundary where private education is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority rather than KHDA and term dates can differ by a week. Both facts change what a tutor should be pacing to. Tell us the school by name and the plan follows its calendar and its entries rather than the neighbourhood's average.

sections.heading: What specification-correct teaching costs, and what a parent can check for free
paragraphs: Price does not guarantee specification fit, which is the useful thing to know before comparing quotes. A tutor at the published premium end can be teaching the wrong board, and a tutor at the mid band can be teaching exactly the right one. The market bands, read in October 2026 and attributed to their publishers, are these: Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end; qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's survey agreeing; in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate and up to AED 500 with independents; and BartyED advertising AED 650 at the premium end.

So use the five-question test as a filter before using price as one. Any tutor who can name your child's code, paper set, practical route and mark-scheme convention is in the running at whatever band they charge; any tutor who cannot is not worth the lowest rate on this page. That ordering is the single most useful thing a parent can take from a pricing comparison in this market, and nobody else publishes it because nobody else publishes prices at all.

Three further checks cost nothing. The permit: the UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own private tutor licensing service, which lists a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so disregard any figure quoted at you. The regulator: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and publishes inspection outcomes on its own site.

And the accreditation check, which settles a great deal quickly. Nobody offering you private tutoring is accredited, approved or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson to do it. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence for training institutes with physical premises, requiring initial approval first and annual renewal at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and occupies no UAE premises. If a provider claims board approval, ask for the number; Cambridge and Pearson publish their own centre lists.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether an IGCSE tutor near Al Twar teaches Cambridge or Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Considerably, and it is the question proximity hides. The boards cover similar content and examine it differently: question phrasing, paper structure, the way practical skills are assessed, and above all what counts as a complete answer for a given number of marks. A student trained on the wrong board's past papers for a term writes answers that feel right and score short. Ask your examinations officer for the board, the specification code and the tier before choosing a tutor, because the mismatch is invisible until a mock.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to our home in Al Twar?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. IGCSE tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen for worked questions and marked past papers. The reason that helps here is specification fit: the tutor can be selected for teaching Cambridge 0620 Extended or Pearson 4CH1 specifically, rather than for being the nearest person willing to drive on a weekday evening.

faqs.question: Which codes should I ask my child's school about?
faqs.answer: Ask for the code and tier in every subject. Cambridge codes you may see include 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0610 Biology, 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences, 0500 First Language English and 0478 Computer Science. Pearson Edexcel equivalents include 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4BI1. For sciences also ask which practical route the centre enters for, and for Cambridge ask which of the six administrative zones your centre sits in, because the timetable differs by zone.

faqs.question: Can my child's grade be capped by the tier they were entered for?
faqs.answer: In Cambridge subjects with Core and Extended tiering, yes. A Core entry examines a reduced syllabus on a narrower paper set and carries a ceiling below the top grades, and no amount of tutoring lifts it. Entries are set well before the examination year, so this is a Year 10 question. Ask for the tier in writing, ask what evidence placed your child there, and ask the final date for an entry amendment. Pearson Edexcel is untiered in many subjects, which removes the issue there, though Mathematics A is offered at Foundation and Higher tier.

faqs.question: Is an untiered Edexcel paper easier than Cambridge Extended?
faqs.answer: Not easier, differently structured. Because an untiered paper must serve the whole ability range, the hardest and the most accessible questions sit in the same booklet, which makes question selection and time allocation part of the examined skill. Cambridge Extended presents a more uniformly demanding paper to a pre-selected group. Neither is softer; they reward slightly different exam technique, and knowing which applies to your child is exactly the kind of specification detail a board-matched tutor brings.

faqs.question: How can I test whether a tutor really knows my child's specification?
faqs.answer: Five questions. Which board and code do you teach for this subject? How many papers will my child sit and what does each cover? Which practical route does the centre use, and how does your preparation differ? What counts as a complete four-mark answer on this board? And what would you check first if my child kept losing marks on six-mark questions? Precise answers to the first four and a concrete diagnostic answer to the fifth is what you are listening for, rather than fluency.

faqs.question: Why do past papers from the wrong board cause so much damage?
faqs.answer: Because by Year 11 most tutoring time goes into them, so they teach three things at once: content, phrasing and mark-scheme convention. A board-matched paper teaches all three correctly. A mismatched one teaches the content and quietly mis-teaches the other two, and neither student nor parent can see it happening. The student then finds the real paper oddly worded and scores below what they know. It is the most common avoidable waste in this market and it costs nothing to prevent.

faqs.question: My school report shows both numbers and letters. Why?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge reports some IGCSE subjects on a 9-1 scale and others on A*-G depending on the syllabus variant the school entered, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on 9-1. A single report can therefore carry both. Many schools also add internal working-at or predicted grades on their own scale, which may not map onto either. Ask the school which scale each subject uses and how its internal grades relate to the published scale, in writing. It changes how every later report reads.

faqs.question: How are science practical skills examined if my child studies online?
faqs.answer: As a written skill set, which is how the alternative-to-practical route works in any case. Students are assessed on identifying variables, reading instruments to an appropriate precision, tabulating with correct headings and units, choosing a sensible graph scale, spotting anomalies and proposing specific rather than generic improvements. All of that is examinable from a written description of an experiment nobody performed, and it is coachable over a shared screen. Confirm with the school which route your centre enters for, because preparation differs.

faqs.question: Which series will my child in Al Twar sit, and when are results published?
faqs.answer: The June series or the November series. The February and March series is offered to India only and does not apply to a UAE candidate. On published facts: the Pearson Edexcel November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Read the live official timetable from the board for current dates rather than any restatement.

Cambridge mathematics and the three Cambridge sciences at Extended are well covered; Additional Mathematics, Computer Science with its board-specific pseudocode conventions and first-language Arabic are thinner. faqs.question: Is my child's tutor allowed to tutor privately in the UAE at all?

faqs.question: Could my son sit Cambridge sciences and an Edexcel maths paper together?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it happens more often than parents expect, because schools choose board by department rather than by school. A student can sit Cambridge sciences and a Pearson Edexcel mathematics paper in the same series. For tutoring this matters a great deal: each subject needs its own matched past papers and mark-scheme conventions, and a tutor comfortable in one board's mathematics is not automatically comfortable in another's. Ask for the code subject by subject rather than assuming one answer covers the whole report.

It is not a credential for individual private tutors. intro.heading: Al Warqa after 15:30: the hour that decides whether tutoring works
paragraphs: Most tutoring arrangements in this community do not fail because the tutor was poor. They fail because somebody agreed to 16:00 in August, when the day felt long, and then discovered in October that the bus from Al Qusais reaches Al Warqa'a 3 at 16:05, that football finishes at 17:00 on Mondays, and that a tired fifteen-year-old put in front of an algebra paper eight minutes after walking through the door learns very little. The slot is the single most under-examined decision in the whole purchase.

Al Warqa's geography sets the constraint. There is no IGCSE school inside the community, so every child travels: north into Al Qusais, west into Mirdif, or out along Ras Al Khor Road towards Festival City and Academic City. School days in Dubai typically end between 14:30 and 15:30, buses then take twenty-five to fifty minutes depending on the route and the number of drop-offs, and families collecting by car at Damascus Street or Mirdif pickup add their own delay. The realistic range for a first usable hour across this community is 16:30 at the earliest and 17:45 at the far end.

The second constraint is the week rather than the day. A Year 11 timetable already contains mocks, coursework deadlines, PE fixtures and, for most families here, Arabic and Islamic Education lessons that KHDA requires every Dubai private school to deliver alongside the licensed curriculum. Dropping a weekly tutoring hour into that without choosing its place deliberately produces a term of cancellations, and cancellations are what end tutoring arrangements, not disappointment with the teaching.

This is also where the near-me framing misleads most. A radius search answers the question who is close. It cannot answer the question that actually decides the outcome, which is who is genuinely free at 17:30 on a Tuesday and teaches Cambridge 0580 Extended. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. Every Al Warqa lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which means the slot is chosen from availability rather than negotiated around somebody's drive.

So the page below is a scheduling document with an IGCSE syllabus inside it. School end times and bus windows per cluster. The weekly pattern that survives Year 11. What changes in the eight weeks before the June or November series. How Ramadan moves the evening. And which IGCSE tasks actually fit a sixty-minute weeknight slot, because there are some that do not, and pretending otherwise is how a session becomes a chat. Everything here is checkable against your own household's timings, and it should be checked: the published arrival windows are typical rather than universal, bus routes change between terms, and the only number that matters in the end is the hour at which your particular fifteen-year-old can still do hard algebra.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-warqa.programmesIntro: Al Warqa students reach IGCSE through British-curriculum schools in Al Qusais, Mirdif and Academic City, with A Level or the IB Diploma afterwards. These notes cover what each stage demands of an evening timetable.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses with terminal written papers in the June and November series, most subjects tiered as Core or Extended, and sciences adding either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable.
programmes.countryNote: For scheduling purposes the key fact is that Cambridge content is cumulative across two years, so a weekly hour from Year 10 is worth more than three hours a week in the final term. Al Warqa families who start early get to use the 17:30 slot calmly; those who start late end up buying weekends.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Available in May-June and November each year, with Foundation and Higher tiers rather than Core and Extended. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.
programmes.countryNote: Those dates matter for an Al Warqa evening timetable because they tell you when the pressure arrives. A June series means mocks in the preceding winter and a serious revision phase from roughly February onwards, which is when a one-hour slot has to become two and the calendar needs to have room for it.

programmes.name: International A Level
programmes.description: The usual post-16 continuation for Dubai IGCSE students who do not move to the IB Diploma. Entry is constrained by IGCSE tier and grade, so a Core mathematics candidate has a narrower route into A Level Mathematics than an Extended one, which is why the tier conversation belongs in Year 10.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry of Education British-track equivalency requires one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E, or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, alongside five GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB route at the same ages, assessed against four criteria per subject group rather than by terminal examination. Scheduling is easier here because there is no fixed external series driving the calendar, and harder because deadlines arrive continuously rather than in one block.
programmes.countryNote: Al Warqa households with one child on IGCSE and another on MYP find the two calendars genuinely different: one builds towards a June series, the other produces assessed tasks all year. Two separate slots on two evenings handles that better than one shared arrangement.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-warqa.subjectsIntro: Each note names the syllabus code and says what kind of work the subject needs in a weeknight hour, because some IGCSE tasks fit a tired sixty minutes and some do not.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Fits an evening slot well: short topic blocks, then timed question sets marked against the scheme. Extended marks go on algebraic manipulation under pressure and on working an examiner cannot read, both of which improve with weekly repetition rather than long sessions.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two calculator-permitted papers, Foundation reaching grade 5 and Higher running to grade 9. Suits a fixed weekly hour from Year 10, because tier readiness needs to be evidenced before entries close rather than argued about afterwards.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Circuit analysis and graph work fit a weeknight hour; full practical write-ups do not. The alternative-to-practical paper is ideal evening material because it rewards method, variable control and error identification rather than manual skill.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Moles calculations and ionic equations are good short-session work. Organic nomenclature needs spaced repetition across weeks, which is an argument for a weekly hour from Year 10 rather than a block in Year 11.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: The terminology load makes this the subject most often tackled late in the evening and least suited to it. Short, frequent retrieval practice beats a long session, so a 45-minute slot twice a week often outperforms one hour.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (0654, 0653)
subjects.description: One syllabus across all three sciences with fewer papers and a wider spread per paper. Evening work has to be organised by paper rather than by science, otherwise revision drifts towards whichever science the student likes most.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing responds well to a weeknight hour; reading response needs longer. The practical compromise is to use the session for analysis and planning and have the writing done between sessions, which is also how the paper itself is structured.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510, 0511)
subjects.description: Listening and reading tasks are short and fit an evening slot cleanly. The tier affects both grade ceiling and vocabulary expectation, which makes an early readiness check more valuable than extra hours later.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (0455, 0450)
subjects.description: Diagram drill and case application are efficient evening work. Marks are lost where a term is defined correctly and never applied to the material in front of the candidate, which is a fifteen-minute habit rather than a content gap.

subjects.name: ICT and Computer Science (0417, 0478)
subjects.description: Practical components need equipment and time, so the useful evening work is the theory paper and the written problem-solving. Trying to run a full practical task in a weeknight hour wastes most of the hour on setup.

sections.heading: The Al Warqa school run, timed cluster by cluster
paragraphs: Dubai private school days generally end between 14:30 and 15:30, with secondary timetables at the later end. From there the variable is the journey. A bus from an Al Qusais school to Al Warqa'a 1 is a twenty-five to thirty-five minute run with a handful of stops. The same bus continuing into Al Warqa'a 3 and 4 adds drop-offs and arrives closer to 16:15. Families collecting by car at Mirdif or Damascus Street save some of that and lose it again to pickup congestion.

Then there is the part of the afternoon nobody schedules around: the forty minutes after a child walks in. Changing, eating and decompressing is not optional, and a lesson that starts inside it produces an hour of nominal attendance. The practical rule in this community is arrival time plus forty-five minutes, which for most Al Warqa addresses lands between 16:45 and 17:30 and for the far plots later still.

The table below sets that out per cluster. It is worth checking against your own household rather than accepting it, because the single most useful number in this whole arrangement is the real time your child is capable of working, and only you know it. Families who set the slot from that number keep tutoring going for two years. Families who set it from an empty space in a calendar renegotiate in November and give up by February. The difference is not motivation, and it is not the tutor; it is fifteen minutes of honest planning done once in September.

sections.heading: Why the four o'clock slot fails and the half past five slot holds
paragraphs: A 16:00 booking looks efficient. The child is home, the evening is intact, homework happens afterwards. In practice it fails for three reasons stacked on top of each other. The bus is late once a fortnight. The child has not eaten. And Monday football, Wednesday swimming or Thursday Arabic support collide with it on at least two days of the five, so the slot moves, and a slot that moves twice stops being a slot.

A 17:30 booking survives because it sits after all of that. The child has eaten, the activity has finished, the traffic has happened, and the hour is genuinely available rather than theoretically available. It costs the evening some flexibility, which is why families resist it, and it buys two years of uninterrupted weekly contact, which is the thing that actually moves an IGCSE grade.

There is one real exception. Some fifteen-year-olds are finished by 19:00 and a 17:30 session is their last useful hour; others are sharper at 19:30 after a proper break. The right question is not when is the room free but when is this child capable of doing hard work, and the answer differs between siblings in the same house. Online delivery makes that answerable per child, because nobody is driving and two slots on one evening cost no more than one. Try the trial lesson at the hour you actually intend to keep rather than at a comfortable weekend time, and the question answers itself within forty minutes.

sections.heading: A weekly pattern that survives Year 11
paragraphs: Year 11 is not a flat year. It contains a winter mock block, coursework and practical deadlines, the Arabic and Islamic Education lessons KHDA requires of every Dubai private school, and a revision phase that starts roughly three months before the series. A tutoring arrangement that ignores that shape gets cancelled during the busy parts, which is exactly when it was most needed.

The pattern that holds puts the tutoring hour on a day with no fixture, keeps it through mock week rather than suspending it, and uses the session during mocks for paper review rather than new content. Reviewing a failed mock paper with a tutor the week it comes back is among the highest-value hours in the entire course, and it is the hour most families cancel because the week is busy.

The second element is the deliberate step up. Eight to ten weeks before a June or November series the weekly hour becomes two, with a weekend slot for full-length timed papers that genuinely cannot be sat properly on a school night at 17:30. Agreeing that in advance means the calendar has space for it. Discovering it in March means buying weekend hours at whatever is left, which is how a reasonable arrangement turns into an expensive scramble. The third element is knowing when to stop: tutoring that continues through the series itself usually displaces sleep rather than adding marks, so the arrangement should have an end date written into it from the beginning.

sections.heading: Ramadan, prayer times and the evening that moves
paragraphs: The Dubai academic year contains a period when every evening timetable changes, and fixed in-home arrangements handle it badly. School hours shorten during Ramadan, the useful study window shifts to after Iftar, and a household's whole rhythm moves by two or three hours for several weeks. A tutor whose arrangement depends on a drive across the city at a particular hour either renegotiates or disappears.

Online delivery absorbs this with a calendar change and nothing else. A 17:30 slot becomes a 21:00 slot for the month and returns afterwards. Families who prefer to pause entirely can do so and keep the slot. Where a student is sitting a series shortly after, the post-Iftar window is often the better study time anyway, because it is quieter and the child is not coming straight off a shortened school day.

The same flexibility covers the smaller disruptions that break fixed bookings: prayer times that a family schedules around, travel during the long holidays when a student keeps working from another timezone, and the weeks when a school's own examination timetable means a child needs three sessions one week and none the next. None of those require a contract conversation when there is no journey attached to the arrangement. It is worth saying plainly that this is the main practical advantage of the format in a city with a calendar as variable as Dubai's. The academic year here contains a shortened-hours period, two long holiday blocks during which many families leave the country, and a school examination timetable that compresses a term's work into three weeks. An arrangement that bends around all of that without renegotiation is simply more likely to still exist in March than one that does not.
bullets: Shortened school days move the usable study window entirely
Post-Iftar sessions work well and need only a calendar change

sections.heading: Counting backwards from a June or November series
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The February-March series exists but is offered to India only, which is worth repeating because incorrect advice about it circulates in this market. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in June and November, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests at other points in the year, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones. Cambridge states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable.

Pearson's published pattern gives usable anchors. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May-June and November each year; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also issues provisional timetables well ahead of each series, which is why every plan should start from the live official timetable rather than a restated date on any page.

For an Al Warqa evening timetable, that pattern translates into three decisions. Where the mock block sits, because the week a mock paper comes back is the most valuable tutoring hour of the year. Where the step up from one session to two goes, which should be eight to ten weeks before the first paper. And when the arrangement ends, which should be a date rather than a drift, because tutoring that continues through the series itself usually displaces sleep rather than adding marks.

sections.heading: What a near-me search cannot see about 17:30 on a Tuesday
paragraphs: A map result tells you who is close and who paid for the listing. It does not tell you whether that person has a free slot at the only hour your child can work. In Al Warqa this is the binding constraint, because the window between 17:00 and 19:00 is when every family in the community wants a tutor, and a tutor who travels can serve one household in it rather than three.

There are two other things the result hides. Permit status, which in the UAE is a real question with a free answer: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time through its app, website and e-services. And eligibility, because a teacher cannot be paid to tutor a student enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

Reframing the search fixes all of it at once. Ask who teaches Cambridge 0580 Extended and is free at 17:30 on Tuesdays, and the list that comes back is short, honest and composed of people who can actually do the job. That is the list this page is built to produce, and it is produced from availability at Gulf Standard Time rather than from a radius drawn around Al Warqa'a 3. It is a shorter list than a map of pins, and every name on it can take the hour your child can actually work.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE tasks actually fit a weeknight hour
paragraphs: Not everything does, and pretending otherwise is how a session becomes a conversation. A full 0580 Extended Paper 4 takes longer than the slot and leaves no time for marking, so attempting it on a school night produces an unmarked paper and a tired child. The same is true of a full English reading response and of any practical write-up worth doing.

What fits well is the work that produces marks fastest: short topic teaching followed by a timed question set, mark-scheme reading on a specific question type, command-term drill, and review of a paper the student has already sat. Reviewing marked work is the single most efficient use of a weeknight hour, which is a useful thing to know because it means the homework between sessions should usually be a paper, not more questions.

The planning consequence is simple. Keep full papers for weekends or study leave, and use the weeknight slot for teaching, drilling and review. Where a subject is terminology-heavy, as Biology is, two forty-five minute slots across the week beat a single hour, because spaced retrieval is what actually fixes recall. Where a subject is calculation-heavy, as Extended Mathematics and Chemistry are, a single consistent hour with a short timed set each week works better. One more rule is worth adopting: whatever the session does, it should end with the next piece of work named and dated. A session that finishes with a vague instruction to revise produces nothing by the following week, and the hour then starts again from the same place it started the week before.

sections.heading: The mandatory subjects that are already in your evening
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's mandatory-subjects requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For a Year 11 IGCSE student these sit alongside the examined subjects, and they occupy timetable space that families planning tutoring routinely forget.

The organisational rules are specific. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, while non-Arabs study Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. For these subjects, using any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so tutoring support here consolidates the school's own material rather than offering an alternative scheme. Note too that Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five subjects counted for British-track equivalency, so they add work without adding to that count.

process.title: Write down the actual arrival time
process.description: Not the end of the school day, the time your child walks into the house in Al Warqa. Add forty-five minutes for changing and eating. That number, not the gap in a calendar, is where the session should start, and getting it right is most of what makes an arrangement last two years.

process.title: Map the activities first
process.description: Football, swimming, Arabic support and family commitments go on the page before the tutoring hour does. A slot chosen around them survives; a slot chosen into them moves twice and then stops being a slot. This takes ten minutes and saves a term of cancellations.

process.title: Send the syllabus codes and one marked paper
process.description: Codes from the entry form, such as 0580 or 4MA1, tell a tutor which papers to teach. A recently marked paper shows whether marks go on content, technique or illegible working. Together they let the first session be teaching rather than discovery.

process.title: Take the free trial in the real slot
process.description: Run the trial at the time you intend to keep, not at a convenient weekend hour. A session that works at 11:00 on a Saturday tells you nothing about whether your child can think at 17:30 on a Tuesday, which is the question that matters.

process.title: Agree the step up before you need it
process.description: Decide now where the second weekly session goes in the eight to ten weeks before the series, and where the weekend paper slot sits. Booking that in advance costs nothing and avoids buying whatever is left in March at whatever it costs.

whyPoints.title: The slot is treated as part of the purchase
whyPoints.description: Arrival time plus forty-five minutes, activities mapped first, and the trial run at the hour you intend to keep. Most tutoring arrangements in this community fail on scheduling rather than on teaching, and almost nobody discusses it before taking payment.

whyPoints.title: A fixed tutor and a fixed time
whyPoints.description: The same person at the same hour every week, because IGCSE content is cumulative across two years and consistency outperforms flexibility. A rota is easier to staff and worse for the student, so we do not run one.

whyPoints.title: Series dates from the official timetable
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit June and November; the February-March series is India-only. Cambridge allocates centres to six zones and warns that the wrong zone timetable can cost an exam, so every plan starts from the live official document.

whyPoints.title: Ramadan and travel handled by calendar, not contract
whyPoints.description: A 17:30 slot becomes a post-Iftar slot for the month and returns afterwards. Families travelling over the holidays shift the clock rather than cancelling. None of that is possible when a journey is part of the arrangement.

whyPoints.title: Online one-to-one, said before you book
whyPoints.description: Al Warqa lessons run one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service is India-only. The format is stated on every page rather than discovered afterwards.

whyPoints.title: No approval claimed, no grade promised
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson approval and claims none. Nothing here promises a grade, a score or an improvement, because no tutor can deliver what happens in an examination hall.

faqs.question: What time should an IGCSE session start for a child living in Al Warqa?
faqs.answer: Take the time your child actually walks in and add forty-five minutes. For Al Warqa'a 1 with a short Al Qusais run that usually means 16:30. For Al Warqa'a 2 it is nearer 17:00, for Al Warqa'a 3 about 17:15, and for Al Warqa'a 4 and 5 with an Academic City or Festival City run, 17:45. Children schooled locally in Mirdif can manage 16:00. The number that matters is the one for your household, because an hour booked inside the decompression window produces attendance rather than learning.

faqs.question: Why do our tutoring arrangements in Al Warqa keep falling apart after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: Almost always the slot rather than the tutor. A 16:00 booking collides with a late bus roughly once a fortnight, with an unfed teenager every day, and with at least two weekday activities. Once a slot has moved twice it is no longer a slot, and cancellations are what end tutoring arrangements. Mapping football, swimming and Arabic support before choosing the hour, then setting it at 17:15 or 17:30, is unglamorous and is the single change that makes an arrangement last two years.

faqs.question: Are two shorter sessions better than one hour for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For terminology-heavy subjects, yes. Biology and language work respond better to forty-five minutes twice a week than to a single hour, because spaced retrieval is what fixes recall, and two shorter slots are also easier to place in an Al Warqa evening where a full hour competes with sport. For calculation-heavy subjects such as Extended Mathematics and Chemistry, one consistent hour with a timed question set each week works better. The cost is the same either way.

faqs.question: Should we keep tutoring through mock exam week or pause it?
faqs.answer: Keep it, and change what it does. The week a mock paper comes back marked is the most valuable tutoring hour of the entire course: the student has just demonstrated exactly where the marks go, and reviewing that script against the mark scheme converts a disappointing result into a plan. Families routinely cancel during mock weeks because the fortnight is busy, which is precisely backwards. Pause during the real series instead, when extra sessions usually displace sleep rather than add marks.

faqs.question: How far before the June series should we increase to two sessions a week?
faqs.answer: Eight to ten weeks, and agree it in advance so the calendar has room. That phase is for timed question sets, mark-scheme reading and command-term discipline rather than new content, with a weekend slot added for full-length papers that genuinely cannot be sat properly at 17:30 on a school night. Deciding this in February means buying whatever weekend hours remain at whatever they cost, which turns a planned arrangement into an expensive scramble.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change an Al Warqa tutoring timetable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it only requires a calendar change. School hours shorten, the useful study window moves to after Iftar, and a 17:30 slot becomes a 21:00 slot for the month before returning. Families who prefer to pause entirely can hold the slot rather than release it. Where a series falls shortly afterwards, the post-Iftar window is often the better study time anyway, because it is quieter and the child is not working straight off a shortened school day.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE work should not be attempted in a weeknight session?
faqs.answer: Anything that cannot be finished and marked inside the hour. A full Cambridge 0580 Extended Paper 4 takes longer than the slot and produces an unmarked paper and a tired student. The same is true of a full English reading response under timed conditions and of any practical or coursework write-up. Keep those for weekends or study leave, and use the weeknight hour for topic teaching, timed question sets, mark-scheme drill and review of work already marked.

faqs.question: Does my Al Warqa child's bus route really affect which tutor we can use?
faqs.answer: It affects the slot, and the slot affects which tutors are genuinely available. A route that drops at Al Warqa'a 1 first and Al Warqa'a 4 last creates a forty-minute spread across one community, and between 17:00 and 19:00 every household in the area wants a tutor. A tutor who travels can serve one family in that window. Matching from everyone free at Gulf Standard Time rather than everyone nearby is what makes the right hour available at all.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams actually held for Dubai candidates?
faqs.answer: In the June and November series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in those two series and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May-June and November; its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. The February-March series is offered to India only.

faqs.question: How long after the exams do results reach students in the UAE?
faqs.answer: The published Pearson pattern gives the shape: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking citations rather than a promise about a future series, and Pearson issues provisional timetables ahead of each sitting. Always confirm your own dates against the live official timetable and your school's examinations officer rather than any restated figure, including the ones on this page.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education lessons add to my child's IGCSE subject count?
faqs.answer: No. They are mandatory in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA requiring implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, but Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five subjects counted for Ministry of Education British-track equivalency. So they occupy real timetable space, including the after-school slots families want for tutoring, without contributing to that count. Plan the evening around them rather than discovering the clash in October.

faqs.question: Can both our children have sessions on the same evening from one house?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is where online delivery is plainly better for an Al Warqa household. Two children at different schools arrive up to forty minutes apart, and they frequently need different subjects at different levels. Two specialists can teach them at 17:15 and 18:30 on the same evening with nobody waiting and no second journey. A visiting tutor forces a choice between the two children or a second travel premium on an already stretched monthly figure.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start IGCSE tutoring in the final term of Year 11?
faqs.answer: Not too late to be useful, but the work changes. With a few months left, the gains come from paper technique rather than content: timed questions, mark-scheme reading, command-term discipline and review of marked papers. That is a short, finite block of six to ten sessions with a clear end date at the first exam. What will not work is attempting to teach two years of cumulative syllabus content in a weeknight hour, and any provider who says otherwise is selling hours.

faqs.question: Does my tutor need a permit, and does it apply to online lessons?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time via its app, website and e-services, and eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published anywhere official.

intro.heading: The year an IGCSE family in Al Wasl is actually living in
paragraphs: Al Wasl is a villa district on the Al Wasl Road corridor, a few minutes from the Al Safa school cluster and a short run from Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim. The families here searching for an IGCSE tutor are rarely browsing. They have a date in mind, and the single most useful thing a page can do is tell them which dates matter, who sets each one, and which of them have already passed. Nearly every expensive mistake in a Year 10 or Year 11 household is a timing mistake rather than a teaching one.

The published dates are worth stating precisely, because named examination sessions returned zero matches across every competitor page fetched for this research. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and those are the two UAE candidates sit. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026 with results reaching students in January, November 2025 results arrived on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August.

There is a warning in the Cambridge timetable system that no tutoring page mentions. Every examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and it says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson, separately, publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so dates can change. The practical rule for an Al Wasl family is simple: the timetable comes from the school and from the board's own document for your centre's zone, never from a website.

The 'near me' half of the search deserves a direct answer too. What proximity gets a family is a shortlist of people willing to drive to Al Wasl Road on a weekday afternoon, which is a selection criterion unrelated to whether somebody has taught Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4CH1. Published Dubai in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for qualified subject tutors working online, so the proximity requirement costs money as well as choice. IB Gram delivers one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time and provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India.

The rest of this page is the calendar. It counts a series backwards with every milestone named, sets out which decisions close in Year 10 and which in Year 11, explains the November route for resits and splits and the private-candidate option, says what the six weeks after a mock should contain, gives a revision week that works with ten subjects, covers the deadlines that run after results including review of marking, and states where specialist availability is thin and what we will not claim.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-wasl.subjectsIntro: Eight to ten subjects, each with its own place in the calendar. These are the ones Al Wasl families ask about, with what each needs at which point in the year.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The subject whose calendar starts earliest, because tier placement rests on Year 10 evidence and caps the grade range. In Year 11 it responds to short frequent practice on algebraic speed rather than long sessions. Establish which of the three specifications applies before any planning, because the papers and calculator rules differ.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Needs a mid-year diagnostic rather than an end-of-year block, because the quantitative chain from moles to concentration to titration arithmetic breaks at a link a student cannot locate alone. Found in one session; repaired across several weeks. Leaving it until the spring term halves what the same hours achieve.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Responds to short, frequent practice across weeks on formula handling, units and graph work, and badly to a single intensive block, which is a scheduling fact rather than a preference. Electricity and the wave vocabulary carry most losses. Plan it as a daily twenty minutes plus a fortnightly check rather than a weekly hour.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The subject best suited to a timetable rather than a tutor, because the load is recall volume. Build the retrieval schedule in the winter break and run it through the spring. What does need teaching is command-term discipline and the data-interpretation questions, which can be covered in two or three sessions at any point.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.description: Marks move on structure, on answering the question asked and on timing, so the useful intervention is two or three sessions plus marked timed practice rather than ongoing weekly work. Literature has a separate entry at Pearson, and the set texts determine when revision can realistically begin.

subjects.name: Combined and double-award science
subjects.description: The route that materially lightens a Year 11 revision calendar, which is sometimes the right answer for a candidate carrying ten subjects. The decision closes with the entry deadline, so it has to be raised in the autumn. Past-paper practice must come from the combined specification rather than the separate-science papers.

subjects.name: Business, Economics and ICT
subjects.description: Case-study subjects where the technique is applying terminology to the specific scenario. Teachable in a short block and then practised alone, which makes them good candidates for a February block and poor candidates for a year of weekly sessions. ICT and computer science are separate syllabuses.

subjects.name: Modern and community languages
subjects.levels: French, Spanish, Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: The one area where regular short sessions beat blocks, because speaking and listening need frequency rather than intensity. Oral components have their own place in the calendar and need a tutor who will conduct them under timed conditions. Availability varies sharply by language and level.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.levels: KHDA requirement · all Dubai private schools
subjects.description: Mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils and prescribed languages of instruction. They occupy real homework hours during the revision term and are excluded from the Ministry of Education's five-subject equivalency count.

sections.heading: What 'near me' and 'this term' are both asking
paragraphs: Two questions arrive together in this search and only one of them is about geography. The first is whether anyone competent is available. The second, underneath it, is whether there is still time. A family typing this in September is asking something quite different from a family typing it in March, and a page that answers only the proximity question has not helped either of them. So the proximity question first, briefly, and then the calendar, which is the part that actually determines what a household should do.

Proximity gets an Al Wasl family a shortlist of people prepared to drive to Al Wasl Road on a weekday afternoon. That is a filter with no relationship to whether somebody has taught Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4MA1 Higher tier. It also costs money: published Dubai in-home rates run AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 rate table and AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors, against AED 150 to 300 for qualified subject tutors working online. IB Gram delivers one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time and does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE, because in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India.

The timing question is the one worth real attention, because the answer changes by month and nobody tells a family which month they are in. In September almost everything is open: tier placements, entry decisions, subject counts, and twenty-plus usable weeks. By February the decisions have closed and what remains is six or seven usable weeks of triage. In April the honest answer is two topics per subject and exam behaviour. Each of those is a legitimate plan and they cost different amounts, and a family that buys the September plan in April will be disappointed for reasons that have nothing to do with the tutor.

Anchoring facts, with sources. Cambridge runs the June and November series for UAE candidates and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating that the correct zone version of the timetable must be used and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. sections.heading: Year 10 and Year 11: which decisions close when
paragraphs: This is the section that would save Al Wasl families the most money if they read it a year earlier than they do. The decisions with the longest consequences are taken in Year 10 and early Year 11, on evidence that is thinner than anyone would like, and they cannot be reopened afterwards. A tutor hired in March of Year 11 is working inside a set of constraints that were fixed twelve months earlier, and no amount of teaching lifts a ceiling that was set on an entry form.

The three biggest are tier placement, the separate-versus-combined science route, and the number of subjects entered. Tier placement in Cambridge mathematics and the separate sciences, and in Pearson Mathematics A, determines which papers are sat and which grades can be awarded; a Core or Foundation candidate cannot reach the top grades however well they perform. The science route determines the revision volume for the whole of Year 11 and matters for sixth-form science entry. The subject count determines whether a revision calendar is completable at all.

What a parent can do is specific and takes two emails. Ask which tier each mathematics and science entry currently sits in, what evidence the placement rests on, and when the window to change it closes. Then ask the intended sixth form, in writing, what it requires: some A Level and Diploma science courses expect separate sciences, and assumptions made at the school gate are frequently wrong. Both answers are obtainable, both are free, and both are worth more than a term of tutoring bought for the wrong reason.

sections.heading: The November route: resits, splits and the private-candidate option
paragraphs: Both boards run a November series alongside the June or May/June one, and that single fact gives a family more options than most realise. A student can resit a specific subject in November without repeating a year. A student carrying too many subjects can split the load across two series, sitting some in November and the rest in June, which converts an uncompletable revision calendar into two manageable ones. And a student whose June result was close to a boundary has a result in hand by January, which makes planning considerably easier than waiting for the following August.

The administrative decisions belong to the school and the examination centre. Whether a centre will enter a candidate for a particular series, which subjects, and by when are all school questions, and the entry deadline governs everything. Pearson's November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results arrived on 22 January 2026. For Cambridge, the November series is the standard resit route for UAE candidates, with the correct zone timetable as the only reliable source of dates.

There is also a private-candidate route, where a student sits papers at a centre that accepts external candidates rather than through their own school. It is used by home-educated students, by students whose school does not offer a particular subject, and occasionally by a student wanting a subject their timetable could not fit. It involves finding a centre that accepts private candidates, meeting that centre's own deadlines, and paying entry fees set by the centre and the board rather than by any tutor. Those fees vary and are not quoted here. Practical components complicate it: a science entry requiring a practical test needs a centre able to administer one, which is a real constraint worth checking before planning anything.

sections.heading: Mock season, and what the six weeks after it should contain
paragraphs: The mock is the most valuable measurement of the year and the most commonly wasted. A family that receives a set of mock grades and reacts to the numbers has thrown away the data. What matters is each script: which questions were lost, and why. Go through every paper and assign each lost mark to one of five categories, which are content not known, command term misread, notation or units, missing reasoning step, and arithmetic or accuracy. Then count the categories across all subjects, which takes an evening and changes everything that follows.

The counts tell you which of three situations you are in. Content losses concentrated in one or two subjects mean a teaching need in those subjects and nowhere else. Command-term losses spread evenly across four or five subjects mean a reading problem, and three or four sessions on command terms will raise marks in all of them at once, which is the cheapest intervention available. Unanswered questions at the end of papers mean a timing problem, which needs a timer and papers rather than a tutor. Most Year 11 students in this corridor turn out to be in the second or third situation and are sold the first.

Then the hard part, which is writing down what will not be covered. Six usable weeks across eight to ten subjects cannot address a full specification, and naming the abandoned topics converts anxiety into a decision. Students revise better when they know what they are allowed to ignore. A provider who refuses to have that conversation is leaving the only genuinely difficult judgement to the family, and the result is a student spreading six weeks evenly across everything and consolidating none of it.

sections.heading: A revision week that actually exists, with ten subjects
paragraphs: A Year 11 candidate in this corridor is carrying eight to ten subjects plus mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies homework, a school run of fifteen to thirty minutes each way, and whatever sport or music has not been dropped. A revision plan that assumes four free hours an evening is describing a different household. The week below assumes two genuinely usable hours on weekday evenings and a longer weekend morning, which is what most families in Al Wasl actually have once everything else is deducted.

Three design rules make it hold. Retrieval, not reading: every weekday block ends with the student answering something from memory, because rereading notes produces familiarity rather than recall. Rotation, not coverage: subjects cycle on a fixed pattern so that each is touched every five or six days, which is what spacing requires, rather than each being revised intensively once and then abandoned. And one empty evening, which is not slack but the absorber for the mock timetable changing, the school trip nobody mentioned and the week the student is unwell.

The weekend morning is where timed papers belong, because a full paper needs an uninterrupted stretch and weekday evenings do not provide one. In Al Wasl specifically the weekend is unusually usable, because the school run disappears and the house is quieter than in the apartment districts nearby. A family that protects two hours on a Saturday morning for one timed paper, marked properly against the published mark scheme, will get more from the spring term than one that adds a third tutored hour to a weekday evening.

sections.heading: After results: review of marking, resits and what the certificate is for
paragraphs: Three things happen after results and each has a deadline. The first is a review of marking, which both boards offer through the school rather than directly to a family. It is worth understanding two features before requesting one: it is a review of how the mark scheme was applied rather than a re-mark to a different standard, and the outcome can lower a grade as well as raise it. The school makes the submission, there are fees and deadlines set by the board, and the sensible basis for a request is a specific paper whose result is inconsistent with everything else the student produced.

The second is the resit decision, which is a calendar question. A June candidate has results in August and the November series ahead of them; a November candidate has results in January and the following June series ahead. In both cases the entry deadline for the next series sits well before it, so the decision is made quickly and with the school. A targeted resit on one or two subjects, driven by the previous script rather than by the whole specification, is a short block of work. Repeating the entire course is rarely the right answer and is frequently what gets sold.

The third is the certificate itself and what it is for. IGCSE results feed sixth-form entry and, later, the Ministry of Education equivalency process: the published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among those five, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. A competitor ranking for these searches states six subjects, which does not match the published rule. IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees equivalency, it is handled through the official channel, and no tutoring is required for it.

sections.heading: Delivery, cost per usable week, availability and the limits
paragraphs: The useful cost figure in a calendar-driven decision is not the hourly rate, it is what the whole intervention costs against the number of usable weeks left. Six usable weeks of one weekly session, at the published Dubai band of AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor, is a defined and modest commitment. The same money spread across three subjects for the same six weeks buys three sessions that each achieve a third as much. For context, the rest of the market runs from budget online provision at AED 33 to 52 from Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 from EdFlik, through Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, to specialists at AED 200 to 450 with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650, with in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 rate table and AED 200 to 500 from independent home tutors. Those are published figures belonging to the named companies.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own script, the correct board's past paper and the published mark scheme on screen together. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. In a calendar-driven term the practical benefit is that a session moves when the school moves a mock week, which it will, rather than being lost. Availability is finite and we publish where: Extended or Higher tier mathematics and sciences in a narrow weekday window may take several days to fill, and less commonly taught languages longer. When the first choice is unavailable we say so and name the alternative.

The limits in one place. Private tuition in the UAE requires a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years through MoHRE's private tutor licensing service; tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and as no schedule of amounts is published, none is quoted. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, certified or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and holds no UAE premises. We do not reproduce or supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference them and link the official source. And every date on this page must be checked against the school and the board's own timetable for the correct administrative zone.

faqs.question: What does 'IGCSE tutor near me' get an Al Wasl family that online does not?
faqs.answer: A shorter shortlist and a higher price. Proximity selects for willingness to drive to Al Wasl Road on a weekday afternoon, which has no relationship to whether somebody has taught Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4MA1 Higher tier. Published Dubai in-home rates run AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 table and AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors, against AED 150 to 300 for qualified subject tutors working online. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India, and lessons here run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: When does the examination entry deadline close, and what if we miss it?
faqs.answer: Months before the papers, set by the board and administered by the school, which is why the school is the only reliable source. Boards need entries to build timetables, distribute materials to centres and allocate examiners. If it is missed, the realistic options are the next series, which for both boards means June or November, or a private-candidate entry at a centre that accepts external candidates and has its own deadlines. Neither is a disaster and both are easier to arrange with notice, so ask the head of year for the deadline in writing in the autumn term.

faqs.question: Which decisions in Year 10 cannot be changed later?
faqs.answer: Four, in practice. Tier placement in Cambridge mathematics and the separate sciences and in Pearson Mathematics A, which determines the papers sat and the grade range available. The separate-versus-combined science route, which sets the Year 11 revision volume and matters for sixth-form science entry. The number of subjects entered, which decides whether a revision calendar is completable. And which practical component a Cambridge science candidate sits. All four close at the entry deadline, on Year 10 evidence, and no amount of teaching afterwards lifts a ceiling set on an entry form.

faqs.question: Can my child sit some IGCSE subjects as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: Yes, through a centre that accepts external candidates, and it is used by home-educated students, by students whose school does not offer a subject, and occasionally where a timetable could not fit one. The practicalities matter: the centre sets its own deadlines, entry fees are set by the centre and the board rather than by any tutor and vary, and practical components complicate it because a science entry requiring a practical test needs a centre able to administer one. Check the practical position before planning anything, and confirm the deadlines directly with the centre.

faqs.question: How does a request for a review of marking work?
faqs.answer: The school submits it to the board rather than the family approaching the board directly, there is a deadline shortly after results and there are fees. Two features are worth understanding before requesting one. It reviews whether the mark scheme was applied correctly rather than re-marking to a different standard, so a borderline judgement is unlikely to change. And the outcome can lower a grade as well as raise it. The sensible basis for a request is a specific paper whose result is inconsistent with everything else the student produced, discussed with the subject teacher first.

faqs.question: What should the six weeks after a mock actually contain?
faqs.answer: Work driven by the scripts rather than by the grades. Assign every lost mark to one of five categories: content not known, command term misread, notation or units, missing reasoning step, arithmetic or accuracy. Count them across all subjects. Content losses concentrated in one or two subjects mean teaching there and nowhere else. Command-term losses spread across four subjects mean three sessions that raise marks in all four. Unanswered questions mean a timer and papers rather than a tutor. Then write down which topics are being abandoned, because six weeks cannot cover eight to ten specifications.

faqs.question: How do we build a revision week around ten subjects?
faqs.answer: On two usable weekday hours and one weekend morning, which is what most Al Wasl households actually have after the school run, mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education homework and everything else. Three rules make it hold: retrieval rather than reading, so every block ends with something answered from memory; rotation rather than coverage, so each subject is touched every five or six days; and one completely empty evening as the absorber for mock changes, trips and illness. Put the full timed paper on the weekend morning, because a weekday evening cannot provide an uninterrupted stretch.

faqs.question: Is there any advantage to splitting subjects between November and June?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a candidate carrying too many subjects, and it is under-used. Both boards run a November series alongside the June or May/June one, so sitting some subjects in November converts one uncompletable revision calendar into two manageable ones, and the November results arrive in January, which means a result is in hand before the summer series. Pearson's November 2026 timetable ran late October to 19 November 2026 with results to students in January. The decisions are the school's to administer, and the entry deadline for each series governs everything, so raise it in the autumn.

faqs.question: When do certificates arrive, and do we need them for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Statements of results come first and certificates follow later through the school, with timings set by the board. For the Ministry of Education's equivalency process the published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among those five, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. One competitor ranking for these searches states six subjects, which does not match the published rule. Verify through the official channel; IB Gram does not perform equivalency and no tutoring is required for it.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai school calendar leave enough revision weeks?
faqs.answer: Fewer than the calendar suggests, which is why counting honestly matters. Deduct the mock fortnight, school trips, the days around Eid, any family travel and the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education homework that does not stop, and a term that looks like twelve weeks is often seven or eight usable ones. The position of Ramadan within the academic year moves, so it can fall near the mock window one year and near the series the next. Plan the spring term in January when both the mock dates and the entry position are known, rather than renegotiating it in March.

faqs.question: How early should we book a tutor for the spring term?
faqs.answer: Before the January mock results arrive, if the subject is already known, and immediately after if it is not. The constraint is not money, it is slots: by February the early-evening hours between 17:00 and 19:00 are taken across Al Wasl, Al Safa, Jumeirah and City Walk simultaneously, and the tutors with current specification experience are committed. A family booking in September keeps the good hour at the ordinary rate; a family booking in March pays the ordinary rate for a worse hour or a weaker match. Flexibility of thirty minutes usually converts a week's wait into two days.

faqs.question: What is the best use of the winter break for a Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: One structural job per subject rather than general revision, which achieves nothing over a holiday. Build the retrieval timetable that will run through the spring and test it once. Locate and begin repairing the quantitative break in chemistry if there is one. Rebuild the physics formula set from memory. Sit one full paper in the subject you are most worried about and categorise the losses, so January starts with data rather than with a feeling. Ninety-minute sessions are possible in a break because there is no school day to recover from, which is not true in term time.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with sixth-form applications at the same time?
faqs.answer: With the academic part, usefully; with the application itself, only within limits. The useful work is establishing what the receiving sixth form actually requires in writing, subject by subject, because assumptions made at the school gate are frequently wrong and some A Level and Diploma science courses expect separate sciences. Where a personal statement or interview is involved, a tutor may discuss content, question an argument and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not write it. Anything presented as the student's own work has to be the student's own work.

faqs.question: If results come out worse than predicted, what are the options and the deadlines?
faqs.answer: Three options, each with a deadline. A review of marking, submitted by the school within the board's deadline, which reviews how the mark scheme was applied and can lower a grade as well as raise it. A resit in the next series, where the entry deadline sits well before the papers, which for both boards means June or November. Or acceptance and a conversation with the receiving sixth form, which often has more flexibility than a published requirement suggests. Deal with the deadlines first and the decision second, because the deadlines close whether or not a family is ready.

faqs.question: How many weeks does it take to see a mark actually change?
faqs.answer: Four to six, for habit-based losses, and considerably longer for content gaps. Command terms, units, notation and unshown working are habits: they change within a few weeks of being named and counted, and the change shows on the next timed paper. Missing content takes as long as it takes to teach, and in a full specification that is months rather than weeks. This is why the five loss categories matter before anything is bought: they tell a family which of the two they are dealing with, and therefore whether the remaining weeks are enough.

intro.heading: The question underneath the search is about weeks, not kilometres
paragraphs: Almost nobody searching this phrase actually cares where the tutor sits. What they want to know is whether there is still time, how many weeks of help a particular problem needs, and whether the money would be better spent now or in January. Those are answerable questions, and the answers depend on the point in the two-year course rather than on the point on the map. So this page is organised by calendar rather than by catchment.

The IGCSE is a two-year course and families treat it as a one-year course, which is where most of the wasted money in this market goes. Year 10 is where content can be learned with room to breathe, where a weak foundation from Year 9 can still be rebuilt properly, and where the school forms the judgement that sets the tier your child will be entered on. Year 11 is where that judgement gets tested. By the spring of Year 11 the available moves have narrowed to paper technique, and technique is a smaller lever than content.

The second thing worth knowing is that different problems take wildly different lengths of time. One topic that was never taught is two or three sessions. Arithmetic that collapses under time pressure is six to eight weeks, because it needs short frequent practice rather than long lessons. A whole specification still unmarked in November is a two-term project and no honest tutor will tell you otherwise. A parent who knows which of those they are buying can budget. A parent who does not buys weekly hours indefinitely and hopes.

The third is that the price of the same hour moves across the year. September and October are the quietest booking weeks in Dubai and the specialist bands sit at the bottom of their published range. February and March are peak, evening slots are scarce, and April brings examiner-led rates quoted at the top of the market for work that content time has already made harder. The cheap months and the useful months are the same months, which is a pleasant coincidence and the single most actionable thing on this page.

On delivery, the honest position: IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai. Sending tutors to houses is a service we operate only in India. Teaching for families in Arabian Ranches is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing for past papers, mark schemes and working. For a plan measured in weeks that turns out to matter more than it sounds, because the plan only works if the sessions actually happen, and out here a session that depends on a drive along Al Qudra Road at five o'clock is a session that sometimes does not.
