programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: A two-year course examined in a June and a November series in the UAE, with entry deadlines falling a full term or more before each sitting. Most subjects run Core and Extended routes, entered by the school on the strength of Year 10 work. The syllabus code on the entry, 0580 or 0625 for example, fixes exactly which papers are sat and which practical arrangement applies.
programmes.countryNote: The dominant route in the British-curriculum schools serving Arabian Ranches. Because the tier judgement is formed from Year 10 performance, the most consequential tutoring in this qualification happens a full year before the papers, which is precisely when almost nobody buys it and when it costs the least.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Examined in May or June and again in November, with a modular structure available in some subjects. Foundation and Higher routes carry different grade ceilings. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which shows how long a late entry takes to produce a usable grade.
programmes.countryNote: Used by a minority of Dubai schools and sometimes alongside Cambridge in the same school for different subjects. For a family in Arabian Ranches the practical consequence is that two of your child's subjects may sit on different timetables and different practical arrangements, so the plan has to be built per code rather than per child.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level
programmes.description: Examined in the same June and November series as Cambridge IGCSE and assessed by written papers, with fewer practical and coursework options in several subjects. Some schools enter candidates for O Level in particular subjects where it suits the cohort better. The content overlaps substantially with IGCSE but the papers and the practical arrangements are not interchangeable.
programmes.countryNote: Less common in the Dubai schools serving this belt than Cambridge IGCSE, but common enough that it is worth confirming rather than assuming. If a tutor plans from an IGCSE past paper for a subject entered at O Level, the practical component and some of the question styles will be wrong, and nobody will notice until a mock.

programmes.name: A Level, where the grades are heading
programmes.description: Two years of three or four subjects, examined externally. Entry depends on the IGCSE grade in the same subject, usually set school by school and published as a subject-specific condition rather than a single threshold. Further Mathematics in particular tends to carry a high Mathematics condition, which makes one June grade unexpectedly decisive.
programmes.countryNote: Most British-curriculum schools near Arabian Ranches continue to A Level, and their published entry conditions are the real deadline behind this whole page. Read them in Year 10, not in Year 11, because a condition read early is a target and a condition read late is a disappointment with paperwork attached.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ran.subjectsIntro: Lead time varies by subject as much as by problem, mostly because some subjects reward short frequent practice and others need long marked pieces. The notes below give each subject with its codes and with the honest answer to the question this page is about: how long before a grade moves.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The fastest-moving subject on a short timescale, because most of the lost marks are technique. Algebraic manipulation and multi-step problems respond to six to eight weeks of short frequent practice. Calculator rules differ between the two boards and have been revised recently, so confirm on the awarding body's own page which of your child's papers allows one; families routinely discover it three weeks before the series.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading response, plus a speaking endorsement assessed by the centre. Marks move with structure and with answering the actual question, both of which need marked drafts rather than lessons. Budget four to six weeks and expect the student to write between sessions; nothing else works in this subject.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Set texts and extract analysis, with coursework options in some routes. The texts are chosen by the school, so a tutor must be working on the right ones from the first session. Essay structure improves in four weeks; genuine textual knowledge takes a term, which is why Year 10 is the right time.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism carry the largest share of lost marks, and units and significant figures carry the cheapest. The cheap marks come back in two or three weeks. Rebuilding electricity properly takes six. The practical arrangement depends on the entry and should be confirmed before any plan is written.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and electrolysis are the slow repairs, taking five or six weeks because they are conceptual rather than procedural. The alternative-to-practical paper is the fast one: precise experimental writing is teachable in a handful of sessions and is worth more marks than most students expect.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy, which makes it look like a long project and it usually is not. Most of the gap is command terms and precision, and four to six weeks of marked practice moves it. Diagram and data questions are the quickest wins available in any science at this level.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Application rather than knowledge is the problem in nearly every case: a student describes the concept where the question wants it applied to the case material. That is an examination-technique fix of four to six weeks, and it is one of the few places where late intervention genuinely works.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Theory papers plus programming. The theory responds quickly to structured practice; the programming does not, because fluency comes from writing code weekly over months. Start in Year 10 if the programming is the weakness, and do not expect eight weeks to produce a confident programmer.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Case-study detail and command terms carry the marks, and fieldwork or source papers have their own technique. Technique moves in four to six weeks. Case-study knowledge is memory work the student has to do, so the honest lead time depends almost entirely on what happens between sessions.

subjects.name: French, Spanish and other modern languages
subjects.description: Reading, listening, writing and a centre-assessed oral. Writing and the oral improve fastest because both are formulaic once the structures are drilled. Listening is the slow one and needs daily exposure rather than weekly lessons, which makes it a Year 10 project rather than a Year 11 rescue.

sections.heading: Where your child sits in the two-year cycle, and what that means tonight
paragraphs: The first useful thing to establish is not the subject but the year group, because Year 10 and Year 11 are different purchases with different prices and different ceilings. In Year 10 the school is still forming its judgement about which tier to enter your child on, content is still being delivered for the first time, and there is room to go back to Year 9 material without losing ground. Anything bought in Year 10 is an investment in capability.

In Year 11 the available levers shrink month by month. Content can still be taught in the autumn. By January it is being revised rather than taught. By March the honest work is paper technique, and by April it is pacing, command terms and not losing marks you already know how to win. None of that is useless, but it is a narrower kind of help, and the rate for it is higher because everyone wants it at once. A parent deciding in Year 10 is choosing from a wide menu at a low price. A parent deciding in April is choosing from a short menu at the top of the market.

There is a third position worth naming, which is the summer between the two years. A student who finishes Year 10 with a real content gap has eight quiet weeks in which that gap can be taught properly, while the Dubai market is empty and the teachers who are impossible to book in February are available. Families in Arabian Ranches are frequently travelling then, and an online slot follows the family with the time converted. Almost nobody uses that window, which is why it is the best value in the two years.

sections.heading: What each term of the course is actually for
paragraphs: Set the two years out as a grid and the decisions become obvious. Each cell has a natural job, and work done in the wrong cell either costs more or achieves less. The grid below is written for a Dubai three-term school year on the September start, which is what the British-curriculum schools serving this belt run, with the long break across July and August and the shorter breaks in winter and spring.

Two cells deserve particular attention. The spring break in Year 11 is the last long stretch of usable revision time before the series, and it is the right moment for full timed papers rather than for topic revision, because a full paper is the only thing that tests pacing. And the winter break in Year 10 is the cheapest moment in the whole two years to fix a weak foundation, since nothing is urgent, the market is quiet and there is still a year and a half in which the fix can compound.

The grid also exposes the commonest error, which is buying heavily in term three of Year 11 and nothing before it. By then the content is fixed, the tier is fixed, the forecast grade has been submitted, and the only remaining variable is how well the student executes what they already know. That is worth buying. It is simply worth far less than the same money would have bought in the autumn, and it is the single most expensive way to arrive at a June grade.

sections.heading: How long an IGCSE fix actually takes
paragraphs: Ask a provider how many sessions a subject needs and the answer will be a number. Ask how many sessions a problem needs and the answer becomes useful, because the honest range runs from two sessions to two terms depending entirely on what is wrong. Nobody can give that answer without seeing a marked script, which is why the first thing we ask for is work rather than a description of the difficulty.

The pattern across the table is that procedural problems move fast and conceptual ones move slowly. A topic that was never taught is a gap, and gaps close quickly once somebody fills them. Arithmetic that fails under time pressure is a habit, and habits need short frequent practice over weeks rather than long sessions. Moles in Chemistry and listening in a modern language are conceptual, and they need months because the student has to build something rather than learn something.

The last column is the one families skip and it decides everything. Every row depends on work the student does between sessions. Six weeks of weekly lessons with no practice in between produces roughly two weeks of progress, and there is no tutor in Dubai at any rate who can get round that. A plan that specifies what happens between sessions, in hours, is a plan. A plan that specifies only the sessions is a standing order. The same arithmetic explains why two sessions a week rarely doubles progress for a Year 11 student in this community: the hours exist, but the practice time between them does not, and the practice is where the learning settles.

sections.heading: The components that are not sat in the examination hall
paragraphs: A surprising amount of an IGCSE profile is settled outside the examination hall, on the school's own schedule, and those components have deadlines rather than exam dates. Families planning a tutoring block around the June series routinely miss them, then discover in March that a speaking assessment was recorded in January or that a coursework route closed in November. The dates belong to the centre, which means the exams officer is the only reliable source for them.

What tutoring can do with these components is narrower than with written papers, and the boundary matters. Format practice is legitimate and useful: rehearsing the shape of a speaking task, drilling the experimental writing that an alternative-to-practical paper rewards, teaching how a fieldwork write-up is structured. Producing any part of the submitted work is not legitimate, and for coursework routes it is a malpractice question rather than a style question. Feedback belongs on the student's own draft, as comments, never as edits inside the file.

The practical move is to ask the school for a list, in writing, of every component that is assessed internally or recorded by the centre, with its date. Then build the tutoring plan around those dates as well as around the written papers. For a student taking nine subjects there may be four or five such components, scattered from November to April, and each of them is a piece of the final grade that can be prepared for in advance rather than survived.

sections.heading: Mandatory UAE subjects alongside an IGCSE timetable
paragraphs: Any honest conversation about how many tutoring hours a week a Dubai student can absorb has to count the whole timetable, and the whole timetable includes subjects that families outside the UAE never have to think about. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year.

The organisational rules are specific. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; and for non-Arabs the school's licensed-curriculum language applies in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic must have appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential a parent can reasonably ask about.

Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes. Add that to nine IGCSE subjects and a Year 11 week is fuller than a quick count of examined subjects suggests. It is also worth knowing that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five accredited subjects required for Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, where the requirement is five subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus an Advanced Level condition. One page ranking for queries like this states six subjects; the sourced figure is five.

sections.heading: When an IGCSE hour is cheap in Dubai, and when it is dear
paragraphs: Rates in this market move with demand across the year, and the movement is large enough to plan around. September and October are the quietest booking weeks: enquiries are low, specialists have empty evenings, and a qualified subject tutor sits at the bottom of the published band, which Unitors puts at AED 150 for IGCSE. By February and March the same person is at the top of the specialist band that Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table gives as AED 200 to 450 and above, and the good evening slots are gone. In April, examiner-led rates get quoted; BartyED publishes AED 650 an hour.

The homework-help tier moves least, because it is not capacity-constrained in the same way: EdFlik lists online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 throughout. In-home visits move most, because a travelling tutor has fewer slots to sell and sells them to whoever is most desperate; Bestimate quotes AED 180 to 350 with travel included and independent providers advertise up to AED 500, with monthly packages at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions.

Put the two halves of this page together and they point the same way. The cheap months are September, October and the summer. The useful months, where content can still be taught rather than revised, are September, October and the summer. There is no trade-off to manage: the correct time to buy is the time it costs least. Every figure here belongs to the provider named, on the date its own page carried that rate, and none of it is an IB Gram price list. Our first lesson is free so that the teaching can be judged before any money moves at all.

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor your child, and how a parent checks
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and permitted, and it runs on a permit rather than on trust. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the smart app, the website or the e-services system. Because it costs nothing, holding one is a question of diligence rather than of money.

Eligibility is broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and because no schedule of amounts is published, a specific figure circulating online should be treated as unverified. An operation with premises and staff is a different legal category and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained through initial approval and renewed annually.

Two questions cover most of what a parent needs. Can I see the permit, in your own name, with its expiry? And do you teach at my child's school? The second matters because the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules say the same for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff. A third question is worth adding where lessons are delivered over video from outside the UAE: ask where the teacher is based and what time zone they work in, because that should be disclosed rather than discovered.

sections.heading: Booking from Arabian Ranches, and the honest limits
paragraphs: The sequence is short and it starts with paperwork rather than with a conversation. Ask the school's exams officer for the syllabus code, the tier and the administrative zone for each subject, and for a list of internally assessed components with their dates. Then send us the subject, the code, the year group, the last marked piece of work and the evening window that genuinely exists after the bus arrives. That is enough to say who is free and how many weeks the fix should take.

The trial lesson is free and the condition is stated: one session, before any payment, with no card details taken beforehand and written feedback afterwards. It runs as a working lesson on a real topic, because the only test that matters is whether your child can do something at the end of the hour that they could not do at the start. If the match is wrong we change the teacher rather than asking you to persist with it for a term.

Where we cannot help, we say so. Mathematics and the sciences fill first in the evening slots, and November, December and January are the busiest booking weeks of the Dubai year for the reasons set out above. If no specialist is free for your subject and slot, the options are a different evening, a short wait, or a teacher whose subject depth we describe accurately before you decide. Nobody here promises a grade in any subject, and nobody will produce coursework, a draft or any part of an assessed submission. Both of those limits are the point rather than the small print.

process.title: Get the code, the tier and the internal dates
process.description: Ask the exams officer for the syllabus code, the tier and the administrative zone for each subject, plus a written list of internally assessed components and their dates. Those five facts shape the plan more than any conversation about tutoring will, and the school can produce them in a day.

process.title: Say the year group, then the problem
process.description: Year 10 and Year 11 are different purchases with different ceilings and different prices. Naming the year group first means the advice you get is honest about what is still possible, rather than a quotation that would have been identical whichever year your child was in.

process.title: Send a marked script, not a description
process.description: Lead times depend on what kind of problem it is, and only a marked script shows that. Two or three sessions for an untaught topic, six to eight weeks for arithmetic under pressure, two terms for a specification still largely unmarked. Nobody can tell those apart without seeing the work.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson before paying anything
process.description: One lesson at no charge, booked before payment and with no card details taken beforehand. Written feedback follows. The test is whether your child can do something new by the end of the hour, which is a harder and more useful standard than whether the session felt pleasant.

process.title: Agree what happens between sessions
process.description: Every lead time on this page assumes work between lessons, and the plan should say how much, in hours, per week. Six weeks of lessons without practice produces about two weeks of progress. Writing the homework into the plan is the cheapest thing anyone can do to make the rest of it work.

whyPoints.title: Lead times published by problem, not by subject
whyPoints.description: Two or three sessions for an untaught topic, four to six weeks for command terms, two terms for a specification still unmarked. Publishing the slow answers alongside the fast ones is the only way the numbers mean anything, and it is why the first thing we ask for is a marked script.

whyPoints.title: The cheap months and the useful months are the same
whyPoints.description: Specialist rates in Dubai sit at the bottom of their published range in September, October and the summer, which are also the months in which content can still be taught rather than revised. That coincidence is the most actionable thing on this page and nobody else in this search result mentions it.

whyPoints.title: The internal components are counted
whyPoints.description: Speaking endorsements, practical arrangements, oral components and coursework routes are assessed on the school's schedule, not the awarding body's. A plan built only around the June papers misses them. We ask for the list of internal dates before anything is scheduled.

whyPoints.title: The whole timetable is counted too
whyPoints.description: Mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies occupy real weekly hours, calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, in separate classes by group. A plan that pretends a Year 11 week has five free evenings fails in week three, and no competitor page researched for this project mentions these subjects at all.

whyPoints.title: Clear about delivery, limits and claims
whyPoints.description: Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service we operate only in India. No part of coursework or any assessed submission is produced for a student. No grade is promised in any subject. Each of those is stated here rather than implied.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tutor near me in Arabian Ranches, or are lessons online?
faqs.answer: Lessons are online. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending tutors to houses is a service we operate in India only. Teaching here is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing for past papers, mark schemes and working. On a plan measured in weeks that matters practically rather than philosophically: the plan only delivers if the sessions happen, and a 17:30 session that depends on a drive along Al Qudra Road at the worst hour of the day is a session that sometimes does not.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 10. Is it too early to start IGCSE support?
faqs.answer: It is the best time, and almost nobody uses it. In Year 10 the school is still forming the judgement that decides which tier your child is entered on, content is being delivered for the first time, and Year 9 foundations can still be rebuilt without losing ground. The market is also quieter, so specialist rates sit at the bottom of their published range. Everything bought in Year 10 is an investment in capability. Everything bought in April of Year 11 is paper technique at peak prices, which is worth less for more money.

faqs.question: How many weeks does it take to fix one weak IGCSE topic?
faqs.answer: A single topic that was genuinely never taught is usually two or three sessions, and the evidence is a marked past-paper question on that topic scoring well. The slower repairs are habits rather than gaps: arithmetic that collapses under time pressure takes six to eight weeks of short frequent practice, misread command terms four to six weeks of marked rewriting, and a specification still largely unmarked is a two-term project. Every one of those assumes about an hour of the student's own practice a week between sessions.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE components are not sat in the examination hall?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect. Speaking endorsements in English and oral components in modern languages are conducted and recorded by the centre on its own schedule. Science practical arrangements vary by entry between a practical paper and a written alternative. Some English Literature and humanities routes offer coursework marked by the centre and moderated by the board. Art and Design is portfolio-based. Forecast grades are submitted by the school from its own evidence. Ask the exams officer for a written list of all of them with dates, and plan around those as well as the papers.

faqs.question: How is the speaking endorsement in IGCSE English assessed?
faqs.answer: It is conducted and recorded by your child's school as the examination centre, on a schedule the centre sets rather than one published with the written timetable, and the recordings go to the awarding body. What that means practically is that it can be over before a family has thought about it. Tutoring can rehearse the task format, the timing and the kind of development the task rewards, all of which is legitimate preparation. The assessment itself belongs to the school, and nobody outside it has any role in the recording or the mark.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE tutoring rates in Dubai rise closer to the June series?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the movement is large enough to plan around. A qualified subject tutor whom Unitors publishes from AED 150 an hour in the quiet months sits at the top of the specialist band Bestimate gives as AED 200 to 450 and above by February and March, when evening slots are scarce. In April examiner-led rates get quoted; BartyED publishes AED 650 an hour. The homework-help tier moves least, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 throughout. In-home rates move most, because travelling tutors have the fewest slots to sell.

faqs.question: Which months are the cheapest to book IGCSE tuition in Dubai?
faqs.answer: September, October and the summer between Year 10 and Year 11. Enquiries are low, specialists have empty evenings, and published specialist rates sit at the bottom of their range. The useful coincidence is that those are also the months in which content can still be taught rather than revised, so there is no trade-off between the cheap time and the effective time. The dearest months are February, March and April, when demand peaks, the good slots are gone and the only remaining work is examination technique.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education have to be studied alongside IGCSE in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required its arrangements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, with at least twenty-five minutes advised for any mandatory subject lesson. For a Year 11 family the practical consequence is that the week is fuller than a count of examined subjects suggests, which is worth knowing before adding three tutoring sessions to it.

faqs.question: Why must Arabic and Islamic Education classes be taught separately for Arab and non-Arab students?
faqs.answer: Because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ between the two groups. KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, while non-Arabs are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Teachers of these subjects need appropriate KHDA approval to teach them.

faqs.question: How much weekly timetable time do the mandatory UAE subjects take?
faqs.answer: KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, and schools may vary the length of a lesson provided the total weekly time is met, with at least twenty-five minutes advised for any single mandatory subject lesson. The exact weekly total depends on the subject and the year group, so your child's school is the place to get the figure. The reason to ask is budgeting: once those hours are counted alongside nine IGCSE subjects, the number of tutoring sessions a Year 11 week can actually absorb is usually two.

faqs.question: Does the UAE count all nine of my child's IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: No. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. There is also an Advanced Level condition: proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One page ranking for queries like this states that six subjects are required; the sourced figure is five. Verify on moe.gov.ae before relying on either.

faqs.question: Can two children in one villa share an IGCSE session?
faqs.answer: Only where they are in the same year sitting the same specification at the same tier, which is rare outside twins. Otherwise an hour split between a Year 10 student meeting a topic for the first time and a Year 11 student drilling paper technique gives neither of them a proper lesson. Consecutive one-to-one slots on the same evening work better: the house is disturbed once and each lesson stays specific. Where the overlap is genuine we will say so rather than selling two hours that could have been one.

faqs.question: What evening slot works for a Year 11 student in Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: Buses into the community arrive between about 15:45 and 16:15, and a student needs to eat, so 17:00 is the earliest realistic start and 17:30 is more reliable. Further out, in Arabian Ranches 3, DAMAC Hills or Remraam, arrivals are later and 18:00 or 19:30 works better. The practical point is to pick the slot that is comfortably late rather than ambitiously early, because the slot that is always slightly too soon is the slot that gets cancelled, and a cancelled session breaks a plan measured in weeks.

faqs.question: Should my child drop an IGCSE subject to protect the others?
faqs.answer: It is a conversation for the school rather than for a tutor, and it needs to happen before entries close rather than after. The relevant facts are that Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track counts five subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, and that A Level entry conditions are usually subject-specific. So the question is not how many subjects but which ones. Bring the current grades and the published sixth-form conditions to the meeting, and ask the school what dropping one actually frees up in timetable hours.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a permit to teach my child over video from abroad?
faqs.answer: The UAE permit regime applies to people providing private tutoring in the UAE, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 is the route for them. Where a teacher is based outside the country the position is different, and the honest thing a provider can do is tell you where the teacher is and what time zone they work in rather than leave you to assume. Ask that question directly. Two ranking competitors route UAE parents to numbers in other countries without disclosing where the teaching comes from.

faqs.question: What happens if no IGCSE tutor is free in our evening window?
faqs.answer: You get told, with the real options. Mathematics and the sciences fill first in the evening slots, and November, December and January are the busiest booking weeks of the Dubai year. The alternatives are a different evening, a short wait for a slot to open, or a teacher whose subject depth we describe accurately before you decide. intro.heading: What you are really buying when you search for a tutor nearby
paragraphs: A search for an IGCSE tutor near me in Arabian Ranches 2 is a search about distance, but the invoice that follows is about something else entirely. Distance decides who is willing to turn up. It does not decide who has marked a Cambridge 0620 paper, who knows that Extended tier Chemistry candidates sit Paper 2 and Paper 4 rather than Paper 1 and Paper 3, or who can tell the difference between a student who cannot do stoichiometry and a student who runs out of time. Those are the things that move a grade, and none of them correlate with how long it takes to reach Reem on a Tuesday evening.

Arabian Ranches 2 is a villa community off Sheikh Zayed Bin Hamdan Al Nahyan Street, built in clusters named Casa, Rosa, Palma, Lila, Camelia, Azalea, Reem, Yasmin and Rasha. There is no secondary school inside the gates. Children are bussed or driven out to Arabian Ranches, Motor City, Dubai Sports City, Nad Al Sheba, Al Barsha South and the Sustainable City. That geography is the whole of the pricing problem: a tutor who is genuinely near you has a small pool of syllabuses they have taught, and a tutor who has taught yours is rarely near you.

The Dubai tutoring market resolves that tension by charging for travel. Published in-home rates run from around AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table putting the ordinary in-home band at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. The same rate table puts qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300. The gap between those two bands is not a quality gap. It is fuel, parking and forty minutes of someone's evening, billed to you at their hourly rate.

So this page is written as a budget rather than a brochure. It shows the published bands from the cheapest tier upwards, what each tier can realistically do for a Year 10 or Year 11 student, and the four spending patterns that waste the most money in this community specifically. It also covers the costs nobody budgets for: exam entry as a private candidate, a November resit, and the hours lost paying a generalist to work out which paper your child is actually sitting.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE support to Arabian Ranches 2 as one-to-one online lessons over live video. We do not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we offer only in India. What a family here gets instead is a tutor chosen from the whole pool rather than the twenty-minute-drive pool, which matters most for the subjects this neighbourhood struggles to staff locally: Additional Mathematics 0606, Edexcel Further Pure, and the Extended-tier sciences in the final two terms before a June series.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ran.programmesIntro: Arabian Ranches 2 children sit IGCSE under two boards, usually chosen by the school rather than the family. The entry code on the exam slip decides the papers, the tiering and the calculator rules, so it is the first thing a tutor should ask for.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The dominant IGCSE board in Dubai's British-curriculum schools. Subjects are tiered: Core candidates take an easier paper pair with a capped grade ceiling, Extended candidates take the harder pair for the full range. Syllabus codes matter because the 2025-27 Mathematics specification 0580 introduced a non-calculator paper that older teaching materials ignore entirely.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, and those are the only two sittings open to a candidate in the UAE, because the February and March series is offered in India only. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and must use the timetable for its own zone; Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask the school's exams officer which zone your centre sits in.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Tiered as Foundation and Higher rather than Core and Extended, graded 9 to 1, and calculator-permitted in both Mathematics A papers. Mathematics Specification A, code 4MA1, sets two two-hour papers of 100 marks each at both tiers. Foundation tier reports grades 5 to 1; Higher tier reports 9 to 4 with a 3 allowed.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson offers International GCSE in a May/June and a November series each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Provisional timetables are published ahead of each series, so check the live PDF rather than a cached date.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary and Year 9 options
programmes.description: The two years before IGCSE decide which tier a child is entered for, and tier decides the grade ceiling. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October. A Year 9 who is borderline on algebra is a Year 10 who gets entered for Core, and a Core entry in Cambridge Mathematics 0580 cannot be awarded above a C.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest point in the whole sequence to buy help, and the stage Arabian Ranches 2 families most often skip. Ten hours in Year 9 costs a fraction of the thirty hours a Year 11 Extended catch-up takes, and it is the difference between a capped entry and an uncapped one.

programmes.name: What IGCSE grades are being spent on
programmes.description: IGCSE results buy a sixth-form place and a subject combination. A Level and IB Diploma entry requirements inside Dubai are published per school and typically sit at grade 6 or B in the subject to be continued, higher for Mathematics and the sciences. That is the real return on the tutoring spend.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E, or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ran.subjectsIntro: Not every IGCSE subject repays tutoring at the same rate. The list below is ordered by how reliably paid hours convert into marks for a student who is already attending lessons and doing the homework, which is the only honest way to rank spend.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: The highest-yield spend at IGCSE, because the marks are procedural and diagnosable. Extended candidates sit Paper 2, two hours without a calculator, and Paper 4, two hours with one, each 100 marks and each half the grade. The non-calculator paper is where surds, standard form and fraction arithmetic quietly cost a grade.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Both papers permit a calculator, which changes revision completely. Higher tier reports 9 to 4 with an allowed 3, so a student sitting at the tier boundary is deciding between a safe 5 at Foundation and a risky 4 at Higher. That decision is worth an hour of a tutor's time on its own.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for Mathematics at A Level or Analysis and Approaches HL. Calculus and trigonometric identities arrive early and the pace assumes fluency that most Year 11 students do not yet have. The hardest subject in this list to staff locally, and the clearest case for widening the tutor pool.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Extended candidates sit Paper 2 for multiple choice, 45 minutes and 40 marks, Paper 4 for theory, 1 hour 15 and 80 marks, and either Paper 5 practical or Paper 6 alternative to practical for the final 20 percent. Moles and electrolysis absorb the hours; the practical paper absorbs the marks nobody revised for.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Same paper architecture as Chemistry. The losses cluster in electricity, where circuit reasoning fails, and in the required equations, where recall is shaky. Physics rewards drilling more than reading, which makes it good value per paid hour if the tutor sets timed questions rather than lectures.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Content-heavy and deceptively cheap to tutor badly. A session spent re-reading the textbook does nothing; a session spent on command-term discipline and on the eight-mark extended responses does. Students lose most on describe-versus-explain confusion and on data questions in Paper 6.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: One entry, two grades, three sciences taught at reduced depth. Theory sits in Paper 3 or Paper 4 at two hours and 120 marks. Families often buy three single-subject tutors for a double-award child, which is the single most expensive mistake in this list.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 and 0510)
subjects.description: First Language English 0500 is assessed on directed writing and composition; English as a Second Language 0510 and 0511 differ in whether the speaking test is counted. Marks move with structure and timing drills, not vocabulary lists. A tutor should be marking against the published descriptors, not giving impressions.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (0455 and 0450)
subjects.description: Both reward answer architecture: definition, application to the named context, analysis, then evaluation that actually chooses. Students who know the content and write without a structure lose a band. This is correctable in six to eight sessions, which makes it one of the better value subjects to buy late.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside the licensed curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited. These lessons occupy real timetable space in Year 11.

sections.heading: What a search for an IGCSE tutor near me actually returns in this community
paragraphs: The literal answer: for most Extended-tier subjects, a search for an IGCSE tutor near me in Arabian Ranches 2 returns agencies that serve the whole of Dubai and will drive a tutor to you for a travel-loaded hourly rate, plus a handful of independent tutors who happen to live in Dubailand. The agencies rarely publish a price. Of the competitor pages measured for this project in October 2026, three of six published no hourly figure at all, and the two that did quoted US dollars rather than dirhams.

That matters because the first conversation then becomes a quotation exercise rather than a teaching one. A parent who does not know the market band cannot tell whether AED 350 an hour is a specialist rate or a travel surcharge. The single most useful thing you can do before making contact is read the published bands in the next section, so the question changes from how much do you charge to what does that rate include.

The second thing the search returns is a mismatch between what you asked for and what you need. Proximity is a reasonable filter for a Year 7 who needs homework supervision. It is a poor filter for a Year 11 sitting Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, because the number of people in the Dubailand villa belt who have taught that syllabus to exam is small, and the ones who have are already booked by the schools that teach it.

Our position is deliberately narrow. IB Gram matches Arabian Ranches 2 families to one-to-one tutors who teach over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits in the UAE at all. The trade is explicit: you give up a person in the room, and in return the pool you choose from is national rather than a twenty-minute radius, and the rate you pay carries no travel in it.
bullets: Ask for the syllabus code the tutor has taught, not the subject name
Ask whether the quoted rate is per hour or per lesson, and whether it includes travel
Ask how many marked scripts the tutor has worked through for that board

sections.heading: The Dubai rate card, cheapest tier first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom rather than the top, because the cheapest tier is where most families start and where most of the wasted money sits. University-student and general online tutors in Dubai advertise from the mid-forties upward: EdFlik publishes from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For a Year 8 who needs someone to sit with them while they finish a worksheet, that tier is appropriate and the money is well spent.

One step up, qualified subject tutors working online are published at AED 150 to 300 an hour. Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. This is the band where a tutor has actually taught the syllabus and can mark against the descriptors, and it is the band most Year 10 and Year 11 work should sit in. Above it, IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase publishing AED 270; premium named or examiner-track tutors run to AED 500 to 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650.

The in-home band sits across the middle of that ladder at AED 180 to 500 an hour, which is the figure that confuses people. An in-home tutor at AED 300 is not a better teacher than an online tutor at AED 300. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts ordinary in-home visits at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500, and the difference against the online band is travel time priced into the hour. For a family in Camelia or Azalea, at the back of the community, that premium is the largest it gets anywhere in Dubailand.

Monthly packages are quoted too, and they are the easier number to budget against. Published packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Every figure in this section is the market's, with the publisher named; none of them is an IB Gram price list.

sections.heading: Four ways money leaks out of a tutoring budget here
paragraphs: The first leak is paying a travel premium you did not need. A family in Reem books an in-home tutor at AED 320 an hour because the search said near me, when the same qualified teaching is published online at AED 150 to 300. Over a thirty-week Year 11, one hour a week, that difference is a four-figure sum spent on a car journey. If a person in the room genuinely changes your child's behaviour, pay it knowingly. If it was simply what the search returned, it is a leak.

The second leak is buying a generalist for a specific paper. A maths graduate who has never seen Cambridge 0580 will teach the content competently and then prepare your child for the wrong paper pair. Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3; Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4. A tutor who drills calculator methods for a non-calculator Paper 2 has spent your hours making your child slower. Always buy by syllabus code.

The third leak is three tutors for a double-award child. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is one entry producing two grades, taught at reduced depth across biology, chemistry and physics. Families routinely hire three single-subject specialists for it, tripling the bill to cover content their child is not examined on. One tutor who has taught 0654 and knows which sub-topics are excluded costs a third as much and prepares the right paper.

The fourth leak is starting too late and buying intensity instead of time. Six weeks out, at two or three sessions a week in the specialist band, the monthly spend reaches Bestimate's AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. Twenty weeks out, one weekly hour in the mid band covers the same ground for less and leaves room for the content to settle. The cheapest grade is almost always the one bought early in Year 10 or, better, in Year 9 before the tier entry is decided.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE subjects repay the hours, and which do not
paragraphs: Tutoring is not equally efficient across subjects, and a budget should follow the efficiency. Mathematics is the strongest case: the losses are procedural, they repeat, and they can be diagnosed from one marked paper. A student who drops marks on surds, index laws and standard form on Cambridge Paper 2 will drop them again next time until someone sits with them and fixes the arithmetic. Eight to twelve hours of focused work moves a grade boundary more reliably here than anywhere else on the timetable.

The sciences are next, but only if the tutor works on the practical component. Paper 5 and Paper 6 carry twenty percent of the grade in Cambridge Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, and they are the papers students revise last and lose most on. Planning an investigation, identifying a variable that was not controlled and reading a results table are learnable skills, and almost nobody practises them at home.

Content-heavy humanities repay fewer hours per dirham, because the marks move with writing structure rather than with knowledge, and structure can be taught in a handful of sessions. Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450 are the clearest example: a student who already knows the content and writes without definition, application, analysis and a decided evaluation is losing a band for a reason that six sessions can fix permanently.

At the bottom of the efficiency table sit subjects where the student's problem is not the subject. English First Language 0500 marks rarely move for a reader who reads; they move for a student who cannot finish directed writing in time. If the real problem is timing, attention or sleep, more hours of subject teaching is the wrong purchase, and an honest tutor says so in the trial lesson rather than in month four.

sections.heading: A two-year IGCSE budget, from Year 10 to results day
paragraphs: Families almost never plan tutoring as a two-year spend, which is why the money arrives in panicked lumps. Laid out as a budget, the shape of a sensible plan becomes obvious: light and early, heavier in the term before mocks, tapering once papers are being worked independently, and with a reserve left for the costs that are not tutoring at all.

Those other costs are real. Exam entry as a private candidate is charged by the centre, not by the board, and an Arabian Ranches 2 family whose child is entered through school will not see that bill at all. A November resit is a second entry fee plus a short block of teaching, and it is a cost worth budgeting for in advance rather than deciding in August. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27 under the emirate's second economic incentives package, which at least means the fee side of the household education budget is stable while you plan the tutoring side.

The table below sets out an indicative plan at mid-band market rates. It is a planning tool built from published bands, not a quotation, and it assumes one subject at a time rather than three at once. A family running two subjects should double the tutoring rows and reconsider whether both are genuinely weak or whether one of them is a timing problem wearing a subject's clothes.

The single highest-return line in the table is the cheapest one: a short diagnostic block in Year 9 or early Year 10, before the tier entry is submitted. A Core entry in Cambridge Mathematics 0580 cannot be awarded above a grade C, however well the candidate performs. Discovering that in Year 11 costs a resit; discovering it in Year 9 costs four hours.

sections.heading: The deadlines that cost money rather than marks
paragraphs: Most exam-calendar advice is about revision. The expensive deadlines are administrative, and they sit months before the papers. Count a Cambridge June series backwards and the shape is obvious. The papers themselves fall inside the June window printed on your centre's zone timetable, but the entry list that fixes which subjects and which tier a candidate sits closes in the spring, and the forecast grades the centre submits are gathered from mock evidence collected in the term before that. By the time the first paper is handed out, every decision that could have changed the outcome was taken months earlier. The precise entry date belongs to your centre's key dates rather than to anything worth memorising here, and Pearson's published November 2026 International GCSE timetable, running from late October to 19 November 2026, shows the same gap on the other board.

The zone rule costs money too, in a different way. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong zone timetable was used. A family revising to a timetable downloaded from a search result rather than from the school's exams officer is carrying that risk themselves.

Pearson's rhythm is different. International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Results from the June 2026 series reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including the International GCSE November series well before anyone sits it, which is why the only safe reference is the live PDF on the Pearson site rather than any date restated on a page like this one.

Build the tutoring plan backwards from the registration date, not the exam date. If entries for a June series close in the spring, the decision about tier, about which subjects to enter and about whether a November resit is likely all has to be made during the preceding autumn and winter. That is also the point at which a diagnostic block is cheapest and most useful, because it is informing a decision rather than rescuing one.

sections.heading: What a free trial should tell you before any money moves
paragraphs: A trial lesson is a purchasing decision, not a sample. IB Gram offers one free trial lesson per student, booked before any payment is taken and with no card details collected at that stage; that is the condition and there is not a longer version of it. The point of the hour is to find out whether this particular tutor can diagnose this particular child, and a parent can judge that from the outside with three or four checks.

First, did the tutor ask for a marked script? A tutor who starts from the last paper an actual teacher annotated is working from evidence. A tutor who starts from a syllabus checklist is working from a template, and templates are what you are trying not to pay for. Second, did the tutor name the paper? For a Cambridge Extended science candidate the answer should involve Paper 2, Paper 4 and either Paper 5 or Paper 6, with the twenty percent practical weighting mentioned without prompting.

Third, did anything get written down? At the end of a useful trial there should be a short statement of what the problem is, what the first four sessions will cover and what would count as progress by session four. That gives you something to hold the arrangement against in six weeks, which is the point at which most tutoring quietly stops being useful without anybody saying so.

Fourth, what did the tutor decline to promise? Nobody can guarantee a grade, and a tutor who offers one is telling you something about how they sell rather than how they teach. The honest version is a range of plausible outcomes with the conditions attached: this many hours, this much independent practice, this topic fixed first. If the trial produces a number instead of a plan, treat the number sceptically.

sections.heading: Permits, receipts and what a paying parent is entitled to ask
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work, not informal work. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and states a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, and figures circulating online could not be verified against any official source, so no amount appears on this page. What a parent should take from it is simpler: the permit is free and quick, which means a tutor without one has no cost-based excuse, and asking is a reasonable question rather than an awkward one.

There is a second limit worth knowing about in Dubai and a stricter one in Abu Dhabi. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. So the apparently convenient option, your child's own teacher privately, is the one option to rule out. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal again: that requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is not something IB Gram holds or claims.

On receipts and tax, keep the questions concrete. Ask whether the rate quoted is per hour or per lesson, whether it includes anything beyond the lesson itself, and whether a receipt will be issued for each payment. We do not state the VAT treatment of tuition fees as fact, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation; what we will always tell you is whether a quoted figure is inclusive. For anything concerning Ministry of Education equivalency or attestation, the official channel is the authority's own, and no tutor performs or guarantees that process.

sections.heading: When tutoring is the wrong thing to buy
paragraphs: The most useful sentence a tutoring platform can write is the one about not buying. There are situations where paid hours are a poor use of a family's money, and recognising them early saves both the fee and the child's evenings. The clearest is the student whose marks are falling while effort is rising. That pattern is rarely a knowledge gap; it is usually timing, sleep, or a technique problem that shows up as blank final questions and unfinished papers. A diagnostic hour identifies it. Thirty weekly hours of content teaching will not.

The second is the student with five weak subjects and one free evening. Buying five tutors does not produce five improvements; it produces an exhausted child and a bill. Triage is the honest answer: pick the one or two subjects where the grade matters most for the sixth-form place being applied for, fix those properly, and accept a lower outcome elsewhere. A tutor who agrees to all five without saying this is selling, not advising.

The third is the Year 11 who does not want help. Tutoring works on a student who is doing the work and getting it wrong. It does very little for a student who is not doing the work, and the money is better spent on a short, concrete conversation with the school about targets than on a tutor who becomes a weekly argument. A trial lesson will usually show which of the two you are dealing with.

The fourth is the problem that is actually an administrative one. If a child has been entered for Core tier and is working comfortably above it, the fix is an entry change through the school's exams officer, not a term of lessons. If the issue is that nobody knows which board the school enters for, the fix is one email. These are free, and they outperform any amount of paid teaching, which is why they appear on this page before the booking form rather than after it.

process.title: Tell us the code, not just the subject
process.description: Send the syllabus code from the exam entry or the front of the textbook: 0580, 0620, 4MA1, 0654. Codes decide papers, tiers and calculator rules, and matching on a code rather than a subject name is what stops a generalist being prepared for the wrong paper pair.

process.title: Send the last marked script
process.description: A mock paper with a teacher's annotations on it tells us more in two minutes than a description does in twenty. We use it to decide whether the problem is content, technique or timing, and to brief the tutor before the trial so the free hour is spent teaching rather than interviewing.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One free trial lesson per student, booked before any payment and with no card details taken. It runs over live video at a time that works around the Dubailand school run. You end it with a written four-session plan and a definition of what progress by session four would look like.

process.title: Agree the rate and the shape in writing
process.description: Hours per week, length of session, who supplies the papers, and whether the quoted figure is per hour or per lesson. Published market bands are on this page so the conversation starts from the same numbers you have already read rather than from an opening offer.

process.title: Review at session six, honestly
process.description: Six sessions is enough to tell whether the arrangement is working. We look at marks on timed questions rather than at how the lessons felt, change tutor if the match is wrong, and say plainly if the remaining problem is not one a tutor should be paid to solve.

whyPoints.title: Prices on the page, not behind a form
whyPoints.description: Three of the six competitor pages measured for this project in October 2026 published no hourly figure at all, and one FAQ asked the price and then declined to answer it. Every band quoted here carries the name of whoever published it, so you can compare before you talk to anyone.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the hourly rate
whyPoints.description: In-home rates in Dubai are published at AED 180 to 500 because somebody is driving. Online delivery at AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor removes that line from the bill entirely, which matters most from the back clusters of Arabian Ranches 2.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are both IGCSE Mathematics and they set different papers with different calculator rules. We match on the code your child is entered for, which is the difference between useful preparation and plausible-looking preparation.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback on the student's own work. We will not write, complete or produce coursework of any kind, and we say so before anybody asks, because the alternative is an academic-integrity problem that lands on the student rather than on us.

whyPoints.title: Coverage stated rather than implied
whyPoints.description: If no UAE-based specialist is free for your slot and subject, we say so and offer the alternative with the rate attached, instead of filling the slot with whoever is available. Disclosed limits are cheaper for everyone than discovered ones.

whyPoints.title: Sources you can check yourself
whyPoints.description: Regulator facts on this page come from u.ae, web.khda.gov.ae, mohre.gov.ae, cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com. Where a date can be revised, as with Pearson timetables, we point at the live document rather than restating it.

faqs.question: How much should an IGCSE tutor near me in Arabian Ranches 2 actually cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai bands, October 2026: budget online and university-student tutors from roughly AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150; in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 depending on travel; IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. For a Year 10 or Year 11 student the middle band is the sensible default. These are market figures with their publishers named, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home tutor in Arabian Ranches 2 more expensive than an online one?
faqs.answer: Because the hour includes a drive. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts ordinary in-home sessions at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. The difference is travel time priced into the rate, and from the back clusters of Arabian Ranches 2 it is at its largest, because the tutor is driving past Motor City and down Al Qudra Road in evening traffic. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE, so that line never appears on a rate we quote you.

faqs.question: Where do families in this part of Dubailand waste the most tutoring money?
faqs.answer: Four places, in order of size. Paying a travel premium that was not a deliberate choice. Hiring a generalist who prepares the wrong paper pair, which wastes the entire spend rather than part of it. Buying three single-subject tutors for a child entered for Co-ordinated Sciences 0654, which is one entry at reduced depth. And starting six weeks out, where specialist monthly costs reach AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more, instead of twenty weeks out at a quarter of the intensity. The cheapest grade is nearly always the one bought early.

faqs.question: Is a cheap tutor at AED 60 an hour ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the right job. A student in Year 7 or Year 8 who needs company and supervision while homework gets finished is well served by the budget band, and paying specialist rates for that is waste in the other direction. The band stops being appropriate the moment the work becomes board-specific: tier decisions, paper technique, practical papers and timed scripts need somebody who has taught the syllabus. Match the tier of tutor to the tier of problem and the budget looks after itself.

faqs.question: What does it cost to enter my child for IGCSE exams as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: Entry fees are set and collected by the examination centre rather than by Cambridge or Pearson, so there is no single published figure we can honestly quote, and it varies between centres in Dubai. Ask the centre directly for its current private-candidate fee schedule and whether it charges a separate administration fee. If your child is entered through their school, the fee is usually inside the school's own billing and you may never see it as a separate line. Budget for it explicitly if you are planning a November resit.

faqs.question: Which subject should we spend on first if we can only afford one?
faqs.answer: Mathematics, in most cases. The losses are procedural and repeatable, they can be diagnosed from one marked paper, and eight to twelve focused hours move a boundary more reliably than in any other subject. The exception is when a science practical paper is the gap: Paper 5 or Paper 6 carries twenty percent of the grade in Cambridge Biology, Chemistry and Physics and is the component students revise last. Choose on evidence from a marked script, not on which subject feels worst.

faqs.question: Does a Core tier entry limit the grade my child can be awarded?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the most expensive thing most families learn too late. In Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 and cannot be awarded above a grade C; Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 and the range runs A* to E. Pearson tiers differently: Mathematics A Foundation reports grades 5 to 1, Higher reports 9 to 4 with an allowed 3. If your child is working above their entry tier, the fix is an entry change through the school's exams officer, not a term of lessons.

faqs.question: How many sessions should we commit to at the start?
faqs.answer: Four, then review. A block of four lets a tutor diagnose properly, fix one thing and show you evidence on a timed question, which is enough to judge the match. At published mid-band rates four hours is roughly AED 600 to 1,200, which is a reasonable sum to risk on finding out. Open-ended weekly commitments made in week one are how arrangements drift for a term without anyone measuring them. Review at session six against marks, not against how the lessons felt.

faqs.question: Are the Cambridge and Pearson exam timetables the same for a Dubai centre?
faqs.answer: No, and the difference has a cost. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Pearson publishes one timetable per series with provisional versions ahead of time. Get the timetable from your school's exams officer and treat any date restated on a third-party page, including this one, as something to verify.

faqs.question: Can we reduce the bill by sharing a tutor between two children?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and only when the children are genuinely at the same point. Small-group rates are published lower per student than one-to-one, so two siblings in the same subject and tier can work. Two siblings two years apart cannot: the hour splits and each child gets half a lesson at a shared price. For families in Rosa and Lila with several children at different stages, staggered shorter slots usually cost less in total than one long shared session that suits neither child.

faqs.question: What happens to the money if the first tutor is not the right match?
faqs.answer: You change tutor rather than persisting. The free trial exists precisely so that the match question is answered before payment, and if the fit is wrong after the first paid sessions we rematch rather than asking you to make it work. What we will not do is offer a refund tied to a grade outcome, because that is a promise about a result nobody can control. The honest protection is a short initial block, a written plan and a review at session six.

faqs.question: Which work permit lets a teacher in Dubai take paid tutoring work legally?
faqs.answer: It is a fair question to ask and an easy one to answer. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's service page states a two-working-day completion time with no fee. Those offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no official fine schedule is published, so treat quoted amounts with caution.

faqs.question: Can our child be tutored by a teacher from their own school?
faqs.answer: That is the one arrangement to avoid. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the code of conduct attached to the MoHRE private tuition permit also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Beyond the rules, it is a poor arrangement: the person who set the assessment should not be paid to prepare your child for it. Use someone independent of the school instead.

faqs.question: Will tutoring help with the Ministry of Education equivalency our child needs?
faqs.answer: Tutoring helps with the grades; it does not perform the process, and no tutor should imply otherwise. On the British track, students must pass five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Verify current requirements with the Ministry of Education directly, because published summaries change and a competitor page currently states the wrong subject count.

faqs.question: Are IGCSE lessons delivered online as effective for a Year 11 in an exam year?
faqs.answer: For paper technique, which is what an exam year is mostly about, the format barely matters. Timed questions, marked scripts and a shared screen with annotation work well over live video, and recording the session lets a student re-watch a worked method rather than rely on memory. Where online delivery needs more deliberate effort is practical skills for Paper 5 and Paper 6, which require real apparatus discussion and careful walkthroughs of method and variable control. Ask any tutor directly how they handle the practical component before you book.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ran.closingHeading: Start with the numbers, then book the trial
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ran.closingBody: Read the rate bands above before you speak to anyone, so the first conversation is about teaching rather than price discovery. Then send us the syllabus code and the last marked script, and take the free trial lesson: one per student, booked before any payment, with no card details taken. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around a Dubailand school run rather than a drive into it. If the honest answer after the trial is that your child does not need paid hours, we will tell you that instead of selling you a term.
