dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ran.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are listed with the specification they teach rather than the area they live in, because a Pearson 4MA1 entry and a Cambridge 0580 entry need different preparation for the same mathematics. Ask any prospective tutor, here or elsewhere, which code they have actually taught.

intro.heading: Sorting by distance, when distance is the one thing that does not matter
paragraphs: A near me search does something very specific: it ranks results by how close the business is to the phone. For a plumber that is the right sort. For an IGCSE tutor it sorts on the only input with no measurable effect on a grade, and it hides the four inputs that do. Which syllabus code the tutor has taught. Whether they hold the permit the UAE requires. Whether they can teach at the hour your child is actually free. And whether, if the match is wrong in week three, anybody replaces them.

Arabian Ranches 3 makes the point sharply because there is no secondary school inside the gates. Children here are bussed out to the inner Dubailand ring and to campuses further north, which means the family is already absorbing one commute a day. A tutor chosen on proximity adds a second journey to the same evening, or asks the household to absorb it on the tutor's behalf and pay the travel premium that the in-home band in Dubai reflects. Published figures put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. That gap is a car, not a better lesson.

So the plain delivery statement, up front. Nobody is dispatched to a villa here: IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai, and in-home tutoring is something we offer only in India. UAE lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and a recording kept by the family. That is not a workaround for a missing local network. It is the format that lets the match be made on syllabus and level instead of on who lives within a twenty-minute drive of the community gate.

This page is therefore built as a set of comparisons rather than as a sales pitch for one of them. Provider models side by side with the rates their own sites publish. The permit categories, with what a parent can actually ask to see. Cambridge against Pearson for the same subject, by syllabus code. The regulator in each emirate, which matters the moment a family considers a move to Abu Dhabi or Sharjah. And the Ministry of Education's equivalency rule, where at least one page ranking for these queries publishes the wrong subject count.

The conclusion the comparisons reach is worth stating early so the rest can be read against it: for almost every IGCSE need in this community the answer is the same whether you live in Arabian Ranches 3, Mudon, Town Square or Motor City, because the thing being compared is a qualification with the same entry deadline, the same papers and the same mark scheme in all four. What changes between those communities is the drive. What does not change is anything that appears on a results slip.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ran.programmesIntro: An IGCSE comparison is only useful if it is anchored to where a student actually is in the five-year run from Year 7 to a post-16 offer. These four stages are the ones Arabian Ranches 3 families ask about, with the question that matters most at each.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary, before the IGCSE course begins
programmes.description: The years in which a gap becomes a habit. Nothing external is sat, so the only evidence is the school's own assessment and whatever a parent can see in the work at home. Cambridge runs Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which some schools use and many do not. The useful intervention here is diagnostic: establishing whether a comfortable report reflects secure foundations in the two subjects that will matter most at 16.
programmes.countryNote: In the Dubailand belt the Year 9 option choices are made across several campuses with different subject blocks, so two children living on the same street in Arabian Ranches 3 can end up with different subject sets and different boards. That makes the choices worth checking against a post-16 intention rather than against what a friend's child is taking.

programmes.name: The two-year IGCSE course
programmes.description: Two years, one entry deadline and a fixed exam window. The tier is set by the school on the subject teacher's recommendation and submitted with the centre's final entries, which is the single most consequential administrative moment of the course. Content is front-loaded in Year 10 and the hardest material usually lands in Year 11, which is why a student can be comfortable for a year and then meet trouble in a spring mock.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools split between Cambridge and Pearson, sometimes subject by subject inside one campus. For a family comparing tutors, the syllabus code on the entry is more informative than any claim on a tutoring page, and the school's exams officer will supply it. The code also decides which past papers are worth the student's evening.

programmes.name: A second series, after a result
programmes.ageRange: Any point after a first entry
programmes.description: Both boards run two windows a year, so a disappointing grade does not cost a full year. Cambridge runs June and November series; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May or June and in November. A retake is an entry through a school acting as the centre, which means the decision has an administrative deadline rather than being available whenever a family is ready. One session reading the paper breakdown properly is usually worth more than three weeks of general revision.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson's published results dates make the retake calendar concrete for UAE families: June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A summer disappointment can therefore be replaced by a January grade rather than by one the following August, which is often the difference between keeping an offer and renegotiating it.

programmes.name: A Level, the IB Diploma or a vocational route
programmes.description: IGCSE grades are the gate. A Level narrows to three or four subjects; the IB Diploma keeps six with a core; vocational routes assess differently again. Entry requirements are set by the receiving school, and a grade that clears one route can fall short for another, particularly in mathematics and the sciences where the step up is steepest.
programmes.countryNote: From Arabian Ranches 3 both routes are available but at different campuses and different distances, so the post-16 decision carries a commute with it. The inner Dubailand ring mostly runs A Level after IGCSE, while the Diploma campuses sit further out toward Al Barsha South and The Sustainable City.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ran.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is written around the thing worth verifying before you book anybody, local or otherwise. In most cases that is the board and the code, because the content overlaps between Cambridge and Pearson and the question style does not.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Three genuinely different qualifications sit behind this one word. 0580 runs four papers across its tiers, 0607 adds a graphics-calculator component, and 4MA1 sits two papers. Verify which code the entry carries before anyone starts setting past papers, because practising the wrong house style costs real marks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The practical assessment is where the boards diverge most. Cambridge separates a practical route from an alternative-to-practical paper; Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers. Ask which route the school has entered, because it changes what the last three weeks should be spent on.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and organic chemistry decide the grade and are taught late in the course. Qualitative analysis rewards memorised observations, which is the cheapest revision available and the most commonly skipped. Verify whether the entry includes a separate practical component.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume rather than conceptual difficulty, with marks leaving through imprecise terminology and data questions answered by describing the graph instead of explaining the biology. Command-term phrasing differs enough between the boards that answer length has to be retrained when a student switches.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.description: Two award routes covering all three sciences in fewer guided hours than three separate entries. Narrower, not easier, and the papers sample across all three disciplines in one sitting. A student on this route needs breadth-first revision, which is a different plan from the one three separate sciences require.

subjects.name: English Language and English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Three distinct qualifications that are not interchangeable for a sixth-form offer, which families sometimes discover after entries have closed. Check the receiving school's entry requirement against the exact qualification your child is sitting, not against the word English.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Both reward application to the named case rather than textbook recall, and both set answer depth through command terms. Analyse and evaluate carry more marks than explain and are routinely answered at the same depth, which is a habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Two separate subjects that parents often treat as one. Computer Science assesses algorithms, data representation and programming; ICT assesses practical application skills. The tutoring need is entirely different, and so is the post-16 relevance, so the code matters more here than in most subjects.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First and as a Foreign Language
subjects.description: Sat alongside the mandatory Arabic provision every Dubai private school must run, often in a different stream. Marks concentrate in writing. Support means practice inside the school's own scheme of work, because the mandatory-subject content may not be substituted without Ministry permission.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ran.regionsTitle: Arabian Ranches 3 and the communities it is usually compared with
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ran.regionsIntro: Families here compare themselves against the neighbours constantly, usually about schools and traffic. For tutoring the comparison is shorter than expected: the drive differs, the qualification does not. Each note below says what genuinely changes from that community and what does not.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 3
regions.note: No school inside the gates, so the bus timetable rather than the street plan decides when a session can start. What a tutoring plan looks like is set by the campus the child attends, which varies house by house across the phases.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Arabian Ranches 2
regions.note: Older, settled communities on the same school runs, with JESS Arabian Ranches and Ranches Primary School at the centre of most conversations. Earlier handover means more predictable afternoons, and nothing at all about the entry deadline or the papers changes.

regions.name: Mudon
regions.note: Overlapping bus routes and the same inner-ring campuses, so families here ask identical questions about tiers and boards. Households frequently share a tutor with Arabian Ranches 3 neighbours across consecutive evening slots.

regions.name: Town Square
regions.note: A slightly different run toward Al Qudra, which shifts the realistic start time by a quarter of an hour rather than by anything meaningful. The syllabus codes entered from here are the same two boards in the same proportions.

regions.name: Motor City
regions.note: GEMS Metropole is close enough that some students walk or take a very short ride, which makes a 16:30 start genuinely viable. That is the one real difference the comparison turns up, and it is about logistics rather than teaching.

regions.name: Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Victory Heights and the surrounding campuses sit nearby, so afternoon slots work more often than they do from the outer Dubailand phases. The mark scheme, the tier decision and the entry deadline are identical.

They are not better and worse versions of each other; they answer different questions, and the comparison below is meant to be read before a trial rather than after a term.

modes.title: One-to-one online, matched by syllabus code
modes.description: A single student, a single specification, a fixed weekly hour on Gulf Standard Time. The tutor is chosen because they have taught the code on the entry, not because they live nearby. Everything the student writes happens on a shared whiteboard, which is also what makes the method visible to the tutor rather than only the answer.

sections.heading: What a near me search filters for, and the four things it hides
paragraphs: Run the search from inside Arabian Ranches 3 and the results are ordered by distance from the handset. That ordering is doing real work, and none of it is useful. It promotes a classified listing from somebody two communities away over a specialist who has taught the exact paper your child sits, because the specialist is further from the phone. It also promotes whichever provider has spent money on a location page, which is a measure of marketing budget rather than of teaching.

The four things it hides are the four that matter. First, the syllabus code: Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 and Pearson 4MA1 are different qualifications with different papers and different calculator demands, and a tutor who has taught one has not necessarily taught the others. Second, the permit: private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Third, availability at the hour your child is actually free, which in this community is dictated by a bus rather than by a bell. Fourth, what happens in week three if the match is wrong.

Distance does buy one real thing, which is presence in the room, and the market prices it openly. In-home one-to-one with travel included is published at AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. The qualified-tutor band online runs AED 150 to 300 as published, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. For some children, particularly younger ones who will not sit down without an adult beside them, presence is worth the premium. For a Year 11 losing marks on Paper 2 technique, it is not.

The rest of this page replaces the distance sort with comparisons that change outcomes: provider models against their own published rates, the permit categories, the two boards side by side, the regulator in each emirate, and the equivalency rule that determines what these grades are worth to a UAE authority later.

sections.heading: Provider models compared, cheapest first
paragraphs: Every provider in this market compares itself to an unnamed set of other platforms. A comparison is only useful if it compares models rather than brands, and if every rate in it is attributed to whoever published it. So the table below starts at the cheapest band and works up, with the source of each figure named.

The cheapest option is a freelance tutor found through a community group, and the budget online band sits at AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For a Year 7 who needs company and supervision, that is a sensible purchase. What the family takes on in exchange is all the verification: the permit, the syllabus actually taught, and whether the tutor happens to teach at the child's own school, which ADEK's ethics rules bar in Abu Dhabi and which the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also addresses. There is also no replacement if the arrangement ends in March.

A tuition centre with premises is a different legal animal and a different product. A business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That permit is a reasonable thing to ask about. What a centre sells is usually a group class at a set pace, plus a drive at the end of a school day, which from the outer Dubailand phases is the expensive part.

Above those sit agencies, international marketplaces and syllabus-matched online platforms. The honest distinctions are about transparency rather than quality: several agencies publish no rate at all, two of the larger marketplaces quote in US dollars rather than dirhams, and a premium tier advertises examiner experience at AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Where a rate is a claim about marking experience rather than about teaching, the useful question is what evidence of current examiner status can be produced, because that status is not something a family can verify from a website.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is the single question with a documented answer, and almost nobody in this market writes it down. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. The eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page for it is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit, Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

The enforcement position is equally clear and equally often misreported. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published; Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and a figure circulating online could not be verified. Any page quoting you an amount is repeating a rumour, and that is a reasonable signal about the rest of its content.

There is a second rule that catches a common arrangement. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. So the offer that sounds most attractive to a parent, your child's own teacher privately, is the one to decline. It is worth asking in the first conversation rather than the fourth.

A business is different from an individual. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained through initial approval and then a permit and licence process with a maximum of six months to complete, renewed annually with the request made at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific permit issued to premises. It is not something an online matching service holds, and IB Gram does not claim it. Any provider advertising regulator-approved tutors is describing a thing that does not exist in that form.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson for the same subject
paragraphs: Dubai schools are split between the two boards and sometimes use both inside one campus for different subjects. Families generally do not know which their child is entered for, and the comparison is almost never published. It matters because the content overlaps substantially and the assessment does not, so a student who revises from the wrong board's past papers is practising a question style they will not meet.

Mathematics is the clearest case. Cambridge 0580 and Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 are separate syllabuses with separate tiering, and 0607 carries a graphics-calculator component that changes what preparation has to include. Pearson's Mathematics A 4MA1 sits two written papers at the chosen tier rather than four across tiers. A student moved between any two of these mid-course can look mathematically weak when the real problem is unfamiliarity with the paper's shape and the device it expects.

The sciences diverge on practical assessment, which is the part most relevant to a family considering online tuition. Cambridge separates a practical route from an alternative-to-practical paper, so the school's entry decides whether a student sits a laboratory exam or a written paper about laboratory work. Pearson assesses practical skills within the written papers. In both cases the laboratory work itself belongs to the school, and what a tutor contributes is the written and data-handling skill the paper actually marks.

The tiering vocabulary differs too. Cambridge uses Core and Extended, with Core capping the grade at C. Pearson uses Foundation and Higher. Either way the decision belongs to the school on the subject teacher's recommendation and is submitted with the centre's final entries, so it has an administrative deadline rather than being revisable whenever a family notices. English is the quiet trap: Cambridge 0500 English Language, 0510 and 0511 English as a Second Language and Pearson 4EA1 are distinct qualifications, and a sixth-form offer written for one is not automatically satisfied by another.

sections.heading: Arabian Ranches 3 against the communities next door
paragraphs: Families in this belt compare communities constantly, and for schooling the comparison is real: the campuses differ, the bus routes differ and the afternoon traffic differs. For tutoring the comparison collapses almost immediately, because the thing being prepared for is identical in all of them. The same two boards, the same entry deadlines, the same papers, the same mark schemes. A Year 11 in Mudon and a Year 11 in Arabian Ranches 3 at the same campus have the same problem and need the same plan.

What genuinely differs is one variable: how long the child is in a vehicle. From Motor City a student may walk or take a very short ride and be free by a quarter to four. From the outer phases of Arabian Ranches 3, Remraam or DAMAC Hills the bus run is longer and the realistic start drifts toward six. That is a scheduling fact, not an educational one, and it is precisely the variable an online slot removes from the equation, because nobody is adding a second journey on top of the first.

The second apparent difference, which turns out to be about campuses rather than communities, is which board a child sits. Two households on the same street in Arabian Ranches 3 can be entered for different boards because their children attend different schools. That is why a tutoring comparison should start with the campus and the syllabus code rather than with the postcode. The community tells you about traffic. The campus tells you about the examination.

The practical conclusion for a family comparing options is that moving the search radius outward costs nothing and gains a much larger pool of specialists. Moving it inward narrows the pool to whoever is nearby and willing, which is the smallest useful set available to a parent in this part of Dubai.

sections.heading: Who regulates private schools in each emirate, and why it matters to a tutoring plan
paragraphs: This is a comparison no competitor page in the research for this project makes at all: ADEK is named by none of them and SPEA by one. It matters for two reasons. Families in this belt move between emirates more often than the market assumes, usually for work, and the regulator changes what is published about a school and who approves its fees and curriculum.

In Dubai the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. In Sharjah the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and in Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge does the same. For Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah the federal Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools. Those five bodies are the complete map.

The powers are not identical. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval sits with the emirate rather than only inspection. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations, which is the rule behind every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement.

For a Dubai family the practical use is narrow but real. A KHDA inspection band is published and comparable, which is useful when choosing a campus and useless as a measure of whether an individual child needs support. A school rated highly can still have a Year 11 losing fifteen marks a paper on method, and a school rated lower can be teaching a particular subject very well. The inspection band describes the institution; the marked past paper describes the student. Only one of those tells you what to buy.

sections.heading: What these grades are worth later: MoE equivalency, and the count that gets published wrong
paragraphs: IGCSE results eventually meet the UAE Ministry of Education, and the rule is more specific than most families expect. On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That last clause is the one worth writing down, because it changes a subject-choice conversation. A student taking Arabic and Islamic education alongside five other IGCSEs is not taking seven subjects toward the count; they are taking five toward the count and two that are required for other reasons. At least one page currently ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the published clarification says. Publishing the correct number is not a competitive flourish; it is the difference between a family planning around a real rule and planning around somebody's error.

The American track is specified differently. English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. The published clarification does not mention EmSAT and states no IB points threshold, which is why no IB equivalency figure appears anywhere on this page. Any site giving you one without a source on moe.gov.ae is guessing with your child's university application.

Two cautions belong with all of this. Equivalency and attestation are processes the Ministry and the emirate authority run, not something a tutoring service performs, arranges or influences, and nobody should imply otherwise. And tutoring is not required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression; a page suggesting it is has invented an urgency that the regulation does not contain.

sections.heading: Using the trial lesson as the comparison, and what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: Every comparison on this page is something a parent can research. One comparison can only be run, and that is whether a particular tutor works with a particular child. The free first lesson exists for that: one session, one proposed tutor, at the slot you asked for, with no card details taken before it runs. You keep the written notes whether you continue or not. The condition is simply that it is one lesson with one tutor, and if the match is wrong, saying so is the expected outcome rather than an awkward one.

What a good trial produces is a diagnosis you can check. By the end of it you should be able to see which of four things is costing your child marks: content never learned, method known but not executed, answers written at the wrong depth for the command term, or time lost to the clock. Those four have different prices and different timescales, and a tutor who cannot tell you which one applies after a marked paper has not done the job the hour was for.

The honest limitation is coverage. Mathematics, the three sciences, English and Business are reliably staffed on UAE evening hours. Less common subjects, and some combinations in the final weeks before a series, are not always available in the slot a family wants. Where that is the case you are told at the match stage rather than after a fortnight. Should the right tutor turn out to be India-based rather than UAE-based, we say so up front and keep the lesson on Gulf Standard Time. Where there is genuinely nobody suitable, the answer is no with a reason. No competitor page researched for this project publishes a coverage limit at all.

On data, because an enquiry about a child involves some. We collect a name, a school, a year group, the subjects and the tier, because the matching does not work without them. We do not need a photograph, a report card or a grade history to propose a tutor. A deletion request is honoured, and the privacy policy linked below explains what is held and for how long under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection.

process.title: Get the syllabus code from the school
process.description: Before comparing any tutor, ask the exams officer for the board and the code on the entry, and for the administrative zone if the entry is with Cambridge. That one email removes most of the guesswork from every later comparison, including which past papers are worth your child's evening.

process.title: Compare models, not brands
process.description: Decide whether you are buying presence in the room, a group pace at a centre, or a syllabus-matched specialist. The published AED bands differ by a factor of ten across those, and the differences are about what is included rather than about teaching quality.

process.title: Ask for the permit, whoever you hire
process.description: The MoHRE private tuition work permit is free and valid for two years, so there is no legitimate reason for a tutor not to hold one. Ask to see it, and ask separately whether they teach at your child's own school, which is an arrangement to decline rather than to arrange.

process.title: Run one trial as the real comparison
process.description: One free lesson, one proposed tutor, at the hour your child is actually free, with no card details taken first. The output you are judging is the diagnosis: whether the tutor can name which of content, method, depth or timing is costing the marks, from a paper rather than from a conversation.

process.title: Decide with an end date in mind
process.description: Agree what the arrangement is for and when it stops: a mock, a series, a specific topic set. A plan with a finish date can be judged. A standing booking with no end point drifts, and in a market where several providers publish no price at all, drift is expensive.

whyPoints.title: The comparison is published, not implied
whyPoints.description: Provider models, permit categories, syllabus codes, emirate regulators and the equivalency rule are all set out here with their sources. Competitor pages in this market compare themselves against an unnamed other platforms; a model-level comparison with cited rates is a different kind of document.

whyPoints.title: Distance is removed as a variable
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so the pool is every tutor who has taught the code on your child's entry rather than every tutor willing to drive to the community gate. For a specific paper at a specific tier, that is the difference that shows up on a script.

whyPoints.title: The permit question is answered in full
whyPoints.description: Only one competitor researched for this project touches licensing at all, in a single subheading. This page gives the resolution number, the validity, the fee position, the eligible categories, the official application route and the ethics rule that bars tutoring your child's own teacher privately.

whyPoints.title: The equivalency count is the one the Ministry published
whyPoints.description: Five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. At least one ranking page publishes six. A number that is wrong by one subject can change a child's option choices.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are disclosed before booking
whyPoints.description: Some subjects and some last-minute slots cannot be staffed on UAE evening hours, and where that is true you are told at the match stage, including whether the tutor who fits is based outside the UAE. No competitor page researched for this project discloses a limit of any kind.

faqs.question: Does hiring a tutor who actually lives in Arabian Ranches 3 help my child at all?
faqs.answer: It helps only if presence in the room is the thing your child needs, which for a younger student it sometimes is. It does nothing for the four variables that decide marks: the syllabus code the tutor has taught, whether they hold the MoHRE permit, whether they are free at the hour the bus gets back, and whether anyone replaces them if the match fails. The market prices proximity openly, at AED 180 to 500 an hour for an in-home visit against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. That difference buys travel rather than teaching.

faqs.question: Which provider model gives the best value for an IGCSE student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is actually wrong. A Year 7 who will not start homework alone is well served by the budget band at AED 45 to 150 an hour, where EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A Year 11 losing method marks on Extended papers needs the specialist band at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270. Paying specialist rates for homework supervision wastes money, and paying budget rates for Paper 2 technique wastes a term. Diagnose first, then choose the band.

faqs.question: How do I check whether a tutor holds the UAE private tuition work permit?
faqs.answer: Ask to see it. The permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system under the service Issuance of a New Work Permit, Private Tutor Licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing and takes two working days, there is no innocent reason for an active tutor not to hold one. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can a university student legally tutor my child in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the permit. University students are an eligible category for the MoHRE private tuition work permit, as are unemployed individuals, government and private-sector employees, teachers registered in government or private schools, and school students aged 15 to 18. Legality and suitability are separate questions, though. A university student is a reasonable choice for building homework habits and a poor one for Extended-tier paper technique, which needs somebody who has taught the specification and marked against its scheme. Ask which syllabus code they have taught, not which degree they are reading.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in Motor City better value than one-to-one online?
faqs.answer: They are different products. A centre sells a group class at a set pace, which suits a student who is roughly where the group is and benefits from the room. It also adds a drive at the end of a school day, which from the outer Dubailand phases is the costly part. A centre with premises and staff needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, renewed annually with the request made at least thirty days before expiry, and that is a fair thing to ask to see. One-to-one buys pace and diagnosis instead of a room.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE results treated the same for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: The Ministry's published British-track rule speaks about accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates rather than about a particular board: five subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. The board matters enormously for preparation, because the papers and question styles differ, and much less for how the certificate is later counted. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority rather than relying on any tutoring page, including this one.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE Ministry of Education actually count?
faqs.answer: Five. The published clarification states that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, alongside proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. At least one page ranking for these queries states six, which is not what the clarification says. The difference is not academic: it changes which subjects a Year 9 student needs to pick up.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count toward the five equivalency subjects?
faqs.answer: No. The published clarification states explicitly that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. They are nonetheless mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, so a student takes them for a different reason. The practical consequence for option choices is that a child sitting Arabic and Islamic Education plus four other IGCSEs has four toward the count, not six, and that is the sort of arithmetic worth doing in Year 9 rather than after results.

faqs.question: Who regulates the schools if we move from Dubai to Sharjah or Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: The regulator changes with the emirate. Dubai is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are the Department of Education and Knowledge. Sharjah is the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge, and both of those approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education. What is published about a school, and who approves its fees, therefore changes with the move even when the curriculum does not.

faqs.question: Would a tutor based in Mudon or Town Square be any different from one here?
faqs.answer: Not in any way that reaches a results slip. Those communities share bus routes and campuses with Arabian Ranches 3, so children are entered for the same two boards, against the same deadlines, for the same papers. The only genuine difference the comparison turns up is journey length, which affects when a session can start and nothing else. Because lessons run over live video, that difference disappears entirely: the hour is set by when your child is free, not by how far anybody has to drive to reach them.

faqs.question: Why do some tutoring sites quote their prices in US dollars?
faqs.answer: Because they are international marketplaces pricing centrally rather than for this market. It is worth treating as a signal. A provider quoting in dollars has usually not localised anything else either: in the research for this project the marketplace pages named no UAE school, no neighbourhood, no emirate regulator and no AED figure. A UAE family transacts school fees and tuition in dirhams, and a page that cannot quote in dirhams is unlikely to know which board your child's school entered them for.

faqs.question: Can I compare two tutors properly before committing to either?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the comparison should be run on the same artefact. Give each one the same marked past paper and the same question: which of content, method, answer depth or timing is costing the most, and what would the first three weeks do about it. Two useful answers will differ in approach and agree on the diagnosis. A vague answer is itself information. With us that is one free lesson per tutor, with no card details taken, and the written notes stay with you either way.

faqs.question: Does a school's KHDA inspection band tell me whether my child needs a tutor?
faqs.answer: No, and conflating the two is a common mistake. KHDA inspects on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and the outcome describes the institution: leadership, teaching quality across the school, provision for different groups. A strongly rated school can still have a Year 11 losing fifteen marks a paper to unshown method, and a lower-rated school can teach one subject very well. The band helps you choose a campus. A marked past paper tells you what your own child needs, and the two questions are answered with different evidence.

faqs.question: Is a tutor advertising examiner experience worth the higher rate?
faqs.answer: Only if the claim can be evidenced, and it usually cannot. The premium band in this market is published at AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED quoting AED 650. Current marking experience is not something a family can verify from a website, and examiner status does not give anyone access to marking decisions, grade boundaries or unreleased paper content. IB Gram does not describe tutors as examiners for that reason. The verifiable question is which specification they have taught and for how long, which is a better predictor anyway.

faqs.question: What if no IGCSE tutor is free in the evening slot we need?
faqs.answer: You are told at the match stage rather than after a fortnight of waiting. Mathematics, the three sciences, English and Business are reliably staffed on UAE evening hours; less common subjects and last-minute slots in the final weeks before a series sometimes are not. When the only suitable tutor is in India rather than the UAE, that is disclosed before payment and the session still runs on Gulf Standard Time. Where nobody suitable is available, the answer is no with the reason attached rather than a delay.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ran.closingHeading: Replace the radius with the syllabus code
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ran.closingBody: The single most useful thing an Arabian Ranches 3 parent can do before comparing tutors is email the school's exams officer and ask for the board, the syllabus code and the entry tier. With those three facts the comparison becomes concrete: which past papers matter, which question style the student should practise, and which tutors have genuinely taught it. Send us the same three facts plus the hour your child is actually free, and we will propose one tutor who has taught that code, run the first lesson free with no card details taken, and give you the marked script and the notes whether you continue or not.

intro.heading: Count the week before you buy the hours
paragraphs: Almost every tutoring conversation starts with how many sessions. It should start with where the hours currently go, because in a community like Bluewaters Island the honest answer is usually that there is no spare time at all, and a plan that ignores that will be abandoned by October regardless of how good the teaching is.

The island is a compact residential community on reclaimed land off JBR, joined to the mainland by one road bridge and a pedestrian link. Nothing a teenager needs is on it. School is inland, in Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, The Greens, Jumeirah Park or Emirates Hills. Swimming, football, music, tennis and tutoring centres are all across the bridge. So the week contains more travel than a map suggests, and the travel is concentrated in the same two hours every evening.

Add a Year 10 or Year 11 homework load from a school that sets it seriously, and the arithmetic is tight before tutoring is mentioned. Families then add two hour-long sessions, because that is what the enquiry form offered, and within a month the second session is being rescheduled weekly and the first is starting twenty minutes late.

The alternative is to audit first. Write down the actual week: arrival time each day, activities and where they are, homework load by subject, and what time the student is genuinely usable. Then decide what tutoring can occupy, which is frequently one forty-minute weekday slot and one weekend morning rather than two evening hours. Less time, better placed, consistently beats more time badly placed.

The IGCSE content is on this page too, because it matters: board, tier, syllabus codes, the series a UAE candidate sits and what to ask the exams officer. But the sequencing is deliberate. A family with the right slot and a slightly wrong revision plan will outperform a family with a perfect plan and a session nobody attends properly.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run in India only, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. In a week this tight, the relevant feature is that nothing is spent travelling to the lesson at either end, and that a session can be thirty minutes long without becoming uneconomic for anybody. No tutor crosses a bridge in evening traffic for half an hour, which is why in-home arrangements are locked to hour blocks whether or not a tired fifteen-year-old can use the full hour.

One further note on what this page does not argue. It is not a claim that Bluewaters students are over-committed or that their parents have scheduled badly. The week here is full because the community is small and well connected to things that are all somewhere else, which is a reasonable trade for living on it. The planning error is only in treating tutoring as an addition to that week rather than as something that has to be fitted into it, and that error is made identically in every dense, well-off part of this city. Reviewed October 2026.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-bluewaters-.programmesIntro: Three routes appear in Bluewaters households at this stage. Which applies changes both the revision material and what grade is reachable, so settle it with the exams officer before building any schedule.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Mostly tiered Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C and Extended reaching A*. Syllabus codes identify the course: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English. Assessment is linear at the end of the course, with practical or alternative-to-practical routes in the sciences chosen by the school.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. The zone determines which timetable governs study leave, so it belongs on the same email as the syllabus codes.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Uses 4-prefix codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry and 4EA1 English Language, graded 9-1. Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher; the International GCSE sciences are untiered and assess practical skills inside the written papers. Some subjects are available modularly, spreading assessment across sessions.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables a year ahead and revises them, so plan against the live official PDF. The results calendar matters for scheduling: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: AS and A Level progression
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum schools in this part of Dubai move students into AS and A Level at sixteen, with subject-specific IGCSE grade requirements for entry. Mathematics and the sciences typically need a grade 6 or B, and the jump in abstraction from Extended to AS is the steepest a student will have met.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 are required, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. Verify current rules on moe.gov.ae.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-bluewaters-.subjectsIntro: Eight subjects, with the realistic weekly time each needs from a tutor rather than the time a provider would like to sell. The useful question is minutes per week, not sessions per week.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1. Thirty to forty focused minutes a week maintains a student who is coping; method-mark habits are the first target. Needs more only when a genuine content hole has opened, which a timed paper will show.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Cambridge 0500 or 0510, or Pearson 4EA1. Responds fast to structure work on directed writing and the summary task. Forty-five minutes weekly with a piece of written work between sessions is enough for most students.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1. Forty minutes weekly on explanation structure and the electricity topics covers most of what is recoverable. Full timed papers belong at the weekend rather than inside a weekday slot.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1. Mole drill is ideal for a short weekday slot because it is repetitive rather than demanding, and making it automatic pays across the whole paper. Thirty minutes twice a week beats an hour once.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cambridge 0610 or Pearson 4BI1. The highest content volume and the least suited to a short tired slot, so this is the subject to move to a weekend morning if something has to move.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0455 or Pearson 4EC1. Diagram accuracy drills well in short bursts. The data response skill of quoting figures from the extract rather than paraphrasing is a precision habit worth a session of its own.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Cambridge 0450 or Pearson 4BS1. Most students reach the analysis band and stop short of evaluation. Teaching a justified judgement takes three or four sessions and then transfers to every extended answer in the subject.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Cambridge 0478 or Pearson 4CP0. Trace tables, binary conversion and pseudocode discipline are high-frequency and suit short sessions. The programming component needs practice between lessons rather than longer lessons.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0606. A separate qualification taken by a small strong cohort as a bridge to AS, covering early calculus, identities and series. Needs a full fresh session rather than a short tired one, and local specialist supply is thin.

sections.heading: Audit the week before deciding anything
paragraphs: This is the exercise we ask Bluewaters families to do before any conversation about sessions, and it takes fifteen minutes with a sheet of paper. Write the seven days. For each weekday, note the real arrival time at the apartment, not the school finish time. Note every activity, where it is, and the travel at both ends. Note homework by subject and how long it genuinely takes rather than how long it should take.

The pattern that emerges is nearly always the same. Four weekday evenings are effectively full by seven. One is lighter than the family thinks. The weekend contains more usable time than anybody had counted, usually on a morning that is currently being slept through. And somewhere in the week there is an hour of unsupervised homework in which the student is repeating the same error without knowing it.

That last finding is the valuable one, because it means improvement does not require a bigger week. It requires converting an existing hour rather than adding a new one. A student spending an hour on mathematics homework while writing no method steps is generating an hour of practice at losing marks, and a thirty-minute supervised session that fixes the habit changes what the other hour produces.

Only after the audit is the session question answerable. For most island students in Year 10 the answer is one short weekday slot and, if there is a real deficit, one weekend morning. In Year 11 approaching mocks that may rise. Two weekday hours added to an unaudited week is the arrangement we see fail most often, and it fails for reasons that have nothing to do with the tutor.

sections.heading: The activity trade-off nobody wants to discuss
paragraphs: In a community where everything structured is across a bridge, each activity costs more than its duration. An hour of swimming in the Marina is an hour of swimming plus twenty-five minutes of travel plus changing, which is closer to two hours of the evening. Three such commitments and the week has no weekday capacity left for anything academic.

We are not going to tell a family to drop sport. Physical activity does more for a Year 11 student's exam performance than a fourth weekly tutoring hour would, and the research on sleep and exercise is not seriously contested. But the trade-off should be made deliberately rather than by default, and it should be revisited in the mock term rather than assumed to be fixed for two years.

The deliberate version looks like this. List the activities with their true time cost including travel. Mark which are the student's own priority, which are habit, and which are a parent's enthusiasm. Then decide what the academic requirement actually is, which a timed paper will tell you more accurately than a report card. Most families find there is one commitment in the list that nobody would defend if asked directly.

The other half of the trade-off is session length. A family unwilling to lose an activity can still gain a thirty-minute slot, and thirty focused minutes with a specialist is a real intervention. The failure mode is insisting on an hour because an hour sounds like proper tutoring, then not being able to place it, and ending up with nothing.

sections.heading: Session length, and why forty minutes often wins
paragraphs: The standard tutoring hour is a commercial convention rather than a pedagogical finding. For a fifteen-year-old at six in the evening after a long commute, the last twenty minutes of an hour are frequently spent watching a tired student reread a question they could have answered at the start. That time is paid for and produces nothing.

Forty focused minutes, by contrast, can hold a complete cycle: review what was set, teach one thing, apply it to two questions, set the next piece of work. For drill-type work such as mole calculations or method-mark habits, thirty minutes twice a week beats sixty minutes once, because the repetition interval matters more than the block length.

There are exceptions and they are predictable. A full timed paper needs an uninterrupted block, which is why it belongs at the weekend. Extended writing in English Language needs enough time to draft and review. Additional Mathematics needs a fresh student and a proper run at an abstract topic. For those, book the longer session and book it when the student is capable of using it, which on this island means a weekend morning rather than a Wednesday evening after the bridge.

The practical point for a Bluewaters family is that shorter sessions are easier to place in a full week, cheaper, and more likely to still be happening in February. A provider who will only sell hour blocks is selling their convenience. Ask whether a shorter session is available before concluding that tutoring does not fit, because the answer changes what the week can hold.

sections.heading: Board, tier and the ceiling worth knowing early
paragraphs: With the slot settled, the content question starts with one email to the exams officer: the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series for each subject, in writing. In a school entering candidates with both boards the answer differs by subject, which is why a report card can show 9-1 grades beside A*-G grades without any error in it.

The tier answer is the one with a hard consequence. Cambridge 0580 Core is capped at grade C, so a student at the very top of that tier cannot be awarded a B. If a sixth-form entry requirement is a B or a grade 6, the tier has settled the outcome before revision begins. Pearson 4MA1 runs Foundation and Higher with its own published tier arrangements.

That decision is genuinely open in the first term of Year 10 and close to closed by the second term of Year 11, because Extended content never taught would have to be learned alongside revising everything else. If a move is being considered, ask the school for a timed paper from the higher tier and decide from the script rather than from classwork, which flatters a student who is working at a comfortable level.

Two other answers change the revision material. Cambridge sciences offer a practical paper or an alternative-to-practical route, chosen by the school, and the two need different preparation. Some Pearson subjects are modular, spreading assessment across sessions rather than concentrating it in one terminal run, which reshapes a revision term more than any teaching method does.

sections.heading: What a near-me search cannot tell you about fit
paragraphs: A near-me search ranks by proximity and by local listing investment. Neither tells you whether a tutor will work in thirty-minute blocks, whether they teach your child's board, or whether they are free in the one lighter evening the audit identified. Those three are what determine whether the arrangement survives, and all three are invisible to a map.

Proximity also matters less than it appears even for in-home arrangements here. A tutor coming from the Al Barsha campus ring at five faces Sheikh Zayed Road, the Marina approach, one bridge and then visitor parking in a residential tower. The published Dubai travel premium of roughly AED 50-150 an hour, visible in the gap between online and in-home bands, is that journey priced into the lesson rather than itemised on it.

For an online session the journey disappears from the tutor's side entirely, which has a specific scheduling consequence in a tight week: the session can be thirty minutes without being uneconomic. No tutor will cross a bridge in evening traffic for a half-hour lesson, so in-home arrangements are structurally locked to hour-long blocks whether or not the student can use them.

IB Gram does not offer UAE home visits, so this is not a comparison between two things we sell. It is the reason we only sell one of them here. For a younger child who needs an adult physically present, independent local tutors work across the Marina and JBR and can genuinely be the better choice, and we will say so.

sections.heading: The mock term, when the audit has to be redone
paragraphs: Everything the audit established changes in the mock term. School days lengthen with revision sessions, so arrival moves later. Activity schedules often continue unchanged because nobody revisited them. And the academic requirement rises at exactly the point the available time falls, which is why this is the term families most often respond to by buying hours they cannot place.

Redo the audit instead. The lighter evening may have moved. The weekend morning becomes more valuable, because full timed papers are now the highest-return activity available and they need an uninterrupted block. And at least one activity commitment is usually worth pausing for eight weeks, which is a conversation better had in advance than in week three.

The content side should narrow at the same time. Ask the school for component marks rather than the mock grade. Blank or abandoned questions indicate content gaps needing taught order. Attempted questions marked low across the paper indicate command-term misreads, which is the fastest thing to fix and where most recoverable marks sit. A script that thins towards the end is a pacing problem solved by allocating time against mark value.

Those three need different work and different amounts of it, and only the script distinguishes them. A family that redoes the audit and reads the component marks will buy fewer hours than one that panics, place them better, and still be running the arrangement when the series arrives.

One caution about the weeks immediately before the papers. By that point the highest-return activity is timed questions on two or three identified topics, and almost nothing else moves a grade. Families who add broad revision sessions across every subject in those weeks are buying reassurance rather than marks, and the student is usually more tired as a result. Narrow the content and protect the sleep.

sections.heading: What it costs, sized to a short-session week
paragraphs: Pricing a short session honestly matters here, because a family that has concluded tutoring does not fit their week is usually comparing against an hour they cannot place. The Dubai market bands, read in October 2026 from competitor pages and the Bestimate 2026 rate table, are these.

Taken from the top down. Premium or examiner-led provision is advertised from AED 500-650 an hour, with BartyED at AED 650. Specialists sit at AED 200-450, with TutorChase at AED 270. A qualified IGCSE subject tutor online is AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Below that is the budget or university-student tier at AED 45-150 an hour, where EdFlik lists AED 45-65 and Tutopiya starts from AED 33-52. The in-home line is the one this address distorts rather than the one a comparison table explains: AED 180-350 for one-to-one, rising to AED 500 at specialist levels. A tutor visiting Bluewaters crosses from Jumeirah Beach Residence and parks under somebody else's building, so the figure actually quoted to an island household tends to sit at the upper end of that range rather than the lower.

Converted to the patterns this page recommends: one forty-minute weekday session a week across a twelve-week term is eight hours, or AED 1,200 to AED 2,400 at the qualified band. Adding a weekend morning block takes the term to roughly twenty hours, or AED 3,000 to AED 6,000. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240-600 budget and AED 600-1,200 mid-tier.

Context: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. These are market figures and not IB Gram prices. We publish no price list on these pages and start with a free trial lesson instead, because the honest number depends on which of these patterns the week can actually hold.

One comparison worth drawing out of the table below. A thirty-minute weekday slot across a term costs roughly a quarter of what a weekday-plus-weekend arrangement does, and for a student who is coping but careless it frequently recovers a similar number of marks, because the work is habit formation rather than content teaching. The expensive patterns are for genuine deficits, and a timed paper rather than a report card is what tells the two apart.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and what we will not do
paragraphs: Individual tutors in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time through its app, website or e-services system.

u.ae states that individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any specific figure quoted to you is unverified. Dubai private schools themselves are overseen by KHDA, which inspects annually and publishes ratings from Outstanding to Very Weak, and those reports are free to read before any school transfer decision.

On academic honesty, the boundary applies to any school-set investigation, project or controlled task. A tutor teaches the skills, explains what the criteria reward, questions the approach before weeks go into something unworkable, and gives feedback on drafts the student wrote. A tutor never writes, rewrites or completes assessed work or generates data. The consequence of crossing that line falls on the student.

We also do not reproduce or distribute board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, which are copyright material. And we are not KHDA approved, Cambridge accredited or Pearson approved, hold no KHDA Educational Services Permit, and have no UAE office. A provider describing itself as approved should be asked which permit it means.
