process.title: Do the week audit first
process.description: Seven days on a sheet of paper: real arrival times, every activity with its travel at both ends, homework by subject and how long it genuinely takes. Fifteen minutes, and it answers the session question better than any conversation about targets does. Send it with your enquiry.

process.title: Send a recent marked paper
process.description: A marked script shows whether the losses are method marks, specific topics or running out of time, and those three need different work and different amounts of it. A report card only confirms that something is wrong, which is the one thing you already knew before searching.

process.title: Pick the length before the number
process.description: Thirty or forty focused minutes is a real intervention and fits a week that an hour will not. We will quote for the length the work needs rather than the length that is easiest to sell, and for drill-type work two short sessions beat one long one.

process.title: Free trial lesson in the audited slot
process.description: We run the trial at the time and length we intend the weekly session to be, so you find out whether it works before committing. A real teaching hour or half-hour on the current sticking point, a short written note afterwards, no card held and nothing renewing.

process.title: Redo the audit at mocks
process.description: Revision sessions lengthen the school day, so arrival moves later in the term when the requirement rises. Redo the seven days, move the slot if it has stopped working, and consider pausing one activity for eight weeks rather than adding hours to a week that just got smaller.

whyPoints.title: We size the plan to the week, not the ambition
whyPoints.description: An audit comes before any proposal, because in a community where everything is across a bridge the honest starting position is that there is no spare time. A plan that ignores the week is abandoned by October regardless of the teaching quality.

whyPoints.title: Short sessions genuinely offered
whyPoints.description: Thirty and forty-minute sessions are available and often recommended. In-home arrangements are structurally locked to hour blocks because no tutor crosses a bridge in evening traffic for half an hour, which means they cannot offer the length a tired fifteen-year-old can actually use.

whyPoints.title: Converting an hour rather than adding one
whyPoints.description: Most weeks contain an unsupervised homework hour in which a student is repeating the same error. Repurposing that hour keeps the week the same size and changes what it produces, which is a better first move than adding a commitment to a full schedule.

whyPoints.title: Session length matched to work type
whyPoints.description: Mole drill and method habits want thirty minutes twice a week. A full timed paper wants ninety minutes at a weekend. Biology wants a fresh student. Treating all tutoring as an interchangeable hour is how families end up paying for the twenty minutes nobody is using.

whyPoints.title: Board and tier settled before the plan
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 Core is capped at grade C and Pearson 4MA1 runs Foundation and Higher on 9-1. We ask for the syllabus code first, because a tier ceiling may already have decided what grade is reachable and a family should know that in Year 10 rather than Year 11.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you to drop something
whyPoints.description: Sometimes the right recommendation is pausing an activity for eight weeks, or repurposing an existing hour, rather than buying sessions. That costs us the booking, which is the only reason the rest of this page is worth taking seriously.

faqs.question: How many tutoring sessions does a Year 10 student here actually need?
faqs.answer: Usually fewer than families buy, and placed differently. For most Bluewaters students in Year 10 the answer is one short weekday slot of thirty to forty focused minutes, plus a weekend morning if a timed paper has shown a real deficit. Two weekday hours added to an unaudited week is the arrangement we see fail most often, and it fails for scheduling reasons rather than teaching ones. Audit the actual week first: real arrival times, activities with their travel, and homework by subject. Then the session question answers itself.

faqs.question: Why does a week audit matter more than choosing the right tutor?
faqs.answer: Because an excellent tutor in an unplaceable slot produces nothing. Write out seven days with the real arrival time at the apartment rather than the school finish time, every activity and its travel at both ends, and how long homework genuinely takes. The pattern is consistent: four weekday evenings are full by seven, one is lighter than the family thinks, the weekend morning is more usable than anybody counted, and somewhere there is an hour of unsupervised homework repeating the same error.

faqs.question: Is a thirty-minute session long enough to be worth booking?
faqs.answer: For several kinds of work, yes, and it is often better. Thirty focused minutes can hold a full cycle: review what was set, teach one thing, apply it to two questions, set the next piece. For drill-type work such as mole calculations or method-mark habits, thirty minutes twice a week beats sixty minutes once, because the repetition interval matters more than the block length. The hour is a commercial convention, and for a fifteen-year-old at six in the evening its last twenty minutes are frequently wasted.

faqs.question: Should we drop an activity to make room for tutoring?
faqs.answer: Make the trade-off deliberately rather than by default, and do not assume the answer is yes. Exercise and sleep do more for a Year 11 student's exam performance than a fourth weekly tutoring hour would. What is worth doing is listing activities with their true cost including travel, since an hour of swimming in the Marina is closer to two hours of the evening, then marking which are the student's own priority, which are habit and which are a parent's enthusiasm. Most families find one nobody would defend.

faqs.question: Which subject should move to the weekend if something has to?
faqs.answer: Biology, then full timed papers in any subject, then Additional Mathematics. Biology has the highest content volume of the sciences and memory work fails when a student is tired. A full timed paper needs an uninterrupted block and real concentration, which a weekday evening after a bridge crossing rarely supports. Additional Mathematics 0606 is abstract and demanding enough that a tired session achieves very little. Mathematics method drill and chemistry mole work, by contrast, survive a late slot perfectly well because they need persistence rather than insight.

faqs.question: Can tutoring replace an existing homework hour instead of adding to the week?
faqs.answer: Often, and it is the first thing we look for. A student spending an hour on mathematics homework while writing no method steps is generating an hour of practice at losing marks, because the mark scheme awards visible reasoning separately from the answer. A supervised thirty-minute session that fixes the habit changes what that other hour produces. Converting existing low-yield study time keeps the week the same size, which matters enormously on an island where every commitment carries a bridge crossing at both ends.

faqs.question: What should we ask our school before booking any tutoring?
faqs.answer: Four things per subject, in writing: the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series your child is entered for. Also ask which Cambridge administrative zone the school sits in, since Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone and cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. And ask for component marks rather than grades after any school assessment, because that is what tells you whether the problem is content, command terms or pacing.

faqs.question: Does the Cambridge Core tier cap what grade is possible?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cambridge 0580 Mathematics Core is capped at grade C, so a student performing at the very top of that tier cannot be awarded a B. If a sixth-form entry requirement is a B or a grade 6, the tier has settled the outcome before revision begins. The decision is genuinely open in the first term of Year 10 and close to closed by the second term of Year 11, because Extended content never taught would have to be learned alongside revising everything else. Ask for a timed Extended paper and decide from the script.

faqs.question: Our week changes completely in the mock term. What then?
faqs.answer: Redo the audit. School days lengthen with revision sessions so arrival moves later, activity schedules usually continue unchanged because nobody revisited them, and the academic requirement rises exactly as available time falls. The lighter evening may have moved. The weekend morning becomes the most valuable block in the week because full timed papers are now the highest-return activity and need an uninterrupted run. And pausing one activity for eight weeks is often the cheapest hour available anywhere in the schedule.

faqs.question: Why can an online tutor offer half an hour when a local one will not?
faqs.answer: Because the travel has to be worth the trip. A tutor crossing one bridge in evening traffic from the Al Barsha campus ring faces thirty to forty-five minutes each way plus visitor parking, and nobody does that for a thirty-minute lesson. So in-home arrangements are structurally locked to hour blocks whether or not a tired fifteen-year-old can use the full hour. Online, the journey disappears from the tutor's side, which is why short sessions become economic and why they fit a week that an hour will not.

faqs.question: What does a term of short weekly sessions cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: One forty-minute weekday session across a twelve-week term is eight hours, which at the market band for a qualified IGCSE subject tutor online of roughly AED 150-300 an hour is AED 1,200 to AED 2,400. Adding a weekend morning block takes the term to about twenty hours, or AED 3,000 to AED 6,000. Specialists sit higher at AED 200-450, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Those figures were read in October 2026 from competitor pages and the Bestimate Dubai rate table and describe the market rather than our price list.

faqs.question: Do you come to our apartment on Bluewaters Island?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE lessons as one-to-one live video, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. In a week this tight the relevant feature is that nothing is spent travelling to the lesson at either end, and that short sessions become possible. Independent home tutors do work across the Marina and JBR at roughly AED 180-350 an hour on published Dubai market rates, and for a younger child who needs an adult physically present they can genuinely be the better choice.

faqs.question: Which exam sittings will our child be entered for?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables a year ahead and then revises them, so plan study leave against the live official PDF rather than any restatement. The exams officer can confirm the series and board for each subject in the same email as the syllabus codes.

faqs.question: Will the slot survive half-term travel and Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, by moving rather than cancelling. Because sessions are online they follow the laptop, so a fortnight abroad usually means a different clock time rather than a gap, which matters because a missed session does not cost one lesson but breaks the sequence the next one builds on. During Ramadan, school hours shorten and routines move later, so sessions shift to post-Iftar slots as a normal request and we hold the tutor and the time. Tell us the dates when the schedule is set rather than in the week itself.

faqs.question: Are private tutors in Dubai legally required to hold a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. A MoHRE private tuition work permit is required, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time through its app, website or e-services system. u.ae states that tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so distrust any amount quoted.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-bluewaters-.closingHeading: Fit it into the week you actually have
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-bluewaters-.closingBody: On an island where school, sport and everything else sits across one bridge, the binding constraint on IGCSE tutoring is time rather than money or teaching quality. Write out the seven days honestly, find the one lighter evening and the weekend morning nobody is using, and look for the existing homework hour that is producing nothing. Then buy the shortest session that does the work, at a time the student can actually use, and get the board and tier from the exams officer so the hours go into the right material.

intro.heading: Proximity is the wrong filter for an IGCSE subject problem
paragraphs: Near me is a search habit rather than a requirement. It made sense when a tutor had to physically arrive, and it still returns the right answer for a seven-year-old who needs an adult turning the page. For a Year 10 or Year 11 student losing marks on moles calculations or on functions and transformations, proximity is noise. The question that matters is whether the person teaching has sat with that specific paper, marked it against the official scheme, and can name the three question types that are costing your child grades.

That is a narrow skill and it is unevenly distributed. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both award International GCSEs, and a Dubai school will often enter mathematics with one board and the sciences with another. Each board numbers its papers differently, tiers differently, and assesses practical science differently. A tutor drilling Cambridge 0625 past papers with a student entered for Pearson 4PH1 is teaching real physics against the wrong paper structure, and the marks lost are invisible until results day.

So this page is deliberately technical. It sets out the syllabus codes behind the subjects Old Dubai students actually take, what each paper assesses and roughly what it is worth, where marks leave the paper topic by topic, and what the command terms demand in practice. Those four things are what a subject tutor should be working on, and they are almost entirely absent from the pages currently ranking for this search. Across the competitor corpus measured for this project, exactly one syllabus code appeared on seven area-level pages combined.

On delivery, the position is simple and we state it early. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE — a tutor at the door is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with the student's own marked script or past paper on a shared screen and the whiteboard saved afterwards. For syllabus-level work that is a better arrangement than a dining table, because the past paper, the mark scheme and the student's attempt can all be on screen at once.

The practical benefit for a Bur Dubai family is supply. A tutor who has taught Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics is not likely to live in Al Mankhool, and if they do they will already be teaching the families on their street. Removing travel from the arrangement means your child is matched on syllabus experience rather than on postcode, and it buys back the hour a Bur Dubai school run and the creek crossing would otherwise take out of the evening. It also widens the pool for the subjects where supply is thinnest in this part of the city, which in practice means Additional Mathematics, the separate sciences at Extended tier, and Economics.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-bur-dubai.programmesIntro: IGCSE is the Year 10 and 11 stage of a British pathway, and in Old Dubai it is bracketed by two other stages that change what tutoring is worth buying. These are the three a Bur Dubai family actually encounters.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: No external examination, school-set assessment, and the stage where almost every Year 11 problem originates. The recurring gaps are algebraic manipulation, index laws, rearranging formulae, standard form and the written explanation IGCSE mark schemes insist on. None of those are hard to fix in Year 8 and all of them are expensive to fix in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: In Old Dubai this is the stage at which transfers from Indian and American curricula arrive, and the mismatch is almost never in topic coverage. A student may have met more mathematics and still score lower, because IGCSE questions ask for applied reasoning within a stated mark allocation rather than for a recalled procedure.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years, eight to ten subjects, external examination by Cambridge International or Pearson Edexcel. Each subject carries its own syllabus code, paper count and tiering structure, and in the sciences a separate practical-skills assessment. The grade scale differs by board and by subject, so a report can show a 7 and a B in the same term without contradiction.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026 and June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026. Cambridge runs June and November series in the UAE. Always check the live official timetable, since provisional versions get revised.

programmes.name: International A Level, Years 12 and 13
programmes.description: Three or four subjects in depth. The step up from IGCSE Extended in mathematics and the sciences is the largest in the British pathway, and students who reached a grade 7 by memorising procedures frequently stall in the first term. Additional Mathematics at IGCSE is the single best predictor of a comfortable start.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students need one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at grade E or 3. Verify the current detail with the ministry or your emirate's attestation authority.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-bur-dubai.subjectsIntro: Each subject below carries the codes Old Dubai schools actually enter students for, with the topics where marks reliably leave the paper. The codes are the starting point for any session worth paying for.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Extended adds functions, graph transformations, vectors and harder trigonometry. Marks leave on unshown method, on rounding mid-calculation, and on reading a three-step question as a one-step one. Non-calculator and calculator papers need separate practice, and most students only ever drill the one they prefer.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Introduces differentiation, integration and harder algebra before A Level. Students who leaned on a calculator through 0580 struggle with algebraic manipulation here. A term of weekly work in Year 11 is usually what separates a comfortable A Level start from a difficult one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity, moments and anything requiring a graph to be interpreted rather than drawn. Definitions must be reproduced precisely to score, and multi-mark explanation questions need a taught structure. Cambridge's separate practical-skills paper loses students marks on variable control and method, not on physics.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and concentration calculations, electrolysis, and organic reaction pathways. State symbols and significant figures cost single marks repeatedly across a paper. Explanation questions demand a cause rather than a description of a trend, which is the most common reason a confident student stalls in the middle bands.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A long syllabus where command terms set the ceiling. Describe, explain and suggest ask for different things and students who write identical content for all three cap themselves. Data interpretation, graph work and the osmosis and enzyme practicals are the reliable mark sources and the reliable losses.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: Double-award and single-award routes compressing three sciences into fewer entries. The content is narrower than the separate sciences; the question style is identical, so technique work transfers directly. Confirming which route the school entered your child for matters before any revision plan is written.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading response. Fluent speakers lose marks on structure and on evidence selection rather than vocabulary. Summary tasks punish paraphrase that drifts from the text, and the reading questions reward close, short quotation. Timed practice with a marked script is the only intervention that reliably works.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A separate qualification from first-language English with its own mark scheme and a speaking component. Many Old Dubai students are entered for this, and the two need different teaching. Checking the entry code prevents the most common mismatch between a tutor's preparation and the actual paper.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study application under time pressure. Marks sit in applying a concept to the stimulus, so students who memorise definitions score in the lower bands. Calculation questions are quick, reliable marks and are usually the first thing worth drilling in a short block.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the fastest available grade change: a correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram earns marks prose cannot recover. Evaluation questions need a two-sided argument with a supported judgement, which is a taught structure rather than an opinion.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode under exam conditions, logic gates, data representation and the recurring trace-table questions. Students who can code in a real language often lose marks writing pseudocode to the board's conventions, which is a formatting problem rather than a programming one.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires Arab and non-Arab students to be taught in separate classes. First-language and foreign-language entries are different papers with different expectations, which is the most frequent entry mismatch in this district.

sections.heading: What near me really means for an IGCSE search in Bur Dubai
paragraphs: An IGCSE subject tutor working one-to-one online in the Dubai market costs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and a tutor who travels to a Bur Dubai address is quoted at roughly AED 200 to 500 including the drive. The premium buys proximity. What it does not buy is somebody who has taught the specific syllabus your child is entered for, because travel time narrows the pool to whoever lives nearby rather than widening it to whoever knows the paper.

That matters more at IGCSE than parents expect, because the subjects are not interchangeable at the level a tutor needs to work. Cambridge 0620 Chemistry and Pearson 4CH1 Chemistry both cover electrolysis, and they ask about it differently, number the papers differently and reward different written structures. A good general science teacher will teach the chemistry correctly and still leave marks on the table, and nobody in the room will notice until the results arrive.

The three questions that actually screen a tutor are therefore nothing to do with distance. Which syllabus codes have you taught, and for how many series? Can you mark a paper against the official scheme and tell me where the marks went by topic? And do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? All three are answerable in a single message, and the answers vary far more between tutors than the advertised hourly rates do.

IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses — home visits are something we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, which for syllabus work means the past paper, the official mark scheme and the student's own attempt can be on screen together, and the whiteboard is saved afterwards. The rest of this page is the substance a tutor should be bringing to that screen.

sections.heading: The syllabus codes behind your child's IGCSE subjects
paragraphs: Across the competitor pages measured for this project, exactly one syllabus code appeared on an entire seven-page area cluster. That is a strange gap, because the code is the first thing a tutor needs and the easiest thing for a school to supply. Everything downstream of it — which papers are sat, how long each lasts, whether there is a separate practical assessment, what the grade scale looks like — follows from the code and from nothing else.

The table below lists the codes Old Dubai schools commonly use, with the paper pattern for each. Treat it as an orientation rather than a specification: boards revise syllabuses, and the authoritative document is always the current specification on the board's own website. What the table is for is the conversation with the school. If you can ask whether your child sits 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher, and get a straight answer, the rest of the planning becomes concrete.

One structural point worth knowing. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and the board states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone — it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A tutor planning a revision schedule from a timetable found online rather than from the school's own copy is taking a risk nobody needs to take.

The practical use of all this is sequencing. Once you know the papers, the revision plan writes itself: a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper need separate practice, a separate practical-skills paper needs its own block of work, and a subject with two equally weighted papers needs coverage of the whole syllabus rather than the half the student enjoys. Students who revise by topic preference almost always arrive underprepared for one specific paper.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually leave the paper, topic by topic
paragraphs: Ask a Year 11 student what they find hard and they will name the topic they dislike. Mark a past paper against the official scheme and a different list appears. The two overlap less than you would expect, which is why every engagement should open with a marked script broken down by topic and by question type rather than with a conversation about confidence.

In mathematics the recurring losses are method lines that were never written, premature rounding inside multi-step calculations, and multi-step questions read as single-step ones. In Chemistry it is moles and concentration arithmetic, state symbols, and explanation questions answered with a description of a trend instead of a cause. In Physics it is selecting between two plausible equations under time pressure, and definitions reproduced approximately rather than precisely. In Biology it is command terms, graph work and statistical handling of data.

English behaves differently and catches confident families out. A student who speaks and writes fluently can still sit in the middle bands because the reading questions reward close, short selection of evidence and the summary tasks punish paraphrase that drifts. Those are structural habits, trainable in a handful of sessions with marked scripts, and almost never addressed by general conversation practice.

The useful consequence is that a short block beats a long vague one. If a marked paper shows thirty marks lost across moles calculations, electrolysis and state symbols, four sessions on those three things will move a grade boundary. Six months of general chemistry revision quite possibly will not, because it spreads the same hours across topics the student was already scoring on.

sections.heading: Mark-scheme language: the command terms that set the ceiling
paragraphs: Command terms are the most underrated part of IGCSE preparation. Every mark scheme is written around them, and a student who treats describe, explain and evaluate as synonyms has capped their grade before they write a word. The fix takes a few sessions, it transfers across every subject, and it is almost never taught explicitly because teachers assume it is obvious.

The table below sets out what each term actually demands and what typically loses the mark. The pattern across all of them is the same: the term tells you how many distinct things the examiner expects and what kind of thing each one is. A four-mark explain question wants four linked causal steps, not four descriptive statements about the same observation. A two-mark state question wants two facts and no justification, and a student who writes a paragraph wastes three minutes earning nothing extra.

Practising this is mechanical. Take a marked script, find the questions where the student scored half the available marks, and rewrite the answers to the structure the term demands. Within three or four sessions most students start reading the command term first and the stem second, which is the right order. It is the single most portable skill a tutor can leave behind, because it works in June and it still works at A Level.

There is a scheduling argument here too. Command-term work does not need the syllabus to be finished, so it can be done in Year 10 or early Year 11 rather than saved for the final block. Families who do it early find their later revision measurably more productive, because the student is practising against the standard the examiner applies rather than against their own sense of a complete answer.

sections.heading: Past-paper work that actually changes a score
paragraphs: Everybody tells students to do past papers. Almost nobody specifies how, and done badly it is a way to spend six weeks confirming a grade rather than improving it. The common failure is a student working through papers untimed, with notes open, marking generously, and finishing with a folder of completed papers and no change in performance.

The method that works has four parts. Sit the paper to time, without notes, in one go. Mark it against the official scheme rather than from the answers in a revision guide, awarding nothing for what is not written down. Record the loss per topic and per question type in a list, not a feeling. Then reteach only the top three entries on that list before sitting another paper. The folder is irrelevant; the shrinking list is the product.

A tutor's value in that cycle is concentrated in two places. Marking honestly is the first — students and parents both mark too kindly, and a mark scheme is specific in ways that are easy to miss. Reteaching with exam phrasing is the second: a topic retaught from a textbook does not transfer to a paper, whereas the same topic taught through three past-paper questions from different series does. Boards publish those papers and specimen materials themselves, and tutors should reference and link them rather than circulate copies.

A note on honesty here. Reproducing or supplying syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads is copyright infringement, and we do not do it. Our tutors point students at the official source and work from what is legitimately available, which is more than enough material for any revision plan.

sections.heading: What subject-level IGCSE teaching costs in Dubai, and what travel adds
paragraphs: Take the travel premium on its own terms. The difference between an in-home visit at roughly AED 200 to 500 an hour and a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 is not a discount for a lesser service; it is the price of somebody's drive across Dubai at 5pm. Over a twenty-session block that premium is a four-figure sum, and the question worth asking is what it buys that a shared screen does not.

For syllabus-level work the honest answer is very little, and in one respect it buys less. The tutor at the table is drawn from the people who can reach your street before 7pm. The tutor on the screen is drawn from everyone who has taught 0606 or 4CH1. For a subject-specific problem that distinction decides whether the sessions address the actual weakness or merely cover the topic again more slowly.

The dirham figures across this market are published by a handful of providers and they spread widely. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, which buys supervision rather than syllabus teaching. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. TutorChase publishes AED 270. Bestimate puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, and the highest published rate found in this market is AED 650 at a premium named-tutor agency. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240 to 600 for a budget weekly hour, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work.

None of those are IB Gram prices. They are market figures, each attributed to whoever published them, and they are on this page because three of the six competitor pages measured for this project publish no price at all and two quote US dollars to families who transact in dirhams. sections.heading: Reading an IGCSE report: two grade scales, one child
paragraphs: Old Dubai households routinely hold reports on two different scales, sometimes for the same child in different subjects. Cambridge uses A* to G in most syllabuses and a 9 to 1 scale in some variants; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on 9 to 1. A parent comparing a 6 in one subject with a B in another is not comparing like with like, and neither number means what the equivalent UK GCSE number means to a relative back home.

The practical approach is to ignore cross-subject comparison and read within a subject instead. What a parent needs from a report is the direction of travel in that subject, the gap between the current working grade and the target, and the teacher's comment on what is causing it. Those three things are actionable. A ranked list of grades across nine subjects mostly tells you which subjects the student enjoys.

For equivalency purposes the scale does matter, and the published rule is specific. Ministry of Education requirements on the British track ask for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count of five. One competitor page in this market tells UAE parents six subjects are needed, which is wrong. Equivalency is a ministry process; no tutoring provider performs it or guarantees it, and the requirements should be checked on the ministry's own pages.

Where a report shows a working grade well below the target, the question for a tutor is not whether the gap can close but which paper it closes on. A student two grades short usually has one paper carrying most of the loss, and finding out which one takes a single marked script. That is a far more useful piece of information than the report itself contains.

sections.heading: The permit question, and who may legally teach your child in Dubai
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the position is clearer than most of this market lets on. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

MoHRE's own service for it is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, with no fee listed and a stated two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount quoted at you with suspicion — including figures that circulate online.

Two further points a Bur Dubai parent should know. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal entity from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, so nobody should describe themselves as holding KHDA status without that permit. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carrying a similar restriction. Treat that as press-reported and verify against the current policy document before relying on it.

The reason this sits on a subject-focused page is that the permit is the one credential a parent can actually verify in a market full of unverifiable claims. Ask for it. A tutor who holds one will show it; a tutor who objects to the question has answered it. IB Gram holds no regulator or examination-board accreditation and does not claim any, and we would rather say that plainly than imply an approval nobody in this market actually has.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether an IGCSE tutor lives near us in Bur Dubai?
faqs.answer: Only if your child needs an adult physically present to start working, which is mostly a younger-student issue. For a Year 10 or Year 11 subject problem, distance narrows the pool to whoever can reach your street rather than widening it to whoever has taught the paper. The three questions that actually screen a tutor are which syllabus codes they have taught, whether they can mark a paper against the official scheme and report losses by topic, and whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. None of them is about location.

faqs.question: If our school switches maths board, how much of the preparation carries over?
faqs.answer: Both award an International GCSE in mathematics and both are accepted for UAE university entry and ministry equivalency. They tier differently — Cambridge uses Core and Extended, Pearson uses Foundation and Higher — and they structure and number their papers differently, with Cambridge separating non-calculator and calculator assessment. Content overlaps substantially at the top tier, so the real risk is practising the wrong paper structure and the wrong mark-scheme phrasing. Ask the school for the code, then use that board's own specimen papers rather than whatever a revision site offers.

faqs.question: How do I get a proper diagnosis of where my child is losing IGCSE marks?
faqs.answer: Sit one full past paper to time, closed book, in a single session, then mark it against the board's published scheme rather than against a revision guide's answers, awarding nothing for method that is not written down. Record the losses as a list by topic and by question type. That list is almost always different from the topics the student says they find hard, and it is the only sensible basis for deciding what four or eight sessions should contain. Our free trial lesson is spent doing exactly this.

faqs.question: Why do command terms matter so much in IGCSE marking?
faqs.answer: Because every mark scheme is built around them. A four-mark explain question wants four linked causal steps; writing four descriptive statements about the same observation scores one. A two-mark state question wants two facts, and a paragraph earns nothing extra while costing three minutes. Students who treat describe, explain and evaluate as synonyms cap themselves in the middle bands across every subject. It takes three or four sessions to fix, it transfers to every paper, and it can be done in Year 10 before the syllabus is finished.

faqs.question: Is my child's Cambridge practical-skills paper teachable online?
faqs.answer: Yes, because it tests experimental reasoning rather than manual dexterity. The marks go on identifying dependent and independent variables, spotting an uncontrolled factor, choosing sensible axes and scales, drawing a line of best fit, reading a value from a graph, and explaining an anomaly in precise written form. All of that is taught at a desk using the board's own past practical papers and mark schemes. The school runs the laboratory work; the paper rewards the interpretation, and that is where most students are losing marks.

faqs.question: My child does lots of past papers but the score never moves. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always because of how they are being done. Untimed, with notes available, marked generously against a revision guide rather than the official scheme, and never followed by reteaching. That cycle produces a folder of completed papers and no change. The version that works is timed and closed-book, marked against the published scheme with nothing awarded for unwritten method, losses recorded as a list by topic, and only the top three entries retaught before the next paper. The shrinking list is the evidence, not the folder.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a single weak IGCSE topic usually take?
faqs.answer: Two to four for something contained, such as moles and concentration calculations, electrolysis, or functions and graph transformations. The sequence is the same each time: teach the underlying idea properly, work three or four past-paper questions on it from different series, then check it against a question the student has not seen. If the topic is still costing marks after four sessions the diagnosis was probably wrong and the weakness sits one level below, usually in algebra or in reading the question.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Bur Dubai students most often need help with?
faqs.answer: Mathematics by a wide margin, then Chemistry and Physics, then English Language, with Business Studies and Accounting behind. Additional Mathematics appears in Year 11 from students heading for A Level Mathematics or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches. Requests for Arabic rise steadily through the year, which follows from the fact that every Dubai private school timetables it whatever curriculum it is licensed for, and that first-language and foreign-language entries are different papers requiring different teaching.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give us past papers and mark schemes to keep?
faqs.answer: We reference and link the official sources rather than circulating copies, because reproducing syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables is copyright infringement regardless of who does it. Cambridge and Pearson both publish specifications, specimen papers and other materials on their own sites, and schools have access to more through their examinations officer. There is far more legitimate material available than any revision plan needs, and working from the official version also avoids the stale and altered copies that circulate on file-sharing sites.

faqs.question: Does a 6 on my child's report mean the same as a B?
faqs.answer: No, and the two scales should not be compared across subjects. Cambridge reports A* to G in most syllabuses and 9 to 1 in some variants, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports 9 to 1. Neither maps neatly onto the UK GCSE scale a relative abroad might be thinking of. The useful way to read a report is within one subject: direction of travel, the gap to the target, and the teacher's account of what is causing it. Cross-subject ranking tells you mostly about preference.

faqs.question: What does the UAE British-track equivalency rule actually ask of an IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: Five. The published British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, alongside one accredited A-Level at grade E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. One page currently ranking in this market tells UAE parents six subjects are required, which is incorrect. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process that no tutoring provider performs or guarantees, so verify current requirements on the ministry's own pages or with your emirate's attestation authority.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE series will my child in Dubai actually sit?
faqs.answer: June or November. The February and March series circulating online is offered to India only, and revising a UAE child towards it is a genuine error rather than a technicality. For Pearson, the International GCSE November 2026 timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026 with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results arrived on 22 January 2026 and June 2026 results on 20 August 2026. Cambridge also allocates centres to one of six zones with different timetable versions, so use the school's own copy.

faqs.question: Should we start IGCSE tutoring in Year 10 or wait until Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10, if the aim is a grade rather than a rescue. Content is being taught in Year 10, so weekly work that keeps pace with the class is both cheaper across two years and more effective than revisiting the same material under pressure a term before the papers. Year 10 is also when tier decisions are made, and a term of focused work is often what turns a borderline Core recommendation into a viable Extended entry. Year 11 blocks are technique work on content that should already be in place.

faqs.question: How do we verify that a Dubai tutor is permitted to teach privately?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. It is issued through MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so disregard any specific figure quoted at you. A tuition centre with premises needs a separate KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a different thing entirely.

intro.heading: What "near me" is really asking, and the better question underneath it
paragraphs: An IGCSE tutor near me in Business Bay is one of the most-typed tutoring phrases in central Dubai, and almost nobody who types it actually wants a short drive. What they want is somebody who can start this week, who knows the paper their child sits, and who can be checked. Distance is a proxy for all three, and it is a poor one. A tutor eleven minutes away in Downtown Dubai may have never taught Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1 Higher tier. A specialist who has taught it for nine years is reachable in four seconds over a video call.

Business Bay makes this especially clear. The district is a residential and commercial tower cluster along the Dubai Water Canal with almost no schools inside its own boundary. Families here already drive out of the district every morning, to Sobha Hartland, to Al Safa, to Al Quoz, to Al Jaddaf, to Academic City. The school run has already dissolved the idea that your child's education happens within walking distance. Applying a radius filter to tutoring, after accepting a twenty-five minute school commute, is an inconsistency worth noticing.

So this page is written as a comparison, because that is the honest way to answer the query. It compares Business Bay with the districts immediately around it and shows that the answer comes out the same in each of them. It compares a local pool of tutors with a national one, subject by subject. It compares Core and Extended, Cambridge and Edexcel, grades 9-1 and A*-G. And it compares what the Dubai market charges by the month rather than by the hour, because a monthly figure is the number a family actually budgets against.

The one thing we will not do is pretend. IB Gram delivers tuition to UAE families as one-to-one online lessons over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. If a tutor arriving at your tower in Business Bay is a requirement rather than a preference, the market has providers who do that and this page gives you the rates and the questions to ask them. If what you want is the right specialist for a named paper, online is not a compromise in this market, it is the only way to get one reliably.

Everything below is written for a parent who wants to act. The tables carry the numbers. Market rates are attributed to the provider or the source that published them, never presented as our price list. Regulatory statements are attributed to u.ae, KHDA and MoHRE, and where a fact could not be verified against an official source we say so and leave it out rather than guess.

The programmes below are the three routes most often in play in this corridor, with what each one means for a student living in the towers along the canal rather than near a campus.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10-11
programmes.description: Two years of linear courses examined at the end, with Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel the two boards Dubai schools use most. Most students carry eight to ten subjects. Mathematics, the sciences and English Language are usually the ones that decide whether a sixth-form choice stays open, and they are also where tiering decisions bite hardest. Grades arrive as 9-1 on most Edexcel International specifications and as A*-G on many Cambridge ones, which is a frequent source of parental confusion.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the IGCSE year sits under KHDA inspection and alongside the mandatory UAE subjects. Business Bay students travel to schools in Sobha Hartland, Al Safa, Al Quoz and Al Jaddaf, which means a 3.15pm finish can still mean a 4.10pm arrival home. We schedule from 4.30pm so that a session is not taught to a child who is still in a car.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary, Years 7-9
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, assessed by Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests. Checkpoint results are the single most useful piece of evidence a family has when the school proposes Core rather than Extended tier a year later. A Year 9 who is scoring in the lower bands in mathematics has a full year to change the tier conversation, and a year is enough. A Year 11 does not have that year.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. For Business Bay families the practical point is that the October window gives a Year 9 a diagnostic before the tier decision rather than after it, which is when most parents here first hear the word Core.

programmes.name: IB Diploma or A Level, Years 12-13
programmes.description: Where the IGCSE year is pointing. The split matters because the entry requirements differ: an IB Diploma school will usually want grade 6 or 7 at IGCSE for a Higher Level science, while an A Level school may accept a 6. Extended tier mathematics is effectively a prerequisite for IB Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and a Core-tier student cannot reach the grades that route needs.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. For a central-corridor family that widens the sixth-form choice considerably, which makes the Year 11 grade profile more consequential rather than less.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects
programmes.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in every Dubai private school. They are timetabled lessons with real reports, and they are the subjects Business Bay families most often forget to ask about until a report card lands. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA's requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Note that these subjects do not count towards the five IGCSE subjects the Ministry of Education requires for British-track equivalency, so they matter for the school report and not for the equivalency file.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-business-ba.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Business Bay families ask for most, with what each assessment actually rewards. A tutor who can name the paper and the tier is worth more than one who can name your street, which is the whole argument of this page compressed into a sentence.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The subject where tier decides everything. Extended and Higher tier carry the higher grade ceiling and the algebra, trigonometry and calculus-adjacent content that a sixth-form science course assumes. Marks go missing on multi-step problems where working is not shown and on the transformation and vector questions that appear late in the paper.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism are where the Extended tier separates from the Core, and where most Business Bay students lose their grade. The practical or alternative-to-practical component rewards precise description of method, variables and sources of error, which is a writing skill rather than a physics one and responds quickly to coaching.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis and organic chemistry account for a disproportionate share of lost Extended marks. The common failure is arithmetic confidence rather than conceptual understanding: a student who can explain electrolysis will still drop four marks on a titration calculation under time pressure.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: The highest content volume of the three sciences and the one most often treated as memorisation. Extended-tier marks are won on the command terms: explain, suggest and compare each want a different shape of answer, and a student who writes a description where an explanation was asked for scores nothing for correct biology.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990, Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading responses carry the marks, and both are assessed against criteria the student has usually never read. A session spent on the mark scheme rather than on more practice essays often moves a grade faster, because the issue is almost always structure rather than vocabulary.

subjects.name: English Literature (Edexcel 4ET1 / Cambridge 0475)
subjects.description: Textual reference density is the scoring variable. Strong students write perceptively about theme and score in the middle band because they quote too little and analyse language too generally. Closed-book papers need memorised quotations, which is a timetable problem a tutor can structure.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Both reward application to the stimulus material and evaluation that reaches a judgement. The pattern in Dubai is strong theoretical knowledge and weak evaluation, because evaluation marks require committing to a position and justifying it rather than listing both sides neutrally.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 / Edexcel 4CP0)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables are the mechanical marks and the most recoverable ones. Students who code fluently in Python still lose marks writing pseudocode to the board's conventions, and the theory paper on data representation and networks is frequently under-revised.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken by strong Extended candidates as an extra, and the usual preparation for Higher Level mathematics in the Diploma. It assumes complete fluency in the Extended syllabus, so a student who is still consolidating 0580 content will struggle regardless of hours spent.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Both are source and data papers as much as content papers. Geography rewards accurate case-study detail including named places and figures; History rewards source evaluation on provenance and purpose. Vague case studies are the most common reason a well-revised student lands two grades below expectation.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Required in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and taught in separate classes from Arabic as a first language under KHDA rules. It does not count towards the five subjects the Ministry of Education requires for British-track equivalency, but it does appear on the school report and in progression decisions.

subjects.name: Accounting and Information Technology
subjects.description: Both are precision subjects where method marks dominate. Accounting rewards correctly formatted statements even when a figure is wrong; ICT rewards following the task specification exactly. Students lose marks to presentation conventions rather than to misunderstanding, which makes them unusually fast to improve.

regions.note: Tower living along the Dubai Water Canal with no IGCSE school inside the district. Every family commutes out, most towards Sobha Hartland, Al Safa or Al Quoz. A realistic weeknight session starts at 4.30pm or later.

regions.note: One canal crossing away and operationally identical: no school inside the district, the same commute corridors, the same evening traffic on Al Khail and Sheikh Zayed. A tutor here would be eleven minutes from a Business Bay address and no more available.

schoolClusters.city: Al Quoz, Meydan and the southern corridor

sections.heading: The real constraint is availability, not distance
paragraphs: An IGCSE tutor near me in Business Bay is a search for availability wearing the costume of a search for proximity. The question that decides whether your child improves is whether somebody who has taught their exact paper has a free hour at 5pm on a Tuesday. Distance has nothing to do with that, and in a district with no school inside it, distance is not even a proxy.

Here is the arithmetic that matters. Business Bay and its neighbouring districts might hold a few hundred IGCSE candidates. Those candidates are split across two boards, two tiers and nine or ten subjects each. A parent who needs Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1 at Higher tier, on a Wednesday at 5.30pm, is asking a pool of a few dozen locally available tutors to contain one exact match with one exact free hour. Frequently it does not, and the family books whoever is free. That is how a child entered for 4CH1 ends up being taught Cambridge 0620 content by someone who is competent and wrong.

Removing the radius changes the shape of the problem rather than the standard of the tutor. The pool becomes everyone who teaches that paper and is awake in the Gulf timezone window, which is a pool measured in hundreds rather than dozens. The match becomes specific rather than approximate. The table below sets out what each filter a parent applies does to the pool they are choosing from, which is a calculation no competitor in this market publishes.

sections.heading: Business Bay against the districts either side, compared honestly
paragraphs: This page's angle is comparison, so here is the comparison done properly rather than as a list of neighbourhood adjectives. Six districts in the central corridor, compared on the four things that could plausibly change the tutoring answer: whether there is a school inside the district, what the commute does to the evening, which boards the local schools run, and what the local in-home tutor pool looks like.

The finding is dull and useful. Only one variable genuinely differs across these districts, and it is the realistic start time of a weeknight session. Sobha Hartland can begin at 4pm because the school run is five minutes. Meydan cannot begin before 5pm. Everything else, the board mix, the tier decisions, the subjects families struggle with, the shortage of specialists for any named paper, is constant across all six. A family moving from Business Bay to Downtown Dubai or to Culture Village would face the same tutoring market on the other side of the move.

That matters because it tells you what to optimise. If the only thing your postcode controls is what time you can start, then choose on everything else: the specialist's match to the paper, the permit position, whether the trial lesson produced a diagnosis or a sales pitch. And choose a delivery format where start time is negotiable rather than dictated by somebody else's drive across Al Khail Road at rush hour.

One further observation from the table below, since it is the kind of thing a neighbourhood page usually hides. The districts with schools inside them, Sobha Hartland, Al Quoz and Meydan, do not have deeper local tutor pools than the districts without. Proximity to a campus produces proximity to teachers, not availability of specialists for a named syllabus code at a named hour. Several Business Bay families arrive at this conclusion on their own after a term of trying to book locally, which is an expensive way to learn it.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: No tutor, however close, can undo a tier decision made too late. Cambridge IGCSE subjects are frequently tiered into Core and Extended, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics into Foundation and Higher. The tier a student is entered for caps the grade they can be awarded. This is the single most consequential piece of information on a Business Bay child's academic record, and in our experience it is the piece parents are least often told clearly.

The practical version runs like this. A Core-tier candidate sits different papers covering a reduced syllabus, and the grade ceiling is lower than Extended's. If a sixth-form science course asks for grade 6, and the Core ceiling sits below that, the course closes regardless of effort. The school usually makes the entry decision in Year 10 or early Year 11 based on internal assessment, and once entries are submitted the window narrows sharply.

So the first job on this page is to tell you to go and find out. Ask the school, in writing, which tier your child is entered for in each tiered subject, and what evidence that decision rests on. If the answer is Core in a subject your child needs for sixth form, you have a conversation to have and possibly a year in which to change it. A Year 9 has time. A Year 11 in the second term usually does not, and the honest advice then is to maximise the grade within the tier rather than fight the entry.

sections.heading: Reading the report: 9-1, A*-G and what a grade actually says
paragraphs: A Business Bay parent frequently holds a report with two grading scales on it, because a child can sit Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects graded 9-1 alongside Cambridge subjects graded A*-G in the same year. The two scales are not interchangeable and the rough equivalences published by the boards are approximate rather than exact. Treating a 7 as an A is close enough for a conversation and wrong enough to misread a sixth-form requirement.

What matters for tutoring is different again: not the letter or the number, but which component produced it. A grade 5 in physics built on a strong theory paper and a weak alternative-to-practical is a different problem from a grade 5 built on an even performance across both. The first is four weeks of method and error-source writing. The second is a content gap. The grade alone does not distinguish them, and this is why a first session should produce a diagnosis rather than a lesson.

Ask the school for component-level marks, not just the subject grade. Most will provide them on request, and many report them routinely without parents noticing which column means what. Those numbers are the only honest basis for deciding whether tutoring is worth buying and for which subject, and they are free.

There is a second reading problem on Dubai reports, which is the predicted or target grade sitting beside the attained one. A target grade is a school's internal projection, generated from prior attainment data, and it is not a promise from the board. Parents in the central corridor sometimes buy tutoring to close a gap to a target that was never a realistic entry requirement for anything their child wants to do. Check the target against the actual sixth-form requirement before spending money on the difference between them.
bullets: A child can hold 9-1 and A*-G grades in the same year group
Published equivalences between the two scales are approximate

sections.heading: What the Dubai market costs per month, not per hour
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how tutoring is advertised and monthly totals are how families actually budget, so this section leads with the month. Bestimate's "Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026" rate table puts monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to 600 for budget tutoring, AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published monthly packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Working back to the hour from those monthly figures: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end of online tutoring. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 for a qualified subject tutor online. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors reaching AED 200 to 500 once travel is priced in. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work and BartyED AED 650 at the premium named-tutor end. Every one of those figures belongs to the provider named beside it and was read in October 2026.

The gap between the online band and the in-home band is the travel premium, and a Business Bay family should know what it buys. It buys the tutor's drive to your tower, the parking, the lift, and the twenty minutes at the end when nobody wants to be rude about the time. It does not buy a better specialist. Priced monthly, a family paying the in-home premium for two subjects is spending the difference on logistics rather than on teaching hours. IB Gram does not publish a UAE price list on these pages; the free trial lesson and the consultation exist so a family can see the teaching before discussing money.

sections.heading: The two series a UAE candidate sits, and the one that is not for you
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. Those are the two windows a Dubai candidate sits, and a Business Bay family planning a term should plan against one of them specifically rather than against a vague sense of summer.

One warning that costs families real money. The Cambridge February/March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates do not sit it, and any tutoring plan built around a February-March exam window is built on the wrong country's calendar. If a provider quotes you a March deadline for a Dubai candidate, that is a signal about the provider.

Two further operational facts worth more than most of the advice in this market. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your centre's zone; Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. And Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why the table below names milestones rather than restating dates that can be revised. Read the exact dates from the board's live timetable and confirm your own centre's zone with the school's examinations officer.

Dates that are already in the past can be stated safely because they are checkable, and they show the shape of a series better than any projection. Pearson's November 2026 final International GCSE timetable ran to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That pattern, a November sitting with results in the following January, is the resit route a Year 11 who misses a June grade will actually use.

sections.heading: Equivalency: the five subjects the Ministry of Education counts
paragraphs: This is a gap in this market wide enough to drive through. UAE Ministry of Education equivalency decides whether an IGCSE profile is recognised for university admission and employment purposes in the UAE, and most tutoring pages in Dubai do not mention it at all. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The sourced requirement is five.

For the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That is the whole British-track rule in two sentences, and it is the reason a Business Bay family should check the subject list in Year 10 rather than after results.

Two cautions. First, there is no published IB points threshold for equivalency that we have been able to read on an official Ministry source, so this page does not state one; confirm any IB figure on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority. Second, IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation for anybody. We describe the requirement and point you to the official channel. Tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and anyone telling you otherwise is selling urgency.

sections.heading: The permit question, and what a parent can actually verify
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page calls it "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here; figures circulating online for this could not be verified against an official source. The position parents need is simpler than the paperwork: the permit exists, it is free, and a tutor who will not discuss it is telling you something.

One boundary families in the central corridor ask about often. Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK policy document before relying on the exact wording. Either way, hiring your child's own class teacher privately is not the clever shortcut it appears to be. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation, licence or partnership, and we would not describe ourselves as approved by any of them. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises, which we do not operate in the UAE.
bullets: The MoHRE private tuition work permit is free and valid for two years
Applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system
No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: This matters on an IGCSE page because coursework and practical components still carry marks that must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach the content, explain the criteria, model a technique on a different example, and give feedback on the student's draft. A tutor may not write the text, supply sentences to be copied, or edit a piece to completion. The distinction is not a style preference; a breach is a malpractice finding against the student, and the student carries the consequence.

There are providers in this market that cross the line openly, including one that advertises completed Internal Assessments for sale. If a tutoring provider offers to produce assessed work, that offer is the reason not to use them, whatever else they do well. IB Gram will not write, complete or ghost-edit coursework for any student on any board, and will not accept such work if a family offers it.

We also do not publish or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. We reference them and link to the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. Your child's school has legitimate access to all of it, which is another reason the first session should start with the school's own documents rather than with somebody's photocopies.

For a Business Bay family the practical test is easy to apply at the trial lesson. Ask the tutor what they would do with a half-finished piece of coursework. The right answer involves reading it, naming which criterion is underserved, and setting the student a task. The wrong answer involves the tutor taking the document away. One of those answers protects your child's entry and the other puts it at risk, and you can hear the difference inside a minute.
bullets: Teaching, criteria explanation, modelling on a different example and draft feedback: allowed
Writing text, supplying sentences to copy, editing to completion: not allowed, ever
No syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes supplied as downloads from us

sections.heading: Coverage, matching and the honest answer when it is no
paragraphs: No tutoring platform covers every paper at every hour, and the ones that imply otherwise are simply not telling you about the gap. Our position is to disclose it. Core subjects at both boards, both tiers, are reliably covered: mathematics, the three sciences, English Language and Literature, business studies, economics, computer science, geography and history. Narrower subjects are less certain, and specific hours in the 5pm to 7pm Gulf Standard Time peak fill first.

If no specialist for your child's paper is free at the hour you need, you will be told that at the enquiry rather than matched to the nearest available person. Where a UAE-based tutor for a niche subject is not available, the match may be a specialist elsewhere teaching into the Gulf timezone, and that is stated before the trial rather than discovered afterwards. For a Business Bay family that trade-off is usually easy: the same timezone, the same paper, a specialist who has taught it.

The practical first step is small. Bring three things to the consultation: which board and syllabus code each subject is, which tier your child is entered for, and the most recent component-level marks. With those three, a diagnosis is possible in the trial lesson. Without them, the first two sessions get spent working out what the problem is, which is an avoidable expense and the most common one in this market.

It is also worth saying what a sensible volume looks like, because families in this corridor frequently over-buy at the start. Two subjects at one session a week each is a load a Year 11 can absorb alongside nine courses and a thirty-minute commute. Four subjects at two sessions a week is not, and the usual result is attendance that collapses by week five. Start narrow on the subjects where the grade gap is widest and add later if the calendar genuinely has room.
