process.description: Schools use mock results for tier confirmation, setting and intervention, whatever students are told about practice. The four to six weeks before a mock are therefore better value than the four to six weeks after, and they test whether the diagnostic cycle works.

process.title: Book the narrow windows early
process.description: Mock season and the final eight to twelve weeks are the tightest availability of the year across the whole Dubai market, because every cohort arrives together. A slot reserved in the autumn costs exactly the same and comes with a materially better match.

process.title: Write the retake rule before results
process.description: Per subject, what grade triggers a November entry and what grade does not, measured against the destination the student has accepted. It converts results morning into an action and keeps the autumn block bookable while slots still exist.

whyPoints.title: We publish the administrative calendar
whyPoints.description: Entry windows, zone timetables, results dates and the remark window are the facts that decide what support can achieve, and no competitor page in this market sets them out. A family who has them can act in the stage where action is still possible.

whyPoints.title: We publish our own availability pattern
whyPoints.description: Widest in Year 10 autumn, narrowest in mock season and the final eight to twelve weeks, briefly tight after results. Saying so lets a family book when the match is good rather than when the panic arrives, and the price is identical either way.

whyPoints.title: Right about zones and about the series
whyPoints.description: Cambridge allocates centres to six administrative zones with a timetable each and cannot accept responsibility for the wrong version being used. And the February and March series is India-only, so UAE candidates sit June and November.

whyPoints.title: Backward-looking dates only
whyPoints.description: Pearson's June 2026 and November 2025 results dates appear here because they are published and checkable. No future series is given a month and a year, because boards revise windows and a page that ages into being wrong is worse than one naming the month.

whyPoints.title: Honest about home visits and about timing
whyPoints.description: IB Gram makes no UAE home visits. Beyond price, demand concentrates into the same fortnights across the market, which is exactly when a locally bounded tutor has no slot, and a visiting tutor cannot easily supervise a full timed paper.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claims and no permit costs
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson approval, and has no UAE premises. The MoHRE private tuition permit is free, so any provider citing permit costs in a rate is charging for something that does not exist.

faqs.question: Why is my child's IGCSE exam timetable different from a friend's in the same building?
faqs.answer: Because the timetable is set per exam centre and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, publishing a separate version for each. Its own guidance says it is essential to use the correct version for the centre's zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong one was used. Two Culture Village pupils at different schools are candidates at different centres, so print the timetable your own school issues and give the tutor that copy.

faqs.question: How long before the papers do IGCSE entries actually close?
faqs.answer: Months, and the exam office makes them within the board's window. Once the entry is made it fixes the board, the subject list and, where a subject is tiered, the tier. That makes the autumn term of Year 11 a genuine deadline for any conversation about tier or subject choice rather than a soft one. Ask the exam office which board, specification code and tier your child is entered for, and ask before the window closes rather than after a mock result prompts the question.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE results arrive, and does the series change it?
faqs.answer: Substantially. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while the November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A June grade therefore lands before the new academic year and a November grade lands in the middle of one. That difference matters for any sixth-form or university conversation resting on the grade, and it should shape the retake decision rather than being discovered after it.

faqs.question: Can a grade be challenged after IGCSE results?
faqs.answer: Boards run an enquiries about results window for remarks and reviews, administered through the school's exam office rather than directly by a family, and the deadline is short. If a grade looks inconsistent with the student's own marked work and the school's internal evidence, that is the route to raise it. Knowing the window exists before results day is the difference between acting and finding out afterwards. A tutoring provider has no standing in the process and should not offer to submit one.

faqs.question: Should we be preparing for a February or March series in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge's February and March series is offered in India only, and UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge also runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which is sometimes the source of the confusion. A Culture Village family planning revision towards a February or March IGCSE window would be preparing for an exam their school cannot enter them for.

faqs.question: At which point in the academic year is tutor availability widest across Dubai?
faqs.answer: The autumn of Year 10 and the early autumn of Year 11, by a wide margin. Demand has not concentrated, specialists have capacity, and a family can be choosy about subject, level and slot. It is also the window in which the cheapest effective work happens, because fluency gaps are still narrow and the tier conversation is still live. The narrowest windows are mock season and the final eight to twelve weeks, when every Dubai cohort arrives at the same point within a fortnight.

faqs.question: Does booking a pre-series slot early actually get a better tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it costs exactly the same. Availability in the final eight to twelve weeks is the tightest of the year because every school cohort in Dubai reaches that point simultaneously, so a family searching for the first time in that window chooses from whoever remains. A slot reserved in the autumn for spring use is the same price with a materially better match. It is the only free improvement available in this process and it requires a decision rather than money.

faqs.question: Can tutoring change the tier my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Only inside one window: between the department's provisional indication and the final entry. Focused work on the specific Extended or Higher topics they doubt can move the call, because they are watching particular evidence rather than general effort. Generalised extra lessons usually cannot. So the useful question is what evidence would change their mind. Outside that window the ceiling is fixed and support becomes about maximising performance within a limit somebody else set.

faqs.question: What do schools do with IGCSE mock results, really?
faqs.answer: More than students are told. Mock results feed tier confirmation where an entry has not closed, setting and grouping decisions, identification of who needs intervention, and in some schools reference grades for post-16 applications. A student treating the mock as a rehearsal supplies the school with a worse sample of their ability at exactly the moment decisions are being made on it. The four to six weeks before a mock are therefore better value than the weeks after it.

faqs.question: How should a resit be planned given it collides with a new course?
faqs.answer: Deliberately, because the collision is certain. The autumn term after a June series contains both resit preparation and the opening weeks of A Level or the IB Diploma, competing for the same evenings, and the post-16 course carries the longer consequences. Fewer and better-placed sessions beat more of them: keep weekdays short and move the resit paper work to a weekend. Book as soon as the November entry is made rather than when the pressure becomes visible.

faqs.question: Will a tutor visit our Culture Village apartment for IGCSE sessions?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We deliver one-to-one tuition for UAE families online over live video on Gulf Standard Time and send no tutors to UAE addresses; home visiting is a service we operate only in India. Agencies that do visit publish rates of AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's table and AED 200 to AED 500 from home-tutor providers. There is also a timing issue: a visiting tutor with a next appointment to reach cannot easily supervise a full timed paper under real conditions.

faqs.question: How early can a Culture Village student start a weekday session?
faqs.answer: Often 16:30 if the school is next door in Al Jaddaf or across the Creek in Dubai Festival City, since those are short runs from Jaddaf Waterfront. A pupil travelling to Sobha Hartland is realistically 17:00 and one commuting to Nad Al Sheba 17:15 or later. Choose the slot for the worst normal weekday rather than the best. During a pre-series block the full timed papers belong on a weekend morning, with weekday sessions kept shorter and focused on technique.

faqs.question: Why do you link official timetables instead of printing the dates?
faqs.answer: Because boards revise published windows, and Pearson explicitly publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series before finalising them. A date restated on a page can be accurate when written and wrong by the time it is read, and a family plans a term around it. Backward-looking dates are different: those are given here with the series they belong to, because the date is what makes the claim checkable. For any future series, the live official document is the only safe source.

faqs.question: Does the UAE tutoring permit affect what I pay?
faqs.answer: It should not, because it is free. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A provider citing permit costs as a reason for a higher rate is charging for something that does not exist.

faqs.question: Can you give us past papers and mark schemes to work through at home?
faqs.answer: We work from them in sessions and link the official source, but we do not reproduce or supply them. Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are copyright works, and a provider advertising a library of them is offering something a legitimate operation would not. We show the student where the current document lives on the board's own site instead, which matters on a calendar-driven page: a student who can find the live timetable can check a date a tutor quoted.

intro.heading: The two-year course almost nobody plans
paragraphs: IGCSE is a two-year course and it is treated as a one-term emergency. The search volume for tutors in this market peaks in the spring of Year 11, which is the point at which the fewest useful things remain possible. The tier has been entered, the entries have closed, and the weeks left are enough for technique and not for foundations. Everything about that situation was visible eighteen months earlier.

This page is therefore a map rather than a sales pitch. Six terms run from the start of Year 10 to the June papers, and each has a job. Two of them are the only windows in which a genuine content gap can be rebuilt without borrowing time from something else. One contains the decision that sets the grade ceiling. One contains the mock window, which is the richest diagnostic event of the course. One is triage.

For families in DAMAC Hills there is a second clock running. Secondary students here generally travel out of the community to school and arrive home after five, which shortens the usable evening and makes session timing a real constraint rather than an administrative detail. A plan that ignores the commute loses sessions quietly across a term and then concludes that tutoring did not work.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition live, one to one and online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a DAMAC Hills address, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. In this community the format earns its place on the clock alone: a 5.30pm session starts at 5.30pm, and no journey is added to a day that already contains two.

The examination calendar itself is sourced and can be stated. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and the February/March series is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate plans around June with November as the resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

What cannot be stated is a future date. Series are named by month on this page rather than by month and year, because a page that dates itself to one year is wrong the following year with nobody having touched it. Where a date appears it is a backward-looking citation, which is what makes it checkable.

What follows is the map: the six terms and what each is for, the entry deadline and the ceiling it sets, how to choose between series, what results day opens up, and what eight, six or three weeks can honestly achieve. If you read one section, read the one on the mock fortnight. It describes the only free diagnostic in the course, it needs no tutor to carry out, and the tally it produces usually points at a cheaper and shorter block than the one a provider would otherwise propose.

subjects.name: Mathematics — Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher

subjects.description: Calculation layout installs as three templates in about three weeks and recovers marks across every quantitative question. Organic chemistry arrives late in the course, so a block timed for the term it is taught beats one timed after.

subjects.description: Explanation structure and unit discipline move in three to four weeks. Where the same rearrangement fails in physics and mathematics together, the real block is quantitative and takes longer than either subject alone.

subjects.description: Case-study application and diagram discipline respond quickly. These are good candidates for a short block in the term before mocks, because the marks lost are structural rather than knowledge-based.

subjects.name: Geography and History — Cambridge 0460 and 0470
subjects.description: Case-study banks take a term to build properly and source technique takes four sessions. A late block should prioritise the technique and the skills papers, which are the reliable marks nobody drills.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics — Cambridge 0606
subjects.description: Notation conventions and composite differentiation take about six sessions. Requests arrive in the second half of Year 11, which is late but workable because the difficulty is narrow rather than general.

subjects.description: Trace tables and pseudocode logic are two-session techniques that appear in every series. A thin tutor pool means this subject is worth booking earlier than its difficulty would suggest.

sections.heading: What this search means, and the clock behind it
paragraphs: An IGCSE tutor near me in DAMAC Hills means private one-to-one tuition in a Cambridge or Pearson subject for a student living in the community, and IB Gram provides that live online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a DAMAC Hills address; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. In a community where the student has already travelled twice that day, removing the tutor's two journeys as well is the practical benefit rather than a concession.

The word 'near' in the search is usually standing in for 'soon'. The phrase appears after a report, a mock result or a parents' evening, and proximity feels like the route to help arriving quickly. Online matching is faster, because it removes the requirement that somebody be free in the right corridor on the right evening: a specialist for a named code can normally be proposed within a day with a trial lesson in the same week.

Speed matters because of where in the clock these searches happen. A family that finds a tutor in four days after a February mock has ten working weeks before the June papers. One that takes three weeks has seven. The second block is a different piece of work with a lower ceiling, and most of the difference was spent waiting rather than studying.

What the clock cannot be made to do is reverse. The tier entry closes months before the papers and sets a grade ceiling for that series. Content gaps cannot be rebuilt in six weeks while revision is also happening. Those are limits rather than attitudes, and a plan that acknowledges them produces better results than one that does not, because it spends the weeks on marks that are still available.

sections.heading: Six terms, mapped
paragraphs: Laid out as six terms, the IGCSE course stops looking like a long wait followed by a panic. Each term has a job, and the jobs are not interchangeable. Year 10's three terms are for content, foundations and the tier decision. Year 11's are for completing content, the mock window and its review, and the final run.

The two foundation windows are the first and second terms of Year 10. That is the only part of the course in which algebraic fluency, written explanation structure or reading stamina can be rebuilt without taking time from revision, because there is no revision yet. A student who arrives in Year 10 from a weak Year 9 and does nothing about it in those two terms will meet the same limitation in every subject for the next eighteen months.

The tier decision belongs to the second and third terms of Year 10, because entries are usually made then. That is the moment at which a diagnostic against the Extended content list is actionable: it shows whether the gap between a student's position and Extended demand is weeks of work or years of foundations, which is exactly the information the department needs to revisit an entry.

Year 11's first term completes content. Its second contains the mock window and the fortnight afterwards, which together are the most information-dense part of the course. Its third is triage. sections.heading: The entry deadline sets the ceiling
paragraphs: Of all the dates in an IGCSE course, the one with the largest effect is the least discussed. Final entries are made by the school to the board's deadline, months before the papers, and they fix the subject, the board and the tier for that series. Where a Cambridge syllabus is tiered, a Core entry caps the grades available however well the student performs in June.

That means the tiering conversation has a shelf life. Held in Year 10 while entries are open, it is a decision informed by evidence. Held in the spring of Year 11, it is a complaint about something that cannot change for that series. The difference between those two conversations is a date most families never ask about, and the school will tell them if asked.

The evidence that makes the conversation useful is narrow and obtainable. A diagnostic against the Extended content list, showing which topics are absent rather than weak, plus twenty minutes of non-calculator algebra to establish whether manipulation is fluent. Those two pieces of information distinguish a student who needs six weeks of work from one who needs two years of foundations, and the department can act on the distinction.

Pushing every student to Extended is not the recommendation. A candidate on Extended who cannot handle the algebraic demand loses more marks on harder papers than the raised ceiling returns, and sitting a paper they cannot attempt does real damage in the final weeks. The point is that the decision should be made with evidence, in the term when it is still a decision.

sections.heading: June or November, and how to choose
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only, which means UAE candidates have two series rather than three and should discard any revision schedule that references a February window.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the centre's zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. That is a practical warning rather than a formality: the timetable a parent finds by searching is not necessarily the one their school's centre is working to.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is the only version worth planning from. As backward-looking reference points, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

For most students in this belt the default is June, with November reserved for resits. A November entry as a first sitting makes sense in narrow cases: a student joining mid-course, a subject added late, or one where a single resit would unblock a named post-16 requirement. sections.heading: Eight weeks, six weeks, three weeks
paragraphs: Families ask how many sessions they need. The more useful question is how many weeks remain, because the answer changes what is possible rather than only how much gets done. Three ranges behave quite differently, and being honest about each is the difference between a block that works and a block that disappoints.

Eight weeks will change a paper technique, install the mechanical habits that cost one mark at a time, and rebuild two or three specific topics. It will not cover a syllabus. Six weeks will do the habits and one or two topics, with whole-paper practice in the final fortnight. Three weeks is triage only: whole papers, immediate marking, question-order strategy, and explicit decisions about what will be skipped.

The mechanical habits are the reason short blocks work at all. Method held in a calculator instead of written down. An intermediate value rounded and carried forward. Units omitted. A command term misread, so correct knowledge answered a different question. Each costs one or two marks, each repeats across every question, and together they outweigh a whole missing topic on most papers.

The table sets out what each range should contain, and what it should state up front that it will not attempt. Writing the omissions down is the part that makes a short block honest, and it is also what lets a student follow the plan without the guilt that drives re-reading everything lightly instead of drilling anything properly.

sections.heading: The mock fortnight, and the review nobody runs
paragraphs: Mocks generate more usable information than anything else in the two years, and most of it is discarded within a week. A student receives grades, a parent receives a report, and the scripts — which contain the actual evidence — go into a bag. The review that matters takes roughly ninety minutes per subject and needs no tutor at all.

The method is to sort every lost mark by cause rather than by topic. Content not known. Content known but not retrieved under time. Command term misread. Working not written down. Arithmetic, units or significant figures. Question not attempted. Six categories, one tally per subject, and the largest category names the next block.

The results are frequently surprising and almost always cheaper to act on than the family expected. A student whose largest category is 'question not attempted' does not need more teaching; they need three papers sat to the clock with a rule about when to move on. A student whose largest category is command terms needs fifteen definitions and four weeks of applying them. Only a student whose largest category is genuinely absent content needs a long block.

For DAMAC Hills families the practical note is that this review fits into the half-term break that usually follows mocks, and that it is more valuable than the first two sessions of any tutoring block. Arriving at a first session with the tally already done means the session starts at the plan rather than at the diagnosis, which is worth an hour of anybody's money.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the breaks and the revision calendar
paragraphs: Dubai schools run three terms with a winter break, a spring break and a long summer, and Ramadan moves earlier each year. All of those interrupt revision continuity, and all of them can be used rather than endured. The planning instinct — pause during disruption, resume afterwards — costs more than it saves at IGCSE, because the disrupted periods are also the ones with the most free time in them.

Ramadan shortens the school day and lowers late-afternoon concentration. For online lessons the useful adjustment is to move the slot after Iftar, which produces more work than the same hour in the afternoon and needs no journey rearranged on either side. The period suits mark-scheme review and discussion better than full timed papers, which are worth scheduling either side of it.

The winter break is the best position in the Year 11 calendar for whole-paper practice, because there is no new teaching to keep up with and the days are free. Three papers sat properly across that break, marked and reviewed, changes a mock result in a way that three more hours of content teaching does not.

The spring break sits awkwardly close to the June papers and is usually the point at which triage becomes the only honest plan. Its best use is the explicit decision about what will not be revised, followed by timed practice on what will. Students who spend it attempting full coverage arrive at the series having touched everything and drilled nothing.

sections.heading: What it costs, and how the cost moves with the clock
paragraphs: The published rates in this market are these. Tutopiya advertises online tuition from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both at the university-student end. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate places specialists at AED 200 to 450 and beyond, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home visiting is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors once travel is counted.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages advertised locally include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. All of these are provider-published figures read in October 2026 and none is IB Gram's price list.

What the clock does to those numbers is the point. A four-session block in Year 10 on written-method discipline costs a few hundred dirhams at the qualified band and removes a loss that would otherwise repeat across two years and eight subjects. The same problem addressed in the spring of Year 11, inside a specialist exam-year block at two or three sessions a week, costs several times more and recovers less, because fewer weeks remain to consolidate it.

The expensive pattern is neither of those. It is an unmeasured weekly hour running from Year 10 to Year 11 at mid-band rates with no stated target and no review, which costs more than a foundation block and a triage block combined and tends to produce the same result as neither. Buying few sessions, early, with a written target is the cheapest version of all of this.

sections.heading: The regulator, the permit and the omissions
paragraphs: Who regulates the school your child attends depends on which emirate DAMAC Hills sits in, and that single fact decides which inspection report, fee ruling and subject policy applies to you. DAMAC Hills is Dubai, so the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is your regulator: u.ae describes KHDA as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Cross a border and the answer changes. ADEK covers Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority covers Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities go further than Dubai's and approve fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which is worth knowing if a relocation is on the horizon.

KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year and instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a Year 11 student that means the examined subjects are not the whole timetable, so a revision plan drawn from the entry sheet assumes free hours that do not exist.

Searching for someone nearby turns up people who will drive to a DAMAC Hills villa, and the question to put to each of them is whether they hold a permit. The eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18 - which is to say the Year 13 neighbour tutoring your Year 10 is covered by the same framework as a career teacher. The instrument is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, created by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge and valid for two years, with the application running through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Teaching without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any figure quoted at you as invention.

IB Gram holds no Cambridge, Pearson, International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry of Education approval or accreditation, claims none, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. Board timetables, specifications, mark schemes and examiner reports are linked at source rather than reproduced. No future examination date is stated as fact on this page, because a page that dates itself to one year is wrong the next with nobody having edited it.

process.title: Find out when entries close
process.description: The single most useful question a Year 10 parent can ask the school, because the entry fixes board, subject and tier for the series and sets the grade ceiling. Everything a tutoring block can do afterwards happens inside that ceiling.

process.title: Run the mock tally before the first session
process.description: Sort every lost mark on the mock scripts into six categories: content not known, not retrieved under time, command term misread, working not shown, arithmetic and units, question not attempted. The largest category names the block, and doing it yourself saves the first session.

process.title: Agree the hour, then the specialist
process.description: In DAMAC Hills the realistic start is 5.30pm or a weekend morning. Agreeing that before matching avoids a term that loses four sessions to a slot nobody can keep, which is the most common quiet failure of tutoring in this part of Dubailand.

process.title: State the omissions in writing
process.description: Any block with fewer than eight weeks says what it will not attempt. Written down, the omissions let a student follow the plan without guilt; left unstated, guilt drives light re-reading of everything instead of drilling the marks that remain reachable.

process.title: Review at four sessions
process.description: The target is measured on a comparable timed paper under the same conditions. If it has not moved, the diagnosis, the tutor or the frequency changes at no cost. At IGCSE that comparison is unusually clean, which makes the review easy to run honestly.

whyPoints.title: Planned on the two-year clock
whyPoints.description: Six terms, each with a job, and only two of them able to rebuild a genuine gap without competing with revision. Most IGCSE tutoring is bought in the term where the fewest options remain, and naming the clock is the cheapest intervention on this page.

whyPoints.title: The entry deadline treated as the key date
whyPoints.description: A Core or Foundation entry caps the grade available for the series, and the entry closes months before the papers. A tiering conversation with evidence, held while entries are open, changes more than any number of sessions bought afterwards can.

whyPoints.title: Board dates quoted from the boards
whyPoints.description: Cambridge's June and November series, the six administrative zones, and Pearson's May/June and November windows are stated from the boards' own pages, with past results dates kept as citations. The India-only February/March series is excluded rather than mentioned as an option.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what each window can do
whyPoints.description: Eight weeks moves technique and two or three topics; three weeks is triage. Saying so costs bookings occasionally, and the alternative is taking money for work that cannot succeed in the time available, which is the common failure in this market.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around the commute
whyPoints.description: Secondary students here are usually home after five, so sessions run from 5.30pm or on a weekend morning, in two shorter blocks rather than one long one. Online delivery is what makes that pattern choosable instead of dictated by a tutor's driving route.

whyPoints.title: Rates shown against the clock
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure names its source and the month it was read, and the cost table is arranged by when a family starts rather than by tier. The same improvement bought in Year 10 costs a fraction of what it costs in the spring of Year 11.

faqs.question: When is the best term to start IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: The first or second term of Year 10, if the problem is foundations, because that is the only part of the course where algebraic fluency or written explanation can be rebuilt without taking time from revision. If the problem is technique, the term before the mock window is the best value, since mocks inform predicted grades as well as diagnosis. The spring of Year 11 is when most families start and when the fewest options remain available.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE tutor travel to DAMAC Hills?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors do, at published market rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is counted. IB Gram does not: all UAE lessons are delivered live online, one to one, over video in Gulf Standard Time, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. In this community the online format also protects the clock, since the student has already made two journeys and a 5.30pm session starts at 5.30pm rather than whenever the traffic allows.

faqs.question: Which date actually decides my child's grade ceiling?
faqs.answer: The final entry deadline, which the school works to months before the papers. It fixes the board, the subject and, where a Cambridge syllabus is tiered, the tier. A Core entry caps the grades available however well the student performs in June. Ask the school when entries close, in Year 10 rather than Year 11, because a tiering conversation held before that date is a decision and one held afterwards is a complaint.

faqs.question: How do I run the mock review myself?
faqs.answer: Take the marked scripts and sort every lost mark into six categories: content not known, content known but not retrieved under time, command term misread, working not written down, arithmetic or units, and question not attempted. Tally them per subject. It takes about ninety minutes a subject and the largest category tells you what the next block should be. Arriving at a first tutoring session with that tally already done saves an hour of paid diagnosis.

faqs.question: Can three weeks of tutoring change an IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: It can recover marks, and it should be sold on that basis rather than on a grade. Three weeks is triage: whole papers sat to time, marked immediately, question-order strategy decided, and explicit decisions about content that will not be revisited. What it cannot do is teach anything substantial that is new. A provider accepting a three-week booking to cover a syllabus has made a commercial decision rather than an educational one.

faqs.question: Is a November entry worth considering instead of June?
faqs.answer: For most students in this belt, no: June is the main series and November is the resit route. A November first sitting makes sense in narrow cases — a student joining mid-course, a subject added late, or one resit that would unblock a named post-16 requirement. The cost is that a November entry competes with the first term of a new programme, which is usually more expensive than the grade improvement is worth.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge warn about timetable zones?
faqs.answer: Because every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with its own version of the timetable, and Cambridge states that using the correct version is essential, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. The practical risk is real: a timetable found through a search is not necessarily the one your school's centre is working to. Ask the school which zone it sits in and work from that document.

faqs.question: Should revision pause during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: No, but it should change shape. School days shorten and late-afternoon concentration drops, so moving an online session after Iftar produces more work than the same hour at four o'clock, with no journey to rearrange on either side. The period suits mark-scheme review and discussion better than full timed papers, which are worth scheduling either side of it. Pausing entirely wastes free time that the rest of the term does not contain.

faqs.question: How should the winter break of Year 11 be used?
faqs.answer: For whole papers, sat properly and marked. There is no new teaching to keep up with and the days are free, which makes it the best position in the Year 11 calendar for timed practice. Three complete papers across the break, each marked against the official scheme with the losses categorised, changes a mock result in a way that three more hours of content teaching does not. Most families use it for recovery and then regret it in February.

faqs.question: What does starting early actually save in money terms?
faqs.answer: A four to six session block in Year 9 or early Year 10 at the qualified band, published from AED 150 an hour by Unitors, addresses a skill that otherwise repeats as lost marks across eight subjects for two years. The same problem met in the spring of Year 11 needs a specialist exam-year block, which Bestimate's table puts at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month, and recovers less because fewer weeks remain to consolidate it.

faqs.question: My child has eight subjects. Should we tutor all of them?
faqs.answer: Almost never. Look for the shared cause first: if the same rearrangement or the same command-term error is costing marks in four subjects, one block fixes four papers. After that, buy the single weakest subject where a grade actually matters for a post-16 intention. Eight tutors is unmanageable, unreviewable and more expensive than the school fees in some cases, and nobody reviews eight blocks honestly.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week suit a student home after five?
faqs.answer: Two shorter sessions rather than one long one, for most students here. Sixty minutes twice a week at 5.30pm produces more than ninety minutes once, because concentration rather than teaching time is the limit after a commute from Al Barsha or the Ranches. The most resilient pattern in this community is one weekday evening plus a weekend morning, with the longer weekend slot used for whole papers.

faqs.question: What happens to the plan after results in August?
faqs.answer: It becomes a decision rather than a block. Sort the result against the post-16 requirement: if a named grade is blocked and the loss was specific — a component, a tier ceiling, one topic — a November resit in that single subject is reasonable. If the subject is not required for the next programme, a resit competes with the first term of a demanding course. Pearson's published pattern has November results reaching students in January.

faqs.question: Does the school report tell me which block to buy?
faqs.answer: No. A report gives a grade and a comment, and neither says which component produced the grade or why marks were withheld. The marked script does. A student can hold the same grade with strong content and poor timing, or the reverse, and those need opposite blocks. Sending a marked script rather than a report is the single most useful thing a parent can do when making an enquiry at any point on the clock.

intro.heading: Two clocks decide whether IGCSE tutoring works out here
paragraphs: The first clock is the daily one. DAMAC Hills 2 sits out along the Al Qudra corridor, and almost every secondary student in the community is driven to a school somewhere else — Motor City, Dubai Sports City, deeper into Dubailand, sometimes further. A day ending at half three becomes a 4:30pm arrival home once the afternoon traffic on Hessa Street and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road is counted. Whatever happens next has to happen in a tired hour, and a tutor who still has to drive out here makes that hour later still.

The second clock is the one families notice too late. IGCSE is a twenty-four month qualification. Year 10 September to results day in August of Year 11 is the whole window, and most of what decides the grade happens in the first half of it — tier decisions, the topics that go past too fast, the habit of showing method or not showing it. By the time a mock result arrives in the middle of Year 11, roughly eighteen of those twenty-four months are spent.

Most tutoring in Dubai is bought on the second clock reading eighteen. A family searches after a disappointing mock, hires whoever can start quickly, and asks for a grade to move in a term. Sometimes that works, when the content is present and the output is poor. Often it does not, because what was actually missing was a year of algebra or a term of chemistry that nobody noticed going.

IB Gram's answer to the first clock is to remove travel from it. Lessons for DAMAC Hills 2 families are one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, and we make no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. A session can therefore start at 4:30pm, while your child is still awake enough for it to stick, instead of at half six when a visiting tutor has cleared the traffic.

Our answer to the second clock is to ask what year group your child is in before anything else, and to plan differently for Year 10 than for February of Year 11. UK-curriculum schools account for 37% of Dubai's private enrolment, the largest single bloc of the 387,441 pupils KHDA reported across 227 schools in 2024-25, so there is no shortage of general IGCSE tutoring available. There is a shortage of plans that start early enough to be ordinary rather than urgent.

One practical note before the detail. Ask the school office for the exam board and syllabus code of every subject, because Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel set different papers and tier differently, and schools here routinely use both across different departments. A tutor who cannot say immediately which specification they teach is guessing, and a term of the wrong board past papers trains the wrong instincts about what a question is asking for.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-damac-hills.programmesIntro: What stage your child is at changes the whole shape of the help. These are the stages we cover around IGCSE for DAMAC Hills 2 families and what each one actually needs.

programmes.name: Year 9, the year before it counts
programmes.description: The year option choices are made and tier placement begins to be decided by class performance. Nothing is examined externally, which is exactly why it is undervalued: algebraic fluency, scientific explanation and extended writing are all cheaper to fix here than they will ever be again. Reports are internal and tell a parent little about readiness for an Extended-tier paper.
programmes.countryNote: In DAMAC Hills 2 this is the commonest point of arrival from another system, and a child moving in from CBSE, an American school or a different UK school meets a new topic order halfway through. We diagnose on Year 9 material rather than trusting a report grade, because the report may be measuring a syllabus the child only met in March.

programmes.name: Year 10, where the grade is decided
programmes.description: The first of the two examined years. Most of the syllabus content is taught here, tier decisions are confirmed, and the habits that produce or lose method marks are set. A student who ends Year 10 secure in each subject's foundations is in a completely different position from one who ends it a term behind in two of them.
programmes.countryNote: This is the year DAMAC Hills 2 families most often skip and most often regret skipping. One session a week through Year 10 is ordinary, unurgent and considerably cheaper than the three-sessions-a-week rescue it prevents. It is also the only point at which a tier change is still realistic.

programmes.name: Year 11 and the examined series
programmes.description: Mocks, then entries, then the series. The work shifts from learning content to producing marks: timing, command terms, showing method, reading a question for what it actually asks. Grades arrive as 9-1 or A*-G depending on subject and board, and both scales appear on UAE school reports side by side.
programmes.countryNote: By February of Year 11 the honest conversation narrows. Some subjects can move a grade with focused work on technique; others need a November entry instead of a June one. We would rather have that conversation than sell a family sessions in six subjects when three of them cannot realistically move.

programmes.name: What the grades open up
programmes.description: Most UAE British-curriculum schools split after Year 11 into A Levels or the IB Diploma, and IGCSE grades are the gate. A maths-heavy A Level or Higher Level Diploma course expects a strong Extended-tier or high-grade maths result, and the sciences expect the equivalent in theirs.
programmes.countryNote: DAMAC Hills 2 families usually have both routes within a reachable commute, which makes the Year 11 grade more consequential here than in a community with one option. It is worth deciding at the start of Year 10 which doors you intend to keep open, because tier placement closes some of them quietly.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-damac-hills.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects DAMAC Hills 2 students most commonly need, with the board codes to check and the specific place marks go. Coverage is confirmed at the trial lesson rather than promised in advance.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Non-calculator fluency and multi-step unstructured problems are where the marks go. Method marks are routinely lost by students who can reach a right answer but write nothing down. Tier matters more here than in any other subject because the grade ceiling differs.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Precise definitions, units carried through every step, and the ability to rearrange a formula under pressure. Electricity, waves and energy transfer recur as weak topics. Where the school enters the Alternative to Practical route, that paper needs its own preparation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry are the wall almost every student hits. Balancing equations is not the same skill as converting between mass, moles and volume against a clock. Qualitative analysis and the required ion tests are heavily examined and quick to fix once named.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Recall volume plus command-term precision. Describe, explain and suggest want different answers, and a knowledgeable student writing the wrong one scores low. Experimental design and data-interpretation questions respond well to structured weekly practice.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response carry the weight, and both are won on structure and register rather than vocabulary. Reading questions reward precise textual reference against the mark scheme; retelling the passage scores almost nothing.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A common route for students newer to English in Dubai schools, assessed across reading, writing and listening with speaking in some variants. Progress is measurable and fast with targeted work because the component skills are discrete rather than diffuse.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagrams must be drawn and then used in the answer. Data-response questions reward applying a concept to the stimulus and reaching a judgement; definitions alone plateau at the lower bands. Memorising terminology is the commonest wasted revision strategy here.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: The theory paper tests data representation, logic and networks at least as much as code, and students comfortable at a keyboard often lose marks hand-tracing algorithms or writing pseudocode to convention. The practical component needs documented evidence, not just working output.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: A bridge to A Level or Higher Level Diploma maths, taken by stronger sets. Calculus and trigonometric identities arrive early, and any residual algebraic weakness is exposed immediately. The most frequent bridging request we receive from this corridor.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: Cambridge first and additional language routes
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Support has to match the stream the student actually sits.

sections.heading: The twenty-four months from Year 10 to results day
paragraphs: Nobody publishes this, and it is the most useful thing a Year 9 or Year 10 parent in DAMAC Hills 2 can read. IGCSE is not an exam you prepare for in the spring of Year 11. It is a two-year programme in which the content is largely delivered in the first year and the marks are produced in the second, and the decisions with the longest consequences are taken earliest.

Walk it forwards. September of Year 10: options settled, tiers provisionally set, content begins. Through Year 10: most of the syllabus taught, and the point at which a tier change is still realistic because it only requires covering extra content rather than cramming it. Summer between the years: the only unpressured block available, and the cheapest place to fix a foundation gap. Autumn of Year 11: remaining content, then mocks.

Then it accelerates. Mock results, usually mid Year 11, are the first external-feeling signal most families get. Entries are confirmed by the centre months before the papers. The June series runs, results arrive in August, and a November entry becomes the route for anything that did not land. Read backwards from results day and you can see that by the time a mock disappoints, about three quarters of the window has gone.

The table maps that out with what should already be done at each point. Use it to work out which row you are in, because the honest plan for a family in the second row and one in the sixth are not the same plan at all.

sections.heading: Where the usable hours are in a DAMAC Hills 2 week
paragraphs: Scheduling kills more tutoring arrangements than teaching does. A family agrees a time that works in September, then football moves to Tuesdays, a coursework deadline lands in November, and by February the sessions have quietly stopped without anyone deciding to stop them. Choosing the slot properly at the start is worth more than any amount of rescuing later.

Out here there are four real windows. Straight off the school run, between 4:15pm and 5:30pm, which only exists because nobody is driving to you. After dinner from seven, which competes with the student's own best independent hour. Late, from eight, which Year 11 students use well and younger students cannot. And weekend mornings, which are the most reliable and the least booked.

Which window to pick depends on age and on how many children are in the car. A Year 9 or Year 10 student usually does best straight after the run, while the day is still fresh enough to take new teaching. A Year 11 student in exam term often prefers the late slot and a longer session, because a full past-paper section plus marking does not fit comfortably into sixty minutes. A household running three school runs frequently finds that weekend mornings are the only honest answer, and we would rather say that than agree a weekday slot destined to collapse.
The table sets the four windows against what work each actually supports. Decide it with your child present; they know which hour they can think in better than either of us does.

sections.heading: What a Dubai school report does not tell you
paragraphs: A UK-curriculum report in Dubai typically gives a current working grade, a target grade, an effort score and a comment. Each of those is less informative than it looks, and families act on them anyway because there is nothing else to act on.

The working grade is the biggest trap, because it is usually a teacher's judgement against the tier the student is currently entered for. A 6 on Core and a 6 on Extended are not the same achievement, and the report rarely says which. Nor does it usually say what the tier caps at. A parent reading a steady run of 6s can reasonably assume things are fine and discover in Year 11 that the ceiling was below what the intended A Level course requires.

Grading scales add more confusion. Depending on subject and board, UAE reports carry 9-1 and A*-G side by side, sometimes in the same document, and the two do not map neatly. The effort score, meanwhile, measures compliance and is often the only column parents read closely, which is understandable and almost never diagnostic.

What is genuinely diagnostic is a marked past paper from the correct board at the correct tier. That is why our process starts with one rather than with the report. Twenty minutes of watching a student work through real questions tells a specialist more than a term of grades: whether method is being shown, whether command terms are being read, whether the failure is knowledge or timing or technique.

sections.heading: The June series, the November route, and the series that does not apply here
paragraphs: Start with the correction, because it circulates among UAE parents constantly. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. If anyone has told you a March resit is available, they are describing another country's provision, and planning around it costs a term.

Cambridge runs its International GCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school which zone it sits in rather than downloading a timetable from a search result.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For the actual timing of a November route: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November results reach students in January — the November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well in advance, so always work from the live official PDF rather than a date restated on any tutoring site.

For a DAMAC Hills 2 family the practical consequence is that a disappointing June is not a lost year. It is a November entry in the subjects worth re-entering, a focused block over the summer and first term, and a result in January in time to update post-16 applications. That is a plan, and it beats the scramble that usually follows results day.

sections.heading: Is the tutor you hire permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tuition here is a permitted activity rather than an unregulated one, and the silence about that mostly benefits people operating without a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Eligibility is broader than most families assume: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. So a university student tutoring your Year 10 child can hold a valid permit. The question is only whether they do. MoHRE states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, and Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify amounts, so disregard any number circulating informally.

One boundary catches well-meaning families. The permit's code of conduct bars a tutor from serving students affiliated with their own school, and press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes the same prohibition for Abu Dhabi school staff. If a provider offers your child's own classroom teacher privately, that tells you something about the provider.

An individual needs the MoHRE permit; an organisation running tutoring from premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership and claims none.

sections.heading: Five subjects at grade E, and the two that do not count
paragraphs: If a UAE university or an attested certificate is anywhere in the plan, the Ministry of Education's equivalency rules change which grades matter. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The catch is which five. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. Both are mandatory in Dubai private schools — KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the licensed curriculum, with its current arrangements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year — and neither counts towards the equivalency five. A student with five passes of which two are Arabic and Islamic education does not have five for this purpose.

For comparison, the American track requires English proficiency of IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT 450 in reading and writing, plus at least SAT Math 450. For the IB, no points threshold has been verified from an official Ministry source, so we publish none and you should ask anyone who quotes you one where they read it. One competitor page currently ranking for UAE IGCSE queries states that six subjects are required, which is not what the published rule says.

IB Gram does not perform, process or guarantee equivalency or attestation. It is a Ministry process and the Ministry is the only authority on it. What tutoring can do is make sure the five subjects a plan relies on are the five that will actually be passed.

sections.heading: What we do not claim
paragraphs: Some things are absent from this page deliberately, and their presence elsewhere is worth noticing. The list is short, and each item on it is something a competing page in this search result does carry.

No star rating, no satisfaction percentage, no average grade achieved by students we have taught. Competitors publish figures like 4.9 from several hundred reviews, occasionally two conflicting versions in the same document, and none states a sample size, a date or a method. A statistic without those three is decoration, and we would rather publish none than publish decoration.

No regulator claim. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation, licence or partnership, has no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE, and will not send a tutor to a DAMAC Hills 2 address. No past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents or grade-boundary tables are offered as downloads either; those belong to the awarding bodies, and we cite and link them instead.

And no guarantee of a grade or an improvement. Nobody can honestly offer one, the offer itself tells you what kind of operation is making it, and in a market where several ranking pages do offer one, declining to is information. What we will do is diagnose honestly, say which subjects can realistically move in the time available, and tell you when the answer is a November entry rather than more sessions. We also publish no specific IB or Cambridge exam date here beyond the series names, because dates get revised and the awarding body timetable is the only version worth acting on.

faqs.question: When should a DAMAC Hills 2 family start IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 10, if the aim is a grade rather than a rescue. IGCSE is a twenty-four month programme: most content is taught in Year 10, tier decisions are confirmed there, and the habits that win or lose method marks are set there. One unurgent session a week through Year 10 costs considerably less than the three-a-week block it prevents in Year 11. By the time a mock result arrives mid Year 11, about three quarters of the window has already been spent, and some options are no longer available.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE session start after the school run out here?
faqs.answer: For a short run — Jebel Ali School in DAMAC Hills or South View in Remraam — around 4:00pm to 4:15pm. From GEMS Metropole in Motor City or the Dubai Sports City cluster in peak traffic, 4:45pm is realistic. From an inner-city school, closer to 5:15pm, and many of those families use an 8pm slot instead. These times are only possible because nobody is driving to you; a visiting tutor leaving another part of Dubai in the same traffic is realistically starting at half six.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tutor actually living near DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: Some, and for general Year 9 support the local pool is adequate. It thins once you require the correct board and the correct tier for a Year 11 subject. Dubai's tutor supply clusters around the older school corridors rather than the newer Dubailand communities, so a tutor prepared to drive out along Al Qudra Road on a school night is a small subset, and a smaller one again after filtering for Pearson 4MA1 versus Cambridge 0580. Online matching removes the filter that was never relevant to the grade.

faqs.question: Which weekly window works best for a Year 11 student in this community?
faqs.answer: Usually the late one, 8pm to 9:30pm, and usually ninety minutes rather than sixty, because a full past-paper section plus marking does not fit comfortably into an hour. Year 11 students in exam term are often sharpest once the house is quiet. The 4:15pm window suits Years 9 and 10 better, while attention is still fresh enough for new teaching. The 7pm slot looks convenient but consumes the student's own most productive independent hour, which is a poor trade in an examined year.

faqs.question: Can my child resit IGCSE in the February or March series?
faqs.answer: Not in the UAE. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, and UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The belief circulates widely here and acting on it costs a term, so it is worth checking with your school directly. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. A disappointing June result therefore means a November entry in the subjects worth re-entering, a focused block over the summer and first term, and a result in January.

faqs.question: What does my child's working grade on the school report actually mean?
faqs.answer: Less than it appears, because it is usually a judgement against the tier currently entered, and the report rarely states the tier or its ceiling. A 6 on Cambridge Core and a 6 on Extended are different achievements. UAE reports also carry 9-1 and A*-G side by side depending on subject and board, and the two scales do not map neatly. Effort scores measure compliance rather than readiness. The reliable diagnostic is a marked past paper from the correct board at the correct tier, which is where our process starts.

faqs.question: How much should a DAMAC Hills 2 family budget per month for IGCSE help?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Dubai research puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240-600 a month for budget tutoring, AED 600-1,200 for mid-tier and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Advertised packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four in-home two-hour visits. Those figures belong to the providers who published them, read in October 2026, and none is an IB Gram price. We quote after the free trial, because subject, board and year group all change the answer.

faqs.question: Does the in-home travel premium buy anything useful in Year 11?
faqs.answer: For most Year 11 students, not much. In-home visits are published at AED 180-500 an hour including travel, and from the Al Qudra corridor a meaningful share of that is the drive. What it buys is physical presence — genuinely valuable for a younger or less self-managing student, where someone can take a phone off the table. For a Year 11 candidate working through correct-board past papers, the thing that moves the grade is whether the tutor knows the specification, and that is not correlated with how close they live.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should a Year 11 student take tutoring in?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families start with. Three sessions a week across five subjects in Year 11 produces shallow coverage of all of them and a student too tired to use any of it. We would rather diagnose, name the two or three subjects where a grade can realistically move in the time available, concentrate there, and tell you plainly that the others are better served by a November entry or by the student's own revision. That conversation is unpopular and it is the honest one.

faqs.question: Do we need a licensed tutor, and how would we check?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you ask. Any individual charging for private tuition in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE listing a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website or e-services. Eligibility covers school and sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Request the permit and verify it with MoHRE. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no amounts are published.

faqs.answer: On the Al Qudra side: Jebel Ali School in neighbouring DAMAC Hills, South View School in Remraam, The Aquila School, Ranches Primary School, JESS Arabian Ranches and Fairgreen International School. Further in: GEMS Metropole in Motor City, the Dubai Sports City cluster including Victory Heights Primary and GEMS United, Safa Community School, Dubai Heights Academy and Dunecrest American School. faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects count towards UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five, at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus either one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade for the British track. Note which five, though: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five, even though both are mandatory in Dubai private schools under KHDA requirements. So five passes including those two is not five for equivalency purposes. One ranking competitor states six subjects are required; that is not the published rule. Verify on moe.gov.ae — IB Gram does not process equivalency.

faqs.question: How do IGCSE sessions change during Ramadan here?
faqs.answer: They move, and planning the move beats improvising it. School days shorten and evenings reorganise around Iftar, so the usual six o'clock slot stops working. DAMAC Hills 2 families typically switch to a late-morning or early-afternoon session, move to a post-Iftar slot, or pause part of the month and resume with a heavier block. Content also shifts towards consolidation rather than new teaching. Tell us the pattern that suits and we reset the fixed slot deliberately rather than letting a run of cancellations end the arrangement by default.

faqs.question: Can we book a short block for one subject rather than a term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a capable student with one specific gap it is usually the right purchase. Moles in Chemistry, electricity in Physics, algebraic fractions in maths: we agree a topic list as the scope, run six to ten sessions, review honestly and stop. There is no automatic rollover into open-ended tutoring unless you ask for it. The same shape works well for a November resit entry, where the brief is narrow and the endpoint is a specific paper rather than a general improvement.

faqs.question: What if the DAMAC Hills 2 trial lesson does not go well?
faqs.answer: Nothing has been spent and we propose somebody else. A mismatch between a capable tutor and a particular student is common and is not a failure on either side, because pace, explanation style and personality matter more than credentials once basic competence is established. If it only becomes clear two or three sessions in, tell us within the first fortnight and we rematch. What not to do is spend a term hoping, which in an examined year costs the money and the term together.

intro.heading: Four neighbourhoods, one answer
paragraphs: Deira is Dubai's oldest district: apartment blocks, souqs, two Metro lines and a school-age population that travels outward every morning. Al Qusais, a few minutes east, has the highest concentration of large private schools near Deira. Bur Dubai and Oud Metha, across the Creek, carry several of the city's longest-established schools. Mirdif, out to the east, is villas and low-rise with its own small cluster. A parent in any of the four types the same search, and the honest finding is that the right answer is identical in all of them, for reasons worth setting out rather than asserting.

Start with what actually differs. School density differs: Al Qusais has more IGCSE provision per square kilometre than anywhere else in this comparison, Deira has fewer schools than its population would suggest, Mirdif has a small local cluster, and Bur Dubai sits in between. Housing differs sharply: Deira and Bur Dubai are apartment districts where a quiet room at 5pm is not guaranteed, while Mirdif is largely villas with space to work. Commute differs: a Deira child schooling in Al Qusais crosses the airport road at its worst, a Mirdif child schooling locally is home in fifteen minutes.

Now what does not differ. The syllabus is identical — Cambridge 0580 is 0580 in every one of these neighbourhoods. The tier decision is made by the school on earlier attainment, not by the postcode. The mark scheme is the same, the series is the same, the entry deadline is the same. And the supply of tutors who have actually marked against a given specification is thin in all four areas, because IGCSE specialist supply in Dubai is a city-wide shortage rather than a local one, with the UK curriculum accounting for 37 per cent of enrolment across 227 private schools and specialist tutors distributed unevenly across all of it.

That asymmetry produces the conclusion. The things that differ between these neighbourhoods are logistics, and logistics are solved by removing the journey. The things that do not differ are the syllabus, the mark scheme and the specialist shortage, and those are solved by widening the pool. Both point the same way. IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition online, one-to-one, over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India.

The rest of this page is comparisons rather than claims. Neighbourhood against neighbourhood. One-to-one online against in-home, group class and the school's own free clinics. The cost of the same subject in each area under each model. Five questions that reliably separate a specialist from a generalist, with the weak and strong answers written out. The two boards compared without changing school. And the two Ministry of Education equivalency tracks side by side, because that is the comparison families make last and should make first.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-deira.subjectsIntro: The subject list is the same in every neighbourhood on this page, which is part of the argument. What changes between areas is which boards the local schools use, so the syllabus code matters more than the postcode.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Tiered in both boards, with the tier setting the grade ceiling. Comparing the two specifications, the content overlaps heavily while paper count and tiering language differ, so past-paper practice must match the entry. The grade gates more post-16 options than any other IGCSE result.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and forces dominate. The two boards differ in how practical skills are assessed, which is the first thing to establish before buying revision material. Calculation layout — formula, substitution, answer with unit — earns marks that content knowledge alone does not.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic chemistry separate a 6 from an 8 in both specifications. The practical or alternative-to-practical component rewards precise language about apparatus and error, and the question types repeat across series, which makes it unusually learnable.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume rather than conceptual difficulty, and therefore the most improvable subject in a short block. Marks go missing when a student writes fluently without using the specific term the mark scheme requires, which is a drilling problem rather than an understanding one.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.description: All three sciences in one or two awards, far more common in the large-roll Al Qusais schools than in the smaller clusters. The content is narrower than the separate sciences, so revising from separate-science material wastes weeks on topics that will not be examined.

subjects.name: English First Language
subjects.description: Reading analysis carries most of the marks and improves through frequent short marked pieces. Comparing it with English as a Second Language, the two are separate qualifications with separate mark schemes, and the entry decision belongs in Year 10.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Its own specification with a speaking component in some variants. Students in the larger Deira and Al Qusais schools are sometimes entered here when First Language was achievable, which is worth comparing explicitly with the school before entries close.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and justified judgement carry the marks rather than content volume, which makes these the subjects most responsive to a short focused block near the series. Widely offered across all four neighbourhoods compared here.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Two different subjects that families regularly confuse. ICT carries substantial practical coursework running in specific weeks; Computer Science is theory and pseudocode with a steadier rhythm. Confirm which is on the timetable before comparing tutors.

subjects.name: Arabic and modern foreign languages
subjects.description: Speaking components are often assessed weeks or months before the written papers in every school in this comparison. Ask for the oral date explicitly, since it needs its own preparation schedule regardless of which neighbourhood you are in.
