sections.heading: Deira against Al Qusais, Bur Dubai and Mirdif
paragraphs: This is the comparison a parent is implicitly making when they add a neighbourhood to a search, so here it is explicitly. The four areas differ on four things that matter — school density, housing type, commute and local tutor supply — and the table sets them against each other on all four.

Al Qusais wins on school density by a wide margin and loses on commute, because its dismissal times are early but its roads carry the airport traffic. Mirdif wins on study space, because villa housing gives a student a desk and a door, and loses on choice of nearby school. Deira and Bur Dubai are similar to each other: apartment housing, outward commutes, and the specific problem of finding a quiet hour in a full flat. None of the four has a meaningful advantage in local specialist tutor supply, which is the variable most parents assume the postcode controls.

That last point deserves evidence rather than assertion. Dubai had 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum accounting for 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian 26 per cent, American 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate 7 per cent. Specialist IGCSE tutors — people who have marked against a named specification rather than taught the subject generally — are distributed across that whole market thinly and unevenly, and they cluster around where they live rather than where demand is. No neighbourhood in this comparison has enough of them to cover eight to ten subjects across two boards.

So the comparison produces a split verdict. On logistics, the areas genuinely differ and the differences are worth planning around. On access to the right tutor, they are equally constrained, and no amount of moving the search radius fixes it.

sections.heading: Why the answer comes out the same in all four
paragraphs: Comparisons are only useful if they change a decision, so it is worth being clear about why this one does not. The differences between these neighbourhoods are differences in getting to a lesson. The similarities are similarities in what the lesson has to contain. When the differences are all logistical and the similarities are all substantive, the logistics are the part you should remove.

Take the two halves separately. On logistics, Deira's problem is a quiet hour, Al Qusais's is the return journey, Bur Dubai's is both, and Mirdif's is distance from everything else. Every one of those is solved by a session that does not require a tutor to arrive at a fixed time, because the slot can then be set to whenever the student is actually available in a quiet room. A visiting tutor's weekly arrival is the single constraint that none of these neighbourhoods can accommodate well.

On substance, all four need the same thing: somebody who has marked against the exact specification on the entry form. Cambridge 0580 is 0580 in Mirdif and in Deira. The tier is set by the school on attainment. The June series is the June series. The mark scheme does not vary by district. And the person who can diagnose why a student loses four marks on every six-mark explanation question is scarce in all four areas equally.

Put those together and the recommendation is identical regardless of which of the four you live in: remove the journey, widen the pool, and match on the syllabus code. That is not a sales argument dressed as analysis; it is what the comparison actually yields, and if the opposite were true — if one of these areas had deep local specialist supply — this page would say so.

sections.heading: Four ways to buy IGCSE help, compared
paragraphs: Most providers compare themselves against an unnamed set of alternatives, which tells a parent nothing useful. The honest comparison is between models, because the model determines both what you pay and what you can expect, and because two of the four options cost nothing and are routinely ignored.

School clinics are first in this comparison for a reason. Dubai secondaries run subject clinics, examination-technique sessions and catch-up classes free of charge, taught by the people who set and mark the mocks, which gives them an information advantage no external tutor has. They are under-attended because they are communicated to students rather than parents. A group class at a tuition centre — concentrated in Al Qusais and Al Nahda — is the next cheapest, and a small group with a tutor who knows the specification beats a one-to-one hour with a generalist.

One-to-one in-home is the most expensive and buys the least incremental teaching, because what the premium of roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour purchases is proximity. One-to-one online sits in the middle on price and at the top on match quality, because the pool is the whole market rather than the drivable subset. The thing none of the free or group options can do is diagnose one student's specific mark-losing behaviour, which is what the paid one-to-one hour exists for.

The sensible sequence, then, is not to choose one model but to layer them: free clinics for content, a group class if structure is missing, and a single one-to-one session for diagnosis and the fix. Families who do this spend less than families who buy three weekly one-to-one sessions, and get more.

sections.heading: What the same subject costs in each area and model
paragraphs: Prices do not vary much by neighbourhood in Dubai, which is itself a finding worth publishing: a tutor's rate tracks their specialism and their travel, not the affluence of the district. What does vary is the travel component, and in this comparison that is the whole difference between the areas.

The published bands, read in October 2026 and attributed. Online budget generalists advertise from AED 33 to 52 an hour at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists are quoted AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table in the same range. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the named or examiner-level end. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500. Monthly packages advertised in Dubai run near AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Layer the geography on and the pattern is simple. A visiting tutor serving Mirdif from the centre, or Deira from the Jumeirah side, prices a longer journey into the hour; one working within Al Qusais or Hor Al Anz prices a shorter one. Group classes are cheapest where centres cluster, which is Al Qusais. Online rates are identical everywhere, because there is no journey to price. That last row is the only one in the table that does not move between neighbourhoods, which is the comparison's punchline.

These are market figures rather than IB Gram's prices. We quote after a free trial lesson, one per subject before any payment, against a written plan with a term total, because a post-mock repair block and a thirty-week Mathematics plan should not share a rate card.

sections.heading: Five questions that compare two tutors properly
paragraphs: Parents are asked to judge expertise they do not have, in a market where everybody's profile says the same things. These five questions solve that, because they probe structure rather than content and the answers are audibly different without any subject knowledge on your side.

Ask them during the free trial rather than on the phone, where anybody can sound convincing, and write the answers down so two candidates a week apart can be compared honestly. The fifth question is the one that decides it: ask the tutor to mark one page of your child's most recent written work out loud, saying what each annotation is worth and why. A specialist does this comfortably, names command terms and mark-scheme language, and finishes by identifying one behaviour to change. A generalist corrects spelling, says it looks fine and suggests more practice.

A good tutor is usually pleased to be asked, because it is the first time anyone has treated their expertise as a thing with content rather than a set of adjectives. A tutor who deflects all five has answered the question in a different way.

One addition specific to this comparison: ask which board and specification they have taught. The answer should be a code — 0580, 4MA1, 0654 — not a subject name. A tutor who cannot name the specification cannot select the right past papers, and past-paper work is most of what you are paying for. Run the same five questions on two candidates and the gap between them is usually obvious within a minute of the fifth, which is a better use of an hour than reading twenty profiles.

sections.heading: Comparing the two boards without changing school
paragraphs: A family cannot usually choose their board, since the school chooses it, but they can and should know which one they have, because it changes what revision is useful. This is the comparison most parents have never been offered.

Cambridge subjects carry four-digit codes and several use Core and Extended tiers; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses the 4-series with Foundation and Higher in Mathematics. Content overlaps substantially. Paper count, paper length and the route by which practical skills are assessed do not, and several Pearson subjects concentrate the assessment into fewer, longer papers, which changes how a student should pace themselves. A student drilling the wrong board's papers is practising a question type they will not meet.

The calendars differ too. Cambridge runs June and November for UAE candidates, allocating each centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson runs May/June and November; its November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. One point that applies to every neighbourhood in this comparison: Cambridge's February and March series is for India only, so any UAE plan built around a February sitting is wrong.

The action is a two-minute one. Ask the school for every subject's exact syllabus code, write them on a single sheet, and give that sheet to any tutor before the first session. It is the cheapest quality control available to a parent in any of these four areas.

sections.heading: What a Deira address does and does not change
paragraphs: Having run the comparisons, it is worth separating the things about living in Deira that genuinely affect a tutoring decision from the things that merely feel like they should.

What it changes. Study space: in dense apartment housing the quiet hour moves day to day, which argues for weekend mornings and holiday blocks rather than a fixed weekday evening. Transport: both Metro lines run through the district, so an older student can reach a library or a school study room independently, which is a genuine advantage over the villa suburbs. Commute: most secondary students travel outward, so arrival home is late and variable, and sessions must be set from arrival rather than dismissal. Cost sensitivity: households here are generally more price-conscious than in the newer communities, which makes the free-provision-first sequence more valuable, not less.

What it does not change. The syllabus, the tier, the mark scheme, the series, the entry deadline, the equivalency rules and the scarcity of specialist tutors. None of those have a postcode. Nor does the quality of a tutor correlate with how close they live; if anything the correlation runs the other way, since a tutor whose selling point is proximity is competing on the one variable that does not affect teaching.

Which leads to the practical summary for a family in any of these four neighbourhoods. Use the free provision first. Match on the syllabus code, not the radius. Set the slot from arrival home and from when a quiet room is actually available. Use the weekend and the holidays if the flat is busy. And treat an hourly rate that includes a journey as what it is: a teaching fee plus a transport fee, where only one of the two improves a grade.

sections.heading: Comparing tutor categories on legality
paragraphs: One comparison a parent should make and almost nobody does is whether the person teaching their child is permitted to do it. Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work rather than informal work, and the permit is free, so there is no awkwardness in asking.

The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. The published eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service listing is issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted online is unverified.

A second comparison sits alongside it. An individual tutor and a tutoring operation with premises are different legal animals: the latter requires a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute, which involves initial approval, a maximum six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That distinction is why a tuition centre in Al Qusais can hold a KHDA permit while an individual tutor cannot and does not need one. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, operates no UAE premises, and is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

There is also a conduct comparison. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. Treat the detail as press-reported and verify the current policy, but the principle is sound anywhere: paying the person who sets and marks your child's assessments is a conflict, not a convenience.

sections.heading: Comparing the equivalency tracks
paragraphs: The last comparison is the one families make after results and should make in Year 10. Ministry of Education equivalency is how an international qualification becomes something UAE institutions can act on, and the requirements differ by curriculum track in ways that change which subjects are worth protecting.

On the British track the published requirement is passes in five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page currently ranking states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five, and inheriting that error would change a family's decisions for no reason.

On the American track the published requirements are different in kind: English proficiency demonstrated by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the International Baccalaureate, the source we can cite states no points threshold, so none appears here; confirm it on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before planning around it.

Two cautions apply to all tracks. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs; it is not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates, and no tutoring is required for it. And the regulator map matters if a family moves emirate: Dubai's private schools fall under KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education, with the Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities also approving fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

process.title: Start with the free options
process.description: Ask the school for the clinic timetable, the mock scripts with mark schemes and the head of year's view on class weak topics. Compare what remains against what we would charge for, and in many cases the honest answer is one session rather than a package.

process.title: Send the codes, not the subjects
process.description: Give us the exact syllabus code for each subject from the entry form — 0580, 4MA1, 0654 — along with the tier. That single sheet determines which past papers are useful, and it is the cheapest quality control available to a parent in any neighbourhood.

process.title: Compare two tutors on the same five questions
process.description: Use the five questions on this page, in a free trial rather than on the phone, and write the answers down. The fifth — marking one page aloud — separates candidates more reliably than any profile, review or qualification list.

process.title: Set the slot from arrival and from quiet
process.description: Tell us when your child genuinely walks in and when a quiet room is actually free. In apartment districts those are two different questions, and the answer may be a weekend morning rather than a weekday evening.

process.title: Review against a timed paper
process.description: The review point is a paper sat to time, not a session count. If the score moved, we choose the next target; if not, we change the method or the tutor and say which we think it was. Every review is a clean exit point.

whyPoints.title: The comparison published, including where we lose
whyPoints.description: This page says plainly that school clinics are free and better informed than any external tutor, and that a small group class beats a cheap one-to-one hour. Both cost us revenue. A comparison that only flatters the provider writing it is not a comparison.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the syllabus code
whyPoints.description: 0580 is not 4MA1 and 0654 is not the separate sciences. We ask for the code before matching, because past-paper work is most of the value of a session and the wrong board's papers train habits a student cannot use in their own examination.

whyPoints.title: Rates that do not vary by postcode
whyPoints.description: Online rates are identical across all four neighbourhoods compared here, because there is no journey to price. The in-home premium of roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour is a transport fee, and only the teaching half of a visiting tutor's rate improves a grade.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed
whyPoints.description: Each AED band on this page names its publisher and is dated October 2026. Three of the pages ranking for Dubai tutoring queries publish no price at all and two quote dollars, which is not the currency a Deira household transacts in.

whyPoints.title: Legality treated as comparable
whyPoints.description: The permit section exists so you can compare tutors on whether they are permitted to work. The MoHRE private tuition permit is free and runs two years, so a working tutor has no innocent reason not to hold one.

whyPoints.title: Claims we do not make
whyPoints.description: No regulator approval, no board or school partnership, no promise about a grade or score, no self-published ratings, and no statistic without a source. Where the published record has a gap — the IB equivalency threshold — we say so instead of filling it.

faqs.question: Is it easier to find an IGCSE tutor in Al Qusais than in Deira?
faqs.answer: Slightly, for generalists and group classes, and not at all for specialists. Al Qusais has the highest school density and the most tuition centres near Deira, so there are more tutors circulating and more group options. But people who have actually marked against a named specification are scarce across the whole Dubai market, not just in one district, and they cluster around where they live rather than where demand is. For a specialist match, the neighbourhood makes no measurable difference.

faqs.question: Does living in a Deira apartment really affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: Yes, more than families expect. In dense housing a quiet room at 5pm is not guaranteed, and the hour when one is free moves from day to day. That argues for weekend mornings and holiday blocks rather than a fixed weekday evening, and for online sessions that can be set to whenever the room is actually available. It also makes the school's free supervised study rooms genuinely valuable, since for some students the obstacle is space rather than teaching.

faqs.question: Would moving to Mirdif give my child better access to tutors?
faqs.answer: It would give them a desk and a door, which matters, and a shorter commute if they school locally. It would not improve access to specialists: Mirdif has a small school cluster and is further from the centre, so a visiting tutor prices a longer journey into the hour. On the variables that affect a grade — syllabus, tier, mark scheme, specialist availability — the two areas are equivalent. On the variable that affects daily life, villa housing wins.

faqs.question: How do online rates compare between these neighbourhoods?
faqs.answer: They are identical, and that is the most useful line in the cost table. Published Dubai bands read in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 and specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, and those figures do not change between Deira, Al Qusais, Bur Dubai and Mirdif because there is no journey being priced. In-home rates of AED 180 to 500 do vary by area, because the travel component varies, which tells you what that premium actually is.

faqs.question: Which is better value, a group class or a cheap one-to-one hour?
faqs.answer: Usually the group class, and it is dismissed too quickly. A small group taught by somebody who knows the specification, at well below one-to-one rates, generally beats a one-to-one hour at the budget band of AED 33 to 65 with a generalist, because teaching quality matters more than ratio once the group is small. Centres cluster in Al Qusais and Al Nahda. What a group cannot do is identify why one student loses marks in a particular way.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor to compare them against another one?
faqs.answer: Five things: which specification by code they have taught, how many papers at that tier and what each tests, how the practical or oral component is assessed on that specification, what separates a 6 from an 8, and then ask them to mark one page of your child's work aloud saying what each annotation is worth. Write the answers down so two candidates a week apart can be compared honestly. The fifth question decides it in almost every case.

faqs.question: Why does the syllabus code matter more than the neighbourhood?
faqs.answer: Because past-paper practice is most of what a session is worth, and papers are specification-specific. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 differ in paper count and tiering language; 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences is narrower than the separate sciences. A student drilling the wrong board's papers is rehearsing question types they will not meet, and a student revising separate-science content for a Co-ordinated entry is spending weeks on material that is not examined. Codes are two minutes of work and they fix both problems.

faqs.question: Can my child change board if the school's choice does not suit them?
faqs.answer: Not usually without changing school, because the school is the entry centre and chooses the specification. What you can change is how your child prepares for the one they have, which is why knowing the code matters. If the board genuinely does not suit — a student who performs badly in fewer, longer papers, for instance — that is a conversation to have with the school in Year 10, not a tutoring purchase, and realistically it is an argument for a school move rather than a board move.

faqs.question: Can a tuition centre in Al Qusais claim a KHDA permit?
faqs.answer: Only if it holds the relevant permit. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute, which involves initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. An individual tutor neither holds nor needs one; they need the MoHRE private tuition work permit. If a provider claims KHDA approval, ask for the permit number and check KHDA's own listing.

faqs.question: Should I be asking about a tutor's work permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and there is no awkwardness in it, because the permit is free. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is administered by MoHRE and is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists the service with a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Does the November series work the same for all these areas?
faqs.answer: Yes, because series availability is set by the board rather than by location. UAE candidates sit the June series with November available, and Pearson offers May/June and November. The November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. One point applying equally to Deira, Al Qusais, Bur Dubai and Mirdif: the Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only, so no UAE plan should be built around a February sitting.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we compare before choosing one to tutor?
faqs.answer: Compare all of them on one criterion: where a small intervention changes the most. Usually that is Mathematics, because the grade gates the most post-16 options and because method-mark discipline transfers into the sciences. Second is whichever science is both weakest and entered at Extended or Higher tier. Business Studies and Economics respond better to a focused block near the series than to year-long support. Choose one, review at the mocks, and move the slot then rather than rotating.

faqs.question: Is the equivalency subject count five, as the Ministry publishes, or six?
faqs.answer: Five. The published British-track requirement is passes in five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus either one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One currently ranking competitor page states six, which does not match the published rule. Verify on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority, since this is a decision a family acts on.

faqs.question: Would an in-home tutor from Hor Al Anz be cheaper than one from Mirdif?
faqs.answer: Probably, and that is the clearest evidence of what the in-home premium actually pays for. Published in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour include travel, so a tutor working within a short drive prices a shorter journey into the hour than one coming from the eastern suburbs. The teaching is unaffected by either journey. If you are comparing two in-home quotes, you are partly comparing two commutes, which is not a variable that improves a grade.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send a tutor to any of these neighbourhoods?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are part of our India service. The comparison on this page is why: the differences between these four areas are logistical and removable, while the requirement they share is a specialist matched on the syllabus code. In-home tutoring is available in the Dubai market at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel for families who need that format.

faqs.question: If every area is the same, what should actually decide my choice?
faqs.answer: Four things, none of them geographic. Whether the tutor has taught your child's exact specification, which you establish by asking for the code. Whether they can mark a page aloud in mark-scheme language. Whether the session sits at an hour your child is genuinely available and a quiet room is free. And whether you have used the free school provision first, because a clinic run by the teacher who marks the mocks has an information advantage no external tutor can match.

Send us the subject, the exact syllabus code, the tier and the hour your child is genuinely free in a quiet room, and we will propose one slot and tell you honestly what the school's own free provision should cover instead. The first lesson is free, one per subject, before any payment. Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: The week, audited: where the hours actually go
paragraphs: A parent typing "IGCSE tutor near me" from a DIFC tower is solving a scheduling problem and describing it as a geography problem. The constraint is not distance. DIFC has no school inside its boundary, so your child already travels out of the district twice a day, which means you have already accepted a commute. What you have not necessarily audited is what is left of the week once that commute, nine subjects' worth of homework, the mandatory UAE subjects and the school's own calendar have taken their share.

That audit is what this page does. It sets out which boards the schools DIFC families actually use are running, because a tutor matched to the wrong specification is a wasted slot regardless of when it falls. It looks at how the school day ends and how a child gets home, because a bus route and a parent's car produce different arrival times and therefore different earliest sessions. It counts the usable minutes in a Year 11 evening honestly. And it names the weeks that vanish from a Year 11 calendar without anybody planning for it.

DIFC does have one genuine advantage over its neighbours, and it is worth using. The district sits close to the Al Safa and Jumeirah school cluster, which means the return journey is among the shortest in central Dubai. A DIFC family can often make a 4pm session work where a Meydan or Al Barsha family cannot start before 5pm. Since the 5pm to 7pm Gulf Standard Time window is contested by the entire emirate, that half-hour head start is the most valuable scheduling asset a DIFC parent has, and most do not know they have it.

On delivery, plainly. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE and we operate no centre here; home visiting is a service we run only in India. For a scheduling problem this is the material point: an online session can be moved by a day in a message, and a session that depends on somebody's drive across central Dubai cannot. In a Year 11 term where mocks, school events and illness all arrive unannounced, that flexibility is the difference between twelve sessions received and eight.

Everything below is sourced where it can be. Regulatory facts are attributed to u.ae, KHDA and MoHRE. Market rates are attributed to the provider or publication that published them, with the month they were read. Where a fact could not be verified against an official source, including any IB examination date, this page says so and leaves it out rather than guessing. No statistic appears here without a number, a date and a method behind it, which is why there are fewer statistics here than on most pages in this market.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-difc.programmesIntro: The scheduling problem changes shape with the year group, because the competing demands change. These are the stages in play for a DIFC family, described by what each one does to the week.

programmes.name: Year 10, when the week still has slack
programmes.description: Content is being met for the first time and homework volume has not yet peaked. A Year 10 can absorb two tutored subjects at a session each without the week breaking, which a Year 11 generally cannot. This is also the year in which the tier entry decision is made, so a weekly session here does double duty: it consolidates teaching and it builds the evidence the tier conversation needs.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the tier entry decision is usually made during Year 10 or very early Year 11, within the board's deadlines, on the basis of internal assessment. For a DIFC family the practical point is that Year 10 evenings are long enough for this work and Year 11 evenings are not.

programmes.name: Year 11, when the week is already full
programmes.description: Nine or ten subjects, each setting homework, plus coursework deadlines and a mock window. The usable evening after a commute from Al Safa or Al Quoz is roughly three hours and it is already allocated. Adding tuition here is a substitution decision rather than an addition one, and the honest version involves deciding what the session replaces.
programmes.countryNote: A DIFC student arriving home around 4pm has perhaps three productive hours before fatigue sets in, and those hours are contested by eight teachers who do not coordinate with each other. One tutored subject fits. Four do not, and the usual result is attendance that collapses around week five.

programmes.name: Year 9 and the Checkpoint window
programmes.description: Before the IGCSE course begins, with the lightest week of the three and the most leverage. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests give an external datapoint before the school's tier decision, and a Year 9 scoring in the lower bands has a full year to change it. One session a week here is easier to schedule and more consequential than three sessions a week in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The October window produces evidence before the tier decision rather than after it, which is when most DIFC parents first hear the word Core.

programmes.name: The mandatory UAE subjects inside the timetable
programmes.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. They occupy real timetabled periods, which means a Year 11 in Dubai has less curriculum time per IGCSE subject than a student on the same specification in the United Kingdom. That is a scheduling fact with consequences, and almost no tutoring page in this market mentions it.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA's mandatory-subject instructional time is calculated based on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that the length of any mandatory subject lesson is at least 25 minutes. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-difc.subjectsIntro: Nine or ten subjects do not need equal attention, and the scheduling question is which one earns the slot. The list below notes what each subject demands of a week, which is the practical basis for choosing.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Needs frequent short practice rather than long sessions, because fluency decays between sittings. A weekly hour with twenty minutes of practice on four other evenings beats two long sessions. It is also the subject whose procedural losses move fastest, which makes it the usual first choice for a single slot.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: The practical or alternative-to-practical component rewards precise written method, variables and sources of error, which is a writing task that can be done well in a single weekly session. Electricity and electromagnetism, by contrast, need sustained weeks and should not be started in the final month.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole and titration calculations need repetition rather than explanation, so homework between sessions matters more here than session length. Organic chemistry is cumulative and expensive to repair late, which makes it a Year 10 or autumn-term job rather than a spring one.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: The largest content volume of the three sciences, so it is the worst fit for a single weekly slot if the problem is genuinely content. If the problem is command terms, which it often is, three sessions on answer shape for explain, suggest and compare is enough and fits any week.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990, Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Suits a fortnightly rhythm better than most subjects: a session on criteria and structure, then a written piece produced over two weeks and marked. That pattern halves the slot pressure on a crowded Year 11 week while losing almost nothing in effect.

subjects.name: English Literature (Edexcel 4ET1 / Cambridge 0475)
subjects.description: Quotation memorisation is a homework problem, not a session problem, and treating it as a session problem wastes paid hours. The useful session work is textual analysis density against the mark scheme, which is intensive and short.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Evaluation marks are the recoverable ones and they are taught in a handful of sessions. Both subjects reward application to the stimulus and a stated judgement, and the Dubai pattern is strong theory with neutral two-sided answers that score in the middle band.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 / Edexcel 4CP0)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables are mechanical and fast. The theory paper on data representation and networks is a reading and recall task that belongs in homework rather than in a session, which makes this a low slot-demand subject overall.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Both need named, specific case-study detail, which is memorisation, and source or data technique, which is taught. Separating the two is what makes a slot efficient here: the technique is three sessions and the detail is a revision timetable.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: A genuine extra subject in a week that is already full, and worth taking on only where the main specification is secure. A student consolidating Extended content who adds Additional Mathematics support has created a tenth subject rather than strengthened a ninth.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Required in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum and timetabled against the international subjects. It does not count among the five IGCSE subjects the Ministry of Education requires on the British track, so its claim on a crowded evening should be judged against the school report rather than the equivalency file.

subjects.name: Accounting and Information Technology
subjects.description: Method and format marks dominate, and both improve quickly because the losses are to convention rather than to understanding. Low slot demand: three or four sessions on presentation conventions and specification compliance usually settles a grade.

sections.heading: A Year 11 week, counted honestly
paragraphs: Start with the arithmetic nobody does. A DIFC Year 11 leaves home around 7am, finishes school between 3pm and 3.30pm, and arrives back between 3.50pm and 4.45pm depending on the campus and whether they take a bus. That leaves, before fatigue, roughly three productive hours on a weeknight. Call it fifteen productive hours across a school week, plus whatever the weekend yields.

Against that, nine or ten subject teachers are setting homework, none of them coordinating with each other. Coursework deadlines arrive in clusters. The mandatory UAE subjects occupy timetabled periods during the day, which means a Dubai student has less in-school curriculum time per IGCSE subject than a student on the same specification elsewhere, and therefore slightly more to do at home. Then there is a mock window, school events, and the ordinary attrition of illness and travel.

Read that way, a tutoring slot is not an addition to the week. It is a substitution, and the useful question is what it replaces. One hour a week on the subject with the widest grade gap, replacing an hour of unfocused general revision, is a clear improvement. Four hours a week across four subjects, replacing the homework those subjects' teachers have set, is a different and usually worse trade. This is the mechanism behind the familiar pattern where a four-subject plan collapses in week five: the week did not have four hours to give.

The table below audits a typical DIFC Year 11 week so the trade is visible rather than assumed. It is worth filling in with your own child's actual times, because the difference between a 3.50pm and a 4.45pm arrival is close to an hour a day, which across a term is substantial and is the single largest variable a family controls.

sections.heading: Confirm the board before you book the slot
paragraphs: A session at the perfect hour with a tutor matched to the wrong specification is a wasted slot, and in a week with fifteen usable hours a wasted slot is expensive. The schools DIFC families use are split across Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and in some cases across both within one school's subject offer.

The practical consequence is that the first action is administrative. Email the school's examinations officer and ask, in writing, for the exact specification code and the tier of entry in each subject you are considering. Both answers arrive in a reply or two. Many DIFC families discover at this point that they had assumed a board, often from an older sibling or from a previous school in another country.

The second question is which papers are calculator-free and which formulae are printed rather than recalled, because both differ by specification and by tier. Students routinely memorise provided formulae and neglect required ones, which is a pure loss of marks created by a misunderstanding that one email resolves. No tutoring page, including this one, should be the source of record for that list.

The third is the exam zone, which is specific to Cambridge and genuinely consequential. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. Build the revision calendar from the timetable your own examinations officer confirms, never from a version found online.

sections.heading: Bus or car: the hour that decides the slot
paragraphs: How a child gets home from school is a bigger scheduling variable than most families treat it as. A school bus follows a stop pattern that adds twenty to thirty minutes over a direct car journey on the same route, and it is not negotiable on any given day. A parent's car is faster and is subject to the parent's own working day, which in DIFC frequently ends later than the school day.

The practical effect is that the same campus produces two different earliest session times depending on the transport. A DIFC student at a school in Al Safa arriving by car can be ready at 4pm. The same student on the bus may not be ready until 4.40pm. Fixing a weekly slot at 4.15pm for the second child guarantees a term of late starts, shortened sessions and the slow erosion of a plan that was never wrong about the teaching.

A third pattern is worth naming because it is common in this district and rarely discussed: the child who is collected by a driver or helper, which produces a reliable early arrival but no adult at home who can confirm the session happened. Online sessions have an advantage here that is practical rather than pedagogical, in that attendance and duration are recorded rather than reported.

The fix is to measure rather than estimate. For one week, note the actual time your child walks through the door, and set the session fifteen minutes after the latest of those five times. That single measurement prevents the most common scheduling failure in this market, which is a slot chosen from a school's published end time rather than from the child's actual arrival.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects and the time they take
paragraphs: This is a scheduling fact almost no tutoring page in Dubai mentions, and it changes the arithmetic of a Year 11 week. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. They are not an extra-curricular activity; they occupy timetabled periods and they appear on the report.

KHDA sets the instructional time for these subjects and calculates it based on a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that the length for any mandatory subject lesson is at least 25 minutes. KHDA also requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction.

The consequence for a DIFC Year 11 is modest but real. Those periods come out of a fixed school week, which means slightly less in-school time per IGCSE subject than a student on the same specification in another country, and therefore slightly more of the course landing on the evening. When a parent wonders why their child seems to have more homework than a cousin sitting the same papers abroad, this is usually part of the answer.

One constraint worth knowing before buying support for these subjects. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the Ministry of Education, is strictly prohibited. KHDA also requires schools to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach these subjects. A tutor cannot substitute for that provision, and a provider claiming to teach an alternative syllabus in these subjects is describing something that is not permitted.

sections.heading: The weeks that disappear from a Year 11 calendar
paragraphs: A plan drawn in September assumes every week is available, and in Dubai a meaningful number are not. The mock window removes a fortnight of normal evenings. Winter and spring breaks remove two to three weeks each year. Ramadan shortens school days and reorganises evenings around iftar. School events, trips and internal assessment weeks take more. A family that counts the weeks honestly in September usually finds they have four to six fewer usable weeks than they assumed.

This matters for scheduling rather than for content. A twelve-week plan that is really an eight-week plan does not fail because the teaching was wrong; it fails because it was never going to fit. The fix is to count the gaps first and then decide how many subjects the remaining weeks can carry, which almost always produces a narrower plan than the one a worried parent starts with.

Ramadan deserves specific planning rather than improvisation. School days shorten, evening routines reorganise around iftar, and the usual 5pm slot stops working for many DIFC families. Early-afternoon and post-iftar sessions both work; what fails is deciding week by week, which typically costs three or four weeks at a point in the year when weeks are expensive. Agree the alternative pattern before the month begins.

Breaks are the opposite case and are routinely wasted. A break is the only time a student has whole uninterrupted days, which makes it the right window for a full timed paper under examination conditions and the wrong window for new content. Two properly marked timed papers across a one-week break are worth more than six rushed weeknight sessions, and they cost less in both money and goodwill.

sections.heading: What an hour costs, and what a usable hour costs
paragraphs: Because this page is about scheduling, the useful cost measure is not the rate but the rate per hour actually received. A session that starts fifteen minutes late because the bus was late, or that is cancelled because a mock was rescheduled, has the same price and less value. Counting that way changes which format looks cheap.

The published Dubai bands are these, each attributed to the provider or publication that stated it and read in October 2026. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end of online tutoring. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 online. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialist work at AED 200 to 450 or more, with independent home tutors reaching AED 200 to 500 once travel is priced in. TutorChase quotes AED 270, BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. Monthly packages include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Now apply the scheduling lens. An in-home session cannot be moved at short notice, because somebody's drive is inside it, and short-notice movement is exactly what a Year 11 term demands around mocks, school events and illness. Across a twelve-week block, a format that loses two sessions to immovability has raised its own effective hourly cost by roughly a sixth, on top of the travel premium it already carries. An online session reschedules in a message.

sections.heading: Permits, equivalency and the claims we decline
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and this is something a parent can check rather than assume. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here. One boundary is worth knowing before anybody suggests it: in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document, since this is press-reported.

On equivalency, the sourced British-track rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. At least one ranking site in this market publishes six subjects, which is wrong. We publish no IB points threshold, because none could be read on an official Ministry source, and IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency for anybody.

And the claims we decline to make. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation, licence, approval or partnership. We have no office, branch or centre in the United Arab Emirates. We do not describe tutors as examiners without evidence of current status, do not publish any self-asserted rating or review count, and do not write, complete or edit assessed work. Tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and a provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency.

sections.heading: Booking the slot that will actually survive the term
paragraphs: Bring four things and the scheduling decision makes itself. The exact specification code and tier for each subject, confirmed in writing by the school. The two most recent marked papers rather than the grades. The actual arrival-home times measured over one week. And the school's calendar of mock weeks, coursework deadlines and events. With those, the slot and the subject are both determined by evidence rather than by preference.

Coverage for IGCSE across the core subjects at both boards and both tiers is reliable, so a match is normally available within a few working days. The scarce resource is the hour. The 5pm to 7pm Gulf Standard Time window is contested across the whole emirate, and a DIFC family's short westward run is a genuine advantage in getting ahead of it. Use the 4pm or 4.30pm slot if your child's arrival allows it, because those are the easiest hours in the central corridor to hold for a full term.

If no specialist for your child's specification is free at the hour you need, you will be told that at the enquiry rather than matched to whoever is available. Where no UAE-based tutor covers a narrow subject, the match may be a specialist teaching into the Gulf timezone from elsewhere, and that is stated before the trial lesson rather than discovered later.

Last, decide what the session replaces before it starts. One hour a week on the subject with the widest grade gap, taken from unfocused general revision, is a clear gain. Four hours across four subjects, taken from the homework those teachers set, is a trade that usually loses. A Year 11 week has about fifteen usable hours and no amount of planning creates a sixteenth.

faqs.question: What is the earliest an IGCSE session can start for a child living in DIFC?
faqs.answer: It depends on the campus and the transport, and the honest answer comes from measuring rather than estimating. A student travelling by car from a school in Al Safa or Al Wasl can usually be ready at 4pm. The same student on a school bus on a coastal Jumeirah route may not be ready until 4.40pm, because a bus adds twenty to thirty minutes over a direct drive. From Al Quoz or Al Barsha, 4.45pm to 5pm is realistic. Note the actual arrival time for five days and set the session fifteen minutes after the latest one.

faqs.question: Does taking the school bus change what time we should book tuition?
faqs.answer: Yes, by twenty to thirty minutes typically, and it is not negotiable on any given day because the stop pattern is fixed. Families often set a slot from the school's published end time, which produces a term of sessions that start late, run short and gradually stop being taken seriously. If your child is on a bus, build the slot around the bus rather than the bell. A weekly session that starts on time every week is worth noticeably more than one that starts ten minutes late most weeks.

faqs.question: How many usable study hours does a Year 11 in DIFC actually have?
faqs.answer: Roughly three productive hours on a weeknight, so about fifteen across a school week, plus whatever the weekend yields. Against that, nine or ten subject teachers are setting homework without coordinating, coursework deadlines arrive in clusters, and the mandatory UAE subjects occupy timetabled periods during the day. A tutoring slot is therefore a substitution rather than an addition, and the useful question is what it replaces. One hour replacing unfocused revision is a gain; four hours replacing set homework usually is not.

faqs.question: Is a 4pm session too soon after school for a fifteen-year-old?
faqs.answer: For most students it is the best hour of the evening rather than the worst. A Year 11 at 4pm has travelled but not yet worked; the same child at 7.30pm has done two hours of homework from other subjects and is running on less. The caveat is the arrival time: a 4pm session only works if your child is genuinely home by 3.50pm, which in DIFC is realistic from the Al Safa and Jumeirah cluster by car and not realistic from Al Quoz by bus. Test it at the trial lesson.

faqs.question: Would a fortnightly session be enough for IGCSE English?
faqs.answer: Frequently yes, and it fits a crowded week far better. The pattern that works is one session on the assessment criteria and structure, then a substantial written piece produced over two weeks, marked before the next session. English marks in this market are usually lost to structure rather than to vocabulary, and structure is taught against the mark scheme rather than drilled. The same rhythm suits the humanities and the written science components. Mathematics is the exception: fluency decays between sittings, so it needs weekly contact.

faqs.question: Which weeks should we expect to lose from a Year 11 plan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The mock window takes a fortnight of normal evenings. Winter and spring breaks take two to three weeks between them. Ramadan shortens school days and reorganises evenings. School events, trips and internal assessment weeks take more. Most families who count honestly find four to six fewer usable weeks than their September plan assumed. The consequence is that a twelve-week plan is often really an eight-week plan, which is why counting the gaps first usually produces a narrower and more successful plan.

faqs.question: How should we schedule IGCSE sessions through Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Agree the alternative pattern before the month begins rather than deciding week by week. School days shorten and evening routines reorganise around iftar, so the usual 5pm slot stops working for most DIFC families. Early-afternoon sessions and post-iftar sessions both work well; improvisation is what fails, and it typically costs three or four weeks at a point in the year when weeks are expensive. For a Year 11 whose series falls after Ramadan, that is the largest avoidable gap in the whole calendar.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education periods reduce IGCSE teaching time?
faqs.answer: They occupy timetabled periods in every Dubai private school, which means slightly less in-school time per IGCSE subject than a student on the same specification elsewhere, and therefore slightly more of the course landing in the evening. KHDA calculates the instructional time for these subjects based on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and advises a minimum of 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. It is a modest effect, but it is part of why Dubai homework volume surprises families who have moved here.

faqs.question: Can a tutor teach Arabic or Islamic Education alongside my child's school course?
faqs.answer: Within limits that are worth knowing. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, and KHDA requires schools to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. A provider claiming to deliver an alternative syllabus in these subjects is describing something that is not permitted.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subject should get the one slot our week can hold?
faqs.answer: The one with the widest grade gap according to marked papers, not the one causing the most anxiety at the dinner table. Mathematics is often the answer because so many of its lost marks are procedural, meaning reverse percentages, frequency density, circle-theorem naming and rounding discipline, each worth marks on nearly every paper and each learnable in two or three sittings. But that is a prediction, not a diagnosis. Ask for the two most recent marked papers and let the distribution of lost marks choose the subject.

faqs.question: Does a tutor who lives near DIFC teach the IGCSE specification any better?
faqs.answer: No, and the arithmetic explains why. DIFC has no school inside the district, so there is no local pool of teachers who happen to know your child's scheme of work. The candidate population in the central corridor is split across two boards, two tiers and nine or ten subjects each, which is around forty distinct teaching specialisms. Asking a local pool of a few dozen tutors to contain the one exact match with the one free hour you need usually fails, and the family then books whoever is available.

Monthly packages include AED 799 for eight online sessions. IB Gram does not publish a UAE rate card on these pages.

faqs.answer: Count the sessions received, because that is what you are buying. A session that starts fifteen minutes late because the bus was late, or is cancelled because a mock moved, costs the same and delivers less. In-home sessions cannot be rescheduled at short notice because a drive is inside them, and short-notice movement is exactly what a Year 11 term demands. A format that loses two sessions out of twelve to immovability has raised its own effective cost by about a sixth, on top of any travel premium.

faqs.question: Does my child's IGCSE tutor in Dubai need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, which is why no amount appears on this page.

faqs.answer: Not from us. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the United Arab Emirates and has no office, branch or tuition centre here; home visiting is a service we run only in India. All UAE tuition is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For a scheduling problem this is the material advantage: an online session moves in a message around a mock or a sick day, where a session built on somebody's drive across central Dubai in the evening peak cannot.

faqs.answer: You will be told at the enquiry rather than matched to whoever is available. The 5pm to 7pm Gulf Standard Time window is contested across the emirate, so the hours that hold for a full term are 4pm and 4.30pm, anything after 7.30pm, and weekend mornings. DIFC's short westward school run is a genuine advantage in securing the earlier ones. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a narrow subject, the match may be a specialist teaching into the Gulf timezone from elsewhere, stated before the trial lesson.

intro.heading: Five different products, one search result
paragraphs: The hardest part of finding IGCSE help in this corridor is not availability but comparison. A search returns tuition centres with premises, agency rosters that place a tutor with you, freelance tutors advertising in building and community groups, international marketplaces listing people in other time zones, and online one-to-one services. All of them describe themselves in near-identical language, and all of them are genuinely different products with different failure modes.

Discovery Gardens makes the question concrete because the options really are nearby. Ibn Battuta sits next door, the community has its own Route 2020 metro station, and there are learning centres and private tutors within a short distance of 291 residential buildings. A parent can plausibly choose a centre on walking distance alone, which is a reasonable thing to want and a poor basis for a Year 11 decision.

What this page does is compare the options on capability rather than on convenience. A tuition centre group class can do things one-to-one cannot, including structure and peer pace at a lower unit cost. One-to-one can do things a centre cannot, including diagnosing why a specific student loses marks on a specific paper. A school clinic is free and is often the best first move. Knowing which tool fits the problem saves more money than negotiating a rate.

The one variable that cuts across every option is the exam board. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 and the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE equivalent is 4MA1, with different tiers, paper structures and mark-scheme conventions. Several schools in this corridor enter different boards in different departments. A provider who cannot tell you which board they teach has told you something important regardless of their model.

IB Gram's position in that comparison is specific. We are an online one-to-one service: we match on the syllabus code from your child's entry list, name the tutor and their components before the first lesson, and run every UAE session over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30. No tutor attends a UAE address, since home visiting is a service we offer only in India.

That is a limit and this page states it alongside the comparison rather than burying it. It also means we are the wrong answer for some families, including those who want a group class for motivation or a physically present adult for a younger child. The comparison below should let you work out which you are before you spend anything.

There is one more thing worth doing before any of this, and it is free. Most schools in this corridor run a subject clinic, publish a KHDA inspection report, and hold a paper-level breakdown of your child's last mock. Those three documents between them usually identify the problem, and the problem is what should choose the provider. Families who skip them end up comparing rates for a service they have not yet established they need.

A centre revision course plus a weekly one-to-one session on the one subject that is not moving is the combination many families here end up with, and it is usually the right one.

programmes.name: Advanced Level or IB Diploma afterwards
programmes.description: Most schools want grade 6 or 7 before accepting a subject at Advanced Level, and IB Diploma Higher Level entry usually asks the same, so a capped tier closes routes. Post-16 courses move faster and the specialist pool is thinner, which pushes the balance further towards one-to-one with a subject specialist.
programmes.countryNote: Families in this corridor frequently change schools at 16 because full IB Diploma provision nearby is thinner than further north. A summer bridging block is worth more here than in communities where students stay put, because the first term brings a new school and new content simultaneously.

programmes.name: The November series
programmes.description: Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The decision should come from the paper-level breakdown rather than the overall grade, and the window to enter is short after August results.
programmes.countryNote: For a November entry the comparison narrows sharply, because centres rarely run courses for it and the cohort is small. One-to-one through the UAE summer is usually the only real option, and it is also the easiest time of year to secure a specialist, since Dubai demand collapses after results.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-discovery-g.subjectsIntro: Which option fits also depends on the subject, because some are widely taught in this corridor and some are barely taught at all. Each note names the codes and the supply picture.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The most widely available subject in every provider model, so the comparison is genuinely open. Group revision courses exist, centres run them, and one-to-one is plentiful. The deciding factor is whether the student has a diagnosed error pattern, in which case a group cannot address it.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: Barely available in any local model. Few centres run it, few freelancers have taught it recently, and the cohort is small. This is the clearest case in the whole subject list where an online match is not a preference but the only realistic route.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Reasonably available one-to-one and less often as a dedicated group course. The practical or alternative-to-practical component is rarely taught well in group settings, because it needs individual marked feedback on tables, graphs and method descriptions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Widely available at Year 11 level. Mole arithmetic and chemical tests are the reliable losses, and both respond to drilled individual practice rather than to a group walkthrough, because the student needs their own errors corrected repeatedly.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Widely available. The subject's main loss is imprecise language, which is corrected only by having written answers marked individually. A group class can teach the content and cannot mark thirty students' phrasing, which is where the marks go.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: Group provision is thinner than for separate sciences because the cohort is more varied. The structural issue also argues for one-to-one: a weak discipline appears in every paper, so support must concentrate there rather than following a group syllabus.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Group courses are common and genuinely useful for approach and structure. What they cannot do is mark enough of one student's writing, and reading response marks turn on selective quotation and precise explanation of effect in that student's own answers.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: The subject with the widest gap between group and individual value. Set-text teaching works in a group; timed essay practice with marked feedback does not, and the latter is the only thing that reliably moves a literature grade.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Group courses cover content and diagrams well. Command-term discipline, which is what separates grades here, requires individual marked answers, because the error is in the student's own paragraph shape rather than in their knowledge.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Patchy local availability and frequently taught by people strong in programming and unfamiliar with the board's pseudocode conventions. Worth asking any provider, in any model, which conventions they teach before committing.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Case-study content suits a group; source-question technique and essay structure do not. Most students in these subjects know more than their marks suggest, which is a diagnosis problem and therefore an individual one.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory teaching in Dubai private schools under KHDA rules means every student takes Arabic, but entry-level tuition for the first-language qualification is scarce in every model. Confirm which entry your child sits before comparing any provider.

sections.heading: The options a Discovery Gardens search returns, compared
paragraphs: Five models dominate, and the differences are structural rather than reputational. A tuition centre has premises and runs classes to a timetable, usually in groups. An agency keeps a roster and places someone with you, in person or online. A freelance tutor found through a community or building group works independently. An international marketplace lists individuals, often in other time zones. An online service matches and delivers over video.

Each has a characteristic strength. Centres provide structure, pace and peer motivation at a lower unit cost, which suits a student who is broadly on track and needs momentum. Agencies provide screening and replacement if a match fails. Freelancers can be excellent and are the most variable category, because nothing has been checked by anyone other than the parent who recommended them.

Each also has a characteristic failure. Centres cannot diagnose one student's error pattern, because the content is set in advance and the pace belongs to the group. Marketplaces route you to whoever is listed, sometimes teaching a different qualification with a similar name. Two of the most visible competitor pages in this market route UAE parents to Indian phone numbers, and one shows a Dubai footer address on a page written for Abu Dhabi.

The published costs are consistent across the market and worth having in mind while comparing. Budget online provision with student tutors runs AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik. A qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home with travel runs AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate, with independent tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not our prices.

sections.heading: Try the free option first: the school's own clinic
paragraphs: Before comparing paid providers, use the one that costs nothing. Most schools in this corridor run subject clinics or support sessions, and the teacher who set and marked the assessment is better placed than anyone to explain the marking of it. For a specific question about a specific marked answer, that is both free and immediate, and a surprising number of families have never asked whether it exists.

Its limits are real and worth naming. A clinic gives a few minutes per student, it cannot work through a full diagnostic across a subject, and it is not available for the volume of marked practice a Year 11 student needs in the final term. It is a scalpel rather than a programme. But it answers the single-question cases, which are a larger share of the problem than parents assume.

There is a second free document: the KHDA inspection report for your child's school. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes reports that name subject-level strengths and weaknesses. If mathematics attainment is flagged across the school, you are buying support for a structural issue and should brief any provider accordingly.

The third is the paper-level breakdown of the last mock. Schools hold it and often do not send it out. A grade 5 from one weak component needs targeted work; the same grade spread evenly needs broad consolidation; the same grade caused by unfinished papers is a timing problem. Those are three different purchases, and knowing which you need makes every comparison on this page straightforward.

sections.heading: Group class or one-to-one, on the arithmetic
paragraphs: Group classes are genuinely cheaper per hour and sometimes the right purchase, so the comparison deserves better than a sales answer. A centre running an IGCSE revision course for a group of eight can price well below any one-to-one rate, and for a student who is broadly on track and lacks structure or momentum that is money well spent. The pace and the peer effect do real work.

What a group cannot do is diagnose. The content is set in advance and delivered to the middle of the room. A student losing marks because their extended answers describe rather than explain, or because their working is never shown, will sit through a syllabus review that never mentions it. The cheaper per-hour option becomes the more expensive per-grade option whenever the problem is specific.

The split that works in practice, and the one many families in this community land on, is both: a centre revision course for structure and breadth, plus a weekly one-to-one session on the single subject that is not moving. That uses each model for what it does well, and it usually costs less than running one-to-one across three subjects.

On small groups of two to four, sometimes offered at a lower per-student rate: these are good value when the students genuinely match on subject, level and weakness, and poor value otherwise, because one student pays to watch the other get taught. Before agreeing to a pairing, ask what the other student's current grade and specific difficulty are. A vague answer is an answer.

sections.heading: What a community-group recommendation actually tells you
paragraphs: In a community of 291 buildings, recommendations circulate constantly and they are genuinely useful information of a particular kind. What a neighbour's recommendation reliably tells you is that a tutor turned up, was pleasant, and that the family felt better afterwards. Those matter. What it does not tell you is whether the tutor taught the right board, or whether the grade moved for a reason connected to the tutoring.

The gap is not cynicism, it is measurement. Most families cannot attribute a grade change to a specific intervention, because several things change at once: the student matures, the school teaches more, revision intensifies. A recommendation is therefore a reliable signal about reliability and manner, and a weak signal about subject capability. Both are worth having and they are not the same thing.

So use the recommendation to shortlist and then ask the questions yourself. Which board and syllabus code do you teach? What is each paper worth? Where do students in this subject lose marks, and is the answer about a topic or about the mark scheme? How do you mark a timed paper? Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? Five minutes of that tells you more than any number of endorsements.

The permit question is worth asking in every model. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here. Because the permit is free, a tutor charging you for it is billing for nothing.
