sections.heading: Discovery Gardens against Jebel Ali and Dubai Investments Park on supply
paragraphs: Local supply varies across this corridor in ways worth knowing, because it determines whether a proximity search is even a sensible strategy. Discovery Gardens has good access to nearby commercial space and learning centres, thanks to Ibn Battuta next door, and almost no resident subject specialists. So centre provision is realistic here and private specialist provision is not particularly local.

Dubai Investments Park is the opposite case. It holds several of the schools this corridor attends, which means teachers are physically present in the area during the day. That is the one place nearby where a locally based subject specialist is reasonably likely, and families in and immediately around it occasionally find a good private arrangement that would be hard to replicate from Discovery Gardens.

Jebel Ali and the southern districts have the thinnest supply in either model. Fewer centres, fewer resident specialists, longer drives from where Dubai's tutors live, and a working population whose hours push demand to 19:00, which few local options serve. For those households online delivery is less a choice than the only arrangement that fits the evening.

The conclusion from comparing the three is the same conclusion this page keeps reaching. Local supply determines which options exist; it does not determine which option works. A centre class in walking distance that cannot diagnose a command-term problem is still not the right purchase for a command-term problem, however convenient it is. Matching the tool to the diagnosis is what decides the outcome.

sections.heading: The answer that is the same in every model
paragraphs: Whichever option a family chooses, three things decide the outcome and none of them is affected by the model. The first is whether the teaching is aimed at the right board. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different exams with different tiers, paper structures and mark-scheme conventions, and several schools in this corridor enter different boards in different departments. A centre, an agency or a freelancer can all get this wrong equally.

The second is the tier. Core and Foundation entries cap the grade, and post-16 study usually requires grade 6 or 7, so a tier chosen in Year 10 can close a route. No provider model changes that, and no amount of good teaching in Year 11 reopens an entry that closed months earlier. Any provider worth using will ask which tier your child is entered for in the first conversation.

The third is marked practice. Unmarked past-paper work builds recognition of question types and very little else, which is why students who have done a great many papers still plateau. Timed, marked strictly against the real scheme, with errors grouped by cause rather than by topic, is the version that moves marks. Whether that happens is a property of the arrangement rather than of the model.

Which is why the comparison on this page, however carefully drawn, matters less than one document: the entry list from the school's exams officer, naming the board, code and tier for every subject. With it, any provider can be evaluated in five minutes. Without it, the most expensive option in the city can be aimed at the wrong papers and nobody will notice until the mock.

sections.heading: How to compare two quotes properly
paragraphs: Most families compare quotes on the hourly rate because it is the only number offered. A more useful comparison takes five minutes and uses six questions, none of which is about price. What is being compared is capability and honesty, and the differences between two providers at the same rate are usually larger than the differences between two rates.

Ask which board and syllabus code they teach, and listen for the code rather than a reassurance that the syllabuses are similar. Ask what each paper is worth, and whether they can state it from memory. Ask where students lose marks in this subject, and whether the answer names a mark-scheme behaviour or a difficult topic. Only the first kind of answer is useful.

Then ask three more. How do you mark a timed paper, and does marking happen at all? What will you not do with assessed work, which a good provider answers unprompted? And do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free and valid for two years, so there is no reason for an evasive answer.

Finally, check what you are being shown. Treat an untraceable star rating with caution: one competitor in this market displays two different ratings and review counts on the same page. Treat examiner claims with caution unless current status is evidenced, since examiner status gives nobody access to marking, boundaries or paper content. And treat any grade guarantee as a sales device, because no provider can honestly offer one.

sections.heading: Where we are the wrong answer, and our limits
paragraphs: A comparison page that concludes in favour of its author on every axis is not a comparison. So here are the cases where IB Gram is not the right option for a Discovery Gardens family. If you want a group class for motivation and structure at a lower unit cost, a centre near Ibn Battuta is the better buy. If you want a physically present adult for a child under about eight, we cannot provide that in the UAE.

If what the household needs is supervision rather than teaching, a cheaper service is the honest answer, and paying a subject rate for an invigilator is the largest avoidable waste in this market. And if the question is a single query about one marked answer, the school's subject clinic will deal with it today for nothing, which is a better outcome than buying an hour.

Where we do fit is narrower and clearer: a diagnosed problem in a specific subject, a scarce entry no local provider covers, marked paper work that needs one student's answers read closely, and situations where the household needs a 19:00 slot that nothing local serves. We match on the syllabus code, name the tutor and their components before the first lesson, and deliver one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30.

The standing limits apply. No tutor attends a UAE address; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. There is no IB Gram office in the UAE. We do not reproduce board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes, and we cite and link official sources instead. We hold no approval or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson. We do not guarantee grades, and if no specialist is free for your board and slot we say so.

faqs.question: What options does a Discovery Gardens family actually have for IGCSE help?
faqs.answer: Five paid models and three free ones. Paid: a tuition centre group class, an agency roster, a freelance tutor from a community group, an international marketplace, or an online one-to-one service. Free: the school's own subject clinic, the KHDA inspection report for the school, and the paper-level breakdown of the last mock. Most families compare the paid options on price and use none of the free ones, which is the wrong way round, because the free ones tell you which paid option you need.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre near Ibn Battuta a good option for Year 11?
faqs.answer: For structure, pace and momentum, yes, and it prices well below one-to-one. For a diagnosed problem, no. A group class delivers content set in advance to the middle of the room, so a student losing marks because their extended answers describe rather than explain will sit through a syllabus review that never addresses it. Many families here get the best result from both: a centre revision course for breadth, plus one weekly one-to-one session on the subject that is not moving.

faqs.question: What does a neighbour's tutor recommendation really tell me?
faqs.answer: That the tutor turned up, was pleasant and that the family felt better afterwards. Those are worth knowing. What it does not tell you is whether the tutor taught the right exam board, or whether a grade moved for a reason connected to the tutoring, because most families cannot attribute a grade change to one intervention when the student is also maturing and the school is also teaching. Use a recommendation to shortlist, then ask the board and code question yourself.

faqs.question: How do I compare two tutors quoting the same rate?
faqs.answer: With six questions, none about price. Which board and syllabus code do you teach? What is each paper worth? Where do students lose marks in this subject? How do you mark a timed paper? What will you not do with assessed work? Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? Listen for the code rather than a reassurance that the syllabuses are similar, and for a mark-scheme answer rather than a hard-topic answer. The differences at one rate are usually larger than between rates.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects have no local provision in this corridor?
faqs.answer: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Mathematics, Arabic as a first language, Computer Science to any depth, and the smaller humanities entries. Centres rarely run them because the cohort is too small, and few local freelancers have taught them recently. These are the clearest cases where online matching is a practical necessity rather than a preference, because the constraint is the citywide supply of those specialists rather than anything about this community.

faqs.question: Does Discovery Gardens have fewer tutoring options than nearby communities?
faqs.answer: It has more centre provision than most of the corridor, because Ibn Battuta and The Gardens are next door, and about as few resident subject specialists as anywhere. Dubai Investments Park is the one nearby place where a locally based specialist is reasonably likely, because several of this corridor's schools are there and teachers are in the area during the day. Jebel Ali and the southern districts have the thinnest local supply in either model.

faqs.question: Can a tutoring centre tell me whether my child is on the right tier?
faqs.answer: Usually not, because that requires reading several pieces of this student's marked work against the tier demands, and a group class does not involve anyone doing that. The school is the primary source, since it makes the entry recommendation, and an individual tutor reading three marked papers can give a second view. Core and Foundation entries cap the grade, and post-16 study usually needs grade 6 or 7, so the question deserves answering in Year 10 rather than Year 11.

faqs.question: Why does the school's subject clinic get overlooked?
faqs.answer: Because it is not advertised and it feels like asking a favour. In most schools in this corridor it exists, and the teacher who set and marked the assessment is better placed than anyone to explain the marking of it. Its limits are real: a few minutes per student, not a programme, and no capacity for the volume of marked practice a Year 11 student needs. But for a single question about a specific marked answer it is both free and immediate.

faqs.question: Are small groups of two or three students good value?
faqs.answer: When the students genuinely match on subject, level and weakness, yes, and the lower per-student rate is a real saving. When they do not, one student pays a rate only slightly below one-to-one to watch the other get taught. Before agreeing to a pairing, ask what the other student's current grade and specific difficulty are. If the answer is vague, decline, because it means nobody has matched them on anything other than availability.

faqs.question: Should I worry if a tutoring website shows a UAE address or a foreign number?
faqs.answer: Check both. Two of the most visible competitor pages in this market route UAE parents to Indian phone numbers, and one shows a Dubai footer address on a page written for Abu Dhabi. A page can look local without anything behind it being local. Ask directly who will teach, from where, and in which time zone. For the record, IB Gram has no office, centre or branch in the UAE, and we say so rather than implying otherwise.

faqs.question: Can a tutor charge me for their UAE permit?
faqs.answer: No, because it is free. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest way to find out what my child actually needs?
faqs.answer: A single diagnostic session on one marked paper, which ends with a written statement of what pattern connects the lost marks. Many families in this community buy exactly that and nothing else, take the findings to the subject teacher, and decide afterwards. At published Dubai rates of AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified tutor, it is the least expensive way to avoid buying the wrong model for a term, which is the real cost in this market.

faqs.question: Do group revision courses work for English Literature?
faqs.answer: For set-text teaching, yes. For exam preparation, only partly, and this is the subject with the widest gap between group and individual value. A literature grade moves through repeated timed essay practice with marked feedback, and nobody can mark thirty students' essays weekly. If a group course is sold as examination preparation in this subject, ask specifically how much of the student's own writing will be marked and returned, and judge the answer.

faqs.question: When should I book, whichever option I choose?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary, and for structural reasons rather than urgency. Centres fill their revision courses before study leave, and one-to-one specialists in the common subjects fill during the four weeks of study leave before the June series, when every Year 11 family in Dubai is looking at once. The quietest and easiest time to secure anything is the UAE summer and early autumn, when November-series candidates are the only demand in the market.

faqs.question: Is there a case where you would tell me not to hire you?
faqs.answer: Several, and they are on this page. If you want group structure and motivation at a lower unit cost, a centre is the better buy. If you need a physically present adult for a child under about eight, we cannot provide that in the UAE. If the household needs supervision rather than teaching, a cheaper service is the honest answer. And if your question is a single query about one marked answer, the school's clinic will deal with it today for nothing.

faqs.question: What one document makes all of this easier?
faqs.answer: The entry list from the school's exams officer, naming the board, syllabus code and tier for every subject. With it, any provider in any model can be evaluated in five minutes, because you can ask them to describe the papers for that code and listen to whether they can. Without it, the most expensive option in the city can be aimed at the wrong papers and nobody finds out until the mock. It is free and it takes one email to request.

intro.heading: When a tutoring session actually fits in a Downtown week
paragraphs: Most tutoring plans in this corridor fail on logistics rather than teaching. The campuses a Downtown family uses are spread from Al Quoz to Al Safa to Nad Al Sheba, and they do not finish at the same time. A school day ending at 2.45pm and a school day ending at 3.30pm produce different evenings, and a bus route adds thirty to fifty minutes on top of either. A Year 11 student from Kent College Dubai and one from Safa British School may live in the same tower and be free at completely different hours.

Work forward from the real finish time rather than from an ideal. Add the journey, then twenty minutes for food and a change of clothes, and the earliest honest start for most students in this corridor is 4.15pm to 4.30pm. That window stays open until about six, when families eat and younger siblings need attention. The second window opens around 7.30pm and closes when concentration does, usually by nine. Those two windows are the whole of the available week, and every tutoring decision sits inside them.

Which window suits depends on the year group more than the student. Year 10 generally works better at the earlier slot, before fatigue sets in and while the content load is still manageable. Year 11 in the exam term almost always works better later, because the afternoon disappears into school revision sessions, past papers set by teachers, and the simple need to decompress for an hour after a long day. A plan that insists on 4pm in March of Year 11 tends to be abandoned by April.

The school run also decides which format can hold a slot at all. A tutor travelling in from another district has to leave their own home in peak traffic to reach a tower at 4.30pm, and if the road fails they arrive at 4.50pm and the hour becomes forty minutes. Over a twelve-week term that is a lost fortnight. A session delivered over live video starts when it says it will, which is worth more in April of Year 11 than almost anything else on a tutor's profile.

So the position here is simple and stated plainly: IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Downtown Dubai address, because home visiting is a service offered only in India. IGCSE support reaches a student in this corridor as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around the real finish time of the real school, and held in the same slot week after week. One consequence worth stating in the same breath: because the lesson is held on a shared screen, the marked work, the recording and the session note all exist as files afterwards, which is the part of the arrangement a parent can actually audit.

programmes.description: Mocks in the winter, coursework deadlines in the spring, then study leave and the June series. The afternoon is consumed by school revision sessions from January onward, which pushes tutoring into the later window. Past papers replace content teaching from about February.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-downtown-du.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects most often requested across this corridor, with the syllabus code and a note on how much weekly time each realistically needs. Time, not enthusiasm, is the limiting factor in a Year 11 week.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Benefits most from short regular contact rather than long occasional sessions, because fluency decays. One hour a week with set practice between sessions beats a three-hour weekend block. Extended tier work on unstructured multi-step problems needs the student fresh, which argues for the earlier slot.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity, circuits and electromagnetism absorb the most time, and the practical paper rewards precise written method. A tired student at 8.30pm can still do past-paper recall work but struggles with new derivations, so content teaching belongs in the earlier window.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations need concentration and repetition, which makes them a poor fit for a late slot. Organic chemistry pattern work and qualitative analysis recall survive the evening better. Splitting the subject across the two windows by task type is more effective than picking one.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: The most forgiving subject to schedule late, because much of the gain comes from command-term discipline and data interpretation rather than new abstraction. Volume means it rewards little-and-often, and a weekly forty-five minutes is often enough alongside school teaching.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science (Cambridge 0654 / 0653)
subjects.description: Three disciplines in one timetable slot at school, which is exactly why students fall behind in whichever one their teacher moves through fastest. Tutoring here is triage: find the discipline costing marks and use the hour on that rather than rotating evenly.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Needs a slot long enough for a piece of timed writing plus feedback, which makes a cramped 4.15pm session frustrating. The later window suits it, and work between sessions can be reading rather than writing, which fits a full week better.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Speaking practice is easier to schedule than written work because it needs less recovery time, and a student will talk at 8pm when they will not write. Error-pattern feedback on short written tasks is the efficient use of the remaining minutes.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 / 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study and diagram work both need the student alert, and both reward short frequent sessions over long ones. Students in this corridor often take one of the two as a ninth subject, which means it is the first thing dropped from the revision timetable and the first thing tutoring has to protect.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students aiming at A Level Mathematics. Calculus arrives here for the first time and needs the earlier window, because the step from procedural algebra to differentiation is the kind of new abstraction a tired student cannot absorb.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Theory paper content is heavier than students expect and the practical programming skills need uninterrupted time at a keyboard. A video lesson with a shared screen suits this subject unusually well, because the tutor can watch the code being written rather than the finished file.

sections.heading: The school day across this corridor, and the earliest session that works
paragraphs: A direct answer first. Across the campuses a Downtown family typically uses, the school day ends between roughly 2.45pm and 3.30pm, and once the journey, food and a change of clothes are accounted for the earliest realistic tutoring start is 4.15pm to 4.30pm. Families who book 3.45pm because the school finishes at 3pm are booking a session the student arrives at late, hungry and unable to concentrate, and they usually stop within a month.

The variation between campuses is larger than parents expect. A school in Al Quoz is a short run from the towers at the right hour and a long one at the wrong one. Al Safa and Jumeirah campuses sit on the busiest afternoon direction out of the corridor. Nad Al Sheba and Sobha Hartland are further in kilometres but move more freely. A student who takes the school bus rather than a parent's car adds thirty to fifty minutes regardless, because the route serves a dozen other families first.

This is the information a near me search is actually reaching for, and no competitor page in this market publishes it. The table below works the arithmetic through for each part of the corridor, from finish time to journey to earliest honest start. It is the opposite of a tutor directory: it tells a parent what slot to ask for before they ask anybody for anything.

The second column of that table is what makes format matter. A tutor who has to drive into the towers for a 4.30pm session is trying to cross the city during the same pick-up hour the student is travelling home in. A tutor who logs in has no such problem, which is why a video lesson can hold the earlier window and a visiting tutor often cannot.

sections.heading: Which schools this neighbourhood feeds, and which boards they run
paragraphs: A Downtown address does not correspond to a single catchment, which is the first thing that separates Dubai from the cities most parents moved from. Within the same tower you will find children at a British-curriculum school in Al Quoz, an IB continuum school in Sobha Hartland and a bilingual campus in Al Jaddaf. There is no default school, and there is therefore no default tutoring plan for the building.

What this means practically is that the board has to be established before the subject. Hartland International School, North London Collegiate School Dubai, Kent College Dubai, Safa British School and Citizens School all serve this corridor and all sit inside the British-curriculum market, but a British-curriculum school may run Cambridge IGCSE, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, or a mixture by subject. Mixtures are common and are the single most frequent cause of a student revising from the wrong past papers.

The market context is worth stating because it explains why the corridor is this crowded. Dubai had 387,441 private school students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum accounting for 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian 26 per cent and US 14 per cent. Seven more private schools open for 2026-27, four of them UK curriculum, adding 16,846 places in total after a year in which enrolment rose six per cent.

The question to ask the school office, once, is short: which board, which syllabus code, which tier. Written down on a note in a kitchen drawer, that answer is worth more to a tutoring plan than any amount of searching for somebody nearby.

sections.heading: The IGCSE year counted backwards from the June series
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a calendar, which is strange given that an exam year is the one thing every IGCSE family has in common. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November, with a November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026 and provisional timetables published ahead of each series.

Counted backwards from a June series, the useful milestones are not exam dates at all. They are the entry deadline the school works to, the mock window in January or February, the internal coursework deadlines where those apply, the start of study leave, and the point in the spring at which switching tier stops being possible. Every one of those is set by the school or the board rather than by a tutor, and every one of them should be in the plan before term starts.

Results timing closes the loop. June 2026 Pearson results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. So a June candidate who misses a target learns in late August and can enter the November series for a result in January, inside the same academic year. That is a genuinely useful second route and most families do not know it exists until it is too late to use.

One instruction overrides the table below: use the live official timetable from the board, because provisional timetables are revised and a date restated on a tutoring page can be out of date by the time it is read. Cambridge is explicit that centres sit in one of six administrative zones, that it is essential to use the correct version for the zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam.

sections.heading: Ramadan, breaks and the weeks a plan quietly loses
paragraphs: A twelve-week term on paper is rarely twelve weeks of teaching in practice, and this is where a plan written in September falls apart in February. Dubai's academic year runs from late August or early September to late June for most schools, with a substantial winter break in December, a spring break around the end of March and a short autumn half-term. Each of those removes a week or more, and none of them is a surprise.

Ramadan is the variable that most tutoring plans ignore. School days shorten, energy in the late afternoon drops, and families eat at Iftar rather than at seven. For the weeks it covers, the early window effectively closes and the sensible slot moves to after Iftar. Families who try to hold a 4.30pm session through Ramadan usually cancel two of four, and a cancelled session in the spring term of Year 11 is the most expensive kind there is.

Study leave is the third quiet loss. Once Year 11 students go on study leave before the June series the school timetable disappears, which sounds like more tutoring time but often produces less, because the structure that got a student to a session has gone with it. The fix is to agree the study-leave schedule in advance, in writing, including which days carry a double session and which are left clear.

Added up, a plan that accounts for breaks, Ramadan and study leave in September typically delivers thirty to thirty-four teaching weeks across the year. One that does not usually delivers in the low twenties, and the shortfall lands precisely in the spring when it matters most.

sections.heading: Mandatory UAE subjects and the timetable space they occupy
paragraphs: Parents new to Dubai are often surprised to find subjects on a report card that are not part of the British curriculum at all, and then surprised again when those subjects take timetable space away from IGCSE revision. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The rules are unusually specific, which makes them easy to plan around once known. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit; schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited.

Language of instruction is set too. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Schools are required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

For a tutoring timetable the consequence is twofold. These subjects occupy real weekly hours that cannot be reallocated to IGCSE revision, so the available homework time is smaller than a parent assumes. And support in them must follow the school's own scheme of work, because the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the MoE is strictly prohibited.

sections.heading: Equivalency and attestation, the paperwork a Downtown leaver needs later
paragraphs: The part of the IGCSE year nobody explains in Year 10 is what happens to the certificate afterwards. A student who leaves a Downtown Dubai school and applies to a UAE university, or who needs a school record recognised for any official purpose here, goes through the Ministry of Education's equivalency process, and that process counts subjects rather than admiring them. It is worth knowing the shape of it while there is still time to change a subject choice, because by the time the certificate arrives the count is fixed.

On the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or International GCSE subjects at no less than grade E, or grade 3 on the numbered Pearson scale, and Arabic and Islamic Education are excluded from that five even though they sit on the report card. Above that sits one accredited A-Level at grade E, or two AS-Levels at the same grade. Read those two sentences together and a practical rule falls out: a student carrying four examined IGCSE subjects plus Arabic and Islamic Education has not met the count, however good the grades look.

That matters most for the families in this corridor who arrive partway through, because an arriving student sometimes drops a subject to make the timetable work, and dropping the fifth examined subject is a different decision from dropping the sixth. Ask the school, in writing, how many accredited subjects your child is entered for and which of them count. The exams officer can answer it in a line, and the answer is more useful than any projected grade.

Attestation is a separate step from equivalency and it is the one families discover last, usually in the week they need it. Rather than restate a procedure that changes, the honest instruction is to ask the school registrar which authority attests documents for your curriculum and in which order the stamps are collected, and to start collecting them before the certificate is needed rather than after. We do not handle attestation and no tutoring company should claim to; what a tutor can do is make sure the subject count was right while it was still a choice.

sections.heading: What a near me search cannot tell you about a tutor
paragraphs: Distance is the one attribute a map can show and the least useful one on the list. What decides whether an hour is worth paying for is whether the tutor has taught the exact syllabus and tier, whether they mark against the published criteria rather than their own instinct, whether they set work between sessions and read it, and whether they hold the slot. None of that appears on a map, and a listing sorted by proximity actively hides it.

The permit question is checkable and almost never asked. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule.

There is one more question worth asking, and it concerns the tutor's relationship to the school. ADEK's professional-ethics rules in Abu Dhabi prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar. A tutor offering to teach your child privately while teaching them in class is proposing a conflict, not a shortcut.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and it runs no UAE office. The regulators are named here so a parent can check things for themselves, which is the only reason to name them.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE session realistically start after school in Downtown Dubai?
faqs.answer: For most students in this corridor, 4.15pm to 4.30pm. Campuses used from the Downtown towers finish between about 2.45pm and 3.30pm, the journey back takes twenty-five to fifty minutes by car and longer on a school bus, and a student needs twenty minutes to eat and change. Families living in Al Quoz or Sobha Hartland, where the school is minutes away, can often manage 4pm. Booking 3.45pm because school ended at 3pm produces a session the student arrives at late and distracted, and those plans rarely survive a month.

faqs.question: Which evening window works better for a Year 11 student in this corridor?
faqs.answer: The later one, from about 7.30pm to 9pm, from January onward. By the spring term the afternoon is taken by school revision sessions and teacher-set past papers, and a student who has been working since eight in the morning needs an hour's gap before doing more. The later window also suits the work Year 11 actually needs: timed questions, marked-script review and English writing feedback. Year 10 is the opposite, and generally does better in the earlier window while new content is still being taught.

faqs.question: Does the school bus change when we should book a tutor?
faqs.answer: Significantly. A bus route serves several communities before reaching the towers, which commonly adds thirty to fifty minutes to the journey compared with a parent collecting at the gate. A student finishing at 3pm and taking the bus may not be home until a quarter past four, which makes a 4.30pm session tight and a 4pm session impossible. The practical step is to time the arrival for a week before fixing a slot, then set the session fifteen minutes after the latest arrival rather than the average one.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our building in Downtown Dubai after school?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. Home visits are not offered anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Support here is delivered as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time. On the timing question specifically, that is an advantage rather than a compromise: a tutor who has to drive into the towers during the pick-up hour is competing for the same roads your child is travelling home on, and a session that starts on the minute every week is worth more in the exam term than one that starts when the traffic allows.

faqs.question: How do I find out which exam board my child's school actually uses?
faqs.answer: Ask the school office or look at the curriculum letter for the year group, and ask for the syllabus code rather than the subject name. Schools in this corridor commonly mix Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel across subjects, so the answer may be different for Maths and for Physics in the same timetable. Write it down with the tier, Core or Extended for Cambridge and Foundation or Higher for Edexcel. That one note prevents the most common waste in IGCSE revision, which is a term spent on past papers from the wrong board.

faqs.question: How many teaching weeks does an IGCSE year in Dubai really have?
faqs.answer: Thirty to thirty-four if the plan accounts for the calendar, and often in the low twenties if it does not. The year runs from late August or early September to late June for most Dubai schools, with a short autumn half-term, a long December break and a spring break around the end of March. Ramadan shortens school days and moves the workable session to after Iftar for several weeks. Study leave before the June series removes the school structure that got a student to a session. Plan for all four in September.

faqs.question: When should we switch from weekly hours to full timed papers?
faqs.answer: Around eight to ten weeks before the series, and in a longer slot than a school night allows. The exercise that moves grades at that stage is a complete paper written under timed conditions followed by a mark-by-mark review against the published criteria, and that needs about two continuous hours. In this corridor that usually means replacing the weekday hour with a Friday or Saturday double rather than adding to it. Doing it any earlier wastes papers; doing it any later leaves no time to act on what the first one shows.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach two children in the same household at different times?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a common arrangement in this corridor where siblings attend different campuses with different finish times. One child takes the early window and the other the later one, with the same tutor across both where the subject and tier allow. Shared sessions only work when both students sit the same board and the same tier, because Core and Extended need different past papers and a mixed pair means one of them is working on material they will never be examined on.

faqs.question: What happens to our slot if the school moves an exam or adds a revision class?
faqs.answer: The slot moves for that week and returns afterwards, which is easier to arrange when nobody has planned a journey around it. Schools in the spring term add revision sessions, move mocks and occasionally change study-leave dates at short notice. A plan that treats the weekly slot as fixed but the individual week as flexible absorbs that; a plan built around a travelling tutor's route often cannot, because the tutor's other bookings sit in the same afternoon corridor.

faqs.question: Why do subjects like Arabic and Islamic Education appear on an IGCSE report card?
faqs.answer: Because they are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is counted in forty-minute lesson units and schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, with combined classes prohibited. For planning, the point is that these lessons occupy real weekly hours, so a student's available homework time is smaller than a parent assumes when counting only IGCSE subjects.

faqs.question: Can we get support in Arabic or Social Studies alongside IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one condition that comes from the regulator rather than from us. Support in the mandatory UAE subjects has to follow the school's own scheme of work, because the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the MoE is strictly prohibited. Schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. A tutor proposing their own alternative syllabus for these subjects has misunderstood the rule, and the work would not help the school grade.

faqs.question: Is the November series worth using if June goes badly?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is underused because families do not know the timing. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in November, with the November 2026 final timetable from late October to 19 November 2026, and November results reach students in January: November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. June results arrive in late August, so there is time to decide. Cambridge candidates in the UAE use June and November as well. Confirm all dates against the board's live official timetable, which is revised from provisional versions.

faqs.question: How much notice do you need to change a session time?
faqs.answer: Ask any provider this before booking, and get the answer in writing, because it is where published rates and real costs diverge. The practical issue in this corridor is that school events, mock reschedules and traffic produce several changes a term, and a cancellation policy written for a travelling tutor is necessarily stricter than one for a video lesson. Ask what notice is required, what a missed session costs, whether an unused session can be moved rather than lost, and whether the weekly slot is held while a family pauses for school exams.

faqs.question: Does my child need a tutor at all, or just a better revision timetable?
faqs.answer: Genuinely sometimes the second, and an honest first session will say so. A student who knows the content but loses marks on command terms, unshown working or timing does not need twenty hours of teaching; they need technique work and a timetable they will keep. The way to tell is to have a subject specialist mark their most recent real school paper and separate the content gaps from the technique losses. That is one paid hour, it produces a written answer, and a fair number of families leave it knowing they need less than they feared.

intro.heading: What the weeks between now and the June series can actually deliver
paragraphs: Every family searching for an IGCSE tutor from Academic City is working to the same fixed point. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a page telling a Dubai parent to prepare for a February exam is handing them a date for the wrong country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November.

That fixed point is what makes the question answerable. Twenty weeks out, a missing topic can be rebuilt properly, tiering can still be argued about, and the student has time to sit full papers under timed conditions more than once. Eight weeks out, rebuilding a topic from nothing is no longer realistic, and the honest plan becomes technique: command terms, working shown, timing per mark, and systematic work on the two or three question types that keep costing marks. Both plans are worth buying. They are not the same plan.

The reason to say this plainly is that most tutoring sold in Dubai in the spring is sold as though it were the twenty-week version at the eight-week point. A tutor who says yes to everything in March is either not reading the calendar or not telling you what they see. The first session with us is diagnostic for exactly this reason: two timed papers marked against the published mark scheme, and then a statement of what the remaining weeks can and cannot do.

Geography matters less than the calendar here, which is fortunate, because Academic City is not well supplied with international-specification subject specialists. The free zone was built around university campuses; Dubai English Speaking College inside it runs the British route, and the rest of this cluster's families travel to schools in Silicon Oasis, Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais. IB Gram delivers one-to-one lessons live online and does not send tutors to homes in the UAE, which is an India-only service.

There is one more calendar fact worth absorbing before the plan. Demand for IGCSE tutoring in this emirate is not spread evenly; it spikes in the fortnight after mock results and again in the final weeks before the papers. Those are exactly the weeks when the fewest subject specialists have a free slot, so the family that books latest pays a specialist rate for whoever remains. Booking earlier does not change the hourly figure at all. It changes which tutors are still available to take the work. What follows is the calendar in usable form. The series counted backwards with who sets each deadline. A term-by-term map of Years 10 and 11, so you can see which term you are actually in rather than which one you hoped for. An eight-week sprint broken down week by week. How to read a mock result forensically instead of emotionally. And the November resit decision, which is a different decision from the one most families think they are making.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-acade.programmesIntro: Which term your child is in changes everything about what tutoring is for. These are the four positions families in this cluster write to us from.

programmes.name: Year 10, first term
programmes.description: The cheapest and most effective place to start, and the one almost nobody uses. There is time to rebuild foundations, to practise at the intended tier, and to gather the evidence needed if a tier change is worth arguing for. Nothing is urgent, which is exactly why it works: the student can be taught rather than drilled.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Academic City and Silicon Oasis who start here typically buy fewer total hours across the two years than those who start after the Year 11 mocks, because the work is building rather than repairing. The practical ask at this point is narrow: one subject, one session a week, and a clear statement of which topics are not secure.

programmes.name: Year 11, first term
programmes.description: Content is still being taught but the end is visible. This is the last point at which a genuinely missing topic can be rebuilt without stealing time from revision. It is also when past-paper work should begin in earnest rather than being saved for after the mocks, which is the single commonest planning error at IGCSE.
programmes.countryNote: In this cluster the first term of Year 11 collides with school internal deadlines for any coursework components, and with mock preparation in some schools. Ask the school for the mock timetable and the coursework deadlines in September, and plan the term against both rather than against the examination date alone.

programmes.name: After the Year 11 mocks
programmes.description: The most common starting point and a workable one, provided the mock paper itself is used as the diagnosis. The mock is not a grade; it is a document showing where marks were lost question by question. A family that brings the marked paper to the first session saves two sessions of exploratory work.
programmes.countryNote: Mock results in Dubai schools typically arrive in the second term, leaving a defined run to the June series. That run is enough for technique, targeted topic repair and timed practice. It is not enough to cover a syllabus that was never learned, and a tutor who implies otherwise at this stage is selling rather than teaching.

programmes.name: November resit
programmes.description: A subject taken again in the November series after a June result below a sixth-form requirement. Cambridge and Pearson both run November sessions, so the gap is roughly five months rather than a year. Entry goes through the school or an approved centre, and the registration deadline sits months before the exam window.
programmes.countryNote: The resit decision should be made on the component breakdown, not the grade. Request it from the school as soon as results are out. June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which gives a sense of how the two series sit relative to a sixth-form start date.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-acade.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is described in terms of what the remaining weeks should target, because at this stage the question is not what the syllabus contains but where the recoverable marks are.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / 0980)
subjects.description: Fastest recoverable marks: showing working, avoiding early rounding, and attempting the final long questions partially rather than leaving them blank. Topic repair in the remaining weeks should prioritise algebra and trigonometry, which appear across both papers rather than in one place.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two equally weighted papers, calculator allowed throughout, so non-calculator drilling is wasted time here. The recoverable marks sit in the extended multi-step problems at the end of each paper, which reward a partial attempt far more than most students believe.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism carry the heaviest load and the most confusion. In the final weeks the quickest gains are equation selection, unit discipline, and rewriting descriptive answers as causal explanations. Check whether the school entered a practical paper or the alternative-to-practical.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Moles calculations and electrolysis repay targeted drilling more than any other topic at this stage. Practical-skills questions reward exact vocabulary for separation techniques and gas tests, which is memorisable in a fortnight and worth several marks.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The problem is volume rather than difficulty, so the final weeks should be spent on command terms and on data and graph questions rather than on re-reading notes. Genetics questions reward drawing the cross out on paper every time.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: Revise by paper section rather than by subject, because the examination moves between biology, chemistry and physics inside a single paper and students lose real time re-orienting. Practising that switching under timed conditions is a specific, teachable skill.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Form is where whole mark bands disappear: a competent essay written when a letter or article was specified scores badly regardless of quality. The other quick gain is quoting economically and analysing a phrase rather than copying a paragraph.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Accuracy beats ambition in the mark scheme: controlled correct sentences score better than complex attempts with errors. Note-taking and summary tasks are the most teachable components and where the fastest movement happens in a short run.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450) and Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Both punish generic answers. In Economics, diagrams must be titled, labelled and referred to in the prose to score at all. In Business Studies the top bands need a justified judgement rather than a list of advantages and disadvantages, which is a writing habit rather than knowledge.

subjects.name: Geography (0460) and History (0470)
subjects.description: Geography marks go missing on case-study specificity: a named place, a figure, a date. History marks go on source answers that discuss content rather than provenance. Both are techniques rather than content and both move quickly in the final weeks.

sections.heading: The series counted backwards, with who sets each deadline
paragraphs: Almost no tutoring page in this market names a session, a deadline or a results date, which is odd given that the calendar is the most useful thing a parent can be handed. Here it is in order, with the body responsible for each milestone, because knowing who sets a deadline tells you who to ask when it moves.

Two sourced reference points give the shape. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, which is why any table like this one should send you to the live official timetable rather than standing in for it.

One Cambridge detail belongs here because it has caused missed papers. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different timetable version for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. If you check dates yourself rather than relying on the school, establish the zone first.

Read the table from the bottom up if you are already inside the final term. The rows below the mock window are the ones you can still act on; the rows above it are the ones to get right for a younger sibling.

sections.heading: A term-by-term map of Years 10 and 11
paragraphs: Families almost always believe they are earlier in this process than they are. The map below exists to settle that question in thirty seconds. Find the term you are actually in, read what is realistic from there, and plan against that rather than against the term you wish you were in.

The pattern worth noticing is how quickly the available options narrow. In the first term of Year 10 you can change tier, rebuild a foundation topic and still have a year of timed practice ahead. By the second term of Year 11 the tier is fixed, the content is nearly complete, and the only lever left is technique. Technique is a good lever - it is worth real marks - but it is one lever rather than three.

The other pattern is that the cheapest intervention is always the earliest one. A tier argument won in Year 10 costs a term of targeted sessions. The same argument lost means a grade ceiling that closes sixth-form options two years later, at which point the remedy is a resit or a different course. This is the clearest case in school education of a small early cost beating a large late one.

Use the map with the school's own calendar beside it. Internal coursework deadlines and the mock timetable are set by the school, not the board, and in this cluster they vary by several weeks between schools a few kilometres apart.

sections.heading: The eight-week sprint, week by week
paragraphs: This is the plan most families in this cluster actually buy, so it deserves to be set out rather than implied. Eight weeks, two sessions a week, one subject. The first week is spent entirely on diagnosis, which feels like a waste and is the opposite: without it the remaining fourteen sessions are spent on whatever the tutor happens to know rather than on what the student is losing marks for.

The middle weeks work the error types the diagnosis found, and there are usually three or four rather than twenty. In mathematics they are typically working not shown, early rounding, and the long final question abandoned. In the sciences, command-term confusion, missing units, and descriptions offered where explanations were asked for. In English, wrong task form. Each of these is worth marks across every paper, which is why technique outperforms content at this stage.

The final fortnight introduces nothing new on purpose. Full papers to time, marked properly, with the error log checked for recurrence. A student who meets unfamiliar content in the last two weeks loses confidence disproportionately, and confidence is worth marks of its own in a three-hour paper.

What the sprint cannot do is replace a year. If your child has not learned electromagnetism, eight weeks of technique will not produce a grade as though they had. We say that at the end of week one in writing, with the realistic range, because the alternative is taking money for an outcome nobody can deliver.

sections.heading: How to read a mock result forensically
paragraphs: A mock grade is almost useless on its own and the marked paper is extremely useful, which is the reverse of how most families treat the two. The grade tells you roughly where the student stands against a boundary that will move. The paper tells you which questions lost marks, how many, and for what reason, and that is the entire basis of a sensible plan.

So ask the school for three things: the marked script, the mark breakdown by question or by paper section, and the mark scheme if they will release it. Then look for pattern rather than for the worst score. Marks lost evenly across a paper usually mean timing or technique. Marks lost in clusters usually mean a topic. Marks lost in the last third of a paper almost always mean pacing, which is the easiest of the three to fix.

The second thing to look for is the difference between papers. A student whose Paper 1 is solid and whose Paper 2 collapsed does not have a knowledge problem; they have a problem with the question style of Paper 2, and that is a fortnight of targeted work rather than a term. Families who skip this analysis buy a general course and pay for the repetition of everything their child already knows.

Bring the marked script to the first session. It saves two sessions of exploratory questioning, which at market rates for a qualified online subject tutor - roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour across this market, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 - is real money.

sections.heading: The November resit decision, made properly
paragraphs: A disappointing June result produces a fast decision, and fast decisions here are usually wrong. The resit question is not 'should we try again' but 'is there a specific, identifiable reason the grade was low, and can that reason be addressed in the available months'. Those are different questions and only the second one has a useful answer.

The evidence you need is the component breakdown, requested from the school as soon as results arrive. A grade built on one collapsed paper is a strong resit case: the problem is named and roughly five months is ample. A grade that was uniformly weak across every component is a weak resit case, because the same preparation repeated produces the same result, and the honest alternative may be a different subject or a different sixth-form route.

The timing matters for sixth-form entry. June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026 - which means a November resit result lands after most sixth-form courses have started. Ask the receiving school in writing whether a conditional place survives until a January result, before entering.

Cambridge and Pearson both run November series and both set entry deadlines months before the exam window. Entry is arranged through the school or an approved centre rather than by a tutoring provider, and if your child's school will not enter them, an approved centre that accepts private candidates is the route. Confirm the Cambridge zone timetable applies to that centre.

sections.heading: Practical and coursework deadlines nobody warns you about
paragraphs: Written papers are the visible deadline and the internal ones arrive first. Several IGCSE subjects carry coursework or internally assessed components - English in some variants, ICT, art, and internally assessed practical work in the sciences - and those deadlines are set by the school, not the board, which means they vary between schools in this cluster by weeks.

The practical science position is worth stating clearly for anyone considering online tutoring. Cambridge sciences carry either a practical examination or the alternative-to-practical paper, and the school chooses. Pearson's 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 have no practical examination and assess experimental skills inside the written papers instead. Apparatus work happens in the school laboratory either way; what a tutor can do is everything around it.

And that turns out to be where the marks are. These papers test identifying variables, choosing a sensible range and interval, stating controls, reading scales to appropriate precision, recording to consistent significant figures, plotting with a sensible scale, drawing a line of best fit rather than joining points, and writing an evaluation that names one specific limitation and one specific improvement. Every item on that list is teachable on a screen with real data.

What we do not do is contribute to internally assessed work. Where the school assesses a piece as the student's own, the tutor teaches the underlying skill and questions the student's write-up, and the student produces it. Nor do we supply board practical papers or mark schemes - we cite and link cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com, which is also the only place certain to hold the current version.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the deadline is close
paragraphs: Pressure is where the boundary gets tested, so it is worth being explicit about where it sits. Wherever a mark is awarded for work your child submits as their own, a tutor may teach the skill the task depends on, explain what the criteria reward, show what a strong response looks like in general terms, and read the student's own draft and comment on it. That is the whole of it.

A tutor may not supply sentences that end up in the submission, rewrite a paragraph into better English, choose the topic, or generate or process the data. The working test is simple: if the student could not explain, unprompted and without notes, why a sentence says what it says, it does not belong there. Applied honestly, this makes coursework sessions slower, because a draft comes back with questions rather than corrections.

This matters commercially as well as ethically. The search results your child's subject sits in include an operator that sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price. The exposure from that is not the seller's. A malpractice finding falls on the candidate, and at sixteen that can mean a subject grade withheld in a series that cannot be retaken before a sixth-form offer lapses.

We also make no promises about outcomes, which belongs in the same section because it is the same kind of honesty. No guaranteed grade, no predicted score published, no claim about improvement. What we will give you in writing at the end of week one is a realistic range and the reasoning behind it, which is a more useful document than a guarantee nobody can honour.

sections.heading: What the calendar does to availability and price
paragraphs: The last calendar fact is a market one. Demand for IGCSE tutoring in Dubai is not spread across the year; it spikes after mock results and again in the final weeks before the series. Those are precisely the weeks when the fewest subject specialists have free slots, which is how a family ends up paying a specialist rate for a generalist and discovering the mismatch in the third session.

The rates themselves, read in October 2026 and attributed to the providers publishing them: budget and university-student online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home one-to-one with travel included runs AED 180 to 500, per Bestimate at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500. Monthly packages seen include AED 799 for eight online sessions.

Booking early does not reduce the hourly figure but it does change what you can buy with it, because in January the specialist who is fully committed in April is still free. That is the whole of the argument for planning, and it is also why we publish our coverage limits: when we cannot staff a combination properly, you need to know before the sprint window closes rather than during it.

On regulation, since the pressure period is when corners get cut: private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tutor work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published. Ask to see the permit, whatever the deadline.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tutor near me in Dubai International Academic City?
faqs.answer: There is one-to-one IGCSE tutoring available for students living in Dubai International Academic City, delivered live online rather than by a tutor travelling to you. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. When a series deadline is close, the online version has a specific advantage beyond the rate: no travel time at either end, so two sessions a week is a realistic commitment rather than a logistical one, and the tutor is chosen for knowing your child's exact specification.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams held for UAE candidates?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only, so ignore any page that tells a Dubai family to prepare for a February exam. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. For scale, Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Always check the live official timetable, since provisional versions are revised.

faqs.question: My child's mocks were in January and the series is in June. Is that enough time?
faqs.answer: It is enough for a great deal and not enough for everything, and which one depends on the marked script rather than the grade. Enough time for technique work, targeted repair of two or three topics, and several full papers under timed conditions. Not enough to learn a syllabus that was never taught. Bring the marked mock to the first session: marks lost evenly across the paper point to timing, marks lost in clusters point to a topic, and those two diagnoses lead to completely different plans.

faqs.question: What can eight weeks of tutoring realistically achieve before a series?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks at two sessions a week, on one subject, reliably recovers technique marks: working shown, command terms answered correctly, units included, timing per mark, and the long final questions attempted rather than abandoned. Across a whole paper that is often worth several marks. What it cannot do is substitute for content never learned. Our first week is diagnostic and ends with a written range and the reasoning behind it, because a tutor who says yes to everything in the final stretch is not reading the calendar.

faqs.question: Should my son resit in November or move on?
faqs.answer: Decide on the component breakdown, not the grade. Request it from the school as soon as results arrive. A grade built on one collapsed paper with the others solid is a strong resit case, because the problem is named and roughly five months is ample. A uniformly weak profile is a weak case, since the same preparation repeated tends to produce the same result. Also check the timing: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, after most sixth-form courses had begun.

faqs.question: What are Cambridge timetable zones and could we get them wrong?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different timetable version for each. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. If you check dates yourself rather than relying on the school, establish which zone your child's centre sits in first. It is a detail almost no tutoring page mentions and it has genuinely caused missed papers.

faqs.question: How do we find out which board and syllabus code my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer for the full entry list: subject, board, syllabus code, tier and option for every paper. It takes them minutes and it is the most useful document you can give a tutor. In this cluster it is common for a single Year 11 student to sit Cambridge in three subjects and Pearson Edexcel in two, and the two boards differ in assessment architecture - Cambridge Physics carries a practical or alternative-to-practical option, Pearson 4PH1 has no practical paper at all.

faqs.question: Can online sessions prepare my daughter for the alternative-to-practical paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, because that paper mostly tests things a screen handles well. Identifying independent and dependent variables, choosing a sensible range and interval, stating controls, reading scales to appropriate precision, recording to consistent significant figures, plotting with a sensible scale, drawing a line of best fit rather than joining points, and writing an evaluation naming one specific limitation and one specific improvement. Apparatus handling happens in the school laboratory; the marks in the written practical components sit in that list of skills.

faqs.question: How much does short-notice IGCSE tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Rates do not rise for short notice in this market, but availability collapses, which amounts to the same thing. Read in October 2026: budget online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from 33 to 52; qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; in-home one-to-one with travel runs AED 180 to 500. Those are market figures attributed to the providers named, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Why is it harder to book a tutor after mock results come out?
faqs.answer: Because every family in the emirate reads their mock results in the same fortnight. Demand for IGCSE tutoring in Dubai spikes twice, after mocks and again in the final weeks before a series, and those are exactly the weeks when subject specialists have the fewest free slots. The practical consequence is that families booking late often pay a specialist rate for a generalist. Booking in the first term does not reduce the hourly rate; it changes which tutors are still available to you.

faqs.question: Can my child do two sessions a week alongside school in this area?
faqs.answer: From Silicon Oasis or Mirdif, where schools sit inside the district, yes comfortably - a 4.45pm start works. From Academic City, 5pm is realistic. From International City, where children travel out to Al Warqa or Mirdif, 6pm is the honest earliest weekday start, so one weekday session plus a weekend morning usually works better than two weekday evenings. Weekend mornings are the right slot for full timed papers anyway, because a three-hour paper cannot be sat properly at seven in the evening.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a MoHRE permit even for a short run of sessions?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the deadline is not a reason to skip the question. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so disregard any amount quoted at you. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents and university students.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help finish coursework that is due next week?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skill the task depends on, explain what the criteria reward, and read your child's own draft and comment on it, including under deadline pressure. A tutor cannot supply sentences, rewrite a paragraph into better English, choose the topic, or generate or process the data. The test is whether your child could explain without notes why each sentence says what it says. One operator in these search results sells completed coursework; a malpractice finding from that falls on the candidate, not the seller.

faqs.question: Will you tell us if the grade we want is not achievable in the time left?
faqs.answer: Yes, in writing, at the end of the diagnostic week. You get the recurring error types the tutor found, what the remaining weeks will target, and a realistic range with the reasoning. We publish no guaranteed grades and no predicted scores, because no provider can honour either. That note is more useful than a guarantee anyway: it tells you whether to buy eight weeks of technique work, to change the plan, or to consider the November series instead and prepare properly.

faqs.question: Do you provide past papers for the remaining weeks?
faqs.answer: We cite and link the official sources on cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com rather than distributing copies, because that material belongs to the boards and reproducing it is a copyright matter. The official site is also the only place certain to hold the current version rather than a syllabus two revisions old. Schools hold past papers and will usually release them to candidates on request, and your child's subject teacher is the fastest route to the specific ones that match their tier and option.
