dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-creek.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors who cover IGCSE for families around Dubai Creek Harbour: Cambridge and Edexcel subject specialists who teach the paper your child is actually entered for, with evening availability that survives a 15:30 bell and a Ras Al Khor crossing.

intro.heading: What a Creek Harbour parent is really searching for
paragraphs: Dubai Creek Harbour has apartments, a marina, a promenade and, as of the current academic year, no private school inside its own boundary. Every secondary-age child who lives there travels out each morning: across Ras Al Khor to Dubai Festival City, down Al Khail Road to Sobha Hartland and Nad Al Sheba, or along the Creek towards Al Jaddaf. That single fact shapes everything about tutoring in this neighbourhood. The bottleneck is never the quality of teaching available in the UAE. It is the ninety minutes between the school bell and a child who can still concentrate.

So when a parent searches for an IGCSE tutor near me in Dubai Creek Harbour, the useful answer is not a list of names with pins on a map. It is a timetable. A Year 11 student at Deira International School finishes around 15:10 and is usually home by 16:00 if the Ras Al Khor crossing behaves. A student at Repton School Dubai or Kent College Dubai in Nad Al Sheba can be twenty minutes later. A child doing a co-curricular session on Tuesdays is home at 17:30 and has homework before anything else. A tutor who physically drives to the apartment has to fit into that window too, plus their own travel from wherever the previous family lives.

IB Gram removes the travel from both sides. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, from a tutor who has taught the exact syllabus your child is entered for. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending tutors into homes is a service that exists only in India. That is a deliberate limit, and on a page like this it is worth being blunt about, because it is also what makes the match possible. A Creek Harbour family needing Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 Extended gets a Chemistry specialist, not whichever generalist happens to live within a twenty-minute drive of Ras Al Khor.

The second thing a Creek Harbour parent needs is board accuracy. Dubai's British-curriculum schools do not all use the same examination board, and the difference is not cosmetic. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580, sat as Core or Extended across two written papers. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A is 4MA1, sat at Foundation or Higher tier, also across two papers but with different formula support and a different style of question stem. A tutor who prepares a 4MA1 Higher candidate with 0580 Extended past papers is doing honest work on the wrong material. Before the first lesson we confirm the board, the specification code, the tier and the series the school has entered your child for.

The third is honesty about the calendar. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February/March series is offered in India only, so any page or tutor quoting a March window to a Dubai family has the wrong country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. Entry deadlines sit months in front of the papers, which is why a decision made in the autumn term matters more than one made in the spring. The calendar section below counts the whole thing backwards from the exam to the week a family should be acting.

What follows is written for this neighbourhood specifically: the schools Creek Harbour actually feeds, the time each school day ends, what the Dubai market charges for IGCSE support, how Cambridge and Edexcel differ paper by paper, what KHDA and the MoHRE tutoring permit mean for the person teaching your child, and where the line sits between coaching coursework and doing it. No grade promises. Nothing we cannot show you a source for.

programmes.name: What comes after IGCSE
programmes.description: Creek Harbour's feeder schools split after Year 11 into Cambridge International AS and A Level, Pearson A Level, or the IB Diploma Programme. The choice changes what a strong IGCSE grade needs to look like. An A Level Physics route rewards depth in the mechanics and electricity topics; an IB Diploma route rewards the written fluency and data analysis that the Internal Assessment demands.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students submit proof of five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One competing page in this market publishes a six-subject figure; the sourced rule is five. Verify your own case with the Ministry before acting on any page, including this one.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-creek.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Creek Harbour families most often ask for, with what each one actually assesses and where marks go missing. Where a syllabus code is given, it is the Cambridge code; the Pearson equivalent is named alongside it in lessons.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher tier
subjects.description: Two written papers, no coursework. Extended and Higher candidates lose most of their marks in the same four places: algebraic fractions, transformation of formulae, compound functions and the multi-step probability questions where a tree diagram was never drawn. Method marks are available even when the final answer is wrong, and most students do not claim them.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Mechanics, thermal physics, waves, electricity and magnetism, and atomic physics. The reliable mark-losers are unit conversion inside multi-stage calculations, the difference between a stated law and an applied one, and the six-mark extended-response question where the command term asked for an explanation and received a description.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Atomic structure, bonding, stoichiometry, electrochemistry, organic chemistry and qualitative analysis. Moles arithmetic is where the grade is decided; the second biggest loss is ionic equation balancing under time pressure. Students who can write a half-equation from scratch rather than recall one score consistently higher on Paper 4.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Characteristics of living organisms through to inheritance, ecology and human influence on ecosystems. The content is wide and the trap is recall without precision. Marks are awarded for named structures, named processes and correctly directed arrows on a diagram, not for a general sense of what happens.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Science (Cambridge 0653 / 0654)
subjects.description: Two or three sciences compressed into a smaller award. The content depth is lower but the breadth per paper is higher, so revision needs to rotate rather than block. Students moving from Combined Science into a post-16 single science usually have a real gap in quantitative chemistry and in electricity.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing, plus composition. Marks move when a student stops summarising the passage and starts selecting evidence for an argument. The directed-writing task is scored on audience and form as much as on content, and most lost marks are register errors rather than grammar errors.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0993)
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and an optional speaking endorsement. The listening paper rewards prediction before the audio starts; the writing paper rewards a plan that fixes paragraph purposes in advance. Vocabulary range is scored, so a student who repeats one connective across four paragraphs caps their own band.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: The basic economic problem, allocation of resources, microeconomic decision makers, government and the macroeconomy, and international trade. The data-response question is the discriminator: it needs a diagram drawn correctly, labelled fully, and then referred to in the prose rather than left to speak for itself.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Business activity, people in business, marketing, operations and finance. Case-study application is everything. A generic answer about motivation earns knowledge marks and stops; the same answer anchored to the named firm in the stem earns application and analysis marks too.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Data representation, networks, hardware and software, and algorithm design with pseudocode. Students who can trace a given algorithm by hand, line by line, outscore students who can write code fluently but never check it. The theory paper is where most of the grade is won or lost.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge 0460)
subjects.description: Population and settlement, the natural environment, and economic development, with a skills paper on maps, graphs and photographs. Case-study specificity is the mark scheme's main lever: a named place, a named figure and a named consequence beat three paragraphs of general description.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Functions, quadratics, binomial expansion, differentiation and integration, trigonometry and vectors, taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Mathematics. It is the single best bridge into post-16 maths and the subject where Creek Harbour families most often ask for support in the second half of Year 11.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-creek.regionsTitle: The neighbourhoods around Dubai Creek Harbour, and what the commute does to a session
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-creek.regionsIntro: Creek Harbour sits on the Ras Al Khor side of the Creek, between Al Jaddaf and Nad Al Sheba. Each neighbouring community has a different school pattern and therefore a different realistic session window. These are the ones we schedule around most often.

regions.name: Dubai Creek Harbour
regions.note: Apartment towers and the Creek Beach district, with no private school inside the community. Secondary pupils travel to Festival City, Nad Al Sheba or Al Jaddaf. First workable session slot for most households is 16:45-17:15 GST, later on co-curricular days.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Immediately across the Creek, with Swiss International Scientific School Dubai inside the district. Journeys are short, so Al Jaddaf students often start sessions ten to fifteen minutes earlier than Creek Harbour neighbours on the same bus network.

regions.name: Culture Village
regions.note: Jaddaf Waterfront, sharing the same Creek-side road network. Families here commute to the same Festival City and Sobha Hartland schools and face the same late-afternoon pinch on Al Khail Road heading south.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland and Mohammed Bin Rashid City
regions.note: Home to Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai. Many Creek Harbour pupils are enrolled here, which puts them on Al Khail Road at the worst hour and pushes the first feasible session towards 17:00.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Repton School Dubai, Kent College Dubai and GEMS Modern Academy sit in this corridor. It is the longest routine run from Creek Harbour, and the one where a 16:30 session is realistic only on a half-day.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City and Ras Al Khor
regions.note: Deira International School and Universal American School Dubai are the closest established secondary options to Creek Harbour, reached by the Ras Al Khor crossing. Short distance, but a single bridge incident changes the whole evening.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown Dubai
regions.note: No large private secondary schools inside either district, so pupils travel outward like Creek Harbour pupils do. Parents working here often take the trial lesson themselves from an office before handing the schedule to the family.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Al Quoz 4
regions.note: A mixed industrial and school district including long-established Indian-curriculum schools. Relevant to Creek Harbour families with children on two different curricula in one household, which is a scheduling problem more than a teaching one.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Festival City, Ras Al Khor and Al Jaddaf
schoolClusters.note: The closest secondary cluster to Dubai Creek Harbour, reached across the Ras Al Khor crossing or along the Creek. British and international curricula dominate, with IGCSE taken at 16 before a split into A Level or the IB Diploma. These are the schools whose end-of-day times set the earliest session slot for most Creek Harbour households.

schoolClusters.city: Sobha Hartland, Meydan and Nad Al Sheba
schoolClusters.note: The corridor south of the Creek along Al Khail Road, and the second big destination for Creek Harbour pupils. British-curriculum IGCSE provision is strong here and several of these schools run IB alongside it, which is why mixed-board households in Creek Harbour are common rather than unusual.

schoolClusters.city: Downtown, Al Safa and Al Quoz
schoolClusters.note: A longer run from Creek Harbour but a frequent one for families who enrolled before moving to the Creek. Sessions for pupils travelling this far almost always land after 17:15, and we schedule them on the assumption that homework has not yet been started.

sections.heading: What "IGCSE tutor near me" actually returns in Dubai Creek Harbour
paragraphs: Searching for an IGCSE tutor near me in Dubai Creek Harbour returns a mix of three things: agencies that will send someone to an apartment for a travel-inclusive rate, independent tutors advertising within a few kilometres, and online platforms with no geography at all. None of those categories is dishonest, but only one of them is actually selected on the thing that matters, which is whether the tutor has taught your child's syllabus code and tier before.

Proximity is a weak proxy for fit in this particular neighbourhood. Creek Harbour's secondary population is spread across at least three school clusters on two sides of the Creek, and those schools do not use one board. A tutor who lives in the next tower is still the wrong tutor if your child sits Pearson 4CH1 and their experience is Cambridge 0620, because the papers differ in structure, in the practical-skills route and in how much formula support is given. Distance solves a logistics problem that live video has already solved. It does not solve the specification problem.

IB Gram's position on this is deliberately narrow. Tuition for UAE families is one-to-one, online, over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Dubai Creek Harbour or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is an India-only service. What that limit buys a Creek Harbour family is the whole national pool of specialists rather than the subset within driving range of Ras Al Khor. For a mainstream subject at a popular tier that difference is modest. For Additional Mathematics 0606, for Computer Science 0478, or for a Pearson science at Higher tier, it is the difference between a specialist and a near-miss.
The rest of this page is built around the thing a proximity search is really trying to settle: when the session can happen. That starts with the school run.

sections.heading: The Creek Harbour school run, hour by hour
paragraphs: This is the table nobody writing about tutoring in Dubai bothers to publish, and it is the one that decides whether a weekly slot survives past week three. The end-of-day times below are the routine secondary finish times reported by families in this cluster; they move on half-days, assessment weeks and co-curricular days, and they are not a substitute for your own school's bulletin. What matters is the pattern: the further south and west of the Creek the school sits, the later the first feasible session.

Two operational points follow from it. First, a 16:00 slot is not realistic for a Creek Harbour household unless the child attends a Festival City school and the Ras Al Khor crossing is clear. Booking one anyway produces a student who arrives nine minutes late, eats during the first ten minutes and achieves half a session. Second, the slot should be chosen for the worst normal day of the week, not the best. A family whose Tuesday involves swimming until 17:30 should book at 17:45 every day rather than at 16:45 four days a week and nothing on Tuesday.

The third column is the one parents rarely consider: what the student has already spent before the session starts. A child who has been awake since 05:40 for a 06:50 bus has done a full working day by 16:30. The honest consequence is that a sixty-minute session at 17:00 is worth more than a ninety-minute session at 18:30, and that for a Year 11 in the run-up to a series, one weekend morning session is often worth two weekday evening ones. We build schedules on that basis rather than selling the larger package.

Where a household has two children on two curricula, the sequencing matters more than the timing. Running both sessions back to back on one evening keeps the rest of the week clear and keeps the parent supervising once rather than four times.

sections.heading: Why the nearest tutor is rarely the right tutor for an IGCSE paper
paragraphs: Consider two Year 11 students living in the same Creek Harbour tower. One is entered for Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 Extended. The other sits Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1. Both will be taught mechanics, waves and electricity. Both will answer extended-response questions. And yet the preparation is not interchangeable, because the papers are not built the same way, the formula support differs, and the route by which practical skills are assessed differs. A tutor selected on distance has no reason to know which of the two your child sits.

This is the specific failure mode that a proximity search produces. The tutor is competent, available, close by, and preparing the student for a paper adjacent to the one they will actually sit. It shows up in the mock: the student recognises the content and misreads the question format, loses marks on structure rather than knowledge, and everybody concludes they need more hours. More hours on the wrong paper does not help. The fix is a board and tier confirmation before the first session, which costs five minutes and a photograph of the entry sheet.

The second failure mode is subject depth at the edges of the timetable. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 is taken by a minority of students. So is Computer Science 0478, and so is a separate-science combination at Extended across all three. In a pool bounded by driving distance from Ras Al Khor, the number of tutors who have actually taught 0606 to completion is small. In a national online pool it is not. That is the practical argument for online delivery, and it holds regardless of what a family would prefer in the abstract.

The third is replacement. A tutor who drives to your building and then changes jobs, moves emirate or has a child of their own leaves a hole that takes weeks to fill locally. An online match can be replaced inside the same week, which matters most in the eight weeks before a series, which is exactly when a local tutor is hardest to find.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs around Dubai Creek Harbour
paragraphs: Start with the monthly number, because that is the one a family actually budgets. A single weekly hour with a qualified online subject tutor at Dubai market rates lands somewhere between AED 600 and AED 1,200 a month on Bestimate's published mid-tier estimate for weekly one-hour sessions, and between AED 1,000 and AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Budget provision comes in lower, at roughly AED 240 to AED 600 a month. Those are market figures from a published rate table, not IB Gram's price list, and they are the band against which any quote you receive should be read.

The hourly figures behind those monthly numbers are worth seeing separately, because the spread is wide and the reasons for it are legible. Three of the six strongest competitor pages in this market publish no price at all; two quote in US dollars, a currency Dubai families do not transact in. The table below pulls the published AED figures together with the source that published each one, which is the minimum standard a parent should expect before accepting a number.

The pattern to notice is that the travel premium is real and separable. In-home one-to-one visiting rates in Dubai are quoted from AED 180 to AED 350 by Bestimate and from AED 200 to AED 500 by home-tutor providers, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified tutor online. A meaningful part of that difference is time in a car on Al Khail Road, not teaching quality. For a Creek Harbour family the question is therefore concrete: what does the travel premium buy that live video does not, and is it worth more than the widened choice of specialists that removing travel provides?

IB Gram does not publish an hourly rate on this page, and the reason is not coyness. The right figure depends on subject, level, series proximity and session length, and a fixed number printed on a landing page would be wrong for most of the people reading it. The honest route is the free trial lesson first, one per student, with the quote given after a tutor has seen the work. Nothing is charged before that lesson happens and no card details are taken to book it.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: which IGCSE your child is actually sitting
paragraphs: Dubai's British-curriculum schools are split across two main examination boards for IGCSE, and a family can go three years without ever being told which one their child is entered for. It appears on the entry confirmation, on the statement of entry and on the school's exam-office bulletin. Finding it takes one email and it changes the whole shape of preparation, so it is worth doing before buying a single hour of tuition.

The differences are structural rather than philosophical. Cambridge divides many subjects into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C or 5 and Extended carrying the full range. Pearson tiers mathematics into Foundation and Higher instead, with different formula support. Cambridge science syllabuses have historically offered a practical assessment route; Pearson International GCSE sciences assess practical skills inside the written papers through apparatus, variables and data-handling questions. Neither is harder in the abstract. They are differently harder, and the past papers a student should be working through differ accordingly.

There is a scheduling difference too, and it catches families out. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable per zone, stating plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong zone timetable was used. That is why two Creek Harbour pupils at different schools can sit the same paper at different local times. Any revision plan built from a timetable downloaded without checking the zone is built on sand. We work from the school's own issued timetable.
The table below is the comparison in one view. It is deliberately specific about codes, because the codes are what a parent can check against a statement of entry in thirty seconds.

sections.heading: The exam calendar, counted backwards from the school run
paragraphs: Every tutoring decision a Creek Harbour family makes is really a decision about weeks. The exam date is fixed by the board; the entry deadline is fixed by the school's exam office and sits months earlier; the only variable a family controls is when they start. Counting backwards is more useful than counting forwards, because it converts a vague worry in November into a specific action in a specific week.

For a Cambridge candidate the two series available to UAE students are June and November. The June series is the main one and the November series is the standard resit and retake route. Entries close well in advance of the papers, and late entry carries a fee and, past a point, is refused outright. Internal school deadlines for anything coursework-bearing sit earlier again. For a Pearson International GCSE candidate the pattern is May/June and November, with the November window running from late October through the middle of the month and results arriving in January.

The practical consequence is that the useful question in the autumn term is not "should we get a tutor" but "which series is my child entered for, and has the entry been made". A Year 11 planning a November resit in a single subject needs the entry made in the autumn and the work started before the main series revision begins, because the two overlap badly. A Year 11 sitting the June series has the long winter holiday as the one uninterrupted block of time available, and it is almost always better used for timed papers than for re-reading notes.

We plan against the school's own dates. Where a date below is given as a month, that is deliberate: boards revise published windows, and a month-only reference stays true. Where a past date appears, it is cited so you can check it.

sections.heading: KHDA, the tutoring permit, and what a Creek Harbour parent can verify
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Every school a Creek Harbour child might attend is inspected by KHDA and given a published rating. That rating is a school-level judgement about the school; it is not a judgement about any tutor, and no tutoring provider can inherit it. If a page tells you its tutors carry KHDA endorsement, that is the single most misleading phrase available in this market. IB Gram holds no KHDA approval, accreditation, licence or partnership, and neither does any claim on this page depend on one.

Private tutoring itself is regulated separately, by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The official application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, listed with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you, and none is quoted here.

Two further points a parent can act on. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, a condition the MoHRE permit's code of conduct echoes. So the honest answer to "can we hire my child's own teacher privately" is no, and a provider who offers it is offering something the teacher should refuse.

What this means in practice for a Creek Harbour family: ask whether the individual teaching your child holds the MoHRE permit, ask what the permit category is, and treat any claim of regulator endorsement as a reason to look more carefully rather than less.

sections.heading: Where a tutor's help ends: academic honesty on IGCSE coursework
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than the IB Diploma, but where it exists the boundary is the same and it is not negotiable. A tutor teaches, explains, models technique, asks questions and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not write, complete, substantially rewrite or supply the work. There are providers in this market selling completed assessments; one advertises finished IB Internal Assessments at a fixed price. That is a malpractice trigger for the student, not a shortcut, and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than the seller.

In practice the line is easier to hold than it sounds, because the useful version of help sits entirely on the legitimate side. A tutor can take a student's own draft and mark it against the published criteria. A tutor can explain what a criterion is actually asking for when the wording is opaque. A tutor can model the analysis on a different dataset and then hand the student's own back untouched. A tutor can teach referencing properly, which prevents more honesty cases than any warning does. What a tutor cannot do is type into the document.

The same principle governs materials. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright works and should be referenced and linked, not reproduced or supplied as downloads. In lessons we work from the official source, cited, and we tell students where to find it themselves. A student who can navigate the board's own site is a student who can check a claim, including a claim made by a tutor.

Creek Harbour parents sometimes ask what happens if a school raises a question about work a tutor was involved in. The answer is that we keep a session note recording what was covered and whose work was in front of us, and a parent can hand that to the school. Transparency is cheaper than defence.
bullets: A tutor reviews and gives feedback; the student writes every word submitted

sections.heading: Getting started from Dubai Creek Harbour, including what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The sequence is short. Tell us the subject, the board and specification code, the tier, the series your child is entered for and the two or three evening windows that genuinely work after the school run. We match a specialist, run one free trial lesson, and only then discuss a plan and a quote. Nothing is charged before the trial and no card details are needed to book it. If the trial does not work, you have lost an hour and we have lost an hour, and that is the correct allocation of risk.

The part most providers leave out is what happens when no specialist is free. It does happen, and it happens most for minority subjects in the weeks immediately before a series, which is exactly when demand spikes. Our answer is to say so rather than to place whoever is available. If no tutor with the right specification experience has a slot in your window, we will tell you that, tell you the realistic wait, and offer the nearest honest alternative: a different time slot, a shorter weekly commitment with a specialist who has limited availability, or a different format such as paper-technique work while the subject slot is pending.

There is one more constraint worth naming openly. Scheduling for Creek Harbour runs on Gulf Standard Time and the available evening window is narrow because the school run eats the late afternoon. Families who can use a weekend morning have materially more choice of tutor than families restricted to 17:00 to 19:00 on weekdays, because that window is the busiest in the UAE tutoring day. If your schedule has any flexibility at all, the weekend morning is where it is worth spending it.

Finally, the honest limit on what tutoring can do. Nobody can promise a grade, and this page does not. Nothing on it implies that tutoring is required for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission or for progression at school; those are regulatory and school processes with their own rules, and you should verify them with the authority rather than with a tutoring provider. What a good match can do is turn the hours a student is already spending into marks they can actually claim.

process.title: Tell us the paper, not just the subject
process.description: Subject, board, specification code, tier and the series your child is entered for. A photograph of the statement of entry settles all five in one message. This is the step that prevents the most common failure in this market, which is good teaching aimed at an adjacent paper.

process.title: Give us the real school-run window
process.description: Which school, what time the bus actually gets back to Creek Harbour, and which weekday has the co-curricular fixture. We schedule for the worst normal day rather than the best, because a slot that only works four days in five does not survive the term.

process.title: Match to a specification specialist
process.description: We look for a tutor who has taught your child's exact code and tier to completion, not merely the subject. Where the subject is a minority one such as Additional Mathematics 0606 or Computer Science 0478, the match may take longer and we will say how long before you wait.

process.title: Run one free trial lesson
process.description: Live, one-to-one, in the slot you intend to keep, so you are testing the real arrangement rather than a demonstration. One trial per student, no payment taken beforehand and no card details required to book it. The tutor writes a short note on what they found.

process.title: Plan in weeks, not in hours
process.description: Count backwards from the series to fix how many weeks exist, then decide what each week has to achieve. The output is a topic list that gets shorter, supported by timed papers marked against the published scheme, rather than a package of hours with no finish line.

process.title: Review at the next assessment, and change if needed
process.description: The school's own mock or assessment is the checkpoint. If marks have not moved where the plan said they would, we change the plan or change the tutor. Replacement inside the same week is possible precisely because the match is not bounded by driving distance.

whyPoints.title: The specification, confirmed before the first hour
whyPoints.description: We will not start without the board, code and tier in writing. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers teaching the same mathematics, and a term of preparation aimed at the wrong one shows up only in the mock, when there is no time left to fix it.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built around the Creek crossing
whyPoints.description: Session times are set from the real end of the school day and the real journey home, not from an ideal. For most Creek Harbour households that means a first slot between 16:45 and 17:15, later for Nad Al Sheba and Downtown schools, and a weekend morning where one is available.

whyPoints.description: Removing travel widens the choice of tutor rather than narrowing it. For a minority subject at Extended or Higher tier, the pool within driving range of Ras Al Khor is thin and the online pool is not. That is the concrete benefit of online delivery, stated without decoration.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tutor near me in Dubai Creek Harbour who can come to the apartment?
faqs.answer: Agencies in Dubai do offer visiting tutors, and the market rate for an in-home one-to-one hour runs from around AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's published table, with some home-tutor providers quoting AED 200 to AED 500. IB Gram is not one of them. We deliver one-to-one tuition for UAE families online over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, and we do not send tutors to any UAE address. Home visiting is a service we offer only in India. For Creek Harbour that trade is usually favourable: you lose the visit and gain a specialist in your child's exact syllabus code rather than whoever lives nearby.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start if my child comes back from Dubai Festival City?
faqs.answer: Allow about ninety minutes between the bell and a usable session. Secondary schools in the Festival City and Ras Al Khor cluster finish in the mid-afternoon, and a Creek Harbour child is typically home by 16:00 when the Ras Al Khor crossing is clear. That makes 16:45 a workable first slot. Pupils travelling to Sobha Hartland are better at 17:00, and Nad Al Sheba or Downtown schools at 17:15 or later. Choose the slot for your worst normal weekday, not your best, because the co-curricular fixture is what breaks a weekly arrangement in the third week.

faqs.question: Which schools do Dubai Creek Harbour families actually send their children to?
faqs.answer: No private school currently sits inside Dubai Creek Harbour, so every secondary pupil commutes. The nearest established cluster is across the Ras Al Khor crossing in Dubai Festival City, including Deira International School and Universal American School Dubai. A second cluster runs south along Al Khail Road through Sobha Hartland and Mohammed Bin Rashid City, including Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai, and continues into Nad Al Sheba and Meydan. Swiss International Scientific School Dubai sits just across the Creek in Al Jaddaf. These are named as market context only; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: Which exam board does a Dubai Creek Harbour child's school enter them with, and how do I check it?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exam office directly, or look at the statement of entry. It will name the board and the specification code, and the code is the thing that matters: Cambridge Mathematics is 0580, Pearson Specification A is 4MA1, Cambridge Physics is 0625 and Pearson Physics is 4PH1. One email settles it. It is worth doing before buying any tuition, because the past papers, the tier structure and the way practical science skills are assessed all differ between the two boards, and preparation aimed at the wrong one shows up only at mock time.

faqs.question: Does my child's Cambridge exam timetable depend on where in Dubai the school is?
faqs.answer: It depends on the school's administrative zone rather than its district. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, and it states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. In practice that is why two Creek Harbour pupils at different schools can sit the same paper at different local times. Always print the timetable your child's own school issues, not one downloaded from a general search, and give the tutor the same copy.

faqs.question: Can my child resit an IGCSE paper in November rather than waiting a whole year?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit both of those. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and in November. The November route is the standard resit path. Two things to plan for: the entry has to be made through the school's exam office shortly after the June results, and the results arrive in the new year rather than in August, which matters if a sixth-form or university conversation depends on them. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

faqs.question: Why should I not be looking at the Cambridge February or March series?
faqs.answer: Because it is not available to your child. Cambridge's February/March series is offered in India only. UAE candidates sit the June and November series. This matters because several pages aimed at Gulf parents quote a February or March window and an entry deadline that belongs to the Indian calendar, and a family acting on that date would plan a term of revision towards an exam their school cannot enter them for. If a provider quotes you a March IGCSE window for a Dubai school, treat it as a signal to check everything else they have told you.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tuition cost per month for a Creek Harbour family?
faqs.answer: Taking the monthly view rather than the hourly one, Bestimate's published estimates for a weekly one-hour session run from roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages seen in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices. Our quote follows the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Is the travel premium on a home tutor worth paying in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Decide it as a separate purchase. Online qualified tutors in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour; in-home visiting rates run from AED 180 to AED 500. The gap is substantially the tutor's time in a car, and around Ras Al Khor and Al Khail Road at the school-run hour that time is considerable. What the premium buys is physical presence. What it costs, beyond money, is the size of the pool you can choose from, because a visiting tutor must live within a practical drive. For a minority subject that constraint usually decides it.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram hold KHDA approval for its tutors?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody offering tutoring to your family should claim it. KHDA is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. It regulates and inspects schools. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises and staff, and IB Gram does not hold one. We are not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We explain what each body does and link its own published page.

faqs.question: Does the person teaching my child need a UAE tutoring permit?
faqs.answer: An individual providing private tutoring in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service with no fee and a stated two working days. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you are quoted as unverified.

faqs.question: Can we hire one of my child's own teachers for private lessons instead?
faqs.answer: You should not, and a good teacher will decline. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Beyond the rules, it creates a conflict nobody benefits from: the person teaching the class, setting the internal assessment and marking it should not be paid separately by one family in it. An independent specialist avoids the problem entirely.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help with coursework, or is that against the rules?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach, explain, model and give feedback on work the student has written. A tutor may not write it, complete it, rewrite it to a standard or supply it. That boundary is set by the board's academic-honesty rules and the consequence of breaching it falls on the candidate. Practically, the legitimate help is the useful help: marking a draft against the published criteria, explaining what an opaquely worded criterion is actually asking for, modelling the analysis on a different dataset, and teaching referencing properly. We keep a session note recording whose work was in front of us.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does my child need for UAE equivalency later?
faqs.answer: On the British track, the Ministry of Education's published requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects. One page currently ranking for Gulf parents states six subjects, which does not match the sourced rule. Verify your own case with the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority; IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency.

faqs.question: Eight weeks are left before the Creek Harbour mocks end and the papers begin — can tuition still change anything?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is enough to change marks and not enough to change the amount of content known, so the plan has to be different from a term plan. Start with a timed past paper on the correct board and tier, mark it against the published scheme, and let the marking choose the topics. Then work on claimable marks: method lines, command terms, minute-per-mark timing, and the checking habit in the final five minutes. Expect a shortening list rather than a syllabus review. What nobody can offer you is a promised grade, and this page does not.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor with the right specification is free in our evening slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you, give a realistic wait, and offer the nearest honest alternative rather than placing whoever is available. Scarcity is real and it concentrates in two places: minority subjects such as Additional Mathematics 0606 or Computer Science 0478, and the weeks immediately before a series. The alternatives we offer are a different time slot, a shorter weekly commitment with a specialist who has limited availability, or paper-technique sessions while the subject slot is pending. Weekend mornings reliably widen the choice, because the weekday 17:00 to 19:00 window is the busiest in the UAE tutoring day.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-creek.closingHeading: Start with the paper and the school run, in that order
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-creek.closingBody: If you are searching for an IGCSE tutor near me in Dubai Creek Harbour, the two facts that decide the outcome are which paper your child sits and what time the bus gets home. We will match a specialist who has taught that exact paper, run one free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep, and give you a plan counted backwards from the series rather than a package of hours. Lessons are one-to-one and online on Gulf Standard Time. No grade promises, no regulator claims, and every AED figure on this page attributed to whoever published it.

intro.heading: IGCSE tuition around Dubai Festival City, priced from the bottom up
paragraphs: The cheapest published tutoring in Dubai starts at AED 33 to 52 an hour at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik, both online and both frequently delivered by university students. That band is real, it is legitimate, and most families dismiss it too quickly. For keeping a Year 9 student on top of set work, drilling arithmetic that should have been automatic two years ago, or rebuilding a student's willingness to open a textbook, it is the correct purchase. Paying four times that rate for the same job is not generosity, it is waste.

The band that most Dubai Festival City IGCSE families actually need sits higher. Unitors advertises IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts qualified subject specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, and TutorChase publishes AED 270. What the extra buys is someone who knows which board your child is entered with, what the tier decision has already capped, and where a specific paper takes marks off a specific kind of student. Those are not general teaching skills.

Above that is the in-home band, quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors, with the travel inside the figure. And at the top, a premium named tier at AED 650 an hour from BartyED. Every one of these numbers was published by the named provider and read in October 2026. None of them is an IB Gram price, and we have deliberately not invented one, because a single hourly figure spanning Year 7 English and Extended Chemistry would mislead in both directions.

The interesting part of an IGCSE budget is not the rate, though. It is the quantity. A Year 11 student sits eight or nine subjects and almost never needs tuition in all of them. The commonest overspend in this neighbourhood is a parent reacting to a mixed report by booking three subjects at once, when two of those three were weak for one term and one is weak structurally. One costs a term of tuition. The other costs a grade.

So this page is organised as a budget rather than as a brochure. What the bands are and who publishes them. Which subjects need the specialist end and which do not. What group tuition and tuition centres actually cost against one-to-one. The extras nobody quotes. Where IGCSE money specifically gets wasted in this market. And when in the year the spend has to happen for it to do anything at all.

None of this is an argument for spending less as a principle. It is an argument for spending in the right order. A Dubai Festival City family that buys one diagnosed subject properly in Year 10 usually spends less across the two years than one that buys three subjects reactively in Year 11, and ends up with a better grade profile at the point where sixth-form entry requirements start mattering. The order is the saving.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-festi.programmesIntro: An IGCSE budget only makes sense against what comes before and after it, because spending in the wrong year is the most expensive error available. These are the three stages a Dubai Festival City family is actually budgeting across.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: No external examinations, so nothing is at stake in grade terms, which is exactly why this is the cheapest place to buy. Algebraic fluency, scientific vocabulary and the structure of an extended written answer are all established here. Every one of them resurfaces in an IGCSE paper, and fixing them in Year 9 costs a fraction of fixing them in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Festival City families routinely underspend in Year 9 and overspend in Year 11, which is the wrong way round. A term of budget-band support at AED 45 to 65 an hour aimed at one named weakness in Year 9 prevents a specialist booking at three to five times that rate two years later. The arithmetic is not close.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Externally marked papers at the end of a two-year course, graded 9 to 1 on most Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel syllabuses. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended routes, and the entry decision made during Year 10 caps the grade available. Subjects are usually taken in groups of eight or nine.
programmes.countryNote: This is the band where the money is actually spent, and where quantity matters more than rate. Two well-chosen subjects at the qualified band cost less and achieve more than four subjects at the budget band, because the four will not include the one that was structurally weak. Prioritise before you price.

programmes.name: A Level or IB Diploma after Year 11
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum schools in Dubai split at 16 into A Level or the IB Diploma, with a few offering both. Entry requirements are subject-specific, particularly in mathematics and the sciences, so an IGCSE grade profile either opens or closes a sixth-form route rather than merely describing it.
programmes.countryNote: The financial consequence of an IGCSE grade lands here. A student short of a mathematics requirement either resits in the November series, which costs entry fees and a term of preparation, or changes sixth-form plan. That is the real cost of underspending in Year 10, and it never appears on a tutoring invoice.

programmes.name: Equivalency and the mandatory UAE subjects
programmes.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. Separately, Ministry of Education equivalency for the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count.
programmes.countryNote: Families planning a UAE university route sometimes enter extra subjects out of caution, at real examination cost. The requirement is five, not six, and at least one page currently ranking for UAE tutoring queries states six. Verify on moe.gov.ae; IB Gram does not perform equivalency and cannot affect its outcome.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-festi.subjectsIntro: This grid is written as a spending guide. For each subject it says what level of tutor the work actually needs, because the single biggest saving available to a Dubai Festival City family is not booking the specialist band for work the budget band does perfectly well.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Needs the qualified band in Year 11 and often only the budget band in Year 9. The expensive part is the Extended or Higher tier content: algebraic fractions, functions, vectors and harder trigonometry. Topic-level drilling below that is work a competent generalist can do well.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Qualified band, because the marks lost are structural rather than factual: dropped units in multi-step calculations and six-mark answers that describe an effect without naming the mechanism. Both are taught by someone who has marked the paper, not by someone who knows the physics.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Qualified band, and the best value in the whole IGCSE list, because moles calculations and the Cambridge qualitative analysis tables are learnable procedures. A short focused block on those two areas moves marks faster than a term of general chemistry support.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Qualified band for exam technique, budget band for content recall. Biology punishes imprecise sentences, so the paid skill is teaching a student to name the structure, the process and the consequence. Memorisation itself needs supervision rather than expertise.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Science
subjects.description: Needs a tutor comfortable across all three sciences, which is scarcer and therefore priced higher than a single-science specialist. Worth asking directly, because a chemistry specialist covering a combined entry will quietly leave the physics content thin.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Qualified band. Marks go missing in directed writing where audience and form are specified and ignored. That is a technique problem with a short fix, so this is a subject where a six-session block usually beats a term-long booking.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Qualified band, and genuinely hard to shortcut. Quotation selection and close analysis are the technical skills that separate grades, and both take repeated marked practice rather than explanation. Budget the hours over two terms rather than compressing them.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Budget to qualified band depending on the student. Data-response and extended evaluation questions reward a stated judgement, which is teachable quickly. Content is accessible enough that supervised self-study covers much of it.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Qualified band for the theory paper, which is where grades are lost even by strong programmers. Practical coding help is widely available at the budget band around Academic City, so split the spend rather than paying specialist rates for both halves.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic in every Dubai private school, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Support works from the school's approved material, since using different or additional content requires prior Ministry permission, which also means the market for it is narrower and less price-competitive.

sections.heading: Eight subjects does not mean eight tutors
paragraphs: A Year 11 student in Dubai sits eight or nine IGCSE subjects. A mixed report arrives and the instinct is to cover the low grades, which is how a family ends up quoting for three or four subjects at once. The problem is that a low grade in January is not evidence of a structural gap. It can be a missed unit, a bad test week, a teacher change, or a student who revised the wrong topic. Only one of those needs paid tuition.

The diagnostic question to ask about each weak subject is whether the student can explain what went wrong. A student who says the paper covered the one unit they missed has described a fixable absence and probably needs two sessions. A student who cannot say what the questions were asking has described something structural and needs a term. The second case is where specialist money belongs, and it is rarely more than two subjects at once.

There is also a sequencing argument. Mathematics underpins the quantitative parts of physics and chemistry, so fixing mathematics first often lifts two other subjects without anyone being paid to teach them. English Language technique transfers to the extended written answers in biology, geography and business. Spending in the right order reduces how much spending is needed, and no provider has any incentive to tell you that.

One further caution. A report that shows four weak grades sometimes reflects a term in which the whole year group was taught by a cover teacher, or a student who was unwell for a fortnight in October. Before committing to anything, ask the school whether the pattern is particular to your child or visible across the class. That single question has saved more Dubai families more money than any discount a tutoring provider has ever offered them.

sections.heading: One-to-one, small group or a tuition centre
paragraphs: One-to-one is the most expensive hour and the only one that is paced to your child. Small-group tuition of two to four students lowers the cost per student and works well for shared content: a past-paper walkthrough, a revision sweep across a topic everyone needs, a board-specific technique session. It stops working the moment the students in the room have different gaps, because the hour then serves an average that describes none of them.

Tuition centres sit differently again. A centre with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That is a genuine compliance burden and it is reflected in centre pricing. It also means a centre's regulatory position is checkable in a way an individual's is not.

The honest comparison is in the table below, written by model rather than by brand, because comparing named competitors on quality claims is neither fair nor useful. What it shows is that the cheapest option per hour is rarely the cheapest per mark moved, and that the right answer changes by subject. Shared revision belongs in a group. A structural algebra gap belongs one-to-one, and buying the group version of it twice costs more than buying the right version once.

A practical hybrid often beats either option on cost. Buy one-to-one for the diagnosed structural subject and put the shared revision into a small group or into supervised self-study with past papers from the school. Families who split the spend this way across Years 10 and 11 consistently report paying less in total than those who choose a single model and apply it to everything, because the expensive hours go only where they are actually required.

sections.heading: The extras nobody quotes
paragraphs: An hourly rate is not a price. The gaps between them are where a budget quietly doubles, and almost none of these appear in a first conversation. Registration or matching fees. Minimum booking blocks that have to be paid in advance. Cancellation windows short enough that a sick child costs a full session. Assessment or report fees. Materials charges. Rate increases at the start of an examination term, when a family has least leverage to change provider.

Then there are the structural extras specific to IGCSE. A private-candidate examination entry, if a student is resitting outside their school, is paid to a centre rather than to a tutor. A remark after results costs money and has a short deadline. A November resit means an entry fee plus a term of preparation. None of these is a tutoring cost in anyone's accounting, and all of them land on the same family in the same year.

One further item deserves naming: VAT. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as fact, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation we do not have. What a parent can reasonably demand is clarity about whether a quoted figure includes VAT or not, in writing, from whoever is quoting it. A provider who cannot answer that about its own prices has told you something about its administration.

The pattern behind all six items is the same: ambiguity favours the provider. A rate quoted without a lesson length, a cancellation policy described as flexible, a VAT position left unstated. None of those is necessarily dishonest, and all of them are resolved by one written exchange before the first lesson. Keep the reply. A provider who answers all six plainly has told you more about how it operates than any testimonial on its website could.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE money is specifically wasted
paragraphs: Three leaks account for most of it. The first is the wrong board. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different courses with different structures, and a tutor who prepares a student for the other one teaches a perfectly good term of the wrong material. This is invisible until a mock paper arrives looking unfamiliar. Confirming the code costs one message to the school and protects every hour afterwards.

The second is the tier. On many Cambridge syllabuses a student is entered for Core or Extended, and the Core route does not reach the top grades. The window to review that entry is Year 10 and early Year 11. A family that spends heavily in the spring of Year 11 on a Core entry is paying specialist rates for a grade ceiling that was fixed months earlier, which is the most expensive misunderstanding in this market.

The third is starting late. Bestimate puts an exam-year specialist at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above per month for one weekly hour. Compressing a structural fix into the final term means buying more of those months at once, under worse conditions, with a student who is also revising eight other subjects. The same gap addressed in Year 10 costs a fraction and succeeds more often. Nobody sells Year 10 tuition hard, because panic is a better sales environment.

A fourth leak deserves naming because it is almost invisible. Families pay for sessions through a term in which the student is not attempting the work set between them, so each hour is spent re-teaching the last. If homework from the tutor is not being done, the correct response is to pause the booking and deal with that, not to add a session. Paying for repetition feels like persistence and is simply expense.

sections.heading: Timing the spend against the June and November series
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so no student at a Dubai school will sit it, and any page handing a UAE parent a February entry deadline has imported another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them. So take dates from your school's exams officer or the board's live timetable, never from a tutoring page.

What a budget can be planned around is the shape. Entries close months before the papers. Mocks sit a term earlier and are free diagnostic data, so the cheapest diagnosis in the year is reading a mock paper properly rather than buying an assessment. The intensive spend belongs in the weeks before the series, not spread thinly across two years. And the November series is the resit route, with Pearson's November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026, which is early enough to matter for sixth-form conversations.

There is one exception to spending late, and it is worth knowing. Marked timed practice in the final six to eight weeks genuinely does move marks, because exam technique responds faster than content knowledge does. So a late intensive is not wasted money in itself; it is wasted when it is being asked to do a structural job it cannot do in the time available. Know which of the two you are buying.

sections.heading: Compliance is a cost, and an unpermitted tutor is cheap for a reason
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states that it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, which lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time.

Because the permit is free, a tutor who does not hold one has not saved money by skipping it. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts is published anywhere official, so this page quotes none, and a figure circulating online could not be verified against any ministry source. Ask the question directly; the answer is informative either way.

The institutional version is different. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, up to six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and does not describe itself as KHDA approved, because that phrase names a specific authorisation rather than a general endorsement.

Two further checks sit outside the regulator's remit and are worth making anyway. Ask who the tutor is accountable to if something goes wrong, and ask what happens to the money if sessions stop. An individual working privately answers to nobody but you, which is fine when all goes well and offers no recourse when it does not. A platform should be able to answer both questions in a sentence each.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Festival City, and the hours we will not sell you
paragraphs: Send the subject, the syllabus code, the tier if you know it, and what the student says about why the subject is going wrong. That last item is the cheapest diagnostic input there is and almost nobody asks for it. We match a tutor to the code and run a free trial lesson as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, at no cost. You then get a written note of the gap by topic and a recommended number of hours.

Sometimes that recommendation is two sessions. Sometimes it is that the subject does not need paid tuition at all and a different one does. We would rather say so, because a family that spends correctly once comes back, and a family that spends badly tells everyone in Nad Al Hamar about it. If the recommendation is smaller than you expected, that is the diagnosis working rather than a soft sell.

The limits, stated. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. There is no UAE office, centre or branch, and we do not claim one. We hold no regulator or board approval. We do not supply board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads, because reproducing them is not ours to do, and we will not describe a tutor as a current examiner without evidence. Everything else is a conversation.

What you should expect from the first month is specific and modest. Your child should know which paper and which tier they are being prepared for. You should hold a written list of the topics costing marks. And one element of exam technique should visibly improve, because technique moves before content does. Grade movement takes longer and nobody can promise it; a provider opening with a predicted grade has shown you how it sells.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest IGCSE tutoring available to a Dubai Festival City family?
faqs.answer: The lowest published rates in this market are Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both online, both read in October 2026. That band is often delivered by university students and it is the correct purchase for homework supervision, content recall and Key Stage 3 gaps. It is the wrong purchase for Extended tier content or marked exam technique, where a term at that rate typically produces reassurance without grade movement.

faqs.question: How much should we expect to pay for a good IGCSE subject tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures rather than ours: roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified online subject tutor, with Unitors advertising IGCSE from AED 150, and AED 200 to 450 and above for a specialist, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to 500 because travel is inside the figure. IB Gram's own terms follow the free trial lesson and a diagnosis, since one hourly number across Year 7 English and Extended Chemistry would mislead in both directions.

faqs.question: My child has four weak IGCSE grades. Do we need four tutors?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not. A low grade in one report can be a missed unit, a bad test week or revision aimed at the wrong topic, and only a structural gap needs a term of paid tuition. Ask the student about each subject: if they can say which weeks they missed, that is two sessions. If they cannot say what the questions were asking, that is the structural one. Fixing mathematics first also lifts the quantitative parts of physics and chemistry at no extra cost.

faqs.question: Is small-group tuition worth the saving for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For shared content, yes. A past-paper walkthrough, a revision sweep across a topic everybody in the group needs, or a board-specific technique session all work well in a group of two to four and cost less per student. It stops working when the students have different gaps, because the hour then serves an average that fits none of them. The test is whether the group shares the same board, the same tier and roughly the same weakness.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel to homes in Al Badia or Mirdif, and does that change the price?
faqs.answer: IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Across the wider market, in-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour by Bestimate and by independent home tutors, with travel inside the figure, and monthly in-home packages at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions against about AED 799 for eight online sessions. Our delivery is live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, so no travel component exists to price.

faqs.question: What hidden charges should we ask about before booking IGCSE tuition?
faqs.answer: Six, and all of them are reasonable to ask in the first conversation. Any registration or matching fee before the first lesson. Minimum booking blocks paid in advance. The cancellation window, and whether it applies to the provider as well as to you. Whether a quoted figure is per hour or per lesson, and how long a lesson is. Whether the rate can rise mid-engagement. And whether the figure includes VAT, which should be answered in writing either way.

faqs.question: Does the Core or Extended decision affect how much we should spend?
faqs.answer: It is the single largest financial variable in Years 10 and 11. On many Cambridge syllabuses a student is entered for Core or Extended, and the Core route does not reach the top grades. The window to review that entry is Year 10 and early Year 11, with the school. Spending heavily in the spring of Year 11 on a Core entry means paying specialist rates for a ceiling fixed months earlier, which is the most expensive misunderstanding available in this market.

faqs.question: When should a Dubai Festival City family start paying for IGCSE support?
faqs.answer: Earlier and smaller than most do. Year 9 has no external stakes, so a term of budget-band work on one named weakness costs a fraction of fixing the same thing in Year 11, when Bestimate puts an exam-year specialist at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above per month for one weekly hour. Nobody markets Year 10 tuition hard because panic sells better, but the same gap addressed early costs less and closes more often. Start with a diagnosis, not a booking.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subject gives the best return on tutoring money?
faqs.answer: Chemistry, usually, because two of its hardest areas are learnable procedures rather than vague skills: moles calculations and the Cambridge qualitative analysis tables. A short targeted block on those moves marks faster than a term of general chemistry support. English Language is similar, since most lost marks come from ignoring a specified audience or form in directed writing, which is a technique fix rather than a knowledge one.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE exam entry cost if my child resits in November?
faqs.answer: Entry fees are set by the examination centre rather than by a tutor, so ask your school or the centre directly, and hold a reserve for them before you commit the whole budget to tuition. The relevant timing is that Pearson's November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026, which makes the November series a workable resit route for a June candidate. A remark is a separate cost with a short deadline after results.

faqs.question: Does a tutor in Dubai need a licence, and does it cost them anything?
faqs.answer: Yes, and no. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Because it is free, a tutor without one has saved nothing by skipping it. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no amounts are published.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE actually require for university equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track, five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. At least one page ranking for UAE tutoring queries states six, which is wrong and leads families to enter extra subjects at real cost. Verify on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre cheaper than one-to-one tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Per hour, usually, and per diagnosed gap, often not. A centre teaches to a group, so it is good value for structured revision courses and poor value for a student whose weakness is specific. Centres with premises and staff in Dubai need a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry, which is a compliance cost reflected in pricing and also a regulatory position you can check.

faqs.question: Can we pay for fewer hours and get a written plan instead?
faqs.answer: That is close to how we would prefer it to work. A free trial lesson plus a written gap note gives you the diagnosis and the recommended hours at no cost, and some families take that away and act on it themselves with school support. Where paid hours follow, the best-value shape is a short targeted block on one named thing rather than an open weekly booking. A provider that only offers the open booking has told you what it is optimising for.

faqs.question: What should we do if the tutor's rate rises in the exam term?
faqs.answer: Ask about it before you book, because the exam term is when a family has least leverage and most urgency, which is precisely why rate changes land there. Get the rate fixed in writing for a stated period, along with the cancellation window and whether the figure is per hour or per lesson. If a provider will not commit to a fixed rate through the series, treat the quoted number as an opening figure rather than a price.
