intro.heading: The subjects nobody advertises, and where the marks actually sit
paragraphs: Search for IGCSE support in this part of Dubai and the results converge on four subjects: maths, chemistry, physics and biology. There is a reason, and it is supply rather than need. Those subjects have the clearest diagnosis, the most abundant resources and the largest tutor pool, so that is where the market forms. Meanwhile a typical Year 11 timetable in this district carries eight to ten subjects, and the two or three grades holding a transcript down are frequently in English, Economics, Business Studies or a humanity.

Those subjects fail in a way that is less visible and more fixable. In English First Language, a student who reads well loses reading marks for retelling a passage rather than selecting from it, and loses composition marks to register drift rather than to grammar. In Economics, a correct diagram with an unlabelled axis scores below what the student knew. In Business Studies, a textbook definition applied to no named organisation collects the first mark and stops. In History, a source question answered without using the source is the single commonest loss on the paper.

None of that is addressed by re-teaching content, which is what a general tutor will do because content is what they can see. It is addressed by working on the student's own written answers against the mark scheme, repeatedly, which requires someone who has read those mark schemes. The tutor pool for that is genuinely thin locally, and it is the main practical reason a family in this district should not be filtering a shortlist by distance.

Dubai Harbour makes that filter particularly unhelpful. The district is new, built around a cruise terminal and marina berths, approached through a single corridor off King Salman Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud Street shared with Emaar Beachfront and the Palm Jumeirah approach. There is no school and no tuition centre inside it, and children travel to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Jumeirah, leaving before 07:00 and returning after 15:30. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service.

What follows works through those subjects by code: English First Language and Second Language, Economics and Business Studies, History and Geography, ICT and Computer Science, and the Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies that Dubai private schools must deliver alongside any international curriculum. Each section names what the paper rewards and where the marks leak. Confirm the board and syllabus code for each subject with your exams officer, because the code decides which past papers are worth working.

sections.heading: English 0500: where a strong reader loses marks
paragraphs: First Language English is the subject that most often surprises families in this district, because a child who reads constantly and writes fluently comes home with a grade in the middle. The explanation is almost always technique. On the reading paper, students answer by retelling the passage when the question asked them to select from it, analyse it, or infer from it. The content is present, the question was not answered, and the mark scheme cannot credit the difference.

On directed writing the dominant loss is register drift. A student is asked to write a letter, a report or a speech, begins correctly, and twenty lines later is writing an essay. Form carries marks on these questions, so the drift costs even where the prose is good. On composition, the problem is shape rather than style: fluent writing with no deliberate structure, no planned ending, and no variation in sentence length to control pace. All three are mechanical and all three improve quickly.

The repair is writing and marking, not reading and discussing. A student who writes one timed response a week, marks it against the official scheme themselves, and has the marking audited will move within a month, because the mark scheme teaches what the examiner wants in a way no amount of advice does. Confirm whether your child sits 0500 or 0990, since the grading scale differs, and whether they are on First Language or Second Language English, because those are different examinations entirely.

sections.heading: Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450: the application marks
paragraphs: Both subjects are marked on application and both are taught as content, which is the whole problem. In Economics, a question about a price change in a named market wants the diagram drawn for that market, with axes labelled, the shift direction marked, and a sentence explaining what the diagram shows about that market. Students supply a correct generic diagram and a paragraph of theory, which collects the knowledge marks and none of the application marks.

In Business Studies the same pattern appears in prose. A question about a named company's decision wants reasoning that could only apply to that company, drawn from the case material. Students supply a definition and a general advantage and disadvantage, which again collects the first mark and stops. Evaluation questions then want a judgement with a reason, and students supply a balanced list and no conclusion, which caps the answer below the top band however much they know.

Both repairs are short and both are structural. In Economics, draw the diagram first and label it before writing a word; in Business Studies, name the context in the first sentence of every paragraph and finish every evaluation with a judgement sentence that begins with a decision. Four sessions of enforcing those two rules on the student's own answers typically moves both grades, and it is work almost nobody buys because it looks like technique rather than teaching.

There is a third pattern worth naming, common to both subjects. Students answer the question they expected rather than the one printed, particularly where a familiar topic appears with an unfamiliar instruction. A question asking whether a decision was justified is not a question asking what the decision was, and an answer explaining the decision thoroughly collects very little. Reading the instruction aloud before writing is a crude habit and it prevents the most expensive single error in either paper.

sections.heading: History 0470 and Geography 0460: using the material you are given
paragraphs: History papers hand students the evidence they need and the commonest loss on the paper is not using it. A source question asks what a source suggests, how two sources differ, or how useful a source is, and the answer must refer to the source's content, its provenance, or both. Students answer from their own knowledge, which is often correct and cannot score, because the question was about the source. Recognising which kind of source question is being asked is a ten-minute lesson that pays for the rest of the course.

Essay questions fail differently. Students narrate the events in order and reach the end of the available time without having argued anything. The mark scheme wants a case made against the question, with evidence selected because it supports the case rather than because it happened. Writing the conclusion first, in one sentence, and then selecting evidence for it, is the single most effective structural change available in the subject.

Geography loses marks on case studies. The mark scheme wants named places, specific figures and dates, and a student who writes generically about coastal erosion or urban growth collects the general marks and misses the specific ones. The fix is a case-study card per topic with five facts on it, learned as facts. Skills questions, by contrast, are the most reliably scoring part of the paper, and students who practise map, graph and photograph interpretation under timing gain marks faster there than anywhere else in the subject.

sections.heading: ICT 0417 and Computer Science 0478: documentation and trace tables
paragraphs: The practical components in ICT are lost on documentation rather than on capability. Evidence requirements are specific: particular screenshots, particular filenames, evidence presented in the order the tasks were set. A student who completes every task competently and submits evidence in the wrong order, or with a file named incorrectly, loses marks that have nothing to do with their ability. A checklist drawn up once, before the component, prevents nearly all of it.

Computer Science fails on a different habit. Algorithmic questions reward pseudocode that declares its variables, uses consistent indentation, and is accompanied by a trace table where one is asked for. Students write logic that works and omit the surrounding structure, then lose method marks. The trace table in particular is the fastest single improvement in the subject: students avoid it because it is tedious, and it is where several marks sit on most algorithm questions.

Both subjects reward a kind of discipline that is easy to teach and difficult to self-impose, which makes them unusually good value for tutoring. Four sessions on evidence requirements and trace tables will typically recover more marks than a term of content revision, and neither requires the tutor to be in the room. What a tutor may not do is complete a task, supply working files, or produce the documentation; the component must be the student's own work and the school supervises it.

One more point about both subjects. They are the two where families most often assume a screen is a disadvantage and where it is arguably an advantage, because the work is produced on a computer anyway. A shared screen lets a tutor watch a file being named, a screenshot being taken and a trace table being filled, and intervene at the moment the convention is broken rather than after the component is submitted and the marks are gone.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies alongside IGCSE
paragraphs: Families arriving in Dubai Harbour from outside the UAE are often surprised that their child's timetable includes subjects their curriculum does not set. Dubai private schools must deliver Arabic language, Islamic Education and social and moral studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed to teach. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond those subjects but must follow the Ministry's general regulations, and KHDA's mandatory-subjects guidance set the start of the 2025-26 academic year as the implementation point, with April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The structure has consequences for support. KHDA requires separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies: combined classes for Arab and non-Arab students are prohibited, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, while for non-Arab students Islamic Education and the moral, social and cultural studies strand are taught in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two practical points follow. A tutor has to know which stream the child sits in, because the material is not interchangeable and matching it wrongly wastes the sessions. And for these subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is prohibited, so support works with the school's own material rather than substituting a parallel syllabus. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with KHDA advising that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes, and schools must ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach them.

sections.heading: Answer length, timing and the last question on the paper
paragraphs: In the essay and application subjects, timing costs more marks than content. A student who writes a thorough answer to a four-mark question and then has nine minutes for a twelve-mark question has lost marks through allocation rather than through ignorance. This is more acute in English, History, Geography, Economics and Business Studies than in maths and the sciences, because extended answers invite over-writing and there is no natural signal to stop.

The discipline is arithmetic. Divide the available minutes by the available marks before writing anything, write the per-question allowance on the paper, and stop when it is spent. A student who leaves a question half-finished at its allowance and returns to it later scores more than one who finishes it perfectly and never reaches the final question. Most students have never been told this explicitly, and it is the single largest recoverable loss in a humanities paper.

The second half of the discipline is knowing what a mark allowance implies about length. A two-mark question wants two points, not a paragraph. A six-mark question wants development, not a list. A twelve-mark question wants a structure with a judgement at the end. Students who match length to marks finish papers; students who write as much as they know do not. Counting unattempted marks on a mock script is the quickest way to find out which kind of student you have, and it takes about a minute.

The habit has to be practised under timing to exist at all. A student who agrees with the arithmetic in a session and then writes without a clock in the examination will do exactly what they always did, because the behaviour is driven by anxiety rather than by ignorance. Two or three full papers sat under real timing, with the allowances written on the paper beforehand, is what converts the principle into something that holds when the room goes quiet.

sections.heading: Why this support is scarce locally, and what that means
paragraphs: The local tutoring market in this cluster forms around maths and the sciences for sound reasons. Those subjects have abundant resources, a clear diagnosis from a script, and the largest number of available teachers. English, Economics, Business Studies, History and Geography have fewer tutors, and a greater proportion of those who do advertise are generalists who teach content confidently and have not recently read the relevant mark scheme.

That matters because in these subjects the mark scheme is the entire difference between a 5 and a 7. A tutor who has not read it will discuss the topic knowledgeably, the student will enjoy the sessions, the content knowledge will improve and the grade will hold. Families then conclude the child has reached their ceiling in a subject where the ceiling was never the problem. The question to ask any prospective tutor in these subjects is simple: when did you last mark an answer in this subject against the official scheme?

Removing travel from the arrangement widens the pool enough to find someone who can answer that question. That is the practical argument for the format in this part of the timetable, and it is stronger here than in maths or science where a local specialist can usually be found. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the comparison is between our online sessions and a local market that, for these subjects specifically, is thin in exactly the way that matters.

sections.heading: Booking support for a full subject basket
paragraphs: Send the whole timetable rather than the one subject you are most worried about, with the board and syllabus code for each. Add the marked mock scripts if the school will release them, and the hours that genuinely exist after a bus that leaves before 07:00 and returns after 15:30. The full timetable matters because the same technique failure often appears in three subjects at once, and reading three scripts together turns three tutoring decisions into one block of work.

We match one tutor per subject and propose slots in Gulf Standard Time. One free trial lesson per student, no card required, producing a written breakdown of lost marks by subject and by habit. Most families start with the technique block when the scripts support it, because it produces gains across several subjects, and then add a single-subject slot where a genuine content gap remains.

The limits. Support in the less-tutored subjects takes longer to match than maths or science, and for a few subjects at particular hours there is nobody suitable in a given week. We will say so and offer alternatives rather than putting a generalist into a mark-scheme problem, which is the arrangement most likely to produce pleasant sessions and a static grade. We cannot promise a grade, and in these subjects the student has to write between sessions, because the marks are awarded for what is on the page.

Finally, a note about order. Where a school assessment is imminent in one subject, that subject takes the first slot regardless of where the biggest long-term gap sits, because a near date beats a large gap. After that assessment the plan reverts to the ranking. Saying this at the outset prevents the common pattern where a family keeps reshuffling the plan around whichever subject was most recently difficult.

faqs.question: Should we buy support for one subject or several?
faqs.answer: Send all of them and let the scripts decide. The same technique failure often appears across English, Economics and a humanity, in which case a single technique block on command terms, source use, context naming and judgement sentences moves three or four grades for the cost of one subject's sessions. Where a genuine content gap remains in one subject afterwards, add a single-subject slot then. Buying three subjects in week one usually buys the same block three times.

faqs.question: Is English Literature worth tutoring if my child likes the texts?
faqs.answer: Often yes, because enjoyment and marks diverge in this subject. Set-text responses reward close reference, and a student who knows the text thoroughly and quotes nothing specific scores in the middle bands. The repair is mechanical: one embedded quotation per paragraph, used in the argument rather than displayed before it. A few sessions on quotation selection and paragraph purpose typically move the grade more than further reading of the text does.

faqs.question: What should the first session in an essay subject look like?
faqs.answer: The student writing. A timed answer produced in the session, marked by the student against the official scheme, then audited by the tutor. That produces an immediate diagnosis of whether the marks are going to content, command terms, application, judgement or timing, and it sets the pattern for every session afterwards. A first session spent discussing the subject is pleasant and tells you very little, because these subjects are marked on what reaches the page.
